description_content.value:
First TEI version, based on Oliver
                Hellwig's plain text file in the Digital Corpus of Sanskrit.

Did a lot of line groups and cleaning
                up, and got the file to a point where it validates against the TEI schema.  There's still
            a great deal to do to bring the file into line with the SARIT guidelines, but I want to get the file
            out to the public so that alchemical vocabulary can be searched in SARIT.  Expect this file to 
            undergo quite a bit of revision in the coming months.  I put "label" tags around a number of headings; that should
            be re-thought. The "Mugdhāvabodhinī" comments need to be changed into proper structural tags.

children.text: jayati sa dainyagadākulam akhilam idaṃ paśyato jagad yasya /
children.translated_text: Victorious is he who, seeing this entire world afflicted by the disease of misery,

children.text: hṛdayasthaiva galitvā jātā rasarūpiṇī karuṇā // GRht_1.1 //
children.translated_text: whose compassion, having the nature of <s>rasa</s> (mercury/essence), arose by melting forth from within his very heart. (GRht 1.1)

children.text: śrīmanmahāgaṇādhipataye namaḥ /
children.translated_text: Salutations to the glorious great Lord <s>Gaṇādhipati</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>).

children.text: bhavabhayarakṣaṇadakṣaṃ natvā mugdhāvabodhinīṃ tanute /
children.translated_text: Having bowed to that which is capable of protecting [one] from the fear of worldly existence, [the commentator] composes, for the instruction of the ignorant,

children.text: rasahṛdayasuprayuktāṃ ṭīkāmṛjubhāvagāmāptaḥ // GRhtCM_1.1:1 //
children.translated_text: a commentary on the <s>Rasahṛdaya</s>, well-composed, conveying the straightforward meaning — [he who is] trustworthy. (GRhtCM 1.1:1)

children.text: guṇavāridhikurapakupe hariharamiśraḥ pratītamahimākhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the ocean of virtues, in the [family] well — <s>Hariharamiśra</s>, known for his well-established greatness,

children.text: tatputro bhuvi mahito maheśa iti nāmavikhyātaḥ // GRhtCM_1.1:2 //
children.translated_text: his son, honored in the world, was renowned by the name <s>Maheśa</s>. (GRhtCM 1.1:2)

children.text: tadanvaye bhāratībhāvasaṃyutas tadātmajaḥ prastutavāgbhirīśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: In his lineage, endowed with devotion to <s>Bhāratī</s> (goddess of speech), his son <s>Īśvara</s>, [master] of accomplished speech,

children.text:
caturbhujo bhāvitabhāvamānasaḥ svapokajātasya kupānubhāvataḥ // GRhtCM_1.1:3
                        //
children.translated_text: four-armed [in skill], with a mind devoted to meditation, by the power of [his family] well. (GRhtCM 1.1:3)

children.text:
jyeṣṭho+abhūd bhuvi pārijātakataruḥ khaṇḍepavāpānvaye tatputraḥ kipa
                        nāthabappavasudaḥ prāṇair yaśo+arthānvitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The eldest arose in the world like a <s>Pārijāta</s> tree in the <s>Khaṇḍepā</s> lineage — his son, <s>Kipa-nātha-bappa</s>, bestowing wealth, endowed with life, fame, and wealth.

children.text:
tatputreṇa ca sāvareṇa patinā bandhasya dharmārthinā gīrvāṇāśu rugoñcajena
                        satataṃ tenātra yatnaḥ kṛtaḥ // GRhtCM_1.1:4 //
children.translated_text: By his son <s>Sāvara</s>, the master seeking <s>dharma</s> and liberation, effort was constantly made here in the language of the gods [Sanskrit], by <s>Rugoñcajena</s>. (GRhtCM 1.1:4)

children.text:
iha śāstrārambhe ācāryaśrīmadgovindapādāḥ śiṣṭasamayaparipāpanārthe śāstrasya
                        deśayato gurupādasya bhagavato vastunirdeśarūpaṃ maṅgapam ācaranti
                        jayatītyādi // GRhtCM_1.1:5 //
children.translated_text: Here, at the commencement of the treatise, the teacher <s>Śrīmad Govindapāda</s>, for the purpose of upholding the conventions of the learned — as the <s>guru</s>, the blessed one, teaches the treatise — performs an auspicious invocation (<s>maṅgala</s>) in the form of a statement of the subject matter, beginning with 'Victorious' and so forth. (GRhtCM 1.1:5)

children.text:
maṅgapapakṣaṇaṃ yathā āśīr namaskriyā vastunirdeśo maṅgapa iti //
                        GRhtCM_1.1:6 //
children.translated_text: The definition of an auspicious invocation (<s>maṅgala</s>): a benediction (<s>āśīḥ</s>), an act of obeisance (<s>namaskriyā</s>), or a statement of the subject matter (<s>vastunirdeśa</s>) — [any of these] is a <s>maṅgala</s>. (GRhtCM 1.1:6)

children.text:
vastunirdeśaḥ pañcadhā yathāsti bhāti priyaṃ rūpaṃ nāma cetyaṃśapañcakam //
                        GRhtCM_1.1:7 //
children.translated_text: The statement of the subject matter is fivefold: existence (<s>asti</s>), consciousness (<s>bhāti</s>), dearness (<s>priya</s>), form (<s>rūpa</s>), and name (<s>nāma</s>) — these are the five aspects. (GRhtCM 1.1:7)

children.text: ādyaṃ trayaṃ brahmarūpaṃ śaktirūpaṃ tato dvayam iti // GRhtCM_1.1:8 //
children.translated_text: The first three are of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>; the latter two are of the nature of <s>Śakti</s> (power). (GRhtCM 1.1:8)

children.text: sa haro jayati sarvotkarṣeṇa vartate // GRhtCM_1.1:9 //
children.translated_text: He — <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) — is victorious, meaning he exists with supreme excellence. (GRhtCM 1.1:9)

children.text: akhipaṃ jagat paśyata iti vastunirdeśābjayaddraṣṭā // GRhtCM_1.1:10 //
children.translated_text: 'Seeing the entire world' — this is the statement of the subject matter — the victorious one is the seer. (GRhtCM 1.1:10)

children.text: tathā ca śrutiḥ apāṇipādo javano grahītā // GRhtCM_1.1:11 //
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>śruti</s> [says]: 'Without hands or feet, [yet] swift and grasping.' (GRhtCM 1.1:11)

children.text: paśyatyacakṣuḥ sa śṛṇotyakarṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He sees without eyes, he hears without ears.'

children.text:
sa vetti vedyaṃ na ca tasya vettā tamāhur agryaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇam iti //
                        GRhtCM_1.1:12 //
children.translated_text: 'He knows what is to be known, yet there is no knower of him — they call him the foremost, the ancient <s>Puruṣa</s>.' (GRhtCM 1.1:12)

children.text:
yasya hṛdayasyaiva rasarūpiṇī karuṇā ghṛṇā jātā prādurbhūtā // GRhtCM_1.1:13
                        //
children.translated_text: Whose compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), having the nature of <s>rasa</s> (mercury/essence), arose — manifested — from within the heart itself. (GRhtCM 1.1:13)

children.text:
kiṃbhūtvā gapitvādravitvā gapitasya sthānāccyutir iti yuktam // GRhtCM_1.1:14
                        //
children.translated_text: In what manner? By melting — <s>galana</s> (flowing/liquefying) is the falling from a fixed state — this is appropriate. (GRhtCM 1.1:14)

children.text: eṣā hṛdayasthaiva // GRhtCM_1.1:15 //
children.translated_text: This [compassion] abides in the heart itself. (GRhtCM 1.1:15)

children.text: evāvyayam anyasthānaniṣedhavāci // GRhtCM_1.1:16 //
children.translated_text: The particle 'eva' (indeed) is indeclinable and negates [its being in] another location. (GRhtCM 1.1:16)

children.text: rasarūpiṇīti rasaḥ pāradastatsvarūpaṃ yasyāḥ sā // GRhtCM_1.1:17 //
children.translated_text: 'Having the nature of <s>rasa</s>' — <s>rasa</s> means <s>pārada</s> (mercury); that whose essential nature is mercury. (GRhtCM 1.1:17)

children.text: tathā ca vākyam /
children.translated_text: And thus the saying [defines <s>rasa</s>]:

children.text: raso japaṃ raso harṣo rasaḥ śṛṅgārapūrvakaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> means sentiment, <s>rasa</s> means joy, <s>rasa</s> means [that which begins with] the erotic (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>),

children.text: svādvādiṣu ca niryāse pārade'pi raso viṣe /
children.translated_text: <s>rasa</s> means essence in sweet and other [flavors], <s>rasa</s> also means mercury, and <s>rasa</s> means poison —

children.text: ityanekārthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.1:18 //
children.translated_text: thus it has multiple meanings. (GRhtCM 1.1:18)

children.text:
sāmānyatastadrūpaṃ dravatvaṃ viśeṣato rasarūpaṃ sarvopakāritvam //
                        GRhtCM_1.1:19 //
children.translated_text: In general, its nature is liquidity (<s>dravatva</s>); specifically, its essential nature as <s>rasa</s> is its capacity to benefit all. (GRhtCM 1.1:19)

children.text: tathā ca vākyaṃ rasaratnākare /
children.translated_text: And thus the statement in the <s>Rasaratnākara</s>:

children.text:
ājanmapāpakṛtanirdahanaikavahnir dāridryaduḥkhagajavāraṇasiṃharūpaḥ iti //
                        GRhtCM_1.1:20 //
children.translated_text: '[Mercury is] the sole fire for burning away sins accumulated since birth, [and has] the form of a lion [destroying] the elephant of the suffering of poverty.' (GRhtCM 1.1:20)

children.text:
kiṃbhūtasya harasya dainyagadākupaṃ jagat saṃsāraṃ paśyataḥ dainyayaṃ ca
                        gadāśca tair ākupaṃ vyāptaṃ dainyaṃ dīnabhāvo dāridryaṃ gadā vyādhaya iti //
                        GRhtCM_1.1:21 //
children.translated_text: Of <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>/mercury), who possesses what quality? — seeing the world, the cycle of existence (<s>saṃsāra</s>), afflicted by wretchedness and disease: wretchedness (<s>dainya</s>) is the state of being destitute, poverty; diseases (<s>gadā</s>) are ailments — pervaded by them. (GRhtCM 1.1:21)

children.text: akhipamiti sarvavyāpipadam // GRhtCM_1.1:22 //
children.translated_text: 'Entire' (<s>akhila</s>) — a word denoting all-pervasiveness. (GRhtCM 1.1:22)

children.text: yathā mañjaryā /
children.translated_text: As [stated] in the <s>Mañjarī</s>:

children.text: yasya rogasya yo yogastenaiva saha dāpayet /
children.translated_text: 'For whatever disease, whatever [alchemical] preparation [is applicable], one should administer it along with that [preparation].'

children.text: rasendro haro rogānnarakuñjaravājinām // GRhtCM_1.1:23 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Rasendra</s> (the lord of mercury) — <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) — destroys the diseases of men, elephants, and horses.' (GRhtCM 1.1:23)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_1.1:24 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 1.1:24)

children.text: anyanmataṃ ca /
children.translated_text: And another view:

children.text: rasabhasma vinā tatra kathyate saṃhitākramaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Without the ash of mercury (<s>rasa-bhasma</s>), the method of the compendium (<s>saṃhitā</s>) is stated here;

children.text: anuktamapi vijñeyaṃ tatra tatrāṅgaśāntaye // GRhtCM_1.1:25 //
children.translated_text: even what is not [explicitly] stated should be known [as applicable] in the respective contexts for the pacification of [bodily] parts.' (GRhtCM 1.1:25)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_1.1:26 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 1.1:26)

children.text: pītāmbaro+atha balijinnāgakṣayabahalarāgagaruḍacaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Yellow-robed, then conqueror of <s>Bali</s>, whose great passion is for the destruction of serpents, who moves like <s>Garuḍa</s> —

children.text: jayati sa haririva harajo vidalitabhavadainyaduḥkhabharaḥ // GRht_1.2 //
children.translated_text: Victorious is he, <s>Haraja</s> (born of <s>Hara</s>), like <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), who has shattered the burden of worldly wretchedness and suffering. (GRht 1.2)

children.text: pītetyādi // GRhtCM_1.2:1 //
children.translated_text: 'Yellow-robed' and so forth — (GRhtCM 1.2:1)

children.text:
anena padyena kavirharajasya hareśca samatvaṃ sūcayati // GRhtCM_1.2:2
                            //
children.translated_text: By this verse, the poet indicates the equality of <s>Haraja</s> (mercury/son of <s>Śiva</s>) and <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>). (GRhtCM 1.2:2)

children.text:
sa purāṇakavivarṇito harajo jayati sarvotkarṣeṇa vartate harādīśvarājjāto
                            harajaḥ // GRhtCM_1.2:3 //
children.translated_text: <s>Haraja</s>, as described by the ancient poet, is victorious — exists with supreme excellence — born from <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), hence <s>Haraja</s>. (GRhtCM 1.2:3)

children.text: sa utprekṣyate haririva viṣṇur iva // GRhtCM_1.2:4 //
children.translated_text: He is imagined as being like <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>). (GRhtCM 1.2:4)

children.text:
kiṃbhūto hariḥ pītāmbaraḥ pīte ambare vastre yasya saḥ dukūpayugmatvāt //
                            GRhtCM_1.2:5 //
children.translated_text: What is <s>Hari</s> like? Yellow-robed — one whose garment (<s>ambara</s>) is yellow; because of the pair of silk garments. (GRhtCM 1.2:5)

children.text:
punaḥ kimbhūto bapijit bapiṃ bapināmānaṃ daityaviśeṣaṃ jayatīti tathoktaḥ
                            // GRhtCM_1.2:6 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, what is he like? Conqueror of <s>Bali</s> — he conquers <s>Bali</s>, the particular demon named <s>Bali</s> — thus he is called. (GRhtCM 1.2:6)

children.text:
punaḥ kiṃbhūtaḥ nāgakṣayetyādi nāgānāṃ śeṣādīnāṃ kṣayāya nāśāya
                            bahaparāgo bahuprīto yo 'sau garuḍaḥ khageśvaraḥ tatra carati gacchati
                            tathoktaḥ // GRhtCM_1.2:7 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, what is he like? 'For the destruction of serpents' and so forth — one who has great passion (<s>rāga</s>) for the destruction of serpents such as <s>Śeṣa</s> and others, that <s>Garuḍa</s>, the lord of birds — he moves there, goes there — thus he is called. (GRhtCM 1.2:7)

children.text:
punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ vidapitetyādiḥ viśeṣaṇena dapito dūrīkṛto bhavasya
                            saṃsārasya duḥkhabharo yena saḥ dainyaṃ dāridryaṃ duḥkhaṃ vyādhirūpaṃ
                            tayorbharo bāhupyam iti // GRhtCM_1.2:8 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, what distinguishes him? 'Having shattered' and so forth — he by whom the burden of the suffering of worldly existence (<s>bhava</s>) has been shattered, split apart: wretchedness (<s>dainya</s>) is poverty, suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>) is in the form of disease, and their burden means abundance. (GRhtCM 1.2:8)

children.text:
adhunā harajaṃ viśeṣayati kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ pītāmbaraḥ pītāmbaraḥ pūrvārthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_1.2:9 //
children.translated_text: Now he qualifies <s>Haraja</s> (mercury): what distinguishes it? Yellow-robed — the same meaning as before. (GRhtCM 1.2:9)

children.text:
kathaṃ yuktaḥ tamarthe spaṣṭayatyanena sūtarājenāpi catvāri vāsāṃsi
                            dhṛtāni viprādivarṇabhedāt // GRhtCM_1.2:10 //
children.translated_text: How is this appropriate? He clarifies the meaning with this — the king of mercury (<s>sūtarāja</s>) too has four coverings, due to the distinction of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and other classes. (GRhtCM 1.2:10)

children.text: rasaratnākare yathā /
children.translated_text: As [stated] in the <s>Rasaratnākara</s>:

children.text: śvetāruṇaharidrābhakṛṣṇā viprādipāradāḥ iti // GRhtCM_1.2:11 //
children.translated_text: 'The mercuries [corresponding to] <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and other [classes] are white, red, yellow, and dark.' (GRhtCM 1.2:11)

children.text:
brāhmaṇakṣatriyavaiśyaśūdrāḥ śvetaraktapītakṛṣṇavastradhāriṇo jñātavyāḥ
                            na tv eṣāṃ svarūpam iti // GRhtCM_1.2:12 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, and <s>Śūdra</s> [types of mercury] should be known as wearing white, red, yellow, and dark coverings respectively — but this is not their essential nature. (GRhtCM 1.2:12)

children.text: rasamañjaryā yathā /
children.translated_text: As [stated] in the <s>Rasamañjarī</s>:

children.text:
antaḥ sunīpo bahirujjvapo yo madhyāhnasūryapratimaprakāśaḥ iti //
                            GRhtCM_1.2:13 //
children.translated_text: 'That which is dark blue within and brilliant without, shining like the midday sun.' (GRhtCM 1.2:13)

children.text: antaḥ svarūpaṃ bahirvāsāṃsīti kiṃvadantī // GRhtCM_1.2:14 //
children.translated_text: Within is its essential nature; without are its coverings — so goes the tradition. (GRhtCM 1.2:14)

children.text: atheti samuccaye prasādaḥ // GRhtCM_1.2:15 //
children.translated_text: 'Atha' (now) — [used here] in the sense of conjunction, [meaning] favour/grace. (GRhtCM 1.2:15)

children.text:
atheti maṅgapānantarārambhapraśnakāpasvādhikārapratijñāsamuccayeṣv iti //
                            GRhtCM_1.2:16 //
children.translated_text: 'Atha' is [used] in the senses of: auspiciousness, subsequent commencement, question, time, proper qualification, declaration, and conjunction. (GRhtCM 1.2:16)

children.text:
punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ bapijit bapīn jayatīti bapiścarma jarākṛtam //
                            GRhtCM_1.2:17 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, what distinguishes him? Conqueror of <s>Bali</s> — he conquers <s>bali</s> (wrinkles); <s>bali</s> also means the skin produced by old age. (GRhtCM 1.2:17)

children.text: ityanekārthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.2:18 //
children.translated_text: Thus it has multiple meanings. (GRhtCM 1.2:18)

children.text:
punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ nāgakṣayetyādi nā puṃsvarūpaḥ punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ gamyate
                            'neneti gaḥ pakṣayor gaḥ gakṣaye pakṣanāśe sati bahaparāgo bahurāgavān
                            yaḥ sa rasaḥ tena garuḍa iva cāryate iti // GRhtCM_1.2:19 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, what distinguishes it? 'For the destruction of serpents' and so forth — <s>nā</s> means [in] the form of a man; furthermore, what distinguishes it? — that which is known as 'ga' (that by which one goes) — in both [literal] senses, <s>ga</s> [means] wings; when the wings are destroyed, the one having great passion (<s>rāga</s>) — that is <s>rasa</s> (mercury) — it is carried like <s>Garuḍa</s>. (GRhtCM 1.2:19)

children.text:
kiṃ pāradaḥ pakṣanāśe sati ākāśagamanaṃ dadātīti tātparyārthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_1.2:20 //
children.translated_text: Does mercury, when the wings [of base metals] are destroyed, grant the power of moving through the sky? — this is the intended meaning. (GRhtCM 1.2:20)

children.text: rasaratnākare yathā /
children.translated_text: As [stated] in the <s>Rasaratnākara</s>:

children.text: hato hanti jarāmṛtyuṃ mūrchito vyādhighātakaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'When killed (<s>hata</s>), it destroys old age and death; when solidified (<s>mūrchita</s>), it destroys diseases;

children.text:
datte ca khe gatiṃ baddhaḥ ko 'nyaḥ sūtāt kriyākaraḥ // GRhtCM_1.2:21
                            //
children.translated_text: when bound (<s>baddha</s>), it grants the ability to move through the sky — who other than <s>Sūta</s> (mercury) is such a doer of [wondrous] deeds?' (GRhtCM 1.2:21)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_1.2:22 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 1.2:22)

children.text:
punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ vidapitetyādiḥ pūrvārthaḥ karuṇāparatvena
                            dainyaduḥkhahāritvaṃ sūcayati // GRhtCM_1.2:23 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, what distinguishes it? 'Having shattered' and so forth — the same meaning as before; [the verse] indicates mercury's capacity to remove wretchedness and suffering through its compassionate nature. (GRhtCM 1.2:23)

children.text: mūrchitvā harati rujaṃ bandhanamanubhūya muktido bhavati /
children.translated_text: Having been solidified (<s>mūrchita</s>), it removes ailment; having undergone binding (<s>bandhana</s>), it grants liberation (<s>mukti</s>).

children.text: amarīkaroti sumṛtaḥ ko 'nyaḥ karuṇākaraḥ sūtāt // GRht_1.3 //
children.translated_text: Being well-processed (<s>sumṛta</s>), it bestows immortality — who other than <s>Sūta</s> (mercury) is such a compassionate one? (GRht 1.3)

children.text:
yaḥ pūrvaviśiṣṭo harajas tasmādanyaḥ karuṇāparo dayāvān kaḥ na ko 'pi
                            yato rujaṃ śarīravyathāṃ harati // GRhtCM_1.3:1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Haraja</s> (mercury), possessing the qualities described above — who other than he is so compassionate and merciful? None — because he removes bodily suffering. (GRhtCM 1.3:1)

children.text: kiṃbhūtvā mūrchitvā mūrchito bhūtvā // GRhtCM_1.3:2 //
children.translated_text: In what state? Having been solidified (<s>mūrchita</s>) — having become <s>mūrchita</s> (solidified). (GRhtCM 1.3:2)

children.text: mūrchitapakṣaṇaṃ rasaratnākare /
children.translated_text: The definition of <s>mūrchita</s> (solidified mercury) in the <s>Rasaratnākara</s>:

children.text: kajjapābho yadā sūto vihāya ghanacāpapam /
children.translated_text: 'When <s>sūta</s> (mercury), abandoning its dense fluidity, appears with the colour of lampblack (<s>kajjala</s>),

children.text: dṛśyate 'sau tadā jñeyo mūrchitaḥ sūtarāḍbudhaiḥ // GRhtCM_1.3:3 //
children.translated_text: then it should be known by the wise as <s>mūrchita</s> (solidified) — the king of mercury.' (GRhtCM 1.3:3)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_1.3:4 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 1.3:4)

children.text:
punarbandhanamanubhūya dhṛtvā muktido bhavati muktiṃ dadātīti //
                            GRhtCM_1.3:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, having undergone binding (<s>bandhana</s>) — having been fixed — it grants liberation (<s>mukti</s>), gives liberation. (GRhtCM 1.3:5)

children.text:
muktiścaturdhā varṇitā sāpokyasārūpyasāmīpyasāyujyabhedāt // GRhtCM_1.3:6
                            //
children.translated_text: Liberation (<s>mukti</s>) is described as fourfold, due to the distinctions of <s>sālokyā</s> (same world), <s>sārūpya</s> (same form), <s>sāmīpya</s> (proximity), and <s>sāyujya</s> (union). (GRhtCM 1.3:6)

children.text:
bandhanaṃ ca mukhyatayā dvividham avāntaravyāpāreṇa ca caturvidham //
                            GRhtCM_1.3:7 //
children.translated_text: And binding (<s>bandhana</s>) is principally of two kinds, and of four kinds with secondary processes. (GRhtCM 1.3:7)

children.text:
adhunā dvividhabandhanoddeśaḥ nirbījabaddho bījabaddhaśca // GRhtCM_1.3:8
                            //
children.translated_text: Now, the enumeration of the two kinds of binding: <s>nirbīja-baddha</s> (bound without seed) and <s>bīja-baddha</s> (bound with seed). (GRhtCM 1.3:8)

children.text: nirbījabaddho yathā rasamañjaryām /
children.translated_text: <s>Nirbīja-baddha</s> (seedless binding) as [described] in the <s>Rasamañjarī</s>:

children.text: rasastu pādāṃśasuvarṇajīrṇaḥ piṣṭīkṛto gandhakayogataśca /
children.translated_text: 'When mercury has consumed a quarter-part of gold, is made into a paste (<s>piṣṭī</s>), and through combination with sulphur,

children.text:
tupyāṃśagandhaiḥ puṭitaḥ krameṇa nirbījanāmākhiparogahartā //
                            GRhtCM_1.3:9 //
children.translated_text: is heated in stages with one-third portion of sulphur — it is called <s>nirbīja</s> (seedless), [and] removes all diseases.' (GRhtCM 1.3:9)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_1.3:10 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 1.3:10)

children.text: punar bījabaddho yathā /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>bīja-baddha</s> (seeded binding) is as follows:

children.text: bījīkṛtair abhrasattvahematārārkakāntaiḥ saha sādhito yaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'That which is prepared with seeding agents — essences of mica (<s>abhra</s>), gold, silver (<s>tārā</s>), and loadstone (<s>arkakānta</s>) —

children.text:
yutastataḥ ṣaḍguṇagandhacūrṇaiḥ sa bījabaddhe 'pyadhikaprabhāvaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_1.3:11 //
children.translated_text: and then combined with sixfold sulphur powder — even in the seeded binding, it has superior power.' (GRhtCM 1.3:11)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_1.3:12 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 1.3:12)

children.text: avāntaracaturvidhabandhoddeśo yathā /
children.translated_text: The enumeration of the four secondary types of binding is as follows:

children.text: poṭaḥ khoṭo japaukā ca bhasmatvaṃ ca caturvidham /
children.translated_text: '<s>Loṭa</s> (lump/pellet), <s>khoṭa</s> (impure solidification), <s>jalaukā</s> (leech-like), and calcination (<s>bhasmatva</s>) — these four

children.text: bandhaścaturvidhaḥ sūte vijñeyo bhiṣaguttamaiḥ // GRhtCM_1.3:13 //
children.translated_text: types of binding in mercury should be known by the best physicians.' (GRhtCM 1.3:13)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_1.3:14 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 1.3:14)

children.text: tappakṣaṇaṃ saṃketakapikāyām /
children.translated_text: Their definitions in the <s>Saṃketakalikā</s>:

children.text: poṭaḥ parpaṭībandhaḥ piṣṭīstambhastu khoṭakaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Loṭa</s> is the flake-binding (<s>parpaṭī-bandha</s>); the paste-solidification (<s>piṣṭī-stambha</s>) is <s>khoṭaka</s>.

children.text:
dhmāto druto bhavetkhoṭas tv āhataścūrṇatāṃ vrajet // GRhtCM_1.3:15
                            //
children.translated_text: When smelted and melted, it becomes <s>khoṭa</s>; when struck, it crumbles to powder.' (GRhtCM 1.3:15)

children.text: punardhmāto drutaḥ khoṭa iti khoṭasya pakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: 'Again smelted and melted — [that is still] <s>khoṭa</s>' — this is the definition of <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: japaukā pāṭabandhaśca bhasma bhasmanibhaṃ bhavet // GRhtCM_1.3:16 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Jalaukā</s> is the split-binding (<s>pāṭa-bandha</s>), and <s>bhasma</s> (calcined ash) becomes ash-like in appearance.' (GRhtCM 1.3:16)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_1.3:17 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 1.3:17)

children.text: punaḥ sumṛtaḥ san amarīkarotīti // GRhtCM_1.3:18 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, being well-processed (<s>sumṛta</s>), it bestows immortality. (GRhtCM 1.3:18)

children.text: sumṛta iti suḥ iti pūjāyāṃ yathā vidagdhamukhamaṇḍanabahirpāpikāyām /
children.translated_text: '<s>Su</s>' in '<s>sumṛta</s>' is [used] in the sense of veneration/excellence — as in the <s>Vidagdhamukhamaṇḍana-bahirpālikā</s>:

children.text: pūjāyāṃ kiṃ padaṃ proktam astanaṃ ko bibhartyuraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'What word is used in the sense of worship/veneration? What does the chest bear as a non-star?

children.text: ka āyudhatayā khyātaḥ prapambāsuravidviṣaḥ // GRhtCM_1.3:19 //
children.translated_text: What is known as the weapon of the enemy of the demon <s>Pralamba</s>?' (GRhtCM 1.3:19)

children.text: sunāsīraḥ iti pūjyaḥ // GRhtCM_1.3:20 //
children.translated_text: [The answer is] '<s>Sunāsīra</s>' (a name of <s>Indra</s>) — meaning 'the venerable one.' (GRhtCM 1.3:20)

children.text: mṛta iti viśeṣārthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.3:21 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Mṛta</s>' (killed/processed) has a specific meaning. (GRhtCM 1.3:21)

children.text: mṛto yathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Mṛta</s> (killed/calcined [mercury]) as follows:

children.text: ārdratvaṃ ca ghanatvaṃ ca cāpapyaṃ gurutaijasam /
children.translated_text: Moistness, density, flexibility, and heaviness with lustre —

children.text: yasyaitāni na vidyante taṃ vidyānmṛtasūtakam // GRhtCM_1.3:22 //
children.translated_text: that in which these [qualities] are not found, know that to be dead mercury. (GRht 1.3:22)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_1.3:23 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRht 1.3:23)

children.text: pūjya iti rasendramaṅgape yathā /
children.translated_text: 'Venerable' — as [stated] in the <s>Rasendramaṅgala</s>:

children.text:
abaddhasūtaṃ tu hataṃ pramādāt karoti kaṣṭaṃ prabapaṃ rasendraḥ //
                            GRhtCM_1.3:24 //
children.translated_text: 'Mercury that is unbound, killed through carelessness, causes great distress, O <s>Rasendra</s> (king of mercury).' (GRht 1.3:24)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_1.3:25 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRht 1.3:25)

children.text:
mūrchanādibandhanaparamparayā yo mṛtaḥ sa pūjyo nānyathā // GRhtCM_1.3:26
                            //
children.translated_text: That which has been killed through the successive [processes of] <s>mūrchanā</s> (swooning) and binding — that is venerable, not otherwise. (GRht 1.3:26)

children.text: yathā ca rasamañjaryām /
children.translated_text: And as [stated] in the <s>Rasamañjarī</s>:

children.text: ajīrṇaṃ cāpyabījaṃ ca sūtakaṃ yastu ghātayet /
children.translated_text: 'He who would kill mercury that is undigested and without seed —

children.text: brahmahā sa durācārī mama drohī maheśvari // GRhtCM_1.3:27 //
children.translated_text: he is a slayer of <s>Brahmā</s>, a wicked one, hostile to me, O <s>Maheśvarī</s>.' (GRht 1.3:27)

children.text: iti yukto+ayam arthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.3:28 //
children.translated_text: This meaning is appropriate. (GRht 1.3:28)

children.text: karuṇāparatvaṃ satāṃ svabhāva iti // GRhtCM_1.3:29 //
children.translated_text: Compassion toward others is the natural disposition of the virtuous. (GRht 1.3:29)

children.text: yathā /
children.translated_text: As [the saying goes]:

children.text:
chede'pi candanataruḥ surabhayati mukhaṃ kuṭhārasya iti // GRhtCM_1.3:30
                            //
children.translated_text: 'Even when cut, the sandalwood tree perfumes the mouth of the axe.' (GRht 1.3:30)

children.text: suragurugodvijahiṃsāpāpakalāpodbhavaṃ kilāsādhyam /
children.translated_text: That which is born from the mass of sins arising from violence against gods, teachers, cows, and <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s — [a disease] indeed incurable —

children.text: tadapi ca śamayati yasmāt ko 'nyas tasmāt pavitrataraḥ // GRht_1.4 //
children.translated_text: since it pacifies even that, who else is more purifying than it [mercury]? (GRht 1.4)

children.text: suretyādi // GRhtCM_1.4:1 //
children.translated_text: 'Sura' and so forth — [commentary begins]. (GRht CM 1.4:1)

children.text:
tasmāt sūtarājāt anyo dvitīya pavitratara atiśayena pavitraḥ kaḥ kipa
                            śrūyate na ko 'pi // GRhtCM_1.4:2 //
children.translated_text: Than that king of mercury, who else — what second — is more purifying, exceedingly pure? What is heard? No one at all. (GRht CM 1.4:2)

children.text:
yasmāddhetoḥ apīti niścayena asādhyaṃ rujaṃ śamayati
                            sarvarūpānvitamasādhyaṃ divyauṣadhibhir api karmavipākenāpi sādhyate
                            tacca kiṃviśiṣṭam asādhyaṃ suretyādiḥ surāś ca guravaś ca gāvaś ca
                            dvijāś ca teṣāṃ yā hiṃsā hananam avamānanaṃ vātād utpanno yaḥ pāpakapāpo
                            duṣkṛtapaṭapa etasmād udbhavatīti // GRhtCM_1.4:3 //
children.translated_text: For the reason that — 'api' [signifying] certainty — it pacifies an incurable disease — one that cannot be cured by divine herbs nor by the ripening of <s>karma</s> — and that [disease] of what kind? That which is born from the mass of sins, evil deeds — violence against gods, teachers, cows, and <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s — namely their killing and disrespect — a sin born from wind [i.e., from these causes]. (GRht CM 1.4:3)

children.text: tasya svayaṃ hi sphurati prādurbhāvaḥ sa śāṃkaraḥ ko 'pi /
children.translated_text: Its manifestation, which is of the nature of <s>Śaṅkara</s> (the beneficent one), appears of its own accord —

children.text: kathamanyathā hi śamayati vilasanmātrācca pāparujam // GRht_1.5 //
children.translated_text: how else could it pacify the disease of sin by its mere appearance? (GRht 1.5)

children.text: tasyetyādi // GRhtCM_1.5:1 //
children.translated_text: 'Tasya' and so forth — [commentary begins]. (GRht CM 1.5:1)

children.text: kavinānenānumānena pokapratītaḥ kriyate // GRhtCM_1.5:2 //
children.translated_text: By this inference, the poet establishes popular conviction. (GRht CM 1.5:2)

children.text:
yaḥ pūrvoktaḥ sūtarājas tasya ko 'pyanirvacanīyaḥ sa sarvadeśīyatvena
                            śāṃkaraḥ prādurbhāvaḥ śamayatīti duḥkhamupaśamayatīti śaṃ prasādaḥ śaṃ
                            karotīti śaṃkaraḥ tasyāyaṃ śāṃkaraḥ duḥkhopaśamāyāyaṃ prādurbhavatīti
                            tātparyārthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.5:3 //
children.translated_text: The previously mentioned king of mercury — its manifestation, which is indescribable and universal in all lands, is of the nature of <s>Śaṅkara</s> (the beneficent): <s>śam</s> means 'pacification' — it pacifies suffering; <s>śam</s> means 'grace' — one who produces grace is <s>Śaṃkara</s>; that which belongs to him is <s>Śāṃkara</s> — the purport is that it manifests for the pacification of suffering. (GRht CM 1.5:3)

children.text:
duḥkhamādhivyādhyātmakena dvividhaṃ punar
                            ādhibhautikādhidaivikādhyātmikabhedācca trividham // GRhtCM_1.5:4 //
children.translated_text: Suffering is twofold — pertaining to physical affliction and mental affliction; and again threefold by the division into <s>ādhibhautika</s> (caused by other beings), <s>ādhidaivika</s> (caused by fate), and <s>ādhyātmika</s> (caused by oneself). (GRht CM 1.5:4)

children.text:
sa punarasya sūtarājasya svayaṃ sphurati prakāśata iti // GRhtCM_1.5:5
                            //
children.translated_text: Moreover, it manifests of its own accord — becomes visible — for this king of mercury. (GRht CM 1.5:5)

Otherwise — without the manifestation of the <s>Śāṃkara</s> [nature] — how would one pacify the disease of sin (<s>kuṣṭha</s>, leprosy) born from the mass of sins arising from violence against gods, teachers, cows, and <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s by any other means? (GRht CM 1.5:6)

children.text: kutaḥ vipasanmātrāt dṛṣṭigocaratvāt // GRhtCM_1.5:7 //
children.translated_text: By what [means]? By mere appearance — by becoming visible to sight. (GRht CM 1.5:7)

children.text: rasendramaṅgape yathā /
children.translated_text: As [stated] in the <s>Rasendramaṅgala</s>:

children.text: śatāśvamedhena kṛtena puṇyaṃ gokoṭidānena gajendrakoṭibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The merit produced by performing a hundred horse-sacrifices, by the gift of ten million cows, by ten million elephants —

children.text:
suvarṇabhūdānasamānadharme naro pabhet sūtakadarśanena iti //
                            GRhtCM_1.5:8 //
children.translated_text: equal to the merit of giving gold and land — a man obtains by merely seeing mercury.' (GRht CM 1.5:8)

children.text: rasabandhaśca sa dhanyaḥ prārambhe yasya satatamiva karuṇā /
children.translated_text: Blessed is that binding of mercury at whose commencement there is constant compassion —

children.text: siddhe rase kariṣye mahīmahaṃ nirjarāmaraṇam // GRht_1.6 //
children.translated_text: 'When mercury is perfected, I shall make the earth free from old age and death.' (GRht 1.6)

children.text:
mūrchitabaddhamṛtasyāvasthayā trividhaṃ sūtarājasya bandhanaṃ praśaṃsati
                            kaviḥ rasa ityādi // GRhtCM_1.6:1 //
children.translated_text: The poet praises the threefold binding of the king of mercury — in the states of swooned, bound, and killed — [saying] 'rasa' and so forth. (GRht CM 1.6:1)

children.text:
bho janāḥ rasabandhaḥ pāradabandhanaṃ dhanyaḥ yasya prārambhe satataṃ
                            nirantaraṃ karuṇā jāyata iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_1.6:2 //
children.translated_text: O people! The binding of mercury — the fixation of <s>pārada</s> (mercury) — is blessed, at whose commencement constant, uninterrupted compassion arises — this is the completion [of the sentence]. (GRht CM 1.6:2)

children.text:
kiṃrūpā ahaṃ govindanāmā rase siddhe sati samyagbandhanatvaṃ prāpte sati
                            mahīṃ medinīṃ nirjarāmaraṇaṃ yathā tathā kariṣye // GRhtCM_1.6:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what nature? 'I, named <s>Govinda</s>, when mercury is perfected — when it has attained proper binding — shall make the earth free from old age and death.' (GRht CM 1.6:3)

children.text: atisāmīpyādvartamāna eva ḷṭ // GRhtCM_1.6:4 //
children.translated_text: Due to extreme proximity [of the event], the present tense [is used for future meaning]. (GRht CM 1.6:4)

children.text: nirjarāmaraṇamiti kriyāviśeṣaṇam // GRhtCM_1.6:5 //
children.translated_text: 'Free from old age and death' qualifies the action. (GRht CM 1.6:5)

children.text:
jarā pāpityaṃ maraṇaṃ prāṇatyāga ābhyāṃ rahitaṃ yathā mahyāṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ
                            na yuktam // GRhtCM_1.6:6 //
children.translated_text: Old age is deterioration; death is the departure of life-breath — free from these two, meaning that old age and death would not be fitting on the earth. (GRht CM 1.6:6)

children.text:
atra mahīpadena mahīmadhikṛtya nivasanti ye manujādayas ta eva
                            pakṣaṇāvṛttitvāt // GRhtCM_1.6:7 //
children.translated_text: Here, by the word 'earth' (<s>mahī</s>), those humans and others who dwell upon the earth are indicated, by the figure of metonymy. (GRht CM 1.6:7)

children.text: punā rasāyanavaśājjarāniṣedho bhaved iti yuktam // GRhtCM_1.6:8 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, through the power of <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation alchemy), the prevention of old age is possible — this is reasonable. (GRht CM 1.6:8)

children.text: hitopadeśe yathā /
children.translated_text: As [stated] in the <s>Hitopadeśa</s>:

children.text: yajjarāvyādhividhvaṃsi bheṣajaṃ tad rasāyanam /
children.translated_text: 'That medicine which destroys old age and disease is <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: ādye vayasi madhye vā śuddhakāyaḥ samācared /
children.translated_text: One should practice it in the first or middle stage of life, with a purified body.'

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_1.6:9 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRht CM 1.6:9)

children.text:
maraṇaniṣedhaḥ kathamauṣadhena anyauṣadhiśaktihrāsato na yuktaḥ
                            raseśvaraśaktyādhikyād yuktaḥ // GRhtCM_1.6:10 //
children.translated_text: How is the prevention of death [possible] through medicine? [Prevention] through other medicines is not reasonable due to the limitation of their power; [but it is] reasonable due to the superiority of the power of the lord of mercury. (GRht CM 1.6:10)

children.text: rasaratnākare yathā /
children.translated_text: As [stated] in the <s>Rasaratnākara</s>:

children.text:
mṛtyorjarāviṣadharasya ca vainateya tubhyaṃ namāmi suravanditasūtarāja
                            /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Garuḍa</s>'s son [<s>Vainateya</s>], [enemy] of death, old age, and poison — O king of mercury worshipped by the gods, I bow to you.'

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_1.6:11 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRht CM 1.6:11)

children.text: ye cātyaktaśarīrā haragaurīsṛṣṭijāṃ tanuṃ prāptāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who have not abandoned the body, who have obtained a body born of the creation of <s>Hara</s> and <s>Gaurī</s> —

children.text: vandyāste rasasiddhā mantragaṇāḥ kiṃkarā yeṣām // GRht_1.7 //
children.translated_text: those <s>Rasasiddha</s>s (mercury-adepts) are worthy of veneration, for whom hosts of mantras are servants. (GRht 1.7)

children.text:
jarāmaraṇaniṣedhatvena kimādhikyaṃ tadāha ya ityādi // GRhtCM_1.7:1
                            //
children.translated_text: What further excellence [is there] beyond the prevention of old age and death? To that [the text] says 'ye' and so forth. (GRht CM 1.7:1)

children.text:
ye evaṃvidharasasiddhāste vandyā abhivādanayogyāḥ stutyāśca //
                            GRhtCM_1.7:2 //
children.translated_text: Those <s>Rasasiddha</s>s of such description are worthy of veneration — fit for salutation and praise. (GRht CM 1.7:2)

children.text: vadi abhivādanastutyoḥ // GRhtCM_1.7:3 //
children.translated_text: The root 'vad' [is used] in the sense of salutation and praise. (GRht CM 1.7:3)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭā atyaktaśarīrāḥ na tyaktaṃ śarīraṃ yaiste jīvanmuktā ityarthaḥ
                            // GRhtCM_1.7:4 //
children.translated_text: Of what qualification? '<s>Atyaktaśarīra</s>' — those who have not abandoned the body, meaning they are <s>jīvanmukta</s>s (liberated while living). (GRht CM 1.7:4)

children.text:
śarīraṃ dvividhaṃ sthūpasūkṣmabhedāt pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśātmakaṃ sthūpaṃ
                            kośatrayātmakaṃ sūkṣmam // GRhtCM_1.7:5 //
children.translated_text: The body is twofold — gross and subtle: the gross consists of earth, water, fire, air, and space; the subtle consists of the three sheaths (<s>kośa</s>s). (GRht CM 1.7:5)

children.text: yathā sūtram /
children.translated_text: As the <s>sūtra</s> [states]:

children.text:
vijñānamayaṃ manomayaṃ prāṇamayam etat kośatrayaṃ mipitaṃ
                            sūkṣmaśarīramutpadyate // GRhtCM_1.7:6 //
children.translated_text: 'The sheath of knowledge (<s>vijñānamaya</s>), the sheath of mind (<s>manomaya</s>), the sheath of vital breath (<s>prāṇamaya</s>) — this triad of sheaths combined constitutes the subtle body.' (GRht CM 1.7:6)

children.text: anye eva sūkṣmaśarīram // GRhtCM_1.7:7 //
children.translated_text: Others [define] the subtle body [differently]. (GRht CM 1.7:7)

children.text: atyaktaśarīrarasasiddhāśca ucyante /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Rasasiddha</s>s who have not abandoned the body are named:

children.text: manthānabhairavo yogī siddhabuddhaśca kanthaḍī /
children.translated_text: <s>Manthānabhairava</s> the yogin, <s>Siddhabuddha</s>, and <s>Kanthaḍī</s>,

children.text: koraṇṭakaḥ surānandaḥ siddhapādaśca carpaṭī // GRhtCM_1.7:8 //
children.translated_text: <s>Koraṇṭaka</s>, <s>Surānanda</s>, <s>Siddhapāda</s>, and <s>Carpaṭī</s>; (GRht CM 1.7:8)

children.text: kaṇerī pūjyapādaśca nityanātho nirañjanaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṇerī</s>, <s>Pūjyapāda</s>, <s>Nityanātha</s>, <s>Nirañjana</s>,

children.text: kapāpī bindunāthaśca kākacaṇḍīśvaro gajaḥ // GRhtCM_1.7:9 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kapālī</s>, <s>Bindunātha</s>, <s>Kākacaṇḍīśvara</s>, <s>Gaja</s>; (GRht CM 1.7:9)

children.text: āppamaḥ prabhudevaśca ghoḍācopī ca ṭhiṇṭhinī /
children.translated_text: <s>Āppama</s>, <s>Prabhudeva</s>, <s>Ghoḍācopī</s>, and <s>Ṭhiṇṭhinī</s>,

children.text: bhāpukir nāgadevaśca khaṇḍī kāpāpikas tathā // GRhtCM_1.7:10 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bhālukī</s>, <s>Nāgadeva</s>, <s>Khaṇḍī</s>, and <s>Kāpālika</s> likewise; (GRht CM 1.7:10)

children.text: ityādayo mahāsiddhā rasabhogaprasādataḥ /
children.translated_text: these and other <s>Mahāsiddha</s>s (great adepts), by the grace of mercury-practice,

children.text: khaṇḍayitvā kāpadaṇḍaṃ tripokyāṃ vicaranti te // GRhtCM_1.7:11 //
children.translated_text: having broken the staff of death, wander in the three worlds. (GRht CM 1.7:11)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_1.7:12 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRht CM 1.7:12)

children.text:
punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ tanuṃ prāptāḥ śarīraṃ grahītāraḥ // GRhtCM_1.7:13
                            //
children.translated_text: Further, of what qualification? 'Having obtained a body' — having acquired a body. (GRht CM 1.7:13)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭāṃ tanuṃ haragaurīsṛṣṭijāṃ haro mahādevaḥ gaurī pārvatī tayoḥ
                            sṛṣṭiḥ sarjanaṃ maithunasaṃyogas tajjātā putrā evetyarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_1.7:14 //
children.translated_text: A body of what kind? 'Born of the creation of <s>Hara</s> and <s>Gaurī</s>' — <s>Hara</s> is <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Gaurī</s> is <s>Pārvatī</s>; their creation is their procreation, their sexual union; those born from that — meaning their very sons. (GRht CM 1.7:14)

children.text:
punaryeṣāṃ mantragaṇāḥ kiṃkarāḥ mantrasamūhā ājñākarā ityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_1.7:15 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, those for whom hosts of mantras are servants — meaning assemblies of mantras are obedient [to them]. (GRht CM 1.7:15)

children.text: sukṛtaphalaṃ tāvadidaṃ sukule yajjanma dhīśca tatrāpi /
children.translated_text: This indeed is the fruit of merit: birth in a good family, and intelligence there too;

children.text: sāpi ca sakalamahītalatulanaphalā bhūtalaṃ ca suvidheyam // GRht_1.8 //
children.translated_text: and that [intelligence] whose fruit equals the weighing of the entire earth — and the earth is well-governable. (GRht 1.8)

children.text: bhūtalavidheyatāyāḥ phalamarthāste ca vividhabhogaphalāḥ /
children.translated_text: The fruits of mastery over the earth are purposes, and those have various enjoyments as their fruits;

children.text: bhogāḥ santi śarīre tadanityamaho vṛthā sakalam // GRht_1.9 //
children.translated_text: enjoyments exist in the body — but that [body] is impermanent. Alas, all is in vain! (GRht 1.9)

children.text:
tāvaditi sākapye yāvattāvad ityetau sākapyāvadhimānavadhāraṇeṣv iti
                            prasādataḥ // GRhtCM_1.8-9:1 //
children.translated_text: 'Tāvat' [denotes] co-extensiveness — 'yāvat-tāvat' [are particles] used in the senses of co-extensiveness, limit, and determination — [this is explained] clearly. (GRht CM 1.8-9:1)

children.text:
idaṃ sukṛtaphapaṃ suvihitakarmaphapam idaṃ kiyat sukṛte śubhānvaye janma
                            svatantrā dhīḥ svādhīnabuddhir ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.8-9:2 //
children.translated_text: This is the fruit of meritorious action — the fruit of well-performed <s>karma</s>. This much [constitutes] merit: birth in a virtuous lineage; independent intelligence — meaning self-reliant understanding. (GRht CM 1.8-9:2)

children.text: apīti niścayena // GRhtCM_1.8-9:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Api' [denotes] certainty. (GRht CM 1.8-9:3)

children.text:
sā buddhiḥ sakapamahītapatupanaphapā sakapasya niravaśeṣasya mahītapasya
                            tupanaṃ phapaṃ yasyāḥ sā tathoktā // GRhtCM_1.8-9:4 //
children.translated_text: That intelligence whose fruit equals the weighing of the entire earth — the weighing of the totality of the earth without remainder is the fruit of which — it is so described. (GRht CM 1.8-9:4)

children.text:
tupanam iti tupayā svatantrabuddhirūpayā sakapamahītapasya tupanaṃ
                            bhavatyeveti yuktaṃ kimākārā kiyanmānā kaiḥ śritā kair dhṛtā ca bhūr iti
                            jyotiṣasiddhāntavidhānād adṛṣṭāntā bhūr buddhyopapakṣyate //
                            GRhtCM_1.8-9:5 //
children.translated_text: 'Weighing' — by means of the balance in the form of independent intelligence, the weighing of the entire earth becomes possible. Of what form, of what measure, by whom supported, by whom upheld is the earth? — through the method of astronomical calculations, the unseen earth is comprehended by the intellect. (GRht CM 1.8-9:5)

children.text:
punaḥ sukupajanmasvatantrabuddhibhyāṃ bhūtapaṃ suvidheyaṃ pūjyaṃ
                            jñātavyam // GRhtCM_1.8-9:6 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, through birth in a good family and independent intelligence, the earth is well-governable — worthy of reverence and knowledge. (GRht CM 1.8-9:6)

children.text:
ekadeśagrahaṇāt sarvaṃ grāhyaṃ mahāntastokā bhūtapaṃ bahu īdṛśā mahānto
                            yatra tiṣṭhanti tatsthānaṃ pūjyaṃ vettumaśakyatvāt sarvamiti //
                            GRhtCM_1.8-9:7 //
children.translated_text: By mentioning one part, the whole is to be understood. The earth is great — such great [places] where many great ones reside — that place is worthy of reverence; being impossible to fully know — therefore 'all' [is stated]. (GRht CM 1.8-9:7)

children.text: sukupajanmasambandho vyākhyāyate bhūtapetyādi // GRhtCM_1.8-9:8 //
children.translated_text: The connection with birth in a good family is explained — 'bhūtala' and so forth. (GRht CM 1.8-9:8)

children.text:
bhūtapavidheyatāyāḥ bhūtape pṛthivīmaṇḍape yā vidheyatā
                            sarvakarmapravīṇatā tasyā arthāḥ kāryāṇi kathaṃbhūtāḥ vividhabhogaphapāḥ
                            vividhāśca te bhogāśca vividhabhogāḥ nānābhogāḥ phapaṃ yeṣāṃ te
                            tathoktāḥ // GRhtCM_1.8-9:9 //
children.translated_text: Mastery over the earth — the proficiency in all actions on the earth — its purposes are activities; of what kind? Having various enjoyments as fruits — various enjoyments, manifold pleasures, whose fruits are such — they are so described. (GRht CM 1.8-9:9)

children.text: te phapaṃ phaparūpāḥ // GRhtCM_1.8-9:10 //
children.translated_text: Those are of the nature of fruits. (GRht CM 1.8-9:10)

children.text: bhogāḥ śarīre santi bhavanti // GRhtCM_1.8-9:11 //
children.translated_text: Enjoyments exist — arise — in the body. (GRht CM 1.8-9:11)

children.text:
kutaḥ yato vedāntasūtraṃ prārabdhakarmaphapabhogāyatanaṃ śarīram iti //
                            GRhtCM_1.8-9:12 //
children.translated_text: Why? Because the <s>Vedānta Sūtra</s> [states]: 'The body is the locus of experiencing the fruits of <s>prārabdha karma</s>.' (GRht CM 1.8-9:12)

children.text: ata eva bhogānām āśrayāḥ śarīram // GRhtCM_1.8-9:13 //
children.translated_text: Therefore indeed, the body is the support of enjoyments. (GRht CM 1.8-9:13)

children.text: aho iti kaṣṭe āścarye vā // GRhtCM_1.8-9:14 //
children.translated_text: 'Aho' [expresses] distress or wonder. (GRht CM 1.8-9:14)

children.text: etaccharīraṃ tu sarvotkṛṣṭamiti tātparyārthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.8-9:15 //
children.translated_text: The purport is: this body is the most excellent of all. (GRht CM 1.8-9:15)

children.text: sā muktiḥ piṇḍapātane iti vacanāt // GRhtCM_1.8-9:16 //
children.translated_text: Because of the statement: 'Liberation [comes] at the fall of the body.' (GRht CM 1.8-9:16)

children.text: iti dhanaśarīrabhogān matvānityān sadaiva yatanīyam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, considering wealth, body, and enjoyments to be always impermanent, one should always strive —

children.text: muktau sā ca jñānāt taccābhyāsāt sa ca sthire dehe // GRht_1.10 //
children.translated_text: Liberation comes from that [knowledge], and that [knowledge comes] from practice, and that [practice is possible] when the body is stable. (GRht 1.10)

children.text:
sarvasādhanaṃ śarīraṃ matvābhimataṃ diśati bho janāḥ sadā sarvasmin kāpe
                            aharniśaṃ yatanīyam kiṃ kṛtvā dhanaśarīrabhogān anityān naśvarān matvā
                            yatanīyam iti // GRhtCM_1.10:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Knowing that the body is the instrument for all spiritual attainments, O people, one should always strive day and night in every moment — how? By considering wealth, body, and pleasures as impermanent and perishable, one should strive. (GRhtCM 1.10:1)

children.text:
kiṃ yathā śarīraṃ nityasthāyi bhavati śarīre nitye sarvaṃ nityam
                            ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.10:2 //
children.translated_text: How? So that the body becomes permanently stable. When the body is permanent, everything is permanent — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 1.10:2)

From the knowledge of that body as permanent — through the most excellent understanding that the body can be made permanent — and from the practice of that very [knowledge], liberation arises. (GRhtCM 1.10:3)

children.text: kva sati sthire dehe sati // GRhtCM_1.10:4 //
children.translated_text: When? When the body is stable. (GRhtCM 1.10:4)

children.text:
manaso dharmaiḥ śarīrāśritaiḥ ṣaṅkikāraś ca dehāsthiratvam
                            etanniṣedhatvaṃ dehasthiratvaṃ mokṣaḥ // GRhtCM_1.10:5 //
children.translated_text: The instability of the body [is caused] by the properties of the mind residing in the body, and by the six modifications (<s>ṣaḍvikāra</s>). The negation of this [instability] — bodily stability — is liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). (GRhtCM 1.10:5)

children.text: tadevāha rāmaṃ prati gurorvacanam /
children.translated_text: On this very point, the word of the guru to <s>Rāma</s>:

children.text: na mokṣo nabhasaḥ pṛṣṭhe na pātāpe na bhūtape /
children.translated_text: Liberation is not on the surface of the sky, nor in the nether world, nor on earth.

children.text: sarvāśāsaṃkṣayaś cetaḥ śamo mokṣam itīkṣate iti // GRhtCM_1.10:6 //
children.translated_text: The cessation of all desires and the tranquility of the mind — that is regarded as liberation. (GRhtCM 1.10:6)

children.text: tatsthairyaṃ na samarthaṃ rasāyanaṃ kimapi mūlalohādi /
children.translated_text: For that stability [of the body], no <s>rasāyana</s> (elixir) whatsoever — whether from roots, metals, or the like — is [fully] capable,

children.text: svayamasthirasvabhāvaṃ dāhyaṃ kledyaṃ ca śoṣyaṃ ca // GRht_1.11 //
children.translated_text: since [the body] is by nature unstable, burnable, liquefiable, and desiccable. (GRht 1.11)

children.text:
tasya dehasya sthairyeṇa sthirabhāvena kṛtvā rasāyanaṃ jarāvyādhināśanaṃ
                            prati samarthaṃ kārakataram // GRhtCM_1.11:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] With regard to achieving stability — the state of being stable — of that body, the <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation therapy), the destroyer of old age and disease, is [most] capable, [is] the foremost agent. (GRhtCM 1.11:1)

children.text: apīti niścayena // GRhtCM_1.11:2 //
children.translated_text: The word 'api' (even) is used in the sense of certainty. (GRhtCM 1.11:2)

children.text:
kiṃ sūtapohādiḥ sūtaḥ pāradaḥ pohāḥ svarṇādayo navakāḥ
                            kṛtrimākṛtrimabhedayuktāḥ rājarītikharparīghoṣāḥ kṛtrimāḥ
                            svarṇatāratāmranāgavaṅgapohā akṛtrimāḥ ādiśabdānmahārasā uparasāśca
                            jñātavyāḥ // GRhtCM_1.11:3 //
children.translated_text: What [is this rasāyana]? <s>Sūta</s> (mercury) and <s>poha</s> (metals) and the like. <s>Sūta</s> is mercury (<s>pārada</s>). <s>Pohas</s> are the nine [metals] such as gold and the like, of two kinds — artificial and natural. <s>Rājarīti</s>, <s>kharparī</s>, and <s>ghoṣa</s> are artificial. Gold, silver, copper, lead, and tin are the natural <s>pohas</s>. By the word 'ādi' (and so forth), the <s>mahārasas</s> (great minerals) and <s>uparasas</s> (subsidiary minerals) should be understood. (GRhtCM 1.11:3)

children.text: ke ta ime rasāvatāre yathā /
children.translated_text: What are these? As [stated] in the <s>Rasāvatāra</s>:

children.text:
hiṅgūpatāpyavimapācapasasyakāntavaikrāntapakṣipatayaś ca mahārasāḥ syuḥ
                            /
children.translated_text: Hing, <s>upatāpya</s>, mica (<s>vimala</s>), <s>pāca</s>, lodestone (<s>sasyakānta</s>), <s>vaikrānta</s>, and <s>pakṣipati</s> — these are the <s>mahārasas</s> (great minerals).

children.text:
sauvīragandhakaśipāpaviraṅgadhātukāsīsakāṃkṣy uparasāḥ kathitā rasajñaiḥ
                            iti // GRhtCM_1.11:4 //
children.translated_text: Antimony (<s>sauvīra</s>), sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), <s>śipā</s>, <s>paviraṅga</s>, <s>dhātu</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s>, and <s>kāṃkṣī</s> — these are called <s>uparasas</s> (subsidiary minerals) by those who know <s>rasa</s> (mercury). (GRhtCM 1.11:4)

children.text:
athavā sthairyeṇa samarthe tat dehaṃ prati rasāyanaṃ kiṃ sūtapohādi //
                            GRhtCM_1.11:5 //
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the <s>rasāyana</s> — consisting of <s>sūta</s> (mercury) and <s>poha</s> (metals) and the like — is capable of [giving] stability to that body. (GRhtCM 1.11:5)

children.text:
sūte yadabhivyāptaṃ grāsamānena pohādi tattathoktaṃ sūte iti abhivyāpake
                            // GRhtCM_1.11:6 //
children.translated_text: In <s>sūta</s> (mercury), [substances] that are pervaded by it — <s>poha</s> (metals) and the like — are so called because <s>sūta</s> is the pervader. (GRhtCM 1.11:6)

children.text: adhikaraṇe saptamī // GRhtCM_1.11:7 //
children.translated_text: The seventh case ending [locative] is used in the sense of substratum. (GRhtCM 1.11:7)

children.text:
taddehaṃ svayamasthiram asthirībhāvatvabhāvaṃ punar dāhyaṃ dagdhuṃ śakyaṃ
                            punaḥ kpedyam ārdrībhāvena śīrṇayituṃ śakyaṃ punaḥ śodhyaṃ śoṣayitum
                            agnijapānipaiḥ dāhyaṃ kpedyaṃ śoṣyaṃ ca śarīramityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_1.11:8 //
children.translated_text: That body is by nature unstable — having the character of instability; further, it is burnable — capable of being burnt; further, it is liquefiable — capable of being dissolved through moisture; further, it is desiccable — capable of being dried. By fire and wind and such, it is burnable, liquefiable, and desiccable — this is the meaning regarding the body. (GRhtCM 1.11:8)

children.text:
sūtapohādinā dehamanityaṃ nityaṃ bhavet ayameva yatna iti tātparyārthaḥ
                            // GRhtCM_1.11:9 //
children.translated_text: Through <s>sūta</s> (mercury), <s>poha</s> (metals), and the like, the impermanent body may become permanent — this very effort is the essential purport. (GRhtCM 1.11:9)

children.text: Auflösung Pflanzen - amaratva
children.translated_text: Section: Dissolution of plants — immortality

children.text: kāṣṭhauṣadhyo nāge nāgaṃ vaṅge vaṅgamapi līyate śulve /
children.translated_text: Herbal preparations dissolve in lead; lead dissolves in tin; [tin dissolves] in copper;

children.text: śulvaṃ tāre tāraṃ kanake kanakaṃ ca līyate sūte // GRht_1.12 //
children.translated_text: copper dissolves in silver; silver in gold; and gold dissolves in <s>sūta</s> (mercury). (GRht 1.12)

children.text: paramātmanīva niyataṃ layo yatra sarvasattvānām /
children.translated_text: Just as in the supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), where the dissolution of all beings is certain,

children.text: eko+asau rasarājaḥ śarīramajarāmaraṃ kurute // GRht_1.13 //
children.translated_text: this one, the king of <s>rasas</s> (mercury), makes the body free from old age and death. (GRht 1.13)

children.text:
pūrvaśpoke sūtapohādikamuktaṃ tatrādhivyāpakādhikaraṇasya kramaṃ
                            darśayati kāṣṭhauṣadhya ityādi // GRhtCM_1.12-13:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In the previous verse, <s>sūta</s> (mercury) and <s>poha</s> (metals) and the like were mentioned. Now he shows the sequence of pervader and substratum with 'herbal preparations' and so forth. (GRhtCM 1.12–13:1)

children.text:
kāṣṭhauṣadhyaḥ kumārikādayaḥ nāge pīyante tannāgaṃ vaṅge pīyate
                            tadvaṅgamapi śupbe tāmre pīyate tacchupbaṃ tāre pīyate tattāraṃ rūpyaṃ
                            kanake suvarṇe pīyate tatkanakaṃ sūte pārade pīyate iti //
                            GRhtCM_1.12-13:2 //
children.translated_text: Herbal preparations such as <s>kumārikā</s> (aloe) and the like are consumed in lead; that lead is consumed in tin; that tin also is consumed in copper; that copper is consumed in silver; that silver is consumed in gold; that gold is consumed in <s>sūta</s> (mercury, <s>pārada</s>). (GRhtCM 1.12–13:2)

children.text:
kathaṃ pīyate vidhānata ekaikena yuktaṃ samudāyenāpi ca //
                            GRhtCM_1.12-13:3 //
children.translated_text: How is it consumed? According to the prescribed method — each one individually as well as in combination. (GRhtCM 1.12–13:3)

children.text:
dhātūnām arivargatvān mahārasoparasānām api yogam apiśabdāśca //
                            GRhtCM_1.12-13:4 //
children.translated_text: Because metals are enemies [of mercury's impurities], the conjunction of <s>mahārasas</s> and <s>uparasas</s> also [occurs] — the word 'api' [indicates this]. (GRhtCM 1.12–13:4)

children.text: samudāyatvenopavarṇayati paramātmanītyādi // GRhtCM_1.12-13:5 //
children.translated_text: He describes the totality with 'just as in the supreme Self' and so forth. (GRhtCM 1.12–13:5)

children.text:
asau eko dhātvādyantarbhūto rasarājaḥ śarīramajarāmaraṃ
                            jarāmaraṇavarjitaṃ kurute // GRhtCM_1.12-13:6 //
children.translated_text: This one alone — the king of <s>rasas</s>, which contains within itself metals and the rest — makes the body free from old age and death (<s>ajarāmara</s>), devoid of old age and death. (GRhtCM 1.12–13:6)

children.text:
rasair mahārasoparasair antarbhūto rājate śobhate vā prakāśate iti
                            rasarājaḥ athavā raseṣu mahārasoparaseṣu anādarībhūteṣu satsu rājata iti
                            viśeṣārthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.12-13:7 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rasarāja</s> (king of rasas): it shines, is resplendent, or illuminates among the <s>rasas</s> — <s>mahārasas</s> and <s>uparasas</s> — that which is contained within [them] — hence <s>rasarāja</s>. Alternatively, when the <s>rasas</s>, <s>mahārasas</s>, and <s>uparasas</s> are disregarded, it [still] shines — this is the specific meaning. (GRhtCM 1.12–13:7)

children.text:
tathā ca sūtraṃ ṣaṣṭhīsaptamyau cānādare iti athavā rasānāṃ
                            mahārasoparasadhātūnāṃ rājā teṣu mukhyatvenopadiṣṭaḥ mukhyatvenāsya
                            grahaṇamityupapakṣaṇam // GRhtCM_1.12-13:8 //
children.translated_text: And thus the grammatical rule: 'The sixth and seventh case endings [are used] in the sense of disregard.' Alternatively, the king of <s>rasas</s> — of <s>mahārasas</s>, <s>uparasas</s>, and metals — is primarily taught among them; its apprehension as primary is the supplementary explanation. (GRhtCM 1.12–13:8)

children.text: anenaiva sarvasaṃgrahaṇaṃ jñātavyam // GRhtCM_1.12-13:9 //
children.translated_text: By this very [principle], the comprehension of all [substances] should be understood. (GRhtCM 1.12–13:9)

children.text: iveti sādṛśye // GRhtCM_1.12-13:10 //
children.translated_text: The word 'iva' (like) is in the sense of similarity. (GRhtCM 1.12–13:10)

children.text:
ātmani brahmaṇi niyataṃ niścitaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ sakapajīvānāṃ payo
                            bhavati payo+antarbhāvaḥ vā tasminsarve // GRhtCM_1.12-13:11 //
children.translated_text: In the Self, in <s>Brahman</s>, the dissolution of all beings — all living creatures — is certain; dissolution means absorption into it — in that [<s>Brahman</s>], all beings abide. (GRhtCM 1.12–13:11)

children.text:
sattvā pīnā eva tiṣṭhantītyātmānaḥ taṭasthasvarūpataitappakṣaṇadvayam
                            uktam // GRhtCM_1.12-13:12 //
children.translated_text: Beings exist as absorbed — these are the selves. Thus the two definitions — <s>taṭastha</s> (extrinsic) and <s>svarūpa</s> (intrinsic) — have been stated. (GRhtCM 1.12–13:12)

Similarly, he shows with regard to <s>rasarāja</s> (king of rasas, mercury) also: the dissolution of herbal preparations, metals, <s>mahārasas</s>, <s>uparasas</s>, and the like should be understood. By the extrinsic definition, the sequence of dissolution has been taught. (GRhtCM 1.12–13:13)

children.text:
svarūpapakṣaṇenauṣadhīdhātumahārasoparasādayaḥ pṛthaktvena sthitā api
                            guṇairantarbhūtā eva jñātavyāḥ yataḥ sarveṣāṃ guṇāntarbhūtaḥ sūtas tato
                            'nantaguṇa ācāryair upavarṇitaḥ // GRhtCM_1.12-13:14 //
children.translated_text: By the intrinsic definition: herbal preparations, metals, <s>mahārasas</s>, <s>uparasas</s>, and the like, though existing separately, should be understood as contained within [mercury] through their qualities. Since <s>sūta</s> (mercury) contains within itself the qualities of all, it has been described by the masters as possessing infinite qualities. (GRhtCM 1.12–13:14)

children.text: payaviśeṣādubhayoḥ sāmyamiti rahasyam // GRhtCM_1.12-13:15 //
children.translated_text: The secret is that there is equality between the two [<s>Brahman</s> and mercury] due to a special kind of absorption. (GRhtCM 1.12–13:15)

children.text: amṛtatvaṃ hi bhajante haramūrtau yogino yathā līnāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as yogins who are absorbed in the form of <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) attain immortality,

children.text: tadvatkavalitagagane rasarāje hemalohādyāḥ // GRht_1.14 //
children.translated_text: so too, when the king of <s>rasas</s> (mercury) has swallowed mica (<s>gagana</s>), gold, metals, and the rest [attain immortality]. (GRht 1.14)

children.text: sarvaṃ samīkartumāha amṛtatvamityādi // GRhtCM_1.14:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He speaks to equate everything, with 'immortality' and so forth. (GRhtCM 1.14:1)

children.text:
te svātmanā ātmanā saha yogakartṛkā yogino yathā haramūrtau
                            mahādevaśarīre pīnāḥ santaḥ amṛtatvaṃ bhajante muktatvaṃ prāpnuvanti //
                            GRhtCM_1.14:2 //
children.translated_text: Those yogins who practice yoga with their own selves — who, being absorbed in the form of <s>Hara</s> (<s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Śiva</s>'s body), attain immortality — attain the state of liberation. (GRhtCM 1.14:2)

children.text:
muktiḥ kaivapyanirvāṇaśreyoniḥśreyasāmṛtam ityamaraḥ // GRhtCM_1.14:3
                            //
children.translated_text: Liberation, <s>kaivalya</s>, <s>nirvāṇa</s>, <s>śreyas</s>, <s>niḥśreyasa</s>, and <s>amṛta</s> — [these are synonyms,] according to <s>Amara[koṣa]</s>. (GRhtCM 1.14:3)

children.text:
tadvattenaiva prakāreṇa rasarāje pārade kavapitagagane grāsīkṛtābhrake
                            sati hemapohādyā pīnāḥ santa amṛtatvaṃ pīyūṣabhāvaṃ bhajante
                            amarīkaraṇayogyā bhavanti // GRhtCM_1.14:4 //
children.translated_text: In the same manner, when the king of <s>rasas</s> (mercury) has swallowed mica (<s>abhraka</s>) — when mica has been made into a bolus for it — then gold, metals, and the rest, being absorbed [in mercury], attain the state of ambrosia (<s>pīyūṣa</s>) — they become fit for bestowing immortality. (GRhtCM 1.14:4)

children.text:
hema ca pohaśca hemapohau ādyau yeṣāṃ vā hemasaṃjñako poha ādyo yeṣāṃ te
                            tathoktāḥ // GRhtCM_1.14:5 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Hemapoha</s>': gold and <s>poha</s> (metal) together are <s>hemapoha</s>; 'ādi' means those beginning with them; or, the <s>poha</s> called gold is the first among them — they are so called. (GRhtCM 1.14:5)

children.text: abhrake kavapite sati cāraṇā syānnānyatheti // GRhtCM_1.14:6 //
children.translated_text: When mica has been swallowed [by mercury], then <s>cāraṇā</s> (the process of transmutation) is possible, not otherwise. (GRhtCM 1.14:6)

children.text: sthiradeho+abhyāsavaśātprāpya jñānaṃ guṇāṣṭakopetam /
children.translated_text: One whose body is stable, through practice, having attained knowledge endowed with the eight qualities,

children.text: prāpnoti brahmapadaṃ na punarbhavāvāsaduḥkhena // GRht_1.15 //
children.translated_text: attains the state of <s>Brahman</s> and is not [subject to] the suffering of rebirth. (GRht 1.15)

children.text: adhunā sthiradehasya phapaṃ vyanakti sthiretyādi // GRhtCM_1.15:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now he reveals the fruit [for one with] a stable body, with 'stable' and so forth. (GRhtCM 1.15:1)

children.text:
pūrvoktasyaiva rasarājasyābhyāsāt sevanāddhetoḥ sthiradehaḥ pumān
                            brahmapadaṃ prāpnoti // GRhtCM_1.15:2 //
children.translated_text: Through the practice — the regular use — of the aforementioned king of <s>rasas</s> (mercury), a person with a stable body attains the state of <s>Brahman</s>. (GRhtCM 1.15:2)

children.text: brahmapadaṃ paramānandasvarūpam // GRhtCM_1.15:3 //
children.translated_text: The state of <s>Brahman</s> is the nature of supreme bliss. (GRhtCM 1.15:3)

children.text: kiṃkṛtvā jñānaṃ prāpya // GRhtCM_1.15:4 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? Having attained knowledge. (GRhtCM 1.15:4)

children.text:
kīdṛśaṃ jñānaṃ guṇāṣṭakopetam aṇimādyaṣṭasiddhyupetam // GRhtCM_1.15:5
                            //
children.translated_text: What kind of knowledge? Endowed with the eight qualities (<s>guṇāṣṭaka</s>) — endowed with the eight <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural powers) beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> (the power of becoming infinitely small). (GRhtCM 1.15:5)

children.text: kathaṃ brahmapadaṃ prāpnoti // GRhtCM_1.15:6 //
children.translated_text: How does one attain the state of <s>Brahman</s>? (GRhtCM 1.15:6)

children.text:
yathā punaraprathamaṃ bhavāvāsaduḥkhe saṃsāranivāsanatāpatrayātmakakaṣṭe
                            na patatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.15:7 //
children.translated_text: Such that one does not again fall into the suffering of the abode of worldly existence (<s>bhavāvāsa</s>) — consisting of the threefold afflictions (<s>tāpatraya</s>) of <s>saṃsāra</s> — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 1.15:7)

children.text: jñānaṃ prāpya brahmapadaṃ prāpnoti // GRhtCM_1.15:8 //
children.translated_text: Having attained knowledge, one attains the state of <s>Brahman</s>. (GRhtCM 1.15:8)

children.text: katham ṛte jñānānna muktiriti // GRhtCM_1.15:9 //
children.translated_text: How? Without knowledge, there is no liberation. (GRhtCM 1.15:9)

children.text:
anyacca kiṃ mokṣatarorbījaṃ samyagjñānaṃ kriyāsahitam iti
                            praśnottararatnamāpāyām // GRhtCM_1.15:10 //
children.translated_text: Moreover: 'What is the seed of the tree of liberation? Right knowledge combined with practice' — [this is stated] in the <s>Praśnottararatnamālā</s>. (GRhtCM 1.15:10)

children.text: ekāṃśena jaganti ca viṣṭabhyāvasthitaṃ paraṃ jyotiḥ /
children.translated_text: With a single portion, pervading the worlds, stands the supreme light;

children.text: pādaistribhistadamṛtaṃ sulabhaṃ na viraktimātreṇa // GRht_1.16 //
children.translated_text: with three feet, that immortal [<s>Brahman</s>] is easily attainable — not by mere dispassion alone. (GRht 1.16)

children.text: jñānagamyaṃ brahmopavarṇayatyekāṃśenetyādi // GRhtCM_1.16:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He describes <s>Brahman</s>, which is attainable through knowledge, with 'with a single portion' and so forth. (GRhtCM 1.16:1)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ prakāśasvarūpaṃ tatparaṃ jyotir jaganti
                            saṃsārāṇi svargamṛtyupātāpādīni viṣṭabhya vyāpya sthitaṃ kena ekāṃśena
                            anekabrahmāṇḍanāyakatvāt ekaikasmin brahmāṇḍe bahūni saṃsārāṇi vartante
                            ata ekāṃśenetyuktaṃ punas tatparaṃ jyotīrūpam amṛtaṃ tribhiḥ pādair
                            abhyāsasthiradehajñānasaṃjñakaiḥ supabhaṃ sukhena pabhyam ityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_1.16:2 //
children.translated_text: What is the nature of <s>Brahman</s>? The supreme light — whose nature is radiance — that supreme light, pervading the worlds — <s>saṃsāras</s> such as heaven, death, the netherworld, and the like — stands [pervading them]. By what? By a single portion — because of being the lord of countless <s>brahmāṇḍas</s> (cosmic eggs); in each <s>brahmāṇḍa</s>, many <s>saṃsāras</s> exist; hence 'by a single portion' is said. Furthermore, that supreme light, which is immortal (<s>amṛta</s>), is easily attainable through three feet — namely practice, a stable body, and knowledge. 'Easily attainable' (<s>sulabha</s>) means obtainable with ease — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 1.16:2)

children.text: prathamam abhyāso+amṛtasupabhatve // GRhtCM_1.16:3 //
children.translated_text: The first [foot] — practice — is [the first] cause of attaining immortality easily. (GRhtCM 1.16:3)

children.text:
heturekaḥ sthiradehaś ca dvitīyo hetur jñānaṃ tṛtīyaheturmokṣe
                            yathāvākyaṃ na viraktimātram // GRhtCM_1.16:4 //
children.translated_text: A stable body is the second cause; knowledge is the third cause of liberation. According to the [scriptural] statement, mere dispassion [alone is not sufficient]. (GRhtCM 1.16:4)

children.text: na hi dehena kathaṃcid vyādhijarāmaraṇaduḥkhavidhureṇa /
children.translated_text: For with a body that is afflicted by disease, old age, death, and suffering,

children.text: kṣaṇabhaṅgureṇa sūkṣmaṃ tadbrahmopāsituṃ śakyam // GRht_1.17 //
children.translated_text: that is momentarily perishable — it is not possible to worship that subtle <s>Brahman</s>. (GRht 1.17)

children.text:
pūrvāparābhyāmabhyāsajñānābhyāṃ sthiradeho heturgarīyāniti sūcayannāha
                            netyādi // GRhtCM_1.17:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Indicating that a stable body is the weightier cause compared to the preceding and following [causes] — practice and knowledge — he says 'not' and so forth. (GRhtCM 1.17:1)

children.text:
ubhayoḥ sādhakatvāt tādṛśadehavyatiriktaṃ kathaṃcidapi kiṃcin na
                            sidhyatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.17:2 //
children.translated_text: Because both [body and its attributes] are instrumental [to spiritual attainment], nothing whatsoever distinct from such a body can be accomplished by any means — that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 1.17:2)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭena vyādhijarāmaraṇaduḥkhavidhureṇa vyādhirāmayaḥ jarā pāpityaṃ
                            maraṇaṃ prāṇatyāgaḥ duḥkhaṃ mohaśokādikam etair vidhuraṃ tāḍitaṃ vyadha
                            tāḍane ityasya ghāto rūpaṃ vidhuram urapratyayāntam // GRhtCM_1.17:3
                            //
children.translated_text: With what characteristic? Afflicted by disease, old age, death, and suffering — disease means illness; old age means decrepitude; death means the abandonment of life-breath; suffering means delusion, grief, and the like. 'Afflicted' (<s>vidhura</s>) means struck by these — from the root <s>vyadh</s> meaning 'to strike' — its form is <s>vidhura</s>, ending in the <s>ura</s>-suffix. (GRhtCM 1.17:3)

children.text:
punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭena kṣaṇabhaṅgureṇa kṣaṇavināśinā dehena tadbrahma
                            cidghanānandasvarūpam upāsituṃ sevituṃ kathaṃ kena prakāreṇa śakyaṃ kuto
                            yataḥ sūkṣmam indriyāgrāhyatvāt // GRhtCM_1.17:4 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, with what characteristic? With a body that is momentarily perishable (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅgura</s>) — how can one worship, serve, that <s>Brahman</s>, whose nature is condensed consciousness and bliss (<s>cidghanānanda</s>), by what means? Because it is subtle — imperceptible to the senses. (GRhtCM 1.17:4)

children.text: nāmāpi yogasiddheḥ ko gṛhṇīyādvinā śarīreṇa /
children.translated_text: Without the body, who could even grasp the name of <s>yoga-siddhi</s> (yogic accomplishment)?

children.text: yadyogagamyamamalaṃ manaso+api na gocaraṃ tattvam // GRht_1.18 //
children.translated_text: That reality (<s>tattva</s>) which is attainable through <s>yoga</s>, which is pure, which is beyond even the reach of the mind. (GRht 1.18)

children.text:
sarvopāyena śarīraṃ sthiraṃ kāryam ityāha nāmetyādi // GRhtCM_1.18:1
                            //
children.translated_text: He says that the body must be made stable by every means — [beginning with] 'the name' and so on. (GRhtCM 1.18:1)

children.text:
dehasiddheḥ śarīravibhūteḥ nāmāpyabhidhānamapi ko gṛhṇīyānna ko
                            'pītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.18:2 //
children.translated_text: Even the name — even the designation — of bodily <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment), the glory of the body: who could grasp it? — no one could; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 1.18:2)

children.text:
kena vinā śarīreṇa śarīramantareṇa siddhirastu paraṃ tannāma kenāpi na
                            gṛhyate śarīranāmagrahaṇamiti tātparyārthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.18:3 //
children.translated_text: Without what? Without the body — without a body, let there be accomplishment, but that name cannot be grasped by anyone — the purport is: the grasping of both body and its name [requires the body]. (GRhtCM 1.18:3)

children.text:
anaśvaraṃ śarīraṃ bhavatu cet tad amapaṃ nirañjanaṃ tattvaṃ brahmāvaśyaṃ
                            prāpyate // GRhtCM_1.18:4 //
children.translated_text: If the body becomes imperishable, then that pure (<s>amala</s>), untainted (<s>nirañjana</s>) reality — <s>Brahman</s> — is certainly attained. (GRhtCM 1.18:4)

children.text:
tattattvaṃ manaso+api na gocaraṃ cittenāpi na gamyam ityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_1.18:5 //
children.translated_text: That reality is not within the reach even of the mind — meaning it cannot be attained even by thought. (GRhtCM 1.18:5)

children.text:
tarhi kena gamyam ubhayor mepanam ekīkaraṇaṃ yogastenaiva
                            prakṛtipuruṣayor ekīkaraṇenetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.18:6 //
children.translated_text: Then by what is it attained? By <s>yoga</s> — the union of the two, the unification — meaning through the unification of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (consciousness). (GRhtCM 1.18:6)

children.text: yajñāddānāttapaso vedādhyayanāddamātsadācārāt /
children.translated_text: From sacrifice, from charity, from austerity, from the study of the <s>Veda</s>s, from self-restraint, from righteous conduct —

children.text: atyantaṃ śreyaḥ kila yogavaśādātmasaṃvittiḥ // GRht_1.19 //
children.translated_text: exceedingly greater is the welfare [that comes] from the power of <s>yoga</s>, namely self-knowledge (<s>ātmasaṃvitti</s>). (GRht 1.19)

children.text:
adhunā yogasya sarvakarmabhya utkṛṣṭatvaṃ darśayati yajñād ityādi //
                            GRhtCM_1.19:1 //
children.translated_text: Now he shows the superiority of <s>yoga</s> over all other [ritual] actions — [beginning with] 'from sacrifice' and so on. (GRhtCM 1.19:1)

children.text:
atyantaṃ śreya iti adhikatarakapyāṇaṃ sarvopadravanivāraṇātmakaṃ bhaved
                            ityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_1.19:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Exceedingly greater welfare' means superior well-being, which consists in the removal of all afflictions — this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 1.19:2)

children.text:
kutaḥ yajñādaśvamedhādeḥ na kevapaṃ yajñāt punardānāt dhanasyārpaṇāt
                            pātreṣu punastapasaḥ kṛcchrātikṛcchracāndrāyapasaṃcāgnitapanādeḥ
                            punarvedādhyayanāt vedānām ṛgyajuḥsāmātharvaṇāṃ adhyayanaṃ
                            pāṭhākramastataḥ punardamāt vedāntānusāreṇa damastāvat bāhyendriyāṇāṃ
                            tadvyatiriktaviṣayebhyo manasā nirvartanaṃ tadvyatiriktaṃ
                            śravaṇādivyatiriktaṃ tataḥ punaḥ sadācārāt brāhmamuhūrtam ārabhya
                            prātaḥsaṃgavamadhyāhnāparāhṇasāyāhnādiṣu śayanaparyantaṃ vedabodhito
                            vidhiḥ sadācārastata iti samudāyaḥ śreyaskaro nātmasaṃvittikaraḥ
                            punarātmasaṃvittiḥ brahmavedanaṃ yogavaśādeva syāt yogaḥ pūrvamuktaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_1.19:3 //
children.translated_text: From what? From sacrifice — from the <s>Aśvamedha</s> and the like — not merely from sacrifice, but also from charity — the offering of wealth to worthy recipients; again from austerity — <s>kṛcchra</s>, <s>atikṛcchra</s>, <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>, and fire-austerities and the like; again from study of the <s>Veda</s>s — the study, the course of recitation, of the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāma</s>, and <s>Atharva</s> <s>Veda</s>s; then again from self-restraint (<s>dama</s>) — self-restraint according to <s>Vedānta</s> means the withdrawal of the external senses from objects other [than <s>Brahman</s>] through the mind; other than those — other than hearing and the rest; then again from righteous conduct (<s>sadācāra</s>) — the practice enjoined by the <s>Veda</s> from the <s>Brāhma muhūrta</s> (pre-dawn hour) through the morning, forenoon, midday, afternoon, evening, and other [periods] up to retiring for the night — the aggregate of all these is productive of welfare but not of self-knowledge. Rather, self-knowledge — the realization of <s>Brahman</s> — arises from the power of <s>yoga</s> alone; <s>yoga</s> has been described previously. (GRhtCM 1.19:3)

children.text: galitānalpavikalpasarvārthavivarjitaś cidānandaḥ /
children.translated_text: One from whom all manifold false notions have fallen away, who is devoid of all objects — [he is] consciousness-bliss (<s>cidānanda</s>);

children.text: sphurito+apyasphuritatanoḥ karoti kiṃ jantuvargasya // GRht_1.20 //
children.translated_text: though manifest, what does he do for the host of beings whose bodies remain unmanifest? (GRht 1.20)

children.text:
yasya jīvasya yogavaśātsaṃvittirjātā sa kīdṛśa ityāha gapitetyādi //
                            GRhtCM_1.20:1 //
children.translated_text: He describes what the <s>jīva</s> (individual self) is like when self-knowledge has arisen through the power of <s>yoga</s> — [beginning with] 'fallen away' and so on. (GRhtCM 1.20:1)

children.text:
gapitānappavikappa iti gapito dūrībhūto 'nappo bahutaro vikappo
                            mithyājñānaṃ yasya īdṛk syāt // GRhtCM_1.20:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Fallen away from manifold false notions' — 'fallen away' means made remote; 'manifold' means abundant; 'false notions' (<s>vikalpa</s>) means false knowledge — one who is of such a nature. (GRhtCM 1.20:2)

children.text:
