punaḥ kīdṛk sarvārthavivarjitaḥ sarve ca te arthāśca tair vivarjitāḥ
                            samyagrahito bhavati kāryāṇāṃ smaraṇakaraṇayorabhāva ityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_1.20:3 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, of what nature? 'Devoid of all objects' — all objects, being properly abandoned — meaning there is an absence of both remembering and performing actions. (GRhtCM 1.20:3)

children.text:
punaḥ kathaṃbhūtaḥ cidānandaś cidā prakāśena ānandaḥ sukhasampattir yasya
                            sa tathoktaḥ // GRhtCM_1.20:4 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, of what nature? '<s>Cidānanda</s>' (consciousness-bliss) — through consciousness (<s>cit</s>), meaning luminosity, there is bliss (<s>ānanda</s>), the attainment of happiness — one who possesses this is so described. (GRhtCM 1.20:4)

children.text:
prakāśahetunā ānandatā bhavet jaḍahetunā tadviparyayaḥ // GRhtCM_1.20:5
                            //
children.translated_text: Through the cause of luminosity there would be bliss; through the cause of inertness, the opposite. (GRhtCM 1.20:5)

children.text:
īdṛk saḥ sphurito+api prakāśamāno+api asphuritatanorjantuvargasya
                            aprakāśaśarīrasya jīvasamūhasya kiṃ karoti pṛcchāṃ karoti //
                            GRhtCM_1.20:6 //
children.translated_text: Such a one, though manifest — though luminous — what does he do for the host of beings whose bodies remain unmanifest, for the multitude of <s>jīva</s>s whose bodies are unluminous? He asks the question. (GRhtCM 1.20:6)

children.text: kimiti pṛcchājugupsayoḥ iti prasādaḥ // GRhtCM_1.20:7 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Kim</s>' is used in the sense of questioning and disgust — this is [an expression of] grace. (GRhtCM 1.20:7)

children.text:
pṛcchati ca hasati ca roditi pramattavan mānavo+api tappīna iti //
                            GRhtCM_1.20:8 //
children.translated_text: He asks and laughs and weeps; like a madman, even the human being who is absorbed in that [state]. (GRhtCM 1.20:8)

children.text: bhrūyugamadhyagataṃ yacchikhividyunnirmalaṃ jagadbhāsi /
children.translated_text: That which, situated between the two eyebrows, illuminates the world, pure like the fire of a peacock-feather lightning —

children.text: keṣāṃcit puṇyakṛtām unmīlati cinmayaṃ jyotiḥ // GRht_1.21 //
children.translated_text: for some meritorious ones, the light that is of the nature of consciousness (<s>cinmaya</s>) opens [itself]. (GRht 1.21)

children.text:
ātmasaṃvitter virapatvaṃ sūcayann āha bhrūyugetyādi // GRhtCM_1.21:1
                            //
children.translated_text: Indicating the rarity of self-knowledge, he says [beginning with] 'between the two eyebrows' and so on. (GRhtCM 1.21:1)

children.text:
yat bhrūyugamadhyagataṃ bhrūdvayāntargataṃ sat prakāśate tatra dṛṣṭiṃ
                            nidhāya yoginaḥ paśyanti khecaryā mudrayā haṭhapradīpikāyāṃ padyam /
children.translated_text: That which, situated between the two eyebrows — within the space between the two brows — while existing, illuminates. <s>Yogin</s>s, fixing their gaze there, perceive [it] through <s>Khecarī Mudrā</s>. A verse in the <s>Haṭhapradīpikā</s>:

children.text: kapāpakuhare jihvā praviṣṭā viparītagā /
children.translated_text: The tongue, inserted into the cavity of the palate, turned upward,

children.text: bhruvor antargatā dṛṣṭirmudrā bhavati khecarī // GRhtCM_1.21:2 //
children.translated_text: the gaze directed between the brows — this becomes <s>Khecarī Mudrā</s>. (GRhtCM 1.21:2)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_1.21:3 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 1.21:3)

children.text:
punaḥ śikhividyutsu vahnisaudāminīṣu nirmapaṃ sat yatprakāśate punaryat
                            jagadbhāsi jagat saṃsāraṃ prakāśate tat cinmayaṃ prakāśapracuraṃ jyotiḥ
                            keṣāṃcit puṇyakṛtāṃ suvihitakarmakartḥṇām unmīpati prādurbhavati na tu
                            sarveṣāṃ yato nirmapaṃ prakāśaṃ dhyātvā vipupapuṇyena nirmapatvāya
                            jāyate ataḥ prakāśo yuktaḥ // GRhtCM_1.21:4 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, [that which shines] in fires and lightnings — in fires and streaks of lightning — being pure; moreover, that which illuminates the world — the entire <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of existence) — that light, which is full of consciousness (<s>cinmaya</s>), full of luminosity, opens — becomes manifest — for some meritorious ones, for those who have performed virtuous deeds — but not for all. Because having meditated on the pure, luminous [reality], one is born into purity through abundant merit; therefore, luminosity is fitting. (GRhtCM 1.21:4)

children.text: paramānandaikamayaṃ paramaṃ jyotiḥsvabhāvamavikalpam /
children.translated_text: Consisting solely of supreme bliss, of the nature of the supreme light, free from false notions (<s>avikalpa</s>),

children.text: vigalitasarvakleśaṃ jñeyaṃ śāntaṃ svayaṃsaṃvedyam // GRht_1.22 //
children.translated_text: free from all afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), to be known, peaceful (<s>śānta</s>), self-luminous (<s>svayaṃvedya</s>). (GRht 1.22)

children.text:
pūrvavarṇitaṃ cinmayaṃ viśeṣayannāha paramānandaikamayam ityādi //
                            GRhtCM_1.22:1 //
children.translated_text: Specifying the previously described consciousness-nature, he says [beginning with] 'consisting solely of supreme bliss' and so on. (GRhtCM 1.22:1)

children.text:
tadbrahma īdṛśaṃ jñeyaṃ paramānandaikamayamiti parama utkṛṣṭo 'sāv
                            ānandaḥ paramānandaḥ sa eva eko 'dvitīyas tātprācuryaṃ yasmiṃs tathoktaṃ
                            punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ paramaṃ jyotiḥsvabhāvaṃ paramaṃ yajjyotiḥ tatsvabhāvaḥ
                            svarūpaṃ yasya tad aśarīratvātsvaprakāśitvācca punaḥ avikappaṃ
                            mithyājñānaśūnyaṃ punarvigapitasarvakpeśaṃ vigapitā viśeṣeṇa dūrīkṛtāḥ
                            sarvakpeśāḥ duḥkhāni yasmāt tat svarūpatvāt punaḥ śāntaṃ śamamayaṃ punaḥ
                            svayaṃvedyam anyena veditum aśakyam ātmanaiva vedyaṃ tasmānnāparo+astīti
                            bhāvāt // GRhtCM_1.22:2 //
children.translated_text: That <s>Brahman</s> is to be known as being of such a nature: 'consisting solely of supreme bliss' — the supreme, most excellent bliss — that supreme bliss alone, without a second, whose abundance [characterizes it] — thus it is described. Moreover, of what characteristic? 'Of the nature of the supreme light' — that which is the supreme light, that is its nature, its essential form — because it is bodiless and self-luminous. Moreover, 'free from false notions' (<s>avikalpa</s>) — devoid of false knowledge. Moreover, 'free from all afflictions' — all afflictions, sufferings, have been specially removed from it — because of its essential nature. Moreover, 'peaceful' (<s>śānta</s>) — consisting of tranquility. Moreover, 'self-luminous' (<s>svayaṃvedya</s>) — unable to be known by another; knowable by the self alone — because there is no other [knower than it]. (GRhtCM 1.22:2)

children.text: tasminnādhāya manaḥ sphuradakhilaṃ jagatpaśyan /
children.translated_text: Fixing the mind on that, seeing the entire world as it flashes forth,

children.text: utsannakarmabandho brahmatvamihaiva cāpnoti // GRht_1.23 //
children.translated_text: with the bondage of <s>karma</s> destroyed, one attains <s>Brahman</s>-hood here in this very [life]. (GRht 1.23)

children.text: jñeyopadeśamāha tasminnityādi // GRhtCM_1.23:1 //
children.translated_text: He teaches how the knowable [<s>Brahman</s>] is [to be approached] — [beginning with] 'on that' and so on. (GRhtCM 1.23:1)

children.text:
tasminnādhāyeti pūrvanirūpite tasminnevātmani mana ādhāya saṃsthāpya pumān
                        utsannakarmabandho bhavet tyaktakarmapāśaḥ syāt // GRhtCM_1.23:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Fixing on that' — fixing, establishing, the mind on that very <s>Ātman</s> previously described, a person would have the bondage of <s>karma</s> destroyed — meaning he would be freed from the noose of <s>karma</s>. (GRhtCM 1.23:2)

children.text:
sa ihaiva janmani brahmatvaṃ prāpnotīti viśeṣaḥ brahmavid brahmaiva bhavati
                        iti śruteḥ // GRhtCM_1.23:3 //
children.translated_text: He attains <s>Brahman</s>-hood in this very birth — this is the special point, because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'The knower of <s>Brahman</s> becomes <s>Brahman</s> itself.' (GRhtCM 1.23:3)

children.text: sa pumān mana ādadhāti // GRhtCM_1.23:4 //
children.translated_text: That person fixes the mind. (GRhtCM 1.23:4)

children.text:
kiṃ kurvan san akhipaṃ jagat sarvasaṃsāraṃ cinmayaṃ prakāśasvarūpaṃ
                        cidvikāraṃ paśyan avapokamāno manaścakṣuṣā kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ jagat sphurat
                        adhyāropāpadeśena dedīpyamānam // GRhtCM_1.23:5 //
children.translated_text: Doing what? Seeing the entire world — the whole of <s>saṃsāra</s> — as of the nature of consciousness (<s>cinmaya</s>), of the nature of luminosity, a modification of consciousness, observing through the eye of the mind — the world as possessing what characteristic? Flashing forth — through the method of superimposition and negation (<s>adhyāropāpavāda</s>), blazing brightly. (GRhtCM 1.23:5)

children.text: tathā ca bhagavadvacanam /
children.translated_text: And thus the word of the Lord (<s>Bhagavān</s>):

children.text: karmaṇyakarma yaḥ paśyedakarmaṇi ca karma yaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He who sees inaction in action and action in inaction,

children.text: sa buddhimānmanuṣyeṣu sa yuktaḥ kṛtsnakarmakṛt // GRhtCM_1.23:6 //
children.translated_text: he is the wise one among men; he is the accomplished one, the performer of all actions.' (GRhtCM 1.23:6)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_1.23:7 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 1.23:7)

children.text: he pārtha sa pumān manuṣyeṣu buddhimān // GRhtCM_1.23:8 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Pārtha</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), that person is the wise one among men. (GRhtCM 1.23:8)

children.text: anena sāmānyatvamuktam // GRhtCM_1.23:9 //
children.translated_text: By this, the universality [of the teaching] is stated. (GRhtCM 1.23:9)

children.text:
viśeṣaśca yathā rajjau sarpabhramo yathā śuktau rajatajñānaṃ yathā
                        gandharvanagaraṃ yathā marusthape vāri tathaiva saṃsāro nāsīt nāsti na
                        bhaviṣyatīti advaitavādānmithyaiva // GRhtCM_1.23:10 //
children.translated_text: And the specific [teaching] is: just as there is the delusion of a snake in a rope, just as there is the perception of silver in a shell, just as there is a city of <s>Gandharva</s>s (a mirage-city), just as there is water in a desert — in the same way, <s>saṃsāra</s> neither was, nor is, nor will be — according to the doctrine of non-duality (<s>Advaita</s>), it is false indeed. (GRhtCM 1.23:10)

children.text: astaṃ hi yānti viṣayāḥ prāṇāntaḥkaraṇasaṃyogāt /
children.translated_text: Sense-objects set, through the conjunction of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) and the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>);

children.text: sphuraṇaṃ nendriyatamasāṃ nātaḥ sphurataśca duḥkhasukhe // GRht_1.24 //
children.translated_text: the sense-organs and [their] darkness do not flash forth; hence, for one who has [truly] flashed forth, there is neither suffering nor pleasure. (GRht 1.24)

children.text: utsannakarmabandhasya viṣayā astaṃ yānti // GRhtCM_1.24:1 //
children.translated_text: For one whose bondage of <s>karma</s> has been destroyed, sense-objects set [like the sun]. (GRhtCM 1.24:1)

children.text:
prāṇāntaḥkaraṇasaṃyogāt na indriyāṇāṃ sphuraṇaṃ bhavet // GRhtCM_1.24:2
                        //
children.translated_text: Through the conjunction of <s>prāṇa</s> and the inner organ, there would be no flashing forth of the sense-organs. (GRhtCM 1.24:2)

children.text:
tathā ca nyāyaśāstre ātmā manasā saṃyujyate mana indriyeṇa
                        indriyamarthenetīndriyāṇāṃ vastuprāpyaprakāśakāritvaniyamād iti //
                        GRhtCM_1.24:3 //
children.translated_text: And thus in the <s>Nyāya Śāstra</s>: the <s>Ātman</s> is conjoined with the mind, the mind with the sense-organ, the sense-organ with the object — because there is a rule that sense-organs illuminate [objects] only by reaching them. (GRhtCM 1.24:3)

children.text: ato hetośca duḥkhasukhe na sphurataḥ // GRhtCM_1.24:4 //
children.translated_text: For this reason, suffering and pleasure do not flash forth [for the liberated one]. (GRhtCM 1.24:4)

children.text:
ātmanaḥ prakāśāt prāṇāntaḥkaraṇānāṃ prakāśaḥ prāṇāntaḥkaraṇāni tameva
                        prakāśaṃ prāpyendriyāṇi prakāśayanti // GRhtCM_1.24:5 //
children.translated_text: From the luminosity of the <s>Ātman</s>, there is luminosity of <s>prāṇa</s> and the inner organ; <s>prāṇa</s> and the inner organ, having reached that very luminosity, illuminate the sense-organs. (GRhtCM 1.24:5)

children.text: ata ubhayoḥ paraprakāśaḥ // GRhtCM_1.24:6 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the illumination of both [senses and their objects] is dependent on [the <s>Ātman</s>'s] luminosity. (GRhtCM 1.24:6)

children.text:
tadvad gahanatama agrāhyamandhakāraṃ cidbhinnaṃ prakāśena prakāśitaṃ syāditi
                        // GRhtCM_1.24:7 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, the dense, ungraspable darkness — being different from consciousness — would be illuminated by [the <s>Ātman</s>'s] luminosity. (GRhtCM 1.24:7)

children.text: abhāvapadārthatvād indriyatamasorjaḍatvāt sāmyam // GRhtCM_1.24:8 //
children.translated_text: Because [darkness and the senses] are of the nature of non-existence and inertness, they are similar. (GRhtCM 1.24:8)

children.text: rāgadveṣavimuktāḥ satyācārā narā mṛṣārahitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Free from attachment and aversion, truthful in conduct, devoid of falsehood,

children.text: sarvatra nirviśeṣā bhavanti cidbrahmasaṃsparśāt // GRht_1.25 //
children.translated_text: they become everywhere impartial, through contact with the conscious <s>Brahman</s>. (GRht 1.25)

children.text:
adhunā antaḥkaraṇānāṃ pravṛttiṃ darśayati rāgetyādi
                            cidbrahmasaṃsparśāditi cidbrahmaṇi prakāśasvarūpe ātmani yaḥ sparśaḥ
                            tanniṣṭhā tato hetoḥ puruṣā rāgadveṣaviyuktāḥ snehaśatrutvavirahitāḥ
                            syuḥ // GRhtCM_1.25:1 //
children.translated_text: Now he shows the activity of the inner organs, with 'rāga' and so forth. 'Through contact with the conscious <s>Brahman</s>' — the contact with the conscious <s>Brahman</s>, whose nature is luminosity, the Self — that is, steadfastness in it — from that cause, persons become free from attachment and aversion, devoid of love and enmity. (GRht CM 1.25:1)

children.text:
punaḥ satyaḥ ācāraḥ pravṛttidharmo yeṣāṃ te punarmṛṣārahitāḥ
                            atyācārādyasatyavarjitā ityarthaḥ punaḥ sarvatra nirviśeṣāḥ sarvasmin
                            mānāpamānayoḥ samāḥ tathā ca bhagavadvacanam /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, those whose conduct (<s>ācāra</s>) — mode of activity and <s>dharma</s> — is truthful; moreover, 'devoid of falsehood' — free from misconduct, untruth, and the like — that is the meaning. Furthermore, 'everywhere impartial' — equal in all [situations], in honor and dishonor. And so says the <s>Bhagavad</s> statement:

children.text: samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā mānāpamānayoḥ // GRhtCM_1.25:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Equal toward enemy and friend, likewise in honor and dishonor.' (GRht CM 1.25:2)

children.text: ityādi // GRhtCM_1.25:3 //
children.translated_text: And so forth. (GRht CM 1.25:3)

children.text: tiṣṭhantyaṇimādiyutā vilasaddehā mudā sadānandāḥ /
children.translated_text: They abide, endowed with <s>aṇimā</s> and other [powers], with radiant bodies, with joy, ever blissful —

children.text: ye brahmabhāvamamṛtaṃ samprāptāścaiva kṛtakṛtyāḥ // GRht_1.26 //
children.translated_text: those who have attained the immortal state of <s>Brahman</s>, and who have fulfilled all purposes. (GRht 1.26)

children.text:
ātmani sparśatvamuktiprāptiṃ darśayannāha tiṣṭhantītyādi // GRhtCM_1.26:1
                            //
children.translated_text: Showing the attainment of liberation through contact with the Self, he says 'they abide' and so forth. (GRht CM 1.26:1)

children.text:
ye brahmabhāvamamṛtaṃ muktisārūpyatvaṃ prāptāste kṛtakṛtyāḥ
                            kṛtasarvakāryāḥ pūrṇatāṃ prāptā ityarthaḥ punaste aṇimādiyutā
                            aṇimādibhiryutā iha jagati tiṣṭhantīti aṇimādayo yathā /
children.translated_text: Those who have attained the immortal state of <s>Brahman</s> — the nature identical with liberation — they are <s>kṛtakṛtya</s> (those who have accomplished all duties) — who have attained completeness — that is the meaning. Moreover, they are 'endowed with <s>aṇimā</s> and other [powers]' — endowed with <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness) and the rest — they abide in this world. The <s>aṇimā</s> and other [powers] are as follows:

children.text: aṇimā mahimā cātha paghimā garimā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Aṇimā</s> (minuteness), <s>mahimā</s> (greatness), then <s>laghimā</s> (lightness), <s>garimā</s> (heaviness),

children.text: prāptiḥ prākāmyamīśitvaṃ vaśitvaṃ cāṣṭabhūtayaḥ // GRhtCM_1.26:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>prāpti</s> (attainment), <s>prākāmya</s> (irresistible will), <s>īśitva</s> (lordship), and <s>vaśitva</s> (control) — [these are] the eight supernatural powers (<s>vibhūtis</s>). (GRht CM 1.26:2)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_1.26:3 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRht CM 1.26:3)

children.text:
punarvipasaddehāḥ tejaḥprāyaśarīrāḥ punaḥ sadānandāḥ kena mudā harṣeṇa
                            sadā sarvasminkāpe ānando yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ paramānande magnatvāt //
                            GRhtCM_1.26:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, 'with radiant bodies' — having bodies that are predominantly luminous. Moreover, 'ever blissful' — with what? With joy, delight — [they are those] who have bliss always, in all conditions — they are so called, because of being immersed in supreme bliss. (GRht CM 1.26:4)

children.text: āyatanaṃ vidyānāṃ mūlaṃ dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇām /
children.translated_text: The abode of all sciences, the root of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s> —

children.text: śreyaḥ paraṃ kimanyat śarīramajarāmaraṃ vihāyaikam // GRht_1.27 //
children.translated_text: what other supreme good is there, having left aside one body that is free from old age and death? (GRht 1.27)

children.text: śarīramūpaṃ sarve jñātavyamityāhāyatanam ityādi // GRhtCM_1.27:1 //
children.translated_text: Saying that the form of the body should be known by all, he states 'the abode' and so forth. (GRht CM 1.27:1)

children.text:
ekam ajarāmaraṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitaṃ śarīraṃ vihāya tyaktvā anyat
                            paramutkṛṣṭaṃ śreyaḥ kapyāṇasvarūpaṃ kiṃ na kim apītyarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_1.27:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Having left aside' — having abandoned — one body that is free from old age and death — devoid of old age and death — what other supreme, excellent good (<s>śreyas</s>) — whose nature is auspicious — is there? Nothing at all — that is the meaning; because of the absence of any fruit without the body for [pursuing] the stages [of life]. (GRht CM 1.27:2)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ śarīram āyatanaṃ vidyānāṃ vyākaraṇādicaturdaśasaṃkhyākāṅgānāṃ
                            nivāsasthānaṃ punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ mūpaṃ dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ caturṇāṃ
                            padārthānāṃ mūpaṃ hetuḥ dharmādayaś catvāraḥ pratītā eva //
                            GRhtCM_1.27:3 //
children.translated_text: A body of what distinction? 'The abode of all sciences' — the dwelling place of the fourteen sciences beginning with grammar and the rest. Moreover, of what distinction? 'The root of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s>' — the root, the cause, of the four goals of life. <s>Dharma</s> and the other four are well-established [goals]. (GRht CM 1.27:3)

children.text: pramāṇato+api pratyakṣādyo na jānāti sūtakam /
children.translated_text: Even by means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) — one who does not know <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) through direct perception and the like —

children.text: adṛṣṭavigrahaṃ devaṃ kathaṃ jñāsyati cinmayam // GRht_1.28 //
children.translated_text: how will he know the god whose form is invisible, who consists of consciousness? (GRht 1.28)

children.text:
ātmano 'vekṣayā sūte sugamatvaṃ sūcayannāha pramāṇata ityādi //
                            GRhtCM_1.28:1 //
children.translated_text: Showing the easy accessibility [of Self-knowledge] in relation to the Self, he says 'by means of valid knowledge' and so forth. (GRht CM 1.28:1)

children.text:
yaḥ puruṣaḥ sūtakaṃ rasendraṃ na jānāti kutaḥ pramāṇataḥ pramākaraṇaṃ
                            pramāṇaṃ pramitisādhanaṃ vā tataḥ kimbhūtāt pramāṇataḥ pratyakṣāc
                            cakṣurindriyagrāhyarūpāt sa pumān cinmayam atisūkṣmam ātmānaṃ kathaṃ
                            jñāsyati na katham apītyarthaḥ indriyāgocaratvāt // GRhtCM_1.28:2 //
children.translated_text: The person who does not know <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) — from what? From valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) — the instrument of valid cognition, or the means of ascertaining — from such [means]; of what kind? From direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) — [that which is] graspable by the sense organs such as the eye — that person, how will he know the Self that consists of consciousness and is exceedingly subtle? In no way — that is the meaning; because it is beyond the range of the senses. (GRht CM 1.28:2)

Of what qualification? 'Of invisible form' — <s>ādi</s> (beginning) and <s>vigraha</s> (body) [are absent] — in which there is neither origin nor body — due to the absence of origination and [gross] body, there is absence of gross knowledge — this is the purport. (GRht CM 1.28:3)

children.text: yajjarayā jarjaritaṃ kāsaśvāsādiduḥkhavaśamāptam /
children.translated_text: That [body] which is worn out by old age, afflicted by suffering from cough, asthma, and the like —

children.text: yogyaṃ tanna samādhau pratihatabuddhīndriyaprasaram // GRht_1.29 //
children.translated_text: is not fit for <s>samādhi</s>, its faculties of intellect and senses being obstructed. (GRht 1.29)

children.text: bālaḥ ṣoḍaśavarṣo viṣayarasāsvādalampaṭaḥ parataḥ /
children.translated_text: A child, [then] one of sixteen years, addicted to the enjoyment of sense-pleasures; beyond that,

children.text: jātaviveko vṛddho martyaḥ kathamāpnuyānmuktim // GRht_1.30 //
children.translated_text: when discrimination arises one is old — how can a mortal attain liberation? (GRht 1.30)

children.text:
śarīrasya vayovibhāgenāsthiratvaṃ darśayannāha bāpa ityādi //
                            GRhtCM_1.29-30:1 //
children.translated_text: Showing the instability [of the body] through the division of the stages of life, he says 'a child' and so forth. (GRht CM 1.29-30:1)

children.text:
ṣoḍaśavarṣa iti ṣoḍaśa varṣāṇi yasya vayasi sa ṣoḍaśābdo bāpa ityarthaḥ
                            // GRhtCM_1.29-30:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Of sixteen years' — one whose age has sixteen years — that is the meaning of 'a sixteen-year-old child.' (GRht CM 1.29-30:2)

children.text: granthāntare bāpatve'pi vayobhedā vartante // GRhtCM_1.29-30:3 //
children.translated_text: In other texts, even within childhood, there are divisions of age. (GRht CM 1.29-30:3)

children.text: yathā padyam /
children.translated_text: As the verse [states]:

children.text: ā pañcamācca kaumāraḥ paugaṇḍo navahāyanaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Up to [age] five is <s>kaumāra</s> (infancy); <s>paugaṇḍa</s> (boyhood) [lasts] until nine years;

children.text: ā ṣoḍaśācca kiśoro yauvanaṃ ca tataḥ param // GRhtCM_1.29-30:4 //
children.translated_text: up to sixteen is <s>kiśora</s> (adolescence); and youth (<s>yauvana</s>) [comes] thereafter.' (GRht CM 1.29-30:4)
Thus. (GRht CM 1.29-30:5)

children.text: bāpo vastujñāne aśaktaḥ // GRhtCM_1.29-30:6 //
children.translated_text: A child is incapable of [grasping] the knowledge of reality. (GRht CM 1.29-30:6)

children.text:
punaḥ ṣoḍaśavarṣebhyaḥ paraḥ viṣayarasāsvādapampaṭo bhavati viṣayāḥ
                            śabdasparśarūparasagandhā rasāḥ
                            śṛṅgārahāsyakaruṇaraudravīrabhayānakabībhatsādbhutaśāntāḥ //
                            GRhtCM_1.29-30:7 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, after sixteen years, one becomes addicted to the enjoyment of sense-pleasures. The sense-objects are sound, touch, form, taste, and smell. The <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments) are <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), <s>hāsya</s> (comic), <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic), <s>raudra</s> (furious), <s>vīra</s> (heroic), <s>bhayānaka</s> (terrible), <s>bībhatsa</s> (odious), <s>adbhuta</s> (wondrous), and <s>śānta</s> (tranquil). (GRht CM 1.29-30:7)

children.text:
kecit śāntaṃ rasaṃ na bruvanti nirvikāratvāt eteṣām āsvādaḥ svādas tatra
                            pampaṭo vyāsaktaḥ atha vā viṣayānantaraṃ snehastatreti //
                            GRhtCM_1.29-30:8 //
children.translated_text: Some do not include <s>śānta</s> (tranquil) as a <s>rasa</s>, because of its quality of being without modification. The enjoyment (<s>āsvāda</s>) of these — their relishing — therein one is addicted (<s>lampaṭa</s>), meaning attached. Or alternatively, 'sense-pleasures thereafter' means attachment [develops]. (GRht CM 1.29-30:8)

children.text:
ataḥ parato jātaviveko bhavati utpannavicāro bhavati // GRhtCM_1.29-30:9
                            //
children.translated_text: After that, discrimination arises — discriminating inquiry develops. (GRht CM 1.29-30:9)

children.text:
tadā vṛddho+akṣamaḥ paraṃ manuṣyaḥ muktiṃ kaivapyaṃ katham āpnuyāt na
                            kathamapītyartho vayasyupappavabhāvāt // GRhtCM_1.29-30:10 //
children.translated_text: Then, being old and incapacitated, how can a human being attain liberation (<s>kaivalya</s>)? In no way — that is the meaning; because of the absence of fitness [for yoga] at that stage of life. (GRht CM 1.29-30:10)

children.text: asminn eva śarīre yeṣāṃ paramātmano na saṃvedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those in whose case there is no direct experience of the Supreme Self in this very body —

children.text: dehatyāgādūrdhvaṃ teṣāṃ tadbrahma dūrataram // GRht_1.31 //
children.translated_text: for them, after the abandonment of the body, that <s>Brahman</s> is farther away. (GRht 1.31)

children.text:
pūrvapadyābhiprāyaṃ vicārya muktiprāptau praśaṅkitaḥ prāhāsminn ityādi //
                            GRhtCM_1.31:1 //
children.translated_text: Having considered the import of the previous verse, addressing one who has doubts about the attainment of liberation, he says 'in this' and so forth. (GRht CM 1.31:1)

children.text:
asmin śarīre vartamāne kṣetrarūpe yeṣāṃ puṃsām ātmasaṃvedo na jātaḥ
                            brahmajñānaṃ na jātaṃ teṣāṃ puṃsāmeva dehatyāgād ūrdhvaṃ śarīrotsargataḥ
                            paścāt tadbrahma dūrataraṃ dūrāddūrataram ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.31:2
                            //
children.translated_text: In this body — the present one, which is in the form of a field (<s>kṣetra</s>) — for those persons in whom Self-realization has not arisen, in whom knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> has not arisen — for those very persons, after the abandonment of the body — after the casting off of the body — thereafter, that <s>Brahman</s> is farther away — more distant than the distant — that is the meaning. (GRht CM 1.31:2)

children.text: brahmādayo yajante yasmin divyāṃ tanuṃ samāśritya /
children.translated_text: In which [state] <s>Brahmā</s> and others worship, having attained a divine body —

children.text: jīvanmuktāścānye kalpāntasthāyino munayaḥ // GRht_1.32 //
children.translated_text: and other sages who are <s>jīvanmukta</s>s (liberated while living), enduring until the end of the cosmic cycle (<s>kalpa</s>). (GRht 1.32)

children.text: adhunā pūrvamataṃ draḍhayati brahmādaya ityādi // GRhtCM_1.32:1 //
children.translated_text: Now he strengthens the previous view, with '<s>Brahmā</s> and others' and so forth. (GRht CM 1.32:1)

children.text:
yasmin brahmādayo viṣṇurudrendrādayo brahmavido yajante saṃgatiṃ kurvanti
                            samāpnuvantītyarthaḥ yaja devapūjāsaṃgatikaraṇadāneṣu atra
                            saṃgatikaraṇam artho darśitaḥ // GRhtCM_1.32:2 //
children.translated_text: In which [state], <s>Brahmā</s> and others — <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the rest, the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> — worship (<s>yajante</s>), meaning they unite, they attain — that is the meaning. [The root] 'yaj' [is used] in the senses of deity-worship, union, and giving. Here, the meaning of 'union' is indicated. (GRht CM 1.32:2)

children.text:
kiṃ kṛtvā prāpnuvanti divyāṃ tanuṃ paramāṃ samāśritya samprāpya tebhyo
                            brahmādibhyo 'pyanye apare munayo nāradādayo jīvanmuktā yajante saṃgatiṃ
                            kurvanti // GRhtCM_1.32:3 //
children.translated_text: Having done what do they attain [this]? 'Having attained a divine body' — having obtained the supreme [body]. Other sages apart from <s>Brahmā</s> and the rest — such as <s>Nārada</s> and others — who are <s>jīvanmukta</s>s, worship, meaning they attain union. (GRht CM 1.32:3)

children.text:
te 'pi kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ kappāntasthāyinaḥ prapayānte'pi tiṣṭhantīti bhāvaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_1.32:4 //
children.translated_text: Of what qualification are they? 'Enduring until the end of the <s>kalpa</s>' — they remain even at the time of dissolution — this is the purport. (GRht CM 1.32:4)

children.text: brahmādayas tiṣṭhanta eva // GRhtCM_1.32:5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> and the others do endure [thus]. (GRht CM 1.32:5)

children.text: tasmājjīvanmuktiṃ samīhamānena yoginā prathamam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, a yogin desiring <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living) should first

children.text: divyā tanurvidheyā haragaurīsṛṣṭisaṃyogāt // GRht_1.33 //
children.translated_text: create a divine body, through the union of the creation of <s>Hara</s> and <s>Gaurī</s>. (GRht 1.33)

children.text:
iti bahudhā vicāryeṣṭavastustutim āha tasmād ityādi // GRhtCM_1.33:1
                            //
children.translated_text: Having thus deliberated in many ways, he states the praise of the desired substance, with 'therefore' and so forth. (GRht CM 1.33:1)

children.text:
yato brahmādayo jīvanmuktāś cānye divyāṃ tanuṃ vidhāya muktiṃ prāptās
                            tasmāddhetor yoginā yogayuktena prathamaṃ divyā tanur vidheyā
                            dṛḍhaśarīraṃ kāryam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.33:2 //
children.translated_text: Since <s>Brahmā</s> and others, and other <s>jīvanmukta</s>s, having created a divine body, attained liberation — therefore, for this reason, by the yogin — one endowed with yoga — first a divine body should be created; meaning, a firm body should be made. (GRht CM 1.33:2)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭena yoginā jīvanmuktiṃ samīhamānena yoginā divyā tanur vidheyā
                            // GRhtCM_1.33:3 //
children.translated_text: By a yogin of what qualification? By a yogin desiring <s>jīvanmukti</s>, a divine body should be created. (GRht CM 1.33:3)

children.text: kutaḥ haragaurīsṛṣṭisaṃyogāt // GRhtCM_1.33:4 //
children.translated_text: From what? From the union of the creation of <s>Hara</s> and <s>Gaurī</s>. (GRht CM 1.33:4)

children.text: umeśvarasṛṣṭo rasendras tasya sevanād ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_1.33:5 //
children.translated_text: The lord of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>) is the creation of <s>Umā</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>; through the service of that — that is the meaning. (GRht CM 1.33:5)

children.text: dṛḍhaśarīreṇa vāñchitaṃ sādhyate na tv anyathā // GRhtCM_1.33:6 //
children.translated_text: With a firm body, the desired [goal] is accomplished; but not otherwise. (GRht CM 1.33:6)

children.text: tasyāpi sādhanavidhau sudhiyā pratikarmanirmalāḥ prathamam /
children.translated_text: In the procedure for accomplishing that [mercury] too, the wise one should first [learn]

children.text: aṣṭādaśasaṃskārā vijñātavyāḥ prayatnena // GRht_1.34 //
children.translated_text: the eighteen <s>saṃskāras</s> (purificatory processes), pure in each operation, with effort. (GRht 1.34)

children.text:
divyatanorhetutvād rasendrasya sādhanavidhau sādhanopadeśe sudhiyā
                            pūjyamatinā puṃsā prathamam aṣṭādaśasaṃskārāḥ prayatnena jñātavyāḥ //
                            GRhtCM_1.34:1 //
children.translated_text: In the procedure for accomplishing <s>rasendra</s> (mercury), which is the cause of the divine body — in the teaching of the method — by the wise one, a person of venerable intellect, the eighteen <s>saṃskāras</s> should first be known with effort. (GRht CM 1.34:1)

children.text: saṃskriyanta iti saṃskārāḥ // GRhtCM_1.34:2 //
children.translated_text: They are called <s>saṃskāras</s> because they purify (<s>saṃskriyante</s>). (GRht CM 1.34:2)

children.text:
puṃsyapi garbhādhānādayaḥ ṣoḍaśa saṃskārā vartante ata eva saṃskārair
                            ubhayoḥ sāmyaṃ doṣābhāvatvaṃ guṇavattvaṃ ca syāt // GRhtCM_1.34:3 //
children.translated_text: In the case of a person too, there are sixteen <s>saṃskāras</s> beginning with <s>garbhādhāna</s> (conception rite). Therefore, through <s>saṃskāras</s>, there is equality between the two [mercury and person] — absence of faults and presence of virtues [in both]. (GRht CM 1.34:3)

children.text: ato brāhmaṇakṣatriyavaiśyaśūdrāḥ syuḥ // GRhtCM_1.34:4 //
children.translated_text: Hence [the analogy with] <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Śūdras</s> [applies]. (GRht CM 1.34:4)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ saṃskārāḥ pratikarmanirmapāḥ karma karma prati nirdoṣāḥ //
                            GRhtCM_1.34:5 //
children.translated_text: Of what qualification are the <s>saṃskāras</s>? 'Pure in each operation' — flawless in each and every operation. (GRht CM 1.34:5)

children.text: 18 saṃskāras
children.translated_text: [The] 18 <s>saṃskāras</s>:

children.text: svedanamardanamūrchotthāpanapātananirodhaniyamāśca /
children.translated_text: <s>Svedana</s> (sweating), <s>mardana</s> (grinding), <s>mūrcchā</s> (swooning), <s>utthāpana</s> (raising), <s>pātana</s> (sublimation), <s>nirodhana</s> (restraining), <s>niyama</s> (regulation),

children.text: dīpanagaganagrāsapramāṇamatha cāraṇavidhānaṃ ca // GRht_2.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>dīpana</s> (kindling), <s>gaganagrāsa</s> (devouring of space/mica), and <s>cāraṇavidhāna</s> (the procedure of <s>cāraṇa</s>); (GRht 2.1)

children.text: garbhadrutibāhyadrutijāraṇarasarāgasāraṇaṃ caiva /
children.translated_text: <s>Garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction), <s>bāhyadruti</s> (external liquefaction), <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion), <s>rasarāga</s> (coloring of mercury), <s>sāraṇa</s> (extraction/streaming),

children.text: krāmaṇavedhau bhakṣaṇamaṣṭādaśadheti rasakarma // GRht_2.2 //
children.translated_text: <s>krāmaṇa</s> (pervasion), <s>vedha</s> (penetration), and <s>bhakṣaṇa</s> (consumption) — thus the operations on mercury are eighteen-fold. (GRht 2.2)

children.text: yasyopajīvyate kīrtiḥ saṅgameva sudhābhujām /
children.translated_text: He whose fame is relied upon — the association with those who partake of nectar —

children.text: sa śrīmān kārayāmāsa vṛttiṃ mugdhāvabodhinīm // GRhtCM_2.1-2:1 //
children.translated_text: that illustrious one caused the composition called <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s> to be made. (GRht CM 2.1-2:1)

children.text: āryādvayena rasāṣṭādaśasaṃskāroddeśaḥ kṛtaḥ // GRhtCM_2.1-2:2 //
children.translated_text: By means of two <s>āryā</s> verses, the enumeration of the eighteen <s>saṃskāras</s> of mercury has been made. (GRht CM 2.1-2:2)

children.text: 1. svedana>
children.translated_text: 1. <s>Svedana</s> (Sweating):

children.text: āsurīpaṭukaṭukatrayacitrārdrakamūlakaiḥ kalāṃśaistu /
children.translated_text: With <s>āsurī</s> (mustard), <s>paṭu</s> (sharp substances), the three pungents (<s>kaṭukatraya</s>), <s>citrā</s> (Plumbago), fresh ginger, and radish, in fractional portions —

children.text: sūtasya kāñjikena tridinaṃ mṛduvahninā svedaḥ // GRht_2.3 //
children.translated_text: mercury [is subjected to] sweating (<s>sveda</s>) with sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>), for three days, with a gentle fire. (GRht 2.3)

children.text: adhunā saṃskārāṇāṃ sādhane pakṣaṇam āha // GRhtCM_2.3:1 //
children.translated_text: Now he states the method for accomplishing the <s>saṃskāras</s>. (GRht CM 2.3:1)

children.text:
tatra prathamoddiṣṭasya svedanasaṃskārasya sādhanaṃ spaṣṭayannāha
                            āsurītyādi // GRhtCM_2.3:2 //
children.translated_text: Explaining the method of accomplishing the first-mentioned <s>svedana saṃskāra</s> (sweating process), he says '<s>āsurī</s>' and so forth. (GRht CM 2.3:2)

children.text:
sūtasya pāradasya tridinaṃ dinatrayaparimāṇaṃ yathā syāttathā mṛduvahninā
                            svappāgninā svedaḥ svedanaṃ kāryam // GRhtCM_2.3:3 //
children.translated_text: The <s>svedana</s> (steaming) of <s>sūta</s> (mercury) should be done for three days — for a duration of three days — with a gentle fire, a mild flame. (GRhtCM 2.3:3)

children.text: kena kāñjikena sauvīreṇa // GRhtCM_2.3:4 //
children.translated_text: With what? With <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel), <s>sauvīra</s> (a type of fermented liquid). (GRhtCM 2.3:4)

children.text:
kaiḥ saha āsurīpaṭukaṭukatrayacitrārdrakamūpakaiḥ saha // GRhtCM_2.3:5
                            //
children.translated_text: With what [substances]? Together with <s>āsurī</s> (mustard), <s>paṭu</s> (rock salt), the three pungent [spices], <s>citraka</s> (leadwort), fresh ginger, and <s>mūlaka</s> (radish). (GRhtCM 2.3:5)

children.text:
āsurī rājikā paṭu saindhavaṃ pavaṇaviśeṣaḥ kecitpaṭuśabdena kṣāramapi
                            vyācakṣate kaṭukatrayaṃ śuṇṭhīmaricapippapyaḥ citrakaṃ pratītam ārdrakaṃ
                            kandaviśeṣo nāgarahetuḥ mūpakaṃ kandaviśeṣaḥ prasiddhaḥ // GRhtCM_2.3:6
                            //
children.translated_text: <s>Āsurī</s> is mustard (<s>rājikā</s>). <s>Paṭu</s> is rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>), a type of salt; some explain the word <s>paṭu</s> as also meaning alkali. The three pungent [spices] are dried ginger (<s>śuṇṭhī</s>), black pepper (<s>marica</s>), and long pepper (<s>pippalī</s>). <s>Citraka</s> (leadwort) is well-known. <s>Ārdraka</s> is a type of tuber, the source of dry ginger (<s>nāgara</s>). <s>Mūlaka</s> is a well-known type of tuber [radish]. (GRhtCM 2.3:6)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭairetaiḥ kapāṃśaiḥ ṣoḍaśāṃśaiḥ ṣoḍaśāṃśaḥ pratyekaṃ saṃyujyate
                            // GRhtCM_2.3:7 //
children.translated_text: Of what specification? In portions — in sixteenth parts — a sixteenth part of each is combined. (GRhtCM 2.3:7)

children.text: sarvasaṃmatamidaṃ vyākhyānām // GRhtCM_2.3:8 //
children.translated_text: This explanation is accepted by all [authorities]. (GRhtCM 2.3:8)

children.text:
atra viśeṣaḥ kāñjike sarvadhānyāmpasaṃdhānaṃ tuṣavarjye tu kārayet //
                            GRhtCM_2.3:9 //
children.translated_text: Here is a specification: for the <s>kāñjika</s>, the fermentation of all grains should be done, but excluding the husk. (GRhtCM 2.3:9)

children.text: uragā triphapā krāntā paghuparṇī śatāvarī // GRhtCM_2.3:10 //
children.translated_text: <s>Uragā</s> (serpent-herb), <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits), <s>krāntā</s>, <s>laghuparṇī</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s> — (GRhtCM 2.3:10)

children.text: tena yuktaṃ rasasvinnaṃ tridinaṃ mṛduvahninā // GRhtCM_2.3:11 //
children.translated_text: combined with these, the mercury should be steamed for three days with a gentle fire. (GRhtCM 2.3:11)

children.text: dopāyantreṇa tīvreṇa mardayitvā punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: In a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing-apparatus), grinding it repeatedly and thoroughly —

children.text: iti rasendramaṅgapāt // GRhtCM_2.3:12 //
children.translated_text: thus from the <s>Rasendramaṅgala</s>. (GRhtCM 2.3:12)

children.text: kṣārāmpair oṣadhair vāpi dopāyantre sthitasya hi /
children.translated_text: With alkaline waters, or with herbs, while placed in the <s>dolāyantra</s>,

children.text: pācanaṃ svedanākhyaṃ syānmapaśaithipyakārakam /
children.translated_text: the cooking, called <s>svedana</s> (steaming), should loosen the impurities —

children.text: iti paribhāṣā // GRhtCM_2.3:13 //
children.translated_text: thus is the definition. (GRhtCM 2.3:13)

children.text: dravadravyeṇa bhāṇḍasya pūritārdhodarasya ca /
children.translated_text: Having filled the vessel half-full with liquid substance,

children.text: mukhasyobhayato dvāradvayaṃ kṛtvā prayatnataḥ // GRhtCM_2.3:14 //
children.translated_text: and having carefully made two openings on both sides of its mouth — (GRhtCM 2.3:14)

children.text: tasyopari kṣipeddaṇḍaṃ tanmadhye rasapoṭapīm /
children.translated_text: one should place a rod above it, and in its middle hang the mercury-pouch,

children.text: baddhvā tu svedayedetaddopāyantramiti smṛtam /
children.translated_text: and having tied it, steam it — this is known as the <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing-apparatus).

children.text: iti dopāyantrapakṣaṇam // GRhtCM_2.3:15 //
children.translated_text: Thus is the description of the <s>dolāyantra</s>. (GRhtCM 2.3:15)

children.text: 2. mardana
children.translated_text: 2. <s>Mardana</s> (Grinding)

children.text: guḍadagdhorṇālavaṇair mandiradhūmeṣṭakāsurīsahitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With jaggery, burnt wool, salt, incense, brick-powder, and mustard together,

children.text: rasaṣoḍaśāṃśamānaiḥ sakāñjikairmardanaṃ tridinam // GRht_2.4 //
children.translated_text: in sixteenth-part measures relative to the mercury, with <s>kāñjika</s>, grinding [should be done] for three days. (GRht 2.4)

children.text:
dvitīyoddiṣṭasya mardanasya sādhanaṃ spaṣṭayannāha guḍetyādi //
                            GRhtCM_2.4:1 //
children.translated_text: Clarifying the means for the second prescribed [process], <s>mardana</s> (grinding), [the commentator] says 'guḍa' and so forth. (GRhtCM 2.4:1)

children.text:
etair auṣadhair dinatrayaṃ parimāṇaṃ rasasya mardanaṃ kāryam //
                            GRhtCM_2.4:2 //
children.translated_text: With these medicines, the grinding of mercury should be done for a duration of three days. (GRhtCM 2.4:2)

children.text:
etaiḥ kaiḥ guḍadagdhorṇāpavaṇaiḥ guḍa ikṣuvikāraḥ prasiddhaḥ dagdhorṇā
                            dagdhā cāsau ūrṇā ceti samāsaḥ ūrṇā pratītā meṣaromanicayam ityarthaḥ
                            pavaṇaṃ saindhavamekaṃ guḍadagdhorṇārajanī iti vā pāṭhaḥ tatra haridrā
                            grāhyā na saindhavam // GRhtCM_2.4:3 //
children.translated_text: With what? With jaggery, burnt wool, and salt: jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>) is a well-known product of sugarcane; burnt wool (<s>dagdhorṇā</s>) — 'burnt' and 'wool' is the compound — wool means the collection of sheep's hair; salt (<s>lavaṇa</s>) is rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>). One [reading is] 'jaggery, burnt wool, and <s>arajanī</s> (turmeric)' — in that case, turmeric should be taken, not rock salt. (GRhtCM 2.4:3)

children.text: rasaṣoḍaśāṃśamānaiḥ rasātṣoḍaśāṃśapramāṇaiḥ // GRhtCM_2.4:4 //
children.translated_text: In sixteenth-part measures relative to the mercury — in proportions that are one-sixteenth of the mercury. (GRhtCM 2.4:4)

children.text: aṃśa ityasya pratyekaṃ sambandhaḥ // GRhtCM_2.4:5 //
children.translated_text: The word 'part' (<s>aṃśa</s>) is connected with each [ingredient] individually. (GRhtCM 2.4:5)

children.text:
viśeṣaścātra vastraiścaturguṇair baddhaḥ sūtaḥ sthāpyaḥ śubhe 'hani //
                            GRhtCM_2.4:6 //
children.translated_text: And the specification here: the mercury, bound in cloth folded fourfold, should be placed on an auspicious day. (GRhtCM 2.4:6)

children.text: pohārkāśmajakhapve tu tapteṣveva tu mardayet // GRhtCM_2.4:7 //
children.translated_text: One should grind it in [a mortar of] heated metal, stone, or <s>khalva</s> (mortar). (GRhtCM 2.4:7)

children.text: uddiṣṭair oṣadhaiḥ sārdhaṃ sarvāmpaiḥ kāñjikairapi /
children.translated_text: Together with the prescribed medicines and all [types of] sour liquids and <s>kāñjika</s>,

children.text:
peṣaṇaṃ mardanākhyaṃ syāttadbahirmapanāśanam iti paribhāṣā //
                            GRhtCM_2.4:8 //
children.translated_text: the pestle-grinding is called <s>mardana</s> — that destroys external impurities. Thus is the definition. (GRhtCM 2.4:8)

children.text: atra yantraṃ tu khapvākhyaṃ jñeyam // GRhtCM_2.4:9 //
children.translated_text: The apparatus here is the one called <s>khalva</s> (mortar) as mentioned before. (GRhtCM 2.4:9)

children.text:
tappakṣaṇaṃ tu khapvayogyā śipā nīpā śyāmā snigdhā dṛḍhā guruḥ //
                            GRhtCM_2.4:10 //
children.translated_text: And the description of that: the stone suitable for the <s>khalva</s> should be blue-black, smooth, firm, and heavy. (GRhtCM 2.4:10)

children.text: ṣoḍaśāṅgupikotsedhā navāṅgupikavistarā iti // GRhtCM_2.4:11 //
children.translated_text: Sixteen finger-breadths in height and nine finger-breadths in width. (GRhtCM 2.4:11)

children.text: khapvayogyaśipāpakṣaṇaṃ prasaṅgād uktam // GRhtCM_2.4:12 //
children.translated_text: The description of the stone suitable for the <s>khalva</s> is stated incidentally. (GRhtCM 2.4:12)

children.text:
utsedhena navāṅgupaḥ khapu kapātupyāṅgupāyāmavān vistāreṇa daśāṅgupo 'tha
                            munibhir nimnas tathaivāṅgupaiḥ // GRhtCM_2.4:13 //
children.translated_text: Nine finger-breadths in height; the <s>khalva</s> — the slab — is one-and-a-half finger-breadths in the lengthwise dimension; ten finger-breadths in width; and, according to the sages, equally [deep] in finger-breadths in depth. (GRhtCM 2.4:13)
The width of the grinding-slab is smooth in finger-breadths, very much shaped like a half-moon; the pestle is twelve finger-breadths — this <s>khalva</s> is prescribed for grinding. (GRhtCM 2.4:14)

children.text: 3. mūrchana
children.translated_text: 3. <s>Mūrchana</s> (Swooning/Stupefaction)

children.text: malaśikhiviṣābhidhānā rasasya naisargikās trayo doṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: The three natural defects of mercury are called <s>mala</s> (impurity), <s>śikhi</s> (fire), and <s>viṣa</s> (poison).

children.text: mūrchāṃ malena kurute śikhinā dāhaṃ viṣeṇa mṛtyuṃ ca // GRht_2.5 //
children.translated_text: Through <s>mala</s> it causes <s>mūrchā</s> (stupefaction, sensory confusion); through <s>śikhi</s> (fire), burning; and through <s>viṣa</s> (poison), death. (GRht 2.5)

children.text: gṛhakanyā harati malaṃ triphalāgniṃ citrakaśca viṣam /
children.translated_text: <s>Gṛhakanyā</s> (aloe vera) removes <s>mala</s>; <s>triphalā</s> [removes] fire (<s>agni</s>); and <s>citraka</s> (leadwort) [removes] poison.

children.text: tasmād ebhir miśrair vārān saṃmūrchayetsapta // GRht_2.6 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, with these mixed together, one should stupefy [the mercury] seven times. (GRht 2.6)

children.text: rasasya pāradasya doṣās trayo vartante // GRhtCM_2.5-6:1 //
children.translated_text: The defects of mercury (<s>pārada</s>) are three. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:1)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ mapaśikhiviṣābhidhānāḥ mapaśca śikhī ca viṣaṃ ca
                            tānyevābhidhānaṃ nāma yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ // GRhtCM_2.5-6:2 //
children.translated_text: Of what description? Named <s>mala</s> (impurity), <s>śikhi</s> (fire), and <s>viṣa</s> (poison) — impurity, fire, and poison — these very ones are the names (<s>abhidhāna</s>) of which — they are so described. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:2)

children.text:
punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ naisargikāḥ nisarga utpattis tatsambandhinaḥ sahajā
                            ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_2.5-6:3 //
children.translated_text: Further, of what description? Natural (<s>naisargika</s>) — <s>nisarga</s> means origin; related to that — meaning innate. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:3)

children.text:
viśeṣaścātra mapādyāḥ pañcadoṣāḥ syur bhūjādyāḥ saptakañcukāḥ //
                            GRhtCM_2.5-6:4 //
children.translated_text: And the specification here: 'The five defects beginning with <s>mala</s>; the seven sheaths (<s>kañcuka</s>) beginning with <s>bhūja</s> (earth-born).' (GRhtCM 2.5-6:4)

children.text:
kuṣṭānaṣṭau rasāntaḥsthā rase te 'nantadoṣadāḥ iti rasasaṃketakapikāyām
                            // GRhtCM_2.5-6:5 //
children.translated_text: 'The eight diseases (<s>kuṣṭha</s>) inherent in mercury — they give infinite defects to mercury.' — [This is stated] in the <s>Rasasaṃketakalikā</s>. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:5)

children.text:
yadyapi rasendramaṅgape pañca mapādayo naisargikā doṣāḥ kathitās
                            tathāpyatra traya eva anye dve gurutvacapapatve naisargikadoṣarūpe kuto
                            na staḥ tribhiḥ svedanamardanamūrchanātmakaiḥ saṃskārair anivṛtteḥ //
                            GRhtCM_2.5-6:6 //
children.translated_text: Although in the <s>Rasendramaṅgala</s>, five natural defects beginning with <s>mala</s> are described, here only three [are mentioned]. Why are the other two — heaviness and volatility — which are in the nature of natural defects, not [mentioned]? Because they are not removed by the three processes (<s>saṃskāra</s>s) of <s>svedana</s>, <s>mardana</s>, and <s>mūrchana</s>. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:6)

children.text:
naisargikagrahaṇād vaikārikāṇām api grahaṇaṃ syāt // GRhtCM_2.5-6:7
                            //
children.translated_text: By the mention of 'natural' [defects], acquired (<s>vaikārika</s>) [defects] are also implied. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:7)

children.text:
atra naisargikā uktā vaikārikāḥ kuto noktāḥ vaikārikāṇāṃ bhāvābhāvāt //
                            GRhtCM_2.5-6:8 //
children.translated_text: Here the natural [defects] are stated — why are the acquired ones not stated? Because acquired [defects] may or may not be present. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:8)

children.text:
raso doṣatrayāvṛtaḥ prāśyamānaḥ kiṃ karoti mapena mapadoṣeṇa mūrchām
                            indriyamohaṃ kurute śikhinā vahninā dāhaṃ viṣeṇa mṛtyuṃ maraṇaṃ ceti
                            samuccaye // GRhtCM_2.5-6:9 //
children.translated_text: When mercury, enveloped by the three defects, is consumed, what does it do? Through <s>mala</s> (the impurity-defect) it causes <s>mūrchā</s> (stupefaction) — confusion of the senses; through <s>śikhi</s> (fire) it causes burning; and through <s>viṣa</s> (poison) it causes <s>mṛtyu</s> (death) — and [these are stated] in conjunction. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:9)

children.text: eṣāmapaharaṇaṃ kāryamiti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_2.5-6:10 //
children.translated_text: The purport is: the removal of these [defects] should be performed. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:10)

children.text: svarūpasya vināśena piṣṭitvāpādanaṃ hi yat /
children.translated_text: The reduction to powder through the destruction of its [natural] form —

children.text: vidvadbhir jitasūto 'sau naṣṭapiṣṭaḥ sa ucyate // GRhtCM_2.5-6:11 //
children.translated_text: that mercury which has been conquered by the learned — it is called <s>naṣṭapiṣṭa</s> (destroyed and pulverized). (GRhtCM 2.5-6:11)

children.text: mardanoddiṣṭabhaiṣajyair naṣṭapiṣṭatvakārakam /
children.translated_text: That which produces the state of <s>naṣṭapiṣṭa</s> through the medicines prescribed for <s>mardana</s> —

children.text: tanmūrchanam iti proktaṃ doṣatrayavināśanam iti // GRhtCM_2.5-6:12 //
children.translated_text: that is called <s>mūrchana</s> (swooning) — it destroys the three defects. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:12)

children.text: yantram atra khapvam eva pūrvoktaṃ yat // GRhtCM_2.5-6:13 //
children.translated_text: The apparatus here is the very <s>khalva</s> (mortar) that was previously described. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:13)

children.text: tridoṣāpaharaṇaṃ mūrchanaṃ cāha gṛhakanyetyādi // GRhtCM_2.5-6:14 //
children.translated_text: The removal of the three defects through <s>mūrchana</s> is stated with '<s>gṛhakanyā</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:14)

children.text:
gṛhakanyā gṛhakumārikā mapaṃ prathamaṃ doṣaṃ harati // GRhtCM_2.5-6:15
                            //
children.translated_text: <s>Gṛhakanyā</s> (aloe vera, lit. 'the maiden of the house') removes <s>mala</s> (impurity), the first defect. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:15)

children.text:
punastriphapā trayāṇāṃ phapānāṃ samāhāraḥ triphapā agniṃ dvitīyaṃ doṣaṃ
                            harati samāhāro yathā ekā harītakī yojyā dvau ca yojyau vibhītakau /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>triphalā</s> — the aggregate of three fruits — removes <s>agni</s> (fire), the second defect. The aggregate is as follows: one <s>harītakī</s> (chebulic myrobalan) is to be used; two <s>vibhītaka</s>s (beleric myrobalan);

children.text: catvāryāmapakānyeva triphapeyaṃ prakīrtitā /
children.translated_text: and four <s>āmalaka</s>s (Indian gooseberry) — this is declared to be <s>triphalā</s>.

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_2.5-6:16 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:16)

children.text:
punaścitrako+agniḥ viṣaṃ tṛtīyaṃ doṣaṃ harati dūrīkarotītyarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_2.5-6:17 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>citraka</s> (leadwort, called <s>agni</s>) removes <s>viṣa</s> (poison), the third defect — meaning it drives it away. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:17)

Therefore — for this reason — with these three — <s>gṛhakanyā</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, and <s>citraka</s> — mixed together, one should stupefy the mercury seven times — perform the <s>mūrchana</s> procedure properly. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:18)

children.text: viśeṣaścātra /
children.translated_text: And the specification here:

children.text: mūrchanaṃ rasarājasya kartavyaṃ vādibhiḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: The <s>mūrchana</s> of the king of mercury should always be performed by practitioners.

children.text: viṣais triphapayā pūrvaṃ bṛhatyopaviṣastathā // GRhtCM_2.5-6:19 //
children.translated_text: First with poisons and <s>triphalā</s>, also with <s>bṛhatī</s> and lesser poisons; (GRhtCM 2.5-6:19)

children.text: karkoṭī kṣārakandābhyāṃ citreṇa gṛhakanyayā /
children.translated_text: with <s>karkoṭī</s>, with alkali and tuber, with <s>citraka</s>, and with <s>gṛhakanyā</s> —

children.text: ekenāpyatha saṃmardyo yāmamekaṃ tu pāradaḥ // GRhtCM_2.5-6:20 //
children.translated_text: with even one of these, the mercury should be ground for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours). (GRhtCM 2.5-6:20)

children.text: kiṃnarayantram ādāya hy oṣadhyā pepayettapam /
children.translated_text: Taking a <s>kiṃnara</s> apparatus, one should dissolve [the mercury] heated with the medicine.

children.text: navatārayutaṃ sūtaṃ yantramadhyagataṃ nyaset // GRhtCM_2.5-6:21 //
children.translated_text: One should place the mercury combined with <s>navatāra</s> within the apparatus. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:21)

children.text: dadyād rasopari śarāvaṃ saṃdhipepaṃ dṛḍhaṃ mṛdā /
children.translated_text: One should place a saucer over the mercury, seal the joint firmly with clay,

children.text: pavaṇena ca sampūrya dvāraṃ saṃrudhya yatnataḥ // GRhtCM_2.5-6:22 //
children.translated_text: fill [the apparatus] with salt, and carefully close the opening. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:22)

children.text: cuhpikopari saṃsthāpya dīptāgniṃ jvāpayet sudhīḥ /
children.translated_text: Placing it upon a <s>culhikā</s> (stove), the wise one should kindle a bright fire.

children.text: yāmaikena taduttārya kartavyaḥ śītapo rasaḥ // GRhtCM_2.5-6:23 //
children.translated_text: After one <s>yāma</s>, removing it, the mercury should be cooled. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:23)

children.text: yantrāduddhṛtya yatnena sūtamutthāpya mūrchitam /
children.translated_text: Carefully extracting [it] from the apparatus, having raised and stupefied the mercury —

children.text: amūrchitas tadā deyaḥ kapāṃśaṃ mūrchite rasaḥ // GRhtCM_2.5-6:24 //
children.translated_text: if unstupefied, one should give a portion [more of medicine] to the stupefied mercury. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:24)

children.text:
sindhūtthaṭaṅkaṇābhyāṃ ca mardayen madhusaṃyutaṃ dopāyantre tataḥ svedyaḥ
                            kṣārāmpapavaṇaiḥ saha /
children.translated_text: With <s>sindūra</s> (red lead) and borax, one should grind [it] combined with honey; then in the <s>dolāyantra</s>, it should be steamed together with alkaline water and salt.

children.text: utthāpya mūrchayetpaścāt vāraṃvāraṃ raseśvaram /
children.translated_text: Having raised [it], one should afterward stupefy the lord of mercury again and again.

children.text: punarutthāpitaṃ kuryād ekaviṃśativārakam // GRhtCM_2.5-6:25 //
children.translated_text: One should perform the raising [process] twenty-one times. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:25)

children.text: iti rasasāre // GRhtCM_2.5-6:26 //
children.translated_text: Thus from the <s>Rasasāra</s>. (GRhtCM 2.5-6:26)

children.text: saṃskāra:: utthāpana
children.translated_text: Process: <s>Utthāpana</s> (Raising/Sublimation)

children.text: amunā vimardanena hi suviśuddho nāgavaṅgaparimuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: By this thorough grinding, [mercury], well-purified and freed from lead and tin,

children.text: sūtaḥ pātanayantre samutthitaḥ kāñjikakvāthāt // GRht_2.7 //
children.translated_text: is raised in the sublimation apparatus from the decoction of <s>kāñjika</s>. (GRht 2.7)

children.text:
sūto nāgavaṅgaparimukto bhavati nāgavaṅgābhyāṃ doṣābhyāṃ virahitaḥ pārado
                            bhavatītyarthaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ san samutthitaḥ san // GRhtCM_2.7:1 //
children.translated_text: Mercury becomes freed from lead and tin — freed from the defects of lead (<s>nāga</s>) and tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) — the mercury becomes [purified] — that is the meaning. Of what qualification? Being raised. (GRhtCM 2.7:1)

children.text:
pātanayantre sthāpīdvayasampuṭe samyagvidhānenotthitaḥ san //
                            GRhtCM_2.7:2 //
children.translated_text: In the sublimation apparatus — in the pair of vessels joined together — properly raised by the prescribed method. (GRhtCM 2.7:2)

children.text:
kasmāt kāñjikaṃ sauvīraṃ pūrvavarṇitaṃ tatkvāthasaṃyogād ityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_2.7:3 //
children.translated_text: From what? <s>Kāñjika</s> is the <s>sauvīra</s> (fermented liquid) described earlier — from the conjunction with its decoction — that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 2.7:3)

children.text: hi niścitam // GRhtCM_2.7:4 //
children.translated_text: 'Hi' [means] certainly. (GRhtCM 2.7:4)

children.text:
amunā virecanena uktaśodhanena sūtaḥ suviśuddho bhavet viśeṣaśuddho
                            bhaved ityutthāpanam // GRhtCM_2.7:5 //
children.translated_text: By this purification — the cleansing as described — the mercury becomes well-purified, specially purified — this is <s>utthāpana</s> (raising). (GRhtCM 2.7:5)

children.text:
anena vidhinā hiṅgupasthasya sūtasyāpi utthāpanaṃ bhavati // GRhtCM_2.7:6
                            //
children.translated_text: By this method, even mercury smeared with asafoetida can be raised. (GRhtCM 2.7:6)

children.text: svedanādikayogena svarūpāpādanaṃ punaḥ // GRhtCM_2.7:7 //
children.translated_text: The restoration to its original form through the procedure of steaming and the like — (GRhtCM 2.7:7)

children.text: tadutthāpanamityuktaṃ mūrchāvyāpattināśanam iti // GRhtCM_2.7:8 //
children.translated_text: that is called <s>utthāpana</s> — it destroys the deterioration caused by <s>mūrchā</s> (swooning). (GRhtCM 2.7:8)

children.text: ut ūrdhvaṃ sthāpanam utthāpanam // GRhtCM_2.7:9 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Ut</s>' means upward; '<s>sthāpana</s>' means placement — [hence] <s>utthāpana</s> (raising up). (GRhtCM 2.7:9)

children.text: atra yantraṃ tu /
children.translated_text: And the apparatus here:

children.text: aṣṭāṅgupaparīṇāhamānāhena daśāṅgupam /
children.translated_text: Eight finger-breadths in circumference, ten finger-breadths in height by measurement,

children.text: caturaṅgupakotsedhaṃ toyādhāro 'ṅgupādadhaḥ // GRhtCM_2.7:10 //
children.translated_text: four finger-breadths in depth — the water-container [is] one finger-breadth below. (GRhtCM 2.7:10)

children.text: adhobhāṇḍe mukhaṃ ca tasya bhāṇḍasyoparivartinaḥ /
children.translated_text: The mouth of the lower vessel — and of that vessel which is on top —

children.text: ṣoḍaśāṅgupavistīrṇapṛṣṭhasyāsye praveśayet // GRhtCM_2.7:11 //
children.translated_text: should be inserted into the opening of [the vessel] whose back is sixteen finger-breadths wide. (GRhtCM 2.7:11)

children.text: pārśvayor mahiṣīkṣīracūrṇamaṇḍūraphāṇitaiḥ // GRhtCM_2.7:12 //
children.translated_text: on both sides, [apply] buffalo milk, powder, frog, and jaggery. (GRhtCM 2.7:12)

children.text: vipipya śoṣayet saṃdhiṃ japādhāre japaṃ kṣipet /
children.translated_text: Having smeared, one should dry the joint; in the water-base, one should place water.

children.text: cuppyām āropayedetat pātanāyantram īritam // GRhtCM_2.7:13 //
children.translated_text: One should mount this upon the <s>cullī</s> (furnace) — this is called the <s>pātana-yantra</s> (distillation apparatus). (GRhtCM 2.7:13)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_2.7:14 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 2.7:14)

children.text: saṃskāra:: pātana:: ūrdhvapātana
children.translated_text: [Section: Processing — Distillation — Upward distillation (<s>ūrdhvapātana</s>)]

children.text: kṛtvā tu śulbapiṣṭiṃ nipātyate nāgavaṅgaśaṅkātaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having made a paste with copper, [mercury] is distilled [to separate it] from the faults of lead (<s>nāga</s>), tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), and their suspicion.

children.text: tasmindoṣān muktvā nipatati śuddhas tathā sūtaḥ // GRht_2.8 //
children.translated_text: Having released those defects therein, the purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury) descends. (GRht 2.8)

children.text:
pañcamoddiṣṭaṃ pātanasaṃskāraṃ spaṣṭayannāha kṛtvetyādi // GRhtCM_2.8:1
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Clarifying the fifth prescribed processing — <s>pātana</s> (distillation) — he says 'having made' and so forth. (GRhtCM 2.8:1)

children.text:
tu punaḥ utthitaṃ sūtaṃ śupbapiṣṭiṃ kṛtvā śupbena tāmreṇa saha
                            tayormepanaṃ yathā syāttathā peṣaṇaṃ vidhāya tasmin pātanayantre
                            nipātyate karmavideti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_2.8:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Tu' means again — the risen <s>sūta</s> (mercury), having made a paste with copper (<s>śulba</s>) — with copper (<s>tāmra</s>) — grinding them together such that they become well mixed — having performed the trituration, it is distilled in that <s>pātana-yantra</s> (distillation apparatus) — 'by one skilled in the procedure' is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 2.8:2)

children.text: kutaḥ nāgavaṅgaśaṅkātaḥ nāgavaṅgadoṣagpānitaḥ // GRhtCM_2.8:3 //
children.translated_text: From what [is it freed]? From the defects of lead (<s>nāga</s>) and tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) — meaning freed from the faults of lead and tin. (GRhtCM 2.8:3)

children.text:
tathā uktavidhānena nipatati sati pātanakarmaṇi kṛte sati śuddhaḥ sūto
                            bhavet // GRhtCM_2.8:4 //
children.translated_text: Thus — by the prescribed method — when distilled, when the distillation process has been performed, the <s>sūta</s> (mercury) becomes purified. (GRhtCM 2.8:4)

children.text:
vāramityanukte granthāntare trisaptaikaviṃśativāraṃ pātanakarmaṇi kṛte
                            sati samyak nāgavaṅgaśaṅkā naśyatīti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_2.8:5 //
children.translated_text: Though the number of times is not stated [in the root text], in other treatises, when the distillation process has been performed twenty-one times (three times seven), the suspicion of lead and tin is thoroughly destroyed — this is the purport. (GRhtCM 2.8:5)

children.text: viśeṣaścātra pātanayantre /
children.translated_text: And the specific [instructions] here regarding the distillation apparatus:

children.text: dvau bhāgau śuddhasūtasya śupbabhāgaikasaṃyutau /
children.translated_text: 'Two parts of purified mercury, combined with one part of copper,

children.text: viṃśāṃśaṃ pavaṇaṃ dattvā piṣṭīkuryācca sundaram // GRhtCM_2.8:6 //
children.translated_text: adding one-twentieth part of salt (<s>lavaṇa</s>), one should make a fine paste.' (GRhtCM 2.8:6)

children.text: aṣṭāṅgupavistīrṇaṃ dairghyeṇa daśāṅgupaṃ tv adhobhāṇḍam /
children.translated_text: 'The lower vessel should be eight <s>aṅgulas</s> wide and ten <s>aṅgulas</s> in length;

children.text: kaṇṭhādadhaḥ samantāccaturaṅgupīkṛtajapādhāram // GRhtCM_2.8:7 //
children.translated_text: from the neck downward, all around, a water-base of four <s>aṅgulas</s> should be made.' (GRhtCM 2.8:7)

children.text: antaḥ praviṣṭatapabhāṇḍavadanaṃ japamagnanijamukhaprāntam /
children.translated_text: 'The mouth of the inner vessel should be inserted into the outer vessel, with the rim of its own mouth immersed in water.

children.text: upariṣṭāc ciṇṭighaṭī deyodaraṣoḍaśāṅgupaviśāpā // GRhtCM_2.8:8 //
children.translated_text: On top, a flat-bottomed pot should be placed, with a belly sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> wide.' (GRhtCM 2.8:8)

children.text: tasminnadhordhvabhāṇḍe nipātitaḥ sakapadoṣanirmuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In that lower-and-upper vessel [apparatus], the distilled [mercury], freed from all defects,

children.text: sutarāṃ bhavati rasendro jīrṇagrāso+api pātyo+asau // GRhtCM_2.8:9 //
children.translated_text: becomes the excellent <s>Rasendra</s> (lord of mercury); even one that has consumed [metals] should be distilled.' (GRhtCM 2.8:9)

children.text: adha ūrdhvaṃ tathā tiryak pātastrividha ucyate /
children.translated_text: 'Downward, upward, and sideways — distillation is said to be threefold.

children.text: yatra tiṣṭhati sūtendro vahnis tatrānyathā japam // GRhtCM_2.8:10 //
children.translated_text: Where <s>Sūtendra</s> (mercury) is placed, the fire is [applied]; otherwise, [apply] water.' (GRhtCM 2.8:10)

children.text: uktauṣadhairmarditapāradasya yantrasthitasyordhvamadhaśca tiryak /
children.translated_text: 'The driving out — upward, downward, and sideways — of mercury that has been ground with the prescribed herbs and placed in the apparatus

children.text:
niryāpanaṃ pātanasaṃjñamuktaṃ vaṅgāhisamparkajakañcukaghnam //
                            GRhtCM_2.8:11 //
children.translated_text: is called <s>pātana-saṃjña</s> (distillation); it destroys the covering produced by contact with tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) and lead (<s>ahi</s>).' (GRhtCM 2.8:11)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_2.8:12 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 2.8:12)

children.text:
ūrdhvapāte rasasyordhvagamanaṃ tatrādhaḥpātre vahniḥ japamūrdhvapātre
                            adhaḥpāte tu rasasyādhastādgamanaṃ bhavati yantraṃ tadeva paraṃ tu
                            agnijapayorvyatyāsaḥ japam atrādhaḥpātre agnirūrdhvapātre tiryakpāte tu
                            rasastiryak patati tatraikapātrapṛṣṭhe japam anyapātrādho vahniḥ //
                            GRhtCM_2.8:13 //
children.translated_text: In upward distillation (<s>ūrdhvapāta</s>), the mercury moves upward — there the fire is in the lower vessel, the water in the upper vessel. In downward distillation (<s>adhaḥpāta</s>), the mercury moves downward — the apparatus is the same, but the fire and water are reversed: water in the lower vessel, fire in the upper vessel. In sideways distillation (<s>tiryakpāta</s>), the mercury falls sideways — there water is on the back of one vessel, fire beneath the other vessel. (GRhtCM 2.8:13)

children.text: pātanayantra
children.translated_text: [Description of the <s>pātana-yantra</s> (distillation apparatus)]

children.text: aṣṭāṅgulavistāraṃ dairghyeṇa daśāṅgulaṃ tv adhobhāṇḍam /
children.translated_text: 'The lower vessel should be eight <s>aṅgulas</s> wide and ten <s>aṅgulas</s> in length;

children.text: kaṇṭhādadhaḥ samucchritaṃ caturaṅgulaṃ kṛtajalādhāram // GRht_2.9 //
children.translated_text: from the neck downward, raised four <s>aṅgulas</s>, with a water-base made.' (GRht 2.9)

children.text: antaḥpraviṣṭatalabhāṇḍavadanaṃ jalamagnanijamukhaprāntā /
children.translated_text: 'The mouth of the inner vessel should enter [the outer], with the rim of its own mouth immersed in water.

children.text: upariṣṭāccipiṭaghaṭī deyodaraṣoḍaśāṅgulaviśālā // GRht_2.10 //
children.translated_text: On top, a flat-bottomed pot should be placed, with a belly sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> wide.' (GRht 2.10)

children.text: tasminn ūrdhvabhāṇḍe nipātitaḥ sakaladoṣanirmuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In that upper vessel, the distilled [mercury], freed from all defects,

children.text: sutarāṃ bhavati rasendro dravye ca rasāyane yogyaḥ // GRht_2.11 //
children.translated_text: becomes the excellent <s>Rasendra</s> (lord of mercury), fit for use in medicinal preparations and <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation).' (GRht 2.11)

children.text: adhaḥpātana
children.translated_text: [Section: Downward distillation (<s>adhaḥpātana</s>)]

children.text: kṛtvā ca naṣṭapiṣṭiṃ triphalāśikhiśigrurājikāpaṭubhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having made a vanishing paste (<s>naṣṭapiṣṭī</s>) [of mercury] with <s>triphalā</s>, <s>śikhi</s> (chitraka), <s>śigru</s> (drumstick), mustard (<s>rājikā</s>), and <s>paṭu</s> (sharp substances),

children.text: saṃlepya cordhvabhāṇḍe dīptaikapalairadhaḥpātyaḥ // GRht_2.12 //
children.translated_text: and applying it in the upper vessel, with blazing fire of one <s>pala</s> [of fuel], it should be distilled downward.' (GRht 2.12)

children.text: athavā dīpakayantre nipātitaḥ sakaladoṣanirmuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Or else, distilled in a lamp apparatus (<s>dīpaka-yantra</s>), [mercury] becomes freed from all defects.'

children.text: tiryakpātana
children.translated_text: [Section: Sideways distillation (<s>tiryakpātana</s>)]

children.text: tiryakpātanavidhinā nipātyaḥ sūtarājastu // GRht_2.13 //
children.translated_text: 'The king of mercury should be distilled by the method of sideways distillation.' (GRht 2.13)

children.text: ślakṣṇīkṛtamabhradalaṃ rasendrayuktaṃ tathāranālena /
children.translated_text: 'Finely powdered mica leaf (<s>abhradala</s>), combined with mercury (<s>rasendra</s>), together with sour gruel (<s>āranāla</s>),

children.text: khalve dattvā mṛditaṃ yāvat tannaṣṭapiṣṭatām eti // GRht_2.14 //
children.translated_text: placed in a mortar and ground until it reaches the state of a vanishing paste (<s>naṣṭapiṣṭī</s>).' (GRht 2.14)

children.text: kuryāt tiryakpātanapātitasūtaṃ krameṇa dṛḍhavahnau /
children.translated_text: 'The mercury distilled by the sideways distillation method should be gradually [heated] over a strong fire.

children.text: saṃsvedya pātyate'sau na patati yāvaddṛḍhaścāgniḥ // GRht_2.15 //
children.translated_text: Having steamed it, it is distilled — it does not fall as long as the fire is strong.' (GRht 2.15)

children.text: nirodhana
children.translated_text: [Section: <s>Nirodhana</s> (Restraining/Arresting)]

children.text: mardanamūrchanapātaiḥ kadarthito bhajati mandavīryatvāt /
children.translated_text: 'Tormented by grinding (<s>mardana</s>), solidification (<s>mūrchana</s>), and distillation (<s>pāta</s>), it becomes weak in potency;

children.text: sṛṣṭyambujair nirodhāllabdhāpyāyo na ṣaṇḍhaḥ syāt // GRht_2.16 //
children.translated_text: through restraint (<s>nirodha</s>) with [substances called] <s>sṛṣṭi</s> (generative fluids) and lotus, having regained its vigour, it should not become impotent (<s>ṣaṇḍha</s>).' (GRht 2.16)

children.text:
ṣaṣṭhoddiṣṭaṃ nirodhanasaṃskāraṃ spaṣṭayannāha mardanetyādi //
                            GRhtCM_2.9-16:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Clarifying the sixth prescribed processing — <s>nirodhana</s> (restraint) — he says 'by grinding' and so forth. (GRhtCM 2.9–16:1)

children.text:
etair mardanamūrchanapātaiḥ saṃskāraviśeṣaṃ kṛtvā mandavīryatvāt
                            kadarthito bhavati // GRhtCM_2.9-16:2 //
children.translated_text: By these — grinding, solidification, and distillation — having undergone these particular processes, [mercury] becomes tormented due to weakness of potency. (GRhtCM 2.9–16:2)

children.text:
kutsitavidhānena kadarthito bhavatītyarthaḥ punaḥ sūtaḥ sṛṣṭyambujaiḥ
                            saha mardanānantaraṃ nirodhāt mūṣādvayasampuṭe kūpikāyāṃ vā nirodhāt
                            rundhanāt pabdhāpyāyaḥ prāptabapaḥ san na ṣaṇḍhaḥ syāt na śukrarahito
                            bhavati // GRhtCM_2.9-16:3 //
children.translated_text: Tormented by debased procedure — this is the meaning. Then <s>sūta</s> (mercury), after grinding with the <s>sṛṣṭi</s> (generative) substances and lotus, through restraint (<s>nirodha</s>) — confinement in a pair of sealed crucibles (<s>mūṣā</s>) or in a <s>kūpikā</s> (glass flask) — having regained vigour, having obtained strength, it should not become impotent, meaning it should not become devoid of potency. (GRhtCM 2.9–16:3)

children.text:
sṛṣṭiḥ mūtraśukraśoṇitarūpā ambujaṃ pavaṇaṃ saindhavaṃ kamapam iti mandāḥ
                            // GRhtCM_2.9-16:4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sṛṣṭi</s> (generative substances) are in the form of urine, semen, and blood; <s>ambuja</s> is salt (<s>lavaṇa</s>), rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>), and camphor (<s>kamala</s>) — these are the gentle [substances]. (GRhtCM 2.9–16:4)

children.text: sṛṣṭiryathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Sṛṣṭi</s> (generative substances) as follows:

children.text: go+ajāvinaranārīṇāṃ mūtraṃ śukraṃ ca śoṇitam /
children.translated_text: 'The urine, semen, and blood of cows, goats, sheep, men, and women —

children.text: sṛṣṭireṣā samākhyātā ṣaṇḍhadoṣavināśinī /
children.translated_text: this is called <s>sṛṣṭi</s> (generative substances), which destroys the defect of impotence.'

children.text: iti śaktyavatārāt // GRhtCM_2.9-16:5 //
children.translated_text: Thus from the <s>Śaktyavatāra</s>. (GRhtCM 2.9–16:5)

children.text: yantraṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: The apparatus is as follows:

children.text: raktasaindhavakhoṭena mūṣādvaṃdvaṃ prakappayet /
children.translated_text: 'One should prepare a pair of crucibles (<s>mūṣā-dvandva</s>) with a lump of red rock salt.

children.text: tatsampuṭe rasaṃ kṣiptvā navasāraṃ sanimbukam // GRhtCM_2.9-16:6 //
children.translated_text: In their sealed container, one should place mercury along with <s>navasāra</s> (sal ammoniac) and neem.' (GRhtCM 2.9–16:6)

children.text: sampuṭasya prayatnena pepayet saṃdhimuttamam /
children.translated_text: 'One should carefully seal the joint of the sealed container with excellent [clay].

children.text: vajramṛtsnāṃ samādāya veṣṭayettatprayatnataḥ // GRhtCM_2.9-16:7 //
children.translated_text: Taking adamantine clay (<s>vajramṛtsnā</s>), one should wrap it carefully.' (GRhtCM 2.9–16:7)

children.text: chāyāśuṣkaṃ ca tatkṛtvā bhūgarte sthāpayettataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having dried it in the shade, one should then place it in a pit in the ground.

children.text: aṣṭāṅgupapramāṇena mūṣordhvaṃ tatra pūraṇam // GRhtCM_2.9-16:8 //
children.translated_text: Above the crucible, to a height of eight <s>aṅgulas</s>, fill [with fuel].' (GRhtCM 2.9–16:8)

children.text: trisaptadinaparyantaṃ karīṣāgniṃ ca kārayet /
children.translated_text: 'For a period of twenty-one days, one should maintain a dung-fire (<s>karīṣāgni</s>).

children.text: dine dine prakartavyā mūṣā saindhavanūtanā // GRhtCM_2.9-16:9 //
children.translated_text: Each day, a new crucible [lined] with rock salt should be prepared.' (GRhtCM 2.9–16:9)

children.text: svedayet tat prayatnena bhūgarbhe sthāpayettataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'One should steam it carefully and then place it in the earth-pit.

children.text: athavā kūpikāmadhye sūtaṃ saindhavasaṃyutam // GRhtCM_2.9-16:10 //
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the mercury combined with rock salt [should be placed] in the middle of a <s>kūpikā</s> (glass flask).' (GRhtCM 2.9–16:10)

children.text: bhūgarbhe ca tataḥ sthāpyam ekaviṃśaddināvadhi /
children.translated_text: 'It should be placed in the earth-pit for a period of twenty-one days.

children.text: ayaṃ nirodhako nāmnā mahāmukhakaro rase // GRhtCM_2.9-16:11 //
children.translated_text: This [process] called <s>nirodhaka</s> (restrainer) makes the mercury greatly potent.' (GRhtCM 2.9–16:11)
Thus. (GRhtCM 2.9–16:12)

children.text: 7 niyamana
children.translated_text: [Section 7: <s>Niyamana</s> (Controlling/Regulating)]

children.text: iti labdhavīryaḥ samyak capalo+asau saṃniyamyate tadanu /
children.translated_text: 'Thus, having duly regained its potency, this restless [mercury] is then controlled.

children.text: phaṇinayanāmbujamārkavakarkoṭīciñcikāsvedāt // GRht_2.17 //
children.translated_text: By steaming with betel leaf (<s>phaṇi</s>), garlic (<s>nayanāmbuja</s>), <s>mārkava</s> (bhṛṅgarāja), <s>karkoṭī</s>, and tamarind (<s>ciñcikā</s>).' (GRht 2.17)

children.text: saptamoddiṣṭasaṃskāraṃ spaṣṭayannāha itītyādi // GRhtCM_2.17:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Clarifying the seventh prescribed processing, he says 'thus' and so forth. (GRhtCM 2.17:1)

children.text:
iti pūrvoktavidhānena yantraṇādinā tadanu rodhanānantaram asau
                            capapaścañcapo raso niyamyate karmavidā saṃniyamanaṃ kriyate //
                            GRhtCM_2.17:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Thus' — by the previously described method, through confinement (<s>yantraṇā</s>) and the like — 'then' — after the restraining — this restless, agitated mercury is controlled by one skilled in the procedure — the process of regulation is performed. (GRhtCM 2.17:2)

children.text:
kasmāt phaṇīpaśunāmbujamārkavakarkoṭīciñcikāsvedāt phaṇī tāmbūpaṃ paśunaṃ
                            rasonaḥ ambujaṃ pavaṇaṃ mārkavaḥ bhṛṅgarājaḥ karkoṭīti pratītā vandhyā
                            ciñcikā ampikā etābhiḥ saha yaḥ svedaḥ yantre agnitāpaḥ tasmāt //
                            GRhtCM_2.17:3 //
children.translated_text: By what means? By steaming with betel leaf (<s>phaṇī</s>, i.e. <s>tāmbūla</s>), garlic (<s>paśuna</s>, i.e. <s>rasona</s>), salt (<s>ambuja</s>, i.e. <s>lavaṇa</s>), <s>mārkava</s> (i.e. <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>), <s>karkoṭī</s> (which is well-known, also called 'barren'), and tamarind (<s>ciñcikā</s>, i.e. <s>amlikā</s>) — the steaming with these in an apparatus, i.e. heating with fire — by that means. (GRhtCM 2.17:3)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ samyak pabdhavīryaḥ prāptabapo vīryavān rasaḥ
                            capapatvanivṛttaye niyamyata ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_2.17:4 //
children.translated_text: What quality does it possess? Having duly regained its potency — having obtained strength, the potent mercury — [it is controlled] for the purpose of removing its restlessness — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 2.17:4)

children.text: viśeṣaścātra kācakūpīṃ mṛdā pipya raso madhye vimucyate /
children.translated_text: And the specific [instructions] here: 'A glass flask (<s>kācakūpī</s>) should be coated with clay; mercury should be released inside.

children.text: kapāṃśaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ dattvā madhye kiṃcit pradīyate // GRhtCM_2.17:5 //
children.translated_text: Adding one-quarter part of borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), a little should be placed in the middle.' (GRhtCM 2.17:5)

children.text: dvāramudrā prakartavyā vajramṛttikayā dṛḍhā /
children.translated_text: 'The door-seal should be made firm with adamantine clay (<s>vajramṛttikā</s>).

children.text: bhūgarbhe kūpikāṃ sthāpya sitayā garbhapūraṇam // GRhtCM_2.17:6 //
children.translated_text: Having placed the flask in an earth-pit, fill the interior with white [substance].' (GRhtCM 2.17:6)

children.text: karīṣāgniḥ prakartavya ekaviṃśaddināvadhi /
children.translated_text: 'A dung-fire (<s>karīṣāgni</s>) should be maintained for a period of twenty-one days.

children.text: ayaṃ niyāmako nāma vahnipratyantakārakaḥ // GRhtCM_2.17:7 //
