children.translated_text: This [process] called <s>niyāmaka</s> (regulator) counteracts the [destructive action of] fire.' (GRhtCM 2.17:7)

children.text: rodhanāppabdhavīryasya capapatvanivṛttaye /
children.translated_text: 'For the purpose of removing the restlessness of [mercury] that has regained its potency through restraint,

children.text: kriyate yo rasasvedaḥ proktaṃ niyamanaṃ hi tat // GRhtCM_2.17:8 //
children.translated_text: the steaming of mercury that is performed — that indeed is called <s>niyamana</s> (regulation).' (GRhtCM 2.17:8)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_2.17:9 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 2.17:9)

children.text: yantrapakṣaṇaṃ tu /
children.translated_text: The definition of the apparatus:

children.text: catuḥprasthajapādhāraṃ caturaṅgupakānanam /
children.translated_text: 'Having a water-base of four <s>prasthas</s>, with a neck of four <s>aṅgulas</s> —

children.text:
ghaṭayantramidaṃ proktaṃ tadāpyāyanakaṃ smṛtam iti // GRhtCM_2.17:10
                            //
children.translated_text: this pot-apparatus is described; it is known as the revitalizer (<s>āpyāyanaka</s>).' (GRhtCM 2.17:10)

children.text: 8 dīpana
children.translated_text: [Section 8: <s>Dīpana</s> (Kindling/Stimulating the appetite)]

children.text: bhūkhagaṭaṅkaṇamaricair lavaṇāsurīśigrukāñjikais tridinam /
children.translated_text: 'With earth (<s>bhū</s>), <s>khaga</s> (kāsīsa/green vitriol), borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), pepper (<s>marica</s>), salt (<s>lavaṇa</s>), mustard (<s>āsurī</s>), drumstick (<s>śigru</s>), and sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>), for three days —

children.text: svedena dīpito+asau grāsārthī jāyate sūtaḥ // GRht_2.18 //
children.translated_text: by steaming, the <s>sūta</s> (mercury) is kindled; [it then] becomes desirous of food (<s>grāsārthī</s>).' (GRht 2.18)

children.text:
aṣṭamoddiṣṭasya dīpanasaṃskārasya vidhiṃ spaṣṭayannāha bhūkhagetyādi //
                            GRhtCM_2.18:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Clarifying the procedure of the eighth prescribed processing — <s>dīpana</s> (kindling) — he says 'with earth' and so forth. (GRhtCM 2.18:1)

children.text:
asau pūrvasaṃskṛtarasa etair auṣadhais tridinaṃ nirantaraṃ yathā syāt
                            tathā svedena dīpitaḥ kṣutpīḍitaḥ san grāsārthī kavapābhipāṣī jāyate //
                            GRhtCM_2.18:2 //
children.translated_text: This previously processed mercury, [steamed] with these herbs for three days continuously — such that [steaming is] uninterrupted — being kindled (<s>dīpita</s>) by steaming, pressed by hunger, becomes desirous of a morsel (<s>grāsārthī</s>), eager to consume a bolus. (GRhtCM 2.18:2)

children.text:
etair oṣadhaiḥ bhūkhagaṭaṅkaṇamaricaiḥ na kevapam etaiḥ punar
                            pavaṇāsurīśigrukāñjikaiḥ // GRhtCM_2.18:3 //
children.translated_text: With these herbs — earth, <s>khaga</s>, borax, and pepper — not only with these, but also with salt, mustard, drumstick, and sour gruel. (GRhtCM 2.18:3)

children.text:
bhūḥ tuvarī khagaḥ kāsīsaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ maricam ūṣaṇam etaiḥ //
                            GRhtCM_2.18:4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bhū</s> (earth) means <s>tuvarī</s>; <s>khaga</s> means <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol); <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is borax; <s>marica</s> is <s>ūṣaṇa</s> (pepper) — with these. (GRhtCM 2.18:4)

children.text:
punaḥ pavaṇaṃ saindhavam āsurī rājikā śigruḥ saubhāñjanaṃ vṛkṣaviśeṣaḥ
                            kāñjikaṃ pūrvoktam ampībhūtam etaiśceti // GRhtCM_2.18:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore: <s>lavaṇa</s> is rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>); <s>āsurī</s> is mustard (<s>rājikā</s>); <s>śigru</s> is the drumstick tree (<s>saubhāñjana</s>), a particular tree; <s>kāñjika</s> is as previously described, in a fermented liquid state — with these. (GRhtCM 2.18:5)

children.text: viśeṣaścātra /
children.translated_text: And the specific [instructions] here:

children.text: svedanaṃ rasarājasya kṣārāmpaviṣamadyakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The steaming of the king of mercury [is done] with alkali (<s>kṣāra</s>), sour liquid (<s>amla</s>), poison (<s>viṣa</s>), and spirits (<s>madyaka</s>).

children.text: bījapūraṃ samādāya vṛntamutsṛjya kārayet // GRhtCM_2.18:6 //
children.translated_text: Taking a citron (<s>bījapūra</s>), removing the stalk, one should prepare [the vessel].' (GRhtCM 2.18:6)

children.text: tasya madhye kṣipetsūtaṃ kapāṃśakṣārasaṃyutaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'Inside it, one should place mercury combined with one-quarter part of alkali.

children.text: dvāraṃ nirudhya yatnena vastramadhye nibandhayet // GRhtCM_2.18:7 //
children.translated_text: Closing the opening carefully, one should bind it in a cloth.' (GRhtCM 2.18:7)

children.text: dopāsvedaḥ prakartavya ekaviṃśaddināvadhi /
children.translated_text: '<s>Dolā-sveda</s> (swing-steaming) should be performed for twenty-one days.

children.text: dine dine prakartavyaṃ nūtanaṃ bījapūrakam // GRhtCM_2.18:8 //
children.translated_text: Each day, a fresh citron should be used.' (GRhtCM 2.18:8)

children.text: pepihāno hi dhātūṃśca pīḍyamāno bubhukṣayā /
children.translated_text: 'Licking [i.e., desiring] metals, tormented by hunger,

children.text: amunaiva prakartavyaṃ rasarājasya dīpanam // GRhtCM_2.18:9 //
children.translated_text: by this very [method] should the kindling (<s>dīpana</s>) of the king of mercury be performed.' (GRhtCM 2.18:9)

children.text: tryahaṃ saptadinaṃ vātha caturdaśaikaviṃśatim /
children.translated_text: 'Three days, seven days, or fourteen [days], or twenty-one —

children.text: saṃskāraḥ sūtarāje tu kramāt kramataraṃ varam // GRhtCM_2.18:10 //
children.translated_text: the processing of the king of mercury — progressively better with each increment.' (GRhtCM 2.18:10)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_2.18:11 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 2.18:11)

children.text: cāraṇa
children.translated_text: [Section: <s>Cāraṇā</s> (Transmutation/Driving)]

children.text: iti dīpito viśuddhaḥ pracalitavidyullatāsahasrābhaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Thus, the kindled and purified king of mercury, [shining] like a thousand flashing lightning bolts,

children.text: bhavati yadā rasarājaś cāryo satvādi tadā bījam // GRht_2.19 //
children.translated_text: when it becomes [fit for] driving (<s>cāraṇā</s>) with essences (<s>satva</s>) and the like, then [it has become] the seed [of transmutation].' (GRht 2.19)

children.text:
kṛtāṣṭasaṃskārasya pāradasya saṃskārāntarasiddhāṃ parīkṣām āha itītyādi
                            // GRhtCM_2.19:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Having described the eightfold processing of mercury, he now states the test achieved through further processing, with 'thus' and so forth. (GRhtCM 2.19:1)

children.text:
iti pūrvoktaprakāreṇa rasarājo dīpitaḥ san kṣudutpīḍitaḥ san viśuddho
                            bhavati // GRhtCM_2.19:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus, the king of <s>rasas</s> (mercury), having been kindled (<s>dīpita</s>) in the aforementioned manner, being tormented by hunger (<s>kṣudh</s>), becomes purified. (GRhtCM 2.19:2)

children.text:
yadīdṛśo bhavati rasarājastadā cāryaḥ cāraṇakarma kāryam // GRhtCM_2.19:3
                            //
children.translated_text: When the king of <s>rasas</s> becomes like this, then transmutation (<s>cāraṇā</s>) — the work of transmutation — should be performed. (GRhtCM 2.19:3)

children.text:
kīdṛk pracapitavidyuppatāsahasrābhaḥ prakarṣeṇa capatyaś capanaśīpā yā
                            vidyutastāsāṃ sahasrasyeva bhā dīptir yasya sa tathoktaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_2.19:4 //
children.translated_text: Of what kind? Blazing like thousands of flashing lightning bolts — that which moves intensely, having a restless nature — whose radiance is like that of a thousand lightning flashes — such is described. (GRhtCM 2.19:4)

children.text:
kiṃ kṛtvā cāryaḥ idamagre vakṣyamāṇaṃ kiṃcit
                            dhātūparasamahārasaratnasaṃjñakaṃ dvitīyaṃ rasarājasambandhinaṃ dattvā
                            saṃyojyetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_2.19:5 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? Being fit for transmutation — having given, meaning having combined, some second [substance] related to the king of <s>rasas</s>, to be described hereafter, namely metals, <s>uparasas</s>, <s>mahārasas</s>, and gems. (GRhtCM 2.19:5)

children.text: cāraṇa:: samukha, nirmukha
children.translated_text: [Section on] transmutation: with mouth (<s>samukha</s>) and without mouth (<s>nirmukha</s>)

children.text: pītakriyāsu pītaṃ śvetaṃ tārakriyāsu mukham ādau /
children.translated_text: In operations involving gold, gold [as mouth]; in silver operations, silver should be given as the mouth first.

children.text: deyaṃ khalve ghṛṣṭo divyauṣadhibhiḥ sa nirmukhaś carati // GRht_2.20 //
children.translated_text: Rubbed in a mortar with divine herbs, it transmutes without mouth. (GRht 2.20)

children.text:
iti paramahaṃsaparivrājakācāryaśrīmadgovindabhagavatpādaviracite
                                rasahṛdayatantre rasaśodhanātmako dvitīyo+avabodhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter (<s>avabodha</s>), dealing with the purification of mercury (<s>rasaśodhana</s>), in the <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> composed by the revered <s>Govindabhagavatpāda</s>, the supreme ascetic (<s>paramahaṃsa</s>) and wandering renunciant (<s>parivrājakācārya</s>).

children.text:
kiṃ dvitīyamityāśaṅkya taṃ spaṣṭayannāha pītetyādi // GRhtCM_2.20:1
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Anticipating the question 'What is the second [substance]?', he clarifies it with 'in [operations involving] gold' and so forth. (GRhtCM 2.20:1)

children.text:
ādau prathamaṃ mukhaṃ vidheyam ityadhyāhāraḥ pāradasya mukhaṃ
                            kāryamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_2.20:2 //
children.translated_text: First, a 'mouth' (<s>mukha</s>) should be prepared — this is to be supplied. The meaning is: the mouth of mercury should be made. (GRhtCM 2.20:2)

children.text:
tataścetpītakriyā bhavanti svarṇasambandhīni kāryāṇi bhavanti tadā pītaṃ
                            svarṇaṃ deyam // GRhtCM_2.20:3 //
children.translated_text: Then, if gold operations are [to be performed] — if tasks related to gold are to be done — then gold should be given [as the mouth]. (GRhtCM 2.20:3)

children.text: śvetakriyāsu śvetaṃ deyaṃ śvetaṃ tāram ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_2.20:4 //
children.translated_text: In silver operations, silver should be given — silver means <s>tāra</s> (silver), is the meaning. (GRhtCM 2.20:4)

children.text:
svarṇatārādikaṃ khapve dattaṃ kṛtamukho rasaścarati // GRhtCM_2.20:5
                            //
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, and the like, having been placed in the mortar, mercury with its mouth prepared transmutes. (GRhtCM 2.20:5)

children.text:
punarnirmukho rasaḥ akṛtamukho rasaḥ khapve ghṛṣṭo gharṣitaḥ san
                            pūrvoktaṃ carati bhakṣayati // GRhtCM_2.20:6 //
children.translated_text: Again, mercury without a mouth — mercury whose mouth has not been prepared — being rubbed, ground in the mortar, transmutes as described earlier — it consumes [the metals]. (GRhtCM 2.20:6)

children.text: kābhiḥ saha divyauṣadhībhir vakṣyamāṇābhiḥ saha // GRhtCM_2.20:7 //
children.translated_text: With what? With divine herbs — those to be described hereafter. (GRhtCM 2.20:7)

children.text: yathā padyam /
children.translated_text: As the verse [states]:

children.text: sāsyo rasaḥ syātpaṭuśigrututthaiḥ sarājikair vyoṣaṇakais trirātram /
children.translated_text: Mercury becomes mouthed (<s>sāsya</s>) [when processed] with <s>paṭu</s> (sharp [substances]), <s>śigru</s> (drumstick), and <s>tuttha</s> (blue vitriol), combined with <s>rājikā</s> (mustard) and <s>vyoṣaṇaka</s> (the three pungent spices), for three nights;

children.text:
piṣṭastataḥ svinnatanuḥ suvarṇamukhānayaṃ khādati sarvadhātūn //
                            GRhtCM_2.20:8 //
children.translated_text: ground thus, with its body heated (<s>svinna</s>), it devours gold-mouthed and iron — [it devours] all metals. (GRhtCM 2.20:8)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_2.20:9 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 2.20:9)

children.text: nirmukhaśca ampavargeṇa saṃyuktaṃ yathāpābhena mardayet /
children.translated_text: And without mouth: combined with the <s>amla</s>-group (acidic substances), one should grind [mercury] with the appropriate [substance];

children.text: abhrakādīṃśca carate sūtako vāsanāmukhaḥ // GRhtCM_2.20:10 //
children.translated_text: mercury, with its mouth [formed by] impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), transmutes mica and the rest. (GRhtCM 2.20:10)

children.text: iyanmānasya sūtasya bhojyadravyātmikā mitiḥ /
children.translated_text: For this measure of mercury, the quantity of the substance to be consumed is this measure —

children.text: iyatītyucyate yāsau grāsamānamitīritam // GRhtCM_2.20:11 //
children.translated_text: that quantity which is specified is called the <s>grāsamāna</s> (bolus-measure). (GRhtCM 2.20:11)

children.text: iti paribhāṣā // GRhtCM_2.20:12 //
children.translated_text: This is the definition (<s>paribhāṣā</s>). (GRhtCM 2.20:12)

children.text:
iti
                            śrīmatkurapakupapayodhisudhākaramiśramaheśātmajacaturbhujamiśraviracitāyāṃ
                            mugdhāvabodhinyāṃ rasahṛdayaṭīkāyāṃ rasaśodhanātmako dvitīyo+avabodhaḥ
                            // GRhtCM_2.20:13 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter (<s>avabodha</s>), dealing with the purification of mercury, in the <s>Mugdhāvabodhini</s> commentary on the <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s>, composed by <s>Caturbhujamiśra</s>, son of <s>Maheśa</s> [who was the] moon of the ocean of the renowned <s>Kurapaku</s> [family].

children.text: ghanarahitabījacāraṇasamprāptadalādilābhakṛtakṛtyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who, without mica, through seed-transmutation (<s>bījacāraṇā</s>), having obtained [mere] leaf and the like, consider themselves accomplished —

children.text: kṛpaṇāḥ prāpya samudraṃ varāṭikālābhasaṃtuṣṭāḥ // GRht_3.1 //
children.translated_text: such wretched ones, having reached the ocean, are content with cowrie shells. (GRht 3.1)

children.text: sudhākaragrāsasattvaṃ padmākarasukhāvaham /
children.translated_text: The ability of the moon to consume (<s>grāsa</s>), [its] essence (<s>sattva</s>), and [its capacity to bring] happiness like a lotus-lake,

children.text: tathā vibhūtayaścāsya sajjanānandakārakāḥ // GRhtCM_3.1:1 //
children.translated_text: and likewise its powers (<s>vibhūtis</s>) which delight good people — (GRhtCM 3.1:1)

children.text:
anena padyena granthasya guṇādhikyaṃ saṃmatatvaṃ ca varṇayannāha
                            ghanetyādi // GRhtCM_3.1:2 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] With this verse, he praises the superior quality and the authoritative status of the treatise, saying 'without mica' and so forth. (GRhtCM 3.1:2)

children.text: ye evaṃvidhāḥ puruṣāste kṛpaṇā eva // GRhtCM_3.1:3 //
children.translated_text: Those who are of this kind are indeed wretched. (GRhtCM 3.1:3)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ ghanarahitabījacāraṇasamprāptadapādidravyakṛtakṛtyāḥ
                            ghanenābhrakeṇa rahitaṃ varjitaṃ yad bījacāraṇam anyadhātvādīnāṃ
                            bījakavapanaṃ tena yatprāptaṃ dapādidravyaṃ
                            pattrarañjanavarṇavṛddhitārakṛṣṭī mepāpakādikaṃ vastu tena ye kṛtakṛtyāḥ
                            pūrṇāḥ ātmānaṃ manyante ityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_3.1:4 //
children.translated_text: Of what kind? Those who consider themselves accomplished through substances such as leaf (<s>dala</s>) obtained by seed-transmutation without mica — <s>bījacāraṇā</s> means sowing seeds of other metals and the like, devoid of mica (<s>abhraka</s>); the substances obtained thereby — leaf (<s>pattra</s>), coloring (<s>rañjana</s>), color-enhancement (<s>varṇavṛddhi</s>), silver-extraction (<s>tārakṛṣṭi</s>), <s>melāpaka</s>, and the like — those who are fulfilled by these, who consider themselves complete — this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 3.1:4)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ kṛpaṇāḥ samudraṃ prāpya ratnākaraṃ pabdhvā
                            varāṭikāpābhasaṃtuṣṭāḥ kapardikāpābhena saṃtuṣṭiṃ prāptaḥ
                            daridrabhāvāditi bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_3.1:5 //
children.translated_text: What kind of wretched ones? Having reached the ocean — having found the jewel-mine — they are content with cowrie-shell-like [trifles]; having attained satisfaction with cowrie-shell-like [things] — out of a state of poverty, is the implication. (GRhtCM 3.1:5)

children.text:
tathā evaṃvidhāḥ kṛpaṇā idaṃ śāstraṃ ratnākararūpaṃ bahuratnaṃ prāpya
                            dapādidravyeṇa kṛtakṛtyāḥ // GRhtCM_3.1:6 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, such wretched ones, having obtained this treatise which is in the form of a jewel-mine containing many gems, consider themselves accomplished with [mere] leaf and other substances. (GRhtCM 3.1:6)

children.text:
śāstrasamudrayor guṇaratnaiḥ sāmyaṃ varāṭikādapādirdravyayoḥ sāmyaṃ
                            tucchatayā yata ubhāv api nikṛṣṭāv eva // GRhtCM_3.1:7 //
children.translated_text: The treatise and the ocean are similar by virtue of their qualities-as-gems. Cowrie shells and leaf-substances are similar in their worthlessness — because both are indeed inferior. (GRhtCM 3.1:7)

Because this treatise bestows much — being capable of bestowing ring-transmutation (<s>mudrikāvedha</s>), touch-transmutation (<s>sparśavedha</s>), smoke-transmutation (<s>dhūmavedha</s>), sound-transmutation (<s>śabdavedha</s>), <s>dhāmyavedha</s>, and base-metal transmutation (<s>dhātuvedha</s>). (GRhtCM 3.1:8)

children.text: anye punarmahānto lakṣmīkarirājakaustubhādīni /
children.translated_text: Others, however, who are great — having disdained <s>Lakṣmī</s> (wealth), elephants, kings, <s>Kaustubha</s> gems, and the like —

children.text: avadhīrya labdhavantaḥ parāmṛtaṃ cāmarā jātāḥ // GRht_3.2 //
children.translated_text: have obtained the supreme immortality and have become immortal. (GRht 3.2)

children.text:
punaratra granthe guṇādhikyaśataṃ ca varṇayannāhānye ityādi //
                            GRhtCM_3.2:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Again, to describe the hundredfold superior qualities of this treatise, he says 'others' and so forth. (GRhtCM 3.2:1)

children.text: punar ity aprathamaviśeṣaṇayor iti prasādaḥ // GRhtCM_3.2:2 //
children.translated_text: The word 'again' (<s>punar</s>) is used as a qualifier — this is [for] clarity. (GRhtCM 3.2:2)

children.text: atra punarviśeṣaṇe // GRhtCM_3.2:3 //
children.translated_text: Here, 'again' is used as a qualifier. (GRhtCM 3.2:3)

children.text: anye pūrvebhyo mahānto vartante // GRhtCM_3.2:4 //
children.translated_text: Others — great ones, unlike the previous [wretched ones] — exist. (GRhtCM 3.2:4)

children.text:
kiṃ kurvantaḥ parāmṛtaṃ pabdhavantaḥ santa amarā jātā maraṇarahitā
                            jīvanmuktā jātā ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.2:5 //
children.translated_text: What have they done? Having obtained the supreme immortality (<s>parāmṛta</s>), they have become immortal — free from death, <s>jīvanmuktas</s> (liberated while living) — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 3.2:5)

children.text: paraṃ ca tadamṛtaṃ ceti samāsaḥ mokṣam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.2:6 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Para</s>' (supreme) and '<s>amṛta</s>' (immortality) [combine as] a compound — meaning liberation. (GRhtCM 3.2:6)

children.text:
kiṃ kṛtvā pakṣmīkarirājakaustubhādīni avadhīrya avahepanaṃ vidhāya
                            pakṣmīrharipriyā karirāja airāvata indravāraṇaḥ kaustubho harermaṇiḥ
                            ityādīni caturdaśaratnāni // GRhtCM_3.2:7 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? Having disdained — having shown contempt for — <s>Lakṣmī</s> (the beloved of <s>Hari</s>/Viṣṇu), <s>Karirāja</s> (<s>Airāvata</s>, <s>Indra's</s> elephant), <s>Kaustubha</s> (<s>Hari's</s> jewel), and the like — the fourteen [divine] gems. (GRhtCM 3.2:7)

children.text:
satām ayameva svabhāvaḥ daridrāṇāṃ kṛpaṇānāṃ pūrvavat // GRhtCM_3.2:8
                            //
children.translated_text: This is indeed the nature of the noble; of the poor and wretched, [it is] as before. (GRhtCM 3.2:8)

children.text: ata evaitacchāstraṃ kṛpaṇamahatāṃ nikaṣarūpam // GRhtCM_3.2:9 //
children.translated_text: Hence, this treatise serves as a touchstone for [distinguishing] the wretched and the great. (GRhtCM 3.2:9)

children.text: kṣārauṣadhipaṭvamlaiḥ kṣudbodho rāgabandhane svedāt /
children.translated_text: Through alkalis, herbs, sharp [substances], and acids, the arousal of hunger [in mercury occurs]; in coloring and binding, through heating (<s>sveda</s>),

children.text: na punaḥ pakṣacchedo dravatvaṃ vā vinā gaganam // GRht_3.3 //
children.translated_text: but clipping of wings and fluidity — [these are] not [possible] without mica (<s>gagana</s>). (GRht 3.3)

children.text:
sarvotkṛṣṭatvena gaganagrāsasādhanam āha kṣāretyādi // GRhtCM_3.3:1
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He speaks of the means for mica-consumption as the most excellent, with 'alkalis' and so forth. (GRhtCM 3.3:1)

children.text: kṣudbodho rasarājasya jāyate iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_3.3:2 //
children.translated_text: The arousal of hunger of the king of <s>rasas</s> (mercury) occurs — this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 3.3:2)

children.text:
kaiḥ kṛtvā kṣārauṣadhipaṭvampaiḥ kṣārauṣadhayo 'himārādayaḥ paṭu
                            saindhavam ampam ampavetasādi etaiḥ kṣudutpattir bhaved ityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_3.3:3 //
children.translated_text: By means of what? By alkalis, herbs, sharp [substances], and acids. Alkaline herbs are <s>ahimāra</s> and the like. <s>Paṭu</s> (sharp) means rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>). <s>Amla</s> (acid) means <s>amlavetasa</s> and the like. By these, the arousal of hunger occurs — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 3.3:3)

children.text: kṣārauṣadhayo yathā /
children.translated_text: The alkaline herbs are as follows:

children.text: ahimāramapāmārge taṇḍupīyakasaṃyutam /
children.translated_text: <s>Ahimāra</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, combined with <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>,

children.text: snuhyarkakaravīraṃ ca pāṅgapīkṣīrakandau // GRhtCM_3.3:4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Snuhī</s> (cactus spurge), <s>arka</s> (milkweed), <s>karavīra</s> (oleander), <s>lāṅgalī</s>, and the milky plants and bulbs. (GRhtCM 3.3:4)

children.text: karkoṭīṃ kañcukīṃ tumbāṃ papāśaṃ cāgnimanthakam /
children.translated_text: <s>Karkoṭī</s>, <s>kañcukī</s>, <s>tumbā</s> (bottle gourd), <s>palāśa</s> (flame of the forest), and <s>agnimanthaka</s> (fire-churner),

children.text: karīraṃ citrakaṃ śigruṃ varuṇaṃ vetasaṃ vaṭam // GRhtCM_3.3:5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Karīra</s>, <s>citraka</s> (leadwort), <s>śigru</s> (drumstick), <s>varuṇa</s>, <s>vetasa</s> (willow), and <s>vaṭa</s> (banyan). (GRhtCM 3.3:5)

children.text: paṭopyarjunakūṣmāṇḍakadapīvajrakandakam /
children.translated_text: <s>Paṭola</s>, <s>arjuna</s>, <s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s> (pumpkin), <s>kadalī</s> (plantain), and <s>vajrakanda</s>,

children.text: aśvatthaṃ sūraṇaṃ jāpīṃ dahet kandān anekaśaḥ // GRhtCM_3.3:6 //
children.translated_text: <s>Aśvattha</s> (sacred fig), <s>sūraṇa</s> (elephant yam), <s>jālī</s> — one should burn the bulbs of these in various ways. (GRhtCM 3.3:6)

children.text: antardhūmena sarvāṃśca devadāpīṃ dahettathā /
children.translated_text: And <s>devadālī</s> — one should burn with internal smoke;

children.text: auṣadhikṣāranāmāsau gaṇastu parikīrtitaḥ // GRhtCM_3.3:7 //
children.translated_text: this group has been proclaimed as the herbal alkalis (<s>auṣadhikṣāra</s>). (GRhtCM 3.3:7)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_3.3:8 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 3.3:8)

children.text: ampaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: The acids are as follows:

children.text: ampavetasajambīraṃ pakucaṃ bījapūrakam /
children.translated_text: <s>Amlavetasa</s>, <s>jambīra</s> (citron), <s>lakuca</s>, <s>bījapūra</s> (citrus),

children.text: cāṅgerī caṇakāmpaṃ ca nāraṅgaṃ tittiḍī tathā // GRhtCM_3.3:9 //
children.translated_text: <s>Cāṅgerī</s> (sorrel), <s>caṇakāmla</s> (sour chickpea water), <s>nāraṅga</s> (orange), and <s>tittiḍī</s>. (GRhtCM 3.3:9)

children.text: ambaṣṭhā karamardaśca kapitthaḥ karaṇādikaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Ambaṣṭhā</s>, <s>karamarda</s> (karonda), <s>kapittha</s> (wood apple), <s>karaṇa</s>, and the like;

children.text: pañcāmpasaṃyuto vā syādampavargaḥ prakīrtitaḥ // GRhtCM_3.3:10 //
children.translated_text: or combined with the five acids — this is called the acid group (<s>amlavarga</s>). (GRhtCM 3.3:10)

children.text: caṇakāmpaṃ ca sarveṣām ekameva praśasyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Caṇakāmla</s> (sour chickpea water) alone is recommended as the best among all [acids];

children.text: ampavetasamekaṃ vā sarveṣāmuttamottamam // GRhtCM_3.3:11 //
children.translated_text: or <s>amlavetasa</s> alone is the most supreme of all. (GRhtCM 3.3:11)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_3.3:12 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 3.3:12)

children.text:
ityetaiḥ kṣārauṣadhipaṭvampaiḥ kṣudbodho bhavet rāgabandhane ca bhavetāṃ
                            rāgo rañjanaṃ bandhanaṃ pūrvam upavarṇitam // GRhtCM_3.3:13 //
children.translated_text: Thus, through these alkalis, herbs, sharp substances, and acids, the arousal of hunger [in mercury] occurs; and coloring (<s>rāga</s>) and binding (<s>bandhana</s>) [also occur] — binding was described earlier. (GRhtCM 3.3:13)

children.text: kuto hetoḥ etaiḥ pūrvoktaiḥ karaṇarūpaiḥ svedāt // GRhtCM_3.3:14 //
children.translated_text: From what cause? Through heating (<s>sveda</s>) by means of the aforementioned instrumental agents. (GRhtCM 3.3:14)

children.text: punariti viśeṣaṇe // GRhtCM_3.3:15 //
children.translated_text: The word 'again' (<s>punar</s>) is used as a qualifier. (GRhtCM 3.3:15)

Clipping of wings (<s>pakṣaccheda</s>) — the cutting of the wings of mercury — so that it becomes stable; and fluidity (<s>dravatva</s>) or qualitative excellence — [these are] not [possible] without mica (<s>gagana</s>, <s>abhraka</s>) — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 3.3:16)

children.text: abhrakajīrṇo balavān bhavati rasastasya cāraṇe proktāḥ /
children.translated_text: Mercury that has digested mica becomes powerful; for its transmutation, the following are prescribed:

children.text: saṃdhānavāsanauṣadhinirmukhasamukhā mahāyogāḥ // GRht_3.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sandhāna</s> (ferment), <s>vāsana</s> (impression), herbs, mouthless, and mouthed — [these are] the great conjunctions (<s>mahāyogas</s>). (GRht 3.4)

children.text: dravyatvam abhrakeṇāhābhrakajīrṇa ityādi // GRhtCM_3.4:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the fluidity [achievable] through mica, with 'having digested mica' and so forth. (GRhtCM 3.4:1)

children.text: baparahite atikṣudbodhe ṣaṇḍhatā bhavet // GRhtCM_3.4:2 //
children.translated_text: When there is excessive arousal of hunger without sufficient power, impotence (<s>ṣaṇḍhatā</s>) would result [in mercury]. (GRhtCM 3.4:2)

children.text: yathā /
children.translated_text: As [stated]:

children.text: śītatvānmardanābhāvāp pohāśuddhasya jāraṇāt /
children.translated_text: Due to coldness, absence of grinding, because of impure metals being made to be digested,

children.text: viḍaprabhūtadānād vā bhuṅkte jīrṇādajīrṇagaḥ // GRhtCM_3.4:3 //
children.translated_text: or due to excessive giving of <s>viḍa</s> (alkaline salt) — [mercury] that eats [but] does not digest consumes yet remains undigested. (GRhtCM 3.4:3)

children.text: atyagnito nirāhārāt krāmaṇārahitasya ca /
children.translated_text: Due to excessive fire, due to absence of food, and due to lack of <s>krāmaṇa</s> (progressive treatment) —

children.text: ityetā vikriyā jñeyā aṣṭabhiḥ ṣaṇḍhatāṃ vrajet // GRhtCM_3.4:4 //
children.translated_text: these disorders should be known; through [these] eight [faults], it goes to impotence. (GRhtCM 3.4:4)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_3.4:5 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 3.4:5)

children.text:
ato raso+aṣṭasaṃskārānantaram abhrakajīrṇaḥ kartavyaḥ yato+abhrakajīrṇaṃ
                            bapavān bhavati // GRhtCM_3.4:6 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, mercury should be made to digest mica after the eight <s>saṃskāras</s> (purificatory processes), because mercury that has digested mica becomes powerful. (GRhtCM 3.4:6)

children.text:
abhrakajīrṇe grāsanyāye na jāritaṃ yasmin sa tathoktaḥ // GRhtCM_3.4:7
                            //
children.translated_text: In the process of mica-digestion, [mercury] in which [mica] has not been properly digested according to the bolus-method is described as such. (GRhtCM 3.4:7)

children.text:
tasyābhrajāraṇāyogyasya rasasya cāraṇe kevapakavapane ete proktāḥ //
                            GRhtCM_3.4:8 //
children.translated_text: For that mercury — fit for mica-digestion — in its transmutation, in mere consuming, these are prescribed: (GRhtCM 3.4:8)

children.text:
ete ke saṃdhānavāsanauṣadhinirmukhasamukhā eva mahāyogāḥ
                            mahaddravyatvakārakāḥ saṃdhānaṃ sarvadhānyānām aṣṭauṣadhyādīnāṃ ca
                            saṃdhānaṃ yathā sarvadhānyāni nikṣipya āranāpaṃ tu kārayet //
                            GRhtCM_3.4:9 //
children.translated_text: What are these? <s>Sandhāna</s> (ferment), <s>vāsana</s> (impression), herbs, mouthless, and mouthed — these are the great conjunctions (<s>mahāyogas</s>) — that which produces great fluidity. <s>Sandhāna</s> is [prepared from] all grains, the eight herbs, and the like. The <s>sandhāna</s> is as follows: all grains should be placed [in a vessel], and the fermented liquor (<s>āranāla</s>) should be made. (GRhtCM 3.4:9)

children.text: sapattramūpasaṃyuktā auṣadhīstatra niḥkṣipet // GRhtCM_3.4:10 //
children.translated_text: The herbs combined with leaves and roots should be placed therein. (GRhtCM 3.4:10)

children.text: kṣitikāsīsasāmudrasindhutryuṣaṇarājikaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With earth, <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol), <s>sāmudra</s> (sea salt), <s>sindhu</s> (rock salt), <s>tryuṣaṇa</s> (three pungent spices), and <s>rājikā</s> (mustard) —

children.text: saṃyuktaṃ kārayettattu soṣme saptāhasaṃsthitam // GRhtCM_3.4:11 //
children.translated_text: combined [with these], one should prepare that; kept warm for seven days. (GRhtCM 3.4:11)

children.text: taccāranāpasaṃyuktaṃ tāmrabhāṇḍe tu saṃdhayet /
children.translated_text: That, combined with the fermented liquor, should be fermented in a copper vessel.

children.text: ityabhrakacāraṇārthaṃ saṃdhānam // GRhtCM_3.4:12 //
children.translated_text: This is the <s>sandhāna</s> (ferment) for the purpose of mica-transmutation. (GRhtCM 3.4:12)

children.text: vāsanauṣadhyo yathā /
children.translated_text: The <s>vāsanauṣadhi</s>s (aromatic/impregnating herbs) are as follows:

children.text: vijñeyamauṣadhīvargaṃ yathā śāstrairudāhṛtam /
children.translated_text: One should know the group of herbs as described in the treatises.

children.text: japajaṃ sthapajaṃ caiva samyak jñātvā tu kārayet // GRhtCM_3.4:13 //
children.translated_text: Having properly understood those born from <s>japa</s> (recitation/prayer plant) and those born from standing [water], one should employ them. (GRhtCM 3.4:13)

children.text: japajā utpapī padmā sthapajā ca prasāriṇī /
children.translated_text: <s>Japajā</s> is <s>utpalī</s> (lotus); <s>padmā</s> [is another]; <s>sthapajā</s> is <s>prasāriṇī</s>;

children.text: jāpinī abhracandrā ca citraparṇī triparṇikā /
children.translated_text: <s>Jāpinī</s>, <s>abhracandrā</s>, <s>citraparṇī</s>, <s>triparṇikā</s>,

children.text: rasacandraukasaś caiva tathā ca japamūpakaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Rasacandra</s>, <s>aukasa</s>, and likewise <s>japamūlaka</s>,

children.text: samaṅgā vāribhūtā ca apāmārgo japodbhavā // GRhtCM_3.4:14 //
children.translated_text: <s>Samaṅgā</s>, <s>vāribhūtā</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>japodbhavā</s>; (GRhtCM 3.4:14)

children.text: ajamārī upāmbuśca kumbhikā japapippapī /
children.translated_text: <s>Ajamārī</s>, <s>upāmbu</s>, <s>kumbhikā</s>, <s>japapippalī</s>,

children.text: japapūrvāmbusītā ca kumārī nāginī tathā // GRhtCM_3.4:15 //
children.translated_text: <s>Japapūrvāmbusītā</s>, <s>kumārī</s>, and likewise <s>nāginī</s>; (GRhtCM 3.4:15)

children.text: sitajaṅghā svaraścaiva tathā sarpaḥ sugandhikā /
children.translated_text: <s>Sitajaṅghā</s>, <s>svara</s>, and likewise <s>sarpa</s>, <s>sugandhikā</s>,

children.text: vṛddhā ca bṛhatī tadvanmūrtir mārjārapādikā // GRhtCM_3.4:16 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛddhā</s> and <s>bṛhatī</s>, and likewise <s>mūrti</s>, <s>mārjārapādikā</s>; (GRhtCM 3.4:16)

children.text: tathā japacakorī ca mīnākṣī ahipocanā /
children.translated_text: And likewise <s>japacakorī</s>, <s>mīnākṣī</s>, <s>ahilocanā</s>,

children.text: jayāṃvica varāhī ca apattrā īśvarī tathā // GRhtCM_3.4:17 //
children.translated_text: <s>Jayā</s>, <s>ambicā</s>, <s>varāhī</s>, <s>alattrā</s>, and likewise <s>īśvarī</s>; (GRhtCM 3.4:17)

children.text: kurkurī hapinī caiva bṛhatī vajrakandakam /
children.translated_text: <s>Kurkurī</s>, <s>halinī</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, <s>vajrakandaka</s>,

children.text: musapī vanamāpā ca vidārī mohinī tathā // GRhtCM_3.4:18 //
children.translated_text: <s>Musalī</s>, <s>vanamālā</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, and likewise <s>mohinī</s>; (GRhtCM 3.4:18)

children.text: māṇḍūkī pavaṇā caiva ugrā ca uttamā tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Māṇḍūkī</s>, <s>palvaṇā</s>, <s>ugrā</s>, and likewise <s>uttamā</s>,

children.text: śikhipādī kapotī ca nandinī vṛścikāpikā /
children.translated_text: <s>Śikhipādī</s>, <s>kapotī</s>, <s>nandinī</s>, <s>vṛścikālikā</s>,

children.text: haṃsapādī śikhā caiva sārivā vāyasī tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Haṃsapādī</s>, <s>śikhā</s>, <s>sārivā</s>, and likewise <s>vāyasī</s>,

children.text: dantī gojihvikā caiva garuḍī hemapuṣpikā // GRhtCM_3.4:19 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dantī</s>, <s>gojihvikā</s>, <s>garuḍī</s>, <s>hemapuṣpikā</s>; (GRhtCM 3.4:19)

children.text: samaṅgā japajā caiva māṃsī pāṣāṇabhedikā /
children.translated_text: <s>Samaṅgā</s>, <s>japajā</s>, <s>māṃsī</s>, <s>pāṣāṇabhedikā</s>,

children.text: apambuṣā meghanādā śukanādā kapotikī // GRhtCM_3.4:20 //
children.translated_text: <s>Alambuṣā</s>, <s>meghanādā</s>, <s>śukanādā</s>, <s>kapotikī</s>; (GRhtCM 3.4:20)

children.text: kṣīrikā tupasī dhānyā meṣikā ca vanārjakā /
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣīrikā</s>, <s>tulasī</s>, <s>dhānyā</s>, <s>meṣikā</s>, and <s>vanārjakā</s>,

children.text: vārāhī caṇakāyāsī tathā ca aparājitā // GRhtCM_3.4:21 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vārāhī</s>, <s>caṇakāyāsī</s>, and likewise <s>aparājitā</s>. (GRhtCM 3.4:21)

children.text: catuḥṣaṣṭigaṇo hy eṣa auṣadhīnāṃ prakīrtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: This group of sixty-four herbs has been proclaimed.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhāṣṭakaprayogena avasthāṃ naiva kārayet // GRhtCM_3.4:22 //
children.translated_text: By the application of the sixty-eighth [method?], one should not [merely] bring about [a single] state. (GRhtCM 3.4:22)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_3.4:23 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 3.4:23)

children.text: ayamoṣadhīgaṇaḥ saṃdhāne 'pi yojyaḥ // GRhtCM_3.4:24 //
children.translated_text: This group of herbs is also to be used in <s>saṃdhāna</s> (conjunction/fermentation). (GRhtCM 3.4:24)

children.text:
saṃdhānaṃ ca vāsanauṣadhayaśca tābhiḥ kṛtvā ye nirmukhasamukhā eva yogāḥ
                            akṛtamukhakṛtamukhā ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.4:25 //
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃdhāna</s> (conjunction) and the aromatic herbs — with those, the preparations are either <s>nirmukha</s> (without 'mouth'/unseeded) or <s>samukha</s> (with 'mouth'/seeded) — meaning either without the addition of seed-metal or with the addition of seed-metal. (GRhtCM 3.4:25)

children.text: abhra:: preparation for cāraṇa
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Abhraka</s> (mica) — preparation for <s>cāraṇa</s> (making mercury 'devour' mica)

children.text: niścandrikaṃ hi gaganaṃ kṣārāmlairbhāvitaṃ tathā rudhiraiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Gagana</s> (mica) without lustre (<s>niścandrika</s>), processed with alkalis and acids, and with [animal] blood,

children.text: sṛṣṭitrayanīrakaṇātumbarurasamarditaṃ carati // GRht_3.5 //
children.translated_text: ground with the three excretions, <s>nīrakaṇā</s> (long pepper), and <s>tumburu</s> juice — [thus mercury] devours [it]. (GRht 3.5)

children.text:
nirmukhatvenābhrakacāraṇopāyamāha niścandrikam ityādi // GRhtCM_3.5:1
                            //
children.translated_text: He states the method for making mercury devour mica through the <s>nirmukha</s> (unseeded) [method], beginning with '<s>niścandrika</s>' and so on. (GRhtCM 3.5:1)

children.text:
hi niścitaṃ yadgaganamabhrakaṃ niścandrikaṃ candrarahitaṃ bhavati
                            vajrasaṃjñakam ityarthaḥ tadgaganaṃ rucirair nirdoṣair manoramair
                            vividhaiḥ kṣārāmpair bhāvitaṃ ppāvitaṃ kāryaṃ kṣārā
                            yavakṣārasvarjikṣāraṭaṅkaṇakṣārādayo 'mpā ampavetasajambīrādyāḥ
                            pūrvoktāḥ // GRhtCM_3.5:2 //
children.translated_text: Indeed, that <s>gagana</s> (mica) which is <s>niścandrika</s> — devoid of lustre — becomes of the variety called <s>vajra</s> (diamond-mica); that is the meaning. That <s>gagana</s> should be processed (<s>bhāvita</s>) — purified — with excellent, flawless, beautiful, various alkalis and acids. The alkalis are: <s>yavakṣāra</s> (barley-alkali), <s>svarjikṣāra</s> (natron), <s>ṭaṅkaṇakṣāra</s> (borax-alkali), and others. The acids are: sour gruel from <s>amlavetasa</s> (tamarind), <s>jambīra</s> (citron), and others as previously mentioned. (GRhtCM 3.5:2)

children.text:
nanu kṣārā rucirāḥ kathaṃ bhavanti ucyate yathā sarjikācūrṇabhāgaikaṃ
                            viṃśadbhāgaṃ japasya ca // GRhtCM_3.5:3 //
children.translated_text: But how can alkalis be 'excellent'? It is explained: [Take] one part of <s>sarjikā</s>-powder and twenty parts of [a plant], (GRhtCM 3.5:3)

children.text:
tāvatkvāthyaṃ kṣiped bhāṇḍe yāvatphenaṃ sitaṃ bhavet // GRhtCM_3.5:4
                            //
children.translated_text: boil them that much and pour into a vessel until white foam appears, (GRhtCM 3.5:4)

children.text: kṣīṇe kṣīṇe japaṃ dattvā śvetaphenaṃ ca gṛhyate // GRhtCM_3.5:5 //
children.translated_text: as [the liquid] diminishes and diminishes, add [the plant] and collect the white foam; (GRhtCM 3.5:5)

children.text: tadā tu ḍekayantreṇa drāvayedagniyogataḥ // GRhtCM_3.5:6 //
children.translated_text: then, with a <s>ḍeka</s>-apparatus, one should liquify [it] by the application of fire; (GRhtCM 3.5:6)

children.text: triḥsaptavāraṃ kartavyaṃ drāvaṇaṃ mūtrasaṃyutam // GRhtCM_3.5:7 //
children.translated_text: the liquefaction should be done twenty-one times (thrice-seven), combined with urine; (GRhtCM 3.5:7)

children.text: svarjikākṣāranāmāyaṃ drāvaṇe paramo mataḥ // GRhtCM_3.5:8 //
children.translated_text: this is called <s>svarjikā-kṣāra</s> (processed natron) — it is considered supreme for liquefaction. (GRhtCM 3.5:8)

children.text: iti viśeṣavidhiḥ // GRhtCM_3.5:9 //
children.translated_text: Thus is the special procedure. (GRhtCM 3.5:9)

children.text: evamatyuttamāḥ kṣārāḥ syuḥ sampakvāḥ himāḥ // GRhtCM_3.5:10 //
children.translated_text: In this way, the most excellent alkalis become fully prepared and pure. (GRhtCM 3.5:10)

children.text:
punaḥ sṛṣṭitrayanīrakaṇātumbarurasamarditaṃ go+ajāvinārīṇāṃ mūtraṃ śukraṃ
                            ca śoṇitaṃ sṛṣṭitrayaṃ nīrakaṇā japapippapī paṭuriti poke tumburu
                            pratītaṃ japakaṇā ca tumbaruśca anayo rasaḥ sṛṣṭitrayaṃ ca
                            japakaṇātumbarurasaśca tābhyāṃ mardanaṃ kāryam // GRhtCM_3.5:11 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, ground with the three excretions — the urine, semen, and blood of cow, goat, and sheep-woman — <s>nīrakaṇā</s> is <s>japapippalī</s> (long pepper), <s>paṭu</s> (pungent) in the vernacular; <s>tumburu</s> is well known; <s>japakaṇā</s> and <s>tumburu</s> — with their juice, along with the three excretions — grinding should be done. (GRhtCM 3.5:11)

children.text:
rasaḥ pāradaḥ nirmukho+api evaṃvidhaṃ gaganaṃ carati grāsīkaroti //
                            GRhtCM_3.5:12 //
children.translated_text: Mercury (<s>pārada</s>), even without seed-metal (<s>nirmukha</s>), devours — absorbs — mica processed in this manner. (GRhtCM 3.5:12)

children.text: karaṇaṃ granthāntare'sti /
children.translated_text: The procedure is [found] in other treatises:

children.text: dugdhatrayaṃ kumāryambu gaṅgāputraṃ trimūtrakam /
children.translated_text: The three milks, <s>kumārī</s> (aloe) water, <s>gaṅgāputra</s> (a mineral), the three urines,

children.text: vaṭaśuṅgamajāraktam ebhir abhraṃ sumarditam // GRhtCM_3.5:13 //
children.translated_text: banyan shoots, and goat's blood — mica well-ground with these, (GRhtCM 3.5:13)

children.text: śatadhā puṭitaṃ cāpi jāyate padmarāgavat /
children.translated_text: even when calcined a hundred times, becomes like a ruby (<s>padmarāga</s>).

children.text: niścandrikaṃ mṛtaṃ tv abhraṃ vṛddhadehe rasāyanam // GRhtCM_3.5:14 //
children.translated_text: Lustre-free, calcined mica is a rejuvenative (<s>rasāyana</s>) for aged bodies, (GRhtCM 3.5:14)

children.text: kāminīmadadarpaghnaṃ śastaṃ puṃstvopaghātinām /
children.translated_text: it destroys the intoxication and pride of women, and is recommended for those with impaired virility.

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_3.5:15 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 3.5:15)

children.text: mercury:: abhracāraṇa
children.translated_text: [Section:] Mercury — <s>abhraka cāraṇa</s> (making mercury devour mica)

children.text: yavaciñcikāmbupuṭitaṃ tanmūlaśatāvarīgadākulitam /
children.translated_text: Calcined with the juice of <s>yavaciñcikā</s> (a plant), [then processed with] its root, <s>śatāvarī</s>, and <s>gadā</s> (Gmelina),

children.text: ghanaravaśigrupunarnavarasabhāvitamabhrakaṃ carati // GRht_3.6 //
children.translated_text: processed with the juices of <s>ghanarava</s> (Indian bay), <s>śigru</s> (drumstick tree), and <s>punarnava</s> (Boerhavia) — [thus mercury] devours mica. (GRht 3.6)

children.text: vidhānāntaramāha yavetyādi // GRhtCM_3.6:1 //
children.translated_text: He states another method, beginning with '<s>yava</s>' and so on. (GRhtCM 3.6:1)

children.text:
punarabhrakaṃ yavaciñcikāmbupuṭitaṃ kāryaṃ yavaciñcikā pratītā
                            yavaciñciketi poke tasyā ambudravaḥ tena puṭitam ātapayogena bhāvitam //
                            GRhtCM_3.6:2 //
children.translated_text: Mica should be further calcined (<s>puṭita</s>) with the juice of <s>yavaciñcikā</s> — <s>yavaciñcikā</s> is the well-known [plant] called <s>yavaciñcikā</s> in the vernacular — with its liquid, calcined, meaning processed by sun-drying. (GRhtCM 3.6:2)

children.text:
punastanmūpaśatāvarīgadākupitaṃ kāryaṃ tasyā yavaciñcikāyā mūpaṃ tanmūpaṃ
                            śatāvarī śatapād gadaḥ kuṣṭhaḥ etair ākupaṃ vyāptaṃ paripputam //
                            GRhtCM_3.6:3 //
children.translated_text: Further, it should be processed with its root, <s>śatāvarī</s>, and <s>gadā</s> (<s>kuṣṭha</s>) — the root of that <s>yavaciñcikā</s>, its root; <s>śatāvarī</s> [is] <s>śatapād</s>; <s>gadā</s> is <s>kuṣṭha</s> — pervaded, saturated, soaked with these. (GRhtCM 3.6:3)

children.text: yadā sarasauṣadhābhāvas tadāyaṃ vidhiḥ yathā /
children.translated_text: When fresh herbs are unavailable, the rule is as follows:

children.text: śuṣkadravyam upādāya svarasānām asaṃbhave /
children.translated_text: In the absence of fresh juices, taking the dried substance,

children.text: vāriṇyaṣṭaguṇe sādhyaṃ grāhyaṃ pādāvaśeṣitam // GRhtCM_3.6:4 //
children.translated_text: it should be prepared in eight times the amount of water, and collected when reduced to one-quarter. (GRhtCM 3.6:4)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_3.6:5 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 3.6:5)

children.text:
punar ghanaravaśigrupunarnavarasabhāvitaṃ kāryaṃ ghanaravas taṇḍupīyakaḥ
                            śigru saubhāñjanaṃ suhijanā iti poke punarnavā varṣābhūḥ pratītā eteṣāṃ
                            rasena bhāvitaṃ paripputam ātapayogena śoṣyam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.6:6
                            //
children.translated_text: Further, it should be processed with the juices of <s>ghanarava</s> (<s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>, Amaranth), <s>śigru</s> (<s>saubhāñjana</s>, drumstick tree, called <s>suhijanā</s> in the vernacular), <s>punarnava</s> (<s>varṣābhū</s>, the well-known [plant]) — processed, meaning saturated; dried by sun-drying — that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 3.6:6)

children.text: evaṃvidham abhraṃ rasaś carati // GRhtCM_3.6:7 //
children.translated_text: Mercury devours mica prepared in this manner. (GRhtCM 3.6:7)

children.text:
nirmukhena bhāvanāśabdena śatavāraṃ jñātavyaṃ granthāntarasāmyāt //
                            GRhtCM_3.6:8 //
children.translated_text: In the unseeded [method], by the word 'processing' (<s>bhāvanā</s>), one hundred repetitions are to be understood — from comparison with other treatises. (GRhtCM 3.6:8)

children.text: atra viśeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_3.6:9 //
children.translated_text: Here is a special [procedure]: (GRhtCM 3.6:9)

children.text: somavappīrase piṣṭvā dāpayecca puṭatrayam /
children.translated_text: Grinding in <s>somavallī</s> juice, one should give three calcinations;

children.text: somavappīrasenaiva sapta vārāṃśca bhāvayet // GRhtCM_3.6:10 //
children.translated_text: and one should process [it] seven times with <s>somavallī</s> juice itself. (GRhtCM 3.6:10)

children.text: dāpayenmṛnmaye bhāṇḍe rasena saṃyutam /
children.translated_text: One should place [it] in an earthen vessel, combined with mercury;

children.text: mūpaṃ tu śarapuṅkhāyā gavyakṣīreṇa gharṣayet /
children.translated_text: the root of <s>śarapuṅkhā</s> should be rubbed with cow's milk;

children.text: kapkena mepayet sūtaṃ gaganaṃ tadadhaūrdhvagam // GRhtCM_3.6:11 //
children.translated_text: one should mix mercury with mica, with the paste, [placing] the latter below and the former above. (GRhtCM 3.6:11)

children.text: sthāpayedravitāpe tu nirmukho grasate kṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: One should place [it] in sunlight; the unseeded [mercury] devours [the mica] in a moment;

children.text: jāyate piṣṭikā śīghraṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā // GRhtCM_3.6:12 //
children.translated_text: a pellet (<s>piṣṭikā</s>) forms quickly — no deliberation is needed here. (GRhtCM 3.6:12)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_3.6:13 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 3.6:13)

children.text: anyacca /
children.translated_text: And another [method]:

children.text: tipaparṇīrasaṃ nītvā gaganaṃ tena bhāvayet /
children.translated_text: Having taken <s>tilaparṇī</s> juice, one should process mica with it;

children.text: mardanājjāyate piṣṭī nātra kāryā vicāraṇā // GRhtCM_3.6:14 //
children.translated_text: through grinding, a pellet forms — no deliberation is needed here. (GRhtCM 3.6:14)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_3.6:15 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 3.6:15)

children.text: anyacca /
children.translated_text: And another [method]:

children.text: muṇḍīniryāsake nāgaṃ bahuśastu niṣecayet /
children.translated_text: One should thoroughly immerse lead (<s>nāga</s>) many times in the exudate of <s>muṇḍī</s>;

children.text: tenābhrakaṃ tu saṃyojya bhūyo bhūyaḥ paṭe dahet // GRhtCM_3.6:16 //
children.translated_text: combining mica with that, one should burn [it] on cloth again and again. (GRhtCM 3.6:16)

children.text: citrakārdrakamūpānām ekaikena tu saptadhā /
children.translated_text: Seven times with each — the roots of <s>citraka</s> (leadwort) and <s>ārdraka</s> (ginger) —

children.text: ppāvitavyaṃ prayatnena gandhakābhrakacūrṇakam // GRhtCM_3.6:17 //
children.translated_text: the powder of sulphur and mica should be processed carefully. (GRhtCM 3.6:17)

children.text: nāgamuṇḍīrasākṣiptaṃ rasapuṅgāmpabhāvitam /
children.translated_text: Immersed in the juice of <s>nāgamuṇḍī</s>, processed with the juice of <s>rasapuṅga</s> (mercury-mass),

children.text: ṣoḍaśāṃśena dātavyaṃ dopāyantre caredrasaḥ // GRhtCM_3.6:18 //
children.translated_text: in a one-sixteenth proportion, it should be administered; in the <s>dolā</s>-apparatus, mercury will devour [it]. (GRhtCM 3.6:18)

children.text: iti nirmukhacāraṇam // GRhtCM_3.6:19 //
children.translated_text: Thus is the <s>nirmukha cāraṇa</s> (unseeded devouring [of mica by mercury]). (GRhtCM 3.6:19)

children.text: āranāla for jāraṇa
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Āranāla</s> (fermented gruel) for <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion [of metals by mercury])

children.text: sarjīkṣitikhagaṭaṅkaṇalavaṇānvitam arkabhājane tridinam /
children.translated_text: Endowed with natron (<s>sarjī</s>), alum (<s>kṣiti</s>), green vitriol (<s>khaga</s>), borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), and salt (<s>lavaṇa</s>), [placed] in a copper vessel of the sun for three days,

children.text: paryuṣitamāranālaṃ gaganādiṣu bhāvane śastam // GRht_3.7 //
children.translated_text: the aged <s>āranāla</s> (fermented gruel) is recommended for the processing of mica and the like. (GRht 3.7)

children.text: tasminnāgaṃ śuddhaṃ pradrāvya niṣecayecchataṃ vārān /
children.translated_text: Having melted purified lead (<s>nāga</s>) into that, one should immerse [it] a hundred times;

children.text: vaṅgaṃ vā tāravidhau rasāyane naiva tadyojyam // GRht_3.8 //
children.translated_text: or tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) [may be used]; in the procedure for silver, [these] should not be combined with rejuvenatives (<s>rasāyana</s>). (GRht 3.8)

children.text: gaganarasoparasāmṛtaloharasāyasādicūrṇāni /
children.translated_text: The powders of mica (<s>gagana</s>), mercury (<s>rasa</s>), semi-metals (<s>uparasa</s>), <s>amṛtaloha</s> (a metal), iron (<s>āyasa</s>), and the like —

children.text: sarvamanena ha bhāvyaṃ yatkiṃcit cāraṇāvastu // GRht_3.9 //
children.translated_text: all of these should be processed with this; whatever is the substance for <s>cāraṇa</s> (devouring). (GRht 3.9)

children.text: samukhacāraṇamāha sarjītyādi // GRhtCM_3.7-9:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the <s>samukha cāraṇa</s> (seeded devouring [method]), beginning with '<s>sarjī</s>' and so on. (GRhtCM 3.7-9:1)

children.text: āranāpaṃ svedanasaṃskāre yaduktaṃ kāñjikaṃ tat // GRhtCM_3.7-9:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Āranāla</s> — that which was called <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel) in the <s>svedana</s> (sweating) process. (GRhtCM 3.7-9:2)

children.text: arkabhājane tāmrapātre // GRhtCM_3.7-9:3 //
children.translated_text: 'In a copper vessel of the sun' (<s>arkabhājana</s>) — in a copper vessel. (GRhtCM 3.7-9:3)

children.text:
tridinaṃ yāvattāvatparyuṣitaṃ saṃdhānīkaraṇaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_3.7-9:4
                            //
children.translated_text: For three days — one should ferment [it] for that long. (GRhtCM 3.7-9:4)

children.text:
kīdṛgvidham āranāpaṃ sarjīkṣitikhagaṭaṅkaṇapavaṇānvitaṃ sarjī pratītā
                            sājīti poke kṣitiḥ sphaṭikā khagaḥ kāsīsaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ sohāgā
                            iti poke pavaṇaṃ saindhavaṃ tadabhāve pavaṇāṣṭakeṣu yatra yappabhyaṃ
                            tadeva yojyaṃ pavaṇoddeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Of what kind is the <s>āranāla</s>? Endowed with natron (<s>sarjī</s>, known as <s>sājī</s> in the vernacular), alum (<s>kṣiti</s>, meaning <s>sphaṭikā</s>), green vitriol (<s>khaga</s>, meaning <s>kāsīsa</s>), borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, meaning <s>saubhāgya</s>, called <s>sohāgā</s> in the vernacular), salt (<s>lavaṇa</s>, meaning rock salt); in its absence, whichever of the eight salts is easily obtainable, that should be used — this is the reference to salt. [The verse:]

children.text: saindhavaṃ rucakaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ viḍaṃ sāmudram audbhidam /
children.translated_text: 'Rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>), <s>rucaka</s>, black salt (<s>kṛṣṇa</s>), <s>viḍa</s> salt, sea salt (<s>sāmudra</s>), <s>audbhida</s>,

children.text: romakaṃ pāṃśujaṃ ceti pavaṇāṣṭakam ucyate // GRhtCM_3.7-9:5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Romaka</s>, and earth-born salt (<s>pāṃśuja</s>) — these are called the eight salts.' (GRhtCM 3.7-9:5)

children.text: iti etair anvitaṃ mipitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_3.7-9:6 //
children.translated_text: Thus — endowed with these, meaning mixed [with them]. (GRhtCM 3.7-9:6)

children.text:
tadāranāpaṃ gaganādikabhāvane abhrakādippāvane śastaṃ pradhānam
                            abhrakādikā agre vakṣyamāṇāḥ // GRhtCM_3.7-9:7 //
children.translated_text: That <s>āranāla</s> is recommended — primary — for the processing of mica and the like; the mica and the like will be described further ahead. (GRhtCM 3.7-9:7)

children.text:
nirmukhā samukhā ceti dvividhā cāraṇā matā nirmukhā cāraṇā proktā
                            bījādhānena bhāgataḥ // GRhtCM_3.7-9:8 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Nirmukha</s> (unseeded) and <s>samukha</s> (seeded) — thus <s>cāraṇa</s> is considered twofold. <s>Nirmukha cāraṇa</s> is said to be [done] through the fractional addition of seed [metal].' (GRhtCM 3.7-9:8)

children.text:
śuddhaṃ svarṇaṃ ca rūpyaṃ ca bījam ityabhidhīyate // GRhtCM_3.7-9:9
                            //
children.translated_text: 'Purified gold and silver are called the seed [metals].' (GRhtCM 3.7-9:9)

children.text: catuḥṣaṣṭyaṃśato bījaprakṣepo mukham ucyate // GRhtCM_3.7-9:10 //
children.translated_text: 'The addition of seed in a one-sixty-fourth proportion is called <s>mukha</s> (mouth/seeding).' (GRhtCM 3.7-9:10)

children.text: evaṃ kṛte raso grāsapopupo mukhavān bhavet /
children.translated_text: When done thus, mercury becomes well-nourished by its food and acquires <s>mukha</s> (the capacity to devour);

children.text: kaṭhinānyapi pohāni kṣamo bhavati bhakṣaṇe // GRhtCM_3.7-9:11 //
children.translated_text: it becomes capable of consuming even hard metals. (GRhtCM 3.7-9:11)

children.text: iyaṃ hi samukhā proktā cāraṇā varavārttikaiḥ /
children.translated_text: This is called <s>samukha cāraṇa</s> (seeded devouring) by the excellent commentators.

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_3.7-9:12 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 3.7-9:12)

children.text:
abhrakādyapadhātūnāṃ nirmukhacāraṇaṃ hemādidhātūnāṃ samukhacāraṇam iti
                            viveko jñeyaḥ // GRhtCM_3.7-9:13 //
children.translated_text: The <s>nirmukha cāraṇa</s> (unseeded devouring) is for mica and other sub-metals; the <s>samukha cāraṇa</s> (seeded devouring) is for gold and other metals — this distinction should be known. (GRhtCM 3.7-9:13)

children.text:
rasāyane śarīrakārye nāgavaṅgau na cāraṇīyau kiṃtu svarṇādikaṃ bījaṃ
                            cāraṇīyam iti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_3.7-9:14 //
children.translated_text: For <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) — bodily purposes — lead and tin should not be made to be devoured [by mercury]; rather, the seed-metal of gold and the like should be used for <s>cāraṇa</s> — that is the purport. (GRhtCM 3.7-9:14)

children.text:
ādiśabdena nāgavaṅgayor adhikāraviśeṣam āha tasminnityādi //
                            GRhtCM_3.7-9:15 //
children.translated_text: By the word 'and the like' (<s>ādi</s>), he states the specific scope of lead and tin, beginning with 'in that' and so on. (GRhtCM 3.7-9:15)

children.text:
tasmin pūrvoktasaṃdhāne śuddhaṃ nirmapīkṛtaṃ nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ pradrāvya
                            japarūpaṃ vidhāya vahniyogāt iti śeṣaḥ niṣecayet niṣekaḥ kartavyaḥ vā
                            tatraiva saṃdhāne vaṅgaṃ raṅgaṃ pradrāvya niṣecayet // GRhtCM_3.7-9:16
                            //
children.translated_text: In that previously described conjunction (<s>saṃdhāna</s>), having melted purified, refined lead (<s>nāga</s>/tin), making it silvery [in appearance] — by the application of fire (this is to be understood as completing the sentence) — one should pour [it in]; or alternatively, in that very conjunction, having melted <s>vaṅga</s> (tin/pewter), one should pour [it in]. (GRhtCM 3.7-9:16)

children.text: kativārān śataṃ vārān pratiśatam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.7-9:17 //
children.translated_text: 'How many times?' — a hundred times; meaning 'for each hundred.' (GRhtCM 3.7-9:17)

children.text:
tadvaṅgaṃ tāravidhau rūpyavidhāne yojyaṃ rasena saha mipitaṃ kāryam
                            ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.7-9:18 //
children.translated_text: That <s>vaṅga</s> (tin) is to be employed in the silver-making procedure — it should be combined with mercury — that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 3.7-9:18)

children.text:
āsyām āryāyāṃ svarṇādhikāre'nuktamapi nāgaṃ granthāntarāt samāyojyam iti
                            viśeṣārthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.7-9:19 //
children.translated_text: In this <s>āryā</s> verse, although lead is not mentioned in the context of gold[-making], it should be incorporated from other texts — this is the special meaning. (GRhtCM 3.7-9:19)

children.text:
tannāgaṃ vaṅgaṃ ca rasāyane śarīrasiddhinimittaṃ na yojyamiti yato
                            nāgavaṅgaprabhavāv aupādhikau doṣau gapabandhagupmadau kathitau
                            etannāgaṃ vaṅgaṃ ca grāsārthe yojyamiti yuktaṃ yata
                            etenāntargatenānyadapi grāhyaṃ dravyaṃ grasatīti bhāvaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_3.7-9:20 //
children.translated_text: That lead and tin should not be employed in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) for the purpose of bodily perfection (<s>śarīrasiddhi</s>), because the incidental defects arising from lead and tin — namely, binding of the throat and dullness — have been mentioned. This lead and tin should be employed for the purpose of <s>grāsa</s> (devouring/assimilation) — this is proper, because through [mercury] which has absorbed them internally, other substances too can be devoured — this is the purport. (GRhtCM 3.7-9:20)

children.text: vaṅge viśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: A distinction regarding <s>vaṅga</s> (tin):

children.text: khurakaṃ miśrakaṃ ceti dvividhaṃ vaṅgam ucyate /
children.translated_text: 'Tin is said to be of two kinds: <s>khuraka</s> and <s>miśraka</s>.

children.text:
khurakaṃ guṇataḥ śreṣṭhaṃ miśrakaṃ na rase hitam // GRhtCM_3.7-9:21
                            //
children.translated_text: <s>Khuraka</s> is superior in qualities; <s>miśraka</s> is not beneficial for mercury[-work].' (GRhtCM 3.7-9:21)

children.text: iti rajatakarmaṇi yogyaṃ grāhyam // GRhtCM_3.7-9:22 //
children.translated_text: Thus, what is suitable for silver-making operations should be selected. (GRhtCM 3.7-9:22)

children.text: gaganādikramaṃ spaṣṭayann āha gaganetyādi // GRhtCM_3.7-9:23 //
children.translated_text: Explaining the sequence [of operations] beginning with <s>gagana</s> (mica), he says '<s>gagana</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 3.7-9:23)

children.text:
anena pūrvoktasaṃdhānena sarvaṃ sakapaṃ bhāvyaṃ bhāvitaṃ kuryāt //
                            GRhtCM_3.7-9:24 //
children.translated_text: With the previously described conjunction, everything complete with <s>kalpa</s> (proportions) should be processed — should be made to undergo <s>bhāvana</s> (impregnation). (GRhtCM 3.7-9:24)

children.text:
sarvamiti kiṃ gaganarasoparasāmṛtapoharasāyasādicūrṇāni //
                            GRhtCM_3.7-9:25 //
children.translated_text: 'Everything' — meaning what? The powders of <s>gagana</s> (mica), <s>rasa</s> (mercury), <s>uparasa</s> (secondary minerals), <s>amṛta</s> (nectar-substances), <s>loha</s> (metals), <s>rasāyasa</s> (mercury-iron compounds), and so forth. (GRhtCM 3.7-9:25)

children.text:
gaganamabhrakaṃ vajrasaṃjñikaṃ rasā mahārasā
                            hiṅgupasvarṇamākṣikarūpyamākṣikaśipājatucapapacumbakavaikrāntakharparagairikasphaṭikakāsīsasaṃjñakā
                            amṛtaṃ viṣaṃ vā amṛtapohā na mṛtā amṛtā amṛtāśca te pohāś ca dhāvata iti
                            rasāḥ pūrvoktāḥ āyasā pohās teṣāṃ saṃyogajāni yāni cūrṇāni kapkāni
                            śupbābhrādīni // GRhtCM_3.7-9:26 //
children.translated_text: <s>Gagana</s> is mica, [also] known as <s>vajra</s> (diamond-mica). The <s>rasas</s> (minerals) and <s>mahārasas</s> (great minerals) are: <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar), <s>svarṇamākṣika</s> (gold-pyrite), <s>rūpyamākṣika</s> (silver-pyrite), <s>śilājatu</s> (bitite), <s>capala</s> (bismuth), <s>cumbaka</s> (loadstone), <s>vaikrānta</s> (tourmaline), <s>kharpara</s> (calamine), <s>gairika</s> (ochre), <s>sphaṭika</s> (crystal), and <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol) — so named. '<s>Amṛta</s>' means poison, or the <s>amṛtalohas</s> — those which are not dead (<s>amṛta</s>); and those lohas (metals) also run (<s>dhāvanti</s>), hence they are <s>rasas</s>. The <s>rasas</s> mentioned before — metals (<s>āyasa</s>) — and the powders (<s>kalkas</s>) born from combining them, such as <s>śulba</s> (copper), mica, and the like. (GRhtCM 3.7-9:26)

children.text: ādiśabdād uparasānām api grahaṇam // GRhtCM_3.7-9:27 //
children.translated_text: By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), the inclusion of <s>uparasas</s> (secondary minerals) is also indicated. (GRhtCM 3.7-9:27)

children.text:
na kevapametānyeva saṃdhānena bhāvyāni kiṃtvanyad api yat kiṃcic
                            cāraṇāvastu cāraṇayogyaṃ dravyaratnādikaṃ tadapyetena saṃdhānena bhāvyaṃ
                            cāraṇārtham // GRhtCM_3.7-9:28 //
children.translated_text: Not only these are to be processed with the conjunction, but also whatever other substance is suitable for <s>cāraṇa</s> (pervasion) — any material such as gems and the like — that too should be processed with this conjunction, for the purpose of <s>cāraṇa</s>. (GRhtCM 3.7-9:28)

children.text: ādau khalve mṛditāṃ piṣṭīṃ hemnaśca tāṃ rasaścarati /
children.translated_text: First, the foil of gold, ground in the mortar — that, mercury pervades.

children.text: tārasya tārakarmaṇi dattvā sūte tato gaganam // GRht_3.10 //
children.translated_text: For silver-work, giving [silver foil] to the mercury, then [one gives] <s>gagana</s> (mica). (GRht 3.10)

children.text: svarṇarūpyayoradhikāraviśeṣam āhādāv ityādi // GRhtCM_3.10:1 //
children.translated_text: Stating the specific procedure for gold and silver, he says 'first' and so forth. (GRhtCM 3.10:1)

children.text:
tato+anantaraṃ hemnaḥ svarṇasya piṣṭīṃ khapve mṛditāṃ vakṣyamāṇena iti
                            śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_3.10:2 //
children.translated_text: Then, next — the foil (<s>piṣṭī</s>) of gold — ground in the mortar — by the method to be described — this completes [the sentence]. (GRhtCM 3.10:2)

children.text: tāṃ piṣṭīṃ rasaścarati // GRhtCM_3.10:3 //
children.translated_text: Mercury pervades (<s>carati</s>) that foil. (GRhtCM 3.10:3)

children.text:
kiṃ kṛtvā piṣṭīṃ dadyāt ādau prathamataḥ sūteśvare gaganamabhrakaṃ dattvā
                            // GRhtCM_3.10:4 //
children.translated_text: Having done what should one give the foil? First — initially — having given <s>gagana</s> (mica) to the lord of mercury (<s>sūteśvara</s>). (GRhtCM 3.10:4)

children.text: hemno+adhikāro darśitaḥ // GRhtCM_3.10:5 //
children.translated_text: The procedure for gold has been shown. (GRhtCM 3.10:5)

children.text: hemakarmaṇi hemaiva tārakarmaṇi tārameva dadyāt // GRhtCM_3.10:6 //
children.translated_text: In gold-work, gold itself [should be given]; in silver-work, silver itself should be given. (GRhtCM 3.10:6)

children.text: hemni viśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: A distinction regarding gold:

children.text: svarṇaṃ pañcavidhaṃ proktaṃ prākṛtaṃ sahajāgnijam /
children.translated_text: 'Gold is said to be of five kinds: natural (<s>prākṛta</s>), innate (<s>sahaja</s>), and fire-born (<s>agnija</s>) —

children.text: etatsvarṇatrayaṃ caiva yojyaṃ ṣoḍaśavarṇakam // GRhtCM_3.10:7 //
children.translated_text: this triad of gold is to be used [when it is of] sixteen-<s>varṇa</s> [purity].' (GRhtCM 3.10:7)

children.text: khanijaṃ rasavādotthaṃ supattrīkṛtaśodhitam /
children.translated_text: 'That which is mine-born (<s>khanija</s>) or produced by alchemy (<s>rasavādottha</s>), well-beaten into foil and purified —

children.text: taccaturdaśavarṇāḍhyaṃ manujānāṃ rujāpaham // GRhtCM_3.10:8 //
children.translated_text: that is endowed with fourteen-<s>varṇa</s> [purity] and removes diseases of humans.' (GRhtCM 3.10:8)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_3.10:9 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 3.10:9)

children.text: tāre'pi viśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: A distinction regarding silver too:

children.text: kaipāse sahajaṃ rūpyaṃ khanijaṃ kṛtrimaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: 'Silver [is of three kinds]: that from the <s>kalpā</s> mine is innate; mine-born; and artificial.

children.text:
vyutkrameṇa guṇaiḥ śreṣṭhaṃ nāgottīrṇe rase hitam // GRhtCM_3.10:10
                            //
children.translated_text: In reverse order, each is superior in qualities. That which has had lead removed is beneficial for mercury[-work].' (GRhtCM 3.10:10)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_3.10:11 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 3.10:11)

children.text: tāramapi pūrvavarṇaṃ cāryam // GRhtCM_3.10:12 //
children.translated_text: Silver too should be of the aforementioned quality [for use in operations]. (GRhtCM 3.10:12)

children.text: truṭiśo dattvā mṛditaṃ sāre khalve 'bhrahemalohādi /
children.translated_text: Giving in small portions, ground in the iron mortar — mica, gold, metal, and the like —

children.text: carati rasendraḥ kṣitikhagavetasabījapūrāmlaiḥ // GRht_3.11 //
children.translated_text: the lord of mercury pervades [them], with [the juices of] earthworm (<s>kṣiti</s>), <s>khaga</s> (a plant), willow (<s>vetasa</s>), citron (<s>bījapūra</s>), and sour [substances]. (GRht 3.11)

children.text: piṣṭīmardane pātrauṣadhānyāha truṭiśa ityādi // GRhtCM_3.11:1 //
children.translated_text: Stating the vessels and medicines for grinding the foil, he says 'in small portions' and so forth. (GRhtCM 3.11:1)

children.text:
abhrahemapohādīni abhramabhrakaṃ pratītaṃ hema kanakaṃ tadeva pohaḥ
                            abhrakaṃ ca hemapohaśca tāv ādī yasya tat // GRhtCM_3.11:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Mica-gold-metal and the like' — <s>abhra</s> is mica, well-known; <s>hema</s> is gold; that itself is the <s>loha</s> (metal); mica and gold-metal — these are the beginning of which — that [compound]. (GRhtCM 3.11:2)

children.text:
evaṃvidhaṃ dravyaṃ kṣitikhagavetasabījapūrāmpaiḥ kṣitiśca khagaś ca
                            vetasaṃ ca bījapūraś ca kṣitikhagabījapūrāḥ bījapūro mātupuṅgaḥ teṣāṃ
                            trayāṇāmampāḥ tair mṛditaṃ gharṣitaṃ sat rasendraś carati //
                            GRhtCM_3.11:3 //
children.translated_text: Such substances [are ground] with [the juices of] earthworm (<s>kṣiti</s>), <s>khaga</s> (a plant), willow (<s>vetasa</s>), and citron (<s>bījapūra</s>) — <s>bījapūra</s> is the citron fruit — the sour juices of these three; ground — rubbed — with those, the lord of mercury pervades [them]. (GRhtCM 3.11:3)

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā mṛditaṃ truṭiśo 'ppamātraṃ dattvā // GRhtCM_3.11:4 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? 'In small portions' — having given [the substance] in minute quantities. (GRhtCM 3.11:4)

children.text: kasmin sāre khapve // GRhtCM_3.11:5 //
children.translated_text: In what? In the iron (<s>sāra</s>) mortar. (GRhtCM 3.11:5)

children.text: sārasya tīkṣṇajātasyāyaṃ sārastasminnevaṃvidhe // GRhtCM_3.11:6 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Sāra</s>' — of <s>sāra</s> (iron), which is of the sharp (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) variety — in such a [mortar]. (GRhtCM 3.11:6)

children.text: sāre viśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: A distinction regarding iron:

children.text: muṇḍaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ tathā kāntaṃ bhedāstasya trayodaśa /
children.translated_text: '<s>Muṇḍa</s> (cast iron), <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (steel), and <s>kānta</s> (magnetic iron) — its varieties are thirteen.

children.text: mṛdu kuṇṭhaṃ ca kaḍāraṃ trividhaṃ muṇḍamucyate // GRhtCM_3.11:7 //
children.translated_text: Soft, blunt, and <s>kaḍāra</s> (yellowish) — <s>muṇḍa</s> is said to be threefold.' (GRhtCM 3.11:7)

children.text: kharasāraṃ ca hannāpaṃ tārāvartaṃ viḍaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: '<s>Kharasāra</s>, <s>hannāla</s>, <s>tārāvarta</s>, <s>viḍa</s>,

children.text: kāpapohaṃ gajākhyaṃ ca ṣaḍvidhaṃ tīkṣṇamucyate // GRhtCM_3.11:8 //
children.translated_text: <s>kālaloha</s>, and <s>gajākhya</s> (elephant-named) — <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (steel) is said to be sixfold.' (GRhtCM 3.11:8)

children.text: kāntaṃ pohaṃ caturdhoktaṃ romakaṃ bhrāmakaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: '<s>Kānta</s> iron is said to be fourfold: <s>romaka</s>, <s>bhrāmaka</s>,

children.text: cumbakaṃ drāvakaṃ ceti guṇās tasyottarottarāḥ // GRhtCM_3.11:9 //
children.translated_text: <s>cumbaka</s>, and <s>drāvaka</s> — and its qualities are progressively superior.' (GRhtCM 3.11:9)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_3.11:10 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 3.11:10)

children.text: khapvo yathā /
children.translated_text: The mortar (<s>khalva</s>) [is described] as follows:

children.text: khapvo+aśmādyo nirudgāro dvir aṅgupakaṭāhakaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The mortar (<s>khalva</s>) should be made of stone or similar material, without fissure, with a bowl two finger-breadths [deep];

children.text: aṣṭāṅgupāvaṭī kāryā dīrghā vā vartupā tathā // GRhtCM_3.11:11 //
children.translated_text: the cavity should be eight finger-breadths, either elongated or circular.' (GRhtCM 3.11:11)

children.text: dvādaśāṅgupadīrgheṇa mardakaś caturaṅgupaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The pestle should be twelve finger-breadths long [and] four finger-breadths [wide].

children.text: mukhaṃ vṛttaṃ tu kartavyaṃ darpaṇodarasaṃnibham // GRhtCM_3.11:12 //
children.translated_text: Its face should be made round, resembling the interior of a mirror.' (GRhtCM 3.11:12)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_3.11:13 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 3.11:13)

children.text: aśmādya iti aśmapohārkāṇāṃ jñātavyaḥ // GRhtCM_3.11:14 //
children.translated_text: 'Of stone and similar materials' — [mortars] made of stone, iron, and copper should be known. (GRhtCM 3.11:14)

children.text: samukhaṃ nirmukhamathavā tulyaṃ dviguṇaṃ caturguṇaṃ vāpi /
children.translated_text: Equal [to mercury], or double, or quadruple, or also

children.text: aṣṭaguṇaṃ ṣoḍaśaguṇamathavā dvātriṃśatāguṇitam // GRht_3.12 //
children.translated_text: eightfold, sixteenfold, or multiplied by thirty-two — (GRht 3.12)

children.text: iti pattrābhrakam uktaṃ tena vidhānena cārayetsūtam /
children.translated_text: thus the foil-mica has been described; by that procedure one should make mercury pervade [it].

children.text: cāraṇa
children.translated_text: <s>Cāraṇa</s> (Pervasion):

children.text: grāsaḥ piṣṭī garbhastrilakṣaṇā cāraṇā bhavati // GRht_3.13 //
children.translated_text: <s>Grāsa</s> (devouring), <s>piṣṭī</s> (foil-incorporation), and <s>garbha</s> (internal absorption) — <s>cāraṇa</s> (pervasion) has three characteristics. (GRht 3.13)

children.text:
dhātvādīnāṃ cāraṇāyāṃ parimāṇamāha samukham ityādi // GRhtCM_3.12-13:1
                            //
children.translated_text: Stating the proportion of metals and the like in <s>cāraṇa</s>, he says 'equal' and so forth. (GRhtCM 3.12-13:1)

children.text:
iti pūrvoktaṃ pattrābhrakam uktaṃ pattrābhrakacāraṇam ityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_3.12-13:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Thus the foil-mica has been described' — meaning the <s>cāraṇa</s> of foil-mica [is described]. (GRhtCM 3.12-13:2)

children.text:
samukhaṃ mukhasahitaṃ cāraṇaṃ bhavatu vātha nirmukhaṃ mukhavarjitaṃ
                            cāraṇaṃ bhavatu ubhayatrāpi tupyaṃ samānaṃ sūtaṃ cārayet dhātvādīniti
                            śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_3.12-13:3 //
children.translated_text: 'With opening' — [whether] the <s>cāraṇa</s> is with opening (<s>samukha</s>), or 'without opening' (<s>nirmukha</s>) — without opening — in both cases, equal [quantities] of mercury should be made to pervade metals and the like — this completes [the sentence]. (GRhtCM 3.12-13:3)

children.text:
atra vikappo dviguṇaṃ sūtād dviguṇitaṃ cārayed vā caturguṇitaṃ
                            sūtāccaturguṇitaṃ vā aṣṭaguṇaṃ sūtādaṣṭaguṇitaṃ vā ṣoḍaśaguṇaṃ sūtāt
                            ṣoḍaśaguṇitaṃ vā dvātriṃśatāguṇitaṃ sūtād dvātriṃśadguṇitaṃ cārayet //
                            GRhtCM_3.12-13:4 //
children.translated_text: Here the options are: double — two times the [amount of] mercury — or fourfold — four times the mercury — or eightfold — eight times the mercury — or sixteenfold — sixteen times the mercury — or multiplied by thirty-two — thirty-two times the mercury — one should make [mercury] pervade [them]. (GRhtCM 3.12-13:4)

children.text:
tena vidhānena pūrvoktena vidhānena truṭiśo dattvetyādinā //
                            GRhtCM_3.12-13:5 //
children.translated_text: 'By that procedure' — by the previously described procedure, 'having given in small portions' and so forth. (GRhtCM 3.12-13:5)

children.text:
cāraṇā tripakṣaṇā bhavati trīṇi pakṣaṇāni cihnāni yasyāṃ sā tathoktā //
                            GRhtCM_3.12-13:6 //
children.translated_text: <s>Cāraṇa</s> has three characteristics — [it is that] which has three signs (<s>lakṣaṇas</s>) — it is so called. (GRhtCM 3.12-13:6)

children.text:
kathaṃ grāsaḥ abhrakasya grāsanaṃ nirmukhatvena samukhatvena vāparā piṣṭī
                            rasenābhrāder mepanaṃ punargarbho rasasya garbhe rasarūpaṃ gaganaṃ
                            tiṣṭhatīti // GRhtCM_3.12-13:7 //
children.translated_text: How [are these three]? <s>Grāsa</s> — the devouring of mica, either without opening or with opening. The second is <s>piṣṭī</s> — the amalgamation of mica and the like with mercury. The third is <s>garbha</s> — [when] <s>gagana</s> (mica) in mercury-form resides within the interior of mercury. (GRhtCM 3.12-13:7)

children.text: śpokadvayānvayasambandhād yugmam // GRhtCM_3.12-13:8 //
children.translated_text: The connection [of these two verses] forms a pair, due to the syntactic relationship of the two half-verses. (GRhtCM 3.12-13:8)

children.text: wrong ideas about jāraṇa
children.translated_text: Wrong ideas about <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion):

children.text: dolanavidhinā yair api nānāvidhabhaṅgasaṃskṛtaṃ gaganam /
children.translated_text: Even by those who, through the <s>dolana</s> (swinging) method, [process] mica treated with various bhaṅga-preparations —

children.text: cāraṇavidhau pradiṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ noddhūyamānaṃ taiḥ // GRht_3.14 //
children.translated_text: [mica] prescribed in the <s>cāraṇa</s> procedure is not seen to be sublimated by them. (GRht 3.14)

children.text: anye 'pi tucchamatayo gandhakaniṣpiṣṭiśulbapiṣṭirajaḥ /
children.translated_text: Others too, of shallow intellect — [thinking that] the powder of sulphur-paste and copper-paste,

children.text: dolanavidhinoddhūtaṃ rasajīrṇaṃ taditi manyante // GRht_3.15 //
children.translated_text: sublimated by the <s>dolana</s> method, is [mercury that has] digested [mica] — thus they think [erroneously]. (GRht 3.15)

children.text:
iti gaganādigrāsapramāṇaṃ kathitam atha cāraṇāvidhānamāha
                            dopanavidhinetyādi // GRhtCM_3.14-15:1 //
children.translated_text: Thus the measure of <s>gagana</s> (mica) and other substances for <s>grāsa</s> (devouring) has been stated. Now he states the procedure of <s>cāraṇa</s>, with 'by the <s>dolana</s> method' and so forth. (GRhtCM 3.14-15:1)

children.text:
gaganamabhrakaṃ yair auṣadhaiḥ piṣṭaṃ peṣitaṃ bhavati tair evauṣadhair
                            nāppamānair bahumānair nānāvidhabhaṅgasaṃskṛtaṃ kuryāditi śeṣaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_3.14-15:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Gagana</s> (mica) — that which is ground with certain medicines — with those very medicines, not in small quantities but in large quantities, processed with various <s>bhaṅga</s>-preparations — one should make [it so] — this completes [the sentence]. (GRhtCM 3.14-15:2)

children.text:
nānāvidhā anekaprakārā ye bhaṅgās taraṃgā āgamābdhijātās taiḥ saṃskṛtam
                            upaskṛtam // GRhtCM_3.14-15:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Various <s>bhaṅgas</s>' — manifold, of many kinds — the <s>bhaṅgas</s> (wave-like processes) that arise from the ocean of tradition (<s>āgama</s>) — processed, prepared by those. (GRhtCM 3.14-15:3)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ gaganaṃ māraṇavidhinā pañcatvavidhānena uddiṣṭam uddeśitam
                            /
children.translated_text: Of what qualification is the <s>gagana</s> (mica)? Prescribed by the <s>māraṇa</s> method — the procedure of reduction to ash (<s>pañcatva</s>).

children.text:
evaṃvidham api gaganaṃ dopanavidhinā cāraṇāyāṃ yojyamiti bhāvaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_3.14-15:4 //
children.translated_text: Even such mica should be employed in <s>cāraṇa</s> through the <s>dolana</s> (swinging) method — this is the purport. (GRhtCM 3.14-15:4)

children.text: adhunāppamatīnāṃ matam āhānya ityādi /
children.translated_text: Now he states the view of those of little intelligence, with 'others' and so forth.

children.text:
anye mahadbhyo 'pare tucchamatayas tucchā stokā matirbuddhiryeṣāṃ te
                            tathoktāḥ appabuddhaya iti yāvat // GRhtCM_3.14-15:5 //
children.translated_text: 'Others' — those apart from the great ones, 'of shallow intellect' — those whose intellect (<s>mati</s>, <s>buddhi</s>) is meager (<s>tuccha</s>, <s>stoka</s>) — they are so called — meaning those of little intelligence. (GRhtCM 3.14-15:5)

children.text:
rasaṃ jīrṇaṃ jāraṇasaṃskāropapannaṃ rasaṃ manyante iti //
                            GRhtCM_3.14-15:6 //
children.translated_text: They think that [such] mercury has undergone <s>jāraṇa</s> — has been endowed with the <s>jāraṇa saṃskāra</s> (digestion process). (GRhtCM 3.14-15:6)

children.text:
kiṃ gandhakaniṣpiṣṭiśupbapiṣṭirajo gandhakena yā niṣpiṣṭiḥ piṣṭībhūtā
                            śupbena yā piṣṭiḥ piṣṭībhūtā tāmrapiṣṭītyarthaḥ gandhakaniṣpiṣṭiśca
                            śupbapiṣṭiśca tayoryadrajaḥ pāṃśuḥ gandhakapiṣṭī yathā /
children.translated_text: What [do they use]? The powder of sulphur-paste and copper-paste — that paste which is made with sulphur, that which is made into paste with copper (<s>śulba</s>), meaning copper-paste — and the powder (<s>rajas</s>, dust) of those two. The sulphur-paste [is prepared] as follows:

children.text: gandhapāṣāṇacūrṇaṃ ca caṇakasya rasena tu /
children.translated_text: 'The powder of <s>gandhapāṣāṇa</s> (orpiment/sulphur-stone), with the juice of chickpea,

children.text: bhāvayetsaptavāraṃ tu strīraktena ca saptadhā // GRhtCM_3.14-15:7 //
children.translated_text: should be impregnated seven times, and seven times with women's menstrual blood.' (GRhtCM 3.14-15:7)

children.text: śuddhasūtaṃ papaikaṃ tu kharpare dāpayettataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Pure mercury, one <s>pala</s> [in quantity], should then be placed in a <s>kharpara</s> (saucer);

children.text: bhāvitaṃ gandhakaṃ dadyānnarapiṇḍena saṃyutam // GRhtCM_3.14-15:8 //
children.translated_text: the impregnated sulphur should be given, combined with a <s>narapiṇḍa</s> (human-shaped lump).' (GRhtCM 3.14-15:8)

children.text: dopāyantre'pi tāpena piṣṭikā bhavati kṣaṇāt // GRhtCM_3.14-15:9 //
children.translated_text: Even in the <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing-apparatus), through heating, a pellet (<s>piṣṭikā</s>) is formed instantly. (GRhtCM 3.14-15:9)
Thus. (GRhtCM 3.14-15:10)

children.text: eva śupbapiṣṭyapi jāyate // GRhtCM_3.14-15:11 //
children.translated_text: Indeed, [it can also be formed] through the copper pellet [method]. (GRhtCM 3.14-15:11)

children.text:
kimbhūtaṃ gandhakaniṣpiṣṭiśupbapiṣṭirajaḥ dopanavidhinodbhūtaṃ
