                            dopikāyantravidhānenotpannam // GRhtCM_3.14-15:12 //
children.translated_text: Of what kind? The sulfur pellet and copper pellet [methods] — produced by the <s>dolana</s> (swing) procedure — generated by the method of the <s>dolikāyantra</s> (swing-apparatus). (GRhtCM 3.14-15:12)

children.text: iti yaduktaṃ tadasamañjasamiti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_3.14-15:13 //
children.translated_text: What was stated thus — that is inappropriate — this is the purport. (GRhtCM 3.14-15:13)

children.text: golakamukha
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Golakamukha</s> (Pellet-mouth method)

children.text: tailādikataptarase hāṭakatārādigolakamukhena /
children.translated_text: When mercury is heated with oils and the like, through the pellet-mouth [method] with gold, silver, and the like,

children.text: carati ghanaṃ rasarājo hemādibhir eti piṇḍatvam // GRht_3.16 //
children.translated_text: the king of mercury consumes [mica] densely, and through gold and other [metals] it attains compactness. (GRht 3.16)

children.text:
samukhacāraṇāntarbhūtaṃ vāsanāmukhacāraṇaṃ darśayannāha taipetyādi //
                            GRhtCM_3.16:1 //
children.translated_text: Showing the <s>vāsanāmukhacāraṇā</s> (feeding through oil-mouth), which is included within the <s>samukhacāraṇā</s> (mouth-feeding), [the commentator] says 'taila' and so forth. (GRhtCM 3.16:1)

children.text:
rasarājaḥ pārado hāṭakatārādi svarṇarūpyādi dhātudravyaṃ
                            kṛtrimākṛtrimātmakanavasaṃkhyākaṃ pūrvamuktaṃ carati bhakṣati //
                            GRhtCM_3.16:2 //
children.translated_text: The king of mercury (<s>pārada</s>) consumes — devours — metallic substances of gold, silver, and the like — the nine [metals] of both artificial and natural [kinds] previously mentioned. (GRhtCM 3.16:2)

children.text: kena gopakamukhena // GRhtCM_3.16:3 //
children.translated_text: By what [method]? Through the <s>golaka</s>-mouth (pellet-mouth). (GRhtCM 3.16:3)

children.text:
gopakaśca mukhaviśeṣaḥ tena viḍasya gopakenetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.16:4
                            //
children.translated_text: A <s>golaka</s> (pellet) is a particular kind of mouth [i.e., binding medium]; by it — meaning through the pellet [form] of <s>viḍa</s> (a binding substance). (GRhtCM 3.16:4)

children.text: kva sati taipādikataptarase sati // GRhtCM_3.16:5 //
children.translated_text: Under what condition? When the mercury is heated with oils and the like. (GRhtCM 3.16:5)

children.text:
taipam ādiḥ yeṣāṃ te taipādikās taipavasāmūtraśukrapuṣpāḥ etaistapto yo
                            rasa uṣṇatvaṃ nīto yo 'sau pāradastasmin satyevaṃ ghanamabhrakaṃ carati
                            rasendraḥ // GRhtCM_3.16:6 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Taila</s>' (oil) is the first of which — those beginning with oil are oils and the like — oils, fats, urines, seminal fluids, and menstrual fluids. Heated — brought to a state of warmth — that mercury in which [this is done]; when this is the case, the lord of mercury consumes <s>ghana</s> (dense, i.e., mica) thus. (GRhtCM 3.16:6)

children.text:
punarhemādibhirnavakairgrāsīkṛtaiḥ piṇḍatvameti nibiḍatvaṃ prāpnoti //
                            GRhtCM_3.16:7 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, through the nine [metals] beginning with gold, having been made into morsels [for mercury], it attains compactness — achieves density. (GRhtCM 3.16:7)

children.text: taipāni yathā /
children.translated_text: The oils are as follows:

children.text: kaṅguṇītumbinīghoṣākarañjaśrīphapodbhavam /
children.translated_text: Derived from <s>kaṅguṇī</s>, <s>tumbinī</s>, <s>ghoṣā</s>, <s>karañja</s>, and <s>śrīphala</s>;

children.text: kaṭuvātārisiddhārthasomarājīvibhītajam // GRhtCM_3.16:8 //
children.translated_text: from <s>kaṭu</s> (pungent seeds), <s>vātāri</s>, <s>siddhārtha</s> (mustard), <s>somarājī</s>, and <s>vibhīta</s>; (GRhtCM 3.16:8)

children.text: atasījaṃ mahākāpīnimbajaṃ tipajaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: from flax (<s>atasī</s>), from <s>mahākālī</s>, neem (<s>nimba</s>), sesame (<s>tila</s>) likewise;

children.text: apāmārgo devadāpī dantītumbaruvigrahāḥ // GRhtCM_3.16:9 //
children.translated_text: <s>Apāmārga</s> (rough chaff), <s>devadālī</s>, <s>dantī</s> (croton), and <s>tumbaru</s> (Zanthoxylum); (GRhtCM 3.16:9)

children.text: aṅkoponmattabhappātaphapebhyas taipasambhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: from <s>aṅkola</s>, <s>unmatta</s> (datura), <s>bhallātaka</s> (marking nut), and <s>phala</s> (fruits) — oils are produced. (GRhtCM 3.16:10)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_3.16:10 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 3.16:10)

children.text: vasā yathā /
children.translated_text: The fats (<s>vasā</s>) are as follows:

children.text: ajoṣṭrakharameṣāṇāṃ mahiṣasya vasā tathā /
children.translated_text: The fat of goat, camel, donkey, sheep, and buffalo likewise. (GRhtCM 3.16:11)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_3.16:11 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 3.16:11)

children.text: mūtrapuṣpaśukrāṇi yathā /
children.translated_text: The urines, menstrual fluids, and seminal fluids are as follows:

children.text: mūtrāṇi hastikarabhamahiṣīkharavājinām /
children.translated_text: The urines of elephant, young elephant, female buffalo, donkey, and horse;

children.text: striyaḥ puṃsas tathā mūtraṃ puṣpaṃ vīryaṃ ca yojayet /
children.translated_text: the urine of woman and man; likewise menstrual fluid and semen should be employed. (GRhtCM 3.16:12)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_3.16:12 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 3.16:12)

children.text: mukha:: śukapicchamukha
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Śukapicchamukha</s> (Parrot-feather-mouth method)

children.text: anye svacchaṃ kṛtvā śukapicchamukhena cārayanti ghanam /
children.translated_text: Others, having made [mercury] clear, feed it mica through the parrot-feather-mouth,

children.text: siddhopadeśavidhinā āśitagrāse na śuṣkeṇa // GRht_3.17 //
children.translated_text: by the method instructed by the <s>Siddha</s>s — with a moist morsel, not a dry one. (GRht 3.17)

children.text: tasminnabhiprāye 'nyamatam āhānya ityādi // GRhtCM_3.17:1 //
children.translated_text: In the context of this [same] intent, [the commentator] states another opinion with 'anye' (others) and so forth. (GRhtCM 3.17:1)

children.text:
eke uktavidhānena cāraṇāṃ kurvanti anye apare rasaṃ pāradaṃ svacchaṃ
                            kṛtvā svedanādyaṣṭasaṃskāropasaṃskṛtaṃ vidhāya vā hiṅgupotthaṃ ghanam
                            abhrakaṃ cārayanti abhrakasya cāraṇāṃ kurvanti // GRhtCM_3.17:2 //
children.translated_text: Some perform <s>cāraṇā</s> (feeding) by the stated method; others — different [practitioners] — having made the mercury (<s>pārada</s>) clear — prepared through the eight <s>saṃskāra</s>s (purificatory processes) beginning with <s>svedana</s> — or having rendered it as mercury extracted from <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar) — feed it <s>ghana</s> (mica) — perform the <s>cāraṇā</s> of mica [into mercury]. (GRhtCM 3.17:2)

children.text:
kena śukapicchamukhena śukapicchaṃ saṃdhānaviśeṣaḥ mukhaṃ viśeṣo yeṣāṃ
                            saṃdhānānāṃ tena // GRhtCM_3.17:3 //
children.translated_text: By what [method]? Through the <s>śukapiccha</s>-mouth — <s>śukapiccha</s> (parrot-feather) is a particular type of binding medium; that which has this as its mouth [i.e., form] — through that. (GRhtCM 3.17:3)

children.text:
kva sati cārayanti āśitagrāse sati bhuktakavape sati punaś cāryam
                            ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.17:4 //
children.translated_text: Under what condition do they feed [it]? When a morsel has been consumed — when a portion has been eaten [by the mercury]; then further feeding should be done — that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 3.17:4)

children.text:
kena siddhopadeśavidhinā siddhā rasasiddhā nityanāthavīranāthādayaḥ
                            pūrvoktāḥ teṣāṃ ya upadeśavidhis tena // GRhtCM_3.17:5 //
children.translated_text: By what [authority]? By the method taught by the <s>Siddha</s>s — the <s>Rasasiddha</s>s (mercury-adepts) such as <s>Nityanātha</s>, <s>Vīranātha</s>, and others previously mentioned — by their instructional method. (GRhtCM 3.17:5)

children.text:
na śuṣkeṇa saṃdhānenārdrībhāvāt nīrasatāṃ prāptena punaścāraṇā na syāt //
                            GRhtCM_3.17:6 //
children.translated_text: Not with a dry one — not with a binding medium that has become dry through loss of moisture; with [such a dry medium], further <s>cāraṇā</s> should not be done. (GRhtCM 3.17:6)

children.text: śukapicchaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: The <s>śukapiccha</s> [preparation] is as follows:

children.text: bhasmakṣārān suśuṣkāṃstu kṣārāṃśca pavaṇāni ca /
children.translated_text: Having mixed ash-alkalis, well-dried, and alkaline [substances] together with salts,

children.text: āpoḍya hy ampavargeṇa śupbabhāṇḍe nidhāpayet // GRhtCM_3.17:7 //
children.translated_text: with [decoctions of] the <s>amla</s>-group (sour substances), one should deposit [them] in a copper vessel. (GRhtCM 3.17:7)

children.text: yāvacca śukapicchābhamabhrakaṃ tena bhāvayet /
children.translated_text: Until [the preparation] resembles a parrot's feather, one should treat the mica with it;

children.text: grasate tatkṣaṇātsūto gopakastu vidhīyate // GRhtCM_3.17:8 //
children.translated_text: mercury then consumes [the mica] instantly — the <s>golaka</s> (pellet) is [thus] prepared. (GRhtCM 3.17:8)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_3.17:9 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 3.17:9)

children.text: mercury:: cāraṇa
children.translated_text: [Section:] Mercury — <s>Cāraṇā</s> (Feeding/Assimilation)

children.text: athavā mākṣikagaganaṃ samabhāgaṃ paṭuyutaṃ pakvam /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, combining equal parts of <s>mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite) and <s>gagana</s> (mica), joined with salt and cooked,

children.text: prakṣipya lohapātre svedāntaścarati kṛṣṇābhram // GRht_3.18 //
children.translated_text: placing [them] in a metal vessel — at the end of steaming, [mercury] consumes the black mica. (GRht 3.18)

children.text: anyamatābhiprāye prakārāntaram āhāthavetyādi // GRhtCM_3.18:1 //
children.translated_text: In the context of another opinion, [the commentator] states an alternative with 'athavā' (alternatively) and so forth. (GRhtCM 3.18:1)

children.text:
pūrvoktaṃ vidhānaṃ kuryāt athavā pakṣāntare idaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ kuryāt //
                            GRhtCM_3.18:2 //
children.translated_text: One may perform the previously stated procedure; alternatively, in another view, one may do what is about to be described. (GRhtCM 3.18:2)

children.text:
mākṣikagaganamiti mākṣikena yuktaṃ gaganam abhrakaṃ samabhāgaṃ dvayaṃ
                            tupyabhāgaṃ puṭitaṃ bhāvitaṃ yat paṭu saindhavaṃ pavaṇaṃ
                            śāstrāntarasāmyād ampavargeṇa puṭitaṃ tena yutaṃ mipitaṃ sat pakvaṃ
                            vahnipuṭitaṃ kuryāt iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_3.18:3 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Mākṣikagagana</s>' means mica combined with <s>mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite); in equal parts — the two in equal portions; calcined — treated by roasting; '<s>paṭu</s>' is rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>); from the similarity with other texts, [it means] calcined with the <s>amla</s>-group (sour substances); combined with this — mixed; 'cooked' means calcined with fire — this is the completion. (GRhtCM 3.18:3)

children.text:
kiṃ kṛtvā pohapātre muṇḍādibhājane prakṣipya madhye sthāpya //
                            GRhtCM_3.18:4 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? Having placed [it] in a metal vessel — in a container such as <s>muṇḍa</s> (a type of iron pot) — having placed [it] in the middle. (GRhtCM 3.18:4)

children.text:
evaṃvidhaṃ kṛṣṇābhraṃ svedāntarvahnitāpamadhye rasaḥ pāradaś carati
                            grasati mākṣikasaṃyogāt kṣipram iti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_3.18:5 //
children.translated_text: Such black mica — at the end of steaming, in the midst of fire's heat — the mercury (<s>pārada</s>) consumes, devours [it] — quickly, due to the conjunction with <s>mākṣika</s> — this is the purport. (GRhtCM 3.18:5)

children.text: taṃ pravakṣyāmyupadeśaṃ gandhābhrakasaṃpraveśanaṃ yena /
children.translated_text: I shall describe that instruction by which the entry of sulfur and mica [into mercury is achieved],

children.text: pakṣachinnaś ca raso yogyaḥ syād rasarasāyanayoḥ // GRht_3.19 //
children.translated_text: and by which mercury, with its wings clipped, becomes fit for both medicine and <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation). (GRht 3.19)

children.text: upadeśavidhānamāha tam ityādi /
children.translated_text: He states the instructional method with 'tam' (that) and so forth.

children.text:
yenopadeśena gandhābhrakapraveśanaṃ gandhapāṣāṇasaṃyogād
                            yadabhrapraveśena bhavati abhrasya pāradāntaḥpraveśo bhavati
                            tamupadeśamahaṃ kavir vakṣyāmi kathayiṣye // GRhtCM_3.19:1 //
children.translated_text: That instruction by which the entry of sulfur and mica [is achieved] — through the conjunction with sulfur stone (<s>gandhapāṣāṇa</s>), by which the entry of mica [into mercury] occurs — that instruction I, the poet, shall describe — shall speak. (GRhtCM 3.19:1)

children.text: atisāmīpyād vartamāna eva ḷṭ // GRhtCM_3.19:2 //
children.translated_text: Due to extreme proximity [of the future event], the present tense is used. (GRhtCM 3.19:2)

children.text: tu punaḥ // GRhtCM_3.19:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Tu' [means] furthermore. (GRhtCM 3.19:3)

children.text:
pakṣachinnaśca raso rasarasāyanayor yogyaḥ rase jvarādiroganāśake
                            jvarāṅkuśādau rasāyane ca jarāvyādhināśane prayoge yogyaḥ samarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_3.19:4 //
children.translated_text: And mercury with its wings clipped becomes fit for both <s>rasa</s> (medicine) — [i.e.,] in preparations that destroy diseases such as fever, like <s>Jvarāṅkuśa</s> — and for <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) — in applications that destroy old age and disease — fit, meaning capable. (GRhtCM 3.19:4)

children.text: yathā mañjaryām /
children.translated_text: As [stated] in the <s>Mañjarī</s>:

children.text: mārito dehaśuddhyarthaṃ mūrchito vyādhināśanaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Killed [mercury] is for body-purification; stupefied [mercury] destroys diseases.

children.text: rasabhasma kvacidroge dehārthe mūrchitaṃ kvacit // GRhtCM_3.19:5 //
children.translated_text: Mercury-ash [is used] in certain diseases; stupefied [mercury] in certain [cases] for the body. (GRhtCM 3.19:5)

children.text: baddhaṃ dvābhyāṃ prayuñjīta śāstradṛṣṭena karmaṇā // GRhtCM_3.19:6 //
children.translated_text: Bound [mercury] should be employed for both [medicine and rasāyana], according to the procedure seen in the texts.' (GRhtCM 3.19:6)

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_3.19:7 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 3.19:7)

children.text:
gandhābhrakapraveśena pakṣachinno 'capo bhaved iti bhāvaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_3.19:8 //
children.translated_text: Through the entry of sulfur and mica, [mercury] becomes wing-clipped and immobile — this is the purport. (GRhtCM 3.19:8)

children.text: sulfur:: special role in alchemy
children.translated_text: [Section:] Sulfur — special role in alchemy

children.text: rasarājarāgadāyī bījānāṃ pākajāraṇasamarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: It gives passion (<s>rāga</s>) to the king of mercury; it is capable of cooking and assimilating (<s>jāraṇa</s>) the seeds;

children.text: sūtakapakṣacchedī rasabandhe gandhako 'bhihitaḥ // GRht_3.20 //
children.translated_text: it clips the wings of mercury — sulfur is described [as essential] in the binding of mercury. (GRht 3.20)

children.text: gandhakaṃ viśeṣayannāha rasarājetyādi // GRhtCM_3.20:1 //
children.translated_text: Specifying sulfur, [the commentator] says 'rasarāja' and so forth. (GRhtCM 3.20:1)

children.text:
rasabandhane pāradabandhane gandhako 'bhitaḥ pepinakaḥ sarvotkṛṣṭaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_3.20:2 //
children.translated_text: In the binding of mercury — in the fixation of <s>pārada</s> — sulfur is the preeminent one, the most excellent of all. (GRhtCM 3.20:2)

children.text:
kuto yataḥ sūtakapakṣacchedī gandhakaḥ sūtasya pāradasya pakṣau chinatti
                            // GRhtCM_3.20:3 //
children.translated_text: Why? Because sulfur clips the wings of mercury — it cuts the wings (volatility) of <s>pārada</s>. (GRhtCM 3.20:3)

children.text:
punaḥ kuto rasarājarāgadāyī rasarājaḥ pāradaḥ tasya rāgaṃ rañjanaṃ
                            dadātīti // GRhtCM_3.20:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, why? Because it gives passion (<s>rāga</s>, color/tinge) to the king of mercury — it gives coloring to <s>pārada</s>. (GRhtCM 3.20:4)

children.text:
punaḥ kuto bījānāṃ pākajāraṇasamarthaḥ pākaśca jāraṇaṃ ca pākajāraṇe //
                            GRhtCM_3.20:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, why? Because it is capable of <s>pāka</s> (cooking) and <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation) of the seeds — cooking and assimilation [are the processes]. (GRhtCM 3.20:5)

children.text: mercury:: māraṇa, pakṣacheda
children.translated_text: [Section:] Mercury — <s>māraṇa</s> (killing) and <s>pakṣacheda</s> (wing-clipping)

children.text: dattvā khalve truṭiśo gandhakam ādau rasaṃ ca truṭiśo+api /
children.translated_text: Having placed sulfur little by little in the mortar, and mercury also little by little,

children.text: tāvacca mardanīyaṃ yāvatsā piṣṭikā bhavati // GRht_3.21 //
children.translated_text: one should grind [them] until that becomes a pellet (<s>piṣṭikā</s>). (GRht 3.21)

children.text: tadanu ca drutabalivasayā samabhāganiyojitaṃ tathā gaganam /
children.translated_text: Then, with melted <s>balivasā</s> (aquatic animal fat), having combined equal parts of mica,

children.text: truṭiśo rasaṃ ca dattvā kurvīta yathepsitāṃ piṣṭim // GRht_3.22 //
children.translated_text: and adding mercury little by little, one should prepare the desired pellet. (GRht 3.22)

children.text: sāpi ca dīptairupalairnipātyate 'dho 'tha dīpikāyantre /
children.translated_text: And that [pellet] is brought down in the <s>dīpikāyantra</s> (lamp-apparatus) by blazing coals.

children.text: tadanu ca nirmuktamalo nikṛntapakṣo 'bhragandhābhyām // GRht_3.23 //
children.translated_text: Thereafter, freed from impurity, [mercury has] its wings clipped through mica and sulfur. (GRht 3.23)

children.text: bhasmākāraś ca raso hemnā saha yujyate sa ca dvaṃdve /
children.translated_text: And mercury in ash-form combines with gold — and that in pairs.

children.text:
gandhakābhrakābhyāṃ rasapakṣāpakartanaṃ yathā syāttathāha dattvetyādi
                                // GRhtCM_3.21-23:1 //
children.translated_text: The cutting of mercury's wings through sulfur and mica — how it should be [done] — [the text] says 'dattvā' (having placed) and so forth. (GRhtCM 3.21-23:1)

children.text:
ādau prathamaṃ khalve lohārkāśmamaye gandhakaṃ truṭiśo dattvā
                                alpamātraṃ vāraṃ vāraṃ gandharasau dattvā tāvanmardanīyaṃ yāvat sā
                                piṣṭikā ekaśarīratā bhavati kajjaliketi vyaktārthaḥ //
                                GRhtCM_3.21-23:2 //
children.translated_text: First, having placed sulfur little by little — in small quantities, repeatedly — in a mortar made of metal, sun-stone, or stone, and mercury; one should grind until that becomes a pellet — a unified body — this is <s>kajjalī</s> (black paste) — the meaning is clear. (GRhtCM 3.21-23:2)

children.text:
tadanu tatpaścāt rasagandhakapiṣṭīkaraṇānantaraṃ tatra
                                rasagandhakapiṣṭyā gaganam abhrakaṃ samabhāganiyojitaṃ
                                gandharasābhyāṃ tulyāṃśaṃ militaṃ kāryam ityarthaḥ //
                                GRhtCM_3.21-23:3 //
children.translated_text: Then — after that — after making the mercury-sulfur pellet, upon that mercury-sulfur pellet, mica should be combined in equal parts — meaning mixed in equal portions with the mercury and sulfur. (GRhtCM 3.21-23:3)

children.text:
kayā kṛtvā drutabalivasayā drutā dravībhūtā yā balivasā
                                bhekamatsyakarkaṭaśiśumārāṇāṃ tailarūpā śarīrajātā tayā //
                                GRhtCM_3.21-23:4 //
children.translated_text: With what [medium]? Having prepared with melted <s>balivasā</s> — <s>balivasā</s> that has become liquid — the fat of frogs, fish, crabs, and crocodiles, of an oily nature, produced from the body — with that. (GRhtCM 3.21-23:4)

children.text:
samabhāgābhrakaniyojanānantaraṃ balivasayā mardanaṃ kāryamiti
                                tātparyārthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.21-23:5 //
children.translated_text: After combining the mica in equal parts, grinding should be done with <s>balivasā</s> — this is the purport. (GRhtCM 3.21-23:5)

children.text: balivasā yathā /
children.translated_text: The <s>balivasā</s> [sources] are as follows:

children.text: bhekamatsyabhavā yā tu karkaṭasya vasāthavā /
children.translated_text: 'That which is from frogs and fish, or the fat of crabs,

children.text: bhāvyam ebhiḥ kramādgandhaṃ śiśumāravasāpi vā // GRhtCM_3.21-23:6 //
children.translated_text: with these, sulfur should be treated in sequence; or the fat of crocodile.' (GRhtCM 3.21-23:6)

children.text: etāsvekā balivasā samyak sūtasya bandhinī /
children.translated_text: 'One of these <s>balivasā</s>s properly binds mercury

children.text: rañjanaṃ caiva kurute maṇimūṣavidhikramāt // GRhtCM_3.21-23:7 //
children.translated_text: and effects the coloring [of metals], by the method of <s>maṇimūṣā</s> (gem-crucible) in sequence.' (GRhtCM 3.21-23:7)

children.text: eṣā balivasā nāma kṣaṇādbadhnāti sūtakam /
children.translated_text: 'This [substance] named <s>balivasā</s> binds mercury instantly.'
Thus. (GRhtCM 3.21-23:8)

children.text: rasagandhābhrapiṣṭiṃ kurvītetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.21-23:9 //
children.translated_text: One should prepare the mercury-sulfur-mica pellet — that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 3.21-23:9)

children.text:
sā pūrvoktā rasagandhābhrapiṣṭir athetyanantaraṃ dīpikāyantre
                                'dhaḥpātane raso nirmuktamalas tyaktadoṣo bhavati //
                                GRhtCM_3.21-23:10 //
children.translated_text: That previously mentioned mercury-sulfur-mica pellet — then, in the <s>dīpikāyantra</s> (lamp-apparatus), by <s>adhaḥpātana</s> (downward sublimation), the mercury becomes freed from impurity — its defects are removed. (GRhtCM 3.21-23:10)

children.text:
tasminnirmuktamale sati nikṛntapakṣaḥ chinnapakṣo bhavati //
                                GRhtCM_3.21-23:11 //
children.translated_text: When [mercury has] become freed from impurity, it becomes <s>nikṛntapakṣa</s> (wing-clipped) — its wings (volatility) are cut. (GRhtCM 3.21-23:11)

children.text:
kābhyām abhragandhābhyām abhraṃ ca gandhaśca abhragandhau tābhyāṃ
                                gandhakāntaḥ saṃyogāt sukhaṃ rasābhrapiṣṭirbhavet yato gandhako
                                dvaṃdvamelanasamarthaḥ kiṃ punarbalivasayeti tṛtīyaślokārthaḥ //
                                GRhtCM_3.21-23:12 //
children.translated_text: By which two? By mica and sulphur — mica and sulphur [together form] the compound 'mica-sulphur'; by their conjunction with sulphur, the paste of mercury and mica is easily [made], since sulphur is capable of uniting pairs [of substances] — how much more so with the [potent] offering? — this is the meaning of the third verse. (GRhtCM 3.21–23:12)

children.text: kulakam iti // GRhtCM_3.21-23:13 //
children.translated_text: This is a group (<s>kulaka</s>) [of verses]. (GRhtCM 3.21–23:13)

children.text:
pūrvasaṃskṛtarasasyākāraṃ kāryāntarasampattiṃ cāha bhasmetyādi //
                                GRhtCM_3.21-23:14 //
children.translated_text: He describes the form and further accomplishments of the previously processed mercury, with 'ash' and so forth. (GRhtCM 3.21–23:14)

children.text: ca punaḥ // GRhtCM_3.21-23:15 //
children.translated_text: 'Ca' (and) means furthermore. (GRhtCM 3.21–23:15)

children.text:
tato+adhaḥpātanād raso bhasmākāro bhasmasadṛśo bhavet //
                                GRhtCM_3.21-23:16 //
children.translated_text: Then, through downward distillation (<s>adhaḥpātana</s>), the mercury becomes ash-like in appearance — resembling ash. (GRhtCM 3.21–23:16)

children.text:
sa ca bhasmākāro rasaḥ hemnā svarṇena sārdham ubhayamelane yujyate
                                karmavidā iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_3.21-23:17 //
children.translated_text: And that ash-like mercury, together with gold (<s>heman</s>), is united in a mutual combination — 'by one skilled in the procedure' is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 3.21–23:17)

children.text:
athavā samuccaye avyayo rekārthasambandhāt pakṣāntare ca //
                                GRhtCM_3.21-23:18 //
children.translated_text: Alternatively, 'athavā' is an indeclinable [particle used] in the sense of conjunction, with reference to the alternative view. (GRhtCM 3.21–23:18)

children.text: mercury:: māraṇa, compound with gold
children.translated_text: [Section: Mercury — killing (<s>māraṇa</s>), compound with gold]

children.text: athavā gandhakapiṣṭiṃ paktvā drutagandhakasya madhye tu // GRht_3.24 //
children.translated_text: 'Or alternatively, having cooked the sulphur-paste, in the midst of melted sulphur —' (GRht 3.24)

children.text: sā cāpi hemapiṣṭirvipacyate gandhake bhūyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'that gold-paste too is cooked again in sulphur;

children.text: itthaṃ hemnā sūto milati dvaṃdve tathā kṣaṇānmriyate // GRht_3.25 //
children.translated_text: thus mercury unites with gold, and in the paired [compound], it dies in a moment.' (GRht 3.25)

children.text:
athavā hemnā saha pūrvarasavidhānena gandhapiṣṭiṃ kuryāt athavā
                            drutagandhakasya dravībhūtagandhakasya madhye paktvā vahniyogena
                            supakvaṃ kṛtvā rasaṃ piṣṭivat rasahemagandhapiṣṭiṃ kuryādityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_3.24-25:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Alternatively, with gold, by the previously described method for mercury, one should make a sulphur-paste; or alternatively, having cooked it by combination with fire in the midst of melted sulphur — sulphur that has become liquid — having thoroughly cooked the mercury, one should make a paste of mercury, gold, and sulphur in the manner of a paste — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 3.24–25:1)

children.text:
pūrvoddiṣṭasya dvaṃdvamepanasya vidhānamāha setyādi // GRhtCM_3.24-25:2
                            //
children.translated_text: He states the procedure for the previously described paired combination, with 'that' and so forth. (GRhtCM 3.24–25:2)

children.text: ca punaḥ // GRhtCM_3.24-25:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Ca' (and) means furthermore. (GRhtCM 3.24–25:3)

children.text:
sā pūrvoktā hemapiṣṭiḥ rasahemagandhakṛtaretasoḥ sambandhaḥ sadātanaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_3.24-25:4 //
children.translated_text: That previously described gold-paste — the relationship between the mercury-gold-sulphur compound is permanent. (GRhtCM 3.24–25:4)

The paste united with gold — that which enters into the paste-combination — that gold-paste is again cooked in sulphur; the cooking should be done skillfully, as before, in sulphur. (GRhtCM 3.24–25:5)

children.text:
ittham uktavidhānena hemnā saha sūtaḥ pārado mipati granthimeti kva sati
                            dvaṃdve sati ubhayasaṃyoge sati // GRhtCM_3.24-25:6 //
children.translated_text: 'Thus' — by the described procedure — mercury (<s>sūta</s>, <s>pārada</s>) unites with gold, forms a knot. Where? When in the paired [compound], when there is mutual conjunction. (GRhtCM 3.24–25:6)

children.text:
tathoktavidhānena dvaṃdve mipati sati tatkāpād appakāpato mriyate
                            pañcatvamupayāti // GRhtCM_3.24-25:7 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by the described procedure, when the pairing has been accomplished, in a moment — in a short time — it dies, attains dissolution. (GRhtCM 3.24–25:7)

children.text: appakriyāntarakaraṇānmṛto bhavatīti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_3.24-25:8 //
children.translated_text: By performing just a few further operations, it becomes killed (<s>mṛta</s>) — this is the purport. (GRhtCM 3.24–25:8)

children.text: iti pakṣacchedavidhiḥ // GRhtCM_3.24-25:9 //
children.translated_text: Thus is the method of wing-clipping (<s>pakṣaccheda</s>). (GRhtCM 3.24–25:9)

children.text: itare pakṣacchedaṃ dvaṃdve rasamāraṇaṃ na vāñchanti /
children.translated_text: 'Others do not desire wing-clipping in the paired compound, nor the killing of mercury;

children.text: bījānāmapi pākaṃ hṛṣyanti ca tadanu tapyanti // GRht_3.26 //
children.translated_text: they delight in the cooking of seeds (<s>bījas</s>) too, and thereafter they grieve.' (GRht 3.26)

children.text:
etāvatā rasapakṣakartanena nāpaṃ bhavitavyamityāha itare ityādi //
                            GRhtCM_3.26:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He says that not much should be [expected] merely from the wing-clipping of mercury, with 'others' and so forth. (GRhtCM 3.26:1)

children.text:
ye puruṣā iti uktavidhānena pakṣacchedaṃ rasapakṣāpakartanaṃ vāñchanti
                            punaḥ dvaṃdve rasamāraṇaṃ dvaṃdvena pūrvoktena rasahemagandhakena kṛtvā
                            yadrasamāraṇaṃ tanna vāñchanti punarbījānāmapi
                            raktābhrahemarasakādīnāmapi pākaṃ vahniyogena supakvakaraṇaṃ na
                            vāñchanti te puruṣāḥ pūrvaṃ pakṣacchedaṃ jñātvā hṛṣyanti harṣayuktā
                            bhavanti pakṣacchedaṃ vinānyakāryasiddhiṃ jñātvetyarthas tadanu ca
                            kāryāsiddhau tapyanti paritāpayuktā bhavanti // GRhtCM_3.26:2 //
children.translated_text: Those persons [who] — by the described method — desire wing-clipping, the cutting of mercury's wings, but do not desire killing of mercury through the paired [compound], the previously described mercury-gold-sulphur [combination] — furthermore, [those who] do not desire the cooking of seeds (<s>bījas</s>) such as red mica, gold, silver, and the like, through combination with fire — those persons, first knowing the wing-clipping, delight — become filled with joy — knowing that success in other tasks [is possible] without wing-clipping; but thereafter, upon non-accomplishment of the task, they grieve — become filled with distress. (GRhtCM 3.26:2)

children.text: itthamanekadoṣairbahuśramairgaganacāraṇaṃ matvā /
children.translated_text: 'Thus, considering the mica-transmutation (<s>gaganacāraṇā</s>) [to involve] many defects and much labour,

children.text: nirdiśyate prakāraḥ karmaṇi śāstre'pi saṃvādī // GRht_3.27 //
children.translated_text: a method is prescribed that is in accord with this treatise's procedure.' (GRht 3.27)

children.text:
gaganacāraṇaṃ nirdiśyānyasaṃskāraṃ stuvannāha itthamityādi //
                            GRhtCM_3.27:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Having described the mica-transmutation, praising another process, he says 'thus' and so forth. (GRhtCM 3.27:1)

children.text:
mayā granthakartrā asmin śāstre karmaṇyati saṃvādī prakāraḥ
                            agrimaprakaraṇe sattvaniṣkāsanarūpaḥ nirdiśyate nirdeśaḥ kriyate //
                            GRhtCM_3.27:2 //
children.translated_text: By me, the author of the treatise, in this <s>śāstra</s>, a method that is very much in accord — in the form of essence-extraction (<s>sattvaniṣkāsana</s>), in the next section — is prescribed, a directive is given. (GRhtCM 3.27:2)

children.text: saṃvedyate saṃskriyate saṃskāravidbhiriti saṃvādī // GRhtCM_3.27:3 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Saṃvādī</s>' (in accord) means: that which is experienced and processed by those skilled in the procedures. (GRhtCM 3.27:3)

children.text:
kiṃ kṛtvā itthamuktaprakāreṇa anekairdoṣaiḥ anekakaṣṭaiḥ
                            bahuśramairbahvāyāsairgaganacāraṇaṃ matvā abhrakacāraṇaṃ jñātvā //
                            GRhtCM_3.27:4 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? 'Thus' — in the described manner — [considering that] by many defects, many difficulties, and much labour, the mica-transmutation (<s>gaganacāraṇā</s>) is known. (GRhtCM 3.27:4)

children.text:
gaganacāraṇānantaramanyotkṛṣṭaprakāro nirdiśyate iti bhāvaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_3.27:5 //
children.translated_text: After the mica-transmutation, another superior method is prescribed — this is the purport. (GRhtCM 3.27:5)

children.text: agrāhyo nirlepaḥ sūkṣmagatirvyāpako+akṣayo jīvaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Ungraspable, stainless, of subtle movement, all-pervading, imperishable, the living [principle] —

children.text: yāvadviśati na yonau tāvadbandhaṃ kuto bhajate // GRht_3.28 //
children.translated_text: as long as it does not enter the womb [of mica], how can it attain binding?' (GRht 3.28)

children.text:
iti paramahaṃsaparivrājakācāryaśrīmadgovindabhagavatpādaviracite
                                rasahṛdayākhye tantre
                                nirmukhavāsanāmukhāntarbhūtasamukhapattrābhrakacaraṇātmakas tṛtīyo
                                'vabodhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the third chapter — whose subject is the mica-transmutation (<s>cāraṇā</s>) involving mouthless, impression-treated, mouthed-leaf mica — in the treatise called <s>Rasahṛdaya</s>, composed by the <s>Paramahaṃsa Parivrājakācārya Śrīmad Govindabhagavatpāda</s>.

children.text: prakārāntaraṃ darśayannāha agrāhya ityādi // GRhtCM_3.28:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Showing another method, he says 'ungraspable' and so forth. (GRhtCM 3.28:1)

children.text:
evaṃvidho harajo yāvadyonau abhrake na viśati na mipati yāvadbandhaṃ
                            bandhanaṃ kuto bhajate prāpnoti na kuto+api yonāv apraviśati sati na
                            bandhanamāpnotītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_3.28:2 //
children.translated_text: Such a <s>Haraja</s> (mercury) — as long as it does not enter the womb, [i.e.] mica (<s>abhra</s>), does not unite [with it] — how can it attain binding? It does not attain [binding] from anywhere — meaning: without entering the womb, it does not attain binding. (GRhtCM 3.28:2)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭo harajaḥ agrāhyaḥ haraḥ kathamapi na gṛhyate 'navayavatvāt
                            harajastadguṇa eva kāraṇānurūpaṃ kāryamiti nyāyāt /
children.translated_text: What are the qualities of <s>Haraja</s> (mercury)? Ungraspable — <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) is in no way grasped, because of being without parts; <s>Haraja</s> (mercury, born of <s>Hara</s>) possesses the same quality, since 'the effect is in accordance with the cause' — by this principle.

children.text:
punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭo nirpepaḥ vaikārikair doṣaguṇairna pipyata iti
                            doṣaguṇanivṛtteḥ // GRhtCM_3.28:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, what quality? Stainless (<s>nirlepa</s>) — it is not smeared by the modifying qualities of defects — because of the removal of [all] defects and qualities. (GRhtCM 3.28:3)

children.text:
punaḥ sūkṣmagatiḥ sūkṣmā gatir gamanaṃ pravartanaṃ vā yasya saḥ
                            dhūmarūpāvapokanatvāt // GRhtCM_3.28:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, of subtle movement (<s>sūkṣmagati</s>) — one whose movement, going, or activity is subtle — because of its volatility in the form of smoke (<s>dhūma</s>). (GRhtCM 3.28:4)

children.text: punarvyāpakaḥ dehapohādervyāpakatvāt // GRhtCM_3.28:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, all-pervading (<s>vyāpaka</s>) — because of pervading the body, metals, and the like. (GRhtCM 3.28:5)

children.text:
punarakṣayaḥ na kṣayo yasyetyakṣayaḥ sarvadā bhāvarūpatvāt //
                            GRhtCM_3.28:6 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, imperishable (<s>akṣaya</s>) — one for whom there is no decay — meaning always existing in its essential nature. (GRhtCM 3.28:6)

children.text:
punarjīvaḥ ajīve prakāśatvābhāvaḥ svatvaṃ vihāya
                            mapinopādhikatvānnirupādhāv upādhisampattiriti tātparyārthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_3.28:7 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the living [principle] (<s>jīva</s>) — in the non-living, there is absence of luminosity; [mercury], abandoning its own nature, becomes conditioned by impurities (<s>mala</s>) — the intended meaning is: in the unconditioned, there is the acquisition of conditioning. (GRhtCM 3.28:7)

children.text: tadāśrayā tadviṣayā anādyavidyeti vedāntavacanāt // GRhtCM_3.28:8 //
children.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Vedānta</s>: 'Beginningless <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), having that [Self] as its locus and that [Self] as its object.' (GRhtCM 3.28:8)

children.text:
iti śrīmatkurapavaṃśapayodhisudhāramiśramaheśātmajacaturbhujaviracitāyāṃ
                            mugdhāvabodhinyāṃ rasahṛdayaṭīkāyāṃ
                            nirmukhavāsanāmukhāntarbhūtasamukhapattrādhrakacāraṇātmakas tṛtīyo
                            'vabodhaḥ // GRhtCM_3.28:9 //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the third chapter — whose subject is the mica-transmutation involving mouthless, impression-treated, mouthed-leaf mica — in the commentary called <s>Mugdhāvabodhini</s> on the <s>Rasahṛdaya</s>, composed by <s>Caturbhuja</s>, son of <s>Maheśa</s>, who was a moon-drop in the ocean of the <s>Kurala</s> lineage.

children.text: kṛṣṇo raktaḥ pīto yo 'bhraḥ syāt sthūlatārakārahitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The mica that is dark, red, or yellow, and is devoid of coarse flakes,

children.text: vajrī sa pītakarmaṇi pātitasattvo ghano yojyaḥ // GRht_4.1 //
children.translated_text: is <s>vajrī</s> (adamantine); that whose essence has been extracted — the dense [mica] is to be used in the gold-operation.' (GRht 4.1)

children.text:
adhunābhrasattvacāraṇaṃ tatra pītakarmaṇi gaganavarṇabhedānāha kṛṣṇa
                            ityādi // GRhtCM_4.1:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now, the mica-essence transmutation — therein, he describes the colour-distinctions of mica for the gold-operation, with 'dark' and so forth. (GRhtCM 4.1:1)

children.text:
kṛṣṇo ghano rakto ghanaḥ pīto ghanaśceti trividhaḥ pātitasattvaḥ pātitaṃ
                            sattvaṃ yasyeti samāsaḥ // GRhtCM_4.1:2 //
children.translated_text: Dark dense [mica], red dense [mica], and yellow dense [mica] — thus [mica is] of three kinds; 'whose essence has been extracted' — this is a compound meaning 'that whose essence (<s>sattva</s>) has been extracted.' (GRhtCM 4.1:2)

children.text: evaṃvidho vajrī pītakarmaṇi suvarṇakārye yojyaḥ // GRhtCM_4.1:3 //
children.translated_text: Such a <s>vajrī</s> (adamantine [mica]) is to be used in the gold-operation — the procedure for gold. (GRhtCM 4.1:3)

children.text:
vajriṇo pakṣaṇaṃ dhmāto+api haṭhāgnau saṃyojito 'pi yaḥ
                            sthūpatārakārahito bhavati sthūpāśca tāstārakāśca tābhī rahitaḥ
                            dapasamuccayarūpāḥ sthūpatārakāḥ // GRhtCM_4.1:4 //
children.translated_text: The definition of <s>vajrī</s>: that which, even when smelted in intense fire and even when combined [with other substances], is devoid of coarse flakes — coarse ones and flakes together are 'coarse flakes,' meaning scale-like aggregations. (GRhtCM 4.1:4)

children.text:
anukto+api śvetavarṇo ghanaḥ śvetakarmaṇi yojyaḥ granthāntarasāmyād ayam
                            abhiprāyaḥ // GRhtCM_4.1:5 //
children.translated_text: Although not mentioned [in the root text], white dense mica is to be used in the silver-operation — this is the intent, based on agreement with other treatises. (GRhtCM 4.1:5)

children.text:
yathā granthāntare raktaṃ pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ śastaṃ hemakriyāsu gaganaṃ hi //
                            GRhtCM_4.1:6 //
children.translated_text: As [stated] in another treatise: 'Red, yellow, and dark mica is recommended for gold procedures.' (GRhtCM 4.1:6)

children.text:
tārakriyāsu śukpaṃ rasāyane sarvameva tu śreṣṭham iti // GRhtCM_4.1:7
                            //
children.translated_text: 'White [mica] for silver procedures; for <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation), all types are excellent.' (GRhtCM 4.1:7)

children.text:
abhre 'pi vṛttikṛdviśeṣamāha kadācid girijā devī haraṃ dṛṣṭvā manoharam
                            // GRhtCM_4.1:8 //
children.translated_text: Regarding the origin of mica, a special [account] is given: 'Once the mountain-born goddess (<s>Girijā Devī</s>, <s>Pārvatī</s>), seeing the enchanting <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), (GRhtCM 4.1:8)

children.text: amocayat tadā vīryaṃ tajjātaṃ śvetamabhrakam // GRhtCM_4.1:9 //
children.translated_text: released her creative fluid at that time — from that was born white mica.' (GRhtCM 4.1:9)

children.text: śvetaṃ raktaṃ tathā pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ tadbhūmisaṃgamāt /
children.translated_text: 'White, red, yellow, and dark — from contact with the earth [it became these colours].

children.text: pinākaṃ darduraṃ nāgaṃ vajrābhraṃ ca caturvidham // GRhtCM_4.1:10 //
children.translated_text: <s>Pināka</s>, <s>dardura</s> (frog-like), <s>nāga</s> (serpent-like), and <s>vajra</s> (adamantine) mica — thus [mica is] of four kinds.' (GRhtCM 4.1:10)

children.text: dhmātaṃ vahnau dapacayaṃ pinākaṃ visṛjatyapam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Pināka</s> [mica], when smelted in fire, releases a mass of scales and water.

children.text: phūtkāraṃ bhujagaḥ kuryād darduraṃ bhekaśabdavat // GRhtCM_4.1:11 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nāga</s> (serpent-like) [mica] makes a hissing sound; <s>dardura</s> (frog-like) [mica] sounds like a frog.' (GRhtCM 4.1:11)

children.text: caturthaṃ khecaraṃ vajraṃ naivāgnau vikṛtiṃ bhajet /
children.translated_text: 'The fourth — <s>vajra</s> (adamantine) — the sky-moving [mica] — does not undergo alteration even in fire.

children.text:
tasmād vajrābhrakaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ vyādhivārdhakyamṛtyujit iti // GRhtCM_4.1:12
                            //
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>vajra-abhraka</s> (adamantine mica) is the best — conquering disease, old age, and death.' (GRhtCM 4.1:12)

children.text: niścandrikaṃ hi gaganaṃ vāsitamapi vāsanābhir iha śatadhā /
children.translated_text: 'Mica that is without luster (<s>niścandrika</s>), even if impregnated a hundred times with [herbal] impressions —

children.text:
tadapi na carati rasendraḥ sattvaṃ kathamatra yatnataḥ prabhavet //
                                GRht_4.2 //
children.translated_text: even so, the lord of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>) does not consume it; how then can its essence be obtained through effort?' (GRht 4.2)

children.text:
cāraṇāyām abhrapattre vaiṣamyaṃ sattve ca sugamatvaṃ sūcayannāha
                            niścandrikam ityādi // GRhtCM_4.2:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Indicating the difficulty with mica leaves in the transmutation process and the ease [of extracting] the essence (<s>sattva</s>), he says 'without luster' and so forth. (GRhtCM 4.2:1)

children.text:
ihāsmin cāraṇāsaṃskāre niścandrikaṃ gaganaṃ tārakārahitam abhraṃ
                            vāsanābhiḥ pūrvoktābhir vāsanauṣadhibhiḥ śatadhā śataprakāraṃ vāsitaṃ
                            mathitam api rasendraḥ pāradas tadapi bahuśramaiḥ saṃskṛtamapyabhraṃ na
                            carati grāsīkaroti // GRhtCM_4.2:2 //
children.translated_text: Here, in this transmutation process (<s>cāraṇā-saṃskāra</s>), mica that is without luster (<s>niścandrika</s>) — devoid of flakes — even if impregnated (<s>vāsita</s>) — treated, ground — a hundred times, in a hundred ways, with the previously described impression-herbs (<s>vāsana-oṣadhi</s>) — even so, the lord of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>, <s>pārada</s>), even though prepared with much labour, does not consume (<s>carati</s>) — does not make a bolus of — that mica. (GRhtCM 4.2:2)

In this transmutation process, the <s>sattva</s> (essence) through effort — through diligent effort — how would it become capable? How indeed would the <s>sattva</s> become capable through effort? — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 4.2:3)

children.text: muktvaikamabhrasattvaṃ nānyaḥ pakṣāpakartanasamarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Except for the <s>sattva</s> (essence) of mica alone, no other [substance] is capable of clipping the wings [of mercury].

children.text: tena niruddhaprasaro niyamyate badhyate ca sukham // GRht_4.3 //
children.translated_text: By it [mica-essence], having its spreading restrained, [mercury] is controlled and is easily bound. (GRht 4.3)

children.text:
sugamatvādguṇādhikatvācca sattvaṃ praśaṃsati muktvetyādi // GRhtCM_4.3:1
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because of its ease and superior qualities, he praises the <s>sattva</s> (essence) with 'except' and so forth. (GRhtCM 4.3:1)

children.text:
abhrasattvamekaṃ muktvā tyaktvā anyo 'paro rasapakṣāpakartanasamartho na
                            pāradapakṣacchettā na tena sattvena sukhaṃ yathā syāttathā rasaḥ pārado
                            niyamyate pāradasya niyamanaṃ bhavedityarthaḥ badhyate ca bandhanaṃ
                            prāpyate raso baddho bhavatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.3:2 //
children.translated_text: Except for — setting aside — the <s>sattva</s> of mica alone, no other [substance] is capable of clipping the wings of mercury (<s>pārada</s>) — no other is a cutter of mercury's wings. By that <s>sattva</s>, mercury is restrained in such a way that it becomes easy — the restraining of mercury occurs, is the meaning. And it is bound — binding is achieved; mercury becomes bound, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 4.3:2)

children.text:
kimbhūtaḥ san niyamanaṃ bandhanaṃ ca pnoti niruddhaprasaraḥ san niruddha
                            ārundhittaḥ prasaraḥ prasaraṇaṃ prakṛṣṭena gamanaṃ yasya tādṛśaḥ san //
                            GRhtCM_4.3:3 //
children.translated_text: In what state does it attain restraint and binding? Having its spreading restrained — <s>niruddha</s> means obstructed; <s>prasara</s> means spreading, moving extensively — being of such a nature. (GRhtCM 4.3:3)

children.text: pakṣaccheda
children.translated_text: [Section on] wing-clipping (<s>pakṣaccheda</s>)

children.text: pakṣacchedamakṛtvā rasabandhaṃ kartum īhate yastu /
children.translated_text: He who attempts to bind mercury without having performed the clipping of wings —

children.text: bījaireva hi sa jaḍo vāñchatyajitendriyo mokṣam // GRht_4.4 //
children.translated_text: that fool, [merely] with seeds, is like an uncontrolled person desiring liberation. (GRht 4.4)

children.text:
rasabandhane 'dhikāritvaṃ darśayannāha pakṣacchedam ityādi //
                            GRhtCM_4.4:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Showing the qualification for mercury-binding, he says 'wing-clipping' and so forth. (GRhtCM 4.4:1)

children.text:
yo vādī abhrasattvagrasanena vinā pakṣacchedam kṛtvā
                            pakṣāpakartanamavidhāya rasabandhaṃ kartuṃ pāradabandhanaṃ vidhātum
                            īhate ceṣṭate sa vādī na kiṃtu jaḍa evam apaṇḍita iti bhāvaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_4.4:2 //
children.translated_text: Whatever practitioner (<s>vādin</s>) attempts — endeavors — to perform the binding of mercury — to effect the fixation of mercury — without wing-clipping, without accomplishing the cutting of wings through the consumption of mica-essence, that practitioner is nothing but a fool — an ignorant person, is the implication. (GRhtCM 4.4:2)

children.text:
kaḥ kṛtvā rasabandhanaṃ kartumīhate bījaiḥ raktābhrahemarasakair
                            ityādibhiḥ // GRhtCM_4.4:3 //
children.translated_text: Having done what does he attempt to bind mercury? With seeds — namely red mica, gold, <s>rasaka</s> (zinc ore), and the like. (GRhtCM 4.4:3)

children.text: evāvyayam anyadravyavyavacchedī // GRhtCM_4.4:4 //
children.translated_text: The particle 'eva' (indeed) excludes other substances. (GRhtCM 4.4:4)

children.text:
pakṣacchedanaṃ kṛtvā bandhanaṃ kāryamayaṃ vidhiḥ anyathā tv avidhiḥ //
                            GRhtCM_4.4:5 //
children.translated_text: Having performed wing-clipping, binding should be done — this is the proper method; otherwise, it is improper. (GRhtCM 4.4:5)

children.text:
avidher dṛṣṭāntamāha yathā ajitendriyo pampaṭaḥ pumān mokṣaṃ vāñchati //
                            GRhtCM_4.4:6 //
children.translated_text: He gives an illustration of the improper method: just as an uncontrolled, dissolute man desires liberation. (GRhtCM 4.4:6)

children.text: ajitendriyajaḍayoḥ sāmyamiti // GRhtCM_4.4:7 //
children.translated_text: The uncontrolled and the fool are equivalent. (GRhtCM 4.4:7)

children.text: nādhaḥ patati na cordhvaṃ tiṣṭhati yantre bhaved anudgārī /
children.translated_text: It does not fall downward, nor does it rise upward; in the apparatus, it remains without belching —

children.text: abhrakajīrṇaḥ sūtaḥ pakṣacchinnaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ // GRht_4.5 //
children.translated_text: mercury that has digested mica, with its wings clipped — such should it be known. (GRht 4.5)

children.text: pakṣacchinnapāradasya pakṣaṇamāha netyādi // GRhtCM_4.5:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the characteristic of mercury whose wings have been clipped, with 'not' and so forth. (GRhtCM 4.5:1)

children.text:
evaṃvidhaḥ pāradaḥ sūto yaḥ sa pakṣacchinnaḥ pakṣau chinnau cheditau
                            yasyeti samāsaḥ // GRhtCM_4.5:2 //
children.translated_text: Mercury (<s>sūta</s>, <s>pārada</s>) that is of this nature — that is the one whose wings are clipped — whose two wings have been cut off, is the compound. (GRhtCM 4.5:2)

children.text:
sa kaḥ yo nādhaḥ patati adhaḥpātane kṛte ūrdhvato 'dhobhāgo na patati
                            punaradhobhāgata ūrdhvapātane kṛte ūrdhvaṃ na yāti anudgārī acañcapo
                            bhavet yantre svastha eva tiṣṭhatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.5:3 //
children.translated_text: What is it? It does not fall downward — when subjected to downward projection, it does not fall from the upper to the lower part; again from the lower part, when subjected to upward projection, it does not go upward; it remains without belching (<s>anudgārī</s>) — without agitation — in the apparatus, it stays stable — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 4.5:3)

children.text:
punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ abhrajīrṇaḥ abhrakaṃ jīrṇaṃ niḥśeṣatām āptaṃ yasmin
                            rasa iti samāsaḥ // GRhtCM_4.5:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, of what quality? Having digested mica — mica has been completely digested, has reached total [absorption] in which mercury — this is the compound. (GRhtCM 4.5:4)

children.text:
grāsamātreṇa pakṣacchedo na jāyate yāvanna cāritamabhrakaṃ jaratīti
                            dhvanyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.5:5 //
children.translated_text: By mere [mica] bolus-consumption, wing-clipping does not occur; only when the transmuted mica is digested — this is the implied meaning. (GRhtCM 4.5:5)

children.text: sa pakṣacchinnaḥ sūta iti // GRhtCM_4.5:6 //
children.translated_text: Such is mercury with clipped wings. (GRhtCM 4.5:6)

children.text: abhra:: subtypes
children.translated_text: [Section on] mica: subtypes

children.text: śvetādicaturvarṇāḥ kathitāste sthūlatārakārahitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Four colors beginning with white are described; they [should be] free from coarse flakes.

children.text: abhra:: subtypes:: reaction to heating
children.translated_text: [Section on] mica subtypes: reaction to heating

children.text: vajrī satvaṃ muñcatyapare dhmātāśca kācatāṃ yānti // GRht_4.6 //
children.translated_text: The diamond [variety] releases <s>sattva</s> (essence); the others, when smelted, turn to glass. (GRht 4.6)

children.text:
vajrābhraṃ vihāya pinākanāgabhekāḥ satvamocane'samarthā iti darśayannāha
                            śvetetyādi // GRhtCM_4.6:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Setting aside <s>vajrābhra</s> (diamond-mica), showing that <s>pināka</s>, <s>nāga</s>, and <s>bheka</s> [varieties] are incapable of releasing essence, he says 'white' and so forth. (GRhtCM 4.6:1)

Those that are smelted, free from coarse flakes — devoid of layers of leaves — the red, yellow, and black [varieties] that were previously described — they are of four colors beginning with white. (GRhtCM 4.6:2)

children.text:
trayāṇāṃ raktapītakṛṣṇavarṇābhrāṇāṃ cet śvetavarṇa ādau yujyate tadā
                            caturvarṇā bhavantītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.6:3 //
children.translated_text: If to the three — red, yellow, and black colored micas — the white color is added first, then they become four-colored — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 4.6:3)

children.text:
teṣāṃ caturvarṇānāṃ madhye yo vajrī vajrasaṃjñako ghanaḥ sa satvaṃ
                            muñcati dhmātaḥ san satvaṃ tyajati nānye // GRhtCM_4.6:4 //
children.translated_text: Among those four-colored [micas], the one called <s>vajrī</s> (diamond-mica) — the mica designated as <s>vajra</s> — it releases <s>sattva</s> (essence) when smelted, it yields the essence — the others do not. (GRhtCM 4.6:4)

children.text:
apare pinākanāgabhekāhvayāḥ dhmātāḥ santaḥ kācatāṃ yānti kācākāratvam
                            āpnuvanti na ca sattvanirgama iti // GRhtCM_4.6:5 //
children.translated_text: The others — those called <s>pināka</s>, <s>nāga</s>, and <s>bheka</s> — when smelted, turn to glass — they attain a glass-like form; and there is no extraction of <s>sattva</s>. (GRhtCM 4.6:5)

children.text: abhra:: subtypes:: potency
children.translated_text: [Section on] mica subtypes: potency

children.text: sitaraktāsitapītā ye kecidudāhṛtā ghanā loke /
children.translated_text: Whatever micas are mentioned in the world — white, red, black, and yellow —

children.text: alpabalā niḥsattvā vajrī śreṣṭhastu sarveṣām // GRht_4.7 //
children.translated_text: they are of little strength and devoid of <s>sattva</s>; the diamond [variety] is the best of all. (GRht 4.7)

children.text:
sasattvabapavatvābhyām utkṛṣṭatvād vajrābhraṃ punaḥ praśaṃsati sitetyādi
                            // GRhtCM_4.7:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because of possessing <s>sattva</s> and strength, he praises diamond-mica again as superior, with 'white' and so forth. (GRhtCM 4.7:1)

children.text:
poke saṃsāre ye kecit ghanā udāhṛtāḥ kathitāste appabapāḥ appaṃ bapaṃ
                            yeṣu te tathoktāḥ // GRhtCM_4.7:2 //
children.translated_text: In the world — in common parlance — whatever micas are mentioned, described — they are of little strength — those in which strength is meager are so described. (GRhtCM 4.7:2)

children.text:
niḥsattvāḥ satvavarjitāḥ dhmāteṣu teṣu satvābhāva ityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_4.7:3 //
children.translated_text: Devoid of <s>sattva</s> — lacking essence; when they are smelted, there is an absence of <s>sattva</s>, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 4.7:3)

children.text:
te ke ghanāḥ sitaraktāsitapītāḥ śvetaraktakṛṣṇapītavarṇāḥ nānye varṇāḥ
                            santīti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_4.7:4 //
children.translated_text: What are those micas? White, red, black, and yellow-colored — there are no other colors, is the implication. (GRhtCM 4.7:4)

children.text:
sarveṣāṃ caturvarṇānāṃ madhye vajrī vajrasaṃjñakaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ pradhānaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_4.7:5 //
children.translated_text: Among all four-colored [micas], the <s>vajrī</s> — the one designated as <s>vajra</s> (diamond) — is the best, the foremost. (GRhtCM 4.7:5)

children.text: abhra:: inedible variants
children.translated_text: [Section on] mica: inedible variants

children.text: sūte'pi rasāyanināṃ yojyaṃ parikīrtitaṃ paraṃ satvam /
children.translated_text: Even for mercury, for those who practice <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation), the supreme <s>sattva</s> (essence) is proclaimed as suitable.

children.text: trividhaṃ gaganamabhakṣyaṃ kācaṃ kiṭṭaṃ ca pattrarajaḥ // GRht_4.8 //
children.translated_text: Three types of mica are inedible: glass (<s>kāca</s>), slag (<s>kiṭṭa</s>), and leaf-dust (<s>pattrarajas</s>). (GRht 4.8)

children.text: deyamabhramāha sūte'pītyādi // GRhtCM_4.8:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the [type of] mica to be given [to mercury], with 'even for mercury' and so forth. (GRhtCM 4.8:1)

children.text:
rasāyanināṃ rasāyanaṃ jarāvyādhividhvaṃsibheṣajaṃ vidyate yeṣāṃ yeṣu vā
                            te rasāyaninaḥ teṣāṃ paraṃ pradhānaṃ satvamabhrasatvaṃ parikīrtitaṃ
                            saṃkathitaṃ yathā granthāntare /
children.translated_text: For those who practice <s>rasāyana</s> — those who possess <s>rasāyana</s>, the medicine that destroys old age and disease, or those who are engaged in it — for them, the supreme, foremost <s>sattva</s> — the essence of mica — is proclaimed, declared, as in another treatise:

children.text: satvasevī vayaḥstambhaṃ kṛtaśuddhirpabhetsudhīḥ /
children.translated_text: 'One who consumes the <s>sattva</s>, having performed purification, a wise person attains the arrest of aging.'

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_4.8:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 4.8:2)

children.text:
abhrasatvaṃ sūte'pi pārade'pi paramamutkṛṣṭaṃ pakṣacchedanasamarthaṃ
                            bapadaṃ ca // GRhtCM_4.8:3 //
children.translated_text: The <s>sattva</s> of mica is supreme even for mercury — even for <s>pārada</s> — it is most excellent, capable of wing-clipping, and strength-giving. (GRhtCM 4.8:3)

children.text:
punastrividhaṃ gaganam abhakṣyam abhojyaṃ rasāyanināṃ sūte'pi //
                            GRhtCM_4.8:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, three types of mica are inedible — not to be consumed — for those who practice <s>rasāyana</s>, and even for mercury. (GRhtCM 4.8:4)

children.text:
kiṃ tattrividham ekaṃ kācaṃ vahnau dhamanātkācākāratāṃ nītaṃ dvitīyaṃ
                            kiṭṭaṃ yaddhamanātkiṭṭasvarūpaṃ prāptaṃ tṛtīyaṃ pattrarajaḥ patrāṇāṃ
                            samāhitaṃ yadrajas tadevaṃ trividham abhakṣyaṃ sadoṣatvāt //
                            GRhtCM_4.8:5 //
children.translated_text: What are those three? The first is <s>kāca</s> (glass) — what has been brought to a glass-like state by smelting in fire. The second is <s>kiṭṭa</s> (slag) — what has attained the form of slag through smelting. The third is <s>pattrarajas</s> (leaf-dust) — the dust collected from the leaves [of mica]. Thus, these three types are inedible because they are defective. (GRhtCM 4.8:5)

children.text: abhra:: sattva
children.translated_text: [Section on] mica: <s>sattva</s> (essence)

children.text: muñcati satvaṃ dhmātas tṛṇasāravikārakair ghanaḥ svinnaḥ /
children.translated_text: When smelted, mica releases <s>sattva</s> (essence) — when heated with grass-essence preparations.

children.text: parihṛtya kācakiṭṭaṃ grāhyaṃ sāraṃ prayatnena // GRht_4.9 //
children.translated_text: Setting aside glass and slag, the essential [sattva] should be carefully collected. (GRht 4.9)

children.text: satvapātanavidhānaṃ darśayannāha muñcatītyādi // GRhtCM_4.9:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Showing the method of <s>sattva</s>-extraction (<s>sattvapātana</s>), he says 'releases' and so forth. (GRhtCM 4.9:1)

children.text:
ghanas tṛṇasāravikārakaiḥ svinnaḥ tṛṇameva sāro yeṣāṃ te tṛṇasārāḥ teṣāṃ
                            ye vikārakā viśeṣās tair auṣadhaiḥ sūryāvartakādibhiḥ kṛtvā svinnau
                            vahnau dhmāto ghanaḥ satvaṃ muñcati sattvapātaṃ vidadhāti //
                            GRhtCM_4.9:2 //
children.translated_text: Mica, heated with grass-essence preparations — <s>tṛṇasāra</s> means those whose essence is grass; their modifications — special forms — those herbs such as <s>sūryāvartaka</s> and the like — having been treated with those and smelted in fire, the mica releases <s>sattva</s>, yields the essence-extraction. (GRhtCM 4.9:2)

children.text:
punaḥ kācaṃ kiṭṭaṃ ca parihṛtya sattvaṃ patitakācakiṭṭayuktaṃ yadā
                            bhavati tadā prayatnena grāhyam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.9:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, setting aside glass and slag — when the fallen [sattva] is mixed with glass and slag — then it should be carefully collected, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 4.9:3)

children.text: abhra:: sattva:: pātana
children.translated_text: [Section on] mica: <s>sattva</s> extraction (<s>pātana</s>)

children.text: svedya baddhvā piṇḍaṃ māhiṣadadhidugdhamūtraśakṛdājyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The [mica] should be steamed; having bound it into a ball with buffalo curd, milk, urine, dung, and ghee —

children.text: atha paṃcagavyayuktaḥ satvaṃ pātayati lohanibham // GRht_4.10 //
children.translated_text: then, combined with <s>pañcagavya</s> (five products of the cow), it releases <s>sattva</s> resembling metal. (GRht 4.10)

children.text: adhunā viśeṣaprakārāntaram āha svedya ityādi /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now he states another specific method, with 'should be steamed' and so forth.

children.text:
svedyo ghanaḥ pūrvoktaistṛṇasāravikāraiḥ sveditamabhraṃ svedavidhiruktaḥ
                            punarghanasya piṇḍaṃ baddhvā kaiḥ saha māhiṣadadhidugdhamūtraśakṛdājyaiḥ
                            kṛtvā mahiṣyā idaṃ māhiṣaṃ evaṃbhūtaṃ yaddadhi dugdhaṃ mūtraṃ
                            śakṛdviṣṭhā ājyaṃ ghṛtaṃ caitaiḥ piṇḍaṃ baddhvā // GRhtCM_4.10:1 //
children.translated_text: The mica should be steamed — the mica steamed with the aforementioned grass-essence preparations; the steaming method has been stated. Then, having bound the mica into a ball — with what? With buffalo curd, milk, urine, dung, and ghee. Buffalo [products] — that which is of the buffalo cow. Such [products are:] curd, milk, urine, dung (excrement), and ghee (clarified butter). Having bound the ball with these — (GRhtCM 4.10:1)

children.text: atheti samuccaye // GRhtCM_4.10:2 //
children.translated_text: The word 'atha' (then) is in the sense of conjunction. (GRhtCM 4.10:2)

children.text:
pañcagavyaiḥ gavāṃ dugdhadadhimūtraśakṛdājyaiḥ saṃyuktaḥ kāryaḥ piṇḍaṃ
                            baddhvetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.10:3 //
children.translated_text: Combined with <s>pañcagavya</s> — the five products of cows: milk, curd, urine, dung, and ghee — the ball should be bound, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 4.10:3)

children.text:
etatpiṇḍaṃ pohanibhaṃ muṇḍaprabhaṃ sattvaṃ pātayati pūrvasaṃbadhāt
                            ghanasya ityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_4.10:4 //
children.translated_text: This ball releases <s>sattva</s> resembling metal — having a bright luster — from the mica, as previously connected — this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 4.10:4)

children.text: sattva:: extract from cool minerals
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>sattva</s>: extraction from cool minerals

children.text: sūryātapapītarasāḥ svalpaṃ muñcanti dhātavaḥ satvam /
children.translated_text: Minerals whose juices have been absorbed by the sun's heat release only a little <s>sattva</s>;

children.text: svasthānasthāḥ santo muñcanti ta eva bhūyiṣṭham // GRht_4.11 //
children.translated_text: those same [minerals], remaining in their natural state, release much more. (GRht 4.11)

children.text:
sūryātapapītarasā iti sūryātape savitṛgharme pītāḥ śoṣitā rasā dravā yaiḥ
                            evaṃvidhā dhātavo dhmātāḥ santaḥ svappaṃ īṣanmātraṃ sattvaṃ muñcanti
                            tyajanti // GRhtCM_4.11:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Whose juices have been absorbed by the sun's heat' — those minerals whose juices (moisture) have been absorbed — dried — by the sun's heat, the heat of the sun; such minerals, when smelted, release only a little — a small amount — of <s>sattva</s>. (GRhtCM 4.11:1)

children.text:
punasta eva sūryātapapītarasā dhātavaḥ svasthānasthāḥ svakīyaṃ yatsthānaṃ
                            draveṇa sthānapiṇḍaṃ rūpaṃ tasmin tiṣṭhantīti evaṃvidhāḥ santo bahapaṃ
                            bhūyiṣṭhaṃ satvaṃ muñcanti dravantītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.11:2 //
children.translated_text: Again, those same minerals whose juices have been absorbed by the sun's heat — remaining in their natural state — staying in their own natural form with moisture — being of such a nature, they release abundant, copious <s>sattva</s> — they melt, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 4.11:2)

children.text:
sūryātapapītarasā iti keṣāṃ sūryāvartakadapīvandhyākarkoṭakyādīnāṃ
                            drāvakauṣadhīnām // GRhtCM_4.11:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Whose juices have been absorbed by the sun's heat' — of which [plants]? Of the flux-herbs (<s>drāvakauṣadhī</s>) such as <s>sūryāvartaka</s>, <s>dalīvandhyā</s>, <s>karkoṭakī</s>, and the like. (GRhtCM 4.11:3)

children.text: bahugambhīraṃ dhmāto varṣati meghaḥ suvarṇadhārābhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Smelted deeply, mica rains down with streams of gold, like a cloud;

children.text: devamukhatulyamamalaṃ patitaṃ satvaṃ tathā vindyāt // GRht_4.12 //
children.translated_text: the fallen <s>sattva</s>, pure and resembling the face of a god — such should one obtain. (GRht 4.12)

children.text: patitasattvapakṣaṇam āha bahugambhīram ityādi // GRhtCM_4.12:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the characteristic of the fallen <s>sattva</s>, with 'deeply' and so forth. (GRhtCM 4.12:1)

children.text:
megho ghano bahugambhīraṃ yathā syāttathā dhmātaḥ san suvarṇadhārābhiḥ
                            śobhanavarṇadhārābhiḥ vā suvarṇavat kanakavat varṇo yāsāṃ tābhiḥ
                            nirmapatvāt prakāśakatvācca varṣati dhārāpātaṃ vidadhāti //
                            GRhtCM_4.12:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Cloud' means dense — just as [a cloud] when blown deeply would [rain], so when [mica is] smelted, with streams of golden color — with streams of beautiful color — or like gold, like metal, whose color is such — because of purity and luminosity, it rains, it produces a downpour of streams. (GRhtCM 4.12:2)

children.text:
kathaṃbhūtaṃ devamukhatupyaṃ vahninā tupyaṃ samaṃ amapaṃ nirmapaṃ
                            haritapītaraktādidhūmarahitatvāt patitaṃ satvaṃ tathā vindyāt
                            ghanasyetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.12:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what kind? Fit to be heated by fire in the manner of the gods (<s>devamukha</s>), uniform, pure — free from smoke of green, yellow, red, and other [colors] — the essence (<s>sattva</s>) that has fallen [out of the mica], one should obtain from the 'cloud' [mica]; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 4.12:3)

children.text: tathā granthāntare /
children.translated_text: And likewise in another treatise:

children.text: bhastrānapena tīvreṇa mahājvāpe hutāśane /
children.translated_text: By intense bellows-blowing, in a great flame of fire,

children.text: atidīpte bhavedbuddhā aṅgārāḥ kṣayamāgatāḥ // GRhtCM_4.12:4 //
children.translated_text: when it is well-kindled, the embers become exhausted [and appear] awakened. (GRhtCM 4.12:4)

children.text: punaranyā na cenmūrdhni dvistrirvārāṇi buddhimān /
children.translated_text: If more [fuel] is not [placed] on top, [the wise one repeats] two or three times;

children.text: yadā dīpto bhavedvahniḥ śuddhajvāpo mahābapaḥ // GRhtCM_4.12:5 //
children.translated_text: when the fire becomes well-kindled, with a pure flame and great force, (GRhtCM 4.12:5)

children.text: patitaṃ tu tadā vindyāt tatsattvaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: the essence (<s>sattva</s>) falls then — one should obtain it; there is no doubt here.

children.text: patitaṃ tu pṛthakkāryaṃ kiṭṭāṅgāravivarjitam // GRhtCM_4.12:6 //
children.translated_text: The fallen [essence] should be separated, free from slag and charcoal. (GRhtCM 4.12:6)

children.text: nirguṇaṃ pakṣayitvā tu punar dhāmyo yathāvatā /
children.translated_text: Having destroyed the worthless [residue], one should smelt again properly;

children.text: dvistrirevamaśeṣaṃ tu dhmātaḥ sattvaṃ vimuñcati // GRhtCM_4.12:7 //
children.translated_text: two or three times thus, completely smelted, [mica] releases its essence. (GRhtCM 4.12:7)

children.text: abhra:: sattva:: "eaten" without a mukha
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Abhraka</s> (mica) essence — devoured without a <s>mukha</s> (seed-metal)

children.text: yadi lohanibhaṃ patitaṃ jātaṃ gaganasya tadrasaścarati /
children.translated_text: If the fallen [essence] of mica is of metal-like appearance, mercury devours the whole of it;

children.text:
milati ca sarvadvandve hyauṣadhibhiścarati vināpi mukhaiḥ //
                                GRht_4.13 //
children.translated_text: it combines in every paired [combination], and with herbs it devours [metals] even without seed-metals. (GRht 4.13)

children.text: abhra:: sattva:: produces a mukha
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Abhraka</s> (mica) essence — produces a <s>mukha</s> (capacity to devour)

children.text: mākṣikasahitaṃ gaganaṃ dhmātaṃ satvaṃ mukhapradaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: Mica combined with <s>mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite), when smelted, [yields] an essence that bestows <s>mukha</s> (the capacity to devour);

children.text: tadanu ca nāgairvaṅgaiḥ sahitaṃ ca mukhapradaṃ satvam // GRht_4.14 //
children.translated_text: thereafter, that essence combined with lead (<s>nāga</s>) and tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) also bestows <s>mukha</s>. (GRht 4.14)

children.text:
mākṣikasatvāntarasaṃyogāt sattvasya guṇādhikyaṃ darśayannāha mākṣiketyādi
                            // GRhtCM_4.13-14:1 //
children.translated_text: Showing the enhanced quality of the essence through conjunction with <s>mākṣika</s>-essence, he says '<s>mākṣika</s>' and so on. (GRhtCM 4.13-14:1)

children.text:
gagane bhavaṃ gaganaṃ aṇpratyayāntaṃ ṇito vā iti sūtreṇa na vṛddhiḥ
                            gaganaṃ abhrasatvam // GRhtCM_4.13-14:2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Gagana</s>' means that which is born in mica — 'gagana'; by the <s>aṇ</s>-suffix, without <s>vṛddhi</s> [augmentation], according to the sūtra — '<s>gagana</s>' means mica-essence. (GRhtCM 4.13-14:2)

children.text:
mākṣike bhavaṃ mākṣikaṃ mākṣikasatvaṃ tena sahitaṃ pūrvasatvaṃ cet
                            dhmātaṃ tadubhayasatvaṃ mukhapradaṃ bhavati rasasya iti śeṣaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_4.13-14:3 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Mākṣika</s>' means that which is born in <s>mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite) — <s>mākṣika</s>-essence. If the former [mica] essence is smelted combined with that [<s>mākṣika</s>-essence], then the dual essence bestows <s>mukha</s> (the capacity to devour) — to mercury; this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 4.13-14:3)

children.text: mukhaṃ prakṛṣṭena dadātīti samāsaḥ // GRhtCM_4.13-14:4 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Mukha</s>' means it gives [capacity] in an excellent manner — [this is] a compound. (GRhtCM 4.13-14:4)

children.text:
tadanu ca tatpaścācca nāgair vaṅgaiḥ sahitaṃ pūrvaṃ yadgaganaṃ
                            abhrasatvaṃ mukhapradamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.13-14:5 //
children.translated_text: 'Thereafter' — and after that — the mica-essence combined with lead (<s>nāga</s>) and tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) — the former <s>gagana</s>, the mica-essence, bestows <s>mukha</s>; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 4.13-14:5)

children.text:
vā sukhapradaṃ iti pāṭhaḥ asmin yoge bahukpeśaṃ vihāya sukhena cāraṇaṃ
                            bhavatīti vikappārthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.13-14:6 //
children.translated_text: Or the reading is '<s>sukhaprada</s>' (bestowing ease) — in this preparation, abandoning many difficulties, <s>cāraṇa</s> (devouring) occurs with ease — this is the alternative meaning. (GRhtCM 4.13-14:6)

children.text:
abhra:: sattva:: induction of garbhadruti, rañjana and
                                bandhana
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Abhraka</s> (mica) essence — induction of <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction), <s>rañjana</s> (coloring), and <s>bandhana</s> (binding)

children.text: mākṣikasatve yogādghanasatvaṃ carati sūtako nikhilam /
children.translated_text: Through conjunction with <s>mākṣika</s>-essence, mercury devours the mica-essence entirely;

children.text: niyataṃ garbhadrāvī sa rajyate badhyate caivam // GRht_4.15 //
children.translated_text: it certainly becomes <s>garbhadrāvī</s> (inducing internal liquefaction), and becomes colored (<s>rajyate</s>) and bound (<s>badhyate</s>) in this manner. (GRht 4.15)

children.text: mākṣikasatvaṃ mukhyatvenāha mākṣiketyādi // GRhtCM_4.15:1 //
children.translated_text: He states <s>mākṣika</s>-essence as the primary [agent], beginning with '<s>mākṣika</s>' and so on. (GRhtCM 4.15:1)

children.text:
sūtakaḥ pārado ghanasatvaṃ abhrasatvaṃ nikhipaṃ samastaṃ carati //
                            GRhtCM_4.15:2 //
children.translated_text: Mercury (<s>pārada</s>) devours the entire mica-essence (<s>ghanasattva</s>). (GRhtCM 4.15:2)

children.text:
kasmāt mākṣikasatve yogāt mākṣikaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ tatsatve yo yogastasmāt
                            // GRhtCM_4.15:3 //
children.translated_text: Why? Through conjunction with <s>mākṣika</s>-essence — <s>mākṣika</s> means gold-pyrite (<s>svarṇamākṣika</s>); through the conjunction with its essence. (GRhtCM 4.15:3)

children.text: niyataṃ niścitam // GRhtCM_4.15:4 //
children.translated_text: 'Certainly' means assuredly. (GRhtCM 4.15:4)

children.text:
mākṣikasattvayogād ghanasattvaṃ carati raso garbhadrāvī garbhe drāvayati
                            sattvaṃ dravarūpaṃ vidhatte yaḥ sa tathoktaḥ // GRhtCM_4.15:5 //
children.translated_text: Through the conjunction with <s>mākṣika</s>-essence, mercury devours the mica-essence and becomes <s>garbhadrāvī</s> — that which liquefies [metals] within its womb, which produces the essence in liquid form — it is so described. (GRhtCM 4.15:5)

children.text:
sūtasyodare mākṣikābhrasatvaṃ drutirūpaṃ tiṣṭhatītyarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_4.15:6 //
children.translated_text: Within the belly of mercury, the <s>mākṣika</s>-mica essence remains in liquefied form — that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 4.15:6)

children.text:
evamamunā vidhānena saha sūtakaḥ pārado rajyate rāgavān bhavati badhyate
                            baddhaśca bhavatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.15:7 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by this procedure, mercury (<s>pārada</s>) becomes colored (<s>rajyate</s>) — acquires color — and becomes bound (<s>badhyate</s>) — becomes fixed; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 4.15:7)

children.text: abhra:: sattva:: for bandhana of mercury
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Abhraka</s> (mica) essence — for the binding of mercury

children.text: satvaṃ ghanasya kāntaṃ tālakayuktaṃ surundhitaṃ dhmātam /
children.translated_text: The essence of mica, combined with lodestone (<s>kānta</s>) and <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment), well-sealed and smelted,

children.text: vāraistribhiriha satvaṃ bhavati rasendrabandhakāri param // GRht_4.16 //
children.translated_text: in three rounds, the essence becomes the supreme agent for binding mercury (<s>rasendrabandhakāri</s>). (GRht 4.16)

children.text:
mākṣikayogānantaram aparo+abhidhīyate sattvam ityādi // GRhtCM_4.16:1
                            //
children.translated_text: After [the discussion of] the <s>mākṣika</s>-conjunction, another [method] is stated, beginning with '<s>sattva</s>' and so on. (GRhtCM 4.16:1)

children.text:
ghanasyābhrasya satvaṃ tathā kāntaṃ pohaviśeṣaṃ tāpakayuktaṃ tāpakena
                            haritāpena yuktaṃ surundhitaṃ dhmātaṃ sat trayamapi satvarūpaṃ bhavati
                            yadaikavāradhamanena satvaṃ na mipati tathā punardvistrivepābhir
                            dhamanaṃ kāryam // GRhtCM_4.16:2 //
children.translated_text: The essence of mica (<s>abhraka</s>), and lodestone — a specific metal — combined with <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment) — combined with <s>haritāla</s> (orpiment) — well-sealed and smelted; all three become of the nature of essence. If by one smelting the essence is not obtained, then smelting should be done again two or three times. (GRhtCM 4.16:2)

children.text:
samabhāgatāpakayojanaṃ
                            ghanasatvamākṣikasatvayogadrāvaṇāddhamitādatyarthaṃ tatsatvaṃ rakhe
                            pārade bandhakāri bhavati paramamutkṛṣṭaṃ bandhanapradaṃ bhavati //
                            GRhtCM_4.16:3 //
children.translated_text: The conjunction of <s>tālaka</s> in equal proportion — [is obtained] from the liquefaction of the conjunction of mica-essence and <s>mākṣika</s>-essence when smelted; that essence, in mercury, becomes the agent of binding — supremely, the most excellent, bestowing fixation. (GRhtCM 4.16:3)

children.text:
tatsattvasya cāraṇato raso bandhanamavāpnotīti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_4.16:4
                            //
children.translated_text: Through the <s>cāraṇa</s> (devouring) of that essence, mercury attains fixation (<s>bandhana</s>) — that is the purport. (GRhtCM 4.16:4)

children.text: kāntapakṣaṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: Characteristics of lodestone (<s>kānta</s>):

children.text:
pātre yasmin praviśati jape taipabindurna sarpet hiṅgurgandhaṃ visṛjati
                            nijaṃ tiktatāṃ nimbakapkaḥ /
children.translated_text: The oil-drop does not creep on the plate on which [the lodestone] is placed; <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida) releases its own fragrance; the <s>nimba</s> (neem) paste [releases] bitterness;

children.text:
pāke dugdhaṃ bhavati śikharākāratāṃ naiva bhūmau kāntaṃ pohaṃ viduriti ca
                            tappakṣaṇoktaṃ na cānyat /
children.translated_text: when cooked, milk becomes peaked in form [i.e., curdles into peaks] and does not [remain flat] on the ground — [this is] lodestone metal; the stated characteristics are known, and there are no others.

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_4.16:5 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 4.16:5)

children.text: abhra:: sattva:: induction of garbhadruti
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Abhraka</s> (mica) essence — induction of <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction)

children.text: lohaṃ cābhrakasatvaṃ tālakasamabhāgasāritaṃ carati /
children.translated_text: Iron (<s>loha</s>) and mica-essence, combined with <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment) in equal parts, [when mercury] devours [them];

children.text: abhiṣavayogāccāṅgulimṛditaṃ garbhe ca taddravati // GRht_4.17 //
children.translated_text: through the conjunction with pressing (<s>abhiṣava</s>), being crushed with the finger, that liquefies within the womb [of mercury]. (GRht 4.17)

children.text: kāntābhrasatvāpayogakaraṇam āha pohamityādi // GRhtCM_4.17:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the procedure for the conjunction of lodestone and mica-essence, beginning with '<s>loha</s>' and so on. (GRhtCM 4.17:1)

children.text: ceti samuccaye // GRhtCM_4.17:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Ca' [functions] in the sense of aggregation. (GRhtCM 4.17:2)

children.text:
pohaṃ pūrvoktapakṣaṇaṃ muṇḍādikaṃ abhrasatvaṃ ca tāpakasamabhāgasāritaṃ
                            tāpakasya samabhāgena pūrvavidhānena mukhādinā yatsāritaṃ ekaśarīratāṃ
                            nītaṃ sṛ gatāvityasya dhāto rūpaṃ sāritaṃ pramipitam ityarthaḥ
                            evaṃvidhaṃ kāntābhrasatvāpaṃ rasaścarati // GRhtCM_4.17:3 //
children.translated_text: Iron — having the previously stated characteristics — and mica-essence combined with <s>tālaka</s> in equal parts — unified into one body with an equal proportion of <s>tālaka</s>, by the previously described method of seed-addition and such — <s>sārita</s> means extended, merged — that is the meaning. Mercury devours such a lodestone-mica-essence compound. (GRhtCM 4.17:3)

children.text:
ca punaḥ aṅgupimṛditaṃ aṅgupinā marditaṃ tat kāntābhrasatvāpaṃ garbhe
                            rasodare dravati tatsvarūpatvena mipati // GRhtCM_4.17:4 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, being crushed with the finger — ground with the finger — that lodestone-mica-essence compound liquefies within the womb — within the belly of mercury — it merges as its own nature. (GRhtCM 4.17:4)

children.text:
