kasmāt abhiṣavayogāt abhiṣavaḥ saṃmardanaṃ tadyogāt // GRhtCM_4.17:5
                            //
children.translated_text: Why? Through the conjunction with pressing (<s>abhiṣava</s>) — <s>abhiṣava</s> means pressing/crushing; through its conjunction. (GRhtCM 4.17:5)

children.text:
pohasya trayo daśabhedānāṃ madhyāt kenāpi bhedena sahayogaḥ kārya iti
                            pohaśabdena dhvanitam // GRhtCM_4.17:6 //
children.translated_text: Among the thirteen varieties of iron, conjunction with any [particular] variety should be made — this is indicated by the word '<s>loha</s>' (iron). (GRhtCM 4.17:6)

children.text: abhra:: sattva:: induction of cāraṇa
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Abhraka</s> (mica) essence — induction of <s>cāraṇa</s> (devouring)

children.text: vaṃgamatho ghanasatvaṃ tālakaṣaḍbhāgasāritaṃ carati /
children.translated_text: Tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) and mica-essence, combined with <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment) in a one-sixth proportion, [mercury] devours;

children.text: abhiṣavayogāccarati vrajati raso nātra sandehaḥ // GRht_4.18 //
children.translated_text: through the conjunction with pressing, mercury devours [and] moves [into fixation] — there is no doubt here. (GRht 4.18)

children.text: pohayogamuktvā vaṅgayogamāha vaṅgamityādi // GRhtCM_4.18:1 //
children.translated_text: Having stated the iron-conjunction, he states the tin-conjunction, beginning with '<s>vaṅga</s>' and so on. (GRhtCM 4.18:1)

children.text:
atha pohakathanānantaraṃ vaṅgaṃ khurasaṃjñakaṃ abhrakaṃ ca etaddvayaṃ
                            tāpakaṣaḍbhāgasāritaṃ tāpakasya ṣaḍaṃśena ekaśarīratāṃ nītaṃ tatsvarūpaṃ
                            rasaścarati // GRhtCM_4.18:2 //
children.translated_text: Now, after the description of iron, tin — known as <s>khura</s> — and mica: this pair, combined with <s>tālaka</s> in a one-sixth proportion — unified into one body with a sixth-part of <s>tālaka</s> — mercury devours the essence of that. (GRhtCM 4.18:2)

children.text:
kasmāt abhiṣavayogāt abhiṣavaḥ saṃmardanaṃ tadyogāt ṣuñ abhiṣave ityasya
                            dhāto rūpaṃ abhiṣavaḥ // GRhtCM_4.18:3 //
children.translated_text: Why? Through the conjunction with pressing (<s>abhiṣava</s>) — <s>abhiṣava</s> means pressing/crushing; through its conjunction — from the root '<s>ṣu</s>' in the sense of pressing, the form is '<s>abhiṣava</s>.' (GRhtCM 4.18:3)

children.text: punaḥ rasaścarati mipati // GRhtCM_4.18:4 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, mercury devours — merges with [it]. (GRhtCM 4.18:4)

children.text:
cāritaṃ yat taddravati taddrutaṃ rase vrajati pṛthaktvāt saṃ mipati
                            nātrasandehaḥ niḥ saṃdigdhamiva // GRhtCM_4.18:5 //
children.translated_text: What has been devoured (<s>cārita</s>), that liquefies; that which has been liquefied enters into mercury; from separateness it merges — there is no doubt; it is as if certain. (GRhtCM 4.18:5)

children.text:
vaṅgasya paghudravitvāt ṣaḍaṃśayogastāpakasya yuktaḥ pohajāteḥ kāṭhiṇyāt
                            samabhāgatvaṃ uditam // GRhtCM_4.18:6 //
children.translated_text: Because of the high fluidity of tin, the one-sixth proportion of <s>tālaka</s> is appropriate; because of the hardness of iron, the equal proportion was stated. (GRhtCM 4.18:6)

children.text: abhra:: sattva:: induction of cāraṇa
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Abhraka</s> (mica) essence — induction of <s>cāraṇa</s> (devouring)

children.text: bahalaṃ suvarṇavarṇaṃ niculapuṭaiḥ patati pañcabhiḥ satvam /
children.translated_text: Dense, of golden color, with five <s>nicula</s> (Barringtonia) calcinations, the essence falls;

children.text: vaṭakīkṛtamṛtagaganaṃ nirañjanaṃ kiṭṭarahitaṃ ca // GRht_4.19 //
children.translated_text: calcined mica made into pellets, untainted, free from slag. (GRht 4.19)

children.text: taccūrṇīkṛtya tataḥ kṣārāmlairbhāvitaṃ ghanaṃ bahuśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having powdered that [essence], processed with alkalis and acids many times, the mica —

children.text: sṛṣṭitrayanīrakaṇātumbururasamarditaṃ carati // GRht_4.20 //
children.translated_text: ground with the three excretions, <s>nīrakaṇā</s> (long pepper), and <s>tumburu</s> juice — [mercury] devours [it]. (GRht 4.20)

children.text: abhrasatvavidhānamāha bahapamityādi // GRhtCM_4.19-20:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the procedure for mica-essence, beginning with 'dense' and so on. (GRhtCM 4.19-20:1)
'Made into pellets' — that calcined mica which has been made into pellets — here the <s>cvi</s>-suffix [is used] in the sense of 'becoming what it was not.' (GRhtCM 4.19-20:2)

children.text:
pañcabhirnicupapuṭaiḥ pañcasaṃkhyābhirvetasavṛkṣadravabhāvanābhir
                            bhāvitaṃ yanmṛtagaganaṃ mṛtābhraṃ vaṭakīkṛtaṃ satsatvaṃ patati
                            taddrāvakauṣadhayogaṃ vidhāya vahninā vidhamanāditi śeṣaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_4.19-20:3 //
children.translated_text: Calcined mica, processed with five <s>nicula</s> (Barringtonia) calcinations — five treatments with the liquid of the <s>vetasa</s> (rattan) tree — when made into pellets, the essence falls — this being after applying the melting-drug preparations and smelting with fire; this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 4.19-20:3)

children.text:
kiyanmānaṃ satvaṃ patati bahapaṃ bahu anyavidheradhikam //
                            GRhtCM_4.19-20:4 //
children.translated_text: How much essence falls? Dense — abundant, more than other methods. (GRhtCM 4.19-20:4)

children.text:
kīdṛśaṃ svarṇavarṇaṃ pītaśvetaṃ prakāśākhyaṃ punarnirañjanaṃ nirmapaṃ
                            kiṭṭarahitaṃ ca // GRhtCM_4.19-20:5 //
children.translated_text: Of what kind? Of golden color — yellowish-white, called 'luminous'; moreover, untainted — pure, free from slag. (GRhtCM 4.19-20:5)

children.text: asmin satve kācakiṭṭābhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_4.19-20:6 //
children.translated_text: In this [type of] essence, there is absence of glass-slag. (GRhtCM 4.19-20:6)

children.text:
sarvotkṛṣṭavidhirayaṃ pūrvamuditāt bahapasatvapātādityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_4.19-20:7 //
children.translated_text: This is the most excellent of all procedures — superior to the previously stated method due to the abundant yield of essence; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 4.19-20:7)

children.text: kevapasatvacāraṇavidhānamāha tadityādi // GRhtCM_4.19-20:8 //
children.translated_text: He states the procedure for <s>cāraṇa</s> (devouring) with essence alone, beginning with 'that' and so on. (GRhtCM 4.19-20:8)

children.text:
tatastadabhrasatvapātanavidheranantaraṃ tadevābhrasatvaṃ cūrṇīkṛtya
                            kapkaṃ vidhāya kṣārāmpairbhāvitaṃ kuryāt kṣārāḥ svarjikādayaḥ ampā
                            jambīrādayaḥ tairbahuśo bahuvāraṃ gharmapuṭitaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_4.19-20:9 //
children.translated_text: Then — after the procedure for extracting mica-essence — that very mica-essence, having powdered [it], having prepared a paste, should be processed with alkalis and acids — alkalis [such as] natron (<s>svarjikā</s>) and others, acids [such as] citron (<s>jambīra</s>) and others — many times, meaning many rounds, it should be calcined by sun-heat; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 4.19-20:9)

children.text:
punaḥ sṛṣṭitrayanīrakaṇātumbururasamarditaṃ sṛṣṭiḥ pūrvoktā tattrayaṃ
                            mūtraśukraśoṇitamiti nīrakaṇā japapippapī tumbaru pratītaṃ eteṣāṃ rasena
                            marditaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_4.19-20:10 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, ground with the juice of the three secretions (<s>sṛṣṭitraya</s>), <s>nīrakaṇā</s> (long pepper), and <s>tumburu</s> (Zanthoxylum). The three secretions are as previously stated: urine, semen, and blood. <s>Nīrakaṇā</s> is long pepper. <s>Tumburu</s> is well-known. One should grind [the mica-essence] with the juice of these. (GRhtCM 4.19-20:10)

children.text:
abhrasattvamevaṃ kṛtaṃ sat carati grasati rasaḥ ityadhyāhāraḥ //
                            GRhtCM_4.19-20:11 //
children.translated_text: Mica-essence thus prepared — mercury pervades, devours [it] — this is to be supplied [to complete the sentence]. (GRhtCM 4.19-20:11)

children.text: śulvābhra:: production
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Śulvābhra</s> (copper-mica) — production:

children.text: ghanasatvaśulbamākṣikasamabhāganiyojitaṃ tathā militam /
children.translated_text: <s>Ghanasattva</s> (mica-essence) combined in equal parts with copper and <s>mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite), mixed together —

children.text: tacchulbābhraṃ kathitaṃ carati raso jīryati kṣipram // GRht_4.21 //
children.translated_text: that is called <s>śulvābhra</s> (copper-mica). Mercury pervades [it and it] is quickly digested (<s>jīryati</s>). (GRht 4.21)

children.text: iti tāpyaśulbasahitaṃ ghanasatvaṃ lohakhalvake mṛditam /
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>ghanasattva</s> (mica-essence) combined with <s>tāpya</s> (gold-pyrite) and copper, ground in an iron mortar —

children.text: carati rasendraḥ kāñjikavetasajambīrabījapūrāmlaiḥ // GRht_4.22 //
children.translated_text: the lord of mercury pervades [it], with [the juices of] <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel), willow, <s>jambīra</s> (lemon), and citron. (GRht 4.22)

children.text: atha śupbābhramāha ghanetyādi // GRhtCM_4.21-22:1 //
children.translated_text: Now he describes <s>śulvābhra</s> (copper-mica) with '<s>ghana</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 4.21-22:1)

children.text:
ghanasatvaśupbamākṣikasamabhāganiyojitaṃ ghanasatvam abhrasatvaṃ śupbaṃ
                            tāmraṃ mākṣikaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ samabhāgena tupyabhāgena niyojitaṃ
                            prayuktaṃ tanmipitaṃ sat śupbābhraṃ kathitam // GRhtCM_4.21-22:2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Ghanasattva</s>, copper, and <s>mākṣika</s> combined in equal parts' — <s>ghanasattva</s> is mica-essence; <s>śulba</s> is copper; <s>mākṣika</s> is gold-pyrite. Combined in equal parts — meaning in equal portions — when mixed, it is called <s>śulvābhra</s> (copper-mica). (GRhtCM 4.21-22:2)

children.text: atra śupbaṃ kīdṛśaṃ prayojyaṃ tadāha /
children.translated_text: Here, what kind of copper should be used? To that he says:

children.text: dvāvarkau mpecchanepāpau rase nepāpa uttamaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Copper is of two kinds: <s>mleccha</s> and <s>nepāla</s>. In mercury[-work], <s>nepāla</s> is superior.

children.text: ghanaghātasahaḥ snigdho raktapatro+amapo mṛduḥ // GRhtCM_4.21-22:3 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Nepāla</s> copper] withstands hammering, is unctuous, has reddish leaves, is stainless, and soft.' (GRhtCM 4.21-22:3)

children.text: mpecchastu kṣāpitaḥ kṛṣṇo rūkṣasnigdho ghanāsahaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Mleccha</s> [copper] is blackish when heated, rough-unctuous, cannot withstand hammering,

children.text: miśrito nāgapohābhyāṃ na śreṣṭho rasakarmaṇi /
children.translated_text: and is mixed with lead and iron — it is not excellent for mercury-operations.'

children.text: iti ato nepāpakaṃ grāhyamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_4.21-22:4 //
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Nepāla</s> [copper] should be selected — that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 4.21-22:4)

children.text:
tacchupvābhraṃ rasaḥ kṣipraṃ carati punaḥ kṣipraṃ śīghraṃ tacchupbaṃ
                            jīryati jāraṇamāpnoti // GRhtCM_4.21-22:5 //
children.translated_text: That <s>śulvābhra</s> (copper-mica) — mercury quickly pervades [it]; moreover, that copper is quickly digested — undergoes <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation). (GRhtCM 4.21-22:5)

children.text:
atra mākṣikayogaḥ śupbābhrasatvamepanārthaṃ rasaprītyeti bhāvaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_4.21-22:6 //
children.translated_text: Here, the addition of <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) is for the purpose of amalgamating the <s>śulvābhra</s>-essence — [it acts] as a pleasing agent for mercury — this is the purport. (GRhtCM 4.21-22:6)

children.text: śupbābhracāraṇavidhānamāha itītyādi // GRhtCM_4.21-22:7 //
children.translated_text: He states the procedure for <s>cāraṇa</s> (pervasion) of <s>śulvābhra</s> with 'thus' and so forth. (GRhtCM 4.21-22:7)

children.text:
iti pūrvoktaṃ tāpyaśupbasahitaṃ tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ śupbaṃ tāmraṃ
                            nepāpasaṃjñakaṃ tābhyāṃ sahitaṃ miśritaṃ ghanasatvaṃ taptapohakhapvake
                            mṛditaṃ kāryaṃ mardanīyaṃ kaiḥ kṛtvā kāñjikavetasajambīrabījapūrāmpaiḥ
                            kāñjikamuktavidhānaṃ sauvīraṃ vetasaṃ cukraṃ jambīraṃ prasiddhaṃ
                            bījapūro mātupuṅgaḥ eteṣāmampaiḥ dravarūpaiḥ // GRhtCM_4.21-22:8 //
children.translated_text: 'Thus' — as previously stated — 'combined with <s>tāpya</s> (gold-pyrite) and copper' — <s>tāpya</s> is gold-pyrite; <s>śulba</s> is copper of the <s>Nepāla</s> variety; combined with these — mixed — the <s>ghanasattva</s> (mica-essence) should be ground in a heated iron mortar. With what? With the sour [juices] of <s>kāñjika</s>, willow, <s>jambīra</s>, and citron. <s>Kāñjika</s> — the <s>sauvīra</s> (fermented liquid) described in the earlier procedure; <s>vetasa</s> is the tamarind tree; <s>jambīra</s> is well-known; <s>bījapūra</s> is the citron fruit — with the sour juices, the liquid forms, of these. (GRhtCM 4.21-22:8)

children.text:
tataḥ śupvābhraṃ rasendraḥ pāradaścarati grasati // GRhtCM_4.21-22:9
                            //
children.translated_text: Then, the lord of mercury — <s>pārada</s> — pervades, devours, the <s>śulvābhra</s>. (GRhtCM 4.21-22:9)

children.text:
pohakhapvasya kathanāt taptakhapvake mardanaṃ kuryāditi tātparyārthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_4.21-22:10 //
children.translated_text: From the mention of 'iron mortar,' the purport is that grinding should be done in a heated mortar. (GRhtCM 4.21-22:10)

children.text: bhasman (of diff. metals):: rañjana
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Bhasma</s> (ash/calx of different metals) — <s>rañjana</s> (coloring):

children.text: iti tīkṣṇaśulbanāgaṃ mākṣikayuktaṃ ca tatkṛtaṃ khoṭam /
children.translated_text: Thus, steel, copper, and lead — combined with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) — the <s>khoṭa</s> (alloy) made from them —

children.text: tadbhasma ca puṭavidhinā nirvyūḍhaṃ satvarañjakaṃ bhavati // GRht_4.23 //
children.translated_text: and their <s>bhasma</s> (ash/calx), produced by the <s>puṭa</s> (crucible-firing) method, becomes a coloring agent for the <s>sattva</s> (essence). (GRht 4.23)

children.text: prakārāntaramāha itītyādi // GRhtCM_4.23:1 //
children.translated_text: He states another method with 'thus' and so forth. (GRhtCM 4.23:1)

children.text:
iti pūrvoktapakṣaṇaṃ tīkṣṇaśupbanāgaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ tāmraṃ nāgaṃ ca etattrayaṃ
                            mākṣikayuktaṃ svarṇamākṣikayutaṃ samaṃ tupyabhāgaṃ kuryāt //
                            GRhtCM_4.23:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Thus' — as previously described — 'steel, copper, and lead' — steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), copper (<s>tāmra</s>), and lead (<s>nāga</s>) — these three, combined with <s>mākṣika</s> (gold-pyrite), should be made in equal parts. (GRhtCM 4.23:2)

children.text:
tatkṛtaṃ khoṭaṃ taiḥ sarvaiḥ piṣṭīstambhena khoṭabhasma kāryam //
                            GRhtCM_4.23:3 //
children.translated_text: 'The <s>khoṭa</s> (alloy) made from those' — from all of these, by the process of foil-fixation (<s>piṣṭīstambhana</s>), <s>khoṭa</s>-ash should be made. (GRhtCM 4.23:3)

children.text:
puṭavidhinā vahnipuṭavidhānena tatkṛtaṃ khoṭaṃ bhasma kāryaṃ punaḥ
                            tadbhasma satve nirvyūḍhaṃ nirvāhitaṃ sat satvarañjakaṃ bhavati khasatve
                            abhrasatve rāgadāyi bhavati rañjitaṃ tatsatvaṃ rasarañjakaṃ bhavediti //
                            GRhtCM_4.23:4 //
children.translated_text: 'By the <s>puṭa</s> method' — by the method of fire-crucible — the <s>khoṭa</s> (alloy) made from those should be reduced to ash. Furthermore, that ash, introduced into the <s>sattva</s> (essence), becomes a coloring agent for the essence — meaning it gives color (<s>rāga</s>) to the mica-essence; and that colored essence becomes a coloring agent for mercury. (GRhtCM 4.23:4)

children.text: cāryaṃ yatnena rase ghanasatvaṃ tadvidhaṃ ghanaṃ tasya /
children.translated_text: One should make the <s>ghanasattva</s> (mica-essence) pervade mercury with effort; combining the essence of its type with it,

children.text: saṃyojya sarvabījaṃ nirvāhya dvandvasaṃkarataḥ // GRht_4.24 //
children.translated_text: [and] having introduced all the seeds (<s>bījas</s>) and extracted [them] from the pairing mixture. (GRht 4.24)

children.text: rañjitaghanasatvasya cāraṇamāha cāryamityādi // GRhtCM_4.24:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the <s>cāraṇa</s> (pervasion) of the colored <s>ghanasattva</s> with 'should be made to pervade' and so forth. (GRhtCM 4.24:1)

children.text:
tadvidhaṃ pūrvarañjitaṃ ghanasatvam abhrasatvaṃ ca ghanaṃ
                            kevapaghanodbhavaṃ satvaṃ arañjitaṃ rase pārade cāryaṃ
                            grāsagrasanamānenaitad abhrasatvaṃ rase saṃyojyam // GRhtCM_4.24:2
                            //
children.translated_text: 'Of its type' — the previously colored <s>ghanasattva</s> (mica-essence); and '<s>ghana</s>' — the essence produced from mica alone, uncolored — should be made to pervade mercury, by the method of <s>grāsa</s> (devouring) — this mica-essence should be combined with mercury. (GRhtCM 4.24:2)

children.text:
vā satve sarvabījaṃ sarvaṃ rāgadāyi dravyaṃ saṃyojya nirvāhyaṃ nirvāhitaṃ
                            kuryāt // GRhtCM_4.24:3 //
children.translated_text: Or, in the essence, all color-giving substances — all the seeds (<s>bījas</s>) — should be combined and introduced — should be made to enter. (GRhtCM 4.24:3)

children.text:
kutaḥ dvandvasaṃkarataḥ dvandvānāṃ saṃkaro mepāpaḥ saṅkaro+avakara
                            ityamaraḥ // GRhtCM_4.24:4 //
children.translated_text: From what? From the pairing mixture (<s>dvandvasaṃkara</s>) — the mixture of pairs. <s>Saṃkara</s>, <s>melāpa</s>, <s>saṅkara</s>, <s>avakara</s> — [thus says] the <s>Amarakośa</s>. (GRhtCM 4.24:4)

children.text: nirvāhyaṃ iti vaha prāpaṇe ityasya rūpaṃ pūrvavat // GRhtCM_4.24:5 //
children.translated_text: 'Should be extracted' (<s>nirvāhya</s>) — the form of [the root] '<s>vaha</s>' in the sense of 'carrying' — as before. (GRhtCM 4.24:5)

children.text:
niravyayaṃ niścayārthaṃ nirniścayaniṣedhayoḥ ityamaraḥ // GRhtCM_4.24:6
                            //
children.translated_text: The prefix '<s>nir</s>' [is used] in the sense of certainty — '<s>nir</s>' [is used] in the senses of certainty and prohibition — [thus says] the <s>Amarakośa</s>. (GRhtCM 4.24:6)

children.text: abhrakacāraṇamādau garbhadruticāraṇaṃ ca hemno+ante /
children.translated_text: The <s>cāraṇa</s> (pervasion) of mica [should be done] first; the <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction) <s>cāraṇa</s> of gold [should be done] at the end.

children.text: yo jānāti na vādī vṛthaiva so+arthakṣayaṃ kurute // GRht_4.25 //
children.translated_text: One who is an alchemist but does not know [this] — he merely wastes his resources in vain. (GRht 4.25)

children.text: atha rasacāraṇe jñeyamāha abhraketyādi // GRhtCM_4.25:1 //
children.translated_text: Now he states what should be known in the <s>cāraṇa</s> of mercury, with 'mica' and so forth. (GRhtCM 4.25:1)

children.text:
yo vādī rasakartā ādau prathamaṃ abhracāraṇaṃ na jānāti yathā
                            raso+abhrakaṃ carati grasati punaḥ tatpaścāt garbhadruticāraṇaṃ
                            yadrasagarbhe drutaṃ dravarūpaṃ tiṣṭhatyabhrādikaṃ tasya cāraṇaṃ
                            grasanaṃ punarante hemnaḥ svarṇasya cāraṇaṃ grasanaṃ na jānāti sa
                            vṛthaiva mithyaiva arthakṣayaṃ dhananāśaṃ kurute kāryasiddherabhāvāt //
                            GRhtCM_4.25:2 //
children.translated_text: The alchemist (<s>vādī</s>) — the mercury-worker — who does not know first the <s>cāraṇa</s> of mica — how mercury pervades, devours mica — and then the <s>garbhadruti-cāraṇa</s> — the devouring [whereby] liquefied substances such as mica and the like remain in liquid form within mercury's interior — and at the end the <s>cāraṇa</s> of gold — the devouring of gold — he merely wastes his resources in vain, because the desired result cannot be accomplished. (GRhtCM 4.25:2)

children.text: sarvajña eva rasakriyāyāṃ pravarteteti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_4.25:3 //
children.translated_text: The purport is: only one who is omniscient [in these procedures] should engage in mercury-operations. (GRhtCM 4.25:3)

children.text: abhra:: sattva:: grāsa:: only abhra part is "eaten"
children.translated_text: [Section:] Mica-essence devouring — only the mica portion is 'eaten':

children.text: gaganagrāsarahasyaṃ vakṣyāmyekaṃ ghanārkasaṃyogāt /
children.translated_text: I shall declare one secret of <s>gagana</s>-devouring (mica-devouring): from the conjunction of <s>ghana</s> (mica) and <s>arka</s> (copper),

children.text: kevalamabhrakasatvaṃ grasate yatnānna sarvāṅgam // GRht_4.26 //
children.translated_text: [mercury] devours only the mica-essence with effort — not the entire substance. (GRht 4.26)

children.text: grāsarahasyamāha gaganetyādi // GRhtCM_4.26:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the secret of <s>grāsa</s> (devouring) with '<s>gagana</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 4.26:1)

children.text:
ahaṃ śrīmadgovindabhagavatpūjyapādācāryaḥ ekamadvitīyaṃ
                            gaganagrāsarahasyaṃ abhrakakavapane grāsakautukaṃ vakṣyāmi kathayāmi //
                            GRhtCM_4.26:2 //
children.translated_text: I, the revered <s>Govindabhagavatpūjyapāda Ācārya</s>, shall declare — shall speak of — one unique secret of <s>gagana-grāsa</s> (mica-devouring), the marvel of mica-consumption. (GRhtCM 4.26:2)

children.text:
kasmāt ghanārkasaṃyogāt ghanaṃ abhrakasatvaṃ arkastāmraṃ etayoḥ saṃyogaḥ
                            tasmāt ubhayasatvakṛtakhoṭaṃ cāryam // GRhtCM_4.26:3 //
children.translated_text: From what? From the conjunction of <s>ghana</s> (mica-essence) and <s>arka</s> (copper) — <s>ghana</s> is mica-essence; <s>arka</s> is copper. From the conjunction of these two, the <s>khoṭa</s> (alloy) made from both essences should be made to pervade [mercury]. (GRhtCM 4.26:3)

children.text: athaśabdaḥ pakṣāntarasūcakaḥ // GRhtCM_4.26:4 //
children.translated_text: The word 'atha' indicates an alternative view. (GRhtCM 4.26:4)

children.text:
abhrasatvasya yasya dhāto rūpaṃ tena saha yasya dhātorvā saṃyogo bhavati
                            dvandvabhāvāt saṅkarataḥ tatsaṃyuktamabhidhānaṃ bhavati yathā śupvābhraṃ
                            nāgābhraṃ vaṅgābhraṃ mākṣikābhraṃ hemābhram iti evaṃ sarvatra
                            saṃyogānnāmaniṣpattiḥ // GRhtCM_4.26:5 //
children.translated_text: The mica-essence — whatever metal's form it [has been combined with] — with that metal it has conjunction through the pairing state (<s>dvandvabhāva</s>), through mixing. That combined [substance] gets its name [from the combination] — for example, <s>śulvābhra</s> (copper-mica), <s>nāgābhra</s> (lead-mica), <s>vaṅgābhra</s> (tin-mica), <s>mākṣikābhra</s> (pyrite-mica), <s>hemābhra</s> (gold-mica). Thus everywhere, the name arises from the combination. (GRhtCM 4.26:5)

children.text:
grastasya drāvaṇaṃ garbhe garbhadrutirudāhṛtā bahireva dravīkṛtya
                            ghanasatvādikaṃ khapu /
children.translated_text: The liquefaction of what has been devoured — within the interior (<s>garbha</s>) — is called <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction). Having liquefied externally — the mica-essence and the like — in the mortar,

children.text: jāraṇāya rasendrasya sā bāhyadrutirucyate // GRhtCM_4.26:6 //
children.translated_text: for the <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion) of the lord of mercury — that is called <s>bāhyadruti</s> (external liquefaction). (GRhtCM 4.26:6)

children.text: yadi ghanasatvaṃ garbhe na patati no vā dravanti bījāni /
children.translated_text: If the <s>ghanasattva</s> (mica-essence) does not fall into the interior (<s>garbha</s>), nor do the seeds (<s>bījas</s>) liquefy [within],

children.text: na ca bāhyadrutiyogastatkathamiha badhyate sūtaḥ // GRht_5.1 //
children.translated_text: and if the external liquefaction procedure is not applied — then how can mercury be bound (<s>baddha</s>) here? (GRht 5.1)

children.text: vāco marīcibhistaptaṃ toṣaya janakairavam /
children.translated_text: [Invocatory verse:] Heated by the rays of speech, may you delight the night-lotus,

children.text: kumudāni ca kāsārodvartīni cirabhāsayā // GRhtCM_5.1:1 //
children.translated_text: and the water-lilies too, with the long-lasting radiance of the moonlight rising from the lake. (GRhtCM 5.1:1)

children.text: atha garbhadrutibāhyadrutipraśaṃsanamāha yadītyādi // GRhtCM_5.1:2 //
children.translated_text: Now he praises <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction) and <s>bāhyadruti</s> (external liquefaction) with 'if' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.1:2)

children.text:
yadi ced ghanasatvam abhrasatvaṃ garbhe pāradasyāntarna patati dravatvaṃ
                            nāpnoti vā bījāni śupbābhrādīni pāradasyodare no dravanti na rasarūpā
                            bhavanti ca punaḥ bāhyadrutir na yujyate cedevaṃ na syāttarhi iha asyāṃ
                            kriyāyāṃ prāptāyāṃ satyāṃ sūto rasaḥ kathaṃ badhyate anyathā na
                            ko+apyupāyaḥ // GRhtCM_5.1:3 //
children.translated_text: If the <s>ghanasattva</s> (mica-essence) does not fall — does not attain liquidity — into the interior of mercury; or if the seeds (<s>bījas</s>) — <s>śulvābhra</s> and the like — do not liquefy, do not become mercury-form, within mercury's belly; and furthermore, if external liquefaction (<s>bāhyadruti</s>) is not applied — if it does not occur thus — then in this procedure, when [it has] come [to this stage], how can mercury be bound? [Otherwise] there is no other means. (GRhtCM 5.1:3)

children.text: garbhadrutyā rahito grāsaścīrṇo+api naikatāṃ yāti /
children.translated_text: <s>Grāsa</s> (devouring), even when accomplished, if devoid of <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction), does not achieve unity.

children.text: ekībhāvena vinā na jīryate tena sā kāryā // GRht_5.2 //
children.translated_text: Without becoming one (<s>ekībhāva</s>), [the metal] is not digested. Therefore, [<s>garbhadruti</s>] must be performed. (GRht 5.2)

children.text: garbhadruterādhikyaṃ darśayannāha garbhetyādi // GRhtCM_5.2:1 //
children.translated_text: Showing the superiority of <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction), he says 'garbha' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.2:1)

children.text:
cīrṇo 'pi grāsaḥ cāraṇatāṃ prāpto 'pi kavapaḥ yadi garbhadrutyā rahito
                            bhavet rasasyodare rasarūpakaraṇavarjito bhavet tadā ekatāṃ na yāti
                            rasarūpo na bhavati // GRhtCM_5.2:2 //
children.translated_text: Even when <s>grāsa</s> (devouring) has been accomplished — even when the consumption has reached the stage of <s>cāraṇa</s> — if it is devoid of <s>garbhadruti</s> — if [the substance] within mercury's belly is not made to assume mercury-form — then it does not achieve unity — does not become mercury-form. (GRhtCM 5.2:2)

children.text:
punarekībhāvena vinā grāso na jīryate jāraṇatvaṃ nāpnoti // GRhtCM_5.2:3
                            //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, without achieving unity (<s>ekībhāva</s>), the devoured [substance] is not digested — does not attain the state of <s>jāraṇa</s>. (GRhtCM 5.2:3)

children.text:
tena hetunā garbhadrutipūrvikā jāraṇā kāryā rasabandhe jāraṇaṃ heturiti
                            bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_5.2:4 //
children.translated_text: For this reason, <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion) preceded by <s>garbhadruti</s> must be performed. The purport is: <s>jāraṇa</s> is the cause of mercury-binding. (GRhtCM 5.2:4)

children.text: bījānāṃ saṃskāraḥ kartavyaḥ ko+api tādṛśaḥ prathamam /
children.translated_text: The seeds (<s>bījas</s>) should first be given some such preparation (<s>saṃskāra</s>) —

children.text: yena dravanti garbhe rasarājasyāmlavargeṇa // GRht_5.3 //
children.translated_text: by which they liquefy within the interior of the king of mercury — [namely,] with the sour group (<s>āmlavarga</s>). (GRht 5.3)

children.text: jāraṇāyāṃ prathamaṃ kartavyamāha bījānāmityādi // GRhtCM_5.3:1 //
children.translated_text: He states what should be done first for <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion) with 'of the seeds' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.3:1)

children.text:
bījānāṃ śupbābhrādīnāṃ ko+apyanirvacanīyaḥ saṃskāro garbhe drutikārakaḥ
                            prathamaṃ kartavyaḥ saṃskriyata iti saṃskāraḥ // GRhtCM_5.3:2 //
children.translated_text: Of the seeds — <s>śulvābhra</s> and the like — some indescribable <s>saṃskāra</s> (preparation) that causes liquefaction within the interior (<s>garbha</s>) should first be performed. 'They are purified' — hence <s>saṃskāra</s>. (GRhtCM 5.3:2)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ tādṛśaḥ taiḥ bījaiḥ sadṛśaḥ yathā bījāni śaktimanti santi
                            tathā saṃskāro 'pi śaktimān kartavya ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.3:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality? '<s>Tādṛśa</s>' — resembling those seeds — just as the seeds possess potency, so too the <s>saṃskāra</s> should be potent — that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 5.3:3)

children.text: saṃskāraḥ kena kartavyaḥ ampavargeṇa jambīrādinā // GRhtCM_5.3:4 //
children.translated_text: With what should the <s>saṃskāra</s> be performed? With the sour group (<s>āmlavarga</s>) — <s>jambīra</s> (lemon) and the like. (GRhtCM 5.3:4)

children.text:
yena saṃskāreṇa rasarājasya garbhe rasodare bījāni dhātūpadhātujātāni
                            śupbābhrādīni dravantītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.3:5 //
children.translated_text: By which <s>saṃskāra</s>, within the interior of the king of mercury — within mercury's belly — the seeds, consisting of metals and sub-metals such as <s>śulvābhra</s> and the like, liquefy — that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 5.3:5)

children.text: garbhadrutiyogyabīja (1)
children.translated_text: [Section:] Seeds (<s>bījas</s>) suitable for <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction) (1):

children.text: samamākṣikakṛtavāpaṃ samamākṣikasatvasaṃyutaṃ hema /
children.translated_text: Gold combined with equal parts of <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) through the <s>vāpa</s> (pouring) method, joined with equal [parts of] <s>mākṣika</s>-essence —

children.text:
garbhe dravati ca jarati ca jaritaṃ badhnāti nānyathā sūtam //
                                GRht_5.4 //
children.translated_text: within [mercury's] interior it dissolves, and it assimilates; and once assimilated, it binds mercury — not otherwise. (GRht 5.4)

children.text: hemabījapraśaṃsanamāha sametyādi // GRhtCM_5.4:1 //
children.translated_text: He praises the gold-seed with 'sama' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.4:1)

children.text:
samamākṣikakṛtavāpaṃ samabhāgaṃ tupyāṃśaṃ hemnā yanmākṣikaṃ tasya kṛtvā
                            vāpo vāraṃ vāram ākṣepo 'gniyogād yasmin tathoktaṃ punastaddhema
                            samamākṣikasatvasaṃyutaṃ hemnā samaṃ tupyaṃ yanmākṣikasatvaṃ tena
                            saṃyutaṃ kṛtakhoṭaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_5.4:2 //
children.translated_text: 'With equal <s>mākṣika</s>-treated immersion' — equal parts, in equal proportion — to gold, one should repeatedly immerse <s>mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite) by contact with fire; then that gold, combined with <s>mākṣika</s>-essence in equal portion — gold and <s>mākṣika</s>-essence being equal — combined with that, one should make a <s>khoṭa</s> (alloy ingot). (GRhtCM 5.4:2)

children.text: tatkhoṭarūpaṃ hema garbhe pāradāntardravati // GRhtCM_5.4:3 //
children.translated_text: That gold in the form of a <s>khoṭa</s> dissolves within the interior (<s>garbha</s>) of mercury. (GRhtCM 5.4:3)

children.text: punastaddrāvitaṃ hema jarati jīrṇatām āpnoti // GRhtCM_5.4:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, that dissolved gold undergoes assimilation (<s>jaraṇa</s>) — attains the state of being digested. (GRhtCM 5.4:4)

children.text: taddhema jaritaṃ sat sūtaṃ raseśvaraṃ badhnāti // GRhtCM_5.4:5 //
children.translated_text: That gold, once assimilated, binds mercury — the lord of mercury. (GRhtCM 5.4:5)

children.text: anyathā anyaprakāreṇa sūto bandhanaṃ nāpnoti // GRhtCM_5.4:6 //
children.translated_text: Otherwise — by any other means — mercury does not attain binding. (GRhtCM 5.4:6)

children.text: mākṣikasya vāpo hemno varṇotkarṣaprada iti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_5.4:7 //
children.translated_text: The immersion of <s>mākṣika</s> is what enhances the color of gold — this is the purport. (GRhtCM 5.4:7)

children.text: tārāriṣṭa
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Tārāriṣṭa</s> (Silver transmutation)

children.text: mākṣikasatvaṃ hemnā pādādikajāritaṃ drutaṃ sūte /
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s>-essence, assimilated with gold in quarter-portions and more, dissolved in mercury,

children.text: tārāriṣṭaṃ kurute varakanakaṃ pattralepena // GRht_5.5 //
children.translated_text: produces <s>tārāriṣṭa</s> (auspicious silver) — excellent gold — by the application of leaf-coating. (GRht 5.5)

children.text:
mākṣikasatvacāraṇādrase guṇotkarṣam āha mākṣikasatvamityādi //
                            GRhtCM_5.5:1 //
children.translated_text: He describes the superior quality arising from the assimilation of <s>mākṣika</s>-essence into mercury, with '<s>mākṣikasatva</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.5:1)

children.text:
mākṣikasatvaṃ vahnyauṣadhayogadrutaṃ yaddhemamākṣikasāraṃ hemnā kanakena
                            saha sūte pārade pūrvaṃ yadgutaṃ punaḥ pādādikajāritaṃ pādādikavibhāgena
                            pādārdhasatvena niḥśeṣatāmāptaṃ sat ayaṃ sūtaḥ tārāriṣṭaṃ tāraṃ rūpyādi
                            ariṣṭaṃ śubhaṃ varakanakaṃ kurute pūrṇavarṇamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.5:2
                            //
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s>-essence — the essence of <s>mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite) melted through fire and herbal treatment — [combined] with gold; dissolved in mercury, then assimilated in portions of a quarter and more — by the division into quarter, half, [and full] essence — having been completely consumed; this mercury produces <s>tārāriṣṭa</s> — <s>tāra</s> meaning silver and the like, <s>ariṣṭa</s> meaning auspicious — excellent gold, meaning gold of full color. (GRhtCM 5.5:2)

children.text:
kena vidhānena pattrapepanena patraṃ kaṇṭakabhedi tatra yo+asau pepaḥ
                            vahniyogāditi śeṣaḥ tena // GRhtCM_5.5:3 //
children.translated_text: By what method? By leaf-coating (<s>pattralepana</s>) — <s>patra</s> (leaf/foil) that penetrates impurities; upon it, the <s>lepa</s> (coating) through conjunction with fire — this is the complement — by that. (GRhtCM 5.5:3)

children.text:
hemamākṣikasatvajāritasya rūpyapatrapepena kanakaṃ syāditi vyaktārthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_5.5:4 //
children.translated_text: Mercury assimilated with gold and <s>mākṣika</s>-essence, through coating on silver foil, produces gold — the meaning is clear. (GRhtCM 5.5:4)

children.text: garbhadruti:: test for ~
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Garbhadruti</s> (Internal dissolution) — test for it

children.text: samarasatāṃ yadi yāto vastrādgalito+adhikaśca tulanāyām /
children.translated_text: If the morsel has become equal in fluidity to mercury, passes through cloth, and weighs more on the balance —

children.text: grāso drutaḥ sa garbhe drutvāsau jīryate kṣipram // GRht_5.6 //
children.translated_text: that morsel is dissolved internally; having dissolved, it is assimilated quickly. (GRht 5.6)

children.text: garbhadruter pakṣaṇamāha sametyādi // GRhtCM_5.6:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the criterion for <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal dissolution) with 'sama' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.6:1)

children.text:
yadi grāsaḥ samarasatāṃ yāto bhavedrasatupyarūpatāṃ prāpto bhavet
                            punarvastrādgapito bhavet caturguṇaśvetavastrānniḥsṛto bhavet
                            punastupanāyāṃ tupākarmaṇi yadādhiko+api syāttadā garbhe pāradasyāntar
                            druto grāso jñātavyaḥ garbhadruto raso veditavya iti vyaktārthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_5.6:2 //
children.translated_text: If the morsel has attained equality of fluidity with mercury — has reached the appearance equal to mercury; and if it passes through cloth — emerges through cloth folded fourfold; and if on the balance — in the act of weighing — it is even greater [than the original mercury]; then the morsel should be known as dissolved internally — the mercury should be understood as having internal dissolution — the meaning is clear. (GRhtCM 5.6:2)

children.text:
punarasau raso drutvā dravarūpaṃ śīghraṃ prāpto jīryati dhātūnapi
                            vidhāneneti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_5.6:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, that mercury, having dissolved — having quickly attained liquid form — assimilates metals as well, by the [prescribed] method — this is the complement. (GRhtCM 5.6:3)

children.text: Rolle von tāpyasattva
children.translated_text: [Section:] Role of <s>Tāpyasattva</s> (pyrite essence)

children.text: na biḍairnāpi kṣārairna snehairdravati hemaṃ tāraṃ vā /
children.translated_text: Neither through <s>viḍa</s>s (binding agents), nor through alkalis, nor through oils does gold or silver dissolve —

children.text: mākṣikasatvena vinā tridinaṃ nihitena raktena // GRht_5.7 //
children.translated_text: only through <s>mākṣika</s>-essence, steeped for three days in the red [group of substances]. (GRht 5.7)

children.text: mākṣikasatvotkarṣamāha netyādi // GRhtCM_5.7:1 //
children.translated_text: He describes the superiority of <s>mākṣika</s>-essence with 'na' (not) and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.7:1)

children.text:
mākṣikasatvena vinā svarṇamākṣikasāram antareṇa hema kanakaṃ vā tāraṃ
                            rūpyaṃ na dravati // GRhtCM_5.7:2 //
children.translated_text: Without <s>mākṣika</s>-essence — without the essence of <s>svarṇamākṣika</s> (gold-pyrite) — gold or silver does not dissolve. (GRhtCM 5.7:2)

children.text:
kaiḥ kṛtvā viḍaiḥ kṛtvā śaṅkhacūrṇārkakṣārādikṛtapiṇḍaiḥ kṛtvā
                            granthāntare ca /
children.translated_text: By what means? Having prepared <s>viḍa</s>s — pellets made of conch-powder, <s>arka</s>-alkali, and the like. And in another text:

children.text: pavaṇakṣāroparasair ebhir ampairbiḍo mataḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Viḍa</s> is considered [to be made of] salt, alkali, and subsidiary minerals (<s>uparasas</s>), with sour liquids.

children.text: same garbhe tu saṃsthāpyo hyanenaiva dravībhavet /
children.translated_text: It should be placed in an equal interior; with this alone [gold] would become liquid.'

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_5.7:3 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 5.7:3)

children.text:
na kevapaṃ biḍaiḥ kiṃtu kṣārairapi na kṣāraiḥ
                            svarjikāyavakṣāraṭaṅkaṇādyaiḥ // GRhtCM_5.7:4 //
children.translated_text: Not only through <s>viḍa</s>s, but also not through alkalis — such as <s>svarjikā</s> (sodium carbonate), barley-alkali, borax, and the like. (GRhtCM 5.7:4)

children.text: na kevapaṃ kṣāraiḥ kiṃtu snehairapi na snehāni yathā /
children.translated_text: Not only through alkalis, but also not through oils. The oils are as follows:

children.text: kaṅguṇikaṃ vinādoṣākarañjaśrīphapodbhavam /
children.translated_text: Derived from <s>kaṅguṇi</s>, without-defect, from <s>karañja</s> and <s>śrīphala</s>;

children.text: kaṭuvātārisiddhārthasomarājīvibhītajam /
children.translated_text: from pungent [seeds], <s>vātāri</s>, mustard, <s>somarājī</s>, and <s>vibhīta</s>;

children.text: atasījaṃ mahākāpanimbajaṃ tipajaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: from flax, <s>mahākālī</s>, neem, sesame likewise;

children.text: apāmārgadevadāpīdantītumbaravigrahā /
children.translated_text: <s>Apāmārga</s>, <s>devadālī</s>, <s>dantī</s>, and <s>tumbaru</s>;

children.text: aṅkoponmattabhappātaphapebhyastaipasaṃbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: from <s>aṅkola</s>, datura, <s>bhallātaka</s>, and fruits — oils are produced.

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_5.7:5 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 5.7:5)

children.text: taipairapi na dravati /
children.translated_text: Even through oils, [gold] does not dissolve.

children.text: punarmākṣikasatvena garbhe drutirjāyate // GRhtCM_5.7:6 //
children.translated_text: Only through <s>mākṣika</s>-essence does internal dissolution occur. (GRhtCM 5.7:6)

children.text: kiṃviśeṣeṇa mākṣikasatvena raktena raktavargeṇa // GRhtCM_5.7:7 //
children.translated_text: With what specification of <s>mākṣika</s>-essence? Red — treated with the red group [of substances]. (GRhtCM 5.7:7)

children.text:
tridinaṃ dinatrayaṃ nihitena raktavargāntaḥsthāpitena // GRhtCM_5.7:8
                            //
children.translated_text: Steeped for three days — for the duration of three days — placed within the red group [of substances]. (GRhtCM 5.7:8)

children.text: raktavargo yathā /
children.translated_text: The red group is as follows:

children.text: dāḍimaṃ kiṃśukaṃ caiva bandhūkaṃ ca kusumbhakam /
children.translated_text: 'Pomegranate, <s>kiṃśuka</s> (flame of the forest), <s>bandhūka</s> (Pentapetes), and safflower,

children.text: samāñjiṣṭho haridrādyo pākṣārasasamanvitaḥ /
children.translated_text: together with <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> (Indian madder), turmeric and the rest, combined with alkaline salt;

children.text: raktacandanasaṃyukto raktavargaḥ prakīrtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: combined with red sandalwood — this is declared to be the red group.'

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_5.7:9 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 5.7:9)

children.text: mercury:: cāraṇa, garbhadruti
children.translated_text: [Section:] Mercury — <s>cāraṇā</s>, <s>garbhadruti</s>

children.text: lavaṇaṃ devīsvarasaplutam ahipatraṃ vicūrṇitaṃ śilayā /
children.translated_text: Salt, soaked in the juice of <s>devī</s> (Brāhmī), and betel leaf ground with a stone —

children.text: etat puṭanatritayāt sumṛtaṃ saṃsthāpayedayaḥpātre // GRht_5.8 //
children.translated_text: this, well-prepared through three calcinations, should be placed in an iron vessel. (GRht 5.8)

children.text: vihitārdhāṃgulanimnā sphuṭavikaṭakaṭorikā mukhādhārā /
children.translated_text: A saucer-like vessel, with a depression of half a finger-breadth, open-mouthed and broad, serving as the mouth-support;

children.text: tasyoparyādeyā kaṭorikā cāṅgulotsedhā // GRht_5.9 //
children.translated_text: above it, a saucer of one finger-breadth in height should be placed. (GRht 5.9)

children.text: vihitacchidratritayā śastā caturaṃgulordhvachidreṣu /
children.translated_text: Provided with three holes, excellent; at four finger-breadths above in the holes,

children.text: lohaśalākā yojyāstatrāpi ca hemapatrāṇi // GRht_5.10 //
children.translated_text: iron rods should be fitted — and upon them, gold leaves. (GRht 5.10)

children.text: saṃsthāpya vidhūpyante yantrādhastāt pradīpayedagnim /
children.translated_text: Having placed [them] and fumigated, one should kindle fire beneath the apparatus.

children.text: dhūmopalepamātrādbhavanti kṛṣṇāni hemapatrāṇi // GRht_5.11 //
children.translated_text: Merely from the coating of smoke, the gold leaves become black. (GRht 5.11)

children.text: tānyagnitāpitāni ca paścādyantre mṛtāni dhūmena /
children.translated_text: Those [leaves], heated by fire and then killed in the apparatus by smoke,

children.text: pācitahemavidhānāccarati rasendro dravati garbhe ca // GRht_5.12 //
children.translated_text: by the method of treating gold — the lord of mercury assimilates [them] and dissolves [them] internally. (GRht 5.12)

children.text: svarṇajāraṇayantravidhānamāha pavaṇamityādi // GRhtCM_5.8-12:1 //
children.translated_text: He describes the method of the apparatus for gold assimilation (<s>svarṇajāraṇa</s>) with '<s>lavaṇa</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.8-12:1)

children.text:
prathamaṃ pavaṇaṃ saindhavaṃ devīsvarasapputaṃ kuryāt brāhmīsvakīyarasena
                            saṃmiśraṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_5.8-12:2 //
children.translated_text: First, one should prepare rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>) soaked in the juice of <s>devī</s> (<s>Brāhmī</s>) — mixed with its own juice. (GRhtCM 5.8-12:2)

children.text:
punar brāhmīrasapputaṃ pavaṇaṃ ca ahipatraṃ tāmbūpidapaṃ tacca dvayaṃ
                            śipayā vitatagrāveṇa cūrṇitaṃ peṣitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_5.8-12:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Brāhmī</s>-juice-soaked salt and <s>ahipatra</s> (betel leaf) — both should be ground — powdered — with a stone (<s>śilā</s>), a flat grinding-stone. (GRhtCM 5.8-12:3)

children.text: punaretad ayaḥpātre pohabhājane saṃsthāpayet // GRhtCM_5.8-12:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, this should be placed in an iron vessel — a metal container. (GRhtCM 5.8-12:4)

children.text:
etat sthāpitaṃ dravyaṃ puṭatritayāt tripuṭakaraṇādagnisaṃyogena sumṛtaṃ
                            syāt // GRhtCM_5.8-12:5 //
children.translated_text: This placed substance, through three calcinations — by triple calcination through contact with fire — becomes well-prepared. (GRhtCM 5.8-12:5)

children.text:
tasya devīsvarasapputasya sumṛtasaindhavasya mukhādhārā
                            sphuṭavikaṭakaṭorikā pātrī kāryā mukhameva ādhāro yasyāḥ sā evaṃvidhā
                            sphuṭā prakaṭā vikaṭā viparītā adhomukhetyarthaḥ sā kaṭorikā vihitā
                            kāryā ayaḥpātrasya // GRhtCM_5.8-12:6 //
children.translated_text: For that well-prepared rock salt soaked in <s>devī</s>-juice, a mouth-support saucer should be made — a vessel that is open, inverted, meaning mouth-downward — that saucer should be made for the iron vessel. (GRhtCM 5.8-12:6)

children.text:
tasyāḥ kaṭorikāyā upari ūrdhvabhāge eṣā kaṭorikā ādeyā sthāpyā //
                            GRhtCM_5.8-12:7 //
children.translated_text: Above that saucer — in the upper part — this [second] saucer should be placed. (GRhtCM 5.8-12:7)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭā aṅgupotsedhā aṅgupa utsedhaḥ parimāṇaṃ yasyāḥ sā tathoktā //
                            GRhtCM_5.8-12:8 //
children.translated_text: Of what specification? One finger-breadth in height — one finger-breadth is the height of which — it is so described. (GRhtCM 5.8-12:8)

children.text:
punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭā ardhāṅgupanimnā ardhāṅgupaparimāṇanimnā madhyagā //
                            GRhtCM_5.8-12:9 //
children.translated_text: Further, of what specification? Half a finger-breadth in depth — having a depth measuring half a finger-breadth, concave in the middle. (GRhtCM 5.8-12:9)

children.text:
punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭā vihitachidratritayā vihitāni kṛtāni chidratritayāni
                            yasyāṃ sā evaṃvidhā śastā ca saṃtupavihitachidratritayā //
                            GRhtCM_5.8-12:10 //
children.translated_text: Further, of what specification? Provided with three holes — in which three holes have been made — such is its description; excellent, and provided with three holes in equal [spacing]. (GRhtCM 5.8-12:10)

children.text:
caturaṅgupordhvā taduparibhāge kaṭorikā caturaṅgupipramāṇonnateti bhāvaḥ
                            // GRhtCM_5.8-12:11 //
children.translated_text: Four finger-breadths above — the saucer in the upper part is raised by four finger-breadths — this is the purport. (GRhtCM 5.8-12:11)

children.text:
punaśchidreṣu triṣu śapākā yojyā pohaśapākāḥ kṣepyāḥ punastatrāpi
                            chidreṣu hemapatrāṇi kaṇṭakavedhīni kanakapatrāṇi yojyānīti //
                            GRhtCM_5.8-12:12 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, iron rods should be fitted into the three holes; and upon those [rods] in the holes, gold leaves — foils penetrated by needles — should be placed. (GRhtCM 5.8-12:12)

children.text:
evaṃvidhe pūrvaṃ nirmite yantre hemapatrāṇi sthāpya vidhūpyante //
                            GRhtCM_5.8-12:13 //
children.translated_text: In such a previously constructed apparatus, having placed the gold leaves, they are fumigated. (GRhtCM 5.8-12:13)
Then one should kindle fire — beneath the apparatus, in the lower part, one should ignite fire. Then those gold leaves become black — of dark color. (GRhtCM 5.8-12:14)

children.text:
kasmāt dhūmopapepamātrāt dhūmaścāsāvupapepaśca dhūmopapepas tanmātrāt
                            tatpramāṇāt // GRhtCM_5.8-12:15 //
children.translated_text: Why? Merely from the smoke-coating — 'smoke' and 'coating' [form a compound]; merely from its measure — from that extent. (GRhtCM 5.8-12:15)

children.text:
yenauṣadhena dhūpo niruktastenauṣadhenopapepaḥ kāryaḥ patreṣviti //
                            GRhtCM_5.8-12:16 //
children.translated_text: The medicine from which the fumigation is described — with that very medicine, the coating should be applied to the leaves. (GRhtCM 5.8-12:16)

children.text:
punaḥ kiṃbhūtāni hemapatrāṇi rasendro jarati agnitāpitāni santi
                            vahniyogāttaptāni kṛtāni // GRhtCM_5.8-12:17 //
children.translated_text: Further, of what kind are the gold leaves that the lord of mercury assimilates? They are fire-heated — made hot through contact with fire. (GRhtCM 5.8-12:17)

children.text: svarṇajāraṇamidaṃ gaditam // GRhtCM_5.8-12:18 //
children.translated_text: This gold-assimilation [process] has been described. (GRhtCM 5.8-12:18)

children.text: iti pañcabhiḥ śpokaiḥ kupakam // GRhtCM_5.8-12:19 //
children.translated_text: Thus, in five verses, a section (<s>kullaka</s>) [is completed]. (GRhtCM 5.8-12:19)

children.text: silver:: garbhadruti (in mercury)
children.translated_text: [Section:] Silver — <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal dissolution in mercury)

children.text: tenaiva tārapatraṃ vidhinā saṃsvedya yantrayogena /
children.translated_text: By that very method, a silver leaf, having been steamed through the apparatus-method,

children.text: jāyeta kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ tattāraṃ dravati garbhe ca // GRht_5.13 //
children.translated_text: becomes black in color; that silver dissolves internally [in mercury] as well. (GRht 5.13)

children.text: atha rūpyajāraṇamāha tenetyādi // GRhtCM_5.13:1 //
children.translated_text: Now he describes the assimilation of silver with 'tena' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.13:1)

children.text:
tenaiva vidhinā pūrvapidhānena tārapatraṃ rūpyadapaṃ kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ
                            śyāmapaprabhaṃ jāyate // GRhtCM_5.13:2 //
children.translated_text: By that very method — the previously described procedure — the silver leaf becomes dark in color — of blue-black luster. (GRhtCM 5.13:2)

children.text:
kena saṃsvedya yantrayogena saṃsvedaḥ prabapāgnis tasyedaṃ sambandhi
                            yadyantraṃ yasya yo yogastena // GRhtCM_5.13:3 //
children.translated_text: By what [means]? Having steamed through the apparatus-method — the steaming is with strong fire; that apparatus which is related to it — through the method of that. (GRhtCM 5.13:3)

children.text:
tattārapatraṃ punaḥ garbhe rasodare dravati japatvamāpnoti //
                            GRhtCM_5.13:4 //
children.translated_text: That silver leaf furthermore dissolves within the interior of mercury — attains the state of liquidity. (GRhtCM 5.13:4)

children.text:
punastasmin yantre dravati caśabdāt rasendrastatpatraṃ jarati tārakṛṣṇīti
                            // GRhtCM_5.13:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, in that same apparatus, the lord of mercury dissolves; and [by the word] 'ca' (and), [mercury] assimilates that leaf — this is called <s>tārakṛṣṇī</s> (silver-blackening). (GRhtCM 5.13:5)

children.text: gold, silver:: garbhadruti (~)
children.translated_text: [Section:] Gold and Silver — <s>garbhadruti</s>

children.text: athavā balinā vaṅgaṃ nāgābhidhānena yantrayogena /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, tin with the strong one [sulfur], or lead-named [substance], through the apparatus-method,

children.text: hemāhvaṃ tāraṃ vā dravati ca garbhe na sandehaḥ // GRht_5.14 //
children.translated_text: gold-named or silver — dissolves internally, without doubt. (GRht 5.14)

children.text: atha yogāntaraṃ āha athavetyādi // GRhtCM_5.14:1 //
children.translated_text: Now he describes another method with 'athavā' (alternatively) and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.14:1)

children.text: athaveti samuccaye ekārthaniṣṭhatvāt // GRhtCM_5.14:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Athavā' (alternatively) is used in the sense of conjunction, because of being directed to a single purpose. (GRhtCM 5.14:2)

children.text:
bapinā gandhena saha vaṅgaṃ yantrayogena kṛṣṇaṃ jāyeta // GRhtCM_5.14:3
                            //
children.translated_text: With the strong one — sulfur — tin, through the apparatus-method, becomes black. (GRhtCM 5.14:3)

children.text:
kevapaṃ vaṅgaṃ punarnāgābhidhānena saha nāgavidhānamapyevaṃ syāditi
                            vyaktiḥ // GRhtCM_5.14:4 //
children.translated_text: Tin alone — furthermore, with the one named lead (<s>nāga</s>), the procedure for lead too would be the same — this is the clarification. (GRhtCM 5.14:4)

children.text:
nāgābhidhāneneti nāganāmnā ākhyāhve abhidhānaṃ ca nāmadheyaṃ ca nāma ca
                            ityamaraḥ // GRhtCM_5.14:5 //
children.translated_text: 'With the one named lead (<s>nāgābhidhāna</s>)' — <s>ākhyā</s> (appellation), <s>abhidhāna</s> (designation), <s>nāmadheya</s> (given name), and <s>nāma</s> (name) [are synonyms] — [thus says] <s>Amara[koṣa]</s>. (GRhtCM 5.14:5)

children.text:
evaṃvidhaṃ vaṅgaṃ vā nāgaṃ vā hemāhvaṃ hemapatraṃ vā tāraṃ tārapatraṃ vā
                            etatsarvaṃ bapinā kṛṣṇaṃ jāyeta mṛtaṃ ca sarvaṃ garbhe rasāntare dravati
                            nātra saṃdehaḥ asaṃdigdhamidamuktam // GRhtCM_5.14:6 //
children.translated_text: Such tin or lead, gold-designated (gold leaf) or silver (silver leaf) — all of this, when treated with the potent [substance], becomes black, and once killed (<s>mṛta</s>), everything dissolves inside the womb (<s>garbha</s>, i.e., interior of mercury) — there is no doubt about this; this has been stated without ambiguity. (GRhtCM 5.14:6)

children.text: caśabdājjarati niḥśeṣatvamāpnoti // GRhtCM_5.14:7 //
children.translated_text: Due to the word 'ca' (and), it digests — attains complete [dissolution]. (GRhtCM 5.14:7)

children.text: rasaka:: garbhadruti (~)
children.translated_text: [Section: <s>Rasaka</s> (calamine) — <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal dissolution)]

children.text: rasakaṃ balinā yuktaṃ pūrvoktavidhānayogena /
children.translated_text: '<s>Rasaka</s> (calamine), combined with the potent [substance (sulphur)], by the previously described procedural combination,

children.text: pakvaṃ cūrṇaṃ yāvadbhavati bhṛśaṃ dravati garbhe ca // GRht_5.15 //
children.translated_text: when cooked until it becomes powder, dissolves completely inside the womb (<s>garbha</s>).' (GRht 5.15)

children.text: prayogāntaramāha rasakamityādi // GRhtCM_5.15:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another application, with '<s>rasaka</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.15:1)

children.text:
rasakaṃ kharparikaṃ bapinā gandhena saha yuktaṃ sat mipitaṃ sat
                            samabhāgena iti śeṣaḥ kena kṛtvā pūrvoktavidhānayogena pūrvoktaṃ
                            yadvidhānaṃ yantrādikaṃ tasya yo+asau yogastena kṛtvā
                            tāvadbhṛśamatyarthaṃ pakvaṃ kāryaṃ yāvadaśarīratāṃ yāti taccūrṇaṃ garbhe
                            rasodare dravati garbhadrutirbhavati caśabdājjarati ca // GRhtCM_5.15:2
                            //
children.translated_text: <s>Rasaka</s> — <s>kharparika</s> (calamine) — combined with the potent [substance], sulphur, being united, mixed in equal proportion — this is to be supplied. Having performed [the procedure] by what means? By the previously described procedural combination — whatever procedure was described, namely the apparatus and the like, by that very combination. It should be cooked thoroughly — excessively — until it attains a bodiless state (<s>aśarīratā</s>); that powder dissolves inside the womb — in the belly of mercury — internal dissolution (<s>garbhadruti</s>) occurs. Due to the word 'ca,' it also digests completely. (GRhtCM 5.15:2)

children.text: gold:: garbhadruti
children.translated_text: [Section: Gold — <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal dissolution)]

children.text: vyūḍho+atha gandhakāśmā śataguṇasaṃkhyaṃ tathottame hemni /
children.translated_text: 'Then a lump of sulphur-stone, in hundredfold quantity, in the finest gold,

children.text:
sūte ca bhavati piṣṭirdravati hi garbhe na vismayaḥ kāryaḥ //
                                GRht_5.16 //
children.translated_text: and in mercury (<s>sūta</s>), a paste is formed; it dissolves inside the womb — no wonder should be had.' (GRht 5.16)

children.text: vidhyantaramāha vyūḍha ityādi // GRhtCM_5.16:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another method, with 'a lump' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.16:1)

children.text: athetyanantaram // GRhtCM_5.16:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Atha' (then) means subsequently. (GRhtCM 5.16:2)

children.text:
gandhakāśmā gandhapāṣāṇaḥ śataguṇasaṃkhyaṃ yathā syāttathā uttame hemni
                            pūrṇavarṇe vyūḍho nirvāhyaḥ tadgandhavyūḍhaṃ hema sūte pārade
                            piṣṭirbhavati hi niścitaṃ garbhe rasāntardravati garbhadrutir
                            bhavatītyatravismayo // GRhtCM_5.16:3 //
children.translated_text: A sulphur-stone (<s>gandhakāśmā</s>) — a sulphur-rock — in hundredfold quantity — such that the amount is a hundredfold — [processed] in the finest gold — gold of full colour — should be 'driven' (<s>vyūḍha</s>, carried through) — the sulphur-driven gold, when combined with mercury (<s>sūta</s>, <s>pārada</s>), a paste is certainly formed; inside the womb — in the interior of mercury — it dissolves, internal dissolution occurs — in this there is no wonder. (GRhtCM 5.16:3)

children.text: gold:: bīja for garbhadruti
children.translated_text: [Section: Gold — seed (<s>bīja</s>) for <s>garbhadruti</s>]

children.text: athavā śatanirvyūḍhaṃ rasakavaraṃ śuddhahemni varabījam /
children.translated_text: 'Or alternatively, the finest <s>rasaka</s> (calamine), hundred-driven in pure gold, becomes the excellent seed (<s>bīja</s>);

children.text: bījaṃ jarati rasendre dravati ca garbhe na sandehaḥ // GRht_5.17 //
children.translated_text: the seed digests in the lord of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>) and dissolves inside the womb — there is no doubt.' (GRht 5.17)

children.text: vidhyantaramāha athavetyādi // GRhtCM_5.17:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another method, with 'or alternatively' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.17:1)

children.text:
athaveti samuccaye rasakavaraṃ śreṣṭhaṃ kharparikaṃ śuddhahemni
                            pūrṇavarṇe śatanirvyūḍhaṃ kuryāt śataguṇanirvāhaḥ kāryaḥ ekaguṇasvarṇe
                            śataguṇanirvāha iti yuktaṃ evaṃ kṛte sati varabījaṃ śreṣṭhabījaṃ bhavati
                            tadbījaṃ garbhe rasodare dravati garbhe drutirbhavati rasendre pārade
                            śīghraṃ avipambitaṃ jarati ca niḥśeṣatām āpnoti vidhānena iti śeṣaḥ atra
                            dravaṇe jaraṇe ca na sandehaḥ // GRhtCM_5.17:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Or alternatively' — in the sense of conjunction. The finest <s>rasaka</s> — the best calamine (<s>kharparika</s>) — should be hundred-driven (<s>śatanirvyūḍha</s>) in pure gold — gold of full colour — meaning a hundred-fold driving should be performed — with one part gold, a hundredfold driving. When done thus, it becomes an excellent seed (<s>varabīja</s>) — the best seed. That seed dissolves inside the womb — in the belly of mercury — internal dissolution occurs; in the lord of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>, <s>pārada</s>) it digests quickly — without delay — and completely — 'by the [proper] procedure' is to be supplied. Here, regarding both dissolution and digestion, there is no doubt. (GRhtCM 5.17:2)

children.text: gold:: bīja for garbhadruti
children.translated_text: [Section: Gold — seed for <s>garbhadruti</s>]

children.text: athavā tālakasatvaṃ śilayā vā tacca hemni nirvyūḍham /
children.translated_text: 'Or alternatively, the essence (<s>sattva</s>) of orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>), or with realgar (<s>śilā</s>) — that, hundred-driven in gold,

children.text: śataguṇamatha mūṣāyāṃ jarati rasendro dravati garbhe ca // GRht_5.18 //
children.translated_text: then in a crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>), the lord of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>) digests [it] and it dissolves inside the womb.' (GRht 5.18)

children.text: pūrvārthe vidhyantaramāha athavetyādi // GRhtCM_5.18:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another method for the same purpose, with 'or alternatively' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.18:1)

children.text:
tāpakasatvaṃ haritāpasāraṃ śataguṇaṃ śataguṇitaṃ hemni kanake nirvyūḍhaṃ
                            andhamūṣāyāṃ vā prakāśamūṣāyāṃ vahniyogena iti śeṣaḥ tāpakasatvasya
                            hemni nirvāhaḥ kārya iti vyaktiḥ tacca tat sattvaṃ kevapaṃ vā śipayā
                            manaḥśipayā sārdhaṃ nirvyūḍhaṃ kāryaṃ taddhema garbhe rasodare dravati
                            atha rasendro rasarājaḥ drutaṃ jarati vidhāneneti // GRhtCM_5.18:2
                            //
children.translated_text: The essence of orpiment (<s>tālaka-sattva</s>) — the extract of yellow arsenic — hundredfold, multiplied a hundred times, should be driven into gold (<s>kanaka</s>); in a blind crucible (<s>andhamūṣā</s>) or in an open crucible, by combination with fire — this is to be supplied. The driving of the orpiment-essence into gold should be performed — this is the clarification. And that essence, either alone or combined with realgar (<s>śilā</s>, <s>manaḥśilā</s>), should be driven [into gold]. That gold dissolves inside the womb — in the interior of mercury; then the lord of mercury (<s>rasarāja</s>) quickly digests [it] — by the [proper] procedure. (GRhtCM 5.18:2)

children.text: lead, tin:: combined māraṇa
children.translated_text: [Section: Lead, Tin — combined <s>māraṇa</s> (killing)]

children.text: rasadaradābhrakatāpyavimalāmṛtaśulbalohaparpaṭikā /
children.translated_text: 'Mercury, cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), mica (<s>abhraka</s>), pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>), [processed] silver (<s>vimalā</s>), antimony (<s>amṛta</s>), copper (<s>śulba</s>), iron (<s>loha</s>) — [made into] a flake (<s>parpaṭikā</s>);

children.text: snuhyarkadugdhapiṣṭaṃ kaṃkuṣṭhaśilāyutaṃ nāgam // GRht_5.19 //
children.translated_text: lead (<s>nāga</s>), ground with the milk of <s>snuhī</s> (euphorbia) and <s>arka</s> (calotropis), combined with <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> and realgar (<s>śilā</s>).' (GRht 5.19)

children.text: abhrakatālakaśaṅkharasasahitaṃ tatpunaḥ punaḥ puṭitam /
children.translated_text: 'Combined with mica, orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>), conch (<s>śaṅkha</s>), and mercury — that [lead], heated repeatedly,

children.text: ciñcākṣāravimiśraṃ vaṅgaṃ nirjīvatāṃ yāti // GRht_5.20 //
children.translated_text: mixed with tamarind alkali (<s>ciñcākṣāra</s>) — the tin attains a lifeless state.' (GRht 5.20)

children.text: vidhinānena ca puṭitaṃ mriyate nāgaṃ nirutthatāṃ ca gatam /
children.translated_text: 'By this procedure, when heated, lead dies and becomes incapable of rising;

children.text: vaṅgaṃ ca sarvakarmasu niyujyate tadapi gatajīvam // GRht_5.21 //
children.translated_text: tin too, having lost its life, is employed in all [alchemical] operations.' (GRht 5.21)

children.text: atha vidhyantaramāha rasetyādi // GRhtCM_5.19-21:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another method, with 'mercury' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.19–21:1)

children.text:
rasadaradābhrakatāpyamiti rasaḥ pāradaḥ darado hiṅgupaḥ abhrakaṃ pratītaṃ
                            tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ vimapā rukmamākṣikaṃ mṛtaṃ yacchupbaṃ tāmraṃ poho
                            muṇḍādiśca eteṣāṃ rasādīnāṃ rasaparpaṭīvat parpaṭikā kāryā //
                            GRhtCM_5.19-21:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Mercury, cinnabar, mica, pyrite' — mercury (<s>rasa</s>) is <s>pārada</s>; <s>darada</s> is <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar); mica (<s>abhraka</s>) is well-known; <s>tāpya</s> is <s>svarṇamākṣika</s> (gold-pyrite); <s>vimalā</s> is <s>rukmamākṣika</s> (silver-pyrite) that has been killed; copper (<s>śulba</s>) is <s>tāmra</s>; <s>loha</s> is iron (<s>muṇḍa</s>) and the like. From these — mercury and the rest — a flake (<s>parpaṭikā</s>), like a mercury-flake, should be made. (GRhtCM 5.19–21:2)

children.text:
tayā yutaṃ nāgaṃ punaḥ kaṅkuṣṭhaśipāyutaṃ kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ haritapītavarṇo
                            viṣaharapāṣāṇajātiḥ śipā manohvā tābhyāṃ yutaṃ miśritaṃ yannāgaṃ sīsakaḥ
                            snuhyarkadugdhapiṣṭaṃ kāryaṃ snuhī sehuṇḍaḥ arkaḥ prasiddho viṭapī
                            tayordugdhena piṣṭaṃ pāṃśubhūtaṃ mṛtaṃ yannāgaṃ kukkuṭapuṭavidhāneneti
                            śeṣaḥ etadapi bījaṃ siddhaṃ garbhe dravati ca pūrvasaṃbandhāt //
                            GRhtCM_5.19-21:3 //
children.translated_text: Combined with that [flake], lead (<s>nāga</s>) — furthermore, combined with <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> and realgar (<s>śilā</s>) — <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is a type of anti-poison stone of yellowish-green colour; <s>śilā</s> is <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar) — combined, mixed with those two — lead (<s>sīsaka</s>) — should be made into a paste with the milk of <s>snuhī</s> (euphorbia, <s>sehuṇḍa</s>) and <s>arka</s> (calotropis, a well-known shrub) — ground to a powder, killed — by the <s>kukkuṭapuṭa</s> (hen-heating) method — this is to be supplied. This too becomes a perfected seed and dissolves inside the womb, due to the previous connection. (GRhtCM 5.19–21:3)

children.text: atha vaṅgabījavidhānamāha abhraketyādi // GRhtCM_5.19-21:4 //
children.translated_text: Now he states the tin-seed procedure, with 'mica' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.19–21:4)

children.text:
ciñcākṣāravimiśraṃ yadvaṅgaṃ ampikākṣārayuktaṃ vaṅgaṃ
                            abhrakatāpakaśaṅkharasasahitaṃ abhrakaṃ pratītaṃ tāpakaṃ haritāpaṃ
                            śaṅkhaṃ kambugrīvaṃ rasaḥ pāradaḥ etaiścaturbhiḥ sahitaṃ yathā syāttathā
                            punaḥ punaḥ vāraṃ vāraṃ nirutthaṃ yāvat tāvatpuṭitaṃ kuryāt //
                            GRhtCM_5.19-21:5 //
children.translated_text: Mixed with tamarind alkali (<s>ciñcākṣāra</s>) — tin mixed with tamarind (<s>amlikā</s>) alkali, combined with mica, orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>, <s>haritāla</s>), conch (<s>śaṅkha</s>, <s>kambugrīva</s>), and mercury (<s>rasa</s>, <s>pārada</s>) — these four; combined as described, it should be heated (<s>puṭita</s>) again and again, repeatedly, until it becomes incapable of rising (<s>niruttha</s>). (GRhtCM 5.19–21:5)

children.text:
etadauṣadhasyāṃśabhāgena saha puṭanādvaṅgaṃ nirjīvatāṃ yāti
                            pañcatvamāpnoti etadapi bījaṃ siddhaṃ garbhadrāvaṇe jāraṇārthe ca
                            pūrvasaṃbandhāt // GRhtCM_5.19-21:6 //
children.translated_text: Through heating with this medicine in proportionate quantity, tin attains a lifeless state — attains dissolution. This too becomes a perfected seed for internal dissolution (<s>garbhadrāvaṇa</s>) and digestion (<s>jāraṇā</s>), due to the previous connection. (GRhtCM 5.19–21:6)

children.text:
nāgavaṅgayor etad auṣadhaṃ kāraṇamityāha vidhinetyādi // GRhtCM_5.19-21:7
                            //
children.translated_text: He states that this medicine is the cause [of killing] for both lead and tin, with 'by this procedure' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.19–21:7)

children.text:
anena vidhinā uktavidhānena nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ puṭitaṃ sat mriyate mṛtaṃ
                            bhavatīti vāmunā vidhānenaiva nirutthatāṃ gataṃ aśarīratāṃ prāptaṃ
                            vaṅgaṃ sarvakarmasu cāraṇajāraṇabhakṣaṇādikāryeṣu niyujyate rasajñairiti
                            śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_5.19-21:8 //
children.translated_text: By this procedure — by the described method — lead (<s>sīsaka</s>), when heated (<s>puṭita</s>), dies — becomes killed. And by this very method, tin, having attained the state of being incapable of rising — having reached a bodiless state — is employed in all [alchemical] operations — transmutation, digestion, consumption, and other tasks — 'by those who know mercury' is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 5.19–21:8)

children.text:
nāgavaṅgamāraṇam ekavidham evoktam atas tadbhakṣaṇādiṣu parasparaṃ
                            guṇādhikayogyaṃ natu jāraṇādiṣu // GRhtCM_5.19-21:9 //
children.translated_text: The killing of lead and tin has been stated as one and the same procedure; therefore, [either is] suitable for superiority of quality in consumption and the like, but not [interchangeable] in digestion and the like. (GRhtCM 5.19–21:9)

children.text: gold:: bīja for garbhadruti
children.translated_text: [Section: Gold — seed for <s>garbhadruti</s>]

children.text: mṛtanāgaṃ mṛtavaṅgaṃ mṛtavaraśulvaṃ mṛtaṃ tathā tīkṣṇam /
children.translated_text: 'Killed lead, killed tin, killed excellent copper, and killed iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) —

children.text: ekaikaṃ hemavare śatanirvyūḍhaṃ dravati garbhe ca // GRht_5.22 //
children.translated_text: each one, hundred-driven in the finest gold, dissolves inside the womb.' (GRht 5.22)

children.text:
nāgavaṅgaśupvatīkṣṇānāṃ jāraṇavidhānamāha mṛtanāgamityādi //
                            GRhtCM_5.22:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the digestion procedure for lead, tin, copper, and iron, with 'killed lead' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.22:1)

children.text:
mṛtanāgamiti mṛtaṃ nirjīvatāṃ gataṃ yannāgaṃ sīsakaṃ tathānena vidhānena
                            mṛtaṃ vaṅgaṃ tathā mṛtaṃ nirutthatāṃ gataṃ varaśupbaṃ tāmraṃ tathā ca
                            mṛtaṃ tīkṣṇam arivargeṇeti śeṣaḥ eṣāṃ madhye ekaikaṃ nāgaṃ vā vaṅgaṃ vā
                            śupbaṃ vā tīkṣṇaṃ vā pṛthaktvena hemavare pūrṇavarṇe svarṇe
                            śatanirvyūḍhaṃ hemnaḥ śataguṇanirvāhitaṃ kuryāt tatsiddhaṃ garbhe
                            rasodare dravati caśabdājjarati ca // GRhtCM_5.22:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Killed lead' — lead (<s>sīsaka</s>) that has been killed, that has attained a lifeless state; similarly, by this procedure, killed tin; similarly, killed excellent copper (<s>śulba</s>, <s>tāmra</s>); and similarly, killed iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) — 'with the group of enemy [substances]' is to be supplied. Among these, each one — lead or tin or copper or iron — individually, hundred-driven in the finest gold — gold of full colour — one should make a hundred-fold driving of gold. That perfected [seed] dissolves inside the womb — in the belly of mercury; and due to the word 'ca,' it also digests completely. (GRhtCM 5.22:2)

children.text: gold:: mahābīja
children.translated_text: [Section: Gold — <s>mahābīja</s> (great seed)]

children.text: samagarbhe drutikaraṇaṃ hemno vakṣyāmyahaṃ paraṃ yogam /
children.translated_text: 'I shall now describe, for achieving dissolution in an equal womb, the supreme combination for gold.

children.text: bhrāmakasasyakacūrṇaṃ śatanirvyūḍhaṃ mahābījam // GRht_5.23 //
children.translated_text: The powder of <s>bhrāmaka</s> (loadstone) and grain (<s>sasya</s>), hundred-driven — [this is] the great seed (<s>mahābīja</s>).' (GRht 5.23)

children.text: mahābījaprabhāvaṃ darśayannāha samagarbha ityādi // GRhtCM_5.23:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Showing the power of the great seed (<s>mahābīja</s>), he says 'in an equal womb' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.23:1)

children.text:
ihāsmiñśāstre vidhinā śāstroktarītyā yāni bījānyuktāni tāni kartavyāni
                            sāmānyeneti bhāvaḥ paraṃ garbhadrutyarthaṃ ayaṃ vārttikendro yogaḥ
                            vārttāsu kuśapā vārtikāḥ śāstropadeśarahitā ityarthaḥ atra bhāvādyarthe
                            ikpratyayaḥ teṣu vārtikeṣu indraḥ pravaro yogaḥ tathānenaiva prakāreṇa
                            ekamataścāyaṃ śāstropadeśikānāṃ śāstropadeśarahitānāṃ ca abhimata
                            ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.23:2 //
children.translated_text: Here, in this treatise, by the [proper] procedure — in the manner prescribed by the treatise — whatever seeds have been described should be prepared — generally, this is the purport. The supreme [combination] for the purpose of internal dissolution (<s>garbhadruti</s>) — this is the chief among combinations of practitioners (<s>vārtikendra</s>); <s>vārtikas</s> are those skilled in practical matters — meaning those without [merely] textual instruction. Among those practitioners, 'indra' means the foremost combination; and thus, in this very manner, this is agreed upon by both the textually instructed and the practice-skilled — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 5.23:2)

children.text: garbhadruti
children.translated_text: [Section: <s>Garbhadruti</s> (internal dissolution)]

children.text: athavā gandhakadhūmaṃ tālakadhūmaṃ śilāhvarasakasya /
children.translated_text: 'Or alternatively, the fumes of sulphur, the fumes of orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>), and of realgar (<s>śilāhva</s>) —

children.text: dattvādhomukhamūṣāṃ dīrghatamāṃ kharparasyārdhe // GRht_5.24 //
children.translated_text: having placed [them] in a downward-facing crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>), a very long one, over half of a <s>kharpara</s> (shallow dish).' (GRht 5.24)

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ lagnā piṣṭī sudṛḍhā ca yathā tathā ca kartavyā /
children.translated_text: 'The paste, firmly attached above, should be made such that it is very firm.

children.text: dattvā kharparapṛṣṭhe daityendraṃ dāhayettadanu // GRht_5.25 //
children.translated_text: Having placed [the fuel] on the back of the <s>kharpara</s>, one should then heat [it as an offering to] the lord of <s>daityas</s>.' (GRht 5.25)

children.text: stokaṃ stokaṃ dattvā karṣāgnau dhmāpayenmṛdā liptām /
children.translated_text: 'Adding little by little, one should blow [with bellows] over a charcoal fire, [the crucible] coated with clay.

children.text: garbhe dravati hi bījaṃ mriyate tathādhike dāhe // GRht_5.26 //
children.translated_text: The seed dissolves inside the womb; it dies with increased heating.' (GRht 5.26)

children.text: rasodare bījadrāvaṇavidhānamāha athavetyādi // GRhtCM_5.24-26:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the procedure for dissolving the seed inside the womb — in the belly of mercury — with 'or alternatively' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.24–26:1)

children.text: athaveti samuccaye // GRhtCM_5.24-26:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Or alternatively' — in the sense of conjunction. (GRhtCM 5.24–26:2)

children.text:
ūrdhvaṃ dīrghatamamūṣāyantrasya tapabhāge piṣṭī rasendrabījayor nirmitā
                            piṣṭikā ca punaḥ sudṛḍhā yathā syāttathā pagnā kartavyā //
                            GRhtCM_5.24-26:3 //
children.translated_text: Above — in the upper part of the long crucible-apparatus — the paste made from mercury and seed, the formed pellet, should be made to adhere such that it is very firm. (GRhtCM 5.24–26:3)

children.text:
kiṃ kṛtvā kharparasyārdhe mṛnmayapātrasya khaṇḍārdhe khaṇḍaikadeśa
                            ityarthaḥ dīrghatamāṃ adhobhāgamukhīṃ adhobhāge mukhaṃ yasyāḥ sā
                            tathoktā tāṃ dattvā // GRhtCM_5.24-26:4 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? Having placed in half of a <s>kharpara</s> (crucible-lid) — in a fragment-half of an earthen vessel, meaning one section of a fragment — [a tube] with its mouth facing downward, having its opening at the lower part — having placed that. (GRhtCM 5.24–26:4)

children.text:
punaḥ kiṃ kṛtvā gandhakadhūmaṃ dattvā vā stokaṃ stokaṃ appamappaṃ
                            tāpakadhūmaṃ dattvā vā śipāhvarasakasya śipāhvā manaḥśipā rasakaḥ
                            kharparaḥ cakavad bhāvasamāsaḥ tasya dhūmaṃ dattvā // GRhtCM_5.24-26:5
                            //
children.translated_text: Again, having done what? Having given sulphur-smoke; or having given a little heat-smoke bit by bit; or having given the smoke of <s>śilāhva rasaka</s> — <s>śilāhvā</s> is <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar), <s>rasaka</s> is <s>kharpara</s> (calamine) — [these form] a <s>cakravat bhāvasamāsa</s> (cyclic compound) — having given its smoke. (GRhtCM 5.24–26:5)

children.text:
punastatkharparaṃ adhomukhamukhāṃ ca mṛdā piptāṃ mṛdveṣṭitāṃ karīṣāgnau
                            dhmāpayet karīṣavahnāvityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.24-26:6 //
children.translated_text: Again, that <s>kharpara</s> (lid) and the downward-facing mouth-[tube], smeared with clay, should be smelted in cow-dung fire — in cow-dung fuel-fire, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 5.24–26:6)

Thus, having placed the downward-facing [tube] and the <s>kharpara</s>, and [having placed] <s>daityendra</s> (sulphur, 'lord of demons') called <s>balī</s> — after the introduction, one should heat afterwards, after that process. (GRhtCM 5.24–26:7)

children.text:
evaṃ kṛte sati rasendramipitaṃ yadbījaṃ tadgarbhe rasendrāntardravati //
                            GRhtCM_5.24-26:8 //
children.translated_text: When this is done, whatever seed has been placed in the king of <s>rasas</s> (mercury) — that melts inside the interior of mercury. (GRhtCM 5.24–26:8)

children.text:
punarbījasahito rasendro 'dhike dāhe sati mriyata ityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_5.24-26:9 //
children.translated_text: Again, the king of <s>rasas</s> together with the seed dies — is destroyed — when excessive heating occurs, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 5.24–26:9)

children.text: śpokatrayasaṃbandhādviśeṣakam // GRhtCM_5.24-26:10 //
children.translated_text: Due to the connection of the three verses, this is a specification. (GRhtCM 5.24–26:10)

children.text: viḍa:: production
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>viḍa</s> (alkaline salt): production

children.text: gandhakatālakaśailāḥ sauvīrakarasakagairikaṃ daradam /
children.translated_text: Sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>), bitumen (<s>śailā</s>), antimony (<s>sauvīraka</s>), calamine (<s>rasaka</s>), ochre (<s>gairika</s>), and cinnabar (<s>darada</s>);

children.text: kṣārāmlalavaṇāni viḍo mākṣikavaikrāntavimalasamabhāgaiḥ // GRht_5.27 //
children.translated_text: alkalis, acids, and salts — [these constitute] <s>viḍa</s> (alkaline salt) [when combined] with equal parts of <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), <s>vaikrānta</s>, and <s>vimala</s>. (GRht 5.27)

children.text: atha suvarṇajāraṇārthaṃ biḍamāha gandhaketyādi // GRhtCM_5.27:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now, for the purpose of gold-digestion (<s>suvarṇajāraṇā</s>), he describes <s>viḍa</s> with 'sulphur' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.27:1)

children.text:
gandhakatāpakaśaipā iti gandhakaṃ pratītaṃ tāpakaṃ haritāpaṃ śaipaḥ
                            śipājatuḥ dvaṃdvaḥ samāsaḥ tena tathoktāḥ samabhāgāḥ kāryāḥ //
                            GRhtCM_5.27:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Sulphur, orpiment, and bitumen' — <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) is well-known; <s>tālaka</s> is <s>haritāla</s> (orpiment); <s>śaila</s> is <s>śilājatu</s> (bitumen) — [this is] a <s>dvandva</s> compound. Therefore, equal parts of these should be prepared. (GRhtCM 5.27:2)

Further: <s>sauvīraka</s> is antimony eye-salve (<s>śuklāñjana</s>); <s>rasaka</s> is calamine (<s>kharparika</s>); <s>gairika</s> is mineral ochre (<s>dhātugairika</s>); <s>darada</s> is cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>). Here the compound is an <s>ekavadbhāvasamāsa</s> (collective compound); equal parts of each should be prepared. (GRhtCM 5.27:3)

children.text:
punaḥ kṣārāmpapavaṇāni kṣārā yavakṣārādayaḥ ampaṃ jambīrādi pavaṇāni
                            saindhavādīni etānyapi samabhāgāni // GRhtCM_5.27:4 //
children.translated_text: Further: alkalis, acids, and salts — alkalis are barley-alkali (<s>yavakṣāra</s>) and the like; acid is citron (<s>jambīra</s>) and the like; salts are rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>) and the like. These also should be in equal parts. (GRhtCM 5.27:4)

children.text:
