kaiḥ saha mākṣikavaikrāntavimapasamabhāgaiḥ saha mākṣikaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ
                            vaikrāntaṃ vajrabhūmijaṃ rajaḥ vimapaṃ rukmamākṣikaṃ etāni samabhāgāni
                            tairbiḍa ucyate sarvaiḥ samabhāgaiḥ sumarditair biḍaḥ kārya ityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_5.27:5 //
children.translated_text: With what? With equal parts of <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>vaikrānta</s>, and <s>vimala</s>. <s>Mākṣika</s> is gold-pyrite (<s>svarṇamākṣika</s>); <s>vaikrānta</s> is diamond-earth dust (<s>vajrabhūmija rajas</s>); <s>vimala</s> is copper-pyrite (<s>rukmamākṣika</s>). These in equal parts — with all [ingredients] in equal parts, well-ground, the <s>viḍa</s> should be prepared, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 5.27:5)

children.text: viḍa:: for garbhadruti
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>viḍa</s>: for internal dissolution (<s>garbhadruti</s>)

children.text: kṛtvā suvarṇapiṣṭīṃ mṛditāṃ ca suveṣṭitāmanenaiva /
children.translated_text: Having made a cake (<s>piṣṭī</s>) of gold, kneaded and well-wrapped with this very [viḍa],

children.text: tripuṭaistapte khalve mṛditā garbhe tathā dravati // GRht_5.28 //
children.translated_text: ground in a heated mortar with cow-dung-fire cakes (<s>tripuṭas</s>), it thus melts inside [the mercury]. (GRht 5.28)

children.text:
biḍayogādyathā bījaṃ garbhe dravati tathāha kṛtvetyādi // GRhtCM_5.28:1
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He explains how the seed melts inside [mercury] through the <s>viḍa</s> formula, with 'having made' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.28:1)

children.text:
pūrvoktā yā piṣṭī tāmanenaivoktabiḍayogena tapte khapve
                            taptasaṃbandhāppohamaye tripuṭaiḥ karīṣāgnyātmakair mṛditā gharṣitā sati
                            anenaiva ca veṣṭitā kāryā // GRhtCM_5.28:2 //
children.translated_text: The aforementioned cake (<s>piṣṭī</s>), with this very <s>viḍa</s> formula, should be ground in a heated mortar — a metallic mortar brought to heat through contact — with cow-dung-fire cakes (<s>tripuṭas</s>); and it should be wrapped with this very [viḍa]. (GRhtCM 5.28:2)

children.text:
kiṃ kṛtvā suvarṇapiṣṭīṃ kanakapiṣṭīṃ vā anyasyāpi dhātoḥ suvarṇapiṣṭīṃ
                            śobhanavarṇāṃ piṣṭīṃ kṛtvā // GRhtCM_5.28:3 //
children.translated_text: Having made what? A gold cake — a cake of gold; or of any other metal — a cake of beautiful color (<s>suvarṇapiṣṭī</s>) — a cake of fine appearance — having made [it]. (GRhtCM 5.28:3)

children.text:
khapve mṛditā satī tathā tenaiva prakāreṇa natvanyaprakāreṇa garbhe
                            rasodare dravati sapiparūpā tiṣṭhati // GRhtCM_5.28:4 //
children.translated_text: Ground in the mortar, it thus — in that very manner and not otherwise — melts inside the interior — inside the mercury's belly — it remains in a dissolved form. (GRhtCM 5.28:4)

children.text: viḍa:: for garbhadruti
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>viḍa</s>: for internal dissolution (<s>garbhadruti</s>)

children.text: rakte śatanirvyūḍhaṃ netrahitaṃ bhasma vaikrāntakaṃ cātha /
children.translated_text: The ash of <s>vaikrānta</s>, processed a hundred times in the red [group], beneficial to the eyes,

children.text: vimalaṃ śatanirvyūḍhaṃ grasati samaṃ dravati garbhe ca // GRht_5.29 //
children.translated_text: and <s>vimala</s>, processed a hundred times — [mercury] consumes equally and melts inside. (GRht 5.29)

children.text: atha vaikrāntagarbhadrutimāha rakta ityādi // GRhtCM_5.29:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now he describes internal dissolution using <s>vaikrānta</s>, with 'red' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.29:1)

children.text:
vaikrāntabhasma vajrabhūmijaṃ rajas tadudbhavaṃ bhasma rakte raktagaṇe
                            śatanirvyūḍhaṃ śatavāraṃ nirvāhitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_5.29:2 //
children.translated_text: The ash of <s>vaikrānta</s> — the dust born of <s>vajrabhūmi</s> (diamond-earth), the ash produced from it — should be processed a hundred times through the red group (<s>raktagaṇa</s>). (GRhtCM 5.29:2)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ netrahitaṃ netrahitaśabdena maṇitvaṃ darśitaṃ maṇayo
                            netrahitā iti // GRhtCM_5.29:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality? Beneficial to the eyes — the word 'beneficial to the eyes' (<s>netrahita</s>) indicates the gem-like quality; for gems are called 'beneficial to the eyes.' (GRhtCM 5.29:3)

children.text:
vimapaṃ rūpyamākṣikaṃ śvetavarṇaṃ yanmākṣikaṃ raktagaṇe śatanirvyūḍhaṃ
                            kuryāt // GRhtCM_5.29:4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vimala</s> — the white-colored pyrite (<s>rūpyamākṣika</s>) — should be processed a hundred times through the red group. (GRhtCM 5.29:4)

children.text:
tadubhayaṃ vaikrāntaṃ vimapaṃ ca raktaśatanirvyūḍhaṃ sat raso
                            grāsavidhānaṃ vihāya samaṃ grasati kavapayati stadgrasitaṃ garbhe
                            rasāntardravati jarati ca iti caśabdārthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.29:5 //
children.translated_text: Both — <s>vaikrānta</s> and <s>vimala</s> — having been processed a hundred times through the red [group], mercury consumes them equally — it swallows them — dispensing with the [usual] bolus method; and what has been consumed melts inside the interior of mercury — it is digested too, is the meaning of the word 'ca.' (GRhtCM 5.29:5)

children.text: viḍa:: for garbhadruti:: immer mit śatanirvāhaṇa
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>viḍa</s>: for internal dissolution: always with hundred-fold processing (<s>śatanirvāhaṇa</s>)

children.text: ye kecidviḍayogāḥ kṣārāmlalavaṇāni dīptavargāśca /
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>viḍa</s> formulas, alkalis, acids, salts, and kindling groups there are —

children.text: sarve śatanirvyūḍhā garbhadrutikārakāḥ kathitāḥ // GRht_5.30 //
children.translated_text: all, when processed a hundred times, are said to cause internal dissolution (<s>garbhadruti</s>). (GRht 5.30)

children.text: raktagaṇādhikyaṃ darśayannāha ya ityādi // GRhtCM_5.30:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Showing the primacy of the red group, he says 'whatever' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.30:1)

children.text:
ye kecidviḍayogā atra granthāntareṣvapi ca kathitāḥ tathā
                            kṣārāmpapavaṇāni kathitāni kṣārā yavakṣārādayaḥ atha ca
                            vṛkṣauṣadhisamudbhavāḥ ampā jambīrādayaḥ ampavṛkṣaśākasamudbhavāśca
                            yānyetāni kathitāni ca punarye dīptavargāḥ kathitā dīptikarā yogā
                            abhihitāḥ te sarve biḍakṣārāmpapavaṇadīptavargāḥ śatanirvyūḍhā
                            garbhadrutikārakāḥ garbhe rasodare drutaṃ dravarūpaṃ kurvanti
                            dhātumaṇiratnādīnīti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_5.30:2 //
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>viḍa</s> formulas — described here and in other treatises — and likewise the alkalis, acids, and salts that have been described: alkalis such as barley-alkali; acids such as citron and those produced from acid-bearing trees and vegetables; and also whatever kindling groups have been described — agents that produce kindling [in mercury]; all these — <s>viḍa</s>, alkalis, acids, salts, and kindling groups — when processed a hundred times, cause internal dissolution — they make metals, gems, and precious stones dissolve inside the interior of mercury, is the completion. (GRhtCM 5.30:2)

children.text: Menge nirvāhaṇa => grāsa, der assimiliert wird
children.translated_text: [Section:] Quantity of processing → bolus that is assimilated

children.text: śatanirvyūḍhe ca samaṃ pādonaṃ pañcasaptativyūḍhe /
children.translated_text: When processed a hundred times, [mercury consumes] an equal [quantity]; three-quarters when processed seventy-five times;

children.text: pañcāśati tadardhaṃ pādaḥ syātpañcaviṃśatike // GRht_5.31 //
children.translated_text: half when [processed] fifty times; a quarter when [processed] twenty-five times. (GRht 5.31)

children.text: aṣṭāṃśaṃ tu tadardhe ṣoḍaśāṃśaṃ tadardhanirvyūḍhe /
children.translated_text: An eighth at half of that; a sixteenth when processed at half of that;

children.text: tasyārdhe dvātriṃśaccatuḥṣaṣṭyaṃśaṃ tadardhanirvyūḍhe // GRht_5.32 //
children.translated_text: at half of that, a thirty-second; a sixty-fourth when processed at half of that. (GRht 5.32)

children.text: śatanirvāhitādau samādividhānamāha śatetyādi // GRhtCM_5.31-32:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the proportional method beginning with hundred-fold processing, with 'hundred' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.31–32:1)

children.text:
śatanirvyūḍha iti śatavāraṃ nirvāhite raktagaṇe iti śeṣaḥ samaṃ tupyaṃ
                            grasati rasa iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_5.31-32:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Processed a hundred times' — when the red group has been processed a hundred times, is the completion — [mercury] consumes an equal [quantity], is the completion. (GRhtCM 5.31–32:2)

children.text:
punaḥ pañcasaptativyūḍhe sati pādonaṃ caturthāṃśavarjitaṃ samagraṃ
                            grasatīti // GRhtCM_5.31-32:3 //
children.translated_text: Again, when processed seventy-five times, three-quarters — minus one-fourth of the total — it consumes. (GRhtCM 5.31–32:3)

children.text:
punaḥ pañcāśannirvyūḍhe sati tadardhaṃ samasyārdhamiti //
                            GRhtCM_5.31-32:4 //
children.translated_text: Again, when processed fifty times, half — half of the total. (GRhtCM 5.31–32:4)

children.text: punaḥ pañcaviṃśatike sati pādaścaturthāṃśam // GRhtCM_5.31-32:5 //
children.translated_text: Again, when [processed] twenty-five times, a quarter — one-fourth. (GRhtCM 5.31–32:5)

children.text:
nyūnādhike nirvyūḍhe sati nyūnādhikāṃśo jñeya iti viśeṣārthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_5.31-32:6 //
children.translated_text: When the processing is less or more, the proportion should be understood as less or more — this is the specific meaning. (GRhtCM 5.31–32:6)

children.text: appanirvyūḍhakramamāha aṣṭāṃśamityādi // GRhtCM_5.31-32:7 //
children.translated_text: He states the method for lesser processing, with 'an eighth' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.31–32:7)

children.text:
tu punastadardhe sārdhadvādaśake nirvyūḍhe sati aṣṭāṃśaṃ tadardhe
                            ṣaḍvāranirvyūḍhe sati ṣoḍaśāṃśamiti punastasyārdhe trivāranirvyūḍhe sati
                            dvātriṃśadaṃśaṃ tadardhanirvyūḍhe ekadvivāranirvyūḍhe sati
                            catuḥṣaṣṭyaṃśaṃ raso grasatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.31-32:8 //
children.translated_text: Again, at half of that — when processed twelve-and-a-half times, an eighth; at half of that — when processed six times, a sixteenth. Again, at half of that — when processed three times, a thirty-second; at half of that processing — when processed one or two times, mercury consumes a sixty-fourth, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 5.31–32:8)

children.text: garbhadruti
children.translated_text: [Section on] internal dissolution (<s>garbhadruti</s>)

children.text: iti gaditāṃ garbhadrutimabhiṣavayogena cāmlavargeṇa /
children.translated_text: Having known the internal dissolution that has been described, along with the pressing method (<s>abhiṣavayoga</s>) and the acid group,

children.text: svedanavidhinā jñātvā mṛditāṃ tapte tu khalvatale // GRht_5.33 //
children.translated_text: through the steaming method (<s>svedanavidhi</s>), one should grind [it] on a heated mortar surface. (GRht 5.33)

children.text: garbhadrutau satyāṃ kartavyamāha itītyādi // GRhtCM_5.33:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] When internal dissolution has been achieved, he states what should be done, with 'thus' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.33:1)

children.text:
ityuktavidhānena gaditāṃ kathitāṃ garbhadrutiṃ jñātvā tapte khapvatape
                            pohamaye karīṣāgninā uṣṇatāṃ nīte mṛditāṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_5.33:2 //
children.translated_text: Having known the internal dissolution as described — as stated — by the described method, one should grind [it] on a heated mortar surface — a metallic [mortar] brought to heat by cow-dung fire. (GRhtCM 5.33:2)

children.text:
kena abhiṣavayogena abhiṣavaḥ saṃmardanaṃ tasya yogena na kevapamanena
                            ampavargeṇa ca jambīrādinā na kevapamanenāpi svedanavidhinā ca
                            svedanavidhiḥ svedanasaṃskāroktatvānnātrābhihitaḥ jāraṇahetoriti śeṣaḥ
                            // GRhtCM_5.33:3 //
children.translated_text: By what? By the pressing method (<s>abhiṣava</s>) — <s>abhiṣava</s> means thorough grinding; through its method — not by this [method] alone; and by the acid group — citron and the like — not by this alone either; and by the steaming method — the steaming method has been stated under the steaming process (<s>svedasaṃskāra</s>), hence it is not described here — for the purpose of digestion, is the completion. (GRhtCM 5.33:3)

children.text:
Durchfṃhrung von saṃskāra gemĪ“ den verwendeten bījas
                                usw.
children.translated_text: [Section:] Execution of the process according to the seeds used, etc.

children.text: jñātvā bījabalābalamardanayogaṃ kṛtaṃ ca rasarāje /
children.translated_text: Having known the strength and weakness of the seeds, and the grinding method that has been performed on the king of <s>rasas</s>,

children.text: svedavidhānaṃ ca puṭaṃ yantraṃ vā vihitarasakarma // GRht_5.34 //
children.translated_text: along with the steaming method and the <s>puṭa</s> (calcination) or apparatus — [one should perform] the prescribed mercury operations. (GRht 5.34)

children.text:
mardanasvedanayoḥ pūrvopakaraṇaṃ darśayannāha jñātvetyādi //
                            GRhtCM_5.34:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Showing the preliminary requirements for grinding and steaming, he says 'having known' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.34:1)

children.text:
bījabapābapamardanayogaṃ kṛtaṃ jñātvā bījānāṃ dhātūpadhātuyogajanitānāṃ
                            bapābape nyūnādhike yo+asau mardanayogastameva kṛtaṃ jñātvā viditvā
                            rasarāje svedavidhānaṃ kuryāt vā puṭaṃ vahniyogaṃ kuryāt vā yantraṃ
                            vihitarasakarma kuryāt vihitaṃ kṛtaṃ rasasya karma saṃskārarūpaṃ yatra
                            tathoktaṃ garbhayantrādikamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.34:2 //
children.translated_text: Having known the grinding method that accounts for the strength and weakness of the seeds — knowing that particular grinding method [which addresses] the greater or lesser [strength] of the seeds — metals, sub-metals, and compound-produced [substances] — and having done [this] on the king of <s>rasas</s>, one should perform the steaming method; or one should perform <s>puṭa</s> (fire-calcination); or one should perform the apparatus [method] — prescribed mercury operations — prescribed meaning 'performed,' the operation upon mercury in the form of processes (<s>saṃskāra</s>), in which [apparatus] — such as the internal-dissolution apparatus and the like, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 5.34:2)

children.text: sūtavaraṃ lakṣayate bījaṃ nopekṣatāṃ yathā yāti /
children.translated_text: One should observe the foremost mercury; the seed should not reach a state of neglect.

children.text: tadvatkāryaṃ vidhinā sukarma gurupādanirdiṣṭam // GRht_5.35 //
children.translated_text: In the same way, the work should be properly done according to the method, as directed by the guru's feet. (GRht 5.35)

children.text:
sūtakarmaṇo durbodhatvādgurupādaṃ stuvannāha sūtetyādi // GRhtCM_5.35:1
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because the mercury-work is difficult to understand, he praises the guru's feet, saying 'mercury' and so forth. (GRhtCM 5.35:1)

children.text:
yathā yena prakāreṇa sūtavaraṃ pāradaḥ pakṣayate jñāyate karmakṛteti
                            śeṣaḥ punaryathā bījaṃ upekṣatāṃ na yāti samyak mipati tadvattenaiva
                            prakāreṇa gurupādanirdiṣṭaṃ karma ācāryavaryadarśitaṃ pūjyaṃ
                            saṃskārarūpaṃ vidhinā ācāryoktavidhānena kuryāt // GRhtCM_5.35:2 //
children.translated_text: In whatever manner the foremost mercury is observed — is known, as having undergone the process, is the completion; again, in whatever manner the seed does not reach a state of neglect — is properly integrated; in that very manner, the work directed by the guru's feet — shown by the most honored teacher — the venerable process in the form of <s>saṃskāras</s> — should be performed by the method taught by the teacher. (GRhtCM 5.35:2)

children.text: gurupādapakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: The definition of the guru's feet:

children.text: sarvaśāstraviśeṣajñaḥ kuśapo rasakarmaṇi /
children.translated_text: One who is an expert in all the specific sciences, skilled in mercury operations —

children.text: evaṃpakṣaṇasaṃyukto rasavidyāgururbhavet /
children.translated_text: endowed with such characteristics, one becomes a teacher of mercury-science (<s>rasavidyā</s>).

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_5.35:3 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 5.35:3)

children.text: iti garbhadrutijāraṇaprakaraṇam // GRhtCM_5.35:4 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the section on <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction) and <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion). (GRhtCM 5.35:4)

children.text: bāhyadruti
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Bāhyadruti</s> (external liquefaction)

children.text: bāhyadrutirati vimalā sphurati hi keṣāṃcideva siddhānām /
children.translated_text: External liquefaction (<s>bāhyadruti</s>) — pure, it flashes forth for only some accomplished ones (<s>siddha</s>s);

children.text: tebhyaḥ samyak jñātvā kalanāḥ kāryāstathā drutayaḥ // GRht_5.36 //
children.translated_text: having properly learned from them, one should perform the operations (<s>kalanā</s>) and the liquefactions accordingly. (GRht 5.36)

children.text: bāhyadrutiṃ praśaṃsannāha bāhyadrutir ityādi // GRhtCM_5.36:1 //
children.translated_text: Praising external liquefaction, he says '<s>bāhyadruti</s>' and so on. (GRhtCM 5.36:1)

children.text: drutirdvidhoktā garbhadrutirbāhyadrutiśceti // GRhtCM_5.36:2 //
children.translated_text: Liquefaction (<s>druti</s>) has been said to be of two kinds: <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction) and <s>bāhyadruti</s> (external liquefaction). (GRhtCM 5.36:2)

children.text:
garbhadrutiḥ pūrvamuktā bāhyadrutir adhunābhidhīyate // GRhtCM_5.36:3
                            //
children.translated_text: <s>Garbhadruti</s> was described earlier; <s>bāhyadruti</s> is now being described. (GRhtCM 5.36:3)

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭā ativimapā nirmapatarā // GRhtCM_5.36:4 //
children.translated_text: Of what characteristic? Exceedingly pure — purer [than other methods]. (GRhtCM 5.36:4)

children.text:
eṣā ca punaḥ keṣāṃcideva siddhānāṃ sphurati siddhā rasavidyāpāragā
                            nityanāthādayaḥ teṣāṃ te jānantīti // GRhtCM_5.36:5 //
children.translated_text: And this flashes forth — becomes manifest — only to certain accomplished ones (<s>siddha</s>s): <s>Nityanātha</s> and others, who have crossed to the far shore of mercury-science — they know it. (GRhtCM 5.36:5)

children.text: duṣprāpyatvāt bāhyadrutiriha virapā // GRhtCM_5.36:6 //
children.translated_text: Because of its difficulty of attainment, <s>bāhyadruti</s> is rare here [in this world]. (GRhtCM 5.36:6)

children.text:
tebhyaḥ samyak jñātvā tathā tenaiva siddhodeśavidhānena drutayo
                            bāhyadrutayaḥ // GRhtCM_5.36:7 //
children.translated_text: Having properly learned from them — by the very method instructed by those <s>siddha</s>s — the external liquefactions [should be performed]. (GRhtCM 5.36:7)

children.text: jāraṇa of lead
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Jāraṇa</s> (digestion) of lead

children.text: varanāgaṃ rasarājaṃ bījavaraṃ sāritaṃ tathā tritayam /
children.translated_text: Excellent lead (<s>varanāga</s>), the king of mercury (<s>rasarāja</s>), and the best seed (<s>bījavara</s>), combined; and likewise the triad,

children.text: gandhakaśilālasahitaṃ nirnāgaṃ dīpavartito bhavati // GRht_5.37 //
children.translated_text: combined with sulfur, orpiment (<s>śilā</s>), and <s>āla</s> (haritāla) — free from lead, it becomes [when processed by] a lamp-wick. (GRht 5.37)

children.text: baddhvā sudṛḍhe vastre poṭalikāyāṃ śikhīkṛto dīpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having tied [the mixture] in a strong cloth pouch, the lamp being lit [beneath],

children.text: taile magnaṃ kṛtvā nirnāgaṃ jāyate kṣipram // GRht_5.38 //
children.translated_text: having immersed [it] in oil — it becomes lead-free quickly. (GRht 5.38)

children.text: atha nāgajāraṇamāha varanāgamityādi // GRhtCM_5.37-38:1 //
children.translated_text: Now he states the <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion) of lead, beginning with '<s>varanāga</s>' and so on. (GRhtCM 5.37-38:1)

children.text:
varanāgaṃ śreṣṭhajāti sīsakaṃ jāraṇayogyaṃ rasarājaṃ uktasaṃskāraiḥ
                            saṃskṛtaṃ pāradaṃ bījavaraṃ hemabījaṃ etattrayaṃ sāritaṃ mipitaṃ kāryaṃ
                            punargandhakaśipāpasahitaṃ gandhakaṃ pratītaṃ śipā manaḥśipā āpaṃ
                            haritāpaṃ dvandvastāni taiḥ sahitaṃ ca kāryaṃ etat sarvaṣaṭkaṃ
                            dīpavartitaḥ prajvāpitadīpavartiyogāt nirnāgaṃ nāgavarjitaṃ bhavati
                            nāgaṃ jaratītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.37-38:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Excellent lead' (<s>varanāga</s>) — the best variety of lead, suitable for digestion; 'king of mercury' (<s>rasarāja</s>) — mercury purified by the previously described processes; 'best seed' (<s>bījavara</s>) — gold seed. This triad should be combined — merged. Furthermore, combined with sulfur, <s>śilā</s> (<s>manaḥśilā</s>, realgar) and <s>āla</s> (<s>haritāla</s>, orpiment) — a pair — combined with these. This entire sextet becomes lead-free — devoid of lead — through the application of an ignited lamp-wick; meaning the lead is digested. (GRhtCM 5.37-38:2)

children.text:
yathā nirṇāgaṃ syāttathā vidhānam āha baddhvetyādi // GRhtCM_5.37-38:3
                            //
children.translated_text: He states the procedure by which it becomes lead-free, beginning with 'having tied' and so on. (GRhtCM 5.37-38:3)

children.text:
tatpūrvoktaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ sudṛḍhe vastre nūtane vastre atropaśpeṣike 'dhikaraṇe
                            saptamī poṭapikāyāṃ baddhvā punastaipe tipodbhave tatṣaṭkaṃ magnaṃ
                            nimajjitaṃ kṛtvā tadadhaḥ śikhīkṛto dīpo+avadhāryaḥ na śikhī śikhāyuktaḥ
                            kṛtaḥ śikhīkṛtaḥ śikhāvānityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.37-38:4 //
children.translated_text: That previously described sextet, [tied] in a strong cloth — a new cloth — here a locative [case is used] for the container — in a pouch, having tied [it]; then having immersed — submerged — that sextet in sesame oil; beneath that, a lamp should be placed — lit — meaning one having a flame; a flame-possessing [lamp]; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 5.37-38:4)

children.text: anena vidhinā kṣipraṃ śīghraṃ nirnāgaṃ syāditi // GRhtCM_5.37-38:5 //
children.translated_text: By this procedure, it quickly becomes lead-free. (GRhtCM 5.37-38:5)

children.text: jāraṇa of lead
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Jāraṇa</s> (digestion) of lead [continued]

children.text: kṛtvātra dīrghamūṣāṃ sudṛḍhāṃ dhmātaṃ tu bhasmagartāyām /
children.translated_text: Having made a long, sturdy crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>) here, in an ash-pit, having smelted,

children.text: kṣiptvā śilālacūrṇaṃ paścātsūtaṃ tataḥ śilācūrṇaṃ // GRht_5.39 //
children.translated_text: throwing in orpiment (<s>śilāla</s>) powder, then mercury, then orpiment powder again, (GRht 5.39)

children.text: saṃsthāpya bhasmanāto dhmātaṃ syātsvāṃgaśītalaṃ yāvat /
children.translated_text: having covered with ash, smelted until it is self-cooled,

children.text: ākṛṣya tatra sūtaṃ jñātvā nāgaṃ subhakṣitaṃ sakalam // GRht_5.40 //
children.translated_text: extracting mercury therein, knowing that all lead has been well-consumed. (GRht 5.40)

children.text: nirnāgakaraṇe vidhānamāha kṛtvetyādi // GRhtCM_5.39-40:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the procedure for making [mercury] lead-free, beginning with 'having made' and so on. (GRhtCM 5.39-40:1)

children.text:
tu punaḥ dīrghāṃ gostanākārāṃ sudṛḍhāṃ nirvraṇavajropamāṃ mūṣāṃ kṛtvā tāṃ
                            mūṣāṃ prati śipāpacūrṇaṃ kṣiptvā śipā manohvā āpaṃ haritāpaṃ
                            etayoścūrṇaṃ paścātsūtaṃ pūrvoktaṃ pāradaṃ kṣiptvā tato+anantaraṃ
                            śipācūrṇaṃ kṣiptvā tāmeva rasasaṃyuktāṃ mūṣāṃ bhasmagartāyāṃ bhasmanā
                            yuktā yā gartā tasyāṃ dhmātaṃ kuryāt punastāvadbhasmanā ācchādya
                            yāvatsvāṅgaśītapaṃ svayameva śītapaṃ syāt // GRhtCM_5.39-40:2 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, having made a long [crucible] in the shape of a cow's teat, sturdy, flaw-free, diamond-like — the crucible; having thrown into that crucible orpiment powder — <s>śilā</s> being <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar), <s>āla</s> being <s>haritāla</s> (orpiment) — the powder of these two; then having thrown in the previously described mercury; then afterward having thrown in orpiment powder; having placed that very crucible containing mercury in an ash-pit — a pit equipped with ash — one should smelt [it]; then covering it with ash until it becomes self-cooled — until it cools on its own. (GRhtCM 5.39-40:2)

children.text:
tatra tasyāṃ mūṣāyāṃ sakapaṃ samastaṃ nāgaṃ subhakṣitaṃ jīrṇatāṃ gataṃ
                            jñātvā sūtaṃ ākṛṣya uddhārya nirnāgakaraṇavidhānam etat //
                            GRhtCM_5.39-40:3 //
children.translated_text: In that crucible, knowing that all the lead has been well-consumed — has attained the state of being digested — one should extract the mercury; this is the procedure for making [mercury] lead-free. (GRhtCM 5.39-40:3)

children.text: bīja of nāgajīrṇapārada
children.translated_text: [Section:] Seed (<s>bīja</s>) of lead-digested mercury

children.text: jñātvā nāgaṃ truṭitaṃ punarapi dadyādyathā bhavettriguṇam /
children.translated_text: Knowing that the lead has been exhausted, one should add more, so that it becomes three-fold;

children.text: paścācchuddhaṃ kṛtvā bījavaraṃ yojayettadanu // GRht_5.41 //
children.translated_text: thereafter, having purified [the mercury], one should then add the best seed (<s>bījavara</s>). (GRht 5.41)

children.text: nirnāgānantaraṃ yatkartavyaṃ tadāha jñātvetyādi // GRhtCM_5.41:1 //
children.translated_text: He states what should be done after the lead-removal, beginning with 'knowing' and so on. (GRhtCM 5.41:1)

children.text:
nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ truṭitaṃ buddhvā punarapi nāgaṃ dahyāt pūrvoktavidhānena
                            pārade iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_5.41:2 //
children.translated_text: Having ascertained that the lead has been exhausted, one should add more lead again — by the previously stated procedure — into mercury; this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 5.41:2)

children.text: yathā nāgaṃ triguṇitaṃ bhavettathaiva kuryāt // GRhtCM_5.41:3 //
children.translated_text: One should do so until the lead becomes tripled in quantity. (GRhtCM 5.41:3)

children.text:
paścātsūtaṃ śuddhaṃ kṛtvā pāradaṃ nirnāgaṃ vidhāya tadanu
                            nāgajāraṇānantaraṃ bījavaraṃ pūrvoktaṃ yojayet // GRhtCM_5.41:4 //
children.translated_text: Thereafter, having purified the mercury — having made it lead-free — then, after the lead-digestion, one should add the best seed (<s>bījavara</s>), as previously described. (GRhtCM 5.41:4)

children.text: mercury:: jāraṇa of tin
children.translated_text: [Section:] Mercury — <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion) of tin

children.text: athavā tāraṃ vaṅgaṃ sūtaṃ saṃsārya vaṅgaparihīnam /
children.translated_text: Or [one may use] silver (<s>tāra</s>), tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), [and] mercury — having combined [them], making [mercury] tin-free,

children.text: tālakayogena tathā nirvaṅgaṃ yantrayogena // GRht_5.42 //
children.translated_text: by the <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment) method as well, making it tin-free by the apparatus method. (GRht 5.42)

children.text: atha tārayogam āha athavetyādi // GRhtCM_5.42:1 //
children.translated_text: Now he states the silver-method, beginning with 'or' and so on. (GRhtCM 5.42:1)

children.text: athaveti vidhānāntaram // GRhtCM_5.42:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Or' indicates an alternative procedure. (GRhtCM 5.42:2)

children.text:
tāraṃ vaṅgaṃ sūtam iti tāraṃ rūpyaṃ vaṅgaṃ khurakaṃ sūtaṃ saṃskṛtapāradaṃ
                            etattritayaṃ saṃsārya mepanaṃ vidhāya vaṅgaparihīnaṃ kuryāt tathā
                            tenaiva vidhānena tāpasya yo+asau yogastena yantrayogena ca
                            dīrghamūṣāyogena ca nirvaṅgaṃ vaṅgavivarjitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_5.42:3
                            //
children.translated_text: 'Silver (<s>tāra</s>), tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), mercury' — <s>tāra</s> means silver, <s>vaṅga</s> means <s>khuraka</s> (tin), <s>sūta</s> means processed mercury. Having combined this triad — having performed the mixing — one should make it tin-free. Likewise, by that very procedure, by the method of <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment) — through that conjunction; and by the apparatus method — the long-crucible method — one should make it tin-free, devoid of tin. (GRhtCM 5.42:3)

children.text: mercury:: jāraṇa of tin
children.translated_text: [Section:] Mercury — <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion) of tin [continued]

children.text: athavā vastranibaddhaṃ girijatusahitaṃ suveṣṭitaṃ māṣaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Or, tied in cloth, combined with mineral pitch (<s>girijatu</s>), well-wrapped with <s>māṣa</s> (black gram),

children.text: pakvaṃ taile vaṭakaṃ nirvaṅgaṃ jāyate nūnam // GRht_5.43 //
children.translated_text: the pellet, cooked in oil, becomes tin-free, certainly. (GRht 5.43)

children.text: vidhyantaramāha athavetyādi // GRhtCM_5.43:1 //
children.translated_text: He states another method, beginning with 'or' and so on. (GRhtCM 5.43:1)

children.text:
athavā tāraṃ vaṅgaṃ vaṭakākāraṃ taipe tipodbhave pakvaṃ kuryāt nūnaṃ
                            niścitaṃ tadvaṭakaṃ tathā pakvaṃ kuryādyathā nirvaṅgaṃ jāyate
                            vahniyogena iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_5.43:2 //
children.translated_text: Or, the silver, tin, [and mercury] pellet-shaped, should be cooked in sesame oil; certainly — assuredly — that pellet, thus cooked, should be made such that it becomes tin-free — by the conjunction of fire; this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 5.43:2)

children.text: bīja:: for garbhadruti
children.translated_text: [Section:] Seed (<s>bīja</s>) — for <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction)

children.text: piṣṭīstambhaṃ kṛtvā bījavareṇaiva sāritaṃ tadanu /
children.translated_text: Having made a <s>piṣṭī-stambha</s> (foil-fixation), combined with the best seed alone, thereafter —

children.text: bīja:: for garbhadruti
children.translated_text: [Section:] Seed (<s>bīja</s>) — for <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction)

children.text: athavā baddharasena tu sahitaṃ bījaṃ surañjitaṃ kṛtvā // GRht_5.44 //
children.translated_text: Or, with bound mercury, the seed, having been well-colored (<s>surañjita</s>), (GRht 5.44)

children.text: gandhakanihitaṃ sūtaṃ nihitānihitaṃ ca śṛṅkhalāyāṃ tat /
children.translated_text: mercury emplaced in sulfur, placed and unplaced in a chain [apparatus],

children.text: yojitanirvyūḍharase garbhadrutikārakaṃ nūnam // GRht_5.45 //
children.translated_text: in [mercury] that has been joined and extracted — that certainly causes <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction). (GRht 5.45)

children.text: sūtakabhasmavareṇa tu bījaṃ kṛtvā rasendrake garbhe /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, with the best mercury-ash (<s>sūtakabhasma</s>), having made the seed in the interior (<s>garbha</s>) of mercury,

children.text: mṛditā piṣṭī vidhinā hyabhiṣavayogāddravati garbhe ca // GRht_5.46 //
children.translated_text: the pellet, crushed by the procedure, through the pressing conjunction (<s>abhiṣavayoga</s>), liquefies within the interior. (GRht 5.46)

children.text: vidhānāntaramāha piṣṭītyādi // GRhtCM_5.44-46:1 //
children.translated_text: He states another method, beginning with '<s>piṣṭī</s>' and so on. (GRhtCM 5.44-46:1)

children.text:
bījavareṇaiva pūrvakanakabījenaiva sāritaṃ mipitaṃ sat piṣṭīstambhaṃ
                            khoṭastambhaṃ kṛtvā tadanu tatpaścāt athaveti prakārāntaraṃ darśayati tu
                            punaḥ baddharasena khoṭabaddharasena sahitaṃ surañjitaṃ śobhanavidhānena
                            varṇavṛddhīkṛtaṃ bījaṃ svarṇabījaṃ saṃyutaṃ kuryāt yoga eva kārya iti
                            dvividhānam uktam // GRhtCM_5.44-46:2 //
children.translated_text: Combined with the best seed alone — with the previously mentioned gold-seed — having made a <s>piṣṭī-stambha</s> (foil-fixation), a <s>khoṭa</s>-fixation. Then after that, 'or' indicates another method. Furthermore, with bound mercury — mercury bound in <s>khoṭa</s> form — combined, well-colored — made to increase in color through an excellent procedure — the seed, the gold-seed, should be conjoined. The preparation alone should be performed — thus two methods are stated. (GRhtCM 5.44-46:2)

children.text: anyaccāha gandhaketyādi // GRhtCM_5.44-46:3 //
children.translated_text: He states another [method], beginning with 'sulfur' and so on. (GRhtCM 5.44-46:3)

children.text:
gandhakanihitaṃ gandhake nihitaṃ sthāpitaṃ sūtaṃ ūrdhvādho gandhakaṃ
                            dattvā sūtaṃ madhyasthaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.44-46:4 //
children.translated_text: 'Emplaced in sulfur' — mercury placed, established, in sulfur — meaning sulfur placed above and below, with mercury positioned in the middle; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 5.44-46:4)

children.text:
ca punarevaṃvidhaṃ sūtaṃ śṛṅkhapāyāṃ śṛṅkhapīkaraṇayoge nihitānihitaṃ
                            yannihitaṃ tadanihitam ajāritaṃ kāryaṃ nihitānihitasaṃyogāt śṛṅkhapeyaṃ
                            nūnaṃ niścitaṃ yojitanirvyūḍharase pūrvaṃ yojitaṃ paścānnirvāhitaṃ
                            nirvyūḍhaṃ yatra tattasminnevaṃvidharase garbhadrutiḥ pāradasyodare
                            bījāni dravanti // GRhtCM_5.44-46:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, such mercury, in the chain apparatus (<s>śṛṅkhalā</s>), through the conjunction of chaining — 'placed and unplaced' means that which was placed is made 'unplaced,' meaning undigested — it should be made [thus]; through the conjunction of placed-and-unplaced, the chaining [is accomplished]. Certainly — assuredly — in [mercury] that has been joined and then extracted — first joined, then separated, extracted — in such mercury, <s>garbhadruti</s> [occurs] — the seeds liquefy within the belly of mercury. (GRhtCM 5.44-46:5)

children.text: piṣṭīvidhinā jāraṇamāha sūtaketyādi // GRhtCM_5.44-46:6 //
children.translated_text: He states the <s>jāraṇa</s> by the <s>piṣṭī</s>-method, beginning with '<s>sūtaka</s>' and so on. (GRhtCM 5.44-46:6)

children.text:
tu punaḥ rasendrake garbhe rasendrakṛto yo+asau garbhastasmin bījaṃ kṛtvā
                            vidhinā piṣṭīrvidheyā sā piṣṭī mṛditā kāryā kasmāt abhiṣavayogāt
                            saṃmardanayogāt kena saha sūtakabhasmavareṇa saha sūtakasya
                            yadbhasmavaraṃ tena sā piṣṭī garbhe dravati caśabdājjarati ca //
                            GRhtCM_5.44-46:7 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, in the interior (<s>garbha</s>) of mercury — that which is the interior made by mercury, in that — having made the seed, pellets should be prepared by the procedure; those pellets should be crushed. Why? Through the pressing conjunction (<s>abhiṣavayoga</s>) — through the conjunction of pressing. With what? With the best mercury-ash — with that ash of mercury that is excellent — that pellet liquefies within the interior, and from [the word] 'ca,' it is also digested. (GRhtCM 5.44-46:7)

children.text: bīja:: for garbhadruti
children.translated_text: [Section:] Seed (<s>bīja</s>) — for <s>garbhadruti</s> (internal liquefaction)

children.text: patrābhrakaṃ ca satvaṃ kāṃkṣī vā kāntamākṣikaṃ puṭitam /
children.translated_text: Sheet-mica (<s>patrābhraka</s>), or its essence (<s>sattva</s>), or <s>kāṅkṣī</s> (alum), or lodestone-<s>mākṣika</s> (lodestone with pyrite), calcined

children.text: nirguṇḍī gṛhakanyā cāṅgerī palāśaśākaiśca // GRht_5.47 //
children.translated_text: with <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (five-leaved chaste tree), <s>gṛhakanyā</s> (aloe), <s>cāṅgerī</s> (sorrel), and the shoots of <s>palāśa</s> (Butea frondosa) — (GRht 5.47)

children.text: tāvatpuṭitaṃ kṛtvā yāvatsindūrasaprabhaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: calcined until it becomes of the color of <s>sindūra</s> (vermilion),

children.text: tatpādaśeṣalavaṇaṃ haṇḍikapākena pācitaṃ sudṛḍham // GRht_5.48 //
children.translated_text: that, reduced to one-quarter, with salt, cooked firmly in a pot (<s>haṇḍikā</s>), (GRht 5.48)

children.text: ekaikaṃ śatavyūḍhaṃ bījavaraṃ jārayedrasendrasya /
children.translated_text: each [seed], extracted a hundred times, should be made to digest the best seed in the interior of the lord of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>);

children.text:
garbhe dravati ca kṣipraṃ hyabhiṣavayogena mṛditamaṅgulyā //
                                GRht_5.49 //
children.translated_text: it liquefies within the interior quickly, through pressing conjunction (<s>abhiṣavayoga</s>), crushed with the finger. (GRht 5.49)

children.text: bījavaravidhānamāha patrābhrakam ityādi // GRhtCM_5.47-49:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the procedure for the best seed (<s>bījavara</s>), beginning with 'sheet-mica' and so on. (GRhtCM 5.47-49:1)

children.text:
patrābhrakamiti abhrakasya patrāṇi vābhrakasya satvaṃ punaḥ kāṃkṣī
                            saurāṣṭrī kāntamākṣikaṃ kāntaścumbakaḥ mākṣikaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ eteṣāṃ
                            dvandva ekatvaṃ punaretat nirguṇḍīgṛhakanyācāṅgerīpapāśaśākaiḥ puṭitaṃ
                            nirguṇḍī sephāpikā gṛhakanyā kumārī cāṅgerī ampaśākaḥ papāśo
                            brahmavṛkṣaḥ śāko vṛkṣaviśeṣaḥ eteṣāṃ dvandvasamāsaḥ eteṣāṃ rasaṃ
                            gṛhītvā pūrvauṣadhapuṭitaṃ kuryāt gharme iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_5.47-49:2
                            //
children.translated_text: 'Sheet-mica' means the sheets of mica, or the essence of mica. Furthermore, <s>kāṅkṣī</s> is <s>saurāṣṭrī</s> (alum); <s>kāntamākṣika</s> — <s>kānta</s> is lodestone, <s>mākṣika</s> is gold-pyrite — a compound of these pairs. Furthermore, this [should be] calcined with <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (five-leaved chaste tree, called <s>selālikā</s> in the vernacular), <s>gṛhakanyā</s> (<s>kumārī</s>, aloe), <s>cāṅgerī</s> (sour spinach), <s>palāśa</s> (<s>brahmavṛkṣa</s>, a tree), <s>śāka</s> (a specific tree) — a compound of these — having taken the juice of these, one should calcine with the said herbs, in sunlight; this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 5.47-49:2)

children.text:
tadauṣadhaṃ puṭitaṃ kṛtvā punastatpuṭitamauṣadhaṃ tatpādaśeṣaṃ
                            caturthāṃśaṃ pavaṇaṃ saindhavaṃ dattvā haṇḍikāpākena haṇḍikāyāṃ
                            mṛdbhājane yaḥ pākastena pācitaṃ vahnau puṭitaṃ tāvatkuryād yāvat
                            sindūrasaṃprabhaṃ sindūratupyavarṇaṃ bhavati // GRhtCM_5.47-49:3 //

kathaṃ pācitaṃ kuryāt sudṛḍhaṃ yathā syāttathā ekaikaṃ śatavyūḍhamiti //
                            GRhtCM_5.47-49:4 //

pūrvoktānāṃ sindūrīkṛtānām uparasānām adharāt ekaikaṃ ekaṃ ekaṃ
                            pṛthaktvena śatavyūḍhaṃ śatavāraṃ vāhitaṃ bījavaraṃ jāyate kanake iti
                            śeṣaḥ tadbījaṃ rasendrasya garbhe dravati caśabdāt kṣipraṃ śīghraṃ
                            jarati ca // GRhtCM_5.47-49:5 //

kathaṃ aṅgupyā anāmikayā yo 'bhiṣavayogaḥ saṃmardanayogasteneti viśeṣakam
                            // GRhtCM_5.47-49:6 //
gold:: bīja with lead
āvṛtte'pyāvartyaṃ hemavare kṣepyamujjvale nāgam /
triguṇaśilāprativāpaṃ hyahibījaṃ tatsamuddiṣṭam // GRht_5.50 //

nāgena bījakaraṇamāha ujjvapahemavare svarṇaśreṣṭhe āvartye samyagdrute
                            nāgaṃ śuddhasīsakaṃ āvartyaṃ pradrāvyaṃ kiṃ kṛtvā samaṃ
                            svarṇasamabhāgakṣepaṃ kṣiptvā punarnāgopari triguṇaśipāprativāpaṃ
                            triguṇā yā śipā tasyā nirvāpaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_5.50:1 //
śipā manaḥśipā // GRhtCM_5.50:2 //

tatsiddhaṃ ahibījaṃ nāgayogena bījaṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ rasavidbhiḥ iti śeṣaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_5.50:3 //
gold, silver:: bīja with tin
vaṅgaṃ tu tena vidhinā hemavare kṣepya tālavāpena /
tāre vā nirvyūḍhaṃ bījavaraṃ truṭitasaṃyogāt // GRht_5.51 //
atha vaṅgayogena bījamāha vaṅgamityādi // GRhtCM_5.51:1 //

tena pūrvoktena vidhinā vidhānena tu punaḥ hemavare pūrvavarṇite vaṅgaṃ
                            kṣepya tāpavāpena haritāpanikṣepeṇa nirvyūḍhaṃ kuryāt vā tāre āvartye
                            vaṅgaṃ nikṣipya nirvyūḍhaṃ nirvāhitaṃ sadbījavaraṃ bhavet //
                            GRhtCM_5.51:2 //

kasmāt truṭitasaṃyogāt truṭitaṃ bhavati tathā bījavaramiti vaṅgabījaṃ tat
                            pūrvavat dravati jarati ca // GRhtCM_5.51:3 //
rasāṅkuśa
yo niḥsṛto bhujaṅgād rasakeśarīvajrapañjaraḥ sa punaḥ /
phaṇihemaguṇātkuṭilo rasāṅkuśo nāma vikhyātaḥ // GRht_5.52 //
suvarṇābhidhānabījapraśaṃsanamāha ya ityādi // GRhtCM_5.52:1 //

bhujaṅgāt sīsakāt niḥsṛtaḥ bhujaṅgaśipāvāpena kṣayaṃ nītvā yaḥ
                            pṛthagbhūtaḥ sa rasakesarīvajrapañjaraḥ kathitaḥ rasa eva kesarī siṃhaḥ
                            tadarthaṃ vajrapañjaraḥ vajreṇa vyadhitaḥ pañjaro+atidṛḍhatvāt
                            siṃharakṣaṇasamartha ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.52:2 //

punarviśeṣeṇocyate ayaṃ vajrapañjaro na kiṃtu ayaṃ rasāṅkuśaḥ raso
                            gajarūpaḥ tasyāṅkuśaḥ vaśīkaraṇasamarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.52:3 //
nāma saṃbhāvanāyām // GRhtCM_5.52:4 //
vikhyātaḥ prakathitaḥ // GRhtCM_5.52:5 //

kasmāt kuṭipāt kimapi vastuharaṇāt kuṭipo vakro bhavati duṣṭasvabhāva eva
                            anena hemnā nāgaharaṇaṃ kṛtam // GRhtCM_5.52:6 //

kathaṃbhūtāt kuṭipāt phaṇī bhujaṅgaḥ hema svarṇaṃ tayorguṇā vidyante
                            yasmin evaṃvidhāt kuṭipādeśo yuktaḥ aṅkuśo+api vakro bhavatīti //
                            GRhtCM_5.52:7 //

atra bhrāntimānapaṅkāraḥ hemabīje vajrapañjaragajāṅkuśadarśanād
                            bhrāntirjāteti // GRhtCM_5.52:8 //
jāraṇa without preceding garbhadruti; bāhyadruti??
evaṃ pakvaṃ vidhinā bījavaraṃ sūtarāṭ tathāmlena /
kartavyaḥ saṃsvedyo yāvatpiṣṭī bhavecchlakṣṇā // GRht_5.53 //
tailena tena vidhinā svinnā piṣṭī bhavedakhilam /
athavā ślakṣṇaṃ śilayā nighṛṣṭabījaṃ bhavetpiṇḍī // GRht_5.54 //
pāko vaṭakavidhinā kartavyastailayogena /
krāmaṇapiṇḍe kṣiptvā māṣaiśca syāt sudṛḍhapiṇḍatvam // GRht_5.55 //
mṛdvagninā supakvaṃ dagdhaṃ yāvanna bhavetpiṇḍam /
ākṛṣya cātha sūtaṃ piṇḍe śeṣaṃ tathā punaḥ pācyam // GRht_5.56 //
athavāpyauṣadhapiṇḍe dolātapte kharpare vidhinā /
punarapi piṇḍe kṣepyaṃ garbhe yāvaddrutirbhavati // GRht_5.57 //
evaṃ drutaṃ hi garbhe bījavaraṃ jarati rasarāje /
garbhadrutyā rahitaṃ biḍayogairjarati garbhe ca // GRht_5.58 //
bījasyāsya piṣṭīkaraṇamāha evamityādi // GRhtCM_5.53-58:1 //

evaṃ amunā prakāreṇa vidhinārthād upadeśena pakvaṃ yadbījavaraṃ tathā
                            pūrvasaṃskṛtaḥ sūtarāṭ pāradaḥ ampena jambīrādinā saṃsvedyaḥ svedākhyo
                            vidhiḥ kartavyaḥ // GRhtCM_5.53-58:2 //

atra kimavadhistatkartavyo yāvat śpakṣṇā spaṣṭā piṣṭī ekaśarīratā bhavet
                            rasabījayoriti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_5.53-58:3 //
vidhyantaramāha taipenetyādinā // GRhtCM_5.53-58:4 //

tena pūrvoktena vidhinā vadhavidhānena tipataipena svinnā sveditā satī
                            piṣṭirbhavati vahnāviti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_5.53-58:5 //
athaveti vidhānāntaraṃ darśayati // GRhtCM_5.53-58:6 //

śipayā dṛṣanmayayā nighṛṣṭabījaṃ nighṛṣṭaṃ gharṣitaṃ yadbījaṃ nāgākhyaṃ
                            tat sūteneti śeṣaḥ akhipaṃ samastaṃ yathā syāttathā piṣṭirbhavatīti //
                            GRhtCM_5.53-58:7 //
yathā vaṭakaḥ pācyastathāha pāka ityādi // GRhtCM_5.53-58:8 //

vaṭakavidhinā māṣavaṭakavidhinā taipayogena pākaḥ kartavyaḥ vahnau
                            pācanaṃ vidheyamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.53-58:9 //

kiṃ kṛtvā krāmaṇapiṇḍe kṣiptvā biḍapiṇḍamadhye sthāpya ca punarmāṣair
                            annaviśeṣair dṛḍhapiṇḍatvaṃ syāt māṣacūrṇaveṣṭitaṃ krāmaṇapiṇḍaṃ dṛḍhaṃ
                            bhavediti vyaktiḥ // GRhtCM_5.53-58:10 //
tadvidhānamāha mṛdvityādi // GRhtCM_5.53-58:11 //

māṣacūrṇitajātaṃ krāmaṇapiṇḍaṃ tāvat supakvaṃ kartavyaṃ yāvaddagdhaṃ na
                            bhavet // GRhtCM_5.53-58:12 //

kena supakvaṃ mṛdvagninā komapavahninā puṭaḥ tatpiṇḍataḥ śeṣaṃ śiṣṭaṃ taṃ
                            nirmapapāradaṃ ākṛṣya gṛhītvā piṇḍamanyasmin piṇḍe tathā pūrvaprakāreṇa
                            pācyamiti // GRhtCM_5.53-58:13 //
aparaṃ cāha athavetyādi // GRhtCM_5.53-58:14 //
athaveti prakārāntare // GRhtCM_5.53-58:15 //

punarapi piṣṭīrdopātapte auṣadhapiṇḍe dopayottapte uṣṇatāṃ nīte
                            krāmaṇauṣadhānāṃ piṇḍe kṣepya madhye sthāpya kasyopari kharpare
                            mṛnmayapātropari // GRhtCM_5.53-58:16 //
kena vidhinā pūrvoktena taipena vā ampeneti // GRhtCM_5.53-58:17 //

kiyatkāpaṃ yāvadgarbhe rasodare piṣṭī dravati tāvadbiḍāntare piṇḍāntare
                            kṣepyeti tātparyārthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.53-58:18 //
aparaṃ cāha evamityādi // GRhtCM_5.53-58:19 //

evaṃ amunā prakāreṇa garbhe rasodare jarati niḥśeṣatvaṃ rasodare prāpnoti
                            ca punargarbhadrutyā rahitaṃ draveṇa varjitaṃ bījavaraṃ biḍairjarati
                            drutabījamāraṇasamartho biḍa ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_5.53-58:20 //
drutagrāsaparimāṇo biḍayantrādiyogataḥ /
jāraṇetyucyate tasyāḥ prakārāḥ santi koṭiśaḥ /
prakārā yantrāṇāṃ iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_5.53-58:21 //
jāraṇabhedāstu /
grāsasya cāraṇaṃ garbhadrāvaṇaṃ jāraṇaṃ tathā /
iti trirūpā nirdiṣṭā jāraṇā varavārtikaiḥ /
jāraṇa:: method
grāsamiti cārayitvā garbhadrutiṃ tato bhūrje /
lavaṇakṣārāmlasudhāsurabhīmūtreṇa kṛtalepe // GRht_6.1 //
dṛḍhavastrabāhyabaddhe dolāsvedena jārayedgrāsam /
sauvīreṇārdhapūrṇe kumbhe sakṣāramūtrakairathavā // GRht_6.2 //
amunā krameṇa divasaistribhistribhirjārayedgrāsam /
garbhadrutijāraṇamāha grāsamityādi // GRhtCM_6.1-2:1 //

pūrvoktaprakāreṇa grāsaṃ kavalaṃ yathāsaṃkhyaṃ cārayitvā
                                punargarbhadrutiṃ kṛtvā tatastadanantaraṃ tadgarbhadrutaṃ sūtaṃ
                                bhūrje bhūrjavṛkṣatvakpuṭake sthāpayedityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_6.1-2:2 //

kiṃviśiṣṭe bhūrje lavaṇakṣārāmlasudhāsurabhimūtreṇa kṛtalepe lavaṇāni
                                saindhavādīni kṣārāḥ svarjikādayaḥ amlo jambīrādiḥ sudhā śukticūrṇaṃ
                                surabhī dhenustanmūtraṃ etena yogena kṛtvā kṛto lepo yasmin //
                                GRhtCM_6.1-2:3 //
udaradrutiyuktaḥ sūtaḥ sthāpya ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_6.1-2:4 //
jāraṇavidhānamāha dṛḍhetyādi // GRhtCM_6.1-2:5 //
children.translated_text: He states the method of assimilation (<s>jāraṇa</s>) with 'dṛḍha' and so forth. (GRhtCM 6.1-2:5)

children.text:
dṛḍhavastrabāhyabaddhe iti dṛḍhaṃ nūtanaṃ ghanaṃ ca yadvastraṃ tena
                                bāhye sarvato baddhe saṃyate pūrvoktena dolāsvedena
                                dolāyantravidhinā yaḥ svedastaṃ kṛtvā grāsaṃ rasāntardrutaṃ kavalaṃ
                                jārayet // GRhtCM_6.1-2:6 //
children.translated_text: 'Bound externally in firm cloth' — 'firm' means new and dense cloth; bound on the outside, wrapped all around with that; by the previously described <s>dolāsveda</s> (swing-steaming) — by the method of the <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing-apparatus) — having performed that steaming, one should assimilate the morsel — the internally dissolved bolus — into mercury. (GRhtCM 6.1-2:6)

children.text:
kutra kumbhe kalaśe kiṃviśiṣṭe sauvīreṇārdhapūrṇe sauvīreṇa
                                svedanasaṃskāroditakāñjikena kṛtvā ardhapūrṇe // GRhtCM_6.1-2:7 //
children.translated_text: Where? In a <s>kumbha</s> (pot), a vessel. Of what specification? Half-filled with <s>sauvīra</s> — with <s>sauvīra</s>, the <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel) mentioned in the steaming process — having made [it] half-filled. (GRhtCM 6.1-2:7)

children.text: athaveti vidhyantare // GRhtCM_6.1-2:8 //
children.translated_text: 'Athavā' (alternatively) indicates an alternative procedure. (GRhtCM 6.1-2:8)

children.text:
sakṣāramūtrakaiḥ saha kṣāraḥ svarjikādibhiḥ vartante yāni mūtrāṇi
                                go+ajāvinārīṇāmiti śeṣaḥ etaiḥ ardhabhṛte kumbhe jārayedityarthaḥ //
                                GRhtCM_6.1-2:9 //
children.translated_text: With alkali and urines — alkali [means] <s>svarjikā</s> (sodium carbonate) and the like; the urines are those of cow, goat, sheep, and woman — this is the complement; with these, in a half-filled pot, one should assimilate — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 6.1-2:9)

children.text: atha rasajāraṇe kālasaṃkhyāmāha amunetyādi // GRhtCM_6.1-2:10 //
children.translated_text: Now he states the time-count for mercury assimilation with 'amunā' and so forth. (GRhtCM 6.1-2:10)

children.text:
amunā krameṇeti uktaprakāreṇa tribhistribhirdivasaiḥ tribhiḥ
                                saṃkhyākairdivasaiḥ grāse jāte anyagrāsaḥ kriyate garbhadrutagrāsaḥ
                                kriyate garbhadrutagrāsaḥ tridivasairjaratīti bhāvaḥ //
                                GRhtCM_6.1-2:11 //
children.translated_text: 'By this method' — by the stated procedure — in groups of three days each; when one morsel has been [assimilated], another morsel is prepared — an internally dissolved morsel is prepared; [each] internally dissolved morsel is assimilated in three days — this is the purport. (GRhtCM 6.1-2:11)

children.text: jīrṇasya lakṣaṇamatho jñeyaṃ yantrātsamuddhṛtya // GRht_6.3 //
children.translated_text: The criterion of the assimilated [morsel] should then be known, having extracted [mercury] from the apparatus. (GRht 6.3)

children.text: Untersuchung, ob jāraṇa stattgefunden hat
children.translated_text: [Section:] Test for whether <s>jāraṇa</s> (assimilation) has taken place

children.text: uddhṛtamātraṃ pātre prakṣālya kāṃjikenātaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having extracted [mercury], it should be washed in a vessel with <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel); thereafter,

children.text: samalaṃ ca kāṃjikamato haraṇārthaṃ vastrayogena // GRht_6.4 //
children.translated_text: the impure <s>kāñjika</s> should be removed by means of cloth. (GRht 6.4)

children.text: tadanu sukhoṣṇe pātre saṃmardyo+asau yathā na hīye /
children.translated_text: Thereafter, in a pleasantly warm vessel, it should be rubbed such that [mercury] is not diminished;

children.text: tāvadyāvacchuṣyati tallagnaṃ kāñjikaṃ sakalam // GRht_6.5 //
children.translated_text: until all the <s>kāñjika</s> adhering to it dries up completely. (GRht 6.5)

children.text: itthaṃ ca śoṣitajalaḥ karamardanataḥ sunirmalībhūtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, with the water dried off, [mercury] made thoroughly clean through hand-rubbing,

children.text: pīḍyaḥ pātrasyopari vastreṇa caturguṇenaiva // GRht_6.6 //
children.translated_text: should be pressed upon a vessel through cloth folded fourfold. (GRht 6.6)

children.text: yadi parigalitaḥ sakalo vastrād grāsena caikatāṃ yātaḥ /
children.translated_text: If all [mercury] has passed through the cloth, and has become one with the morsel,

children.text: na bhavati yadi daṇḍadharo jīrṇagrāsastadā jñeyaḥ // GRht_6.7 //
children.translated_text: and if it does not hold a rod-shape, then it should be known as having an assimilated morsel. (GRht 6.7)

children.text:
atheti tridinasvedānantaraṃ jīrṇasya rasasya pakṣaṇaṃ jñeyaṃ grāso jīrṇo
                            na veti jñātavyaḥ // GRhtCM_6.3-7:1 //
children.translated_text: 'Atha' [indicates] after three days of steaming — the criterion of the assimilated mercury should be known — whether or not the morsel has been assimilated should be ascertained. (GRhtCM 6.3-7:1)

children.text:
kiṃ kṛtvā yantrāddopikābhidhānād uddhṛtya yantrād bahir gṛhītveti //
                            GRhtCM_6.3-7:2 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? Having extracted from the apparatus called <s>dolikā</s> — having taken [the mercury] out of the apparatus. (GRhtCM 6.3-7:2)

children.text: rasamapāpanayanamāha uddhṛtetyādi // GRhtCM_6.3-7:3 //
children.translated_text: He describes the removal of impurity from mercury with 'uddhṛta' and so forth. (GRhtCM 6.3-7:3)

children.text:
uddhṛtamātramiti yantrād bahir gṛhītamātraṃ tatpātre bhājane mṛnmaye
                            kāñjikena prakṣāpya // GRhtCM_6.3-7:4 //
children.translated_text: 'Having just extracted' — having just taken out of the apparatus — that [mercury] should be washed in a vessel, an earthen container, with <s>kāñjika</s>. (GRhtCM 6.3-7:4)

children.text:
punar ato rasātsamapaṃ mapasaṃyutaṃ kāñjikaṃ haraṇīyaṃ bahiḥ kāryam //
                            GRhtCM_6.3-7:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the impure <s>kāñjika</s> — the <s>kāñjika</s> combined with the impurity from mercury — should be removed, taken out. (GRhtCM 6.3-7:5)

children.text:
kena kṛtvā vastrayogena vastre kṣiptaṃ sat tadeva tiṣṭhati na kāñjikam //
                            GRhtCM_6.3-7:6 //
children.translated_text: By what means? By means of cloth — when cast upon cloth, [the mercury] itself remains while the <s>kāñjika</s> does not. (GRhtCM 6.3-7:6)

children.text: tasyaiva vidhānaṃ cāha tadanvityādi // GRhtCM_6.3-7:7 //
children.translated_text: He states the further procedure for that with 'tadanu' and so forth. (GRhtCM 6.3-7:7)

children.text:
tadanu vastrayogānantaraṃ sukhoṣṇe pātre asau rasaḥ saṃmardyaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_6.3-7:8 //
children.translated_text: 'Tadanu' — after the cloth-procedure — in a pleasantly warm vessel, that mercury should be rubbed. (GRhtCM 6.3-7:8)

children.text:
kathaṃ yathā na hīyate nāśaṃ nāpnuyāt atyauṣṇyāt vā
                            kāṃsyatāmranāgavaṅgakanakatārapātrāt vā dṛḍhakaraghātād raso hīna eva
                            syāt ato+asau pāradas tāvan saṃmardyo yāvappagnakāñjikaṃ
                            rasasaṃsargasauvīraṃ śuṣyati niḥśeṣatāṃ yātītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_6.3-7:9
                            //
children.translated_text: How? Such that it is not diminished — does not undergo loss — either from excessive heat, or from a vessel of bronze, copper, lead, tin, gold, or silver, or from forceful hand-striking, the mercury would indeed be diminished; therefore, that mercury should be rubbed until all the <s>kāñjika</s> — the <s>sauvīra</s> that was in contact with the mercury — dries up, is completely exhausted — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 6.3-7:9)

children.text: tasyaiva vidhānaṃ cāha itthamityādi // GRhtCM_6.3-7:10 //
children.translated_text: He states the further procedure for that with 'ittham' and so forth. (GRhtCM 6.3-7:10)

children.text:
itthaṃ amunā prakāreṇa karamardanataḥ hastatapamardanataḥ sunirmapībhūto
                            maparahitaḥ śoṣitajapo rasaścaturguṇena vastreṇa kṛtvā pānasyopari
                            pīḍyaḥ // GRhtCM_6.3-7:11 //
children.translated_text: Thus — by this method — through hand-rubbing, through rubbing with heated hands — made thoroughly clean, free of impurity, with water dried off — such mercury should be pressed upon a vessel through cloth folded fourfold. (GRhtCM 6.3-7:11)

children.text: jīrṇagrāsapakṣaṇam āha yadītyādi // GRhtCM_6.3-7:12 //
children.translated_text: He states the criterion for an assimilated morsel with 'yadi' (if) and so forth. (GRhtCM 6.3-7:12)

children.text:
tadā pārado jīrṇagrāso jñeyaḥ jīrṇo niḥśeṣatvamāpanno grāso yasmin sa
                            tathoktaḥ // GRhtCM_6.3-7:13 //
children.translated_text: Then the mercury should be known as having an assimilated morsel — the morsel in which [the substance] has reached complete exhaustion — it is so described. (GRhtCM 6.3-7:13)

children.text:
yadi sakapaḥ sarvaḥ vastrātparigapitaḥ caturguṇavastrāt cyuto bhavati
                            pātre iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_6.3-7:14 //
children.translated_text: If all of it — the entirety — has passed through the cloth, fallen through the fourfold cloth into the vessel — this is the complement. (GRhtCM 6.3-7:14)

children.text:
punaryadi grāsena saha ekatāṃ yātaḥ san mipitaḥ san raso daṇḍadharo na
                            bhavati sthirarūpo na syāt tadā jīrṇagrāso jñātavya ityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_6.3-7:15 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, if having become one with the morsel — being united — the mercury does not hold a rod-shape — does not assume a stable form — then it should be known as having an assimilated morsel — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 6.3-7:15)

children.text: grāsājīrṇa:: treatment
children.translated_text: [Section:] Treatment of undigested morsel (<s>grāsājīrṇa</s>)

children.text: grāsādajīrṇapiṣṭīṃ sūtāduddhṛtya pātayedyantre /
children.translated_text: The undigested pellet from the morsel, having been extracted from mercury, should be sublimated in the apparatus;

children.text: svastho bhavati rasendro grāsaḥ pakvaḥ punarjarati // GRht_6.8 //
children.translated_text: the lord of mercury becomes healthy, and the morsel, once cooked, is assimilated again. (GRht 6.8)

children.text: rasājīrṇapakṣaṇamāha grāsādityādi // GRhtCM_6.8:1 //
children.translated_text: He describes the criterion for unassimilated mercury with 'grāsāt' and so forth. (GRhtCM 6.8:1)

children.text:
grāsāt kavapasaṃyogāt ajīrṇapiṣṭīṃ ajīrṇā aparipakvā yā piṣṭī
                            pūrvoktapakṣaṇā tāṃ sūtāt rasāt yantre pātanakarmocite pātayet //
                            GRhtCM_6.8:2 //
children.translated_text: From the morsel — from conjunction with the bolus — the undigested pellet — the pellet that is undigested, unripened, as identified by the previously stated criterion — that should be sublimated from the mercury in an apparatus suited for sublimation. (GRhtCM 6.8:2)

children.text:
evaṃ grāsātpṛthakkṛtya patitaḥ svastho nirmapo bhavati // GRhtCM_6.8:3
                            //
children.translated_text: Thus, having separated [it] from the morsel, the sublimated [mercury] becomes healthy — free from impurity. (GRhtCM 6.8:3)

children.text:
punargrāsaḥ pakvo vahnitape dattvā pakvaḥ kṛtastaṃ rasendro jaratīti //
                            GRhtCM_6.8:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the morsel, cooked — placed in the heat of fire and [thus] cooked — that the lord of mercury assimilates. (GRhtCM 6.8:4)

children.text: dolāyāṃ catvāro grāsā jāryā yathākrameṇaiva /
children.translated_text: In the <s>dolā</s> (swing-apparatus), four morsels should be assimilated in proper sequence;

children.text: śeṣāḥ kacchapayantre yāvad dviguṇādikaṃ jarati // GRht_6.9 //
children.translated_text: the remaining ones [should be assimilated] in the <s>kacchapayantra</s> (tortoise-apparatus), until [mercury] assimilates double [its weight] and more. (GRht 6.9)

children.text: grāsajāraṇāyāṃ yantrādikaraṇamāha dopāyāmityādi // GRhtCM_6.9:1 //
children.translated_text: He describes the apparatus and other [details] for morsel-assimilation with '<s>dolāyām</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 6.9:1)

children.text:
yathākrameṇaiva catuḥṣaṣṭyādinaiva catvāro grāsā dopāyāṃ jāryāḥ śeṣā
                            grāsāścatvāraḥ asaṃkhyā vā kacchapayantre japayantre ca jāryāḥ //
                            GRhtCM_6.9:2 //
children.translated_text: In proper sequence — in groups of sixty-four [portions] and so on — four morsels should be assimilated in the <s>dolā</s> (swing-apparatus); the remaining morsels — four, or an indefinite number — should be assimilated in the <s>kacchapayantra</s> (tortoise-apparatus) and <s>jalayantra</s> (water-apparatus). (GRhtCM 6.9:2)

children.text:
śeṣāścatvāraḥ kutaḥ yato 'nyaśāstreṣu aṣṭaiva grāsāḥ // GRhtCM_6.9:3
                            //
children.translated_text: The remaining four — from where? Because in other treatises, eight morsels are [prescribed]. (GRhtCM 6.9:3)

What is the limit in assimilation? Until [mercury] assimilates double and more — double the weight of mercury; by the word 'ādi' (and more), [the meaning is] not less than double, but more and more is desirable. (GRhtCM 6.9:4)

children.text:
śaktyavatare'ṣṭau bṛhacchāstre kvacid aṣṭau grāsā uktāḥ
                            kvacidviṃśatigrāsā iti // GRhtCM_6.9:5 //
children.translated_text: In some authoritative texts, eight morsels are prescribed; in some, twenty morsels. (GRhtCM 6.9:5)

children.text:
Īussere Merkmale des Hg nach jāraṇa einer best. Menge
                    abhra
children.translated_text: [Section:] External characteristics of mercury after <s>jāraṇa</s> of a certain amount of mica

children.text: nādau kartuṃ śakyo+atra grāsapramāṇaniyamastu /
children.translated_text: At the beginning, a fixed measure of morsel cannot be established here;

children.text: grasate na hi sarvāṅgaṃ gaganamato lakṣaṇairjñeyam // GRht_6.10 //
children.translated_text: [mercury] does not consume mica entirely; therefore, [the degree of assimilation] should be known by [external] signs. (GRht 6.10)

children.text: yadi hi catuḥṣaṣṭyaṃśān grasati rasastadā dhareddaṇḍam /
children.translated_text: If mercury consumes one sixty-fourth part, then it holds a rod-shape;

children.text: catvāriṃśadbhāgapraveśataḥ pāyasākāraḥ // GRht_6.11 //
children.translated_text: from the entry of one-fortieth part, [it takes on] the appearance of <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-pudding). (GRht 6.11)

children.text: bhavati jalaukākāras triṃśadbhāgād avipluṣaśca viṃśatyā /
children.translated_text: It becomes leech-shaped from [assimilation of] one-thirtieth part; and from one-twentieth, [it becomes] free from droplets;

children.text: chedīva ṣoḍaśāṃśādata ūrdhvaṃ durjaro grāsaḥ // GRht_6.12 //
children.translated_text: from one-sixteenth part, [it becomes] cuttable; beyond that, the morsel becomes difficult to assimilate. (GRht 6.12)

children.text: grāse'nirdiṣṭasaṃkhyatvaṃ darśayannāha netyādi // GRhtCM_6.10-12:1 //
children.translated_text: Showing that there is no fixed number for the morsel, [the commentator] says 'na' and so forth. (GRhtCM 6.10-12:1)

children.text:
atrāsmin śāstre ādau prathamaṃ grāsapramāṇaniyamaḥ kartuṃ na śakyaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_6.10-12:2 //
children.translated_text: In this treatise, at the beginning, a fixed measure of morsel cannot be established. (GRhtCM 6.10-12:2)

children.text:
yataḥ kāraṇāt gaganamabhraṃ sarvāṅgaṃ na grasate rasa iti śeṣaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_6.10-12:3 //
children.translated_text: Because mercury does not consume mica entirely — 'mercury' is the complement. (GRhtCM 6.10-12:3)

children.text:
tatsarvāṅgagrastaṃ gaganamabhraṃ pakṣaṇaireva jñātavyamityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_6.10-12:4 //
children.translated_text: That mica, consumed entirely — [the degree to which] mica [has been consumed] should be known by [external] signs alone — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 6.10-12:4)

children.text: catuḥṣaṣṭyaṃśādigrāse rasākāram āha yadītyādi // GRhtCM_6.10-12:5 //
children.translated_text: He describes the appearance of mercury upon assimilation of one-sixty-fourth and other [portions] of morsel with 'yadi' (if) and so forth. (GRhtCM 6.10-12:5)

children.text:
yadi cedrasaḥ catuḥṣaṣṭyaṃśān pramāṇato grāsaṃ grasati hi niścitaṃ tadā
                            daṇḍaṃ dhārayet vastrānna kṣaratītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_6.10-12:6 //
children.translated_text: If indeed the mercury consumes a morsel in the measure of one-sixty-fourth part, then it holds a rod-shape — meaning it does not flow through cloth. (GRhtCM 6.10-12:6)

children.text:
punaścatvāriṃśadbhāgapraveśato rasodare iti śeṣaḥ tadā pāyasākāraḥ
                            kvathitadugdhākāro bhavet nibiḍatvāt // GRhtCM_6.10-12:7 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, from the entry of one-fortieth part into the interior of mercury — this is the complement — then [mercury] becomes of <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-pudding) appearance — resembling boiled milk — due to its density. (GRhtCM 6.10-12:7)

children.text: tadevāha bhavatītyādi // GRhtCM_6.10-12:8 //
children.translated_text: He states that very [point] with 'bhavati' (it becomes) and so forth. (GRhtCM 6.10-12:8)

children.text:
viṃśadbhāgāt triṃśadbhāgasya jāraṇato japaukākāro bhavet rasa
                            ityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_6.10-12:9 //
children.translated_text: From the assimilation of one-twentieth to one-thirtieth part, [mercury] becomes leech-shaped — 'mercury' is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 6.10-12:9)

children.text:
punaḥ viṃśatyā viṃśadbhāgajāraṇena avippuṣo bhaved āsanānna capati //
                            GRhtCM_6.10-12:10 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, from [assimilation of] one-twentieth part, [mercury] becomes free from droplets — does not move from its seat. (GRhtCM 6.10-12:10)

children.text:
punaḥ ṣoḍaśāṃśāt ṣoḍaśāṃśabhāgajāraṇataḥ chedī bhavet kṣurikādibhiḥ chede
                            kṛte pṛthaktvamāpnoti // GRhtCM_6.10-12:11 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, from one-sixteenth part — from the assimilation of one-sixteenth portion — [mercury] becomes cuttable — when cut with a knife and the like, it attains separateness. (GRhtCM 6.10-12:11)

children.text: ataḥ ṣoḍaśabhāgādūrdhvaṃ grāso durjaro bhavet // GRhtCM_6.10-12:12 //
children.translated_text: Beyond one-sixteenth part, the morsel becomes difficult to assimilate. (GRhtCM 6.10-12:12)

children.text: pañcabhirebhirgrāsairghanasatvaṃ jārayitvādau /
children.translated_text: Having first assimilated the dense essence (<s>ghanasattva</s>, mica-essence) with these five morsels,

children.text: garbhadrāve nipuṇo jārayati bījaṃ kalāṃśena // GRht_6.13 //
children.translated_text: one skilled in internal dissolution (<s>garbhadrāva</s>) assimilates the seed in fractional portions. (GRht 6.13)

children.text: taccāha pañcabhirityādi // GRhtCM_6.13:1 //
children.translated_text: He states that with 'pañcabhiḥ' (with five) and so forth. (GRhtCM 6.13:1)

Thus, by the stated procedure, furthermore, one skilled in <s>garbhadrāva</s> (internal dissolution) — a man proficient in effecting dissolution of mica and other metals within the interior of mercury — should add the morsel in fractional portions. (GRhtCM 6.13:2)

children.text:
kiṃ kṛtvā pañcabhiḥ pūrvoktaiḥ grāsaiścāru yathā syāttathā
                            ghanasatvamādau jārayitvā pañcabhirgrāsair ghanasatvajāraṇānantaraṃ
                            ṣoḍaśabhāgena bījaṃ jārayedityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_6.13:3 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? Having first assimilated the dense essence (<s>ghanasattva</s>) properly with the five previously mentioned morsels — after the assimilation of <s>ghanasattva</s> with five morsels, one should assimilate the seed in one-sixteenth portions — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 6.13:3)

children.text: Ōnderung von phys. Eig. von Hg nach jāraṇa
children.translated_text: [Section:] Change of physical properties of mercury after <s>jāraṇa</s>

children.text: dhūmraściṭiciṭiśabdo maṇḍūkagatistathā sakampaśca /
children.translated_text: Smoky-colored, making a crackling sound, having a frog-like movement, and trembling —

children.text: niṣkampo bhavati raso vijñātavyo+abhrajīrṇastu // GRht_6.14 //
children.translated_text: [when mercury] becomes motionless, it should be recognized as having mica assimilated. (GRht 6.14)

children.text: kapilo+atha nirudgārī vipluṣabhāvaṃ ca muñcate sūtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Tawny-brown, free from eructation, and the mercury releases its droplet-state;

children.text: niṣkampo gatirahito vijñātavyo+abhrajīrṇastu // GRht_6.15 //
children.translated_text: motionless and devoid of movement — it should be recognized as having mica assimilated. (GRht 6.15)

children.text: abhrakajīrṇarasapakṣaṇam āha dhūmra ityādi // GRhtCM_6.14-15:1 //
children.translated_text: He describes the criterion for mercury with assimilated mica with 'dhūmra' (smoky) and so forth. (GRhtCM 6.14-15:1)

children.text:
abhrajīrṇarasa evaṃvidho bhavati abhraṃ jīrṇaṃ yasmin sa tathoktaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_6.14-15:2 //
children.translated_text: Mercury with assimilated mica becomes of the following description — that in which mica has been assimilated — it is so described. (GRhtCM 6.14-15:2)

children.text:
vahniyogāt prathamaṃ dhūmro dhūmrābho bhavati punaściṭiciṭiśabdo bhavati
                            tato maṇḍūkagatirbhavati punastathā tena prakāreṇa dhṛte sati sakampo
                            bhavati punarvahnau niṣkampaḥ svastho bhavati abhrasatvadrutasya
                            pakṣaṇamiti // GRhtCM_6.14-15:3 //
children.translated_text: Due to contact with fire, first it becomes smoky — smoke-colored; then a crackling sound occurs; then it moves like a frog; again, when held in that manner, it becomes tremulous; then in the fire it becomes steady and still. This is the characteristic of mercury in which mica-essence has been dissolved. (GRhtCM 6.14–15:3)

children.text: tadevāha kapipa ityādi // GRhtCM_6.14-15:4 //
children.translated_text: He states this very [thing] with 'brownish' and so forth. (GRhtCM 6.14–15:4)

children.text: punarevaṃvidho raso+abhrajīrṇo vijñātavyaḥ // GRhtCM_6.14-15:5 //
children.translated_text: Again, mercury of this nature — having digested mica — should be recognized. (GRhtCM 6.14–15:5)

children.text:
kīdṛśaḥ kapipaḥ varṇataḥ nirudgārī sthirabhāvaḥ punaḥ sa raso
                            vippuṣabhāvaṃ cañcapatvaṃ muñcate // GRhtCM_6.14-15:6 //
children.translated_text: Of what nature? Brownish in color; without belching — of stable nature. Furthermore, that mercury abandons its splashing nature — its agitation. (GRhtCM 6.14–15:6)

children.text:
punarniṣkampaḥ svasthaḥ punargatirahitaḥ pakṣacchinnaḥ iti
                            pakṣaṇānyabhrajīrṇasya bhavanti // GRhtCM_6.14-15:7 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, motionless — steady; again devoid of movement — with wings clipped. These are the characteristics of mica-digested [mercury]. (GRhtCM 6.14–15:7)

children.text: kacchapayantra
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>kacchapa yantra</s> (tortoise apparatus)

children.text: jalapūrṇapātramadhye dattvā ghaṭakharparaṃ suvistīrṇam /
children.translated_text: In the middle of a water-filled vessel, having placed a broad pot-shard (<s>ghaṭakharpara</s>),

children.text: tadupari madhyagataḥ sūtaḥ sthāpyastataḥ kuḍye // GRht_6.16 //
children.translated_text: on top of it, mercury placed in the center should be stationed; then in a furnace (<s>kuḍya</s>) — (GRht 6.16)

children.text: laghulohakaṭorikayā kṛtapaṭamṛtsandhilepayācchādya /
children.translated_text: covered with a light metal cup, with cloth-and-clay joint-sealing,

children.text: pūrṇaṃ tadghaṭakharparam aṅgāraiḥ karīṣatuṣamiśraiḥ // GRht_6.17 //
children.translated_text: the pot-shard should be filled with embers mixed with cow-dung and husk. (GRht 6.17)

children.text: svedanato mardanataḥ kacchapayantrasthito raso jarati /
children.translated_text: Through heating and grinding, mercury stationed in the tortoise apparatus digests [the bolus];

children.text: agnibalenaiva tato garbhadrutiḥ sarvalohānām // GRht_6.18 //
children.translated_text: then by the power of fire alone, the internal dissolution (<s>garbhadruti</s>) of all metals [occurs]. (GRht 6.18)

children.text: kacchapayantramāha japetyādi // GRhtCM_6.16-18:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He describes the <s>kacchapa yantra</s> (tortoise apparatus), with 'water' and so forth. (GRhtCM 6.16–18:1)

children.text:
japapūrṇapātramadhye iti japapūrṇaṃ yatpātraṃ tasya madhye suvistīrṇaṃ
                            sundarāyataṃ ghaṭakharparaṃ kumbhakhaṇḍaṃ dattvā tadupari kharparopari
                            biḍamadhyagataḥ sūtaḥ sthāpyaḥ // GRhtCM_6.16-18:2 //
children.translated_text: 'In the middle of a water-filled vessel' — in the middle of a vessel that is filled with water, having placed a broad — beautifully spacious — pot-shard (<s>ghaṭakharpara</s>), a fragment of a pot; on top of it — on top of the shard — mercury, placed in the center along with <s>viḍa</s>, should be stationed. (GRhtCM 6.16–18:2)

children.text:
kutra kuḍye mṛdā vinirmite viśāpamukhe paghupohakaṭorikayā atipaghvī yā
                            pohasya muṇḍādeḥ kaṭorikā pātraviśeṣaḥ tayā viḍāvṛtaṃ sūtaṃ ācchādya ā
                            samantāt saṃrudhya // GRhtCM_6.16-18:3 //
children.translated_text: Where? In a furnace (<s>kuḍya</s>) — made of clay, with a wide opening; with a light metal cup — a very light cup made of metal such as tin (<s>muṇḍa</s>) — a special vessel — with that, the mercury wrapped with <s>viḍa</s> should be covered — enclosed all around. (GRhtCM 6.16–18:3)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭayā kṛtapaṭamṛtsandhipepayā kṛtaḥ paṭamṛdbhyāṃ sandherpepo rodho
                            yasyāḥ sā tayā // GRhtCM_6.16-18:4 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality? With cloth-and-clay joint-sealing — having the joint sealed with cloth and clay — such [a cup]. (GRhtCM 6.16–18:4)

children.text:
punastatkuḍyāntargataghaṭakharparaṃ aṅgāraiḥ pūrṇaṃ kiṃviśiṣṭaiḥ
                            karīṣatuṣamiśraiḥ karīṣo gomayasya cūrṇaṃ tuṣāḥ śāpyāderdhānyasya tair
                            miśritairiti // GRhtCM_6.16-18:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the pot-shard inside the furnace should be filled with embers — of what quality? — mixed with cow-dung and husk. Cow-dung is the powder of cow dung; husk is [the covering] of rice and other grains; mixed with those. (GRhtCM 6.16–18:5)

children.text:
kacchapayantre yadvihitaṃ tadāha svedanata ityādi // GRhtCM_6.16-18:6
                            //
children.translated_text: He states what is prescribed in the tortoise apparatus, with 'through heating' and so forth. (GRhtCM 6.16–18:6)

children.text:
kacchapayantrastho raso jarati grāsaṃ iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_6.16-18:7
                            //
children.translated_text: Mercury stationed in the tortoise apparatus digests — the bolus, is the completion. (GRhtCM 6.16–18:7)

children.text: kutaḥ svedanataḥ vahnau paritāpataḥ // GRhtCM_6.16-18:8 //
children.translated_text: From what? Through heating — through warming in fire. (GRhtCM 6.16–18:8)

children.text:
na kevapaṃ svedanato mardanataśca viḍādinā ityadhyāhāraḥ //
                            GRhtCM_6.16-18:9 //
children.translated_text: Not through heating alone, but also through grinding — with <s>viḍa</s> and the like — this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 6.16–18:9)

children.text:
tato 'gnibapenaiva sarvapohānāṃ svarṇādīnāṃ asminnantarāpe
                            garbhadrutirbhavati atrāgnibapameva mukhyaṃ // GRhtCM_6.16-18:10 //
children.translated_text: Then, by the power of fire alone, the internal dissolution of all metals — gold and the rest — occurs in this interval. Here, the power of fire alone is the chief [factor]. (GRhtCM 6.16–18:10)

children.text: evaṃ dattvā jīryati na kṣayati raso yathā tathā kāryaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus given [the bolus], one should ensure that mercury digests it without being diminished;

children.text: kṣayameti kṣāraviḍaiḥ sa tūparasairgrāsamudgirati // GRht_6.19 //
children.translated_text: it is diminished by alkalis and <s>viḍa</s>; but by <s>uparasas</s> (subsidiary minerals), it regurgitates the bolus. (GRht 6.19)

children.text: jāraṇāyāṃ vidhidvayamāha evamityādi // GRhtCM_6.19:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the two methods in digestion, with 'thus' and so forth. (GRhtCM 6.19:1)

children.text:
evamamunā prakāreṇa kacchapayantre nidhāya jīryati grāsaṃ rasa iti śeṣaḥ
                            // GRhtCM_6.19:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus — in this manner, having placed [it] in the tortoise apparatus, [mercury] digests the bolus — is the completion. (GRhtCM 6.19:2)

children.text:
yathā raso na kṣayati kṣayaṃ nāpnoti tathā kāryo vidhiḥ iti śeṣaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_6.19:3 //
children.translated_text: The method should be done in such a way that mercury is not diminished — does not reach diminishment, is the completion. (GRhtCM 6.19:3)

children.text: kāryasyāśrayarakṣaṇāyeti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_6.19:4 //
children.translated_text: The purport is: for the protection of the substratum of the operation. (GRhtCM 6.19:4)

children.text:
punaḥ kṣārabiḍaiḥ kṣayameti nāśamāpnoti grāsa ityadhyāhāraḥ //
                            GRhtCM_6.19:5 //
children.translated_text: Again, by alkalis and <s>viḍa</s>, [the bolus] reaches diminishment — perishes — 'the bolus' is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 6.19:5)

children.text:
punaḥ sa rasa uparasairgandhādibhiḥ grāsaṃ utprāvapyena girati
                            gipatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_6.19:6 //
children.translated_text: Again, that mercury, by <s>uparasas</s> such as sulphur and the like, vomits up the bolus — swallows [and then] regurgitates, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 6.19:6)

children.text: kṣārairampaiśca gandhādyair mūtraiḥ paṭubhireva ca /
children.translated_text: With alkalis, acids, sulphur and the like, urines, and sharp substances —

children.text: rasagrāsasya jīrṇārthaṃ biḍaḥ sa parikīrtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: for the purpose of digesting the bolus of mercury, [this compound] is proclaimed as <s>viḍa</s>.

children.text: iti paribhāṣā // GRhtCM_6.19:7 //
children.translated_text: This is the definition (<s>paribhāṣā</s>). (GRhtCM 6.19:7)

children.text: biḍaśabdena piṇḍaḥ // GRhtCM_6.19:8 //
children.translated_text: By the word '<s>viḍa</s>' [is meant] a ball (<s>piṇḍa</s>). (GRhtCM 6.19:8)

children.text: viḍa:: positive effects
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>viḍa</s>: positive effects

children.text:
grāsaṃ na muñcati na vāñchati taṃ ca bhūyaḥ kāṃścidguṇānbhajati
                                bhuktavibhuktimātrāt /
children.translated_text: [Mercury] does not release the bolus, nor does it desire [another] one again; it acquires certain qualities merely from having consumed and digested.

children.text:
yajjīryate pracurakevalavahniyogāt tasmādviḍaiḥ suniviḍaiḥ saha
                                jāraṇā syāt // GRht_7.1 //
children.translated_text: Because it is digested by abundant, pure fire-application alone, therefore digestion should be [done] with well-compacted <s>viḍas</s>. (GRht 7.1)

children.text: biḍairjāraṇāyāḥ sugamatvamāha grāsamityādi // GRhtCM_7.1:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the ease of digestion with <s>viḍas</s>, with 'bolus' and so forth. (GRhtCM 7.1:1)

children.text:
grāsaṃ na muñcati ca punastam evānyagrāsaṃ na vāñchati bhūyaḥ punaḥ
                            bhuktavibhuktimātrāt kāṃścidguṇān nityaṃ bhajati dadhāti
                            grāsagrasanamātrāt guṇaṃ karotītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_7.1:2 //
children.translated_text: [Mercury] does not release the bolus, and again it does not desire that very [same] another bolus; furthermore, merely from having consumed and digested the bolus, it constantly acquires certain qualities — produces quality — merely from consuming the bolus, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 7.1:2)

children.text:
yato hetorbiḍairvakṣyamāṇapakṣaṇaiḥ kṛtvā jīryate grāsamityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_7.1:3 //
children.translated_text: For what reason? Because with <s>viḍas</s> of the characteristics to be described, having applied [them], it digests the bolus, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 7.1:3)

children.text:
kutaḥ pracurakevapavahniyogāt pracura udagro yaḥ kevapavahniyogaḥ
                            śuddhāgniyogastasmāt // GRhtCM_7.1:4 //
