children.translated_text: From what cause? From abundant, pure fire-application alone — 'abundant' means intense; 'pure fire-application' means the application of pure fire alone — from that. (GRhtCM 7.1:4)

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaiḥ sunibiḍaiḥ ghanaiḥ // GRhtCM_7.1:5 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality? Well-compacted — dense. (GRhtCM 7.1:5)

children.text:
yato biḍāḥ śreṣṭhās tasmādviḍair eva jāraṇā syāt sugamatvāditi bhāvaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_7.1:6 //
children.translated_text: Since <s>viḍas</s> are excellent, therefore digestion should be done with <s>viḍas</s> alone — because of the ease, is the implication. (GRhtCM 7.1:6)

children.text: viḍa:: for jāraṇa of copper leafs
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>viḍa</s>: for digestion of copper leaves

children.text: sauvarcalakaṭukatrayakākṣīkāsīsagandhakaiśca viḍaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With <s>viḍas</s> [made of] <s>sauvarcala</s> (black salt), the three pungents (<s>kaṭukatraya</s>), <s>kākṣī</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol), and sulphur,

children.text: śigro rasaśatabhāvyaistāmradalānyapi jārayati // GRht_7.2 //
children.translated_text: processed a hundred times with the juice of <s>śigru</s> (drumstick) — it digests even copper leaves. (GRht 7.2)

children.text: biḍavidhānamāha sauvarcapetyādi // GRhtCM_7.2:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He describes the <s>viḍa</s> method with '<s>sauvarcala</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 7.2:1)

children.text:
tāmradapānyapi jārayati buddhimān iti śeṣaḥ svarṇabījādīnāṃ kā katheti
                            bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_7.2:2 //
children.translated_text: It digests even copper leaves — [by] a wise person, is the completion. What need to mention gold-seeds and the like? — is the implication. (GRhtCM 7.2:2)

children.text: kaiḥ kṛtvā biḍaiḥ kṛtvā // GRhtCM_7.2:3 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? Having made <s>viḍas</s>. (GRhtCM 7.2:3)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭair biḍaiḥ sauvarcapakaṭukatrayakāṃkṣīkāsīsagandhakaiḥ
                            sauvarcapaṃ rucakaṃ kaṭutrayaṃ śuṇṭhīmaricapippapyātmakaṃ kākṣī
                            saurāṣṭrī kāsīsaṃ puṣpakāsīsaṃ gandhakaṃ pepitakaṃ etānyauṣadhāni yeṣu
                            viḍeṣu santi te tathoktāḥ taiḥ // GRhtCM_7.2:4 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality? [Made with] <s>sauvarcala</s>, the three pungents, <s>kākṣī</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s>, and sulphur. <s>Sauvarcala</s> is <s>rucaka</s> (black salt); the three pungents (<s>kaṭutraya</s>) consist of ginger (<s>śuṇṭhī</s>), pepper (<s>marica</s>), and long pepper (<s>pippalī</s>); <s>kākṣī</s> is <s>saurāṣṭrī</s> (a mineral); <s>kāsīsa</s> is <s>puṣpakāsīsa</s> (flower vitriol); <s>gandhaka</s> is yellow [sulphur]. These herbs — the <s>viḍas</s> that contain these — are so designated; with those. (GRhtCM 7.2:4)

children.text:
punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaiḥ śigro rasaśatabhāvyaiḥ śigroḥ saubhāñjanasya rasena
                            śatavāraṃ bhāvyāḥ ye biḍāstaiḥ evaṃ niṣpannairviḍairniścitaṃ jāraṇā
                            syāditi bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_7.2:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, of what quality? Processed a hundred times with the juice of <s>śigru</s> — the juice of <s>saubhāñjana</s> (drumstick tree) — <s>viḍas</s> processed a hundred times [with it]; with such prepared <s>viḍas</s>, digestion is certainly [possible], is the implication. (GRhtCM 7.2:5)

children.text: viḍa:: for jāraṇa of gold
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>viḍa</s>: for digestion of gold

children.text: sarvāṅgadagdhamūlakabhasma pratigālitaṃ surabhimūtreṇa /
children.translated_text: The ash of radish (<s>mūlaka</s>) burnt whole — filtered with fragrant cow's urine —

children.text: śatabhāvyaṃ balivasayā tatkṣaṇato jāryate hema // GRht_7.3 //
children.translated_text: processed a hundred times with the fat of a powerful [animal] — it instantly digests gold. (GRht 7.3)

children.text: biḍāntaramāha sarvetyādi // GRhtCM_7.3:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He describes another <s>viḍa</s>, with 'whole' and so forth. (GRhtCM 7.3:1)

children.text:
sarvāṅgadagdhamūpakabhasma pratigāpitamiti sarvāṅgena
                            mūpatvakpatrapuṣpaphapena saha dagdhaṃ bhasmatāṃ prāptaṃ yanmūpakakandaṃ
                            tadbhasma surabhimūtreṇa gojapena gāpitaṃ kāryaṃ kṣāro grāhya ityarthaḥ
                            // GRhtCM_7.3:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Ash of radish burnt whole and filtered' — burnt together with all parts — root, bark, leaves, flowers, and fruit — the ash that has reached the state of ash, which is the radish bulb — that ash should be filtered with fragrant cow's urine — cow's urine — the alkali should be collected, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 7.3:2)

children.text: punarbapivasayā bapamukhyā yā japaukā maṇḍūkādīnāṃ vasā yathā ca /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, with the fat of a powerful [animal] — the fat whose power is chief, namely of leeches, frogs, and the like. As [stated in the verse]:

children.text: bhekamatsyavasā yā tu kukkuṭasya vasāthavā /
children.translated_text: 'The fat of frogs and fish, or the fat of the rooster,

children.text: bhāvyam ebhiḥ kramādgandhaṃ śiśumāravasāpi vā // GRhtCM_7.3:3 //
children.translated_text: sulphur should be processed with these in sequence; or with the fat of the <s>śiśumāra</s> (Gangetic dolphin).' (GRhtCM 7.3:3)

children.text: ekā bapivasā samyak sūtasya bandhinī param /
children.translated_text: 'The one powerful fat properly binds mercury supremely,

children.text: rañjanaṃ caiva kurute maṇimūṣāvidhikramāt /
children.translated_text: and also produces coloring, through the method of gem-crucible.'

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_7.3:4 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 7.3:4)

children.text:
bapivasayā śataṃ śatavāraṃ kṣārabhūtaṃ bhasma bhāvyaṃ punaḥ
                            tacchatabhāvyam auṣadhaṃ tatkṣaṇataḥ tatkāpato hema svarṇaṃ jāryate raso
                            grāsabhūtaṃ hema jaratīti biḍayogāditi bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_7.3:5 //
children.translated_text: With the powerful fat, the ash that has become alkali should be processed a hundred times. Again, that medicine processed a hundred times, at that very moment — at that time — digests gold. Mercury digests gold that has become the bolus — through the <s>viḍa</s> formula, is the implication. (GRhtCM 7.3:5)

children.text: viḍa:: for jāraṇa
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>viḍa</s>: for digestion

children.text: kadalīpalāśatilaniculakanakasuradālivāstukairaṇḍāḥ /
children.translated_text: Plantain (<s>kadalī</s>), flame of the forest (<s>palāśa</s>), sesame (<s>tila</s>), <s>nicula</s>, <s>kanaka</s> (dhattura), <s>suradālī</s> (devadālī), <s>vāstuka</s>, and castor (<s>eraṇḍa</s>);

children.text: varṣābhūvṛṣamokṣakasahitāḥ kṣāro yathālābham // GRht_7.4 //
children.translated_text: combined with <s>varṣābhū</s> (<s>punarnavā</s>), <s>vṛṣa</s> (<s>vāsaka</s>), and <s>mokṣaka</s> — the alkali [should be prepared] as available. (GRht 7.4)

children.text:
ānīya kṣāravṛkṣān kusumaphalaśiphātvakpravālairupetān kṛtvātaḥ
                                khaṇḍaśastān vipulataraśilāpiṣṭagātrātiśuṣkān /
children.translated_text: Having brought the alkali-yielding trees, together with their flowers, fruits, roots, bark, and shoots; having then cut them into pieces — with bodies thoroughly dried, pounded on a large stone;

children.text:
dagdhvā kāṇḍaistilānāṃ karisurabhihayāmbhobhir āsrāvya vastrair
                                bhasma tyaktvā jalaṃ tanmṛduśikhini pacedvaṃśapākena bhūyaḥ //
                                GRht_7.5 //
children.translated_text: having burnt [them] with sesame stalks, having filtered [the ash] with cow's urine or horse's water through cloths; discarding the ash, one should cook the water on a gentle fire by the bamboo-cooking method again. (GRht 7.5)

children.text:
tacchuṣyamāṇaṃ hi sabāṣpabudbudān yadā vidhatte kṣaṇabhaṅgurān bahūn
                                /
children.translated_text: When that, as it dries, produces many bubbles of steam, momentarily bursting,

children.text:
tadā kṣipettryūṣaṇahiṃgugandhakaṃ kṣāratrayaṃ ṣaḍlavaṇāni bhūkhagau
                                // GRht_7.6 //
children.translated_text: then one should add the three pungent spices (<s>tryūṣaṇa</s>), asafoetida (<s>hiṅgu</s>), sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), the three alkalis (<s>kṣāratraya</s>), the six salts (<s>ṣaḍlavaṇa</s>), and <s>bhūkhaga</s> (two [substances]). (GRht 7.6)

children.text:
dravyāṇi saṃmiśrya nivṛtya bhūtale vyavasthitaṃ śastrakaṭorikāpuṭe
                                /
children.translated_text: Having mixed the substances, having cooled [them] on the ground, [the preparation] should be placed in a blade-cup-container (<s>śastrakaṭorikāpuṭa</s>),

children.text:
saṃsthāpayetsaptadināni dhānyagataṃ prayojyaṃ rasajāraṇādikam //
                                GRht_7.7 //
children.translated_text: stored for seven days in grain — [it is then] to be employed for mercury digestion and the like. (GRht 7.7)

children.text: atha kṣāravṛkṣagupmauṣadhiviśeṣānāha kadapītyādi // GRhtCM_7.4-7:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now he describes the specific alkali-yielding trees and secret herbs, with 'plantain' and so forth. (GRhtCM 7.4–7:1)

children.text:
yathāpābhaṃ pābham anatikramya eṣāṃ kṣāraḥ kartavyaḥ // GRhtCM_7.4-7:2
                            //
children.translated_text: The alkali of these should be prepared as available — not exceeding what is obtainable. (GRhtCM 7.4–7:2)

children.text:
te ke kadapīpapāśatipanicupakanakasuradāpivāstukairaṇḍāḥ kadapī rambhā
                            papāśo brahmavṛkṣaḥ tipāḥ pratītāḥ nicupo vetasavṛkṣaḥ kanako dhattūraḥ
                            suradāpī devadāpī vāstukaṃ kṣāraśākaṃ eraṇḍo vātāriḥ ete kṣārasaṃbhavāḥ
                            // GRhtCM_7.4-7:3 //
children.translated_text: What are they? Plantain (<s>kadalī</s>, banana plant), <s>palāśa</s> (flame of the forest), sesame (<s>tila</s>), <s>nicula</s> (<s>vetasa</s> tree), <s>kanaka</s> (dhattura), <s>suradālī</s> (<s>devadālī</s>), <s>vāstuka</s> (alkali vegetable), and <s>eraṇḍa</s> (castor, enemy of wind). These are alkali-producing [plants]. (GRhtCM 7.4–7:3)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭā ete varṣābhūvṛṣamokṣakasahitāḥ varṣābhūḥ punarnavā vṛṣo
                            vāsakaḥ mokṣako mokhāvṛkṣa iti pratītaḥ etaiḥ saṃyutā ityuddeśaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_7.4-7:4 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality? Combined with <s>varṣābhū</s> (<s>punarnavā</s>), <s>vṛṣa</s> (<s>vāsaka</s>), and <s>mokṣaka</s> (<s>mokhā</s> tree, as commonly known). Combined with these, is the indication. (GRhtCM 7.4–7:4)

children.text: kṣārakaraṇavidhānam āhānīyetyādi // GRhtCM_7.4-7:5 //
children.translated_text: He states the method of alkali preparation, with 'having brought' and so forth. (GRhtCM 7.4–7:5)

children.text:
prathamaṃ kṣāravṛkṣān pūrvoktān ānīya vanāntarādgṛhītvā // GRhtCM_7.4-7:6
                            //
children.translated_text: First, having brought the alkali-trees mentioned before — having obtained them from the forest — (GRhtCM 7.4-7:6)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭān kusumaphapaśiphātvakpapāśairupetān kusumāni prasūnāni
                            pratītāni śiphā mūpaṃ tvaktvacā pravāpā nūtanapappavāḥ etaiḥ
                            pañcāṅgāhvayair upetān saṃyutān // GRhtCM_7.4-7:7 //
children.translated_text: Of what qualities? Endowed with flowers, fruits, roots, bark, and new shoots — flowers means blossoms, well-known ones; <s>śiphā</s> means roots; <s>tvak</s> means bark; <s>pravāla</s> means new shoots — endowed with these five parts (<s>pañcāṅga</s>), i.e., complete with [all five]. (GRhtCM 7.4-7:7)

children.text: khaṇḍaśaḥ bahuśakapān kṛtvā // GRhtCM_7.4-7:8 //
children.translated_text: Having cut them into pieces — into many fragments. (GRhtCM 7.4-7:8)

children.text:
na kevapaṃ khaṇḍaśaḥ vipupataraśipāpiṣṭagātrātiśuṣkān kṛtvā vipupatarā
                            ativistīrṇā yā śipā tasyāṃ piṣṭāni gātrāṇi yeṣāṃ te'śuṣkā nirasāḥ
                            tānevaṃvidhān kṛtvā // GRhtCM_7.4-7:9 //
children.translated_text: Not merely into pieces — having made them exceedingly dried, with limbs ground on a very broad stone — 'very broad' means extremely wide; the stone on which the limbs are ground — those that are dried, i.e., devoid of moisture — having made them in such a manner. (GRhtCM 7.4-7:9)

children.text:
punastāneva ca tipānāṃ kāṇḍairnāpaiḥ saha dagdhvā // GRhtCM_7.4-7:10
                            //
children.translated_text: Then again, having burnt those very [pieces] together with stalks of sesame plants — with reeds. (GRhtCM 7.4-7:10)

Again, having lixiviated with the fragrant urines of cow, horse, and elephant — having dissolved the ash — discarding the [residual] ash, the water should be collected through cloth — this is the completion. (GRhtCM 7.4-7:11)

children.text:
tajjapaṃ mṛduśikhini komapāgnau pacet kena vaṃśapākena vaṃśānāṃ
                            samavahnitvāt // GRhtCM_7.4-7:12 //
children.translated_text: That water should be cooked on a gentle flame, a soft fire — by what [method]? By the bamboo method — because bamboos have an even fire-nature. (GRhtCM 7.4-7:12)

children.text: kṣārajapapākapakṣaṇamāha tadityādi // GRhtCM_7.4-7:13 //
children.translated_text: He states the sign of the alkali-water being properly cooked, with 'that' and so forth. (GRhtCM 7.4-7:13)

children.text:
tajjapaṃ kṣārapānīyaṃ śuṣyamāṇaṃ sat niścitaṃ yadā sabāṣpabudbudān
                            vidhatte saha bāṣpeṇa japātyayadhūmena vartante ye budbudāstān tadā
                            kṣāro niṣpanno jñeyaḥ // GRhtCM_7.4-7:14 //
children.translated_text: That water — the alkali-water — when drying, when it certainly produces steam-bubbles — bubbles that arise with vapor — together with steam and smoke-like vapors — when those bubbles appear, then the alkali should be known as ready. (GRhtCM 7.4-7:14)

children.text:
punastadā tryūṣaṇaṃ śuṇṭhīmaricapippapyaḥ hiṅgu rāmaṭhaṃ gandhakaṃ
                            pepītakaṃ punaḥ kṣāratrayaṃ sarjikāyavāgrajaṭaṅkaṇāhvayaṃ pavaṇāni ṣaṭ
                            saindhavādīni bhūḥ tuvarī khagaṃ kāsīsaṃ etāni kṣipet etatkṣāreṇārdreṇa
                            saha miśraṃ kāryamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_7.4-7:15 //
children.translated_text: Then at that point: <s>tryūṣaṇa</s> — dry ginger, black pepper, and long pepper; <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida); <s>rāmaṭha</s> (a type of salt); <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur); <s>lepītaka</s>; again the three alkalis — <s>sarjikā</s> (soda), <s>yavāgraja</s> (saltpeter), and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax); six salts beginning with <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt); <s>bhūḥ tuvarī</s> (alum); <s>khaga</s> — <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol) — these should be added; mixed together with this still-moist alkali, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 7.4-7:15)

children.text:
tathā ca dravyāṇi tryūṣaṇādīni saṃmiśrya ekīkṛtya nivṛtya ca saṃmardya
                            śastrakaṭorikāpuṭe pohamayapātrasaṃpuṭe vyavasthitaṃ saptadināni
                            dhānyagataṃ kasyaciddhānyasya madhyagataṃ sthāpayet kutra bhūtape
                            pṛthivyā āsthāne tato+anantaraṃ tatsiddhaṃ rasajāraṇādikaṃ prati
                            prayojyaṃ etadbiḍarūpaṃ rasajāraṇādiṣu praśastamityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_7.4-7:16 //
children.translated_text: And thus, having combined the substances beginning with <s>tryūṣaṇa</s> — having unified them, and having rubbed and ground them — [they should be placed] in a sealed metallic vessel (<s>śastrakaṭorikāpuṭa</s>), in a container made of iron; [the preparation], properly arranged, should be stored for seven days inside grain — placed in the midst of some grain — where? In a place on the earth (<s>bhūtala</s>). Thereafter that perfected [substance] should be employed for mercury digestion (<s>rasajāraṇa</s>) and such [operations] — this is the <s>viḍa</s> form, excellent for mercury digestion and similar processes, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 7.4-7:16)

children.text: viḍa:: for garbhadruti
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>viḍa</s>: for internal dissolution (<s>garbhadruti</s>)

children.text: jambīrabījapūrakacāṅgerīvetasāmlasaṃyogāt /
children.translated_text: From the combination of lemon, citron, sorrel, and cane-acid,

children.text: kṣārā bhavanti nitarāṃ garbhadrutijāraṇe śastāḥ // GRht_7.8 //
children.translated_text: alkalis become exceedingly excellent for internal-dissolution digestion (<s>garbhadrutijāraṇa</s>). (GRht 7.8)

children.text: jāraṇāyāṃ kṣāravidhānamāha jambīretyādi // GRhtCM_7.8:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the alkali method for digestion, with 'lemon' and so forth. (GRhtCM 7.8:1)

children.text:
kṣārā uktavṛkṣodbhavāḥ nitarām atiśayena garbhadrutijāraṇe
                            rasāntargrāsajāraṇe śastā utkṛṣṭā bhavanti // GRhtCM_7.8:2 //
children.translated_text: Alkalis — those produced from the aforementioned trees — become exceedingly, i.e., supremely, excellent — superior — for internal-dissolution digestion (<s>garbhadrutijāraṇa</s>), [which is] the digestion of a bolus inside mercury. (GRhtCM 7.8:2)

children.text:
kutaḥ jambīrabījapūrakacāṅgerīvetasāmpasaṃyogāt jambīraḥ pratītaḥ
                            bījapūrako mātupuṅgaḥ cāṅgerī ampapatrikā vetasāmpaṃ cukrakaṃ eṣāṃ yo
                            rasastasya saṃyogāt etairbhāvitāḥ kṣārā biḍavatkāryakarā iti bhāvaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_7.8:3 //
children.translated_text: From what? From the combination of the juices of lemon (<s>jambīra</s>), citron (<s>bījapūraka</s>, also called <s>mātulinga</s>), sorrel (<s>cāṅgerī</s>, also called <s>amlapatrikā</s>), and cane-acid (<s>vetasāmla</s>, i.e., vinegar/<s>cukraka</s>) — from the combination of their juices; alkalis processed with these become efficacious like <s>viḍa</s>, is the import. (GRhtCM 7.8:3)

children.text: viḍa:: how to use
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>viḍa</s>: how to use

children.text: viḍamadharottaramādau dattvā sūtasya cāṣṭamāṃśena /
children.translated_text: Having placed <s>viḍa</s> below and above, at first, in the proportion of one-eighth of the mercury,

children.text: kuryājjāraṇamevaṃ kramakramādvardhayedagnim // GRht_7.9 //
children.translated_text: one should thus perform digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>); gradually one should increase the fire. (GRht 7.9)

children.text: rase viḍayojanamāha biḍamityādi // GRhtCM_7.9:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the method of applying <s>viḍa</s> to mercury, with '<s>viḍa</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 7.9:1)

children.text:
ādau prathamaṃ sūtasya rasasyāṣṭamāṃśena pūrvanirmitaṃ viḍaṃ adharottaraṃ
                            adha uparibhāgaṃ ca dattvā evaṃ amunā prakāreṇa jāraṇaṃ kuryāt punaḥ
                            kramyate aneneti kramo biḍarūpaḥ tatkramaḥ paraṃparā tasmāt agniṃ
                            vivardhayet karmakṛt ityadhyāhāraḥ vāraṃvāraṃ
                            biḍasaṃprayogādagnirvardhate // GRhtCM_7.9:2 //
children.translated_text: At first — initially — having placed the previously prepared <s>viḍa</s> in the proportion of one-eighth of the mercury (<s>sūta</s>), below and above — on the lower and upper parts — in this manner, by this method, one should perform digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>). Again, <s>krama</s> — that by which one proceeds — is the <s>viḍa</s>-form; by that <s>krama</s>, i.e., by the succession [of applications], one should increase the fire — the practitioner should supply this; by repeated application of <s>viḍa</s>, the fire is increased. (GRhtCM 7.9:2)

children.text: rañjana:: colour acc. to abhra
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>rañjana</s> (coloring): color according to <s>abhra</s> (mica)

children.text: jīrṇābhrako rasendro darśayati ghanānurūpiṇīṃ chāyām /
children.translated_text: Mercury that has digested <s>abhra</s> (mica) displays a hue corresponding to the [type of] mica —

children.text: kṛṣṇāṃ raktāṃ pītāṃ sitāṃ tathā saṃkarairmiśrām // GRht_8.1 //
children.translated_text: black, red, yellow, or white, and also mixed [colors] from combinations. (GRht 8.1)

children.text: kṛṣṇābhrakeṇa balavadasitarāgairyujyate rasendrastu /
children.translated_text: With black mica, mercury acquires exceedingly dark colors;

children.text: śvetai raktaiḥ pītairvahneḥ khalu varṇato jñeyaḥ // GRht_8.2 //
children.translated_text: with white, red, or yellow [mica] — [the color] should be known from the color of the fire [used]. (GRht 8.2)

children.text: dyotate divi candro 'sau jīrṇe'bhre kāntimattayā /
children.translated_text: Just as the moon shines in the sky with brilliance when mica is digested,

children.text: tatheha tāmupāśritya śāpate manujeṣu ca // GRhtCM_8.1-2:1 //
children.translated_text: so too, having acquired that [brilliance], it shines among humans. (GRhtCM 8.1-2:1)

children.text: susiddhabiḍadhātvādijāraṇena rasasya hi /
children.translated_text: Through the digestion of well-perfected <s>viḍa</s>, metals, and so forth in mercury,

children.text: pītādirāgajananaṃ rañjanaṃ parikīrtitam /
children.translated_text: the production of yellow and other colors is called <s>rañjana</s> (coloring) —

children.text: iti paribhāṣā // GRhtCM_8.1-2:2 //
children.translated_text: thus is the definition. (GRhtCM 8.1-2:2)

children.text: abhrasya chāyāviśeṣam āha jīrṇābhraka ityādi // GRhtCM_8.1-2:3 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the specific hue [produced] by mica, with 'having digested mica' and so forth. (GRhtCM 8.1-2:3)

children.text:
rasendro yadā jīrṇābhro bhavati tadā ghanānurūpiṇīṃ jīrṇābhrasamavarṇāṃ
                            chāyāṃ darśayati // GRhtCM_8.1-2:4 //
children.translated_text: When mercury has digested mica (<s>jīrṇābhra</s>), then it displays a hue corresponding to the mica — a color matching the digested mica. (GRhtCM 8.1-2:4)

children.text:
kṛṣṇe jīrṇe kṛṣṇāṃ rakte'bhre jīrṇe raktāṃ pīte pītāṃ tathā site śubhre
                            sitāṃ evaṃ caturvidhāṃ chāyāṃ darśayati // GRhtCM_8.1-2:5 //
children.translated_text: When black [mica] is digested — a black [hue]; when red mica is digested — a red [hue]; with yellow — a yellow [hue]; likewise with white, pure [mica] — a white [hue]; thus it displays a fourfold hue. (GRhtCM 8.1-2:5)

children.text:
punardvayostrayāṇāṃ vā caturṇāṃ saṃkare mepāpe sati dvitricaturṇām
                            anurūpiṇīṃ chāyāṃ darśayatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_8.1-2:6 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, when there is a mixture (<s>saṃkara</s>) of two, three, or four [types of mica], it displays a hue corresponding to that combination of two, three, or four, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 8.1-2:6)

children.text: abhrayogād varṇaviśeṣamāha kṛṣṇetyādi // GRhtCM_8.1-2:7 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the specific color [resulting] from the application of mica, with 'black' and so forth. (GRhtCM 8.1-2:7)

children.text:
kṛṣṇābhrakeṇa jīrṇena raso bapavān bhavet tu punaḥ asitarāgaiḥ
                            kṛṣṇarāgairyujyate // GRhtCM_8.1-2:8 //
children.translated_text: With digested black mica, mercury becomes powerful, and furthermore acquires dark colors — black hues. (GRhtCM 8.1-2:8)

children.text:
tathā śvetena śvetai rāgair yujyate raktena raktaiḥ pītena pītaiḥ
                            kapipāgnerdivyasyāpi sarvasyādarśanarūpaṃ kṣayakarasya bapairdravyāṇāṃ
                            tādṛśo varṇo rasavarṇato varṇakovidairjñeyaḥ // GRhtCM_8.1-2:9 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, with white [mica] it acquires white hues; with red, red [hues]; with yellow, yellow [hues]. The color [produced] by the celestial fire — [which causes] the disappearance of all [impurities] and is destructive in power — such a color should be known by experts in mercury-coloration from the [base] color of the mercury. (GRhtCM 8.1-2:9)

children.text: mercury transfers own colour on other substances
children.translated_text: [Section:] Mercury transfers its own color onto other substances

children.text: atha nijakarme varṇaṃ na jahāti yadā sa rajyate rāgaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, when [mercury] does not abandon its own inherent color when it is colored with dyes,

children.text: kramaśo hi vakṣyamāṇairnirṇikto raṃjanaṃ kurute // GRht_8.3 //
children.translated_text: gradually, having been purified by the [methods] to be described, it effects coloring [of other metals]. (GRht 8.3)

children.text: rañjitarasapraśaṃsām āha athetyādi // GRhtCM_8.3:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He praises the colored mercury, with 'now' and so forth. (GRhtCM 8.3:1)

children.text:
athānantaraṃ rasaḥ rasendro yadā vakṣyamāṇaiḥ śvetādibhiḥ rāgaiḥ rajyate
                            tadā nijakarme varṇaṃ svakīyameva svābhāvikaṃ rūpaṃ na jahāti na tyajati
                            punastaireva rāgaiḥ nirṇikto raktaḥ san rañjanaṃ kurute rāgadāyī
                            bhavatīti // GRhtCM_8.3:2 //
children.translated_text: Now, subsequently — when mercury (<s>rasendra</s>) is colored by the dyes to be described — white and others — then it does not abandon its own inherent color — its own natural form — it does not discard [it]; furthermore, having been purified — colored — by those very dyes, it effects coloring — it becomes a bestower of color, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 8.3:2)

children.text:
tathā no rakto na rañjanaṃ kurute avidyamānatvānniṣedhaḥ // GRhtCM_8.3:3
                            //
children.translated_text: Conversely, when not colored, it does not effect coloring — [this] negation is due to [the color's] non-existence. (GRhtCM 8.3:3)

children.text: (Stoffe, die versch. saṃskāras induzieren)
children.translated_text: (Substances that induce various <s>saṃskāras</s>)

children.text: balamāste'bhrakasatve jāraṇarāgāḥ pratiṣṭhitāstīkṣṇe /
children.translated_text: Strength resides in the essence of <s>abhra</s> (mica); digestion and coloring are established in <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron/steel);

children.text: bandhaśca sāralohe sārakamatha nāgavaṃgābhyām // GRht_8.4 //
children.translated_text: and binding in <s>sāraloha</s> (pure metal); and <s>sāraṇa</s> (liquefaction) from lead and tin. (GRht 8.4)

children.text:
abhrasatvādīnāṃ yoge rase vyavasthāmāha bapamityādi // GRhtCM_8.4:1
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the [specific] role of <s>abhrasatva</s> (mica-essence) and others when combined with mercury, with 'strength' and so forth. (GRhtCM 8.4:1)

children.text:
abhrakasatve'dhikaraṇe bapamāste abhrasatvasaṃyogena raso
                            bapamāpnotītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_8.4:2 //
children.translated_text: In the locus of <s>abhrasatva</s> — through the combination of mica-essence, mercury attains strength, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 8.4:2)

children.text:
punastīkṣṇe pohabhede jāraṇarāgā jāraṇena tīkṣṇasthā rāgāḥ pratiṣṭhitā
                            bhavantītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_8.4:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, in <s>tīkṣṇa</s> — a variety of iron — digestion and coloring: colors that are established through digestion of iron, become fixed, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 8.4:3)

children.text:
sāraṇamatha nāgavaṅgābhyām iti nāgavaṅgābhyāṃ duḥsaraṇaṃ sāraṇadravyaṃ
                            sarata iti // GRhtCM_8.4:4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sāraṇa</s> (liquefaction) from lead and tin — <s>nāga</s> (lead) and <s>vaṅga</s> (tin) [provide] the difficult-to-achieve liquefaction; the liquefaction-substance flows, thus [it is called <s>sāraṇa</s>]. (GRhtCM 8.4:4)

children.text: potency of tīkṣṇaloha
children.translated_text: [Section on] the potency of <s>tīkṣṇaloha</s> (iron/steel)

children.text: krāmati tīkṣṇena rasastīkṣṇena ca jīryate kṣaṇādgrāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: By means of <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, mercury performs <s>krāmaṇa</s> (transmutation); and by <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, the bolus is digested instantly;

children.text: hemno yonistīkṣṇaṃ rāgān gṛhṇāti tīkṣṇena // GRht_8.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Tīkṣṇa</s> is the womb (source) of gold; [mercury] acquires colors by means of <s>tīkṣṇa</s>. (GRht 8.5)

children.text: sarvakāraṇaṃ tīkṣṇamāha krāmatītyādi // GRhtCM_8.5:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is the cause of all [operations], with 'performs transmutation' and so forth. (GRhtCM 8.5:1)

children.text:
tīkṣṇena pohabhedena rasaḥ krāmati krāmaṇaṃ vidadhāti punas tīkṣṇena
                            kṛtvā grāsaḥ kṣaṇādappakāpato jīryate jāraṇam āpnoti punarhemnaḥ
                            suvarṇasya yonirutpattisthānaṃ tīkṣṇamasti punaḥ rāgān rañjanabhāvān
                            tīkṣṇena kṛtvā raso gṛhṇāti svasmin rāgān dadhātītyarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_8.5:2 //
children.translated_text: By <s>tīkṣṇa</s> — the variety of iron — mercury performs <s>krāmaṇa</s>, effects transmutation; furthermore, by means of <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, the bolus is quickly — in a short time — digested, achieves digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>); furthermore, <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is the womb — the place of origin — of gold; furthermore, mercury acquires colors — the states of coloring — by means of <s>tīkṣṇa</s>; it holds colors within itself, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 8.5:2)

children.text: tīkṣṇaloha:: cāraṇa, jāraṇa
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>tīkṣṇaloha</s>: <s>cāraṇa</s> (activation) and <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion)

children.text: tadapi ca daradena hataṃ kṛtvā mākṣikeṇa ravisahitam /
children.translated_text: Having killed that [tīkṣṇa] also with <s>darada</s> (cinnabar/mercury-sulphide), combined with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) and copper (<s>ravi</s>),

children.text: vāsitamapi vāsanayā ghanavaccāryaṃ ca jāryaṃ ca // GRht_8.6 //
children.translated_text: and having impregnated [it] with the impregnation-drug, it should be activated and digested like mica. (GRht 8.6)

children.text: tīkṣṇasya hiṅgupayogena guṇādhikyamāha tadapītyādi // GRhtCM_8.6:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the superiority of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> through the use of <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar), with 'that also' and so forth. (GRhtCM 8.6:1)

children.text:
api niścayena tat tīkṣṇaṃ daradena hiṅgupena hataṃ māritaṃ vā mākṣikena
                            svarṇamākṣikena ravisahitaṃ tāmrasaṃyutaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ hataṃ māritaṃ
                            punarvāsanayā vāsanauṣadhena vāsitaṃ paribhāvitaṃ ghanavad abhravat
                            cāryaṃ jāryaṃ ca satvābhravat nānyathā // GRhtCM_8.6:2 //
children.translated_text: Indeed, certainly that <s>tīkṣṇa</s> — killed, i.e., calcined, with <s>darada</s> (cinnabar/mercury-sulphide); combined with <s>mākṣika</s> — gold-pyrite (<s>svarṇamākṣika</s>) — and <s>ravi</s> — combined with copper; the <s>tīkṣṇa</s> [thus] killed/calcined; furthermore, impregnated — saturated — with the impregnation-drug (<s>vāsanauṣadha</s>); like mica (<s>ghana</s>) — like <s>abhra</s> — it should be activated and also digested; [processed] like mica-essence, not otherwise. (GRhtCM 8.6:2)

children.text: rañjana:: suitable substances
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>rañjana</s>: suitable substances

children.text: kāntaṃ vā tīkṣṇaṃ vā kāñcīṃ vā vajrasasyakādīnām /
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s> (magnetite), or <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron/steel), or <s>kāñcī</s> (gold-pyrite), or [substances] from diamond, <s>sasyaka</s>, and others —

children.text: ekatamaṃ sarvaṃ vā rasaraṃjane saṃkaro+abhīṣṭaḥ // GRht_8.7 //
children.translated_text: any one or all of them — a combination is desired for the coloring of mercury. (GRht 8.7)

children.text: tīkṣṇavadetānāha kāntam ityādi // GRhtCM_8.7:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states [the substances] similar to <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, with '<s>kānta</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 8.7:1)

children.text:
rasarañjane rasendre rāgakarmaṇi kāntaṃ cumbakapāṣāṇotthaṃ pohaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ
                            veti samuccaye tīkṣṇaṃ pohabhedo vā kāñcīṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ vā
                            vajrasasyakādīnāṃ vajrasasyakāvādiryeṣāṃ te teṣāṃ hīrakacapapādīnāṃ
                            ekatamaṃ tanmadhyādekatamaṃ sarvaṃ vā atrābhīṣṭaśabdasya pratyekaṃ
                            saṃbandhaḥ hīrakādīni ratnāni sasyakādyā upadhātavaḥ // GRhtCM_8.7:2
                            //
children.translated_text: For the coloring (<s>rañjana</s>) of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>) — for the operation of coloring: <s>kānta</s> — the metal produced from loadstone — is the best; or — the word 'or' is for enumeration — <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, a variety of iron; or <s>kāñcī</s> — gold-pyrite (<s>svarṇamākṣika</s>); or from among diamond, <s>sasyaka</s>, and others — from those beginning with diamond and <s>sasyaka</s> — i.e., from among jewels such as diamond, vitriol, etc. — any one of them, or all of them; here the word 'desired' (<s>abhīṣṭa</s>) relates to each individually — diamonds and such are gems; <s>sasyaka</s> and others are sub-metals (<s>upadhātus</s>). (GRhtCM 8.7:2)

children.text:
vā rasarañjane ayameva saṃkaraḥ sarveṣāṃ kāntādīnāṃ mepāpaḥ
                            sarvatrābhīṣṭaḥ // GRhtCM_8.7:3 //
children.translated_text: Or, in the coloring of mercury, this same mixture is the most beneficial of all — of <s>kānta</s> (magnetite) and others. [It is] desired everywhere. (GRhtCM 8.7:3)

children.text: (chem. Potenzen versch. Stoffe)
children.translated_text: (Chemical potencies of various substances)

children.text: kuṭile balamabhyadhikaṃ rāgastīkṣṇe tu pannage snehaḥ /
children.translated_text: In <s>kuṭila</s> (crooked one, i.e., tin), strength is predominant; in <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (sharp one, i.e., iron/steel), coloring [is predominant]; in <s>pannaga</s> (serpent, i.e., lead), unctuousness [is predominant];

children.text: rāgasnehabalāni tu kamale śaṃsanti dhātuvidaḥ // GRht_8.8 //
children.translated_text: coloring, unctuousness, and strength — all three are in <s>kamala</s> (copper), so declare the experts of metals. (GRht 8.8)

children.text: mercury:: rañjana
children.translated_text: Mercury: coloring (<s>rañjana</s>)

children.text: sarvair ebhir lohair mākṣikanihataistathā drutairgarbhe /
children.translated_text: With all these metals, killed with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) and dissolved inside [mercury],

children.text: viḍayogena tu jīrṇo rasarājo rāgamupayāti // GRht_8.9 //
children.translated_text: digested through the <s>viḍa</s> formula, the king of <s>rasas</s> attains coloring. (GRht 8.9)

children.text: sve sve vikāre vakṣyamāṇamāha bapamityādi // GRhtCM_8.8-9:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Regarding each one's specific effect, he states what is to be described, with 'strength' and so forth. (GRhtCM 8.8–9:1)

children.text: dhātuvido rasavaidyā iti śaṃsanti // GRhtCM_8.8-9:2 //
children.translated_text: The experts of metals — the physicians of <s>rasa</s> — so declare. (GRhtCM 8.8–9:2)

children.text:
iti kiṃ kuṭipe bapaṃ abhyadhikaṃ sarvādhikaṃ punastīkṣṇe'bhyadhiko rāgaḥ
                            rañjanaṃ tu punaḥ pannage nāge'bhyadhikaṃ snehaḥ snigdhatvaṃ tu punaḥ
                            rāgasnehabapāni trīṇyevoktāni kamape tāmre kuṭipatīkṣṇapannagānāṃ
                            jāraṇādrase yathā baparāgasnehā bhavanti tathaikatāmrajāraṇāt trayo
                            bhavantītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_8.8-9:3 //
children.translated_text: Thus, what? In <s>kuṭila</s> (tin), strength is predominant — greatest of all; again, in <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron/steel), coloring (<s>rāga</s>) is predominant — meaning the capacity to impart color; again, in <s>pannaga</s> (lead), unctuousness (<s>sneha</s>) is predominant — meaning oiliness; again, [as for] coloring, unctuousness, and strength — these three are said to be in <s>kamala</s> (copper). From the digestion of <s>kuṭila</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>pannaga</s> into mercury, just as strength, coloring, and unctuousness arise respectively, so from the digestion of copper alone, all three arise — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 8.8–9:3)

children.text: rasabandhanopāyamāha sarvairityādi // GRhtCM_8.8-9:4 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the method for binding mercury, with 'with all' and so forth. (GRhtCM 8.8–9:4)

children.text:
biḍayogena pūrvoktena jīrṇo jāraṇamāpanno rasarājo bandhamupayāti
                            bandhanamādatte // GRhtCM_8.8-9:5 //
children.translated_text: Digested through the <s>viḍa</s> formula described earlier — having undergone digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>) — the king of <s>rasas</s> attains binding (<s>bandha</s>) — it acquires solidification. (GRhtCM 8.8–9:5)

children.text:
kaiḥ saha jīrṇaḥ ebhiḥ pūrvoktaiḥ sarvair pohairdhātubhiḥ //
                            GRhtCM_8.8-9:6 //
children.translated_text: Digested with what? With all these — the aforementioned metals (<s>lohas</s>), [meaning] the metallic substances. (GRhtCM 8.8–9:6)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭaiḥ mākṣikanihataiḥ svarṇamākṣikamāritaiḥ // GRhtCM_8.8-9:7
                            //
children.translated_text: Of what quality? Killed with <s>mākṣika</s> — calcined with gold-pyrite (<s>svarṇamākṣika</s>). (GRhtCM 8.8–9:7)

children.text:
punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaiḥ garbhe rasodare drutairvidrutairiti // GRhtCM_8.8-9:8
                            //
children.translated_text: Again, of what quality? Dissolved inside (<s>garbhe</s>) — melted within the interior of mercury. (GRhtCM 8.8–9:8)

children.text: mercury:: rañjana (with a kṛṣṭi)
children.translated_text: Mercury: coloring (<s>rañjana</s>) (with a <s>kṛṣṭi</s>, attraction)

children.text: tālakadaradaśilābhiḥ snehakṣārāmlalavaṇasahitābhiḥ /
children.translated_text: With orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>), cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), and realgar (<s>śilā</s>), combined with unctuants, alkalis, acids, and salts,

children.text: samakadviguṇatriguṇān puṭo vahedvaṃgaśastrādīn // GRht_8.10 //
children.translated_text: one should calcine with fire-cakes (<s>puṭa</s>) — tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), iron/steel (<s>śastra</s>), and others — in equal, double, and triple [quantities]. (GRht 8.10)

children.text: raktasnehaniṣekaiḥ śeṣaṃ kuryādrasasya kṛṣṭiriyam /
children.translated_text: With sprinkling of red [group] and unctuants, one should do the rest; this is the attraction (<s>kṛṣṭi</s>) of mercury —

children.text: cāraṇajāraṇamātrātkurute rasamindragopanibham // GRht_8.11 //
children.translated_text: merely through sweeping (<s>cāraṇa</s>) and digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>), it makes mercury resemble an <s>indragopa</s> (cochineal insect). (GRht 8.11)

children.text:
vakṣyamāṇadhātūnāṃ māraṇavidhānamāha tāpaketyādi // GRhtCM_8.10-11:1
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the killing procedure for the metals to be described, with 'orpiment' and so forth. (GRhtCM 8.10–11:1)

children.text:
vaṅgaśastrādīn vaṅgaṃ trapuṣaṃ śastraṃ tīkṣṇaṃ te ādiryeṣāṃ te tān //
                            GRhtCM_8.10-11:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vaṅga</s>-<s>śastra</s> and others — <s>vaṅga</s> is tin, <s>śastra</s> is iron/steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>); those beginning with these — those [metals]. (GRhtCM 8.10–11:2)

children.text:
kābhiḥ saha puṭo vahet tāpakadaradaśipābhiḥ tāpakaṃ haritāpaṃ daradaṃ
                            hiṅgupaṃ śipā manaḥśipā tābhiḥ // GRhtCM_8.10-11:3 //
children.translated_text: With what should one calcine with fire-cakes? With orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>), cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), and realgar (<s>śilā</s>) — <s>tālaka</s> is orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>); <s>darada</s> is mercury-sulfide (<s>hiṅgula</s>); <s>śilā</s> is realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>) — with these. (GRhtCM 8.10–11:3)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭābhiḥ snehakṣārāmpapavaṇasahitābhiḥ snehaḥ taipaṃ
                            kaṅguṇitumbinyādīnāṃ kṣāraḥ svarjikādiḥ ampaṃ jambīrādi pavaṇāni
                            saindhavādīni etaiḥ sahitābhiḥ // GRhtCM_8.10-11:4 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality? Combined with unctuants, alkalis, acids, and salts — the unctuant is oil of <s>kaṅguṇī</s> (Celastrus paniculatus), <s>tumbinī</s>, and the like; the alkali is <s>svarjikā</s> (sodium carbonate) and the like; the acid is citron (<s>jambīra</s>) and the like; the salts are rock-salt (<s>saindhava</s>) and the like — combined with these. (GRhtCM 8.10–11:4)

children.text:
ekadhātuto dvādaśāṃśād ārabhya yāvatsamakadviguṇatriguṇabhāgāḥ samāpyante
                            tāvatpuṭo vahediti vyaktiḥ // GRhtCM_8.10-11:5 //
children.translated_text: Starting from a twelfth part of a single metal, [increasing] until the equal, double, and triple portions are completed, one should calcine with fire-cakes — this is the explanation. (GRhtCM 8.10–11:5)

children.text: puṭitadhātukṛtyam āha raktetyādi // GRhtCM_8.10-11:6 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states what to do with the calcined metal, with 'red' and so forth. (GRhtCM 8.10–11:6)

children.text:
uktadhāturgarbhitaṃ rasaṃ raktasnehaniṣekaiḥ rakto raktavargaḥ snehaḥ
                            kaṅguṇyādīnāṃ anayorniṣekāḥ siñcanāni taiḥ śeṣaṃ dhātuvarjitaṃ kuryāt
                            iyaṃ rasasya kṛṣṭiḥ rasasya guṇākarṣaṇaṃ punariyaṃ kṛṣṭiḥ rasendraṃ
                            indragopanibhaṃ kurute atiriktavarṇaṃ kurute // GRhtCM_8.10-11:7 //
children.translated_text: The mercury impregnated with the aforementioned metal — with sprinklings of red [group] unctuants — the red group being pomegranate, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, <s>bandhūka</s>, etc.; the unctuants of <s>kaṅguṇī</s> and the like; with their sprinklings — pourings — one should do the rest — [all] except the metal. This is the <s>kṛṣṭi</s> (attraction) of mercury — the drawing out of qualities; and this <s>kṛṣṭi</s> makes mercury resemble an <s>indragopa</s> — it produces an intense color. (GRhtCM 8.10–11:7)

children.text:
kutaḥ cāraṇajāraṇamātrāt punaḥ puṭitadhātūnāṃ cāraṇaṃ ca jāraṇaṃ
                            jīrṇaṃkaraṇaṃ ca tanmātrāt vā cāraṇasya dravyasya jāraṇaṃ tanmātrāt
                            ubhayoḥ pakṣayoreka evārthaḥ paramuktiviśeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_8.10-11:8 //
children.translated_text: From what? Merely through sweeping (<s>cāraṇa</s>) and digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>) — that is, the sweeping and then digesting of the calcined metals; merely from that. Or alternatively, the digesting of the sweeping substance — merely from that. In both interpretations the meaning is the same; the distinction is only in the mode of expression. (GRhtCM 8.10–11:8)

children.text: mercury:: rañjana
children.translated_text: Mercury: coloring (<s>rañjana</s>)

children.text: athavā kevalam amalaṃ kamalaṃ daradena vāpitaṃ kurute /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, pure (<s>amala</s>) copper (<s>kamala</s>) alone, treated with cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), produces —

children.text: triguṇaṃ hi cīrṇajīrṇaṃ lākṣārasasannibhaṃ sūtam // GRht_8.12 //
children.translated_text: when swept and digested three times — mercury resembling lac-juice (<s>lākṣārasa</s>). (GRht 8.12)

children.text: mukhyatvena tāmrapraṃśasanam āha athavetyādi // GRhtCM_8.12:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Praising copper as primary, he says 'alternatively' and so forth. (GRhtCM 8.12:1)

children.text:
athaveti vidhānāntare kevapaṃ śuddhaṃ vānyasaṃyogena varjitaṃ amapaṃ
                            jātapūrvaśodhanaṃ triguṇaṃ cīrṇajīrṇaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ pūrvaṃ cīrṇaṃ
                            cāraṇamāptaṃ paścājjīrṇaṃ jāraṇamāpannaṃ evaṃbhūtaṃ tāmraṃ sūtaṃ
                            pākṣārasasannibhaṃ apaktakaprabhaṃ kurute // GRhtCM_8.12:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Alternatively' — in another procedure; 'pure' (<s>kevala</s>) — alone, devoid of combination with others; 'spotless' (<s>amala</s>) — having undergone prior purification; [swept and] digested three times — one should do so, is the meaning. First swept — having undergone sweeping (<s>cāraṇa</s>); then digested — having undergone digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>). Such copper makes mercury resemble lac-juice (<s>lākṣārasa</s>) — having the luster of lac. (GRhtCM 8.12:2)

children.text: mercury:: rañjana
children.translated_text: Mercury: coloring (<s>rañjana</s>)

children.text: raktagaṇagalitapaśujalabhāvitatāpyagandhakaśilānām /
children.translated_text: With animal-fluid (<s>paśujala</s>, i.e., cow's urine) infused with the red group, used to process <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite), sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), and realgar (<s>śilā</s>),

children.text: ekena vāpitamṛtaṃ kamalaṃ rañjayati rasarājam // GRht_8.13 //
children.translated_text: treated with one [of these], killed copper (<s>kamala</s>) colors the king of <s>rasas</s>. (GRht 8.13)

children.text: vidhyantaramāha raktetyādi // GRhtCM_8.13:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another method, with 'red' and so forth. (GRhtCM 8.13:1)

children.text:
raktagaṇena dāḍimakiṃśukabandhūkādinā pūrvoktena gapitaṃ yat paśujapaṃ
                            gomūtraṃ tena bhāvitā yās tāpyagandhakamanaḥśipās tāsāṃ madhyād ekena
                            tāpyena svarṇamākṣikena vā gandhakena vā śipayā vāpitamṛtaṃ sat kamapaṃ
                            tāmraṃ rasaṃ rañjayati rāgaṃ dadātītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_8.13:2 //
children.translated_text: With the red group — pomegranate, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, <s>bandhūka</s>, and the like, as previously described — the animal-fluid (<s>paśujala</s>), meaning cow's urine, which has been infused [with the red group] — the <s>tāpya</s> (gold-pyrite, <s>svarṇamākṣika</s>), sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), and realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>) that were processed with it; with one among these — either with <s>tāpya</s> (gold-pyrite), or with sulphur, or with realgar — [copper] having been treated [and] killed, the copper (<s>kamala</s>) colors mercury — it gives [it] color, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 8.13:2)

children.text: duration of colouring acc. to substance
children.translated_text: Duration of coloring according to the substance [used]

children.text: bāhyo gandhakarāgo vilulitarāge manaḥśilātāle /
children.translated_text: The coloring from sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>) is external; when the color is unstable, [use] realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>) and orpiment (<s>tāla</s>);

children.text: mākṣikasatvarasakau dvāveva hi rañjane śastau // GRht_8.14 //
children.translated_text: <s>mākṣika</s>-essence (<s>satva</s>) and <s>rasaka</s> (calamine) — these two alone are praised for coloring. (GRht 8.14)

children.text: rāgādhikārigandhakādīn āha // GRhtCM_8.14:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states which substances — sulphur and others — are entitled to [produce lasting] color. (GRhtCM 8.14:1)

children.text:
tatra gandhakaḥ kīdṛśaṃ rāgaṃ dadāti tatsvarūpamāha bāhya ityādi //
                            GRhtCM_8.14:2 //
children.translated_text: What kind of color does sulphur give? He describes its nature, with 'external' and so forth. (GRhtCM 8.14:2)

children.text:
gandhakarāgo bāhyo bahirbhavaḥ punarmanaḥśipātāpe manaḥśipā manohvā tāpaṃ
                            haritāpaṃ tāvubhe vipupitarāge cañcaparāge punar mākṣikasatvarasakau
                            svarṇamākṣikasatvakharparikau dvāveva rañjane rasarāge śastau
                            gandhakamanaḥśipātāpebhyaḥ pradhānau atyadhikāvityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_8.14:3 //
children.translated_text: The color from sulphur is external — existing on the surface; again, with realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>) and orpiment (<s>tāla</s>) — <s>manaḥśilā</s> is <s>manohvā</s>; <s>tāla</s> is orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>) — these two have unstable color — flickering color; again, <s>mākṣika</s>-essence and <s>rasaka</s> (calamine) — <s>svarṇamākṣika</s>-essence and calamine (<s>kharpara</s>) — these two alone are praised for coloring — praised for mercury-coloring; [they are] principal — far superior to sulphur, realgar, and orpiment, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 8.14:3)

children.text: rasarañjak (15)
children.translated_text: Mercury-colorant (15)

children.text: kramavṛttau ravirasakau saṃśuddhau mūkamūṣikādhmātau /
children.translated_text: When <s>ravi</s> (copper) and <s>rasaka</s> (calamine) are well-purified and smelted in a sealed crucible (<s>mūkamūṣikā</s>), in the proper sequence,

children.text: triguṇaṃ cīrṇo jīrṇo hemābho jāyate sūtaḥ // GRht_8.15 //
children.translated_text: swept and digested three times, mercury becomes gold-like in appearance. (GRht 8.15)

children.text:
pradhānayostāmrakharparayoḥ kṛtyamāha kramavṛttāvityādi // GRhtCM_8.15:1
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states what should be done with the two principal [agents] — copper and calamine — with 'in proper sequence' and so forth. (GRhtCM 8.15:1)

children.text:
kramavṛttau ravirasakau saṃśuddhau viśeṣavidhānena śodhitau vā
                            uttamajātīyau mūkamūṣikādhmātau andhamūṣāyāṃ dhmātau vahniyogīkṛtau
                            kāryau etattriguṇaṃ yathā syāttathā cīrṇo jīrṇaśca sūtaḥ hemanibho
                            jāyate etena cāraṇamāpannaḥ paścāttenaiva jāraṇām āpanno rasaḥ
                            svarṇaprabho bhavedityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_8.15:2 //
children.translated_text: 'In proper sequence' — <s>ravi</s> (copper) and <s>rasaka</s> (calamine), well-purified — purified by a special procedure, or of the best variety — smelted in a sealed crucible (<s>andhamūṣā</s>) — smelted, meaning subjected to fire — should be prepared; this should be done three times so that [mercury], swept and then digested, becomes gold-like in appearance. By this, having first undergone sweeping (<s>cāraṇa</s>) and then undergoing digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>) by that same [agent], mercury would become gold-lustrous, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 8.15:2)

children.text: rasarañjak (16)
children.translated_text: Mercury-colorant (16)

children.text: atha kṛṣṇābhrakacūrṇaṃ puṭitaṃ raktaṃ bhavettathā sakalam /
children.translated_text: Now, black mica (<s>abhraka</s>) powder, when calcined, becomes red; likewise the whole [quantity] —

children.text: triguṇaṃ cīrṇo jīrṇo hemadrutisannibhaḥ sūtaḥ // GRht_8.16 //
children.translated_text: swept and digested three times, mercury [becomes] like molten gold. (GRht 8.16)

children.text: abhrakayogamāha athetyādi // GRhtCM_8.16:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the method using mica, with 'now' and so forth. (GRhtCM 8.16:1)

children.text:
atha rasakayogānantaraṃ kṛṣṇavarṇābhrakacūrṇaṃ śyāmavarṇābhrakarajaḥ
                            tathā ravirasakavidhānena kharparakeṇa sahitaṃ puṭitaṃ sat sakapaṃ
                            samastaṃ raktaṃ bhavet tadraktabhūtamabhraṃ triguṇaṃ yathā syāttathā
                            cīrṇaḥ cāraṇamāpannas tato jīrṇo jāraṇamāpannaśca san sūto
                            hemadrutisannibhaḥ svarṇadravasadṛśo bhaved ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_8.16:2
                            //
children.translated_text: Now — after the calamine method — black-colored mica powder — the dust of dark-colored mica, in the same manner as the copper-calamine procedure, combined with calamine — when calcined, the whole — the entire [quantity] — becomes red; that reddened mica, swept three times and then digested, mercury becomes like molten gold — resembling liquid gold, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 8.16:2)

children.text: mercury:: rañjana
children.translated_text: Mercury: coloring (<s>rañjana</s>)

children.text: triguṇena mākṣikeṇa tu kanakaṃ ca mṛtaṃ rasakatālayutam /
children.translated_text: Gold, killed with triple [its weight of] <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), combined with calamine (<s>rasaka</s>) and orpiment (<s>tāla</s>),

children.text: paṭusahitaṃ tatpakvaṃ haṇḍikayā yāvadindragopanibham // GRht_8.17 //
children.translated_text: mixed with salt (<s>paṭu</s>), cooked in a pot (<s>haṇḍikā</s>) until [it becomes] like an <s>indragopa</s> (cochineal insect). (GRht 8.17)

children.text: taccūrṇaṃ sūtavare triguṇaṃ cīrṇaṃ hi jīrṇaṃ tu /
children.translated_text: That powder, [applied] to the best of mercuries, swept three times and digested —

children.text: drutahemanibhaḥ sūto rañjati lohāni sarvāṇi // GRht_8.18 //
children.translated_text: mercury becomes like molten gold, and it colors all metals. (GRht 8.18)

children.text: atha svarṇamāraṇamāha triguṇenetyādi // GRhtCM_8.17-18:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now he states the killing of gold, with 'triple' and so forth. (GRhtCM 8.17–18:1)

children.text:
tu punaḥ triguṇena mākṣikeṇa svarṇatriguṇitena tāpyena yatkanakaṃ mṛtaṃ
                            tatkanakaṃ indragopako varṣākāpīno raktavarṇo jīvaviśeṣaḥ tadvannibhā
                            dīptiryasya tadindragopanibhaṃ bhavatīti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_8.17-18:2
                            //
children.translated_text: Again, with triple <s>mākṣika</s> — with <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite) triple the weight of gold — the gold that is killed; that gold [becomes] like an <s>indragopa</s> — the <s>indragopa</s> is a particular red-colored insect appearing during the rainy season — having luster like that — it becomes like an <s>indragopa</s>, is the completion. (GRhtCM 8.17–18:2)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ kanakaṃ mṛtaṃ rasakatāpayutaṃ rasakaṃ kharparaṃ tāpaṃ
                            haritāpaṃ tābhyāṃ yutaṃ miśritaṃ sat yanmṛtaṃ pañcatvamāptamityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_8.17-18:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality is the gold that was killed? Combined with calamine (<s>rasaka</s>, i.e., <s>kharpara</s>) and orpiment (<s>tāla</s>, i.e., <s>haritāla</s>) — mixed with these — [the gold] that was killed, meaning that reached the state of death (<s>pañcatva</s>), is the meaning. (GRhtCM 8.17–18:3)

children.text:
punaḥ paṭusahitaṃ pavaṇamiśritaṃ punar haṇḍikayā bhājanena pakvaṃ
                            vahnipuṭitaṃ tadapi pūrvavat // GRhtCM_8.17-18:4 //
children.translated_text: Again, mixed with salt (<s>paṭu</s>) — combined with salt (<s>lavaṇa</s>); again, cooked in a pot (<s>haṇḍikā</s>) — a vessel — cooked, meaning fire-calcined; that too is as before. (GRhtCM 8.17–18:4)

children.text:
mṛtakanakacūrṇaṃ sūtavare pārade triguṇaṃ cīrṇaṃ jīrṇaṃ cāritaṃ jāritaṃ
                            ca sat sūto drutahemanibho bhavet gapitasvarṇaprabha ityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_8.17-18:5 //
children.translated_text: The killed-gold powder, [applied] to the best of mercuries — to <s>pārada</s> — swept and digested three times, mercury would become like molten gold — having the luster of liquefied gold, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 8.17–18:5)

children.text:
evaṃ rañjito rasaḥ sarvapohāni dhātūni kṛtrimākṛtrimāni navavidhāni
                            rañjati svarṇarūpāṇi karotītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_8.17-18:6 //
children.translated_text: Mercury thus colored, colors all metals (<s>lohas</s>) — substances both natural and artificial, the nine types — it makes [them] gold-like, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 8.17–18:6)

children.text: bījjāraṇ kā mahattv
children.translated_text: [Section:] The greatness of seed-digestion (<s>bījajāraṇa</s>)

children.text: patrādaṣṭaguṇaṃ satvaṃ satvādaṣṭaguṇā drutiḥ /
children.translated_text: From leaf (<s>patra</s>), the essence (<s>satva</s>) is eight times [more potent]; from essence, the fluid (<s>druti</s>) is eight times;

children.text: druteraṣṭaguṇaṃ bījaṃ tasmādbījaṃ tu jārayet // GRht_8.19 //
children.translated_text: from fluid, the seed (<s>bīja</s>) is eight times — therefore one should digest [using] the seed. (GRht 8.19)

children.text:
sarveṣāṃ dhāturasānāmuttarottaraṃ viśeṣatvam āha patrādityādi //
                            GRhtCM_8.19:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the progressive superiority of all metals and <s>rasas</s>, with 'from leaf' and so forth. (GRhtCM 8.19:1)

children.text:
patrādaṣṭaguṇaṃ satvaṃ abhrapatre jīrṇe sati rase yo guṇastasmādaṣṭaguṇo
                            guṇastatsatve ityarthaḥ punaḥ sattvāt drutistaddravarūpā aṣṭaguṇā
                            punardruter bījaṃ dhātūparasasaṃyogajanitaṃ pūrvopavarṇitaṃ tadaṣṭaguṇaṃ
                            tataḥ sarvotkṛṣṭatvādbījaṃ jārayennatvanyat // GRhtCM_8.19:2 //
children.translated_text: From the leaf, [the quality of mercury becomes] eightfold in [its] essence — when mica-leaf has been assimilated by mercury, the quality from that [is multiplied]; from that, eightfold quality [arises] in the essence — this is the meaning. Furthermore, from the essence, the dissolution — its liquid form — [is] eightfold. Furthermore, from the dissolution, the seed — produced from the conjunction of metals and subsidiary minerals, as previously described — that [is] eightfold. Therefore, since the seed is the most excellent of all, one should assimilate the seed, not anything else. (GRhtCM 8.19:2)

children.text: bīja (Definition)
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Bīja</s> (Seed/Catalyst) — Definition

children.text: iti rakto+api rasendro bījena vinā na karmakṛdbhavati /
children.translated_text: Thus, even mercury that has been colored (<s>rakta</s>), without the seed, does not become effective in action;

children.text: dvividhaṃ tatpītasitaṃ niyujyate siddhamevaitat // GRht_9.1 //
children.translated_text: that [seed] is of two kinds — yellow and white — [only when] perfected is it to be employed. (GRht 9.1)

children.text: himāṃśuriva dīptyāsau caṇḍāṃśuriva tejasā /
children.translated_text: Like the cool-rayed [moon] in luster, like the hot-rayed [sun] in brilliance,

children.text: niśāhnoriva kartā ca durjanaiḥ sahanāpayaḥ // GRhtCM_9.1:1 //
children.translated_text: and like night and day in action — [yet] intolerable to the wicked. (GRhtCM 9.1:1)

children.text: nirvāpaṇaviśeṣeṇa tadvadvarṇaṃ bhavedyadā /
children.translated_text: When, through a special quenching process, it attains such color,

children.text: mṛdupaṃ citrasaṃskāraṃ tadbījamiti kathyate // GRhtCM_9.1:2 //
children.translated_text: soft, variegated in treatment — that is called the 'seed.' (GRhtCM 9.1:2)

children.text: iti paribhāṣā // GRhtCM_9.1:3 //
children.translated_text: Thus is the definition. (GRhtCM 9.1:3)

children.text: bījapraśaṃsanamāha itītyādi // GRhtCM_9.1:4 //
children.translated_text: He praises the seed with 'iti' and so forth. (GRhtCM 9.1:4)

children.text:
ityuktavidhānena rakto+api rasendro bījena vinā karmakṛnna bhavati
                            bījenaiva karmakārī syādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_9.1:5 //
children.translated_text: By the procedure thus described, even mercury that has been colored — the lord of mercury — without the seed does not become effective in action; only through the seed does it become capable of action — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 9.1:5)

children.text:
tadbījaṃ dvividhaṃ dviprakāraṃ pītasitaṃ ekaṃ pītaṃ aparaṃ sitaṃ śvetaṃ
                            svarṇarūpyakriyāyogyam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_9.1:6 //
children.translated_text: That seed is of two kinds — of two varieties — yellow and white: one is yellow, the other is white, meaning suited for the operations of gold and silver [respectively] — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 9.1:6)

children.text:
tadbījaṃ siddhaṃ sarvapakṣaṇopetaṃ rase pārade niyojyaṃ nāsiddhamiti //
                            GRhtCM_9.1:7 //
children.translated_text: That seed, [when] perfected — endowed with all the [required] characteristics — should be employed in mercury; [but] not when unperfected. (GRhtCM 9.1:7)

children.text: bīja:: śodhana necessary
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Bīja</s> — purification necessary

children.text: tasya viśuddhirbahudhā gaganarasoparasalohacūrṇaiś ca /
children.translated_text: Its purification [is done] in many ways, with powders of mica, minerals (<s>rasa</s>), subsidiary minerals (<s>uparasa</s>), and metals;

children.text: dvividhaṃ bījaṃ tairapi nāśuddhaiḥ śudhyate vai tat // GRht_9.2 //
children.translated_text: the seed is twofold, [yet] even by those [substances], when unpurified, it is not purified. (GRht 9.2)

children.text: tasyetyādi // GRhtCM_9.2:1 //
children.translated_text: He says 'tasya' (its) and so forth. (GRhtCM 9.2:1)

children.text:
tasya bījasya viśuddhiḥ śodhanaṃ bahudhā bahuprakāraiḥ kṛtvā
                            rasoparasadhātūnāṃ bahuvidhatvāt // GRhtCM_9.2:2 //
children.translated_text: The purification — the cleansing — of that seed [is done] in many ways, in many procedures, because of the multiplicity of minerals, subsidiary minerals, and metals. (GRhtCM 9.2:2)

children.text:
kaiḥ kṛtvā gaganarasapohacūrṇaiḥ gaganamabhraṃ rasā vaikrāntādayo+aṣṭau
                            vakṣyamāṇāḥ uparasā gandhakādayaḥ pohā dhātavaḥ teṣāṃ cūrṇāni taiḥ //
                            GRhtCM_9.2:3 //
children.translated_text: With what? With powders of mica, minerals, and metals — <s>gagana</s> is mica; <s>rasas</s> are the eight beginning with <s>vaikrānta</s>, to be described; <s>uparasas</s> are those beginning with sulfur; <s>lohas</s> are metals; their powders — with those. (GRhtCM 9.2:3)

children.text:
ca punaḥ tair gaganarasoparasapohacūrṇair aśuddhaiḥ
                            śuddhivarjitaistadbījaṃ na śudhyate śuddhihīnaṃ syāt kāraṇānurūpaṃ
                            kāryamitinyāyāt // GRhtCM_9.2:4 //
children.translated_text: And furthermore, by those — powders of mica, minerals, subsidiary minerals, and metals — when unpurified, lacking purification, that seed is not purified, would remain devoid of purity; because [of the principle that] the effect accords with the cause. (GRhtCM 9.2:4)

children.text: yaḥ punaretaiḥ kurute karmāśuddhairbhavedrasastasya /
children.translated_text: One who furthermore performs operations with these [substances] unpurified — the mercury of such a person

children.text: avyāpakaḥ pataṃgī na rase rasāyane yogyaḥ // GRht_9.3 //
children.translated_text: becomes non-pervading, volatile — not fit for either medicine or <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation). (GRht 9.3)

children.text: aśuddhabījaprabhāvamāha ya ityādi // GRhtCM_9.3:1 //
children.translated_text: He describes the effect of an unpurified seed with 'yaḥ' (one who) and so forth. (GRhtCM 9.3:1)

children.text:
punarviśeṣeṇa yaḥ saṃskārakṛdetairgaganādyair aśuddhaiḥ kṛtvā rasasya
                            karma kurute tasya puruṣasya rasaḥ pārado 'vyāpako 'saraṇaśīpo bhavet
                            pataṅgī ūrdhvagāmī ca bhavet yantrasyādhobhāge na tiṣṭhatītyarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_9.3:2 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore specifically, one who, with these [substances] beginning with mica — unpurified — performs operations upon mercury, the mercury of that person becomes non-pervading — of non-spreading nature — and volatile — rising upward, not remaining in the lower part of the apparatus — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 9.3:2)

children.text: mahārasa
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Mahārasa</s> (Major minerals)

children.text: vaikrāntakāntasasyakamākṣikavimalādridaradarasakāśca /
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s>, <s>kānta</s>, <s>sasyaka</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>vimala</s>, <s>adridara</s> (bitumen), <s>darasa</s> (cinnabar), and <s>rasaka</s> —

children.text: aṣṭau rasāstathaiṣāṃ sattvāni rasāyanāni syuḥ // GRht_9.4 //
children.translated_text: these are the eight <s>rasas</s> (major minerals); and their essences are [used for] <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation). (GRht 9.4)

children.text: ete vakṣyamāṇā aṣṭau rasāḥ rasasaṃjñakāḥ syuḥ // GRhtCM_9.4:1 //
children.translated_text: These eight, to be described, are designated by the name <s>rasa</s> (major mineral). (GRhtCM 9.4:1)

children.text:
ete ke vaikrāntakāntasasyakamākṣikavimapādridaradarasakāś ceti vaikrāntaṃ
                            vajrabhūmijaṃ rajaḥ kāntaṃ cumbakotthaṃ sasyakaṃ capapaṃ mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ
                            vimapā raupyamākṣikaṃ adri śipājatu daradaṃ hiṅgupaṃ rasakaḥ kharparikaḥ
                            ete rasasaṃjñikā jñeyāḥ // GRhtCM_9.4:2 //
children.translated_text: Which are these? '<s>Vaikrānta</s>, <s>kānta</s>, <s>sasyaka</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>vimala</s>, <s>adridara</s>, <s>darada</s>, and <s>rasaka</s>' — <s>vaikrānta</s> is diamond-earth dust; <s>kānta</s> is that produced from lodestone; <s>sasyaka</s> is <s>capalā</s> (vitriol); <s>mākṣika</s> is iron pyrite; <s>vimala</s> is silver-pyrite; <s>adri</s> is bitumen; <s>darada</s> is cinnabar; <s>rasaka</s> is calamine — these should be known as bearing the designation <s>rasa</s>. (GRhtCM 9.4:2)

children.text:
tathā eṣāṃ satvāni sārāṇi rasāyanāni jarāvyādhināśanāni syuriti //
                            GRhtCM_9.4:3 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, their essences — their extracts — are [used for] <s>rasāyana</s> — they destroy old age and disease. (GRhtCM 9.4:3)

children.text: uparasa
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Uparasa</s> (Subsidiary minerals)

children.text: gandhakagairikaśilālakṣitikhecaramañjanaṃ ca kaṃkuṣṭham / GRht_9.5ab
children.translated_text: Sulfur, ochre (<s>gairika</s>), realgar (<s>śilā</s>), orpiment (<s>āla</s>), alum (<s>kṣiti</s>), green vitriol (<s>khecara</s>), collyrium (<s>añjana</s>), and <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> (red arsite). (GRht 9.5ab)

children.text: uparasasaṃjñakānāha gandhaketyādi // GRhtCM_9.5ab:1 //
children.translated_text: He states those designated as <s>uparasa</s> (subsidiary mineral) with 'gandhaka' (sulfur) and so forth. (GRhtCM 9.5ab:1)

children.text: idaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ uparasasaṃjñakaṃ syāt // GRhtCM_9.5ab:2 //
children.translated_text: The following, to be described, bears the designation <s>uparasa</s>. (GRhtCM 9.5ab:2)

children.text:
kimidaṃ gandhakagairikaśilālakṣitikhecaram iti gandhakaṃ pratītaṃ
                                gairikaṃ dhātugairikaṃ śilā manohvā ālaṃ haritālaṃ kṣitiḥ sphaṭikā
                                khecaraṃ kāsīsaṃ etat sarvamiti ca punaḥ añjanaṃ nīlāñjanaṃ punaḥ
                                kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ viraṅgaṃ ityaṣṭau uparasasaṃjñakā ityarthaḥ //
                                GRhtCM_9.5ab:3 //
children.translated_text: What is this? 'Sulfur, ochre, realgar, orpiment, alum, green vitriol' — sulfur is well-known; <s>gairika</s> is mineral ochre; <s>śilā</s> is <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar); <s>āla</s> is <s>haritāla</s> (orpiment); <s>kṣiti</s> is <s>sphaṭikā</s> (alum); <s>khecara</s> is <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol); all this [is indicated by] 'iti.' Furthermore, <s>añjana</s> is blue collyrium; furthermore, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is <s>viraṅga</s> (red arsenic) — these eight bear the designation <s>uparasa</s> — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 9.5ab:3)

children.text: sāraloha
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Sāraloha</s> (Noble metals)

children.text: uparasasaṃjñakamidaṃ syāt śikhiśaśinau sāralohākhyau // GRht_9.5cd //
children.translated_text: This [above] bears the designation <s>uparasa</s>; <s>śikhi</s> (fire = gold) and <s>śaśin</s> (moon = silver) are called <s>sāraloha</s> (noble metals). (GRht 9.5cd)

children.text: pūtiloha
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Pūtiloha</s> (Base metals)

children.text: tāmrāratīkṣṇakāntābhrasattvalohāni vaṅganāgau ca /
children.translated_text: Copper, brass (<s>āra</s>), steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), <s>kānta</s> (magnetic iron), mica-essence (<s>abhrasattva</s>), iron (<s>loha</s>), tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), and lead (<s>nāga</s>) —

children.text: kathitāstu pūtisaṃjñāsteṣāṃ saṃśodhanaṃ kāryam // GRht_9.6 //
children.translated_text: these are declared to bear the designation <s>pūti</s> (base); their purification should be performed. (GRht 9.6)

children.text:
śikhiśaśinau svarṇatārakau sārapohākhyau sārapohasaṃjñakāvityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_9.5-6:1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śikhi</s> and <s>śaśin</s> — gold and silver — are called <s>sāraloha</s> — bear the designation <s>sāraloha</s> (noble metal) — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 9.5-6:1)

children.text: pūtipohasaṃjñānāha tāmretyādi // GRhtCM_9.5-6:2 //
children.translated_text: He states those bearing the designation <s>pūtiloha</s> (base metal) with 'tāmra' (copper) and so forth. (GRhtCM 9.5-6:2)

children.text:
tāmrāratīkṣṇakāntābhrasatvapohānīti tāmraṃ nepāpakaṃ āraṃ rājarītiḥ
                            tīkṣṇaṃ sāraṃ kāntaṃ cumbakodbhavaṃ abhrasatvaṃ gaganasāraṃ pohaṃ muṇḍaṃ
                            etānīti punarvaṅganāgau ete pūtisaṃjñakāḥ kathitāḥ // GRhtCM_9.5-6:3
                            //
children.translated_text: 'Copper, brass, steel, <s>kānta</s>, mica-essence, and iron' — copper is <s>nepālaka</s> (Nepali copper); <s>āra</s> is <s>rājarīti</s> (brass); <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is steel; <s>kānta</s> is that produced from lodestone; <s>abhrasattva</s> is mica-extract; <s>loha</s> is <s>muṇḍa</s> (wrought iron) — these [are listed], and furthermore tin and lead — these bear the designation <s>pūti</s> (base), as stated. (GRhtCM 9.5-6:3)

children.text:
teṣāṃ pūtipohasaṃjñakānāṃ śodhanaṃ samyaṅmapāpanayanaṃ kāryamiti //
                            GRhtCM_9.5-6:4 //
children.translated_text: The purification — the proper removal of impurity — of those bearing the designation <s>pūtiloha</s> should be performed. (GRhtCM 9.5-6:4)

children.text: ṣaḍlavaṇa
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Ṣaḍlavaṇa</s> (Six salts)

children.text: sauvarcalasaindhavakacūlikasāmudraromakabiḍāni / GRht_9.7ab
children.translated_text: <s>Sauvarcala</s> (sochal salt), <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt), <s>cūlika</s> (vitreous salt), <s>sāmudra</s> (sea salt), <s>romaka</s> (Romaka salt), and <s>biḍa</s> (a special salt). (GRht 9.7ab)

children.text: lavaṇakṣārasaṃjñe āha sauvarcaletyādi // GRhtCM_9.7ab:1 //
children.translated_text: He states those designated as salts and alkalis with '<s>sauvarcala</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 9.7ab:1)

children.text:
etāni vakṣyamāṇāni lavaṇasaṃjñānyāhuḥ ācāryāḥ iti śeṣaḥ //
                                GRhtCM_9.7ab:2 //
children.translated_text: The following, to be described, bear the designation 'salt' — the masters declare — this is the complement. (GRhtCM 9.7ab:2)

children.text:
kāni sauvarcalasaindhavakacūlikasāmudraromakabiḍānīti sauvarcalaṃ
                                rucakaṃ saindhavaṃ maṇikamanthāhvayaṃ cūlikaṃ kācalavaṇaṃ sāmudraṃ
                                kṣārābdhijaṃ romakaṃ pratītaṃ biḍaṃ lavaṇaviśeṣaḥ etānīti //
                                GRhtCM_9.7ab:3 //
children.translated_text: Which are they? '<s>Sauvarcala</s>, <s>saindhava</s>, <s>cūlika</s>, <s>sāmudra</s>, <s>romaka</s>, and <s>biḍa</s>' — <s>sauvarcala</s> is <s>rucaka</s> (appetizing salt); <s>saindhava</s> is also called <s>maṇikamantha</s>; <s>cūlika</s> is vitreous salt; <s>sāmudra</s> is that born from the alkaline ocean; <s>romaka</s> is well-known; <s>biḍa</s> is a special variety of salt — these [are the six]. (GRhtCM 9.7ab:3)

children.text: trikṣāra
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Trikṣāra</s> (Three alkalis)

children.text: ṣaṭ lavaṇānyetāni tu svarjīṭaṅkaṇayavakṣārāḥ // GRht_9.7cd //
children.translated_text: These are the six salts; <s>svarjī</s> (sodium carbonate), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), and barley-alkali [are the three alkalis]. (GRht 9.7cd)

children.text:
punaḥ svarjī sarjikā ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ yavakṣāraḥ pratītaḥ ete kṣārāḥ
                            kṣārasaṃjñikāḥ rasakarmaṇi ityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_9.7cd:1 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>svarjī</s> is <s>sarjikā</s> (sodium carbonate); <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgya</s> (borax); <s>yavakṣāra</s> (barley-alkali) is well-known — these are the alkalis, bearing the designation of alkali — 'in alchemical operations' is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 9.7cd:1)

children.text: uparasa:: śodhana, sattvapātana
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Uparasa</s> — purification and essence-extraction

children.text: sūryāvartaḥ kadalī vandhyā kośātakī ca suradālī /
children.translated_text: <s>Sūryāvarta</s> (sunflower), <s>kadalī</s> (plantain), <s>vandhyā</s> (barren [Kośātakī]), <s>kośātakī</s> (luffa), and <s>suradālī</s> (Devadālī);

children.text: śigruśca vajrakando nīrakaṇā kākamācī ca // GRht_9.8 //
children.translated_text: <s>śigru</s> (drumstick tree), <s>vajrakanda</s> (a tuberous plant), <s>nīrakaṇā</s> (water-long-pepper), and <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade). (GRht 9.8)

children.text: āsāmekarasena tu lavaṇakṣārāmlabhāvitā bahuśaḥ /
children.translated_text: With the juice of one of these, [the minerals], treated many times with salt, alkali, and sour [substances],

children.text: śudhyanti rasoparasā dhmātāḥ sattvāni muñcanti // GRht_9.9 //
children.translated_text: become purified; when smelted, they release their essences. (GRht 9.9)

children.text: sadrāvakaṃ śodhakagaṇamāha sūryāvarta ityādi // GRhtCM_9.8-9:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the group of purifying and dissolving [agents] together with the solvent with '<s>sūryāvarta</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 9.8-9:1)

children.text:
sūryaṃ prati āvartako bhramaṇaṃ yasyetyevaṃvidhaḥ kadapī rambhā vandhyā
                            phaparahitā karkoṭī kośātakī jāpinī suradāpī devadāpī śigruḥ
                            saubhāñjanaṃ vajrakando vadasūraṇakandaḥ nīrakaṇā japapippapī kākamācī
                            vāyasī iti gaṇaḥ śodhanadrāvaṇayogya iti // GRhtCM_9.8-9:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sūryāvarta</s> — that which revolves toward the sun — is such a [plant]; <s>kadalī</s> is plantain; <s>vandhyā</s> is fruit-less <s>karkoṭī</s>; <s>kośātakī</s> is <s>jālinī</s> (luffa); <s>suradālī</s> is <s>devadālī</s>; <s>śigru</s> is <s>saubhāñjana</s> (drumstick); <s>vajrakanda</s> is <s>valasūraṇa</s>-tuber; <s>nīrakaṇā</s> is aquatic long pepper; <s>kākamācī</s> is <s>vāyasī</s> (black nightshade) — this group is suitable for purification and dissolution. (GRhtCM 9.8-9:2)

children.text:
śodhanadrāvakāṇāṃ śodhanadrāvaṇavidhānam āha āsāmityādi // GRhtCM_9.8-9:3
                            //
children.translated_text: He states the method of purification and dissolution with the purifying-dissolving [agents] with 'āsām' (of these) and so forth. (GRhtCM 9.8-9:3)

children.text:
āsāṃ pūrvauṣadhīnāṃ madhyāt ekarasena ekasyā rasena rasoparasā
                            vaikrāntādayo+aṣṭau rasāḥ gandhakādayo 'ṣṭāvuparasāḥ bahuśo+anekavāraṃ
                            bhāvitā gharmapuṭitāḥ kāryāḥ punarpavaṇakṣārāmpabhāvitāśca pavaṇāni
                            sauvarcapādīni ṣaṭ kṣārāḥ svarjikādayaḥ ampā jambīrādayaḥ tairbahuvāraṃ
                            bhāvitās tīvragharmapuṭitā rasoparasāḥ śudhyanti doṣavarjitā bhavanti
                            punaste dhmātāḥ santaḥ satvāni svīyasārāṇi muñcanti tyajantīti //
                            GRhtCM_9.8-9:4 //
children.translated_text: Of these — from among the aforementioned herbs — with the juice of one, the minerals and subsidiary minerals — the eight <s>rasas</s> beginning with <s>vaikrānta</s> and the eight <s>uparasas</s> beginning with sulfur — should be treated many times, subjected to heat-treatment. Furthermore, treated with salts, alkalis, and sour substances — the salts are the six beginning with <s>sauvarcala</s>; the alkalis are those beginning with <s>svarjikā</s>; the sour substances are those beginning with lemon — treated many times with these, subjected to intense heat-treatment, the minerals and subsidiary minerals become purified — become free of defects. Furthermore, when they are smelted, they release — give up — their essences, their inherent extracts. (GRhtCM 9.8-9:4)

children.text: vaikrānta:: śodhana
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Vaikrānta</s> — purification

children.text: svinnaṃ sakṣārāmlairdhmātaṃ vaikrāntakaṃ haṭhād dravati / GRht_9.10ab /
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s>, steamed with alkalis and sour [substances], when smelted by force, melts. (GRht 9.10ab)

children.text: rasānāṃ krameṇa śodhanamāha svinnamityādi // GRhtCM_9.10ab:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the purification of the <s>rasas</s> (major minerals) in sequence with 'svinnam' (steamed) and so forth. (GRhtCM 9.10ab:1)

children.text:
sakṣārāmlairvaikrāntakaṃ svinnaṃ dolābhidhānena sveditaṃ kuryāt tat
                                svinnaṃ vaikrāntaṃ haṭhāt prābalyāt dhmātaṃ sat dravati sāraṃ
                                muñcati drutamātraṃ satvanirgamamātrameva śudhyati pūrvasaṃbandhāt
                                dravati // GRhtCM_9.10ab:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s> should be steamed with alkalis and sour [substances] — steamed by the method called <s>dolā</s> (swing-apparatus); that steamed <s>vaikrānta</s>, by force — with vigorous [heat] — when smelted, melts — releases its essence. The moment of melting alone — the moment of essence-emergence alone — constitutes purification, from the connection with the preceding [statement]; [thus] it melts. (GRhtCM 9.10ab:2)

children.text: kānta (= cumbaka):: śodhana
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Kānta</s> (lodestone) — purification

children.text: tad drutamātraṃ śudhyati kāntaṃ śaśaraktabhāvanayā // GRht_9.10cd //
children.translated_text: That, the moment of melting, constitutes purification; <s>kānta</s> [is purified] by treatment with rabbit's blood. (GRht 9.10cd)

children.text: sasyaka:: śodhana
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Sasyaka</s> (vitriol) — purification

children.text: sasyakamapi raktagaṇaiḥ subhāvitaṃ sneharāgasaṃsiktam /
children.translated_text: <s>Sasyaka</s> also, well-treated with the red group [of substances], sprinkled with oil and [red] dye,

children.text: śudhyati vāraiḥ saptabhirataḥ paraṃ yujyate kārye // GRht_9.11 //
children.translated_text: becomes purified in seven rounds; thereafter it is suitable for use. (GRht 9.11)

children.text: taccāha sasyakamityādi // GRhtCM_9.10-11:1 //
children.translated_text: He states that with '<s>sasyakam</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 9.10-11:1)

children.text:
sasyakamapi capapamapi raktagaṇairdāḍimakiṃśukabandhūkādibhiḥ subhāvitaṃ
                            kuryāt // GRhtCM_9.10-11:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sasyaka</s> — that is, <s>capalā</s> (vitriol) — should be well-treated with the red group — pomegranate, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, <s>bandhūka</s>, and the like. (GRhtCM 9.10-11:2)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ sneharāgasaṃsiktaṃ snehaḥ kaṅguṇitumbunyādīnāṃ rāgo
                            raktavarṇadravaḥ tābhyāṃ vahnau taptaṃ sasyakaṃ saṃsiktaṃ secitamiti
                            ghṛtaiḥ saṃsiktaṃ komapaṃ bhāvanāyogyaṃ syāt // GRhtCM_9.10-11:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what specification? Sprinkled with oil and dye — the oil [is] from <s>kaṅguṇī</s>, <s>tumbinī</s>, and the like; the dye [is] a red-colored liquid — heated in fire, the <s>sasyaka</s> [is] sprinkled with these, meaning doused; sprinkled with ghee, [it becomes] soft and suitable for treatment. (GRhtCM 9.10-11:3)

children.text:
katibhirvāraiḥ subhāvitaṃ kuryāt saptabhiḥ saptasaṃkhyākaiḥ //
                            GRhtCM_9.10-11:4 //
children.translated_text: In how many rounds should it be well-treated? In seven — seven in number. (GRhtCM 9.10-11:4)

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ kārye bījādike yujyate // GRhtCM_9.10-11:5 //
children.translated_text: Thereafter, [it becomes] suitable for use in the preparation of seed and the like. (GRhtCM 9.10-11:5)

children.text: vimala, rasaka, darada, mākṣika:: śodhana
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Vimala</s>, <s>rasaka</s>, <s>darada</s>, <s>mākṣika</s> — purification

children.text: kṣāraiḥ snehairādau paścādamlena bhāvitaṃ vimalam /
children.translated_text: <s>Vimala</s> (silver-pyrite), treated first with alkalis and oils, then with sour [substances],

children.text: śudhyati tathā ca rasakaṃ daradaṃ mākṣikamapyevam // GRht_9.12 //
children.translated_text: becomes purified; likewise <s>rasaka</s> (calamine), <s>darada</s> (cinnabar), and <s>mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite) also in the same way. (GRht 9.12)

children.text: taccāha kṣārairityādi // GRhtCM_9.12:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that, with 'by alkalis' and so forth. (GRhtCM 9.12:1)

children.text:
vimapaṃ raupyamākṣikaṃ ādau prathamaṃ kṣāraiḥ svarjikādibhiḥ
                            snehaistaipaiḥ kaṅguṇyādīnāṃ bhāvitaṃ kuryāt paścādampena jambīrādinā
