                            bhāvitaṃ kuryāt evaṃvidhaṃ kṛtaṃ sat śudhyati // GRhtCM_9.12:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vimala</s> — silver-pyrite (<s>raupyamākṣika</s>) — should first be processed with alkalis such as <s>sarjikā</s> (soda) and others, and with oils such as <s>kaṅguṇī</s> (Celastrus) and others; afterwards it should be processed with acid such as lemon and others. Having been made in this manner, it becomes purified. (GRhtCM 9.12:2)

children.text:
tathā tenaiva vidhinā rasakaṃ kharparakaṃ śudhyati daradaṃ hiṅgupaṃ
                            caivaṃ mākṣikamapyeva śudhyati // GRhtCM_9.12:3 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, by that very method, <s>rasaka</s> (zinc ore/calamine) and <s>kharpara</s> (zinc carbonate) become purified; <s>darada</s> (cinnabar) likewise; and <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) also becomes purified in this very manner. (GRhtCM 9.12:3)

children.text: copper:: rañjana, śodhana
children.translated_text: [Section on] copper: <s>rañjana</s> (coloring) and <s>śodhana</s> (purification)

children.text: tanurapi patraṃ liptaṃ lavaṇakṣārāmlaravisnuhikṣīraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Even a thin foil, smeared with salts, alkalis, acids, [juice of] <s>arka</s> (Calotropis), and <s>snuhī</s> (Euphorbia) milk,

children.text: dhmātaṃ nirguṇḍīrasasaṃsiktaṃ bahuśo bhaveddhi raktaṃ ca // GRht_9.13 //
children.translated_text: when heated and repeatedly quenched in <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex negundo) juice, indeed becomes red. (GRht 9.13)

children.text: svarṇarūpyayoḥ śodhanamāha tanurityādi // GRhtCM_9.13:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the purification of gold and silver, with 'thin' and so forth. (GRhtCM 9.13:1)

children.text: pavaṇetyādi // GRhtCM_9.13:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Salts' and so forth: (GRhtCM 9.13:2)

children.text:
pavaṇāni sauvarcapādīni kṣārāḥ svarjikādayaḥ ampāḥ jambīrādayaḥ
                            ravirarkaḥ snuhī sudhā tayoḥ kṣīrāṇi etaiḥ tanurapi sūkṣmamapi patraṃ
                            dapaṃ sārapohākhyayoḥ iti śeṣaḥ piptaṃ dhmātaṃ sat bahuśo+anekavāraṃ
                            nirguṇḍīrase saṃsiktaṃ śephāpīdrave siñcitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_9.13:3
                            //
children.translated_text: Salts — <s>sauvarcala</s> (black salt) and others; alkalis — <s>sarjikā</s> and others; acids — lemon and others; <s>ravi</s> means <s>arka</s> (Calotropis); <s>snuhī</s> means <s>sudhā</s> (Euphorbia); the milks of these two — with these, even a thin — even a fine — foil (<s>patra</s>), a leaf of <s>sāraloha</s> (pure metal), is the completion — having smeared [it] and heated [it], it should be quenched repeatedly — many times — in <s>nirguṇḍī</s> juice — sprinkled in the extract of <s>śephālikā</s> (five-leaved chaste tree). (GRhtCM 9.13:3)

children.text:
tarhi svarṇaṃ rūpyaṃ ca raktaṃ āraktachaviyutaṃ bhavedityarthaḥ
                            caśabdācchudhyati // GRhtCM_9.13:4 //
children.translated_text: Then gold and silver become red — endowed with a deeply red hue, is the meaning; and by the word 'ca' — it also becomes purified. (GRhtCM 9.13:4)

children.text: lead, tin, bronze, copper:: śodhana
children.translated_text: [Section on] lead, tin, bronze, copper: <s>śodhana</s> (purification)

children.text: śudhyati nāgo vaṃgo ghoṣo raviṇā ca vāramapi munibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Nāga</s> (lead), <s>vaṅga</s> (tin), and <s>ghoṣa</s> (bronze), along with copper, [are purified] seven times

children.text: nirguṇḍīrasasekaistanmūlarajaḥ pravāpaiśca // GRht_9.14 //
children.translated_text: by quenching in <s>nirguṇḍī</s> juice, and by casting in the root-powder thereof. (GRht 9.14)

children.text: pohaśodhanamāha śudhyatītyādi // GRhtCM_9.14:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the purification of metals, with 'is purified' and so forth. (GRhtCM 9.14:1)

children.text:
nāgaḥ sīsakaḥ nirguṇḍīrasasekaiḥ śephāpīrasaṃsecanaiḥ śudhyati nirdoṣo
                            bhavati vaṅgaśca śudhyati // GRhtCM_9.14:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nāga</s> — lead — becomes purified by quenching in <s>nirguṇḍī</s> juice — by sprinkling with <s>śephālikā</s> extract — becomes free of defects; and <s>vaṅga</s> (tin) also becomes purified. (GRhtCM 9.14:2)

children.text:
evaṃ raviṇā tāmreṇa saha ghoṣo+api kāṃsyamapi śudhyati // GRhtCM_9.14:3
                            //
children.translated_text: Likewise, <s>ghoṣa</s> — bronze (<s>kāṃsya</s>) — along with copper (<s>ravi</s>, i.e., <s>tāmra</s>), also becomes purified. (GRhtCM 9.14:3)

children.text:
kativāraṃ secanaiḥ munibhiḥ saptasaṃkhyākaiḥ tanmūparajaḥ
                            nirguṇḍīśiphācūrṇaṃ tatpravāpaiḥ gapiteṣu nāgavaṅgaravighoṣeṣu rajo
                            nikṣepaṇaiśca catvāraḥ śudhyantīti // GRhtCM_9.14:4 //
children.translated_text: How many times by quenching? Seven times — [indicated by] the word 'sages' [meaning seven]; and by casting the root-powder of that [nirguṇḍī] — the powder of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> root — by casting [it] into the melted lead, tin, copper, and bronze — by casting the powder — [thus] the four become purified. (GRhtCM 9.14:4)

children.text: tīkṣṇaloha:: rañjana
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>tīkṣṇaloha</s> (iron/steel): <s>rañjana</s> (coloring)

children.text: raktagaṇagalitapaśujalabhāvitapuṭitaṃ hi rajyate tīkṣṇam /
children.translated_text: Processed with the red group (<s>raktagaṇa</s>), melted, steeped in animal-urine, and calcined — <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron) indeed becomes colored.

children.text: tīkṣṇaloha:: śodhana
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>tīkṣṇaloha</s>: <s>śodhana</s> (purification)

children.text: śudhyati kadalīśikhirasabhāvitapuṭitaṃ tribhirvāraiḥ // GRht_9.15 //
children.translated_text: Steeped in <s>kadalī</s> (plantain) and <s>citraka</s> (leadwort) juice and calcined three times, it becomes purified. (GRht 9.15)

children.text: taccāha raktagaṇetyādi // GRhtCM_9.15:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that, with 'red group' and so forth. (GRhtCM 9.15:1)

children.text:
tīkṣṇaṃ sārākhyaṃ raktagaṇagapitapaśujapabhāvitaṃ puṭitaṃ sat raktagaṇena
                            saha gapitaṃ mipitaṃ yat paśujapaṃ gomūtraṃ tena bhāvitaṃ tato
                            vahnipuṭitaṃ sat rajyate rāgamāpnoti // GRhtCM_9.15:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Tīkṣṇa</s> — also called <s>sāra</s> (steel) — processed with the red group, melted, and steeped in animal-urine: melted together with the red group, [then] steeped — saturated — in animal-urine, i.e., cow's urine; thereafter fire-calcined — it acquires color, attains the dye. (GRhtCM 9.15:2)

children.text:
punastīkṣṇaṃ kadapīśikhirasabhāvitapuṭitaṃ vā rambhācitrakarasabhāvitaṃ
                            gharmapuṭitaṃ tato vahnipuṭitaṃ ca sat tribhirvāraiḥ śudhyatītyarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_9.15:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>tīkṣṇa</s> steeped in <s>kadalī</s> (plantain) and <s>citraka</s> (leadwort) juice and calcined — or steeped in <s>rambhā</s> (plantain) and <s>citraka</s> juice and heat-calcined, then fire-calcined — becomes purified in three rounds, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 9.15:3)

children.text: metals:: śodhana
children.translated_text: [Section on] metals: <s>śodhana</s> (purification)

children.text: sarvaṃ śudhyati loho rajyati suragopasannibho vāpāt /
children.translated_text: All metal becomes purified and colored, resembling a <s>suragopa</s> (firefly/cochineal insect), through the casting

children.text: mākṣikadaradena bhṛśaṃ śulvaṃ vā gandhakena mṛtam // GRht_9.16 //
children.translated_text: of <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) and <s>darada</s> (cinnabar) abundantly; or copper is killed by sulphur. (GRht 9.16)

children.text:
sāmānyena sarvapohānāṃ śodhanamāraṇamāha sarva ityādi // GRhtCM_9.16:1
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the general purification and calcination of all metals, with 'all' and so forth. (GRhtCM 9.16:1)

children.text:
sarvo poho dhātuvargaḥ śudhyati mṛtaśca bhavati punaḥ rajyati ca //
                            GRhtCM_9.16:2 //
children.translated_text: All metal — the class of metallic substances — becomes purified and also killed; furthermore, it becomes colored. (GRhtCM 9.16:2)

children.text:
kena bhṛśaṃ atyarthaṃ yathā syāttathā mākṣikadaradena tāpyahiṅgupena
                            kṛtvā yo vāpaḥ gapiteṣu poheṣu mākṣikadaradaprakṣepaṇaṃ tasmāt
                            suragopasaṃnibha indragopasadṛśaḥ sarvo poho bhavet // GRhtCM_9.16:3
                            //
children.translated_text: By what? By <s>mākṣika</s> and <s>darada</s> — <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite) and <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar) — abundantly, i.e., so that there be great [effect]; the casting of <s>mākṣika</s> and <s>darada</s> into the melted metals — by that casting, all metal becomes like a <s>suragopa</s> — resembling the <s>indragopa</s> (cochineal insect). (GRhtCM 9.16:3)

children.text:
vā śupbaṃ tāmraṃ mākṣikadaradavāpena suragopasannibhaṃ syāt vā gandhena
                            gandhakavāpena mṛtamapyeva syādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_9.16:4 //
children.translated_text: Or copper (<s>śulva</s>, i.e., <s>tāmra</s>) would become like <s>suragopa</s> through the casting of <s>mākṣika</s> and <s>darada</s>; or it would also be killed by <s>gandha</s> — by the casting of sulphur — is the meaning. (GRhtCM 9.16:4)

children.text: atha satvanirgamamabhidhāsyate /
children.translated_text: Now the extraction of essence (<s>sattva</s>) will be described.

children.text: sattva:: importance of ~
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>sattva</s>: importance of essence

children.text: vaikrāntakāntasasyakamākṣikavimalādayo vinā satvam /
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s>, <s>kānta</s> (magnetite), <s>sasyaka</s> (vitriol), <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), <s>vimala</s>, and others — without their essence (<s>sattva</s>),

children.text: śuddhā api no dvandve milanti na ca tān raso grasati // GRht_10.1 //
children.translated_text: even when purified, do not combine; nor does mercury consume them. (GRht 10.1)

children.text: dattavānsatataṃ saukhyaṃ śuddhebhyaśca khapaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: He who has always bestowed happiness, and from the purified ones — the destruction,

children.text: duḥkhamṛtyapyamātmānaḥ kopasya samakārakam // GRhtCM_10.1:1 //
children.translated_text: suffering, and death of selves — [this is] equivalent to the work of anger. (GRhtCM 10.1:1)

children.text:
vaikrāntādīnāṃ rasasaṃjñikānāṃ sattvapraśaṃsanam āha vaikrāntamityādi //
                            GRhtCM_10.1:2 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the praise of the essence (<s>sattva</s>) of those called <s>rasa</s> (minerals) such as <s>vaikrānta</s> and others, with '<s>vaikrānta</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 10.1:2)

children.text:
vaikrāntakāntasasyakamākṣikavimapādayaḥ śuddhā api dvandve na mipanti //
                            GRhtCM_10.1:3 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s>, <s>kānta</s>, <s>sasyaka</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>vimala</s>, and others — even when purified — do not combine. (GRhtCM 10.1:3)

children.text:
vaikrāntaṃ vajrabhūmijaṃ rajaḥ kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ sasyakaścapapaḥ mākṣikaṃ
                            tāpyaṃ vimapā raupyamākṣikam ityādayo gandhakādayaścoparasaṃjñakā na
                            mipanti ekaśarīratāṃ nāpnuvanti // GRhtCM_10.1:4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s> is dust born of diamond-earth (<s>vajrabhūmija rajas</s>); <s>kānta</s> is loadstone; <s>sasyaka</s> is vitriol (<s>capala</s>); <s>mākṣika</s> is pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>); <s>vimala</s> is silver-pyrite (<s>raupyamākṣika</s>) — these and others, including <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) and other sub-metals (<s>uparasa</s>), do not combine — do not attain unity of body. (GRhtCM 10.1:4)

children.text: kva dvandve ubhayamepāpe // GRhtCM_10.1:5 //
children.translated_text: Where? In combination — when there is mixture of both [substances]. (GRhtCM 10.1:5)

children.text: punastān śuddhānapi rasaḥ sūto na grasati // GRhtCM_10.1:6 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, mercury (<s>sūta</s>) does not consume them, even when purified. (GRhtCM 10.1:6)
[Unclear passage]

children.text: nāganāsikābhidhānaṃ candrodakam amṛtam āptakāṭhinyam /
children.translated_text: That which is called <s>nāganāsikā</s> (serpent-nose), [which is] moon-water, ambrosia, having attained hardness —

children.text: rasavaikrāntakam evaṃ badhnāti rasaṃ svasattvena // GRht_10.2 //
children.translated_text: such <s>rasavaikrāntaka</s> binds mercury by its own essence. (GRht 10.2)

children.text: śailodaka
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>śailodaka</s> (rock-water)

children.text: nānāvidhasaṃsthānaṃ nirjaraśikhariśikharasambhūtam /
children.translated_text: Of various forms, born on the peaks of the mountains of the immortals,

children.text: dhārodambhasi śreṣṭhaṃ tadaśma śailodakaṃ prāpya // GRht_10.3 //
children.translated_text: that stone, having obtained rock-water in cascading waters, is the best. (GRht 10.3)

children.text: vaikrāntaprādhānyam āha nāgetyādi // GRhtCM_10.2-3:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the preeminence of <s>vaikrānta</s>, with '<s>nāga</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 10.2-3:1)

children.text: evaṃpakṣaṇaṃ vaikrāntakaṃ jñātavyam // GRhtCM_10.2-3:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrāntaka</s> of such characteristics should be known. (GRhtCM 10.2-3:2)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ nāganāsikābhidhānaṃ nāgānāṃ phaṇināṃ nāsikā eva abhidhānaṃ
                            saṃjñā yasya tat // GRhtCM_10.2-3:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what qualities? Called <s>nāganāsikā</s> — of serpents (<s>phaṇins</s>), the nose-like [formation] is its name — that which has this [designation]. (GRhtCM 10.2-3:3)

children.text:
punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ candrodakaṃ candramasaḥ sambandhi yadudakaṃ bapaṃ
                            tasmādevāmṛtaṃ // GRhtCM_10.2-3:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, of what quality? <s>Candrodaka</s> — the water related to the moon — is its strength; from that itself it is 'ambrosia' (<s>amṛta</s>). (GRhtCM 10.2-3:4)

children.text:
āptakāṭhinyaṃ prāptaṃ kāṭhinyaṃ yena pūrvametacca mṛdūtpannamityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_10.2-3:5 //
children.translated_text: 'Having attained hardness' — that which has acquired hardness; previously this was produced soft, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 10.2-3:5)

children.text:
evaṃvidhaṃ rasavaikrāntaṃ rasasaṃjñakaṃ vaikrāntaṃ rasaṃ sūtaṃ badhnāti
                            // GRhtCM_10.2-3:6 //
children.translated_text: Such <s>rasavaikrānta</s> — <s>vaikrānta</s> called <s>rasa</s> (mineral) — binds mercury (<s>sūta</s>). (GRhtCM 10.2-3:6)

children.text: kena svasatvena svīyasāreṇeti // GRhtCM_10.2-3:7 //
children.translated_text: By what? By its own essence (<s>sattva</s>) — by its own extract. (GRhtCM 10.2-3:7)

children.text: vaikrāntaprakāramāha nānetyādi // GRhtCM_10.2-3:8 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the variety of <s>vaikrānta</s>, with 'of various' and so forth. (GRhtCM 10.2-3:8)

children.text:
pūrvamupavarṇitaṃ vaikrāntaṃ nānāvidhasaṃsthānamasti
                            nānāvidhamanekaprakāraṃ saṃsthānaṃ pakṣaṇaṃ yasya tat saṃsthānaṃ
                            vyañjanaṃ piṅgaṃ pakṣaṇaṃ cihnamākṛtiḥ iti mādhavanidānaṃ
                            sitāsitaraktapītavarṇatvān nānāvidhasaṃsthānam ityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_10.2-3:9 //
children.translated_text: The <s>vaikrānta</s> described previously is of various forms — of manifold, i.e., many kinds of appearance; 'appearance' means characteristic, distinguishing mark, color — as stated in <s>Mādhava Nidāna</s>: 'form, mark, color, sign, shape' — because of being white, dark, red, and yellow in color, it is 'of various forms,' is the meaning. (GRhtCM 10.2-3:9)

children.text:
punarnirjaraśikhariśikharasambhūtaṃ nirjarāṇāṃ devānāṃ yaḥ śikharī
                            parvatastasya śikharaṃ śṛṅgaṃ tatra sambhūtam utpannam //
                            GRhtCM_10.2-3:10 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, born on the peaks of the mountains of the immortals — the mountain of the gods (<s>nirjara</s>), its peak (<s>śikhara</s>), i.e., summit — born there, originated [there]. (GRhtCM 10.2-3:10)

children.text:
nānāvidhasaṃsthānaṃ kutaḥ dhārodambhasi dhārābhirudanta unmattamambho
                            yatra samaye tasmin varṣākāpe śaipodakaṃ śipāsaṃbandhi yadudakaṃ japaṃ
                            tat prāpya śreṣṭhaṃ tadaśma vaikrāntābhidhānaṃ nānāvarṇaṃ bhavati yataḥ
                            śipodakasya nānāvidhatvam // GRhtCM_10.2-3:11 //
children.translated_text: Why 'of various forms'? Because in cascading waters — when the waters are excited by streams, at the time when the water is agitated — during the rainy season — having obtained rock-water — the water associated with rock — that stone called <s>vaikrānta</s> becomes of various colors; because rock-water itself is of various kinds. (GRhtCM 10.2-3:11)

children.text: vaikrānta:: sattva:: pātana
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>vaikrānta</s>: essence (<s>sattva</s>): extraction (<s>pātana</s>)

children.text: bhastrādvayena haṭhato dhmātavyaṃ pañcamāhiṣasubaddham /
children.translated_text: It should be forcefully blown with a pair of bellows, [the vaikrānta] well-bound with the five buffalo [products],

children.text: dattvā daśāṃśasvarjikapaṭuṭaṃkaṇaguñjikākṣārān // GRht_10.4 //
children.translated_text: having added one-tenth [parts of] <s>sarjikā</s> (soda), <s>paṭu</s> (salt), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), and <s>guñjikā</s> (wild-liquorice) alkalis. (GRht 10.4)

children.text: tadgacchati kaṭhinatvaṃ muñcati satvaṃ sphuliṅgakākāram /
children.translated_text: It attains hardness and releases its essence in the form of sparks,

children.text: muktānikaraprāyaṃ grāhyaṃ tat kācam adhivarjya // GRht_10.5 //
children.translated_text: resembling a cluster of pearls — that [essence] should be collected, discarding the glass (<s>kāca</s>). (GRht 10.5)

children.text: vaikrāntasatvapātanamāha bhastretyādi // GRhtCM_10.4-5:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the extraction of <s>vaikrānta</s> essence, with 'bellows' and so forth. (GRhtCM 10.4-5:1)

children.text:
tadvaikrāntaṃ pañcamāhiṣasubaddhaṃ dadhidugdhājyamūtraśakṛdbhiḥ
                            pañcasaṃkhyākair māhiṣaiḥ saha subaddhaṃ piṇḍākṛti kṛtaṃ sat
                            bhastrādvayena khappayugmena haṭhato bapāt dhmātavyam // GRhtCM_10.4-5:2
                            //
children.translated_text: That <s>vaikrānta</s>, well-bound with the five buffalo [products] — with the five buffalo-derived [substances]: curd, milk, ghee, urine, and dung — well-bound, i.e., made into a ball-form, should be forcefully — with strength — blown with a pair of bellows, i.e., with two bellows. (GRhtCM 10.4-5:2)

children.text:
kiṃ kṛtvā daśāṃśasarjikapaṭuṭaṅkaṇaguñjikākṣārān dattvā daśāṃśavibhāgena
                            sarjikāpavaṇasaubhāgyaraktikāyavakṣārān piṣṭavaikrānte kṣepyetyarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_10.4-5:3 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? Having added one-tenth proportions of <s>sarjikā</s> (soda), <s>paṭu</s> (salt/<s>saubhāgya</s>), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), and <s>guñjikā</s> (<s>raktikā</s>/wild-liquorice) alkalis, and barley-alkali (<s>yavakṣāra</s>) — [these] should be cast into the ground <s>vaikrānta</s>, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 10.4-5:3)

children.text: dhmātaṃ sat kiṃ syāttadāha tadityādi // GRhtCM_10.4-5:4 //
children.translated_text: When blown, what happens? He states that, with 'it' and so forth. (GRhtCM 10.4-5:4)

children.text:
sphupiṅgakākāraṃ vahnikaṇanibhaṃ satvaṃ sāraṃ muñcati // GRhtCM_10.4-5:5
                            //
children.translated_text: It releases its essence — its extract — in the form of sparks, resembling fire-particles. (GRhtCM 10.4-5:5)

children.text:
punastatsatvaṃ kaṭhinatvaṃ gacchati kaṭhinaṃ syādityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_10.4-5:6 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, that essence attains hardness — becomes hard, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 10.4-5:6)

children.text:
tatsatvaṃ ākārato muktānikaraprāyaṃ mauktikarāśisadṛśaṃ syāt evaṃvidhaṃ
                            satvaṃ kācaṃ adhivarjya dūrīkṛtya tat nirmapaṃ grāhyamityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_10.4-5:7 //
children.translated_text: That essence, in appearance, resembles a cluster of pearls — like a heap of pearls; such essence, discarding the glass (<s>kāca</s>) — having removed [it] — that pure [essence] should be collected, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 10.4-5:7)

children.text: yugmam // GRhtCM_10.4-5:8 //
children.translated_text: [This concludes] the pair [of verses]. (GRhtCM 10.4-5:8)

children.text: vaikrānta:: bandhana of mercury
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>vaikrānta</s>: binding of mercury

children.text: rasavaikrāntakamevaṃ milati dvandvānvitaṃ samaṃ hemnā /
children.translated_text: Such <s>rasavaikrāntaka</s> (mineral-vaikrānta) combines with gold in equal measure, when accompanied by a pair [of substances];

children.text: nirvyūḍhaṃ ghanasatvaṃ tena raso bandhamupayāti // GRht_10.6 //
children.translated_text: the concentrated mica-essence — by that, mercury attains binding. (GRht 10.6)

children.text: vaikrāntasatvayogamāha rasetyādi // GRhtCM_10.6:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the application of <s>vaikrānta</s> essence, with '<s>rasa</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 10.6:1)

children.text:
tadrasavaikrāntakaṃ sattvaṃ hemnā samaṃ svarṇena samabhāgaṃ dvandvānvitaṃ
                            sat dvandvamepāpakauṣadhasahitaṃ sat evamamunā vidhānena mipati rase iti
                            śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_10.6:2 //
children.translated_text: That <s>rasavaikrāntaka</s> — the essence — [combined] with gold in equal measure, i.e., in equal parts with gold, when accompanied by a pair — endowed with the pairing-drug (<s>melāpakauṣadha</s>) — in this very manner, by this procedure, combines — in mercury, is the completion. (GRhtCM 10.6:2)

children.text:
punastena satvena saha ghanasatvamabhrasāraṃ nirvyūḍhaṃ nirvāhitaṃ sat
                            tenobhayasatvasaṃyogena rasaḥ sūto bandhamupayāti bandhanamāpnoti //
                            GRhtCM_10.6:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, with that essence combined with mica-essence (<s>ghanasattva</s>, i.e., <s>abhrasāra</s>), [when] thoroughly processed, by the conjunction of both essences, mercury (<s>sūta</s>) attains fixation (<s>bandhana</s>) — achieves binding. (GRhtCM 10.6:3)

children.text: minerals:: sattvapātana
children.translated_text: Minerals: essence-extraction (<s>sattvapātana</s>)

children.text: vajrābhrakāntasasyakamākṣikaprabhṛtisakaladhātūnām /
children.translated_text: Of diamond, mica (<s>abhraka</s>), lodestone (<s>kānta</s>), <s>sasyaka</s> (blue vitriol), <s>mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite), and all such minerals —

children.text: pātayati satvameṣāṃ piṇḍī dhmātā dṛḍhāṅgāraiḥ // GRht_10.7 //
children.translated_text: the pellet, smelted with strong charcoals, causes the essence (<s>sattva</s>) to fall from them. (GRht 10.7)

children.text: satvapātanavidhānamāha vajretyādi // GRhtCM_10.7:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the procedure for essence-extraction, beginning with 'diamond' and so on. (GRhtCM 10.7:1)

children.text:
dṛḍhāṅgārair iti dṛḍhakathanāt khadirādīnāṃ pūrvoktatvādbhastrādvayena ca
                            dhmātā satī vajrābhrakāntasasyakamākṣikaprabhṛtisakapadhātūnāṃ
                            vajrasaṃjñakaṃ yadabhraṃ tadvajrābhraṃ kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ sasyakaṃ capapā
                            mākṣikaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ itiprabhṛtayaḥ sakapadhātavaḥ sarvoparasāsteṣāṃ
                            piṇḍī satvaṃ pātayati // GRhtCM_10.7:2 //
children.translated_text: 'With strong charcoals' — because of the emphatic mention of 'strong,' [charcoals] of <s>khadira</s> (Acacia catechu) and the like as previously stated, and smelted with a pair of bellows, the pellet [extracts essence] of diamond, mica, lodestone, <s>sasyaka</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, and all such minerals — 'diamond-mica' (<s>vajrābhraka</s>) means mica known by the designation 'diamond'; <s>kānta</s> is lodestone; <s>sasyaka</s> is copper-sulfate; <s>mākṣika</s> is gold-pyrite — those beginning with these constitute all the minerals, meaning all the sub-metals; the pellet causes their essence to fall. (GRhtCM 10.7:2)

children.text: mākṣika:: sattva:: special alchem. potency
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite): essence — special alchemical potency

children.text: hitvā mākṣikasatvaṃ nānyeṣāṃ śaktirasti lohaghnī /
children.translated_text: Except for <s>mākṣika</s>-essence, no other [essence] has the power to destroy metals;

children.text: na patati tāvatsatvaṃ bhastrānte na yāvad āhriyet // GRht_10.8 //
children.translated_text: the essence does not fall so long as the bellows are not brought to [proximity at] the end. (GRht 10.8)

children.text:
śaktimattvena mākṣikasatvapraśaṃsanam āha hitvetyādi // GRhtCM_10.8:1
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the praise of <s>mākṣika</s>-essence on account of its potency, beginning with 'except' and so on. (GRhtCM 10.8:1)

children.text:
mākṣikasatvaṃ tāpyasāraṃ hitvā tyaktvā anyeṣāṃ rasoparasānāṃ śaktiḥ
                            sāmarthyaṃ nāsti // GRhtCM_10.8:2 //
children.translated_text: Except for <s>mākṣika</s>-essence — the essence of pyrite (<s>tāpyasāra</s>) — setting aside [that], the other sub-metals and <s>rasas</s> do not have the power — the capacity. (GRhtCM 10.8:2)

children.text: kiṃbhūtā śaktiḥ pohaghnīti pohān hantīti vigrahaḥ // GRhtCM_10.8:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what nature is [that] power? 'Metal-destroying' (<s>loha-ghnī</s>) — its analysis is: '[that which] destroys metals.' (GRhtCM 10.8:3)

Furthermore, the essence does not fall so long as the bellows are not brought near — not made to reach the vicinity of the essence; therefore, without a small fire, the essence does not come forth — that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 10.8:4)

children.text: mākṣika:: sattva:: phys. properties
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite): essence — physical properties

children.text: raktaṃ mṛdu nāgasamaṃ satvaṃ yasmāddhi mākṣikātpatitam /
children.translated_text: Red, soft, resembling lead (<s>nāga</s>) — the essence that has fallen from <s>mākṣika</s>;

children.text: gandhāśmano+api tadvatkāryaṃ yatnena mṛdubhāvam // GRht_10.9 //
children.translated_text: likewise from <s>gandhāśman</s> (sulphur-stone), one should carefully make it soft. (GRht 10.9)

children.text:
mākṣikasatvam udāsyānyasatvapravṛttim āha raktamityādi // GRhtCM_10.9:1
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Setting aside <s>mākṣika</s>-essence, he states the procedure for other essences, beginning with 'red' and so on. (GRhtCM 10.9:1)

children.text:
raktaṃ pohitaṃ nāgasamaṃ sīsakatupyaṃ mṛdu komapaṃ evaṃvidhaṃ satvaṃ
                            yasmāddhetor mākṣikāt patati tāpyāt nirgacchati tadvattasmāddhetor vā
                            tasmādvidhānataḥ gandhāśmano gandhakasya yatnena mṛdubhāvaṃ kāryaṃ yathā
                            gandhako+api mṛdurbhavatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_10.9:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Red' means copper-colored; 'resembling lead' means similar to lead or tin; 'soft' means tender — such is the essence that falls — emerges — from <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite); for that reason, or in that manner, by proper procedure, one should make sulphur (<s>gandhāśman</s>) soft — meaning that sulphur also becomes soft; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 10.9:2)

children.text: mākṣika:: sattva:: pātana
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite): essence — extraction (<s>pātana</s>)

children.text: lavaṇāmlena supuṭitaṃ mākṣikamamlena marditaṃ vidhinā /
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s>, well-sealed (<s>supuṭita</s>) with salt and acid, ground with acid by the proper method —

children.text: muñcati soṣṇe grāsam āyasapātre tu piṣṭikā bhavati // GRht_10.10 //
children.translated_text: it releases its morsel while hot; in an iron vessel, it becomes a <s>piṣṭikā</s> (cake). (GRht 10.10)

children.text: mākṣikasatvavidhānamāha pavaṇetyādi // GRhtCM_10.10:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the procedure for <s>mākṣika</s>-essence, beginning with 'salt' and so on. (GRhtCM 10.10:1)

children.text:
mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ pavaṇāmpena pavaṇaṃ mukhyatvāt granthāntarasāmyācca
                            saindhavaṃ ampo jambīrādiḥ tena marditaṃ punarampena jambīrādinā vidhinā
                            uktarītyā puṭitaṃ vahnau pratāpitaṃ sat muñcati pūrvaśpokasaṃbandhāt
                            sattvaṃ iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_10.10:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> — pyrite — [treated] with salt and acid: 'salt' — because of its primacy, and in agreement with other treatises — is rock-salt (<s>saindhava</s>); 'acid' is citron (<s>jambīra</s>) and the like; ground with that, then with acid — with citron and such — by the proper method, in the stated manner, sealed — heated in fire — it releases — from the connection with the preceding [verse], the essence; this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 10.10:2)

children.text: itthaṃ patitaṃ satvaṃ grāhyam // GRhtCM_10.10:3 //
children.translated_text: The essence that has fallen in this manner should be collected. (GRhtCM 10.10:3)

children.text: pavaṇāmpena gandhakamapi mṛdu syāt // GRhtCM_10.10:4 //
children.translated_text: With salt and acid, sulphur too becomes soft. (GRhtCM 10.10:4)

children.text:
tu punaḥ soṣṇe āyasapātre vahnau tāpite pohapātre piṣṭikā bhavati
                            raktavarṇarajorūpety arthaḥ // GRhtCM_10.10:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, 'while hot' — in an iron vessel heated in fire, a <s>piṣṭikā</s> (cake) forms — meaning [it takes the form of] a red-colored powder; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 10.10:5)

children.text: sattva:: colour of diff. ~
children.translated_text: Essence: color of different [minerals]

children.text: tutthāddhi tāpyajasamaṃ samasṛṣṭaṃ patati vai satvam /
children.translated_text: From <s>tuttha</s> (blue vitriol) indeed, the essence falls resembling pyrite-essence (<s>tāpyaja</s>), well-blended;

children.text: abhravaikrāntakāntaprabhṛtīnāṃ tatra lohanibham // GRht_10.11 //
children.translated_text: of mica (<s>abhra</s>), <s>vaikrānta</s>, lodestone (<s>kānta</s>), and the like — therefrom [the essence is] iron-colored. (GRht 10.11)

children.text: tutthādīnāṃ satvapātanamāha tutthādityādi // GRhtCM_10.11:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the essence-extraction of <s>tuttha</s> and others, beginning with '<s>tuttha</s>' and so on. (GRhtCM 10.11:1)

children.text:
tutthāt tutthaṃ śikhigrīvaṃ tasmāt tāpyajasamamiti mākṣikasatvavat
                            mākṣikasatvavidhānenāsya satvapāta ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_10.11:2 //
children.translated_text: From <s>tuttha</s> — <s>tuttha</s> is peacock-necked [in color]; from that, 'resembling pyrite-essence' means by the same procedure as <s>mākṣika</s>-essence extraction — that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 10.11:2)

children.text:
samasṛṣṭaṃ samaṃ tāpyena tupyaṃ varṇamārdavābhyāṃ sṛṣṭaṃ
                            kathitamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_10.11:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Well-blended' means equal to pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>) — described as comparable in color and softness; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 10.11:3)

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ tutthakasatvaṃ patati // GRhtCM_10.11:4 //
children.translated_text: Such <s>tuttha</s>-essence falls. (GRhtCM 10.11:4)

children.text:
abhraketyādi abhrakaṃ pratītaṃ vaikrāntaṃ rasavaikrāntaṃ kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ
                            itiprabhṛtīnām ityādīnāṃ tattvaṃ patrasatvapātanayoge pohanibhaṃ
                            muṇḍavarṇam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_10.11:5 //
children.translated_text: 'Mica' and so on — mica is well-known; <s>vaikrānta</s> is mercury-<s>vaikrānta</s>; <s>kānta</s> is lodestone — the essence of these and similar [minerals], through the procedure of leaf-essence extraction, is iron-colored — of the color of iron; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 10.11:5)

children.text: svarṇamākṣika (?):: sattvapātana (?)
children.translated_text: Gold-pyrite (<s>svarṇamākṣika</s>): essence-extraction

children.text: strīvajrīdugdhabhāvitameraṇḍasnehabhāvitaṃ śataṃ dhmātam /
children.translated_text: Steeped in the milk of female <s>vajrī</s> (Euphorbia), and steeped in castor oil (<s>eraṇḍa-sneha</s>), smelted a hundred times —

children.text:
evaṃ tribhiriha vāraiḥ śulvasamaṃ bhavati rañjakaṃ haimam //
                                GRht_10.12 //
children.translated_text: thus, with three rounds here, it becomes copper-like, a colorant, [producing] gold. (GRht 10.12)

children.text: punarmākṣikavidhānāntaram āha strītyādi /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another procedure for <s>mākṣika</s>, beginning with 'female' and so on.

children.text:
tāpyaṃ strīvajrīdugdhabhāvitaṃ strī nārī vajrī sehuṇḍaḥ tayordugdhaṃ tena
                            bhāvitaṃ gharmapuṭitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_10.12:1 //
children.translated_text: Pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>), steeped in the milk of female <s>vajrī</s> — 'female' means woman, '<s>vajrī</s>' is <s>sehuṇḍa</s> (Euphorbia) — steeped in their milk, one should subject it to sun-calcination (<s>gharmapuṭita</s>). (GRhtCM 10.12:1)

children.text:
punareraṇḍasnehena śataṃ śatavāraṃ bhāvitaṃ ca kuryāt // GRhtCM_10.12:2
                            //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, steeped in castor oil (<s>eraṇḍa-sneha</s>) a hundred times — one hundred rounds — one should prepare it. (GRhtCM 10.12:2)

children.text:
tato vāraistribhireva dhmātaṃ sat haimaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ tasyedaṃ haimaṃ
                            satvaṃ śupbasamaṃ tāmranibhaṃ bhavati rañjakaṃ rase rāgadāyī
                            syātkanake'pi ca // GRhtCM_10.12:3 //
children.translated_text: Then, smelted with just three rounds, the gold-<s>mākṣika</s> (<s>svarṇamākṣika</s>) — its essence (<s>haima sattva</s>) becomes copper-like — resembling copper — and becomes a colorant — it would give color to mercury, and to gold as well. (GRhtCM 10.12:3)

children.text: mākṣika, rasaka:: sattva:: pātana
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> (pyrite), <s>rasaka</s> (calamine): essence — extraction (<s>pātana</s>)

children.text: kadalīrasaśatabhāvitamadhvairaṇḍatailaparipakvam /
children.translated_text: Steeped a hundred times in plantain (<s>kadalī</s>) juice, cooked thoroughly in honey and castor oil —

children.text: tāpyaṃ muñcati satvaṃ rasakaṃ caivaṃ trisantāpaiḥ // GRht_10.13 //
children.translated_text: pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>) releases its essence; likewise <s>rasaka</s> (calamine), with three heatings. (GRht 10.13)

children.text: vidhyantaramāha kadapītyādi // GRhtCM_10.13:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another method, beginning with 'plantain' and so on. (GRhtCM 10.13:1)

children.text:
tāpyaṃ mākṣikaṃ kadapīrasaśatabhāvitamadhvairaṇḍataipaparipakvam iti
                            prathamaṃ rambhādraveṇa śatavāraṃ bhāvitaṃ paścāt madhvairaṇḍataipābhyāṃ
                            saha paripakvaṃ samyak pācitaṃ sat satvaṃ muñcati // GRhtCM_10.13:2
                            //
children.translated_text: Pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>), meaning <s>mākṣika</s>, steeped a hundred times in plantain juice — first steeped with plantain-sap a hundred rounds, then thoroughly cooked — well-boiled — with honey and castor oil — having been so prepared, it releases its essence. (GRhtCM 10.13:2)

children.text: kaiḥ kṛtvā trisaṃtāpaiḥ trivāraṃ dhamanaiḥ // GRhtCM_10.13:3 //
children.translated_text: How? With three heatings — three rounds of bellows-smelting. (GRhtCM 10.13:3)

children.text: evaṃ rasakaṃ kharparakamapi satvaṃ muñcatīti // GRhtCM_10.13:4 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, <s>rasaka</s> — calamine (<s>kharpara</s>) — also releases its essence. (GRhtCM 10.13:4)

children.text: minerals:: sattva:: pātana
children.translated_text: Minerals: essence — extraction (<s>pātana</s>)

children.text: ūrṇāṭaṅkaṇaguḍapuralākṣāsarjarasaiḥ sarvadhātubhiḥ piṣṭaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With wool (<s>ūrṇā</s>), borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>), <s>pura</s> (guggulu resin), lac (<s>lākṣā</s>), and <s>sarjarasa</s> (sal resin), ground with all the metals —

children.text: chāgīkṣīreṇa kṛtā piṇḍī śastā hi satvavidhau // GRht_10.14 //
children.translated_text: a pellet made with goat's milk is recommended indeed for the essence-extraction procedure. (GRht 10.14)

children.text: satvapātane piṇḍīmāha ūrṇetyādi // GRhtCM_10.14:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the pellet for essence-extraction, beginning with 'wool' and so on. (GRhtCM 10.14:1)

children.text:
ūrṇā iti ūrṇā meṣaroma ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ guḍaḥ pratītaḥ puro guggupuḥ
                            pākṣā jatu sarjaraso rāpaḥ etaiḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaiḥ sarvadhātubhiḥ
                            rasoparasairvā svarṇādibhiḥ saha piṣṭaiḥ peṣitaiḥ punaḥ chāgīkṣīreṇa
                            ajāpayasā kṛtā yā piṇḍī sā satvavidhau satvapātanakarmaṇi śastā pradhānā
                            // GRhtCM_10.14:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Wool' (<s>ūrṇā</s>) means sheep's fleece; <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is borax (<s>saubhāgya</s>); <s>guḍa</s> is well-known; <s>pura</s> is guggulu resin; <s>lākṣā</s> is lac; <s>sarjarasa</s> is <s>rāla</s> (sal resin) — with these, having the following specification: ground with all the metals — with the sub-metals and <s>rasas</s>, or with gold and other [metals] — and then a pellet made with goat's milk — with the milk of a she-goat — that pellet is recommended — is primary — in the essence-extraction procedure. (GRhtCM 10.14:2)

children.text: dhāturasoparasānāṃ satvaṃ pātayatyeveti // GRhtCM_10.14:3 //
children.translated_text: It causes the essence to fall from metals and sub-metals indeed. (GRhtCM 10.14:3)

children.text: minerals:: sattva:: pātana
children.translated_text: Minerals: essence — extraction (<s>pātana</s>)

children.text: cūrṇitasatvasambhāraṃ triṃśatpalamādareṇa saṃgṛhya /
children.translated_text: Having collected with care thirty <s>palas</s> of the powdered essence-material,

children.text: ṭaṃkaṇapalasaptayutaṃ guṃjāpalatritayayojitaṃ caiva // GRht_10.15 //
children.translated_text: joined with seven <s>palas</s> of borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), and combined with three <s>palas</s> of <s>guñjā</s> (Abrus seeds), (GRht 10.15)

children.text: tilacūrṇakakiṭṭapalair matsyair āloḍya dviraṃśayuktaiśca /
children.translated_text: having mixed with <s>palas</s> of sesame powder, iron-slag (<s>kiṭṭa</s>), and fish,

children.text: godhūmabaddhapiṇḍī gopañcakabhāvitā bahuśaḥ // GRht_10.16 //
children.translated_text: a pellet bound with wheat [flour], steeped many times in the five cow-products (<s>gopañcaka</s>), (GRht 10.16)

children.text: koṣṭhakadhamanavidhinā tīvraṃ bhastrānalena tatpatati /
children.translated_text: by the furnace-bellowing method, with intense bellows-fire, the essence falls;

children.text: saṃdravati cābhrasattvaṃ tathaiva sarvāṇi satvāni // GRht_10.17 //
children.translated_text: and mica-essence melts; likewise all [other] essences [melt]. (GRht 10.17)

children.text: vidhyantaramāha cūrṇitetyādi // GRhtCM_10.15-17:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another method, beginning with 'powdered' and so on. (GRhtCM 10.15–17:1)

children.text:
cūrṇitasatvasamānaṃ cūrṇitaṃ piṣṭaṃ yat satvaṃ sāraṃ tatsamānaṃ
                            viśuddhatvāt satvasamānaṃ dhāturasoparasacūrṇaṃ iti śeṣaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_10.15-17:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Powdered essence-like' — the powdered, i.e., ground, material that is equivalent to essence — pure, hence essence-like — meaning the powdered minerals and sub-metals; this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 10.15–17:2)

children.text:
evaṃvidhaṃ viśuddhaṃ cūrṇaṃ ādareṇa prītyā ādau saṃgṛhya
                            ṭaṅkaṇapapasaptayutaṃ kuryāt saubhāgyasya papaiḥ saptasaṃkhyākaiḥ
                            sahitaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_10.15-17:3 //
children.translated_text: Such pure powder, having collected it with care — with diligence — first, one should make it joined with seven <s>palas</s> of borax — combined with seven measures of borax (<s>saubhāgya</s>); that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 10.15–17:3)

children.text:
viśuddhe cūrṇe triṃśatpape saptapapaṃ saubhāgyaṃ yojyaṃ evaṃ
                            ṭaṅkaṇavidhānena ca punaḥ guñjāpapatritayena
                            raktikāpapatritayaparimāṇena yojitaṃ kuryād iti // GRhtCM_10.15-17:4
                            //
children.translated_text: To thirty <s>palas</s> of pure powder, seven <s>palas</s> of borax should be added; similarly, by the borax procedure, further combined with three <s>palas</s> of <s>guñjā</s> (Abrus seeds) — with the measure of three <s>palas</s> of <s>raktikā</s> seeds — one should make it so combined. (GRhtCM 10.15–17:4)

children.text:
tipacūrṇakakiṭṭapapaiḥ tipaṃ pratītaṃ teṣāṃ cūrṇakaṃ kiṭṭaṃ muṇḍādīnāṃ
                            mapaṃ tayoḥ papaiḥ papamānairgodhūmabaddhapiṇḍī bahuśo bahuvāraṃ
                            gopañcakabhāvitaṃ gavāṃ kṣīrājyadadhimūtraviṭkena bhāvitā kiṃ kṛtvā
                            matsyair āpoḍya matsyaiḥ kṣudrajapacarair āpoḍya saṃmiśryetyarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_10.15-17:5 //
children.translated_text: With <s>palas</s> — measures — of sesame powder and iron-slag: sesame is well-known; the slag (<s>kiṭṭa</s>) is the scum of iron and the like; a pellet bound with wheat [flour], steeped many times — many rounds — in the five cow-products (<s>gopañcaka</s>), meaning the milk, ghee, curd, urine, and dung of cows; having done what? Having mixed with small aquatic fish — having blended; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 10.15–17:5)

children.text:
koṣṭhake koṣṭhikāyantre dhamanavidhinā utkṣipyotkṣipya dhamanena
                            bhastrānapena tat satvaṃ patati pūrvasaṃbandhāt tāpyādīnāṃ iti śeṣaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_10.15-17:6 //
children.translated_text: In a furnace (<s>koṣṭhaka</s>) apparatus, by the bellowing method — by repeatedly operating the bellows-fire, that essence falls — from the connection with the preceding [verse], of pyrite and such [minerals]; this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 10.15–17:6)

children.text: ca punarabhrasatvaṃ abhrakātsāraṃ saṃdravati // GRhtCM_10.15-17:7 //
children.translated_text: And furthermore, mica-essence — the essence from mica — melts. (GRhtCM 10.15–17:7)

children.text:
tathaivoktavidhānena sarvāṇi samastāni satvāni sārāṇi patanti anuktānāṃ
                            iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_10.15-17:8 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, by the stated procedure, all — every one of — the essences fall; those not [previously] mentioned [are implied]; this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 10.15–17:8)

children.text: atha bījanirvāhaṇam ārabhyate /
children.translated_text: Now the seed-procedure (<s>bīja-nirvāhaṇa</s>) is commenced.

children.text: svarṇamākṣika:: for production of gold (?)
children.translated_text: Gold-pyrite (<s>svarṇamākṣika</s>): for the production of gold

children.text: svīkṛtya sarvasarito gaṅgā jaladhau yathā tathā haimam /
children.translated_text: Just as the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, having received all rivers, [enters] the ocean, so the gold [essence] —

children.text: praviśati rase gṛhītvā saṃmiliti sarvalohaguṇān // GRht_11.1 //
children.translated_text: enters into mercury, having absorbed all the qualities of metals, and merges [with them]. (GRht 11.1)

children.text: jīryati milati ca śulbe tatsatvaṃ kiṭṭatāṃ yāti /
children.translated_text: It is digested and merges in copper — its essence [then] attains the state of slag.

children.text: suvṛttaḥ sadrṛtārambhaḥ sujñaḥ saṃjñānadarśakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Well-conducted, of true beginnings, wise, displaying knowledge,

children.text: abhūcca dhanadharmajño hārī kuñjanasaṃpadām // GRhtCM_11.1:1 //
children.translated_text: he was a knower of wealth and <s>dharma</s>, a captivator of courtly splendors. (GRhtCM 11.1:1)

children.text: ādau haimapraśaṃsām āha svīkṛtyetyādi // GRhtCM_11.1:2 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] First, he states the praise of gold-pyrite essence, with 'having accepted' and so forth. (GRhtCM 11.1:2)

children.text:
haimaṃ svarṇamākṣikasatvaṃ saṃmiliti kiṃkṛtvā sarvalohaguṇān
                                sarvaloheṣu samastadhātuṣu saṃmilitā miśritāḥ ye guṇās tān gṛhītvā
                                tathā rase praviśati yathā gaṅgā sarvā nadyaḥ saritaḥ svīkṛtya
                                aṅgīkṛtya jaladhau samudre praviśati // GRhtCM_11.1:3 //
children.translated_text: The golden [substance] — the essence of <s>svarṇamākṣika</s> (gold-pyrite) — having combined [with mercury], what does it do? Having taken the qualities of all metals — the qualities that are combined, meaning mixed, in all metals, in all mineral substances — it enters mercury just as the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, having accepted all rivers (<s>nadīs</s>), enters the ocean (<s>jaladhi</s>). (GRhtCM 11.1:3)

children.text: tāpyasatvādhikāram āha jīryatītyādi // GRhtCM_11.1:4 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the authority of <s>tāpya</s>-essence, with 'it is digested' and so forth. (GRhtCM 11.1:4)

children.text:
tat haimaṃ tāpyasatvaṃ śulbe tāmre milati sati sattvaṃ jīryati
                                jāraṇatvamāpnoti rase iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_11.1:5 //
children.translated_text: That golden <s>tāpya</s>-essence (<s>satva</s>), when combined with copper (<s>śulba</s>), is digested — attains the state of digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>) — in mercury, is the completion. (GRhtCM 11.1:5)

children.text:
tasmin satve śulbe milati sati kiṭṭatāṃ yāti lohamalasadṛśaṃ syāt //
                                GRhtCM_11.1:6 //
children.translated_text: When that essence is combined with copper, it becomes dross (<s>kiṭṭa</s>) — it becomes like metal-impurity. (GRhtCM 11.1:6)

children.text: passende Stoffe für svarṇa-, tārakriyā
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Suitable substances for gold and silver operations]

children.text: hemakriyāsu kariṇā trapuṇā tārakriyāsu nirvyūḍham // GRht_11.2 //
children.translated_text: In gold operations, with lead (<s>karin</s>); in silver operations, processed with tin (<s>trapuṇa</s>). (GRht 11.2)

children.text:
prathamaṃ tatsatvaṃ kariṇā nāgena saha hemakriyāsu svarṇakāryeṣu
                            nirvyūḍhaṃ rase nirvāhitaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_11.2:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] First, that essence with lead (<s>nāga</s>) — in gold operations, in tasks pertaining to gold — should be processed (<s>nirvyūḍha</s>) in mercury, meaning subjected to <s>nirvāhaṇa</s>, is the sense. (GRhtCM 11.2:1)

Again, with tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) — in silver operations, in tasks pertaining to silver — it should be processed. Lead and tin are praised everywhere for yellow and white operations respectively, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 11.2:2)

children.text: Herstellung eines bījas
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Preparation of a <s>bīja</s> (seed)]

children.text: ghanasatvaṃ khalu raviṇā rasāyane dvaṃdvakaṃ yojyam /
children.translated_text: Mica-essence (<s>ghanasatva</s>) indeed, with copper (<s>raviṇā</s>), in <s>rasāyana</s> (elixir-making), should be combined as a pair;

children.text: raktagaṇapātabhāvitagirijatumākṣikagairikadaradaiḥ // GRht_11.3 //
children.translated_text: with substances processed by sprinklings of the red group — mineral pitch (<s>girijatu</s>), pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>), ochre (<s>gairika</s>), and cinnabar (<s>darada</s>). (GRht 11.3)

children.text: abhrasatvayogamāha ghanasatvam ityādi // GRhtCM_11.3:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the method for mica-essence, with 'mica-essence' and so forth. (GRhtCM 11.3:1)

children.text:
khapu niścaye vākyāpaṅkāre vā ghanasatvam abhrasāraṃ raviṇā tāmreṇa saha
                            rasāyane jarāvyādhināśane dvaṃdvakaṃ ghanasatvatāmraṃ yojyaṃ punaḥ
                            raktagaṇapātabhāvitagirijatumākṣikagairikadaradaiḥ raktagaṇasya yaḥ
                            pātaḥ pātanaṃ nikṣepo vā tena bhāvitāni gharmapuṭitāni
                            girijatumākṣikagairikadaradāni girijatu śipājatu mākṣikaṃ pratītaṃ
                            daradaṃ hiṅgupaṃ etairbījaśeṣaṃ kuryād ityāgāmiśpokājjñeyam //
                            GRhtCM_11.3:2 //
children.translated_text: The particle '<s>kha</s>' [is used] in the sense of certainty or as a sentence-ornament. Mica-essence (<s>ghanasatva</s>) — the essence of mica (<s>abhra</s>) — with copper (<s>raviṇā</s>), in <s>rasāyana</s> — in the destruction of aging and disease — the pair (<s>dvaṃdvaka</s>) of mica-essence and copper should be combined. Again, with mineral pitch (<s>girijatu</s>), pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>), ochre (<s>gairika</s>), and cinnabar (<s>darada</s>) that have been processed by sprinklings of the red group — the sprinkling (<s>pāta</s>), meaning the casting or projection of the red group, processed by that means, meaning calcined with fire-cakes — <s>girijatu</s> is bitumen (<s>śilājatu</s>); <s>mākṣika</s> is well-known; <s>darada</s> is cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>); with these one should prepare the <s>bīja</s> (seed) — the remainder should be understood from the following verse. (GRhtCM 11.3:2)

children.text: gold:: bīja
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Gold — <s>bīja</s>]

children.text: mṛdulatāmrakāntaghanasatvaṃ mṛtanāgatīkṣṇakanakaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Soft copper (<s>mṛdula-tāmra</s>), iron (<s>kānta</s>), mica-essence (<s>ghanasatva</s>), killed lead (<s>mṛta-nāga</s>), steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), and gold (<s>kanaka</s>) —

children.text: kurvīta bījaśeṣaṃ daradaśilātālamākṣikairvāpāt // GRht_11.4 //
children.translated_text: one should prepare the <s>bīja</s> (seed) remainder, by sprinkling (<s>vāpa</s>) with cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), realgar (<s>śilā</s>), orpiment (<s>tāla</s>), and pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>). (GRht 11.4)

children.text: vidhyantaramāha mṛdupetyādi // GRhtCM_11.4:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another method, with 'soft' and so forth. (GRhtCM 11.4:1)

children.text:
mṛdupaṃ nepāpasaṃjñikaṃ tāmraṃ kāntaṃ pohajāti ghanasatvamabhrasāraṃ
                            punarmṛtaṃ nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ pohajāti kanakaṃ hema etattrayaṃ bījaṃ
                            śupbāditrayaṃ ca bījasaṃjñakaṃ daradaśipātāpamākṣikairvāpāt daradaṃ
                            hiṅgupaṃ śipā manohvā tāpaṃ haritāpaṃ etaiḥ kṛtvā vāpaḥ vahnitapte
                            parikṣepaḥ tasmāt bījaśeṣaṃ kurvīta ubhayorbīje abhrasatvahemnaḥ śeṣe
                            kuryādityarthaḥ vā evaṃ kṛte yaccheṣaṃ tiṣṭhati tadbījamiti //
                            GRhtCM_11.4:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Soft' — known as Nepali; 'copper' (<s>tāmra</s>); 'iron' (<s>kānta</s>) — of the <s>loha</s> variety; 'mica-essence' (<s>ghanasatva</s>) — the essence of mica; again, 'killed lead' (<s>mṛta-nāga</s>) — killed tin (<s>sīsaka</s>); 'steel' (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) — of the <s>loha</s> variety; 'gold' (<s>kanaka</s>) — these three are the <s>bīja</s>; the group of three starting with copper is also designated as <s>bīja</s>. With cinnabar (<s>darada</s>, i.e., <s>hiṅgula</s>), realgar (<s>śilā</s>, i.e., <s>manaḥśilā</s>), orpiment (<s>tāla</s>, i.e., <s>haritāla</s>) — by sprinkling (<s>vāpa</s>), meaning projection into the fire-heated [substance], from that, one should prepare the <s>bīja</s> remainder — the remainder of both <s>bījas</s>, mica-essence and gold, is the meaning. Or, what remains after doing thus — that is the <s>bīja</s>. (GRhtCM 11.4:2)

children.text: gold, silver:: bīja
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Gold, silver — <s>bīja</s>]

children.text: mṛtanāgaṃ vaṅgaṃ vā śulvaṃ ghanasatvatārakanakaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: Killed lead (<s>nāga</s>), or tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), or copper (<s>śulva</s>), with mica-essence (<s>ghanasatva</s>), silver (<s>tāra</s>), and gold (<s>kanaka</s>), or —

children.text: dhmātaṃ tadeva sarvaṃ giriṇādhikaśodhanairvāpāt // GRht_11.5 //
children.translated_text: all of that, smelted with bitumen (<s>giriṇā</s>), by sprinkling with the best purificants. (GRht 11.5)

children.text: vidhyantaramāha mṛtaṃ nāgam ityādi // GRhtCM_11.5:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another method, with 'killed lead' and so forth. (GRhtCM 11.5:1)

children.text:
mayannāgaṃ sīsakaṃ tanmṛtanāgaṃ ca mṛtaṃ yadvaṅgaṃ raktagaṇāvāpamṛtaṃ ca
                            yacchupvaṃ vā ghanasatvatārakanakaṃ ghanasatvamabhrasāraṃ tāraṃ rūpyaṃ
                            kanakaṃ hema etannadugaṇasarvaṃ vā pratyekaṃ pṛthak giriṇā śipājatunā
                            saha dhmātaṃ kuryāt adhikaśodhanaiḥ daradaśipātāpairvāpāt bījaśeṣaṃ
                            kuryāditi pūrvasaṃbandhaḥ // GRhtCM_11.5:2 //
children.translated_text: Lead (<s>nāga</s>) means tin (<s>sīsaka</s>); that killed lead, and killed tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), killed by sprinkling with the red group, and copper (<s>śulva</s>); or mica-essence (<s>ghanasatva</s>) — the essence of mica (<s>abhra</s>); silver (<s>tāra</s>) — <s>rūpya</s>; gold (<s>kanaka</s>) — <s>hema</s>; all of this metal group, or each separately, with bitumen (<s>giriṇā</s>, i.e., <s>śilājatu</s>), should be smelted (<s>dhmāta</s>); with the best purificants — cinnabar, realgar, and orpiment — by sprinkling, one should prepare the <s>bīja</s> remainder — this connects with the previous [verse]. (GRhtCM 11.5:2)

children.text: gold:: bija (?)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Gold — <s>bīja</s> (?)]

children.text: raktagaṇaṃ pītaṃ vā mākṣikarājāvartam atho vimalam /
children.translated_text: The red group, or the yellow [group]; <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), <s>rājāvarta</s> (lapis lazuli), and then <s>vimala</s> (pure pyrite);

children.text: ekatamaṃ vā gairikakunaṭīkṣitigandhakakhagairvā // GRht_11.6 //
children.translated_text: or any one among ochre (<s>gairika</s>), <s>kunaṭī</s>, antimony (<s>kṣiti</s>), sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), and green vitriol (<s>khaga</s>). (GRht 11.6)

children.text: nirvyūḍhaireva raso rāgādi gṛhṇāti bandhamupayāti /
children.translated_text: Only when processed (<s>nirvyūḍha</s>) with mercury and metals does mercury acquire coloring (<s>rāga</s>) and the rest, and attain fixation (<s>bandha</s>);

children.text: mṛtalohoparasādyair nirvyūḍhaṃ bhavati śṛṅkhalābījam // GRht_11.7 //
children.translated_text: processed with killed metals, <s>uparasas</s>, and the like, it becomes a chain-seed (<s>śṛṅkhalābīja</s>). (GRht 11.7)

children.text: raktagaṇaṃ dāḍimakiṃśukādikaṃ vā pītagaṇaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The red group consists of pomegranate, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, and the like; or the yellow group, as follows:

children.text: kiṃśukaḥ karṇikāraśca haridrādvitayaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Kiṃśuka</s>, <s>karṇikāra</s>, and the pair of turmeric (<s>haridrā</s>) —

children.text: pītavargo+ayamuddiṣṭo rasarājasya karmaṇi iti // GRhtCM_11.6-7:1 //
children.translated_text: this yellow group is designated for the operations of the king of <s>rasas</s>. (GRhtCM 11.6–7:1)

children.text:
vā mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ vā rājāvartaṃ rājavarto pājavarada iti bhāṣāyāṃ atha
                            vimapaṃ tāramākṣikaṃ ityekatamaṃ sarvameva vā
                            gairikakunaṭīkṣitigandhakakhagaiḥ gairikaṃ pratītaṃ kunaṭī manohvā
                            kṣitiḥ sphaṭakī gandhakaḥ pratītaḥ khagaḥ kāsīsaṃ etairiti //
                            GRhtCM_11.6-7:2 //
children.translated_text: Or <s>mākṣika</s> — <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite); or <s>rājāvarta</s> — known as <s>pājavarda</s> in the vernacular; then <s>vimala</s> — <s>tāramākṣika</s> (silver-pyrite) — thus any one of all [these]; or ochre (<s>gairika</s>) — well-known; <s>kunaṭī</s> — <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar); <s>kṣiti</s> — alum (<s>sphaṭikā</s>); <s>gandhaka</s> (sulphur) — well-known; <s>khaga</s> — green vitriol (<s>kāsīsa</s>); with these. (GRhtCM 11.6–7:2)

children.text:
etaiḥ pūrvoktaireva rase nirvyūḍhe raso rāgādi rañjanādi gṛhṇāti
                            ādiśabdāt sāraṇaṃ ca vijñeyaṃ punarbandham upayāti bandhanamāpnoti punaḥ
                            mṛtapohoparasādyaiḥ mṛtāśca te pohāśca dhātavaśca ta eva uparasā
                            gandhakādyāḥ ādyaśabdāt rasā api tairnirvyūḍhaiḥ kṛtvā śṛṅkhapābījaṃ
                            uttarottaraṃ rañjakaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_11.6-7:3 //
children.translated_text: When processed in mercury with these aforementioned [substances], mercury acquires coloring (<s>rāga</s>) and the rest — from the word 'and the rest,' <s>sāraṇa</s> (extraction) should also be understood; again, it attains fixation (<s>bandha</s>) — achieves binding. Again, with killed metals and <s>uparasas</s> — the killed ones are metals, and the mineral substances beginning with sulphur; from the word 'and the like,' the <s>rasas</s> (mineral essences) too; processed with these, [it becomes] a chain-seed (<s>śṛṅkhalābīja</s>) — a progressively superior colorant, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 11.6–7:3)

children.text: bīja for rañjana and bandhana of mercury
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: <s>Bīja</s> for coloring (<s>rañjana</s>) and binding (<s>bandhana</s>) of mercury]

children.text: āyasaśalākikābhyām advandvākhyaiśca saṅkarākhyaiśca /
children.translated_text: With iron rods (<s>āyasaśalākikā</s>), and with those called non-pairs (<s>advandva</s>) and those called mixtures (<s>saṅkara</s>),

children.text: nirvyūḍhaṃ rasalohairjāraṇakarmocitaṃ bhavati // GRht_11.8 //
children.translated_text: processed with mercury and metals — [this] becomes fit for digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>). (GRht 11.8)

children.text:
rasapohairiti rasā vaikrāntādayo pohā dhātavaḥ pratītās tair nirvyūḍhaṃ
                            kiṃviśiṣṭaiḥ advandvākhyaiḥ ekātmaiḥ saṃkarairvā sarvaiḥ saṃkaro+avakare
                            ityamaraḥ evaṃ niṣpanne bījaṃ jāraṇayogyaṃ sadityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_11.8:1
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Mercury and metals' — the <s>rasas</s> are <s>vaikrānta</s> and the like; the metals (<s>lohas</s>) are the well-known mineral substances; processed with these — of what quality? With those called non-pairs (<s>advandva</s>) — single substances; or with mixtures (<s>saṅkara</s>) — all [combined]; '<s>saṅkara</s>' means mixing, as per <s>Amara[kośa]</s>. When thus prepared, the <s>bīja</s> becomes fit for digestion, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 11.8:1)

children.text: bījamidaṃ raktagaṇe niṣecitaṃ tena kṛtavāpam /
children.translated_text: This <s>bīja</s> (seed), sprinkled into the red group, having undergone sprinkling (<s>vāpa</s>) by that —

children.text: cāritajāritamātraṃ sūtaṃ rañjayati badhnāti // GRht_11.9 //
children.translated_text: merely swept and digested, colors mercury and binds it. (GRht 11.9)

children.text: viśeṣavidhyantaramāha bījamityādi // GRhtCM_11.9:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states a special alternative method, with '<s>bīja</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 11.9:1)

children.text: idaṃ niṣpannabījaṃ raktagaṇe niṣecitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_11.9:2 //
children.translated_text: This prepared <s>bīja</s> should be sprinkled (<s>niṣecita</s>) into the red group. (GRhtCM 11.9:2)

children.text:
punastena raktagaṇena kṛtavāpaṃ kṛto vāpo yasmin tat // GRhtCM_11.9:3
                            //
children.translated_text: Again, with that red group, [it is] that which has undergone sprinkling (<s>vāpa</s>) — that in which sprinkling was done. (GRhtCM 11.9:3)

children.text:
punastadbījaṃ cāritajāritamātraṃ pūrvaṃ ca paścāt jāritaṃ santaṃ sūtaṃ
                            rañjayati rāgaṃ prāpayati badhnāti ceti // GRhtCM_11.9:4 //
children.translated_text: Again, that <s>bīja</s>, merely swept first and then digested, colors mercury — brings it to the state of coloring (<s>rāga</s>) — and binds it. (GRhtCM 11.9:4)

children.text: bīja:: further processing
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: <s>Bīja</s> — further processing]

children.text: raktasnehaviśodhitamṛtaloharasādibhistu sarveṣām /
children.translated_text: With killed metals, mercury-essences (<s>rasādi</s>), and the like, purified with red unctuants, of all —

children.text: bījānāṃ kuru vāpaṃ raktasnehe niṣekaṃ ca // GRht_11.10 //
children.translated_text: the <s>bījas</s>, perform sprinkling (<s>vāpa</s>); and sprinkling (<s>niṣeka</s>) in red unctuant. (GRht 11.10)

children.text: taccāha raktetyādi // GRhtCM_11.10:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That he states, with 'red' and so forth. (GRhtCM 11.10:1)

children.text:
raktasneha iti raktagaṇo dāḍimakiṃśukādikaḥ snehaḥ kaṅguṇyādīnāṃ
                            etairviśodhitāḥ paścānmṛtā ye dhātavo rasādayaśca rasoparasāstaiḥ
                            sarveṣāṃ bījānāṃ pūrvoktānāṃ vāpaṃ kuru rase iti śeṣaḥ vā rakte
                            raktavarṇe snehe snehavarge niṣekaṃ ca vidhānadvayamidam //
                            GRhtCM_11.10:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Red unctuant' — the red group consists of pomegranate, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, and the like; the unctuants are those of <s>kaṅguṇī</s> and the like; purified by these, and then killed metals and <s>rasādi</s> (mercury-essences and <s>uparasas</s>); with these, of all <s>bījas</s> — the previously mentioned ones — perform sprinkling (<s>vāpa</s>) in mercury, is the completion. Or, in red — in the red-colored — unctuant group, [perform] sprinkling (<s>niṣeka</s>) as well; this constitutes a dual procedure. (GRhtCM 11.10:2)

children.text: silver:: bījas
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Silver — <s>bījas</s>]

children.text: vaṅgābhram abhratāraṃ sitaśailamalāhatau ca sitavaṅgau /
children.translated_text: Tin-mica (<s>vaṅgābhra</s>), mica-silver (<s>abhratāra</s>); and white tin (<s>sitavaṅga</s>) struck with whiteite (<s>sitaśailamala</s>);

children.text: raktaṃ sitatāpyahataṃ ramati nirvyūḍhavaṅgābhram // GRht_11.11 //
children.translated_text: the red [gold], struck with white pyrite (<s>sitatāpya</s>), delights in processed tin-mica (<s>nirvyūḍhavaṅgābhra</s>). (GRht 11.11)

children.text:
pītakriyāyāṃ bījānyuktāni atha śvetakriyāyāṃ bījānyāha vaṅgetyādi //
                            GRhtCM_11.11:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Bījas</s> for yellow operations having been stated, now he states the <s>bījas</s> for white (silver) operations, with 'tin' and so forth. (GRhtCM 11.11:1)

children.text:
vaṅgābhramiti vaṅgaṃ raṅgaṃ abhraṃ gaganaṃ ete bījahetave iti śeṣaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_11.11:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Tin-mica' — <s>vaṅga</s> is tin (<s>raṅga</s>); <s>abhra</s> is mica (<s>gagana</s>); these are for the purpose of <s>bīja</s>, is the completion. (GRhtCM 11.11:2)

children.text:
punarabhratāraṃ abhraṃ gaganaṃ tāraṃ rūpyaṃ iti ca sitaṃ śvetaṃ
                            yacchaipamapaṃ śipājatu tena āhatau samyak mṛtau sitavaṅgau tāraraṅgau
                            kāryau punaḥ raktaṃ hema sitaṃ tāraṃ tāpyaṃ mākṣikaṃ tābhyāṃ hataṃ
                            māritaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_11.11:3 //
children.translated_text: Again, 'mica-silver' — <s>abhra</s> is mica (<s>gagana</s>); <s>tāra</s> is silver (<s>rūpya</s>); and 'white' — the white mineral (<s>śailamala</s>) is bitumen (<s>śilājatu</s>); struck by that — properly killed — the white tin and silver should be prepared. Again, 'red' is gold; 'white silver' — <s>tāpya</s> is pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>); struck by these two, meaning killed, one should prepare. (GRhtCM 11.11:3)

children.text:
punastāraṃ rūpyaṃ nirvyūḍhaṃ vaṅgaṃ cābhraṃ ca yatra tadevaṃvidhaṃ kuryāt
                            // GRhtCM_11.11:4 //
children.translated_text: Again, silver (<s>tāra</s>, i.e., <s>rūpya</s>) processed with tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) and mica (<s>abhra</s>) — one should prepare in this manner. (GRhtCM 11.11:4)

children.text: etatsarvaṃ rase tārakriyāsu yojyamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_11.11:5 //
children.translated_text: All of this should be employed in silver operations involving mercury, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 11.11:5)

children.text: nirvāhaṇavidhireṣaḥ prakāśito+aśeṣadoṣaśamanāya /
children.translated_text: This <s>nirvāhaṇa</s> (processing) method has been revealed for the removal of all faults;

children.text: bījānāmapyevaṃ ghanasatvaṃ yujyate prathamam // GRht_11.12 //
children.translated_text: for the <s>bījas</s> too, in this manner, mica-essence (<s>ghanasatva</s>) is to be applied first. (GRht 11.12)

children.text: bīje'bhrasatvaṃ pradhānamāha nirvāhaṇetyādi // GRhtCM_11.12:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that mica-essence is primary in the <s>bīja</s>, with '<s>nirvāhaṇa</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 11.12:1)

children.text:
eṣaḥ kimarthaḥ aśeṣadoṣaśamanāya dhātvādīnāṃ samastadoṣanāśanāyetyarthaḥ
                            // GRhtCM_11.12:2 //
children.translated_text: This — for what purpose? For the removal of all faults — for the destruction of all defects of metals and the like, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 11.12:2)

children.text:
evamamunā prakāreṇa yathā dhātunirvāhaṇavidhistathā bījānāṃ rase
                            nirvāhaṇaṃ kuryāt sarvabījanirvāhaṇe abhrakasatvaṃ prathamaṃ
                            nirvāhyamiti jñeyam // GRhtCM_11.12:3 //
children.translated_text: In this manner — by this method — just as the procedure for metal-processing (<s>dhātu-nirvāhaṇa</s>), so too one should process the <s>bījas</s> in mercury. In the processing of all <s>bījas</s>, mica-essence (<s>abhrakasatva</s>) should be processed first — this should be understood. (GRhtCM 11.12:3)

children.text: crucible for bījanirvāhaṇa
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Crucible for <s>bīja</s>-processing (<s>bījanirvāhaṇa</s>)]

children.text: chāgāsthibhasmanirmitamūṣāṃ kṛtvaiva mallakākārām /
children.translated_text: Having made a crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>) fashioned from goat-bone ash, in the shape of a bowl (<s>mallaka</s>),

children.text: dalayoge ghanarandhrāṃ ṭaṅkaṇaviṣaguñjākṛtalepām // GRht_11.13 //
children.translated_text: with a hole at the junction of the lid (<s>dalayoga</s>), coated with borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), poison, and <s>guñjā</s> (Abrus precatorius seeds). (GRht 11.13)

children.text: nirvāhaṇavidhānamāha chāgetyādi // GRhtCM_11.13:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the <s>nirvāhaṇa</s> procedure, with 'goat' and so forth. (GRhtCM 11.13:1)

children.text:
evaṃvidhāṃ mūṣāṃ kṛtvā dhātunirvāhaṇaṃ kuryāt iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_11.13:2
                            //
children.translated_text: Having made such a crucible, one should perform the metal-processing — is the completion. (GRhtCM 11.13:2)

children.text:
kiṃbhūtāṃ chāgāsthibhasmanirmitamūṣāmiti chāgo bastastasyāsthīni
                            tadbhasmanā nirmitā kṛtā yā mūṣā tām // GRhtCM_11.13:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality? A crucible fashioned from goat-bone ash — the goat (<s>chāga</s>) is a billy-goat (<s>basta</s>); its bones; fashioned, meaning made, from their ash — that crucible. (GRhtCM 11.13:3)

children.text: punaḥ kiṃbhūtāṃ mappakākārāṃ gostanasadṛśīm // GRhtCM_11.13:4 //
children.translated_text: Again, of what quality? In the shape of a bowl (<s>mallaka</s>) — resembling a cow's teat. (GRhtCM 11.13:4)

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭāṃ ghanarandhrāṃ nibiḍachidrām // GRhtCM_11.13:5 //
children.translated_text: Further, of what specification? Having dense holes — having closely-spaced perforations. (GRhtCM 11.13:5)

children.text:
punaḥ ṭaṅkaṇaviṣaguñjākṛtapepāṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ viṣaṃ saktukaṃ guñjā
                            raktikā tābhiḥ kṛto pepo yasyāṃ sā tām // GRhtCM_11.13:6 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, coated with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), <s>viṣa</s> (a poisonous substance), and <s>guñjā</s> (rosary pea) — <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgya</s> (borax); <s>viṣa</s> is <s>saktuka</s> (a toxic substance); <s>guñjā</s> is <s>raktikā</s> (rosary pea); the coating made with these, upon which — that [crucible]. (GRhtCM 11.13:6)

children.text:
evaṃbhūtā mūṣā dapayoge patramepane kāryetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_11.13:7
                            //
children.translated_text: Such a crucible should be made for the conjunction of metals (<s>dalamelana</s>) and leaf-coating (<s>pattralepana</s>) — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 11.13:7)

children.text: atha dvandvamelanamabhidhāsyate /
children.translated_text: Now <s>dvandvamelana</s> (binary fusion) will be described.

children.text: Motivation für dvandvamelana
children.translated_text: [Section:] Rationale for <s>dvandvamelana</s> (binary fusion)

children.text: yāvan nāṅgāṅgatayā na milanti lohāni sarvasattveṣu /
children.translated_text: As long as metals do not fuse limb-to-limb with all the essences,

children.text: tāvatsarvāṅgaṃ na ca carati raso dvandvayogena // GRht_12.1 //
children.translated_text: so long mercury does not pervade completely — [this is achieved] by the binary conjunction method. (GRht 12.1)

children.text: vācāṃ vipāsena sudhānukārī nu jagatkaroti /
children.translated_text: By the loosening of speech, one who imitates nectar indeed acts upon the world;

children.text:
kiṃcitsvayaṃ yatpuruṣatvameva sudhādvijihvāśritam ityadoṣaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_12.1:1 //
children.translated_text: that manhood itself which depends on the nectar-tongue — this is faultless. (GRhtCM 12.1:1)

children.text: atha dvandvayogaprakāramāha yāvadityādi // GRhtCM_12.1:2 //
children.translated_text: Now he describes the method of binary conjunction with 'yāvat' (as long as) and so forth. (GRhtCM 12.1:2)

children.text: yāvadityavadhau // GRhtCM_12.1:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Yāvat' is used in the sense of a limit. (GRhtCM 12.1:3)

children.text:
pohāni hemādīni nāgāṅgatayā bhujaṅgaśarīratayā na mipanti sugamatvena
                            ekaśarīratāṃ nāpnuvanti // GRhtCM_12.1:4 //
children.translated_text: Metals — gold and the like — in the manner of a serpent's body, do not fuse readily — do not attain the state of one body. (GRhtCM 12.1:4)

children.text:
keṣu sarvasattveṣu abhrādīnāṃ sāreṣu sattvasya kāṭhinyādvinopāyaṃ
                            naikatāṃ yānti pohāni // GRhtCM_12.1:5 //
children.translated_text: In what? In all the essences — in the extracts of mica and the like; due to the hardness of the essence, without a special method, metals do not attain oneness [with them]. (GRhtCM 12.1:5)

children.text: atastāvadrasaḥ sarvāṅgaṃ na carati // GRhtCM_12.1:6 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, so long mercury does not pervade completely. (GRhtCM 12.1:6)

children.text:
kena kṛtvā satveṣu pohāni mipanti dvandvayogena daradādinā vā
                            guḍapuraṭaṅkaṇādineti // GRhtCM_12.1:7 //
children.translated_text: By what means do metals fuse with the essences? By the binary conjunction method — with cinnabar and the like, or with jaggery, <s>pura</s> (guggulu), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), and the like. (GRhtCM 12.1:7)

children.text: metals:: preparation for dv.~
children.translated_text: [Section:] Metals — preparation for binary fusion

children.text: mākṣīkarasakasasyakadaradānyatamena vāpitaṃ loham /
children.translated_text: A metal, deposited with any one of <s>mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite), <s>rasaka</s> (calamine), <s>sasyaka</s> (vitriol), or <s>darada</s> (cinnabar),

children.text: saṃtyajati nibiḍabhāvaṃ satve saṃmilati sudhmātam // GRht_12.2 //
children.translated_text: abandons its compact nature; when well-smelted, it fuses with the essence. (GRht 12.2)

children.text: sattvamepanavidhānam āha mākṣiketyādi // GRhtCM_12.2:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the method of fusing with essence with '<s>mākṣika</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 12.2:1)

children.text: pohaṃ svarṇādi // GRhtCM_12.2:2 //
children.translated_text: Metal [means] gold and the like. (GRhtCM 12.2:2)

children.text:
mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ rasakaṃ kharparikaṃ sasyakaṃ capapā daradaṃ hiṅgupaṃ
                            etena catuṣkeṇa vā ebhyo 'nyatamenoktarasoparasena vāpitaṃ sudhmātaṃ
                            śobhanayuktyā dhmātaṃ ca sat niviḍabhāvaṃ saṃtyajati sattve saṃmipati ca
                            // GRhtCM_12.2:3 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> is iron pyrite; <s>rasaka</s> is calamine; <s>sasyaka</s> is <s>capalā</s> (vitriol); <s>darada</s> is cinnabar — deposited with this group of four, or with any other one of the [previously] mentioned minerals or subsidiary minerals; well-smelted — smelted with excellent technique — being such, [the metal] abandons its compact nature and fuses with the essence. (GRhtCM 12.2:3)

children.text: dvandvamelāpaka:: preparation
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Dvandvamelāpaka</s> (binary-fusion agent) — preparation

children.text: guḍapuraṭaṅkaṇalākṣāsarjarasair dhātakīsamāyuktaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With jaggery, <s>pura</s> (guggulu), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), lac (<s>lākṣā</s>), and <s>sarjarasa</s> (sal-resin), combined with <s>dhātakī</s> (woodfordia),

children.text: strīstanyena tu piṣṭaiḥ rasāyane dvaṃdvitaṃ yojyam // GRht_12.3 //
children.translated_text: ground with woman's breast-milk — the binary-fused [metal] should be employed in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation). (GRht 12.3)

children.text: vidhyantaramāha guḍetyādi // GRhtCM_12.3:1 //
children.translated_text: He states an alternative method with 'guḍa' (jaggery) and so forth. (GRhtCM 12.3:1)

children.text:
idaṃ dvaṃdvitaṃ dvaṃdvīkṛtaṃ pohaṃ sattvena mipitaṃ rasāyane
                            jarāvyādhināśane yojyam // GRhtCM_12.3:2 //
children.translated_text: This binary-fused — made into a pair — metal fused with essence, should be employed in <s>rasāyana</s> — in the destruction of old age and disease. (GRhtCM 12.3:2)

children.text:
kairdvandvamepāpakaiḥ kṛtvā dvaṃdvitamityāha guḍetyādi // GRhtCM_12.3:3
                            //
children.translated_text: With what binary-fusion agents is it made binary-fused? He says 'guḍa' and so forth. (GRhtCM 12.3:3)

children.text:
guḍaḥ pratītaḥ puro guggupuḥ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ pākṣā jatu sarjaraso
                            rāpā etaiḥ dhātakīsamāyuktaiḥ dhātakī pratītā tatsamāyuktaiḥ punaḥ
                            strīstanyena nārīdugdhena piṣṭairmarditaiḥ etairdvandvamepāpakaiḥ kṛtvā
                            // GRhtCM_12.3:4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Guḍa</s> (jaggery) is well-known; <s>pura</s> is guggulu; <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgya</s> (borax); <s>lākṣā</s> is lac; <s>sarjarasa</s> is <s>rālā</s> (sal-resin) — with these, combined with <s>dhātakī</s> — <s>dhātakī</s> is well-known, combined with that — furthermore ground with woman's breast-milk — woman's milk — ground means rubbed; with these binary-fusion agents, having performed [the procedure]. (GRhtCM 12.3:4)

children.text: dvandvamelāpaka
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Dvandvamelāpaka</s> (binary-fusion agent)

children.text: ūrṇāṭaṅkaṇagirijatukarṇākṣimalendragopakarkaṭakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With wool, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), bitumen (<s>girijatu</s>), human ear-wax (<s>karṇākṣimala</s>), <s>indragopa</s> (cochineal insect), and crab,

children.text: nārīpayasā piṣṭaiḥ sarve dvandveṣu hi milanti // GRht_12.4 //
children.translated_text: ground with woman's milk — all [metals] indeed fuse in pairs. (GRht 12.4)

children.text:
sarve dvandveṣu satvaṃ prati dvandveṣu mipanti ekībhavanti pohāni iti
                            śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_12.4:1 //
children.translated_text: All [metals] fuse in pairs — with respect to the essence, in pairs they become one — 'metals' is the complement. (GRhtCM 12.4:1)

children.text: etaiḥ kaiḥ ūrṇādibhiḥ // GRhtCM_12.4:2 //
children.translated_text: With these — which? Those beginning with wool and the like. (GRhtCM 12.4:2)

children.text:
ūrṇā pratītā ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ girijatu śipājatu karṇākṣimapaṃ
                            manuṣyasya indragopako jīvaviśeṣaḥ karkaṭakaścakupīraḥ syātkupīraḥ
                            karkaṭakaḥ ityamaraḥ etaiḥ // GRhtCM_12.4:3 //
children.translated_text: Wool is well-known; <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgya</s> (borax); <s>girijatu</s> is mineral pitch (bitumen); <s>karṇākṣimala</s> is human [ear and eye] secretion; <s>indragopa</s> is a particular kind of insect; <s>karkaṭaka</s> is a crab — 'a crab is <s>kulīra</s>, [which is also] <s>karkaṭaka</s>' — thus [says] the <s>Amarakośa</s>; with these. (GRhtCM 12.4:3)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭaiḥ nārīpayasā strīdugdhena piṣṭaiḥ kapkitaiḥ trayo+api
                            dvandvamepāpakayogā iti // GRhtCM_12.4:4 //
children.translated_text: Of what specification? Ground with woman's milk — breast-milk — rubbed; all three binary-fusion agent formulas [have been given]. (GRhtCM 12.4:4)

children.text: dva.~ of rasavaikrānta and gold => bandhana of mercury
children.translated_text: [Section:] Binary fusion of <s>rasavaikrānta</s>-essence and gold — leading to mercury binding

children.text: rasavaikrāntakamevaṃ milati dvandvānvitaṃ samaṃ hemnā /
children.translated_text: Thus <s>rasavaikrānta</s> (mineral <s>vaikrānta</s>), combined in a pair, fuses equally with gold;

children.text: nirvyūḍhaṃ tatsatvaṃ tena raso bandhamupayāti // GRht_12.5 //
children.translated_text: that essence, well-smelted — by that, mercury attains binding. (GRht 12.5)

children.text: vidhyantaramāha rasetyādi // GRhtCM_12.5:1 //
children.translated_text: He states an alternative method with 'rasa' and so forth. (GRhtCM 12.5:1)

children.text:
evamuktavidhānena rasavaikrāntakaṃ dvandvānvitaṃ svakīyadvandvasahitaṃ
                            mipati pṛthagbhāvaṃ tyajati // GRhtCM_12.5:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by the stated procedure, <s>rasavaikrānta</s>, combined with its own pair — accompanied by its own binary [partner] — fuses, abandons its separate state. (GRhtCM 12.5:2)

children.text: kena samaṃ hemnā saha // GRhtCM_12.5:3 //
children.translated_text: With what equally? With gold. (GRhtCM 12.5:3)

children.text:
tadrasavaikrāntasattvaṃ hemnā saha nirvyūḍhaṃ kuryāt tena
                            rasavaikrāntasattvahemayogena raso bandhamupayāti baddho bhavatīti //
                            GRhtCM_12.5:4 //
children.translated_text: That <s>rasavaikrānta</s>-essence, one should smelt well together with gold; by that — by the conjunction of <s>rasavaikrānta</s>-essence and gold — mercury attains binding, becomes bound. (GRhtCM 12.5:4)

children.text: dvandvamelāpaka
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Dvandvamelāpaka</s> (binary-fusion agent)

children.text: śastaṃ sarvadvandve girijatulelītakendragopādyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Recommended for all binary [fusions] are bitumen (<s>girijatu</s>), sulfur (<s>lelītaka</s>), <s>indragopa</s> (cochineal), and the like;

children.text: mahiṣīkarṇamalādyaiḥ syādbījaṃ ṭaṅkaṇālaviṣaiḥ // GRht_12.6 //
children.translated_text: with buffalo's ear-wax and the like, the seed should [be prepared] with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), orpiment (<s>āla</s>), and <s>viṣa</s> (toxic substances). (GRht 12.6)

children.text: atha viśeṣavidhyantaramāha śastamityādi // GRhtCM_12.6:1 //
children.translated_text: Now he states a special alternative method with 'śastam' (recommended) and so forth. (GRhtCM 12.6:1)

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ bījaṃ śastaṃ kva sarvadvandve // GRhtCM_12.6:2 //
children.translated_text: Such a seed is recommended — where? In all binary [fusions]. (GRhtCM 12.6:2)

children.text: punaretaiḥ kṛtvā bījaṃ śastaṃ syāt // GRhtCM_12.6:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, with these, the seed should be recommended. (GRhtCM 12.6:3)
