With what? With bitumen, sulfur, <s>indragopa</s>, and the like — <s>girijatu</s> is mineral pitch; <s>lelītaka</s> is sulfur; <s>indragopa</s> is <s>surendragopa</s>, a particular kind of insect; these are the 'ādi' (etc.) of which — with those. (GRhtCM 12.6:4)

children.text:
na kevapametair mahiṣīkarṇamapādyaiśca mahiṣyāḥ karṇayormapa ādyo yeṣāṃ
                            te ādyaśabdānnāsākṣimapaṃ ca // GRhtCM_12.6:5 //
children.translated_text: Not only with these, but also with buffalo's ear-wax and the like — the wax from the ears of a buffalo, [that which is] the 'ādi' (etc.) — by the word 'ādi,' nasal and eye secretions also [are included]. (GRhtCM 12.6:5)

Furthermore, with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), orpiment, and <s>viṣa</s> — <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgya</s> (borax); <s>āla</s> is <s>haritāla</s> (orpiment); <s>viṣa</s> is a tuberous poison — with these, ground, the binary-fusion [should be done] — this is the further connection. (GRhtCM 12.6:6)

children.text: dvandvamelāpaka
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Dvandvamelāpaka</s> (binary-fusion agent)

children.text: madhusahitairapyetaistārābhraṃ milati tāpyakanakaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: With these same [agents] combined with honey, silver and mica fuse, as do pyrite and gold;

children.text: eraṇḍatailaṭaṅkaṇakaṃkuṣṭhaśilendragopaistu // GRht_12.7 //
children.translated_text: [also] with castor oil, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> (red arsenic), realgar (<s>śilā</s>), and <s>indragopa</s> (cochineal). (GRht 12.7)

children.text: vidhyantaramāha madhvityādi // GRhtCM_12.7:1 //
children.translated_text: He states an alternative method with 'madhu' (honey) and so forth. (GRhtCM 12.7:1)

children.text:
etaiḥ pūrvoktair yogaiḥ madhusahitaiḥ kṣaudrayutaiḥ tārābhraṃ
                            rūpyagaganaṃ mipati // GRhtCM_12.7:2 //
children.translated_text: With these — the previously stated formulas — combined with honey, silver and mica fuse. (GRhtCM 12.7:2)

children.text:
ca punastāpyakanakaṃ mākṣikasvarṇaṃ idaṃ dvandvaṃ ca mipati //
                            GRhtCM_12.7:3 //
children.translated_text: And furthermore, pyrite and gold — <s>mākṣika</s>-gold — this pair also fuses. (GRhtCM 12.7:3)

children.text:
na kevapaṃ pūrvoktayogair mipati punaretair
                            eraṇḍataipaṭaṅkaṇakaṅkuṣṭhaśipendragopaiśca eraṇḍataipaṃ vātārisnehaḥ
                            ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ viraṅgaṃ śipā manohvā indragopako
                            jīvaviśeṣaḥ etaiśca madhusahitaiḥ kṛtvā dvandvaṃ mipatītyavaśyam //
                            GRhtCM_12.7:4 //
children.translated_text: Not only with the previously stated formulas does [it] fuse, but furthermore with these also — castor oil, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, realgar, and <s>indragopa</s> — castor oil is <s>vātāri</s>-fat; <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgya</s> (borax); <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is <s>viraṅga</s> (red arsenic); <s>śilā</s> is realgar; <s>indragopa</s> is a particular insect — with these also, combined with honey, the binary [fusion] necessarily takes place. (GRhtCM 12.7:4)

children.text: melāpana of mercury, gold, and abhra
children.translated_text: [Section:] Fusion (<s>melāpana</s>) of mercury, gold, and mica

children.text: sūtena śuddhakanakaṃ niṣpiṣya samābhrayojitaṃ kṛtvā /
children.translated_text: Having ground purified gold together with mercury, and having made [it] combined with equal mica,

children.text: pādena tu pūrvoktadvandvānyatamakaṃ kalpyam // GRht_12.8 //
children.translated_text: one should prepare, in a quarter-portion, any one of the previously stated binary-[fusion agents]. (GRht 12.8)

children.text: tadvidhānamāha sūtenetyādi // GRhtCM_12.8:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the method for that with 'sūtena' (with mercury) and so forth. (GRhtCM 12.8:1)

children.text:
prathamaṃ sūtena rasena saha śuddhakanakaṃ niṣpiṣya saṃmardya punaḥ
                            samābhrayojitaṃ kṛtvā samaṃ ca tadabhraṃ ca tena yojitaṃ kṛtvā
                            paścātpādena caturthāṃśavibhāgena pūrvoktadvandvānyatamakaṃ kappyaṃ
                            pūrvoktadvandvam eraṇḍataipādikaṃ girijatvādikaṃ ca tebhyo 'nyatamakaṃ
                            dvandvaṃ yojyamiti // GRhtCM_12.8:2 //
children.translated_text: First, having ground purified gold together with mercury — with <s>rasa</s> — having rubbed [them]; furthermore, having made [it] combined with equal mica — equal to it is the mica, combined with that; thereafter, in a quarter-portion — in a one-fourth division — one should prepare any one of the previously stated binary [agents] — the previously stated binary [agent] such as the castor-oil formula or the bitumen formula — from among those, any one binary [agent] should be employed. (GRhtCM 12.8:2)

children.text: melāpana of gold and abhra
children.translated_text: [Section:] Fusion (<s>melāpana</s>) of gold and mica

children.text: rasoparasasya hemno dviguṇaṃ śuddhamākṣikaṃ dattvā /
children.translated_text: Having added double the amount of purified <s>mākṣika</s> (iron pyrite) relative to the gold, from among the minerals and subsidiary minerals,

children.text: svarasena kākamācyā rambhākandena mṛdnīyāt // GRht_12.9 //
children.translated_text: one should grind with the juice of <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade) and with plantain stem. (GRht 12.9)

children.text: kṛtamityetatpiṇḍaṃ hemābhraṃ milati vajramūṣāyām /
children.translated_text: This made [into a] pellet — gold and mica fuse in the diamond-crucible (<s>vajramūṣā</s>).

children.text: vidhyantaramāha rasetyādi // GRhtCM_12.9:1 //
children.translated_text: He states an alternative method with 'rasa' and so forth. (GRhtCM 12.9:1)

children.text:
rasoparasasya vaikrāntagandhakādermadhye śuddhamākṣikaṃ nirdoṣaṃ
                                tāpyaṃ hemno dviguṇaṃ kanakāddviguṇitaṃ dattvā dviguṇamākṣikayutaṃ
                                hema dattvetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_12.9:2 //
children.translated_text: From among the minerals and subsidiary minerals — from among <s>vaikrānta</s>, sulfur, and the like — purified <s>mākṣika</s> — flawless iron pyrite — double the gold, double the amount of gold, having added — meaning the gold combined with double <s>mākṣika</s> having been given — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 12.9:2)

children.text:
etadrasoparasādikaṃ kākamācyā vāyasyāḥ svarasena mṛdnīyāt mardanaṃ
                                kuryāt // GRhtCM_12.9:3 //
children.translated_text: This [preparation] of minerals, subsidiary minerals, and the like should be ground with the juice of <s>kākamācī</s> — <s>vāyasī</s> (black nightshade) — one should perform the grinding. (GRhtCM 12.9:3)

children.text: rambhākandena ca kadalīkandenāpītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_12.9:4 //
children.translated_text: And with plantain stem — with <s>kadalī</s>-stem also — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 12.9:4)

children.text: etatpūrvauṣadhaṃ piṇḍaṃ golākāraṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_12.9:5 //
children.translated_text: This aforementioned medicinal [mixture] should be made into a pellet — a ball-shaped form. (GRhtCM 12.9:5)

children.text: itividhānena hemābhraṃ milati hematāpyaṃ ceti // GRhtCM_12.9:6 //
children.translated_text: By this procedure, gold and mica fuse — as do gold and pyrite. (GRhtCM 12.9:6)

children.text: kva vajramūṣāyām // GRhtCM_12.9:7 //
children.translated_text: Where? In the diamond-crucible (<s>vajramūṣā</s>). (GRhtCM 12.9:7)

children.text: tathāha /
children.translated_text: Thus it is stated:

children.text: mṛdastribhāgāḥ śaṇaladdibhāgau bhāgaśca nirdagdhatuṣopalādeḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Three parts of clay, parts of hemp and lac, and a part of burnt husk and stone,

children.text: kiṭṭārdhabhāgaṃ parikhaṇḍya vajramūṣāṃ vidadhyātkhalu satvapāte /
children.translated_text: half a part of iron slag — having cut [and mixed these], one should make a diamond-crucible for essence-extraction.'

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_12.9:8 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 12.9:8)

children.text: melāpana of abhrasattva with diff. substances
children.translated_text: [Section:] Fusion (<s>melāpana</s>) of mica-essence with different substances

children.text: raviśaśitīkṣṇairevaṃ milanti gaganādisatvāni // GRht_12.10 //
children.translated_text: With copper (sun), silver (moon), and steel — thus the essences of mica and the like fuse [with them]. (GRht 12.10)

children.text:
evam amunā vidhinā raviśaśitīkṣṇaiḥ saha ravistāmraṃ śaśī rūpyaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ
                            pohajātiḥ etaiḥ sārdhaṃ gaganādisatvāni abhrādīnāṃ sārāṇi mipantīti
                            yugmam // GRhtCM_12.10:1 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by this method — with copper (sun), silver (moon), and steel — with these, the essences of mica and the like — the extracts of mica and others — fuse; [this is] the paired [verse]. (GRhtCM 12.10:1)

children.text: melāpana for saṅkarabījas
children.translated_text: [Section:] Fusion (<s>melāpana</s>) for <s>saṅkarabījas</s> (mixed seeds)

children.text: saṅkarabījānāmapi vidhānamityādi gaganasatvayogena /
children.translated_text: The procedure for <s>saṅkarabījas</s> (mixed seeds) also — 'iti' and so forth — by conjunction with mica-essence;

children.text: mākṣīkayogādanyaṃ yojyamavaśyaṃ tu sarvatra // GRht_12.11 //
children.translated_text: other than the <s>mākṣika</s>-conjunction, [another substance] should necessarily be employed everywhere. (GRht 12.11)

children.text: abhrasatvasyādhikāramāha saṃkaretyādi // GRhtCM_12.11:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the domain of mica-essence with 'saṅkara' and so forth. (GRhtCM 12.11:1)

children.text:
saṅkarabījānāmapi vidhānaṃ kartavyārthopadeśa iti yāvat // GRhtCM_12.11:2
                            //
children.translated_text: The procedure for <s>saṅkarabījas</s> should also be done — the instruction for the purpose to be accomplished — this much [is meant]. (GRhtCM 12.11:2)

'Iti' and so forth — as previously stated — but furthermore, by conjunction with mica-essence — together with mica-extract — other than the <s>mākṣika</s>-conjunction should be employed; [meaning] <s>mākṣika</s> should not be together with mica-essence — this is the clarification. (GRhtCM 12.11:3)

children.text: kāntamukhaṃ sarveṣāṃ sattvānāṃ melakaṃ prathamam /
children.translated_text: The <s>kānta</s>-mouth (lodestone-method) is the primary fusing-agent for all essences;

children.text: pūrvoktakalkasahitaṃ mākṣīkamṛtanāgatālaśilam // GRht_12.12 //
children.translated_text: combined with the previously stated paste — <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>mṛta</s> (calcined metal), lead, orpiment, and realgar. (GRht 12.12)

children.text:
iti paramahaṃsaparivrājakācāryaśrīmadgovindabhagavatpādaviracite
                                rasahṛdayatantre dvandvādhikārātmako dvādaśo+avabodhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twelfth chapter (<s>avabodha</s>), consisting of the topic of pairs (<s>dvandvādhikāra</s>), in the <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> composed by the most venerable <s>Govindabhagavatpāda</s>, the teacher of the order of supreme renunciants (<s>paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācārya</s>).

children.text: kāntetyādi // GRhtCM_12.12:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'With <s>kānta</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 12.12:1)

children.text:
mākṣikeṇa mṛtaṃ yannāgaṃ tāpaṃ haritāpaṃ śipā manohvā ca tattathā
                            pūrvoktakapkasahitaṃ yatkapkaṃ rasoparasādīnāṃ tena sahitaṃ yuktaṃ
                            kāntamukhaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: Lead (<s>nāga</s>) killed with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), [combined with] orpiment (<s>tāla</s>, i.e., <s>haritāla</s>) and realgar (<s>śilā</s>, i.e., <s>manohvā</s>), along with the aforementioned compound (<s>kalka</s>) — the compound of <s>rasas</s>, sub-metals, and the like — combined with that, with lodestone (<s>kānta</s>) as the primary [agent]; as [it is said]:

children.text: abhāve'bhrakasattvasya kāntasattvaṃ pradāpayet /
children.translated_text: In the absence of mica-essence (<s>abhraka-sattva</s>), one should give lodestone-essence (<s>kānta-sattva</s>);

children.text: kāntasatvasya vābhāve tīkṣṇapohaṃ tu dāpayet /
children.translated_text: in the absence of lodestone-essence, one should give iron (<s>tīkṣṇa-loha</s>).

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_12.12:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 12.12:2)

children.text: mākṣīkakāntatīkṣṇaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ mākṣīkam abhrakaṃ bījam /
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣīka</s> (pyrite), <s>kānta</s> (lodestone), and <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron) [form one]; <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, <s>mākṣīka</s>, and <s>abhraka</s> (mica) [form] the seed;

children.text: mākṣīkakāntaśulbaṃ tīkṣṇābhrakaṃ mahābījam // GRht_13.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>mākṣīka</s>, <s>kānta</s>, and <s>śulba</s> (copper) [form one]; <s>tīkṣṇa</s> and <s>abhraka</s> [form] the great seed (<s>mahābīja</s>). (GRht 13.1)

children.text: madhuni mādhava eva madhuvrataḥ prakurute mudito madhuraṃ ravam /
children.translated_text: In spring (<s>madhu</s>), the bee (<s>madhuvrata</s>), like <s>Mādhava</s> himself, joyfully produces a sweet sound;

children.text:
vararavo+api satāṃ ca samāgamaṃ śabapatā kimupaiti na cārutām //
                            GRhtCM_13.1:1 //
children.translated_text: even with an excellent voice, does the beauty of a gathering of good people not attain charm through eloquence? (GRhtCM 13.1:1)

children.text:
saṃkarabījānāṃ madhye mahābījasaṃjñānyāha mākṣiketyādi // GRhtCM_13.1:2
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Among the compound seeds (<s>saṃkara-bīja</s>), he states those designated as 'great seed' (<s>mahābīja</s>), with '<s>mākṣīka</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 13.1:2)

children.text:
etattrikaṃ mahābījaṃ kimetat mākṣīkakāntatīkṣṇaṃ mākṣīkakāntaśupbaṃ
                            tīkṣṇābhrakaṃ ca mākṣīkaṃ tāpyaṃ kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ śupbaṃ tāmraṃ tīkṣṇaṃ
                            pohajātir abhrakaṃ gaganaṃ etattritayaṃ bījaṃ mahābījaṃ etattritrimukhaṃ
                            pratyekaṃ mahāsaṃjñam // GRhtCM_13.1:3 //
children.translated_text: This triad is a great seed. What is it? <s>Mākṣīka</s>-<s>kānta</s>-<s>tīkṣṇa</s>, <s>mākṣīka</s>-<s>kānta</s>-<s>śulba</s>, and <s>tīkṣṇa</s>-<s>abhraka</s>. <s>Mākṣīka</s> is <s>tāpya</s> (gold-pyrite); <s>kānta</s> is <s>cumbaka</s> (lodestone); <s>śulba</s> is <s>tāmra</s> (copper); <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is a type of iron (<s>loha</s>); <s>abhraka</s> is <s>gagana</s> (mica). This triad is 'seed' — 'great seed.' Each of these three combinations individually bears the designation 'great' (<s>mahā</s>). (GRhtCM 13.1:3)

children.text: viśeṣo+atra /
children.translated_text: The distinction here [is as follows]:

children.text: bījapākaṃ pravakṣyāmi jāraṇārthaṃ rasasya tu /
children.translated_text: I shall describe the seed-preparation (<s>bīja-pāka</s>) for the purpose of digesting (<s>jāraṇa</s>) mercury.

children.text: sūtrakramo+ayaṃ bījena samajīrṇena śudhyati /
children.translated_text: This is the method (<s>sūtra-krama</s>): [mercury] is purified by the seed that has been equally digested.

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_13.1:4 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 13.1:4)

children.text:
avāntaratvena ca pratyekaṃ dravyaṃ bījasaṃjñābhimatam // GRhtCM_13.1:5
                            //
children.translated_text: And in a secondary sense, each individual substance is intended [to bear] the designation 'seed.' (GRhtCM 13.1:5)

children.text: mākṣīkakāntaśulbaṃ śulbābhrakamākṣikaṃ cāpi /
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣīka</s>, <s>kānta</s>, and <s>śulba</s> [form one]; <s>śulba</s>, <s>abhraka</s>, and <s>mākṣika</s> also [form one];

children.text: kāntābhrakamākṣīkaṃ tāpyakaśulbābhrakaṃ mahābījam // GRht_13.2 //
children.translated_text: <s>kānta</s>, <s>abhraka</s>, and <s>mākṣīka</s> [form one]; <s>tāpya</s>, <s>śulba</s>, and <s>abhraka</s> [form] the great seed. (GRht 13.2)

children.text: taccāha mākṣīketyādi // GRhtCM_13.2:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that, with '<s>mākṣīka</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 13.2:1)

children.text:
mākṣīkakāntaśupbaṃ mākṣīkaṃ tāpyaṃ kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ śupbaṃ tāmraṃ etadapi
                            mahābījaṃ jñeyam // GRhtCM_13.2:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣīka</s>-<s>kānta</s>-<s>śulba</s>: <s>mākṣīka</s> is <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite); <s>kānta</s> is <s>cumbaka</s> (lodestone); <s>śulba</s> is <s>tāmra</s> (copper) — this too should be known as a great seed. (GRhtCM 13.2:2)

children.text:
punaḥ śupbābhrakamākṣīkaṃ punaḥ kāntābhrakamākṣīkaṃ kāntaṃ kāntapāṣāṇaṃ
                            abhrakaṃ gaganaṃ mākṣīkaṃ tāpyaṃ tathā tāpyakaśupbābhrakaṃ etadapi ca
                            mahābījaṃ jñeyamiti // GRhtCM_13.2:3 //
children.translated_text: Again, <s>śulba</s>-<s>abhraka</s>-<s>mākṣīka</s>; again, <s>kānta</s>-<s>abhraka</s>-<s>mākṣīka</s> — <s>kānta</s> is lodestone (<s>kānta-pāṣāṇa</s>); <s>abhraka</s> is <s>gagana</s> (mica); <s>mākṣīka</s> is <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite). Likewise, <s>tāpya</s>-<s>śulba</s>-<s>abhraka</s> — this too should be known as a great seed. (GRhtCM 13.2:3)

children.text: mākṣīkatīkṣṇaśulbaṃ tīkṣṇaśulbābhrakaṃ mahābījam /
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣīka</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>śulba</s> [form one]; <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, <s>śulba</s>, and <s>abhraka</s> [form] a great seed;

children.text: mākṣīkakāntakanakaṃ kanakāruṇamākṣikaṃ mahābījam // GRht_13.3 //
children.translated_text: <s>mākṣīka</s>, <s>kānta</s>, and <s>kanaka</s> (gold) [form one]; <s>kanaka</s>, <s>aruṇa</s> (copper), and <s>mākṣika</s> [form] a great seed. (GRht 13.3)

children.text: taccāha mākṣīketyādi // GRhtCM_13.3:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that, with '<s>mākṣīka</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 13.3:1)

children.text:
mākṣīkatīkṣṇaśupbaṃ mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ sārapohajātiḥ śupbaṃ tāmram
                            // GRhtCM_13.3:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣīka</s>-<s>tīkṣṇa</s>-<s>śulba</s>: <s>mākṣika</s> is <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite); <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is the iron type called <s>sāra</s>; <s>śulba</s> is <s>tāmra</s> (copper). (GRhtCM 13.3:2)

children.text:
punastīkṣṇaśupbābhrakaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ sāraṃ śupbaṃ tāmraṃ abhrakaṃ gaganam //
                            GRhtCM_13.3:3 //
children.translated_text: Again, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>-<s>śulba</s>-<s>abhraka</s>: <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is <s>sāra</s> (steel); <s>śulba</s> is <s>tāmra</s> (copper); <s>abhraka</s> is <s>gagana</s> (mica). (GRhtCM 13.3:3)

children.text:
punarmākṣīkakāntakanakaṃ mākṣīkaṃ tāpyaṃ kāntaṃ kāntapāṣāṇaṃ kanakaṃ
                            svarṇam // GRhtCM_13.3:4 //
children.translated_text: Again, <s>mākṣīka</s>-<s>kānta</s>-<s>kanaka</s>: <s>mākṣīka</s> is <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite); <s>kānta</s> is lodestone (<s>kānta-pāṣāṇa</s>); <s>kanaka</s> is <s>svarṇa</s> (gold). (GRhtCM 13.3:4)

children.text:
punaḥ kanakāruṇamākṣikaṃ kanakaṃ svarṇaṃ aruṇaṃ tāmraṃ mākṣikaṃ
                            svarṇamākṣikaṃ ceti catuṣṭayaṃ mahābījaṃ pravarabījam ityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_13.3:5 //
children.translated_text: Again, <s>kanaka</s>-<s>aruṇa</s>-<s>mākṣika</s>: <s>kanaka</s> is <s>svarṇa</s> (gold); <s>aruṇa</s> is <s>tāmra</s> (copper); <s>mākṣika</s> is <s>svarṇamākṣika</s> (gold-pyrite) — thus this group of four is the great seed — the supreme seed, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 13.3:5)

children.text: caturṇāṃ pratyekaṃ mahābījasaṃjñeti // GRhtCM_13.3:6 //
children.translated_text: Each of the four [individually] bears the designation 'great seed.' (GRhtCM 13.3:6)

children.text: mākṣīkatīkṣṇatāraṃ tārāruṇamākṣikaṃ caivam /
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣīka</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>tāra</s> (silver) [form one]; <s>tāra</s>, <s>aruṇa</s> (copper), and <s>mākṣika</s> likewise [form one];

children.text: kāntaṃ tu śulbatāpyaṃ śulbābhratāpyakāṃcanaṃ cāpi // GRht_13.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>kānta</s> with <s>śulba</s> (copper) and <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite) [form one]; and also <s>śulba</s>, <s>abhra</s> (mica), <s>tāpya</s>, and <s>kāñcana</s> (gold). (GRht 13.4)

children.text: taccāha mākṣīkatīkṣṇatāramiti // GRhtCM_13.4:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that, with '<s>mākṣīka</s>-<s>tīkṣṇa</s>-<s>tāra</s>.' (GRhtCM 13.4:1)

children.text: mākṣīkaṃ tāpyaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ sāraṃ tāraṃ rūpyam // GRhtCM_13.4:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣīka</s> is <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite); <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is <s>sāra</s> (steel); <s>tāra</s> is <s>rūpya</s> (silver). (GRhtCM 13.4:2)

children.text:
punastārāruṇamākṣikaṃ evamuktavidhānena idamapi tāraṃ rūpyaṃ aruṇaṃ
                            tāmraṃ mākṣīkaṃ tāpyam // GRhtCM_13.4:3 //
children.translated_text: Again, <s>tāra</s>-<s>aruṇa</s>-<s>mākṣika</s> — by the same method as stated — this too: <s>tāra</s> is <s>rūpya</s> (silver); <s>aruṇa</s> is <s>tāmra</s> (copper); <s>mākṣīka</s> is <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite). (GRhtCM 13.4:3)

children.text:
punaḥ kānte cumbake'bhivyāpake adhikaraṇe śupbaṃ tāmraṃ tāpyaṃ
                            svarṇamākṣikaṃ yat prayuktam // GRhtCM_13.4:4 //
children.translated_text: Again, in [the combination headed by] <s>kānta</s> (lodestone), which is pervading and serves as the base: <s>śulba</s> is <s>tāmra</s> (copper); <s>tāpya</s> is <s>svarṇamākṣika</s> (gold-pyrite) — that which is employed [with lodestone]. (GRhtCM 13.4:4)

children.text: apīti niścayena // GRhtCM_13.4:5 //
children.translated_text: 'Also' (<s>api</s>) [is used] for emphasis. (GRhtCM 13.4:5)

children.text:
śupbābhratāpyakāñcanaṃ vā śupbaṃ tāmraṃ abhraṃ gaganaṃ tāpyaṃ
                            svarṇamākṣikaṃ kāñcanaṃ hema etaccatuṣṭayamapi mahābījaṃ jñeyam //
                            GRhtCM_13.4:6 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śulba</s>-<s>abhra</s>-<s>tāpya</s>-<s>kāñcana</s>, or: <s>śulba</s> is <s>tāmra</s> (copper); <s>abhra</s> is <s>gagana</s> (mica); <s>tāpya</s> is <s>svarṇamākṣika</s> (gold-pyrite); <s>kāñcana</s> is <s>hema</s> (gold) — this group of four too should be known as a great seed. (GRhtCM 13.4:6)

children.text: mahābījasaṃbandhaḥ pratyekamiti vyaktiḥ // GRhtCM_13.4:7 //
children.translated_text: The connection to the great seed — each [combination] individually — this is the explanation. (GRhtCM 13.4:7)

children.text: kāntendusasyatāpyaṃ kāntābhrakatīkṣṇamākṣikaṃ caiva /
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s> (lodestone), <s>indu</s> (silver), <s>sasya</s> (tin/calamine), and <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite) [form one]; <s>kānta</s>, <s>abhraka</s> (mica), <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron), and <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) also [form one];

children.text: hemābhraśulbatāpyaṃ hemābhrakaśulbamākṣikaṃ vāpi // GRht_13.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>hema</s> (gold), <s>abhra</s> (mica), <s>śulba</s> (copper), and <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite) [form one]; and also <s>hema</s>, <s>abhraka</s>, <s>śulba</s>, and <s>mākṣika</s>. (GRht 13.5)

children.text: taccāha kāntendusasyatāpyamiti // GRhtCM_13.5:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that, with '<s>kānta</s>-<s>indu</s>-<s>sasya</s>-<s>tāpya</s>.' (GRhtCM 13.5:1)

children.text:
kāntaṃ kāntapāṣāṇaṃ industāraṃ sasyaṃ capapā tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ ceti
                            // GRhtCM_13.5:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s> is lodestone (<s>kānta-pāṣāṇa</s>); <s>indu</s> is <s>tāra</s> (silver); <s>sasya</s> is <s>capalā</s> (tin/calamine); <s>tāpya</s> is <s>svarṇamākṣika</s> (gold-pyrite). (GRhtCM 13.5:2)

children.text:
punaḥ kāntābhrakatīkṣṇamākṣikaṃ tathā hemābhraśupbatāpyaṃ
                            punarhemābhrakaśupbamākṣikaṃ vā hema kanakaṃ abhrakaṃ gaganaṃ śupbaṃ
                            tāmraṃ mākṣīkaṃ tāpyaṃ etaccatuṣṭayamapi mahābījaṃ jñeyam //
                            GRhtCM_13.5:3 //
children.translated_text: Again, <s>kānta</s>-<s>abhraka</s>-<s>tīkṣṇa</s>-<s>mākṣika</s>; likewise, <s>hema</s>-<s>abhra</s>-<s>śulba</s>-<s>tāpya</s>; again, <s>hema</s>-<s>abhraka</s>-<s>śulba</s>-<s>mākṣika</s>, or: <s>hema</s> is <s>kanaka</s> (gold); <s>abhraka</s> is <s>gagana</s> (mica); <s>śulba</s> is <s>tāmra</s> (copper); <s>mākṣīka</s> is <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite) — this group of four too should be known as a great seed. (GRhtCM 13.5:3)

children.text: pratyekadravye bījasaṃjñā ceti dhvanyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_13.5:4 //
children.translated_text: The designation 'seed' applies to each individual substance — this is the implied meaning. (GRhtCM 13.5:4)

children.text: kāntābhraśulbatāpyaṃ saṅkarabījaṃ catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ // GRht_13.6 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s> (lodestone), <s>abhra</s> (mica), <s>śulba</s> (copper), and <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite) [form one] — the compound seeds total sixty-four. (GRht 13.6)

children.text: taccāha kāntetyādi // GRhtCM_13.6:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that, with '<s>kānta</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 13.6:1)

children.text:
kāntābhraśupbatāpyaṃ kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ abhrakaṃ gaganaṃ śupbaṃ tāmraṃ
                            tāpyaṃ mākṣikaṃ ityapi mahābījam // GRhtCM_13.6:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s>-<s>abhra</s>-<s>śulba</s>-<s>tāpya</s>: <s>kānta</s> is <s>cumbaka</s> (lodestone); <s>abhraka</s> is <s>gagana</s> (mica); <s>śulba</s> is <s>tāmra</s> (copper); <s>tāpya</s> is <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) — this too is a great seed. (GRhtCM 13.6:2)

children.text:
eteṣāṃ mahābījānāṃ cet saṃkarabījaṃ pratyekaṃ dravyasya bījasaṃjñā sā
                            tarhi catuḥṣaṣṭipramāṇā syādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_13.6:3 //
children.translated_text: If the compound seeds of these great seeds — the designation 'seed' for each individual substance — then the total amounts to sixty-four, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 13.6:3)

children.text: mahābīja:: production
children.translated_text: Great seed: production

children.text: sarveṣāṃ bījānāmādau kṛtvā yathoktasaṃyogam /
children.translated_text: Having first made the prescribed combination of all the seeds,

children.text: śatavāpyaṃ yadvahnau drāvitaṃ hi bījaṃ viśuddhamidaṃ // GRht_13.7 //
children.translated_text: that which is heated a hundred times and melted in fire — this is the purified seed. (GRht 13.7)

children.text: bījavidhānam āha sarveṣām ityādi // GRhtCM_13.7:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the seed-procedure, with 'of all' and so forth. (GRhtCM 13.7:1)

children.text:
ādau prathamaṃ sarveṣāṃ bījānāṃ yathoktaṃ saṃyogaṃ catuḥṣaṣṭīnāṃ
                            uktasaṃjñānāṃ dravyāṇāṃ saṃyogaṃ ekatrīkaraṇaṃ kṛtvā yadekatrīkṛtaṃ
                            vahnau drāvitaṃ bhavati tatsarvaṃ śatavāpyaṃ bījaṃ siddhaṃ prayatnena
                            syāditi śabdārthaḥ // GRhtCM_13.7:2 //
children.translated_text: First — initially — of all the seeds, having made the prescribed combination — the combination as stated — of the sixty-four designated substances, making them into one; that which, when unified, is melted in fire — [heated] a hundred times (<s>śata-vāpya</s>) — all that seed becomes accomplished with effort, is the verbal meaning. (GRhtCM 13.7:2)

children.text: cāraṇa, garbha- and bāhyadruti necessary for bandhana
children.translated_text: <s>Cāraṇa</s> (sweeping), internal and external dissolution (<s>garbha-</s> and <s>bāhya-druti</s>) — necessary for binding (<s>bandhana</s>)

children.text: na patati yadi ghanasatvaṃ garbhe no vā dravanti bījāni /
children.translated_text: If the dense essence (<s>ghana-sattva</s>) does not enter the interior (<s>garbha</s>), or if the seeds do not dissolve inside,

children.text: na ca bāhyadrutiyogastatkathamiha badhyate sūtaḥ // GRht_13.8 //
children.translated_text: and if there is no external dissolution (<s>bāhya-druti</s>) process — then how can mercury be bound here? (GRht 13.8)

children.text: sūtabandhane hetūnāha netyādi // GRhtCM_13.8:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the causes for mercury-binding, with 'not' and so forth. (GRhtCM 13.8:1)

children.text:
yadi garbhe rasodare ghanasattvaṃ abhrakasāraṃ na patati na prāpnoti vā
                            garbhe bījāni asminnadhyāye abhihitāni mākṣikakāntaśupbādīni yāvanno
                            dravanti ca punarbāhyadrutistasyā yogo rase drutimepanaṃ na syāt
                            tattasmāddhetoḥ sūta ihāsyāṃ kriyāyāmasatyāṃ kathaṃ badhyate ghanatvaṃ
                            dhatte // GRhtCM_13.8:2 //
children.translated_text: If the dense essence (<s>ghana-sattva</s>) — the essence of mica (<s>abhraka-sāra</s>) — does not enter, does not reach, the interior (<s>garbha</s>) — the belly of mercury; or if the seeds — those described in this chapter, <s>mākṣika</s>-<s>kānta</s>-<s>śulba</s> and so forth — do not dissolve inside; and again, if there is no external dissolution (<s>bāhya-druti</s>) — if the process of melting the dissolution into mercury does not occur; then, for that reason, mercury — in this procedure — how can it be bound without these? How can it attain solidity? (GRhtCM 13.8:2)

children.text:
garbhadrutibāhyadrutibhyāṃ sūto badhyate niyatamityabhiprāyaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_13.8:3 //
children.translated_text: The intent is that mercury is bound necessarily through internal dissolution and external dissolution. (GRhtCM 13.8:3)

children.text: production of gold:: preparing the mercury
children.translated_text: Production of gold: preparing the mercury

children.text: samād adhi ca yajjīrṇaṃ bījaṃ tenaiva cāvartatā kāryā /
children.translated_text: The seed that has been digested in equal or greater [quantity] — with that very [seed], the revolving (<s>āvarta</s>) should be performed;

children.text: kartavyaṃ tatkaraṇaṃ yasmātkhalu jāyate hema // GRht_14.1 //
children.translated_text: that procedure should be carried out, for from it indeed gold is produced. (GRht 14.1)

children.text: śaradi śāradamegho varṣati varṣāsu vārṣiko vārdaḥ /
children.translated_text: In autumn, the autumn-cloud rains; in the rainy season, the monsoon stream [flows];

children.text:
madhusamaye parapuṣṭaḥ pravarajavaḥ śobhate satatam // GRhtCM_14.1:1
                            //
children.translated_text: in the spring season, the cuckoo (<s>parapuṣṭa</s>), of supreme swiftness, always shines. (GRhtCM 14.1:1)

children.text: bījajāraṇātkiṃ bhavati tadāha samādītyādi // GRhtCM_14.1:2 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] What results from seed-digestion? He states that, with 'equal' and so forth. (GRhtCM 14.1:2)

children.text:
samaṃ sūtatupyaṃ adhiśabdād aparimitaṃ samādadhikaṃ yajjīrṇaṃ
                            jāraṇamāptaṃ bījaṃ niṣpannabījaṃ tenaiva jīrṇena bījena saha āvartatā
                            kāryā āvarta iti āvartaḥ // GRhtCM_14.1:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Equal' — equal to the weight of mercury; by the word 'greater' (<s>adhi</s>), [meaning] unlimited — more than equal; that which has been digested — has undergone digestion (<s>jāraṇa</s>); the seed — the accomplished seed; with that very digested seed, the revolving (<s>āvarta</s>) should be performed — <s>āvarta</s> means 'revolving' (<s>āvartaḥ</s>). (GRhtCM 14.1:3)

children.text:
kiṃ tat yasmādvidhānāddhema kanakaṃ jāyate khapu niścayena tatkaraṇaṃ
                            tasya vidhānasya karaṇam // GRhtCM_14.1:4 //
children.translated_text: What is that? That procedure from which gold (<s>kanaka</s>) is produced — certainly, without doubt; the carrying out of that procedure. (GRhtCM 14.1:4)

children.text:
samādijīrṇasya sūtasya rūpyādiṣu prayogātkanakaṃ bhavediti vyaktiḥ //
                            GRhtCM_14.1:5 //
children.translated_text: The explanation is that from the mercury in which [seed] has been digested in equal or greater quantity, through application upon silver and other [metals], gold would result. (GRhtCM 14.1:5)

children.text: rasabīja:: production
children.translated_text: Mercury-seed (<s>rasa-bīja</s>): production

children.text: pradrāvya śastrapātre gandhapādena sūtakaṃ dadyāt /
children.translated_text: Having melted [it] in an iron vessel, one should add mercury at one-quarter the portion of sulphur (<s>gandha</s>);

children.text: svarasena cauṣadhīnāṃ vaṭikāṃ niṣpiṣya kurvīta // GRht_14.2 //
children.translated_text: with the juice of herbs, having ground [it], one should make a pellet. (GRht 14.2)

children.text: saṃsthāpya lohaphalake chāyāśuṣkāṃ tu tāṃ vaṭikām /
children.translated_text: Having placed the pellet, shade-dried, on an iron plate,

children.text: laghulohakaṭorikayā sthagayitvā lepayetsudṛḍham // GRht_14.3 //
children.translated_text: covering with a small iron bowl (<s>kaṭorikā</s>), one should seal [it] firmly. (GRht 14.3)

children.text: lavaṇārdramṛdā liptāṃ sudṛḍhaṃ kurvīta dhūmrarodhāya /
children.translated_text: Sealed firmly with salt-moistened clay, for the purpose of preventing smoke,

children.text: dattvā sudṛḍhāṃgārān bhastrādvayavahninaiva nirdhūme // GRht_14.4 //
children.translated_text: having placed firm charcoals, with the fire of two bellows alone, in a smokeless [furnace], (GRht 14.4)

children.text: tāvadyāvaddhmātā raktābhā khoṭikā bhavati /
children.translated_text: one should blow until the <s>khoṭikā</s> (lump) becomes red-hued;

children.text: apanīya tato+aṅgārān svabhāvaśītāṃ kaṭorikāṃ matvā // GRht_14.5 //
children.translated_text: having removed the charcoals then, considering the bowl to be naturally cooled, (GRht 14.5)

children.text: utkhanyotkhanya tataḥ kaṭorikāyā raso grāhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: then, having dug out [the contents] from the bowl repeatedly, the mercury should be collected;

children.text: eṣaḥ mṛtasūtarājo golakavadbhavati ca sa sukhādhmātaḥ // GRht_14.6 //
children.translated_text: this is the killed king of mercury — it becomes like a ball, and when easily smelted, (GRht 14.6)

children.text: śikhigalatām ekaraso+atidhmātaḥ kācaṭaṃkaṇataḥ /
children.translated_text: [it takes on] peacock-throat [luster]; this one-mercury (<s>ekarasa</s>), when excessively smelted, with glass (<s>kāca</s>) and borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>),

children.text: triguṇaṃ vaṅgaṃ dadyātkrameṇa nāgam alpālpadānena // GRht_14.7 //
children.translated_text: one should add tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) at three times [the quantity], and lead (<s>nāga</s>) gradually, in small doses. (GRht 14.7)

children.text: paścāddhemnā yojyaṃ rasabījaṃ sūtabandhakaram /
children.translated_text: Afterward, the mercury-seed should be joined with gold — [this is] the agent for binding mercury.

children.text: sūtamāraṇavidhānam āha pradrāvyetyādi // GRhtCM_14.2-7:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the procedure for killing mercury, with 'having melted' and so forth. (GRhtCM 14.2–7:1)

children.text:
śastrapātre tīkṣṇamayapātre aupaśleṣike'dhikaraṇe saptamī //
                                GRhtCM_14.2-7:2 //
children.translated_text: 'In an iron vessel' — in a vessel made of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron); the locative case indicates the container. (GRhtCM 14.2–7:2)

children.text:
gandhapādena gandhasya turyāṃśavibhāgena sūtakaṃ dadyāt
                                tatpātroparibhāge dattaṃ pradrāvya vahninā iti śeṣaḥ //
                                GRhtCM_14.2-7:3 //
children.translated_text: 'At one-quarter the portion of sulphur' — with one-quarter measure of sulphur (<s>gandha</s>); one should add mercury (<s>sūtaka</s>) — placed on the upper part of that vessel; 'having melted' — with fire, is the completion. (GRhtCM 14.2–7:3)

children.text: punaḥ oṣadhīnāṃ svarasena auṣadhyo granthāntare yathā /
children.translated_text: Again, with the juice of herbs — the herbs, as [stated] in other treatises:

children.text: mṛdnīyātkhalu tāvat piṣṭamañjanasadṛśaṃ bhavedyāvat /
children.translated_text: One should indeed grind until the ground [mixture] becomes collyrium-like in appearance;

children.text: tadanu ca niyāmakānāṃ śatāvarīkandukīsudhādīnām /
children.translated_text: and thereafter, [with] the controlling substances (<s>niyāmaka</s>) — <s>Śatāvarī</s> (Asparagus racemosus), <s>Kandukī</s>, <s>Sudhā</s> (lime), and the like —

children.text: iti // GRhtCM_14.2-7:4 //
children.translated_text: Thus. (GRhtCM 14.2-7:4)

children.text:
śatāvaryādīnāṃ svakīyarasena niṣpiṣya pramardya vaṭikāṃ badarākarāṃ
                                kurvīteti // GRhtCM_14.2-7:5 //
children.translated_text: One should grind [the substances] with the juice of <s>śatāvarī</s> (Asparagus racemosus) and others, pressing them, and make a pill the size of a jujube fruit. (GRhtCM 14.2-7:5)

children.text: taccāha saṃsthāpyetyādi // GRhtCM_14.2-7:6 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that, with 'having placed' and so forth. (GRhtCM 14.2-7:6)

children.text:
tāṃ pūrvoktāṃ vaṭikāṃ chāyāśuṣkāṃ lohaphalake śastrapātre saṃsthāpya
                                punaḥ laghulohakaṭorikayā pūrvoktalohaphalakāt laghvī yā
                                lohakaṭorikā tayā sthagayitvā ācchādya dṛḍhaṃ gāḍhaṃ yathā syāttathā
                                lepayet vakṣyamāṇeneti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_14.2-7:7 //
children.translated_text: That aforementioned pill, dried in the shade, should be placed on an iron plate — a metallic vessel; then, having covered [it] with a small iron cup — a smaller cup than the aforementioned iron plate — having concealed [it], one should seal [it] firmly, as tightly as possible, with what will be described — this is the completion. (GRhtCM 14.2-7:7)

children.text: taccāha lavaṇetyādi // GRhtCM_14.2-7:8 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that, with 'salt' and so forth. (GRhtCM 14.2-7:8)

children.text:
tāṃ pūrvoditāṃ laghulohakaṭorikāṃ sudṛḍhaṃ yathā syāttathā
                                lavaṇārdramṛdā lavaṇena saindhavādinā yutā yā ārdrā jalasiktā mṛt
                                tayā liptāṃ kurvīta // GRhtCM_14.2-7:9 //
children.translated_text: That aforementioned small iron cup should be sealed very firmly with salt-moistened clay — clay mixed with salt such as <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt) and others, moistened with water — one should coat [it] with that. (GRhtCM 14.2-7:9)

children.text:
kimarthaṃ dhūmrarodhāya yathā yantrādbahirdhūmodgamo na syāt //
                                GRhtCM_14.2-7:10 //
children.translated_text: For what purpose? For preventing smoke-escape — so that no smoke escapes outward from the apparatus. (GRhtCM 14.2-7:10)

Then, having applied firm charcoals of <s>khadira</s> (Acacia catechu) and others, one should blow with double-bellows fire — indeed with fire from two [bellows] — from the connection with the next verse. (GRhtCM 14.2-7:11)

children.text:
kva sati nirdhūme sati rase dhūmaniḥsaraṇavarjite sati //
                                GRhtCM_14.2-7:12 //
children.translated_text: When? When the mercury is smoke-free — when the emission of smoke has ceased. (GRhtCM 14.2-7:12)

children.text: taccāha tāvadityādi // GRhtCM_14.2-7:13 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that, with 'until' and so forth. (GRhtCM 14.2-7:13)

children.text:
sandhiliptā pūrvoktā lohaśarāvikā tāvadavadhau dhmātā kāryā
                                yāvatkālapramāṇaṃ raktābhā raktadyutiyuktā khoṭikā bhavati
                                khoṭasyeva ākṛtiryasyāḥ sā khoṭikā // GRhtCM_14.2-7:14 //
children.translated_text: The aforementioned iron saucer, sealed at the joints, should be blown until — for such duration of time — the ingot (<s>khoṭikā</s>) becomes red-hued — endowed with red brilliance; a <s>khoṭikā</s> is that which has the shape of a <s>khoṭa</s> (ingot). (GRhtCM 14.2-7:14)

children.text:
tato+anantaraṃ kaṭorikāṃ svabhāvaśītalāṃ svato himāṃ matvā jñātvā
                                punaraṅgārānapanīya apasārya kaṭorikāmutkhanya raso grāhya iti śeṣaḥ
                                āgamiślokasaṃbandhāt // GRhtCM_14.2-7:15 //
children.translated_text: Thereafter, having known the cup to be naturally cooled — cool by itself — then having removed the charcoals, having cleared [them] away, one should dig up the cup and collect the mercury — this is the completion, from the connection with the following verse. (GRhtCM 14.2-7:15)

children.text: taccāha utkhanyetyādi // GRhtCM_14.2-7:16 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that, with 'having dug up' and so forth. (GRhtCM 14.2-7:16)

children.text:
tato+anantaraṃ laghulohakaṭorikāṃ pūrvavarṇitāṃ utkhanyotkhanya
                                prabalatvenotpāṭya rasaḥ sūto grāhyaḥ // GRhtCM_14.2-7:17 //
children.translated_text: Thereafter, having dug up — having forcefully extracted — the previously described small iron cup, the mercury (<s>sūta</s>) should be collected. (GRhtCM 14.2-7:17)

children.text:
utkhanyotkhanyeti kaṭhinataratvādvā atyādareṇa vīpsā //
                                GRhtCM_14.2-7:18 //
children.translated_text: The repetition 'having dug up, having dug up' is either because of [the cup's] extreme hardness, or expresses [the need for] great care. (GRhtCM 14.2-7:18)

children.text:
kutaḥ kaṭorikāsakāśāt eṣa itthamutpanno mṛtasūtarājo jñeyaḥ //
                                GRhtCM_14.2-7:19 //
children.translated_text: From where? From the cup — the mercury produced in this manner should be known as killed mercury (<s>mṛtasūtarāja</s>). (GRhtCM 14.2-7:19)

children.text:
sa ca sukhādhmātaḥ san golakavadbhavati vajramūṣāyāṃ iti śeṣaḥ //
                                GRhtCM_14.2-7:20 //
children.translated_text: And that [killed mercury], when easily blown, becomes like a globule — in a diamond-crucible (<s>vajramūṣā</s>), this is the completion. (GRhtCM 14.2-7:20)

'Glass' (<s>kāca</s>) is well-known; <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is borax (<s>saubhāgya</s>); then the mercury, having crossed beyond the limit, when blown, becomes of uniform essence (<s>ekarasa</s>) — of equal consistency, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 14.2-7:21)

children.text:
keṣāṃ śikhigalatāṃ śikhini galantīti vigrahaḥ śikhigalatāṃ dhātūnāṃ
                                evaṃ galite rase triguṇaṃ vaṅgaṃ raṅgaṃ dadyāt tato
                                vaṅgadānānantaraṃ krameṇa alpamalpadānena nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ ca dadyāditi
                                // GRhtCM_14.2-7:22 //
children.translated_text: Of what [metals]? Of those metals melting in fire — the resolution is: 'those that melt in fire.' When the mercury has thus melted, one should add three parts tin (<s>vaṅga</s>/<s>raṅga</s>); then, after adding tin, gradually — by giving small amounts at a time — one should add lead (<s>nāga</s>/<s>sīsaka</s>). (GRhtCM 14.2-7:22)

children.text: taccāha paścādityādi // GRhtCM_14.2-7:23 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that, with 'afterwards' and so forth. (GRhtCM 14.2-7:23)

children.text:
paścāt triguṇasīsakadānānantaraṃ hemnā kanakena saha rasabījaṃ
                                mahābījaṃ yojyaṃ hemnā sārdhaṃ mahābījaṃ kīdṛgbhavati //
                                GRhtCM_14.2-7:24 //
children.translated_text: Afterwards — after adding three-parts lead — the mercury-seed (<s>rasabīja</s>), i.e., the great seed (<s>mahābīja</s>), should be combined with gold (<s>heman</s>/kanaka); how does the great seed become when combined with gold? (GRhtCM 14.2-7:24)

children.text: mercury:: māraṇa
children.translated_text: [Section on] mercury: <s>māraṇa</s> (killing/calcination)

children.text: tālakasūtenāpi ca kṛtvā vaṭikāṃ niyāmakauṣadhibhiḥ // GRht_14.8 //
children.translated_text: And having also made a pill with <s>tālaka</s> (orpiment) and mercury, together with the restraining drugs (<s>niyāmakauṣadhi</s>) — (GRht 14.8)

children.text: evaṃ nigṛhya dhūmaṃ sudhiyā rasamāraṇaṃ kāryam /
children.translated_text: thus, having restrained the smoke, the wise one should perform the killing of mercury (<s>rasamāraṇa</s>).

children.text:
rasabandhakaraṃ pāradabandhapradaṃ ca punaḥ tālakaṃ haritālaṃ sūto
                                rasaḥ tenāpi niyāmakauṣadhibhiśca śatāvaryādibhiḥ pūrvoktābhir
                                guṭikāṃ kṛtvā nigṛhya dhūmaṃ rundhitadhūmaṃ yathā syāttathā sudhiyā
                                matimatā rasajñena evamamunā vidhinā rasamāraṇaṃ kāryaṃ
                                pāradabandhaḥ kārya ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_14.8:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That which effects the binding of mercury — gives the binding of <s>pārada</s> — and furthermore, <s>tālaka</s> is orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>); <s>sūta</s> means mercury; with that also, and with the restraining drugs — <s>śatāvarī</s> and the rest, mentioned before — having made a pill, having restrained the smoke — so that the smoke is blocked — the wise one — the intelligent one, the knower of mercury — in this very manner, by this method, should perform the killing of mercury — the binding of <s>pārada</s> should be done, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 14.8:1)

children.text: mercury:: māraṇa
children.translated_text: [Section on] mercury: <s>māraṇa</s> (killing/calcination)

children.text: athavā śilayā sūto mākṣikayogena vā siddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Or, mercury perfected with <s>śilā</s> (realgar), or by combination with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite),

children.text: jāyeta śuklavarṇo dhūmarodhena tābhyāṃ vā // GRht_14.9 //
children.translated_text: becomes white-colored — through smoke-restriction, or by [combining] both of these. (GRht 14.9)

children.text: anyaccāha athavetyādi // GRhtCM_14.9:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another [method], with 'or' and so forth. (GRhtCM 14.9:1)

children.text:
athavā vidhyantare śipayā manohvayā kṛtvā vā mākṣikayogena tāpyasaṃyogaṃ
                            kṛtvā sādhitastāpakayogavat sūto rasaḥ śukpavarṇo jayeta //
                            GRhtCM_14.9:2 //
children.translated_text: Or — in an alternative method — having worked with <s>śilā</s>, i.e., <s>manohvā</s> (realgar); or having worked through combination with <s>mākṣika</s> — the conjunction of pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>) — perfected as in the heating method; the mercury becomes white-colored. (GRhtCM 14.9:2)

children.text:
kena dhūmarodhena saindhavārdramṛdā pepena vā tābhyāṃ śipāmākṣikābhyām
                            ubhābhyāṃ tāpakayogavat sādhitaḥ san sūtaḥ śukpavarṇo bhaved iti //
                            GRhtCM_14.9:3 //
children.translated_text: By what? By smoke-restriction — [sealed] with salt-moistened clay — or by [using] both of those — <s>śilā</s> and <s>mākṣika</s> — with both; perfected as in the heating method, the mercury would become white-colored. (GRhtCM 14.9:3)

children.text: mercury:: mṛta:: medic. use
children.translated_text: [Section on] mercury: <s>mṛta</s> (killed/calcined): medicinal use

children.text: mṛtaśulvatāpyacūrṇaṃ kāntayutaṃ tena rañjayetkhoṭam /
children.translated_text: The powder of killed copper and pyrite, combined with magnetite — with that one should color the ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>);

children.text: nirvyūḍhaṃ ghanasatvahemayutaṃ tadrasāyane yojyam // GRht_14.10 //
children.translated_text: concentrated, combined with mica-essence and gold — that is to be employed in <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation therapy). (GRht 14.10)

children.text: anyaccāha mṛtetyādi // GRhtCM_14.10:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another [method], with 'killed' and so forth. (GRhtCM 14.10:1)

children.text:
mṛtaśupbatāpyacūrṇaṃ mṛtaṃ ca yat śupbaṃ tāmraṃ tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ ca
                            taccūrṇaṃ kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ kāntayutaṃ cumbakamiśritaṃ tena
                            mṛtaśupbatāpyacūrṇena kāntayutena pūrvaṃ niṣpannaṃ khoṭaṃ rañjayet //
                            GRhtCM_14.10:2 //
children.translated_text: The powder of killed copper (<s>śulba</s>/<s>tāmra</s>) and pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>/<s>svarṇamākṣika</s>) — of what quality? Combined with magnetite (<s>kānta</s>/loadstone) — with that killed-copper-and-pyrite powder combined with magnetite, one should color the previously produced ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>). (GRhtCM 14.10:2)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ ghanasattvahemayutaṃ abhrasatvasvarṇamiśritam //
                            GRhtCM_14.10:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality? Combined with mica-essence and gold — mixed with <s>abhrasattva</s> (mica-essence) and gold. (GRhtCM 14.10:3)

children.text:
evaṃvidhaṃ tatkhoṭaṃ rasāyane jarāvyādhināśane yojyam // GRhtCM_14.10:4
                            //
children.translated_text: Such an ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>) should be employed in <s>rasāyana</s> — in the destruction of old age and disease. (GRhtCM 14.10:4)
[Unclear passage]

children.text: balinā triguṇena rasāt parpaṭikayutena marditaṃ sūtam /
children.translated_text: Mercury ground with three-parts sulphur (<s>balin</s>), combined with metal-flake (<s>parpaṭikā</s>) —

children.text: niyāmakadivyauṣadhibhiśchāyāśuṣkā kṛtā vaṭikā // GRht_14.11 //
children.translated_text: [with] the restraining divine herbs, a pill dried in the shade is made. (GRht 14.11)
[Unclear passage]

children.text: mūṣādhṛtaparpaṭikāmadhye saṃchādya nigūḍhasudṛḍhena /
children.translated_text: Having covered [the pill] in the middle of a crucible-held metal-flake, with a firmly concealed [seal],

children.text: dhmātaṃ gacchati khoṭaṃ hemayutaṃ sūtabandhakaram // GRht_14.12 //
children.translated_text: when blown, it becomes an ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>) — combined with gold, effecting the binding of mercury. (GRht 14.12)

children.text: anyaccāha bapinetyādi // GRhtCM_14.11-12:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another [method], with 'sulphur' and so forth. (GRhtCM 14.11-12:1)

children.text:
triguṇena bapinā gandhakena saha rasaṃ sūtaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ yathā syāttathā
                            marditaṃ kuryāt ityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_14.11-12:2 //
children.translated_text: With three-parts sulphur (<s>balin</s>/gandhaka), one should grind the mercury (<s>sūta</s>) very firmly — this must be supplied. (GRhtCM 14.11-12:2)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭena bapinā parpaṭikayutena parpaṭiko pohaparpaṭikaḥ pratītastena
                            yutena mipitena niyamasaṃskāroktāḥ niyamakāḥ divyauṣadhayaḥ
                            śatāvarīpramukhās tābhiḥ tato vaṭikā chāyāśuṣkā kāryā chāyāgharmarūpā
                            śuṣkā nīrasā tathā kāryā iti // GRhtCM_14.11-12:3 //
children.translated_text: With sulphur of what quality? Combined with metal-flake (<s>parpaṭika</s>) — iron-flake, well-known — combined, i.e., mixed, with it; the restraining drugs mentioned in the restraining-process — the divine herbs beginning with <s>śatāvarī</s> — with those; then a pill dried in the shade should be made — dried in shade-heat, devoid of moisture — it should be made thus. (GRhtCM 14.11-12:3)

children.text: anyaccāha mūṣetyādi // GRhtCM_14.11-12:4 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another [method], with 'crucible' and so forth. (GRhtCM 14.11-12:4)

children.text:
mūṣādhṛtaparpaṭikā mūṣāyāṃ yā parpaṭikā pūrvoktapohaparpaṭikā sā
                            nigūḍhasudṛḍhena nigūḍhaścāsau sudṛḍhaśca tena mūpakādikṣārabiḍena kṛtvā
                            madhye svāntaḥ ācchādya dhmātaṃ kriyate punas tadūdhmātaṃ sat khoṭaṃ
                            gacchati khoṭatvamāpnoti // GRhtCM_14.11-12:5 //
children.translated_text: The crucible-held metal-flake — the metal-flake (<s>parpaṭikā</s>) as described before, placed in a crucible — that [is sealed] with a firmly concealed [substance] — both firm and concealed — with the root-alkali-<s>viḍa</s>; having done this, in the middle — within — having covered [it], it is blown; furthermore, that which is blown becomes an ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>) — attains the state of an ingot. (GRhtCM 14.11-12:5)

children.text:
tatkhoṭaṃ hemayutaṃ svarṇamipitaṃ sūtabandhakaraṃ syāt rasabandhanapradam
                            ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_14.11-12:6 //
children.translated_text: That ingot, combined with gold — mixed with gold — would effect the binding of mercury — would give the binding of mercury, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 14.11-12:6)

children.text: mercury:: māraṇa, khoṭa
children.translated_text: [Section on] mercury: <s>māraṇa</s> (killing), <s>khoṭa</s> (ingot)

children.text: baliyuktā parpaṭikā mṛditā snuhyarkabhāvitā guṭikā /
children.translated_text: A metal-flake (<s>parpaṭikā</s>) combined with sulphur, ground, a pill steeped in <s>snuhī</s> (Euphorbia) and <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) [milks] —

children.text: madhye gartā kāryā sūtabhṛtācchāditā tadanu // GRht_14.13 //
children.translated_text: a cavity should be made in the middle, filled with mercury, and then covered. (GRht 14.13)

children.text: bāhye dattvā nigaḍaṃ suliptamūṣodare dṛḍhaṃ nyastam /
children.translated_text: Having placed a fastener on the outside, firmly set in the well-sealed crucible-belly,

children.text: sūtaḥ puṭito mriyate dhmātaḥ khoṭaṃ bhavatyeva // GRht_14.14 //
children.translated_text: the mercury, when calcined (<s>puṭita</s>), dies; when blown, it indeed becomes an ingot. (GRht 14.14)

children.text: vidhyantaramāha bapītyādi // GRhtCM_14.13-14:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states an alternative method, with 'sulphur' and so forth. (GRhtCM 14.13-14:1)

children.text:
pūrvoktā yā parpaṭikā pohaparpaṭikā bapiyuktā gandhakamiśritā
                            snuhyarkabhāvitā ca snuhī vajrī arko mandāras tābhyāṃ bhāvitā pputā
                            etayoḥ payaseti bhāvaḥ mṛditā ca gharṣitā ca evaṃ kṛtavidhānā parpaṭikā
                            sati guṭikā vaṭikā kāryā madhye guṭikāntaḥ gartā kāryā sā gartā tataḥ
                            sūtabhṛtā sūtapūritā satī tadanu gartakaraṇānantaraṃ ācchāditā kāryā
                            parpaṭikayeti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_14.13-14:2 //
children.translated_text: The previously described metal-flake (<s>parpaṭikā</s>) — iron-flake — combined with sulphur (<s>balin</s>/gandhaka), steeped in <s>snuhī</s> (Euphorbia/<s>vajrī</s>) and <s>arka</s> (<s>mandāra</s>/Calotropis) — steeped in their milks, this is the import — and ground; the metal-flake having been prepared in this manner, a pill should be made; in the middle — inside the pill — a cavity should be made; that cavity should then be filled with mercury — mercury-filled — and after making the cavity, it should be covered — with the metal-flake, this is the import. (GRhtCM 14.13-14:2)

children.text: taccāha bāhya ityādi // GRhtCM_14.13-14:3 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that, with 'outside' and so forth. (GRhtCM 14.13-14:3)

children.text:
bāhye sūtodaraguṭikopari nigaḍaṃ dattvā supiptamūṣodare supiptā
                            sāraṇakarmābhihitauṣadhīriti śeṣaḥ evaṃvidhā yā mūṣā tasyā yadudaraṃ
                            tasmindṛḍhaṃ yathā syāttathā nigaḍaṃ nyastaṃ sthāpitaṃ kuryāditi śeṣaḥ
                            // GRhtCM_14.13-14:4 //
children.translated_text: On the outside — on top of the mercury-bellied pill — having placed a fastener, in the well-sealed crucible-belly — [the crucible] sealed with the drugs mentioned for the liquefaction-operation, this is the completion — in the belly of such a crucible, firmly — as tightly as possible — one should place the fastener and set [it] — this is the completion. (GRhtCM 14.13-14:4)

children.text:
mūṣodaraguṭikāntasthaḥ sūtaḥ puṭito vahniyogāt mriyate pañcatvamāpnoti //
                            GRhtCM_14.13-14:5 //
children.translated_text: The mercury inside the pill inside the crucible-belly, when calcined (<s>puṭita</s>) — through contact with fire — dies, attains the five-fold dissolution. (GRhtCM 14.13-14:5)

children.text: punaḥ dhmātaḥ san khoṭo bhavati // GRhtCM_14.13-14:6 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, when blown, it becomes an ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>). (GRhtCM 14.13-14:6)

children.text: evāvyayamanyaniṣedhavāci // GRhtCM_14.13-14:7 //
children.translated_text: The particle 'eva' (indeed) negates other [methods]. (GRhtCM 14.13-14:7)

children.text: mercury:: māraṇa, khoṭa
children.translated_text: [Section on] mercury: <s>māraṇa</s> (killing), <s>khoṭa</s> (ingot)

children.text: evaṃ tālaśilābhyāṃ mākṣikarasakaiśca daradaśikhisahitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, with <s>tāla</s> (orpiment) and <s>śilā</s> (realgar), and with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) and <s>rasaka</s> (calamine) combined with cinnabar and fire —

children.text: mriyate puṭasaṃyogād dhmātaṃ khoṭaṃ kṛtaṃ vimalam // GRht_14.15 //
children.translated_text: [mercury] dies through the application of calcination (<s>puṭa</s>); when blown, the ingot produced is pure (<s>vimala</s>). (GRht 14.15)

children.text: anyaccāha evamityādi // GRhtCM_14.15:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another [method], with 'thus' and so forth. (GRhtCM 14.15:1)

children.text:
evaṃ pohaparpaṭikāvidhānena tāpaśipābhyāṃ dhmātaṃ sat yutaṃ yat khoṭaṃ
                            tadvimapaṃ mapavarjitaṃ syāt // GRhtCM_14.15:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by the metal-flake procedure, when blown together with <s>tāla</s> (orpiment) and <s>śilā</s> (realgar), the ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>) produced would be pure (<s>vimala</s>) — free of impurity. (GRhtCM 14.15:2)

children.text:
ca punaḥ mākṣikarasakaistāpyakharparikaiḥ daradaśikhisahitaiśca
                            hiṅgupaśikhimipitaiśca karaṇarūpairvimapaṃ ca punaḥ puṭayogād
                            vahnisaṃparkāt dhmātaṃ mriyate // GRhtCM_14.15:3 //
children.translated_text: And furthermore, with <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>rasaka</s> (calamine) — pyrite and calamine — <s>darada</s> (cinnabar) and <s>śikhin</s> (realgar) combined, mixed with <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar) and <s>śikhi</s> (realgar) — which serve as processing agents — and furthermore, impure [mercury], by fire-calcination (<s>puṭayoga</s>), by contact with fire, when smelted, dies. (GRhtCM 14.15:3)

children.text: ādau mapapakṣaṇamuktam // GRhtCM_14.15:4 //
children.translated_text: At first, the soft-calcination was stated. (GRhtCM 14.15:4)

children.text: mercury:: māraṇa
children.translated_text: Mercury: killing (<s>māraṇa</s>)

children.text: kiṭṭakapurasaṃyogād dhmātaiḥ kiṭṭastu kiṭṭataḥ satvam /
children.translated_text: By the conjunction of iron-slag (<s>kiṭṭaka</s>) and guggulu (<s>pura</s>), [the substances] when smelted [produce] slag; from that slag, the essence —

children.text: nipatati satvaṃ rasasākaṃ janayati tadbhasma tasyāpi // GRht_14.16 //
children.translated_text: the essence falls; the mercury-mixed [essence] produces the ash (<s>bhasma</s>) of that [mercury] as well. (GRht 14.16)

children.text: taccāha kiṭṭapurasaṃyogāt // GRhtCM_14.16:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That he states: 'by the conjunction of slag and <s>pura</s> (guggulu).' (GRhtCM 14.16:1)

children.text:
kiṭṭaṃ pohamapaṃ puro guggupuḥ tayoḥ saṃyogāt dhmātaiḥ
                            mākṣikarasadaradarūpaiḥ pūrvoktaiḥ kiṭṭo bhavet punaḥ kiṭṭato rasasākaṃ
                            sūtamiśritaṃ sattvaṃ sāraṃ nipatati tatsattvaṃ bhasma janayati
                            utpādayati // GRhtCM_14.16:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Slag' (<s>kiṭṭa</s>) means iron-scum; '<s>pura</s>' is guggulu resin; by the conjunction of these two, 'smelted' means with the previously mentioned forms of <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>rasa</s>, and <s>darada</s>; slag results; furthermore, from the slag, the mercury-mixed essence (<s>rasasāka</s>) — the essence blended with mercury — falls; that essence produces ash — generates it. (GRhtCM 14.16:2)

children.text: tasyāpi bhasmanaḥ sattvaṃ ca nipatatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_14.16:3 //
children.translated_text: Of that ash too, the essence falls — that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 14.16:3)

children.text: rañjana with smoke and without mercury (????)
children.translated_text: Coloring (<s>rañjana</s>) with smoke and without mercury

children.text: vaṅgarasagandhatālaṃ khaṭikāyā yogataḥ suparpaṭikā /
children.translated_text: Tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), mercury (<s>rasa</s>), sulphur (<s>gandha</s>), and orpiment (<s>tāla</s>), by conjunction with chalk (<s>khaṭikā</s>), [make] an excellent flake (<s>parpaṭikā</s>);

children.text: rañjayati satvatālaṃ dhūmena vināpi sūtam // GRht_14.17 //
children.translated_text: the essence-orpiment (<s>sattva-tāla</s>) colors with smoke, even without mercury. (GRht 14.17)

children.text: vidhyantaramāha vaṅgarasagandhatāpamiti // GRhtCM_14.17:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another method, beginning with 'tin, mercury, sulphur, orpiment.' (GRhtCM 14.17:1)

children.text:
vaṅgaṃ trapu rasaḥ sūtaḥ gandhako bapiḥ tāpaṃ haritāpaṃ etaccatuṣṭayaṃ
                            khaṭikāyā yogataḥ khaṭikā citrakarajastasyā yogataḥ suparpaṭikāṃ
                            pūrvoktāṃ pohaparpaṭikāṃ rañjayati sūtena vināpi kimuta rasamipitena
                            tāpasattveneti vyaktiḥ // GRhtCM_14.17:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vaṅga</s> is tin; <s>rasa</s> is mercury; <s>gandhaka</s> is sulphur; <s>tāla</s> is orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>) — this quartet, by conjunction with <s>khaṭikā</s> — <s>khaṭikā</s> is chalk [or marking-nut paste], by conjunction with it — colors the excellent <s>parpaṭikā</s> (metal-flake), the previously described iron-flake; even without mercury — how much more so when combined with mercury; with pyrite-essence — this is the clarification. (GRhtCM 14.17:2)

children.text: bīja:: for rañjana
children.translated_text: Seed (<s>bīja</s>): for coloring (<s>rañjana</s>)

children.text: evaṃ khoṭaṃ bījaṃ kṛtvā rañjanavidhinā surañjanaṃ kāryam /
children.translated_text: Thus, having made the <s>khoṭa</s> (alloy-lump) [into] a seed, by the coloring procedure, one should make it well-colored;

children.text: triguṇaṃ rasasya hema saṃyojyaṃ tasya varabījam // GRht_14.18 //
children.translated_text: gold triple [the weight] of mercury should be combined — that is the best seed. (GRht 14.18)

children.text:
mahābījānāṃ bījānāṃ ca viśeṣavidhānamāha evamityādi // GRhtCM_14.18:1
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the special procedure for great seeds and seeds, beginning with 'thus' and so on. (GRhtCM 14.18:1)

children.text:
evam uktavidhānena bījaṃ vidhāya rañjanavidhinā rañjanavidhānena
                            surañjanaṃ kāryam // GRhtCM_14.18:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by the stated procedure, having prepared the seed, by the coloring method — by the coloring procedure — one should make it well-colored. (GRhtCM 14.18:2)

children.text:
tatkārye rasasya sūtasya triguṇaṃ hema saṃyojyaṃ punas tasya hemnaḥ
                            triguṇaṃ varabījaṃ yojyaṃ iti viśeṣavidhiḥ // GRhtCM_14.18:3 //
children.translated_text: In that procedure, gold triple [the weight] of mercury should be combined; furthermore, the best seed [should be] triple [the weight] of that gold — this is the special procedure. (GRhtCM 14.18:3)

children.text: abhra:: sattva:: druti:: causes bandhana of mercury
children.translated_text: Mica (<s>abhraka</s>): essence: liquefaction (<s>druti</s>) — causes fixation (<s>bandhana</s>) of mercury

children.text: vakṣye tvabhrakasatvād vimaladrutim akhilaguṇagaṇādhārām /
children.translated_text: I shall describe the stainless liquefaction from mica-essence, the foundation of all groups of qualities;

children.text: sā hi nibadhnāti rasaṃ saṃmilitā milati ca sukhena // GRht_15.1 //
children.translated_text: that indeed binds mercury; when merged, it merges with ease. (GRht 15.1)

children.text: bhāratī bharatakhaṇḍamaṇḍitā pacaremānandamañjarī /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāratī</s> (the goddess of speech), adorning the land of <s>Bhārata</s>, is a cluster of bliss;

children.text:
kastayā na rasamapaṃ kuto jayā vakrapadmamadhisthayā sadā //
                            GRhtCM_15.1:1 //
children.translated_text: who would not delight in <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic relish/mercury) with her? Whence victory? [She who] always presides over the crooked lotus. (GRhtCM 15.1:1)

children.text: bāhyadrutipraśaṃsāmāha vakṣya ityādi // GRhtCM_15.1:2 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the praise of external liquefaction (<s>bāhyadruti</s>), beginning with 'I shall describe' and so on. (GRhtCM 15.1:2)

children.text:
ahaṃ kaviḥ abhrakasattvādgaganasārato vimapadrutiṃ pakṣe vimapā cāsau
                            drutiśceti vigrahaḥ // GRhtCM_15.1:3 //
children.translated_text: I, the poet, [shall describe] the stainless liquefaction (<s>vimaladruti</s>) from mica-essence (<s>gaganasāra</s>); alternatively, the compound is analyzed as 'stainless and a liquefaction.' (GRhtCM 15.1:3)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭāṃ akhipaguṇagaṇādhārām akhipāśca te guṇagaṇāśca guṇapaṭapāśca
                            teṣāṃ yā ādhārā tāṃ bahavo guṇās tiṣṭhantyasyāmiti vyaktiḥ //
                            GRhtCM_15.1:4 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality? 'The foundation of all groups of qualities' — 'all' and 'groups of qualities' and 'multitude of qualities' — that which is their foundation, in which many qualities reside; that is the clarification. (GRhtCM 15.1:4)

children.text:
sā rasabhūtā drutiḥ rasaṃ sūtāṃ nibadhnāti niścayena badhnātītyarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_15.1:5 //
children.translated_text: That liquefaction, being of the nature of <s>rasa</s>, binds mercury (<s>sūta</s>) — certainly binds; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 15.1:5)

children.text: kiṃbhūtā satī // GRhtCM_15.1:6 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality, being such? (GRhtCM 15.1:6)

children.text:
mipitā satī tupyamiśritā satī punaḥ drutiḥ sukhena mipati patrāder
                            durmipāpatvāt // GRhtCM_15.1:7 //
children.translated_text: Being merged — being mixed with tin — furthermore, the liquefaction merges with ease, because of the difficulty of merging with leaf-[metal] and such. (GRhtCM 15.1:7)

children.text: abhra:: sattva:: druti:: production
children.translated_text: Mica (<s>abhraka</s>): essence: liquefaction (<s>druti</s>) — production

children.text: vajravallyāḥ svarasena gaganaṃ sauvarcalānvitaṃ piṣṭam /
children.translated_text: Mica (<s>gagana</s>), with the juice of <s>vajravallī</s> (a creeper), ground with <s>sauvarcala</s> (black salt),

children.text: paripakvaṃ niculapuṭairnirlepaṃ bhavati rasarūpam // GRht_15.2 //
children.translated_text: cooked with <s>nicula</s> (Barringtonia) calcinations, becomes stain-free, mercury-like in form. (GRht 15.2)

children.text: drutividhānamāha vajravappyā ityādi // GRhtCM_15.2:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the liquefaction procedure, beginning with '<s>vajravallī</s>' and so on. (GRhtCM 15.2:1)

With the juice of <s>vajravallī</s> — with its own juice — mica (<s>gagana</s>), the mica-essence, combined with <s>sauvarcala</s> (<s>rucaka</s>, black salt), should be ground; this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 15.2:2)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ gaganaṃ nicupapuṭair vetasadravabhāvanābhiḥ pakvaṃ
                            vahnipuṭitaṃ tatpakvaṃ san nirpepaṃ saṃparkavarjitaṃ rasarūpaṃ bhavati
                            pāradasya rūpamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_15.2:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality is the mica? Cooked with <s>nicula</s> (Barringtonia) calcinations — steepings with the liquid of the <s>vetasa</s> (rattan) tree — fire-calcined; that [mica] being cooked, becomes stain-free — free from impurity — mercury-like in form — having the appearance of mercury; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 15.2:3)

children.text: abhra:: sattva:: druti:: production
children.translated_text: Mica (<s>abhraka</s>): essence: liquefaction (<s>druti</s>) — production

children.text: ajajalaśatapariplāvitakapitindukacūrṇavāpamātreṇa /
children.translated_text: With a sprinkling of <s>kapitinduka</s> powder that has been steeped a hundred times in goat's urine,

children.text: drutajātamabhrakasatvaṃ mūṣāyāṃ rasanibhaṃ bhavati // GRht_15.3 //
children.translated_text: the mica-essence, liquefied in a crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>), becomes mercury-like. (GRht 15.3)

children.text: vidhyantaramāha ajetyādi // GRhtCM_15.3:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another method, beginning with 'goat' and so on. (GRhtCM 15.3:1)

The liquefied mica-essence — the mica-essence (<s>gaganasāra</s>) — in a crucible designated 'diamond,' when liquefied, becomes mercury-like — becomes [like] <s>pārada</s>; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 15.3:2)

children.text:
kena ajajapaśataparibhāvitakapitindukacūrṇavāpamātreṇa ajaḥ chāgastasya
                            japena mūtreṇa śataṃ śatavāraṃ paribhāvitaṃ gharmapuṭitaṃ
                            yatkapitindukacūrṇaṃ tasya vāpamātreṇa drute'bhrasattve vāpe //
                            GRhtCM_15.3:3 //
children.translated_text: By what means? With a sprinkling of <s>kapitinduka</s> powder that has been steeped a hundred times in goat's urine — 'goat' (<s>aja</s>) is a male goat; with its urine (<s>jala</s>), a hundred times steeped — sun-calcined — the <s>kapitinduka</s> powder, by a mere sprinkling of that, into the liquefied mica-essence, the sprinkling [is made]. (GRhtCM 15.3:3)

children.text: abhra:: sattva:: druti:: production
children.translated_text: Mica (<s>abhraka</s>): essence: liquefaction (<s>druti</s>) — production

children.text: nijarasaśataplāvitakañcukikandotthacūrṇakṛtaparivāpam /
children.translated_text: With a sprinkling of powder from the bulb of <s>kañcukī</s> (a tuberous plant) that has been steeped a hundred times in its own juice,

children.text: drutamāste'bhrakasattvaṃ tadvatsarvāṇi lohāni // GRht_15.4 //
children.translated_text: the mica-essence remains liquefied; likewise all metals. (GRht 15.4)

children.text:
abhrakasattvaṃ vahniyogena drutaṃ āste dravarūpamevāvatiṣṭhate //
                            GRhtCM_15.4:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The mica-essence, by conjunction with fire, remains liquefied — persists in liquid form. (GRhtCM 15.4:1)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ sattvaṃ nijarasaśataparibhāvitetyādi nijarasena
                            svakīyadraveṇa paribhāvitaṃ yatkañcukikandotthacūrṇaṃ tasya āvāpena
                            yathā śatabhāvitakañcukikandotthacūrṇena sattvaṃ drutamāste
                            tadvatsarvāṇi pohāni drutāni tiṣṭhanti // GRhtCM_15.4:2 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality is the essence? 'Steeped a hundred times in its own juice' and so forth — steeped in its own juice, the powder of <s>kañcukī</s> bulb, by a sprinkling of that — just as with the <s>kañcukī</s>-bulb powder steeped a hundred times, the essence remains liquefied; likewise all metals remain liquefied. (GRhtCM 15.4:2)

children.text: abhra:: sattva:: druti:: production
children.translated_text: Mica (<s>abhraka</s>): essence: liquefaction (<s>druti</s>) — production

children.text: gaganaṃ cikuratailaghṛṣṭaṃ gomayaliptaṃ ca kuliśamūṣāyām /
children.translated_text: Mica (<s>gagana</s>), rubbed with hair-oil (<s>cikura-taila</s>), coated with cow-dung, in a diamond-crucible (<s>kuliśa-mūṣā</s>) —

children.text: sudhmātamatra sattvaṃ plavati jalākāramacireṇa // GRht_15.5 //
children.translated_text: well-smelted, the essence there floats in water-form quickly. (GRht 15.5)

children.text: anyaccāha gaganetyādi // GRhtCM_15.5:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another [method], beginning with '<s>gagana</s>' and so on. (GRhtCM 15.5:1)

children.text:
gaganaṃ abhrasāraṃ cikurataipaghṛṣṭaṃ cikurataipaṃ keśataipaṃ pratītaṃ
                            grantheṣu tena ghṛṣṭaṃ marditaṃ gomayapiptaṃ gomayena piptaṃ yathā
                            syāttathā kupiśamūṣāyāṃ vajrābhidhānāyāṃ sudhmātaṃ sat acireṇāppakāpena
                            japākāraṃ bhavatītyanvayaḥ // GRhtCM_15.5:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Mica' (<s>gagana</s>) means mica-essence; 'rubbed with hair-oil' — hair-oil (<s>cikura-taila</s>, <s>keśa-taila</s>) is well-known in the treatises — rubbed, meaning ground, with that; 'coated with cow-dung' — coated with cow-dung in such a manner; in a diamond-crucible — in the crucible designated 'diamond' — well-smelted, it quickly becomes water-like; this is the construction. (GRhtCM 15.5:2)

children.text: abhra:: sattva:: druti:: general rule
children.translated_text: Mica (<s>abhraka</s>): essence: liquefaction (<s>druti</s>) — general rule

children.text: gaganadrutiriha satve jñeyo hi rasasya sampradāyo 'yam /
children.translated_text: The liquefaction of mica-[essence] here, in [the case of] essence, should be known — this indeed is the tradition of mercury;

children.text: prathamaṃ nipātya satvaṃ deyo vāpo drute tasmin // GRht_15.6 //
children.translated_text: first having caused the essence to fall, the sprinkling should be given while it is in a liquefied [state]. (GRht 15.6)

children.text: sāmānyenābhradrutividhānamāha gaganetyādi // GRhtCM_15.6:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the mica-liquefaction procedure in general, beginning with '<s>gagana</s>' and so on. (GRhtCM 15.6:1)

children.text:
ihāsmin śāstre sattve gaganasāre jāte sāṅgatayā gaganadrutiḥ
                            bhavatītyadhyāhāryam // GRhtCM_15.6:2 //
children.translated_text: Here in this treatise, when mica-essence (<s>gaganasāra</s>) has been obtained, as a corollary, the mica-liquefaction (<s>gaganadruti</s>) occurs — this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 15.6:2)

children.text:
ayaṃ pratyakṣāntargataḥ hi niścitaṃ rasasya sūtasya saṃpradāyo jñeyaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_15.6:3 //
children.translated_text: This, [though] hidden within direct perception, should certainly be known as the tradition of mercury (<s>sūta</s>). (GRhtCM 15.6:3)

Furthermore, first — at the beginning — having caused the mica-essence (<s>abhrasāra</s>) to fall, while that essence is in a liquefied state — in liquid form due to fire — the sprinkling (<s>vāpa</s>) should be performed — of the stated herbs; this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 15.6:4)

children.text: gold:: druti
children.translated_text: Gold: liquefaction (<s>druti</s>)

children.text: suragopakadeharajaḥ suradāliphalaiḥ samāṃśakairdeyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The body-powder of <s>indragopa</s> (cochineal insect), with equal parts of <s>suradālī</s> (a type of <s>devadālī</s>) fruits, should be given

children.text: vāpo drute suvarṇe drutamāste tadrasaprakhyam // GRht_15.7 //
children.translated_text: as a sprinkling (<s>vāpa</s>) while gold is in a liquefied [state]; the liquefied [gold] remains, resembling mercury. (GRht 15.7)

children.text:
atha suvarṇadrutividhānamāha suragopakadeharaja iti // GRhtCM_15.7:1
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now he states the procedure for gold-liquefaction, beginning with '<s>indragopa</s> body-powder.' (GRhtCM 15.7:1)

children.text:
indragopaśarīracūrṇaṃ suradāpīphapaiḥ samāṃśakaiḥ
                            suragopacūrṇatupyabhāgaiḥ kṛtvā vāpo deyaḥ drute satyuparikṣepa iti
                            suvarṇe vāpe kṛte suvarṇaṃ drutamāste kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ rasaprakhyaṃ
                            japatupyam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_15.7:2 //
children.translated_text: The powder of the <s>indragopa</s> insect's body, with equal portions of <s>suradālī</s> fruits — portions equal to the <s>indragopa</s>-powder — having prepared [the mixture], the sprinkling should be given — thrown on top — while the gold is in a liquefied state; when the sprinkling is performed on the gold, the gold remains liquefied; of what quality? Mercury-like — resembling liquid tin; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 15.7:2)

children.text: gold:: druti
children.translated_text: Gold: liquefaction (<s>druti</s>)

children.text: atha nijarasaparibhāvitasuradālīcūrṇavāpamātreṇa /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, with a mere sprinkling of <s>suradālī</s> powder that has been steeped in its own juice,

children.text: drutamevāste kanakaṃ labhate bhūyo na kaṭhinatvam // GRht_15.8 //
children.translated_text: gold remains in a liquefied state indeed, and does not acquire hardness again. (GRht 15.8)

children.text: anyaccāha athetyādi // GRhtCM_15.8:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another [method], beginning with 'furthermore' and so on. (GRhtCM 15.8:1)

children.text:
athendragopadevadāpīyogakathanānantaraṃ kanakaṃ hema nijarasaparibhāvitaṃ
                            yat suradāpīcūrṇaṃ tasya vāpamātreṇa gapite hemni kṣepamātreṇa
                            drutamevāste gapitam evāvatiṣṭhatītyarthaḥ punaḥ kanakaṃ kāṭhinyaṃ
                            sthiratvaṃ na pabhate iti cirakāpaprayojanam // GRhtCM_15.8:2 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore — after the description of the <s>indragopa</s>-<s>devadālī</s> conjunction — gold, by a mere sprinkling of <s>suradālī</s> powder that has been steeped in its own juice — by the mere addition into liquefied gold — remains in a liquefied state — persists indeed in a melted condition; that is the meaning. Furthermore, the gold does not acquire hardness — solidity — this [explains] the purpose of prolonged [liquefaction]. (GRhtCM 15.8:2)

children.text: tīkṣṇaloha:: druti
children.translated_text: Steel/iron (<s>tīkṣṇaloha</s>): liquefaction (<s>druti</s>)

children.text: suradālībhasma galitaṃ triḥsaptakṛtvātha gojalaṃ śuṣkam /
children.translated_text: Ash of <s>suradālī</s>, liquefied, [steeped] twenty-one times in cow's urine, then dried;

children.text: vāpena salilasadṛśaṃ kurute mūṣāgataṃ tīkṣṇam // GRht_15.9 //
children.translated_text: by a sprinkling [of this], steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) placed in a crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>) becomes water-like. (GRht 15.9)

children.text: atha tīkṣṇavidhānamāha suradāpītyādi // GRhtCM_15.9:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now he states the procedure for steel, beginning with '<s>suradālī</s>' and so on. (GRhtCM 15.9:1)

children.text:
suradāpībhasmagapitaṃ suradāpī devadāpī tasyāḥ bhasma dāhasambhūtaṃ tena
                            gapitaṃ trisaptakṛtvā ekaviṃśativāraṃ gojapaṃ surabhimūtraṃ bhāvitaṃ
                            kuryādityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_15.9:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Liquefied with <s>suradālī</s>-ash' — <s>suradālī</s> is <s>devadālī</s>; its ash — produced by burning — liquefied with that; 'twenty-one times' means twenty-one rounds; 'in cow's urine' — steeped in cattle urine — one should prepare it; this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 15.9:2)

children.text:
atha mūṣāgataṃ vajrasaṃjñāyāṃ sthitaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ sāraṃ vāpena nikṣepaṇena
                            japasadṛśaṃ japatupyaṃ kurute karmaviditi śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_15.9:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>, i.e., the essence) placed in a crucible — established in the diamond-designated [crucible] — by a sprinkling — by an addition — becomes water-like — like liquid tin; the skilled practitioner does so; this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 15.9:3)

children.text: mākṣikasattvadruti
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s>-essence liquefaction (<s>druti</s>)

children.text: kūrmāsthiśilājatukameṣīmṛgago+asthivāpitā kāñcī /
children.translated_text: Tortoise-bone, mineral pitch (<s>śilājatu</s>), and bone of ewe, deer, and cow, [used as] sprinklings, the [essence] —

children.text: jalasadṛśī bhavati sadā vāpo deyo drutāyāṃ tu // GRht_15.10 //
children.translated_text: becomes water-like always; the sprinkling should be given while in a liquefied [state]. (GRht 15.10)

children.text: atha mākṣikadrutividhānamāha kūrmetyādi // GRhtCM_15.10:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now he states the procedure for <s>mākṣika</s>-liquefaction, beginning with 'tortoise' and so on. (GRhtCM 15.10:1)

children.text:
kūrmāsthi śipājatukaṃ pratītaṃ meṣī meṣapatnī mṛgo hariṇaḥ gauḥ pratītā
                            pratīto vā teṣāṃ yānyasthīni tair nirvāpitā yā kāñcī svarṇamākṣikaṃ sā
                            japasadṛśī bhavati kiyatkāpaparimāṇaṃ sadā nityaṃ punaḥ drutāyāṃ
                            gapitāyāṃ vāpo deyaḥ vāpo nikṣepaṇam // GRhtCM_15.10:2 //
children.translated_text: Tortoise-bone (<s>kūrmāsthi</s>) means bitumen (<s>śilājatu</s>), well-known; <s>meṣī</s> is a ewe; <s>mṛga</s> is a deer; <s>gau</s> is a cow, well-known; with their bones, the quenched gold-pyrite (<s>kāñcī</s>, i.e., <s>svarṇamākṣika</s>) becomes like a rosary bead (<s>japa</s>).
