Of what measure? Always, constantly. Again, when melted (<s>drutā</s>), sprinkling (<s>vāpa</s>) should be given — <s>vāpa</s> means projection. (GRhtCM 15.10:2)

children.text: abhra:: druti:: alchem. properties
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Mica — <s>druti</s> (dissolution) — alchemical properties]

children.text: abhrakadrutiraviśeṣā nirlepā yojitā samāsāttu /
children.translated_text: The dissolution (<s>druti</s>) of mica (<s>abhraka</s>), even of an ordinary kind, when free of residue (<s>nirlepā</s>) and combined in equal proportion —

children.text: āroṭaṃ rasarājaṃ badhnāti hi dvandvayogena // GRht_15.11 //
children.translated_text: binds the king of <s>rasas</s> (mercury) indeed, after processing (<s>āroṭa</s>), through the pair-combination method (<s>dvandvayoga</s>). (GRht 15.11)

children.text: sāmānyābhradruter adhikāramāha abhradrutirityādi // GRhtCM_15.11:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the authority of ordinary mica-dissolution, with 'mica-dissolution' and so forth. (GRhtCM 15.11:1)

children.text:
gaganadravaḥ aviśeṣā sāmānyāpi vidhānena kṛtā nirpepā asparśā samā
                            sūtatupyabhāgayojitā satī āroṭaṃ rasanajaṃ pūrvasaṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛtaṃ
                            sūtaṃ badhnāti kena dvandvayogena ubhayamepāpakauṣadhena //
                            GRhtCM_15.11:2 //
children.translated_text: The mica-fluid (<s>gaganadravaḥ</s>), even of an ordinary kind (<s>aviśeṣā</s>) — even a common one, [when] prepared by [proper] procedure — free of residue (<s>nirlepā</s>), meaning without adherence — combined in equal portions of mercury, when applied, binds the mercury that has been processed (<s>āroṭa</s>) — mercury that has undergone prior preparations — through the pair-combination (<s>dvandvayogena</s>), meaning with both the medicine for dissolution and the medicine [for binding]. (GRhtCM 15.11:2)

children.text: hiśabdo yuktārtha iti // GRhtCM_15.11:3 //
children.translated_text: The particle '<s>hi</s>' is used to convey certainty, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 15.11:3)

children.text: receipe for dvandvana of druti and mercury
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Recipe for <s>dvandvana</s> (pairing) of <s>druti</s> and mercury]

children.text: kṛṣṇāgarunābhisitai rasonasitarāmaṭhairimā drutayaḥ /
children.translated_text: With black aloe (<s>kṛṣṇāgaru</s>), musk (<s>nābhi</s>), camphor (<s>sita</s>), garlic (<s>rasona</s>), sugar (<s>sitā</s>), and asafoetida (<s>rāmaṭha</s>) — these dissolutions,

children.text: soṣṇe milanti rasena mṛditāḥ strīkusumapalāśabījarasaiḥ // GRht_15.12 //
children.translated_text: when warm, combine with mercury, [when] ground with menstrual blood (<s>strīkusuma</s>), <s>palāśa</s> (Butea) seed-juice. (GRht 15.12)

children.text: pūrvoktānāṃ mepanam āha kṛṣṇetyādi // GRhtCM_15.12:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the method of combining the aforementioned [dissolutions], with 'black' and so forth. (GRhtCM 15.12:1)

children.text:
imā drutayaḥ soṣṇatuṣakarīṣādinā tāpite khapve mṛditāḥ satyo mipanti
                            rasena saha tathā kāryam // GRhtCM_15.12:2 //
children.translated_text: These dissolutions (<s>drutayaḥ</s>), when warm — heated in a vessel with husk-fuel, cow-dung, and the like — when ground, combine with mercury; thus it should be done. (GRhtCM 15.12:2)

children.text: kaiḥ kṛtvā kṛṣṇāgarunābhisitaiḥ // GRhtCM_15.12:3 //
children.translated_text: With what? With black aloe (<s>kṛṣṇāgaru</s>), musk (<s>nābhi</s>), and camphor (<s>sita</s>). (GRhtCM 15.12:3)

children.text:
kṛṣṇāgarukastūrikāghanasāraiḥ kṛtvā na kevapametaiḥ rasonasitarāmaṭhaiśca
                            paśunaśarkarāhiṅgubhiḥ punaḥ strīkusumapapāśabījarasaiḥ strīkusumaṃ ca
                            papāśasya bījāni ca rasaśceti dvaṃdvaḥ etaistribhiryogaiḥ
                            pṛthagbhūtairmipanti sarvaiśceti // GRhtCM_15.12:4 //
children.translated_text: With black aloe, musk (<s>kastūrikā</s>), and camphor (<s>ghanasāra</s>) — not with these alone; also with garlic (<s>rasona</s>), sugar (<s>śarkarā</s>), and asafoetida (<s>hiṅgu</s>). Again, with menstrual blood (<s>strīkusuma</s>), <s>palāśa</s>-seeds, and their juice — menstrual blood, <s>palāśa</s>-seeds, and juice [form] a <s>dvandva</s> compound; with these three preparations separately, they combine — and with all [together] as well. (GRhtCM 15.12:4)

children.text: mercury:: baddha:: causes longevity
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Mercury — bound (<s>baddha</s>) — causes longevity]

children.text: iti baddho rasarājo guñjāmātropayojito nityam /
children.translated_text: Thus bound, the king of <s>rasas</s>, employed daily in the amount of one <s>guñjā</s> (Abrus seed),

children.text: ekenaiva palena tu kalpāyutajīvitaṃ kurute // GRht_15.13 //
children.translated_text: with just a single <s>pala</s> (measure), produces a lifespan of ten thousand <s>kalpas</s>. (GRht 15.13)

children.text: itthaṃ baddharasarājasya māhātmyamāha itītyādi // GRhtCM_15.13:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the greatness of mercury thus bound, with 'thus' and so forth. (GRhtCM 15.13:1)

children.text:
iti pūrvoktena drutividhānena baddho rasarājaḥ sūtaḥ ekena papena
                            ṣoḍaśikayā kappāyutaṃ jīvitaṃ kurute kappānām ayutaṃ sahasraparimāṇaṃ
                            jīvitamiti // GRhtCM_15.13:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus — by the aforementioned dissolution-procedure — the bound king of <s>rasas</s>, mercury, with a single <s>pala</s> (a measure of sixteen [<s>guñjās</s>]), produces a lifespan of ten thousand <s>kalpas</s> — a lifespan measuring ten thousand <s>kalpas</s>. (GRhtCM 15.13:2)

children.text:
kasmāt nityaṃ yathā syāttathā guñjāmātropayogataḥ dinaṃ dinaṃ prati
                            raktikāparimāṇasya rasasya yo+asau upayogastena // GRhtCM_15.13:3 //
children.translated_text: Why 'daily'? So that it becomes constant — from the use of a <s>guñjā</s>-measure, meaning through the daily consumption of mercury in the quantity of one <s>raktikā</s> (seed-weight). (GRhtCM 15.13:3)

children.text: atha pūrvoktagrāsakramājjarate raso vidhivat /
children.translated_text: Now, mercury digests properly according to the previously described sequence of feeding (<s>grāsa</s>);

children.text: etāḥ pūrvadrutayo bhavanti rasarājaphaladāśca // GRht_15.14 //
children.translated_text: these aforementioned dissolutions (<s>drutayaḥ</s>) become fruit-bestowing for the king of <s>rasas</s>. (GRht 15.14)

children.text: vidhinā grāsajārito raso guṇavānityāha athetyādi // GRhtCM_15.14:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that mercury digested with feeding according to procedure becomes endowed with virtues, with 'now' and so forth. (GRhtCM 15.14:1)

children.text:
atha drutiyogānantaraṃ rasaḥ sūtaḥ pūrvoktagrāsakramāt yojitakavapakramāt
                            vidhivat śāstroktavidhānena biḍādinā jarate ca punaretāḥ pūrvoktadrutayo
                            rasarājaphapadā bhavanti sūte prayuktāḥ phapadāḥ syurityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_15.14:2 //
children.translated_text: Now — after the dissolution-methods — mercury, according to the previously described sequence of feeding (<s>grāsa</s>) — the established sequence of application — digests properly, meaning according to the procedure prescribed in the <s>śāstras</s>, with <s>biḍa</s> (alkaline salt) and the like. Again, these aforementioned dissolutions become fruit-bestowing for the king of <s>rasas</s> — when applied to mercury, they become fruit-giving, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 15.14:2)

children.text: drutijāraṇa => vedha potency
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: <s>Druti</s>-digestion → <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) potency]

children.text: samajīrṇaḥ śatavedhī dviguṇena rasaḥ sahasravedhī ca /
children.translated_text: When equally digested, [mercury becomes] hundred-fold transmuting (<s>śatavedhī</s>); with double [dissolution], mercury becomes thousand-fold transmuting (<s>sahasravedhī</s>);

children.text: kramaśo hi koṭivedhī dviguṇadviguṇadruteścaraṇāt // GRht_15.15 //
children.translated_text: progressively, [it becomes] ten-million-fold transmuting (<s>koṭivedhī</s>) through the application of doubled and redoubled dissolution (<s>druti</s>). (GRht 15.15)

children.text:
adhikadruter jāraṇād adhikaguṇe raso bhavatītyāha samajīrṇa iti //
                            GRhtCM_15.15:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that from digestion of greater dissolution, mercury acquires greater potency, with 'equally digested' and so forth. (GRhtCM 15.15:1)

children.text: iti samā tupyabhāgā drutirjīrṇā yasminniti // GRhtCM_15.15:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus — the dissolution that is equal in mercury-portion, when digested in it. (GRhtCM 15.15:2)

children.text:
drute dviguṇā yā drutiḥ tasyāścaraṇāt kramaśaḥ koṭivedhī koṭyaṃśena
                            vedhakaḥ syāt // GRhtCM_15.15:3 //
children.translated_text: When the dissolution is doubled relative to the earlier [amount], through its application, progressively [mercury] becomes ten-million-fold transmuting (<s>koṭivedhī</s>) — capable of transmuting in a ratio of one to ten million. (GRhtCM 15.15:3)

children.text: drutibhāgo vṛddhau hyadhikaḥ syāditi vyaktiḥ // GRhtCM_15.15:4 //
children.translated_text: The dissolution-portion, when increased, would indeed become greater — this is the explanation. (GRhtCM 15.15:4)

children.text: ṣoḍaśa vā dvātriṃśadvā grāsā jīrṇāścatuḥṣaṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: When sixteen, or thirty-two, or sixty-four feedings (<s>grāsa</s>) are digested,

children.text: vidhyati tadā rasendro lohaṃ dhūmāvalokanataḥ // GRht_15.16 //
children.translated_text: then the lord of mercury (<s>rasendra</s>) transmutes metal merely from seeing [its] smoke. (GRht 15.16)

children.text: grāsavṛddhyā guṇānāha ṣoḍaśetyādi // GRhtCM_15.16:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the virtues arising from increased feeding, with 'sixteen' and so forth. (GRhtCM 15.16:1)

children.text:
yadā ṣoḍaśagrāsā vā dvātriṃśadgrāsā vā catuḥṣaṣṭigrāsā jīrṇā
                            jāraṇamāpannā bhavanti tadā rasendraḥ sūtaḥ pohaṃ dhātusaṃjñakaṃ
                            vidhyati vedhaṃ karoti kutaḥ dhūmāvapokanataḥ dhūmasya yadavapokanaṃ
                            darśanaṃ // GRhtCM_15.16:2 //
children.translated_text: When sixteen feedings, or thirty-two feedings, or sixty-four feedings are digested — have attained the state of digestion — then the lord of mercury transmutes metal — the substance designated as <s>dhātu</s> — performs transmutation (<s>vedha</s>). From what? From seeing smoke — from the observation of smoke. (GRhtCM 15.16:2)

children.text: sāraṇa:: motivation
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: <s>Sāraṇa</s> (extraction) — motivation]

children.text: iti rakto+api rasendro jāritabījo+api sāraṇārahitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, even though colored (<s>rakta</s>), the lord of mercury, even with digested <s>bīja</s> (seed), if devoid of <s>sāraṇa</s> (extraction),

children.text:
vyāpī na bhavati dehe loheṣvapyathavāpi hi ṣaṇḍhatāṃ yāti //
                                GRht_16.1 //
children.translated_text: does not become pervasive (<s>vyāpī</s>) in the body or in metals — or else it becomes impotent (<s>ṣaṇḍha</s>). (GRht 16.1)

children.text: mano manīṣāyatam āyatātmanā samācaretkarma paropakārī /
children.translated_text: One who benefits others should perform actions with mind established in wisdom, with the self extended —

children.text:
arcīva śobhāṃ pabhate parātparāṃ parāpavādādapi saṃnivṛttaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_16.1:1 //
children.translated_text: like a flame, one radiates a splendor that is supreme beyond the supreme, having withdrawn from even the criticism of others. (GRhtCM 16.1:1)

children.text: sūte sataipayantrasthe svarṇādikṣepaṇaṃ ca yat /
children.translated_text: When mercury is stationed in the <s>sataila</s> apparatus, the projection of gold and other [metals] —

children.text: vedhādhikyakaraṃ pohe sāraṇaṃ tatprakīrtitam /
children.translated_text: that which increases the potency of transmutation (<s>vedha</s>) in metal — that is called <s>sāraṇa</s> (extraction).

children.text: iti paribhāṣā // GRhtCM_16.1:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus is the definition. (GRhtCM 16.1:2)

children.text: sāraṇamutkṛṣṭaṃ matvā stuvannāha itītyādi // GRhtCM_16.1:3 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Considering <s>sāraṇa</s> to be supreme, he praises it, with 'thus' and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.1:3)

children.text:
iti pūrvoktena vidhānena rakto+api rāgavānapi rasendraḥ sūtaḥ
                            jaritabījo+api jāritāni bījāni yasminniti sāraṇarahitaḥ sāraṇā
                            vakṣyamāṇasaṃskārastena varjitaḥ vyāpī na bhavati dehe pohe ca vyāpako
                            na syāt hi niścitaṃ athavāpi sāraṇārahito rasendraḥ ṣaṇḍhatāṃ yāti
                            nirvīryatvam āpnoti // GRhtCM_16.1:4 //
children.translated_text: Thus — by the aforementioned procedure — even though colored (<s>rakta</s>), possessing color; the lord of mercury — even with digested <s>bījas</s>, in which <s>bījas</s> have been digested — if devoid of <s>sāraṇa</s>, the processing to be described, deprived of that — does not become pervasive in body or in metal. Indeed, certainly. Or else, the lord of mercury devoid of <s>sāraṇa</s> becomes impotent (<s>ṣaṇḍha</s>) — attains the state of being without potency. (GRhtCM 16.1:4)

children.text: sāraṇātaila
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: <s>Sāraṇa</s> oil]

children.text: maṇḍūkamatsyakacchapameṣajalaukāhisūkarādīnām /
children.translated_text: Of frog, fish, tortoise, ram, leech, snake, boar, and the like —

children.text: saṃyojyaikasya vasāṃ tataḥ pacetsāraṇātailam // GRht_16.2 //
children.translated_text: combining the fat of any one [of these], then cook the <s>sāraṇa</s> oil. (GRht 16.2)

children.text: jyotiṣmatīvibhītakakarañjakaṭutumbītailamekasmāt /
children.translated_text: Oil of <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> (Celastrus), <s>vibhītaka</s> (Terminalia bellirica), <s>karañja</s> (Pongamia), and bitter gourd (<s>kaṭutumbī</s>) — from one [of these];

children.text: dviguṇitaraktakaṣāyaṃ kṣīreṇa caturguṇena pacet // GRht_16.3 //
children.translated_text: with doubled red decoction, one should cook with four times [the quantity of] milk. (GRht 16.3)

children.text: raktavarga
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Red group (<s>raktavarga</s>)]

children.text: dāḍimapalāśabandhukakusumarajanībhir aruṇasahitābhiśca /
children.translated_text: With pomegranate (<s>dāḍima</s>), <s>palāśa</s> (Butea), <s>bandhūka</s> (Pentapetes) flowers, turmeric (<s>rajanī</s>), along with <s>aruṇa</s> (reddish [substances]),

children.text: mañjiṣṭhālākṣārasacandanasahito+api raktavargo+ayam // GRht_16.4 //
children.translated_text: also accompanied by madder (<s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>), lac-juice (<s>lākṣārasa</s>), and [red] sandalwood (<s>candana</s>) — this is the red group. (GRht 16.4)

children.text: vidrumabhūnāgamalaṃ viṇmakṣikādhvāṅkṣaśalabhānāṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Coral (<s>vidruma</s>), earthworm-excrement (<s>bhūnāgamala</s>), and the droppings of flies (<s>makṣikā</s>), crows (<s>dhvāṅkṣa</s>), and grasshoppers (<s>śalabha</s>),

children.text: karṇamalaṃ mahiṣīṇāṃ krameṇa kalkaṃ kalāṃśena // GRht_16.5 //
children.translated_text: and the ear-wax of female buffaloes (<s>mahiṣī</s>) — [add] a paste of each in sequence, in one-sixteenth portion. (GRht 16.5)

children.text: sāraṇāya vasātaipamāha maṇḍūketyādi // GRhtCM_16.2-5:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the fat-oil for <s>sāraṇa</s>, with 'frog' and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.2–5:1)

children.text:
maṇḍūko bhekaḥ matsyo japacaraviśeṣaḥ kacchapaḥ kamaṭhaḥ pratītaḥ
                            japaukāḥ pratītāḥ ahiḥ sarpaḥ sūkaro varāhaḥ ādiśabdād
                            gomahiṣagajoṣṭrakharanarakarkaṭaśiśumārā api grāhyāḥ // GRhtCM_16.2-5:2
                            //
children.translated_text: <s>Maṇḍūka</s> is a frog; <s>matsya</s> is a particular aquatic creature; <s>kacchapa</s> is a tortoise, well-known; <s>jalaukā</s> (leech) — well-known; <s>ahi</s> is a serpent; <s>sūkara</s> is a boar; from the word 'and the like,' cow, buffalo, elephant, camel, donkey, human, crab, and crocodile (<s>śiśumāra</s>) should also be included. (GRhtCM 16.2–5:2)
Now, combining the fat of each one among these individually, one should cook the <s>sāraṇa</s> oil — the oil that is itself the <s>sāraṇa</s> — cook it with fire, is the completion. (GRhtCM 16.2–5:3)

children.text: sāraṇataipaviśeṣamāha jyotiṣmatītyādi // GRhtCM_16.2-5:4 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the specific <s>sāraṇa</s> oil, with '<s>jyotiṣmatī</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.2–5:4)

children.text:
jyotiṣmatīvibhītakakarañjakaṭutumbītaipaṃ jyotiṣmatī kaṅguṇī vibhītakaḥ
                            kapidrumaḥ karañjaḥ pratītaḥ kaṭutumbī kaṭukā yā tumbī etāsāṃ taipaṃ
                            ekaṃ ato dviguṇito yo raktakaṣāyaḥ raktagaṇasya kvāthaḥ taṃ niyojya
                            pūrvasaṃbandhāt // GRhtCM_16.2-5:5 //
children.translated_text: Oil of <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>, <s>vibhītaka</s>, <s>karañja</s>, and bitter gourd — <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> is <s>kaṅguṇī</s> (Celastrus paniculatus); <s>vibhītaka</s> is the <s>kapidru</s> tree; <s>karañja</s> is well-known; <s>kaṭutumbī</s> is the bitter variety of gourd; the oil of these — one [part]; from this, doubled red decoction — the decoction of the red group — should be applied, connecting with the previous [verse]. (GRhtCM 16.2–5:5)

children.text:
kena saha caturguṇavasayā tathā taipataḥ caturguṇitena dugdhena saha
                            pacet pākaṃ kuryāditi // GRhtCM_16.2-5:6 //
children.translated_text: With what? With fat four times [the amount of oil]; likewise, with milk four times [the amount] of oil, one should cook — perform the cooking. (GRhtCM 16.2–5:6)

children.text: sāraṇataipavidhānāya raktavargamāha dāḍimetyādi // GRhtCM_16.2-5:7 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For the <s>sāraṇa</s> oil procedure, he states the red group, with 'pomegranate' and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.2–5:7)

children.text:
dāḍimaṃ pratītaṃ papāśo brahmavṛkṣaḥ bandhūkapuṣpaṃ
                            madhyāhnavikāśikusumaṃ rajanī haridrā etābhiḥ aruṇasahitābhiḥ aruṇaṃ
                            āraktaṃ yaddravyaṃ kārpāsakusumādikaṃ tatsahitābhiḥ // GRhtCM_16.2-5:8
                            //
children.translated_text: Pomegranate (<s>dāḍima</s>) — well-known; <s>palāśa</s> is the <s>brahma</s>-tree (Butea monosperma); <s>bandhūka</s> flowers — the flowers that bloom at midday; <s>rajanī</s> is turmeric (<s>haridrā</s>); with these, accompanied by <s>aruṇa</s> (reddish) — <s>aruṇa</s> means deeply red, whatever substance [that is], such as cotton flowers and the like, accompanied by those. (GRhtCM 16.2–5:8)

Of what quality is this red group? Accompanied by madder (<s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>) — well-known; lac-juice (<s>lākṣārasa</s>) — the juice of lac (<s>lakṣā</s>); sandalwood (<s>candana</s>) — red sandalwood. (GRhtCM 16.2–5:9)

children.text: sāraṇataipe kapkamāha vidrumetyādi // GRhtCM_16.2-5:10 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the paste for the <s>sāraṇa</s> oil, with 'coral' and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.2–5:10)

children.text:
vidrumaṃ patāmaṇir bhūnāgamapaṃ gaṇḍūpadapurīṣaṃ
                            makṣikādhvāṅkṣaśapabhānāṃ makṣikā jīvaviśeṣaḥ dhvāṅkṣāḥ kākāḥ śapabhaḥ
                            pataṅgaḥ iti haimaḥ teṣāṃ viṭ śakṛt punarmahiṣīṇāṃ karṇamapaṃ krameṇa
                            kapāṃśena ṣoḍaśāṃśena kapkaṃ prativāpaṃ dattvā pūrvataipamuttārayet //
                            GRhtCM_16.2-5:11 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vidruma</s> is coral (<s>latāmaṇi</s>); <s>bhūnāgamala</s> is earthworm-excrement; of flies (<s>makṣikā</s>) — a particular living creature; crows (<s>dhvāṅkṣa</s>); grasshoppers (<s>śalabha</s>) — moths/insects; thus pertaining to gold; their droppings (<s>viṭ</s>, i.e., <s>śakṛt</s>). Again, the ear-wax of female buffaloes — in sequence, in one-sixteenth portion as a paste (<s>kalka</s>), as a counter-additive (<s>prativāpa</s>), having added [this], one should prepare the aforementioned oil. (GRhtCM 16.2–5:11)

children.text: sāraṇa
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: <s>Sāraṇa</s> (extraction procedure)]

children.text: paṭagālitaṃ gṛhītvā sūtaṃ sampūrṇadīrghamūṣāyām /
children.translated_text: Having taken [mercury] strained through cloth, [place it] in a full, elongated crucible (<s>mūṣā</s>);

children.text: tadanu khalu taptataile pradrāvya samaṃ kṣiped bījam // GRht_16.6 //
children.translated_text: then indeed, having melted [it] in hot oil, one should cast the <s>bīja</s> (seed) in equal [proportion]. (GRht 16.6)

children.text: mūṣāvaktraṃ sthagayel latādvayaprotavitatanaddhena /
children.translated_text: One should seal the mouth of the crucible with a cloth tied by two strings (<s>latādvaya</s>), stretched and bound,

children.text: tailārdrapaṭena tato bījaṃ prakṣipya samakālam // GRht_16.7 //
children.translated_text: moistened with oil; then, having cast the <s>bīja</s>, simultaneously — (GRht 16.7)

children.text: piśitānuguṇaṃ bījaiḥ sāraṇavidhinā niyojitaḥ sūtaḥ /
children.translated_text: mercury, combined with <s>bījas</s> proportionate to the flesh (<s>piśita</s>), employed by the <s>sāraṇa</s> procedure,

children.text: akṣīyamāṇo milati ca bījair baddho bhavatyeva // GRht_16.8 //
children.translated_text: combines without diminishing with the <s>bījas</s>, and becomes bound (<s>baddha</s>) indeed. (GRht 16.8)

children.text: siddhataipakṛtyamāha paṭetyādi // GRhtCM_16.6-8:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the procedure with the prepared oil, with 'cloth' and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.6–8:1)

children.text:
tatsiddhataipaṃ paṭagāpitaṃ vastrapūtaṃ gṛhītvā tadanu tatpaścāt //
                            GRhtCM_16.6-8:2 //
children.translated_text: That prepared oil, strained through cloth (<s>paṭagālita</s>) — filtered through fabric — having taken it; then — after that. (GRhtCM 16.6–8:2)

children.text:
sampūrṇadīrghamūṣāyāṃ gostanākārāyāṃ taptataipe koṣṇasāraṇataipe sūtaṃ
                            kṣipet // GRhtCM_16.6-8:3 //
children.translated_text: In a full, elongated crucible — one shaped like a cow's teat — in the warm <s>sāraṇa</s> oil, one should cast the mercury. (GRhtCM 16.6–8:3)

children.text:
kiṃ kṛtvā bījaṃ samaṃ samabhāgaṃ rasatupyaṃ yadbhāvyaṃ mahābījaṃ tat
                            bhāvitaṃ kṛtvetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_16.6-8:4 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? The <s>bīja</s> in equal portion — equal in mercury-portion — that which is to be processed, the great <s>bīja</s>, having processed it, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 16.6–8:4)

children.text: sāraṇayantrasya vidhānamāha mūṣetyādi /
children.translated_text: He states the method of the streaming apparatus (<s>sāraṇāyantra</s>) with 'mūṣā' and so forth.

children.text:
samakāpam ekakāpaṃ yathā syāttathā bījaṃ mūṣāntarnikṣipya tato+anantaraṃ
                            mūṣāvaktraṃ sthagayet ācchādayet // GRhtCM_16.6-8:5 //
children.translated_text: With equal cavities — such that there is a single cavity — having placed the seed inside the crucible, thereafter one should cover the mouth of the crucible — should conceal [it]. (GRhtCM 16.6-8:5)

children.text: kena taipārdrapaṭena sāraṇataipārdravastreṇa // GRhtCM_16.6-8:6 //
children.translated_text: With what? With a cloth moistened with streaming oil (<s>sāraṇataila</s>) — with a cloth wet with streaming oil. (GRhtCM 16.6-8:6)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭena patādvayena vastracīradvayena protaṃ ca tadvitataṃ vistīrṇaṃ
                            ca tat naddhaṃ baddhaṃ tena // GRhtCM_16.6-8:7 //
children.translated_text: Of what specification? With a double cloth — with two pieces of cloth-strips — spread out and extended, tied — bound — with that. (GRhtCM 16.6-8:7)

children.text: akṣīyamāṇo mipati na kṣīyata ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_16.6-8:8 //
children.translated_text: Without being diminished, it fuses — meaning it does not diminish. (GRhtCM 16.6-8:8)

children.text:
sūte mipati baddho jñeyaḥ bījaiḥ saha mipito baddho bhavatītyarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_16.6-8:9 //
children.translated_text: It fuses with the mercury — the meaning is: having fused with the seeds, it becomes bound. (GRhtCM 16.6-8:9)

children.text: pītādivarṇakathanenāpi kartuṃ sūcitam // GRhtCM_16.6-8:10 //
children.translated_text: By the mention of yellow and other colors, [the successful outcome] is also indicated. (GRhtCM 16.6-8:10)

children.text: mercury:: pratisāraṇa
children.translated_text: [Section:] Mercury — <s>pratisāraṇa</s> (counter-streaming)

children.text: tadvadgabhīramūṣe sāraṇatailārdrameva rasarājam /
children.translated_text: Likewise, in a deep crucible, the king of mercury, moistened with streaming oil,

children.text: sūtāddviguṇaṃ kanakaṃ dattvā pratisārayettadanu // GRht_16.9 //
children.translated_text: having added gold double the amount of mercury, one should perform counter-streaming (<s>pratisāraṇa</s>) thereafter. (GRht 16.9)

children.text:
sūtabījasāraṇānantaraṃ kanakasāraṇamāha tadvadityādi // GRhtCM_16.9:1
                            //
children.translated_text: After the streaming of mercury with seed, he describes the streaming of gold with 'tadvat' (likewise) and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.9:1)

children.text:
tadvat pūrvavidhānena gabhīramūṣe dīrghamūṣāyāṃ sāraṇataipārdraṃ
                            sāraṇataipāpputaṃ eva niścayena rasarājaṃ kuryāditi śeṣaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_16.9:2 //
children.translated_text: Likewise — by the previous procedure — in a deep crucible, a long crucible, moistened with streaming oil — smeared with streaming oil — certainly, the king of mercury should be [prepared] — this is the complement. (GRhtCM 16.9:2)

children.text:
tadanu tatpaścātsūtāddviguṇaṃ yatkanakaṃ hema tadatra dattvā
                            pratisārayetsāraṇaṃ kuryātpūrvavat // GRhtCM_16.9:3 //
children.translated_text: Thereafter — after that — gold that is double the mercury, having added that gold, one should perform counter-streaming — should perform streaming as before. (GRhtCM 16.9:3)

children.text: mercury:: anusāraṇa
children.translated_text: [Section:] Mercury — <s>anusāraṇa</s> (follow-up streaming)

children.text: bījena triguṇena tu sūtakamanusārayetprakāśastham / GRht_16.10ab/
children.translated_text: With seed in triple quantity, one should perform follow-up streaming on mercury placed in an open [crucible]. (GRht 16.10ab)

children.text: vidhyantaramāha bījenetyādi // GRhtCM_16.10ab:1 //
children.translated_text: He states an alternative method with 'bījena' (with seed) and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.10ab:1)

children.text:
prakāśasthaṃ prakāśamūṣāgataṃ sūtaṃ triguṇena bījena anusārayet
                                pratisārayet // GRhtCM_16.10ab:2 //
children.translated_text: The mercury placed in an open crucible (<s>prakāśamūṣā</s>) should be follow-up streamed — counter-streamed — with seed in triple quantity. (GRhtCM 16.10ab:2)

children.text: īṣannāgaṃ deyaṃ trividhāyāṃ sāraṇāyāṃ tu // GRht_16.10cd //
children.translated_text: A small amount of lead should be given in the threefold streaming. (GRht 16.10cd)

children.text:
kiṃ kṛtvā īṣadappaṃ nāgaṃ dattvā trividhāyāṃ sāraṇāyāmevaṃ vidheyam iti
                            // GRhtCM_16.10cd:1 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? Having given a small amount of lead, in the threefold streaming — thus it should be done. (GRhtCM 16.10cd:1)

children.text: sāraṇāyantra
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Sāraṇāyantra</s> (streaming apparatus)

children.text: kṛtvā mūṣāṃ dīrghāṃ bandhitatribhāgapraṇālikāṃ tāṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Having made a long crucible with a channel sealed at one-third [of its length],

children.text: tasyāgre prakaṭamūṣā sacchidrā sudṛḍhamṛttikāliptā // GRht_16.11 //
children.translated_text: at its front, an open crucible, perforated, firmly coated with clay. (GRht 16.11)

children.text: tasminprakṣipya rasaṃ sāraṇatailānvitaṃ tapte /
children.translated_text: Having placed mercury in that [apparatus], combined with streaming oil, in the heated [vessel],

children.text: pradrāvya tulyakanakaṃ kṣipte'smin milati rasarājaḥ // GRht_16.12 //
children.translated_text: having melted gold in equal [quantity] and cast [it] therein — the king of mercury fuses [with it]. (GRht 16.12)

children.text: sāraṇayantramāha kṛtvetyādi // GRhtCM_16.11-12:1 //
children.translated_text: He describes the streaming apparatus with 'kṛtvā' (having made) and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.11-12:1)

children.text:
prathamaṃ dīrghāṃ mūṣāṃ kṛtvā ca punaḥ tāṃ bandhitatribhāgapraṇāpikāṃ
                            bandhitā tribhāge praṇāpikā yasyāḥ sā tāṃ ca kṛtvā tasyāgre yantrasyāgre
                            praṇāpikāyāṃ mūṣāntarityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_16.11-12:2 //
children.translated_text: First, having made a long crucible, and furthermore that [crucible] with a channel sealed at one-third — the channel is sealed at one-third of which — that [crucible]; having made it; at its front — at the front of the apparatus — in the channel, meaning inside the crucible — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 16.11-12:2)

children.text:
sudṛḍhamṛttikāpiptā sacchidrā randhrasahitā prakaṭamūṣā prakāśamūṣā
                            kāryeti yantram // GRhtCM_16.11-12:3 //
children.translated_text: Firmly coated with clay, perforated — having holes — an open crucible (<s>prakāśamūṣā</s>) — a visible crucible — should be made; thus [is] the apparatus. (GRhtCM 16.11-12:3)

children.text:
tasminyantre sāraṇataipānvitaṃ rasaṃ prakṣipya tato+anantaraṃ tupyaṃ
                            kanakaṃ pradrāvya gāpayitvā tasminneva tapte yantre kṣipte sati raso
                            mipati ekatāṃ yāti // GRhtCM_16.11-12:4 //
children.translated_text: In that apparatus, having placed mercury combined with streaming oil, thereafter having melted — liquefied — gold in equal [quantity], when cast into that very heated apparatus, mercury fuses — attains oneness. (GRhtCM 16.11-12:4)

children.text: sāraṇāyantra
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Sāraṇāyantra</s> (streaming apparatus)

children.text: kṛtvā nalikāṃ dīrghāṃ ṣaḍaṃgulāṃ dhūrtakusumasaṃkāśām /
children.translated_text: Having made a long tube of six finger-breadths, resembling a datura flower,

children.text: mūṣāpyadho vilagnā kartavyā vai mṛdā lepyā // GRht_16.13 //
children.translated_text: a crucible should be attached below it; it should indeed be coated with clay. (GRht 16.13)

children.text: aparā sūkṣmā nalikā kāryā saptāṃgulā sudṛḍhā /
children.translated_text: Another thin tube of seven finger-breadths, very firm, should be made,

children.text: madhye praviśati ca yathā tadvatkāryā ca dṛḍhamukhā // GRht_16.14 //
children.translated_text: such that it enters the middle [of the first tube]; it should be made with a firm mouth. (GRht 16.14)

children.text: tasminsūtaḥ kṣiptaḥ sāraṇatailānvito madanaruddhamukhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therein mercury is placed, combined with streaming oil, with its mouth sealed with beeswax;

children.text: tadanu bṛhattamayā hema pradrāvya hemakoṣṭhikayā // GRht_16.15 //
children.translated_text: thereafter, having melted gold with a large gold-furnace, (GRht 16.15)

children.text: tasminmadhye kṣiptvā nalikāgramadhomukhīṃ kuryāt /
children.translated_text: having cast [the gold] into the middle of that [apparatus], one should make the tube-tip face downward,

children.text: antarūrdhvaṃ bhārākrāntāṃ sarati raso nātra saṃdehaḥ // GRht_16.16 //
children.translated_text: with weight pressing upward inside — mercury streams [through] — there is no doubt. (GRht 16.16)

children.text: anyadyantramāha kṛtvetyādi // GRhtCM_16.13-16:1 //
children.translated_text: He describes another apparatus with 'kṛtvā' (having made) and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.13-16:1)

children.text:
pūrvavaddīrghāṃ dhūrtakusumasaṃkāśāṃ dhattūrapuṣpasaṃkāśāṃ
                            pūrvayantranapikāyāḥ sthāne evaṃvidhāṃ ṣaḍaṅgupāṃ napikāṃ kuryād iti
                            vyaktiḥ // GRhtCM_16.13-16:2 //
children.translated_text: As before, a long [tube], resembling a datura flower — resembling a <s>dhattūra</s>-blossom — in place of the tube of the previous apparatus, such a tube of six finger-breadths should be made — this is the clarification. (GRhtCM 16.13-16:2)

children.text:
mūṣāpi adho vipagnā napikāyāstapabhāge mūṣā vipagnā saṃpagnā kāryā //
                            GRhtCM_16.13-16:3 //
children.translated_text: A crucible should be attached — connected — below the tube, at the lower part of the tube. (GRhtCM 16.13-16:3)

children.text: sā ca mṛdā mṛtsnayā pepyā // GRhtCM_16.13-16:4 //
children.translated_text: And that should be coated with clay — with earth. (GRhtCM 16.13-16:4)

children.text:
punarapi aparā sūkṣmā nāpikā saptāṅgupā saptāṅgupaparimāṇā sudṛḍhā
                            manoharakaṭhinā kāryā yathā madhye ṣaḍaṅgupanāpikāntaḥ praviśati
                            tadvattathā kāryā // GRhtCM_16.13-16:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, another thin tube of seven finger-breadths — of seven finger-breadths in measure — very firm, attractively hard, should be made such that it enters the middle of the six-finger-breadth tube — in that manner it should be made. (GRhtCM 16.13-16:5)

children.text:
kiṃbhūtā dṛḍhamukhā dṛḍhaṃ mukhaṃ yasyāḥ sā evaṃrūpā tasmin saṃsiddhe
                            yantre sāraṇataipānvitaḥ sūtaḥ kṣiptaḥ san madanaruddhamukhaḥ kāryaḥ
                            madanena sikthakena ruddhaṃ mudritaṃ mukhaṃ yasya saḥ //
                            GRhtCM_16.13-16:6 //
children.translated_text: Of what nature? Having a firm mouth — that of which the mouth is firm — of such form. In that completed apparatus, mercury combined with streaming oil, having been placed, should be made with its mouth sealed with beeswax — <s>madana</s> means beeswax, sealed means closed. (GRhtCM 16.13-16:6)

children.text:
tadanu tatpaścāt hemakoṣṭhikayā hemno yā koṣṭhī eva koṣṭhikā tayā hema
                            svarṇaṃ pradrāvya drāvayitvā tatra kṣipet ityadhyāhāryam //
                            GRhtCM_16.13-16:7 //
children.translated_text: Thereafter — after that — with a gold-furnace — the furnace which is for gold, that very small furnace — with that, having melted gold, one should cast [it] there — this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 16.13-16:7)

children.text:
tasminyantre madhye'ntaḥ napikāgraṃ napikāyāḥ saptāṅgupāyā agrabhāgaṃ
                            kṣiptvā adhomukhīṃ kuryāt punarūrdhvaṃ bhārākrāntāṃ kuryāt //
                            GRhtCM_16.13-16:8 //
children.translated_text: In that apparatus, inside, having inserted the tip of the seven-finger-breadth tube, one should make [it] face downward; furthermore, one should make [it] weight-pressed upward. (GRhtCM 16.13-16:8)

children.text:
iti kṛte sati rasaḥ sarati hemnā mipati na saṃdehaḥ niyatamityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_16.13-16:9 //
children.translated_text: When this is done, mercury streams — fuses with gold — there is no doubt, meaning certainly — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 16.13-16:9)

children.text: sāraṇāyantra
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Sāraṇāyantra</s> (streaming apparatus)

children.text: kṛtvāṣṭāṃgulamūṣāṃ dhūrtakusumopamāṃ dṛḍhāṃ ślakṣṇām /
children.translated_text: A tube of one <s>vitasti</s> (span) in length should also be made; at its front, two firm crucibles,

children.text: aparā madhyagatāpi ca sacchidrā ca saptāṃgulā kāryā // GRht_16.17 //
children.translated_text: one should be made face-up, without a hole; and the other with its hole sealed, thin-bodied. (GRht 16.19)

children.text: niruddhatāṃ ca kṛtvā sūtaṃ prakṣipya tailasaṃyuktam /
children.translated_text: Having placed mercury first, combined with streaming oil, and laying [the apparatus] on the ground,

children.text: nirdhūmaṃ karṣāgnau sthāpya mūṣāṃ susaṃdhitāṃ kṛtvā // GRht_16.18 //
children.translated_text: in the face-up crucible, having covered the seed therein, (GRht 16.20)

children.text: anyadyantravidhānamāha kṛtvetyādi // GRhtCM_16.17-18:1 //
children.translated_text: He describes another apparatus method with 'crucibles should be made.' (GRhtCM 16.19-21:1)

children.text:
aṣṭāṅgupamūṣāṃ aṣṭāṅgupaparimāṇadīrghāṃ dhūrtakusumopamāṃ
                            kanakapuṣpasadṛśāṃ dṛḍhāṃ kaṭhināṃ śpakṣṇāṃ masṛṇāṃ evaṃvidhāṃ mūṣāṃ
                            kṛtvā aparā dvitīyā saptāṅgupā saptāṅgupaparimāṇadīrghā sacchidrā
                            randhrayuktā sā madhyagatā antaḥpraviṣṭā kāryā apītyavaśyaṃ iti
                            mūṣādvayayantraṃ siddham // GRhtCM_16.17-18:2 //
children.translated_text: Of what specification? At its front, of one-span tube [measure] — tubes of <s>vitasti</s> measure — those two of such kind, very firm — both should be made — this is the intent. (GRhtCM 16.19-21:2)

children.text:
taccāha pūrvoktāyāmantaḥpraviṣṭāyāṃ saptāṅgupāyāṃ sūtaṃ taipasaṃyuktaṃ
                            sāraṇataipasahitaṃ prakṣipya niruddhatāṃ ca kṛtvā nirdhūmaṃ yathā syāt
                            tathā karṣāgnau mūṣāṃ sthāpya punaḥ kiṃ kṛtvā susaṃdhitāṃ sandhimudritāṃ
                            kṛtvā pūrvavatsārayedityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_16.17-18:3 //
children.translated_text: Of the two, one crucible should be made face-up; the other [is] concave — this is the purport. (GRhtCM 16.19-21:3)

children.text: sāraṇāyantra
children.translated_text: The face-up one — of what specification? Without a hole — without an opening; hole-sealed — the hole is sealed in which, on the body of the crucible. (GRhtCM 16.19-21:4)

children.text: vitastimātranalikāpi kāryā sudṛḍhe tadagrato mūṣe /
children.translated_text: He states [the procedure]: first, having placed mercury in the previously described apparatus, combined with streaming oil, and having placed [it] on the ground, in the said face-up crucible, having covered — melted — the seed, the great seed, meaning having given [it] — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 16.19-21:5)

children.text: uttānaikā kāryā niśchidrā chidramudritā ca tanau // GRht_16.19 //
children.translated_text: Thereafter, knowing the seed [to be] clear — without impurity, in liquid form — one should place [it] positioned in the hole — should cast [it] inside the hole — this is the intent. From the casting inside the hole, the seed falls upon the mercury; being so, mercury certainly binds — after casting the seed inside the hole, the hole should become un-holed — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 16.19-21:6)

children.text: dattvā sūtaṃ pūrvaṃ sāraṇatailānvitaṃ nidhāpya bhuvi /
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Sāraṇā</s> (Streaming) — sixth [variant]

children.text: uttānāyāṃ mūṣāyāṃ tasyāṃ bījaṃ samāvṛtya // GRht_16.20 //
children.translated_text: And that open crucible should be made face-down, with the tube set in at half a finger-breadth;

children.text: svacchaṃ jñātvā ca tatastadbījaṃ chidrasaṃsthitaṃ kuryāt /
children.translated_text: the tube should be made according to the method — mercury above and seed below. (GRht 16.22)

children.text: bījaṃ sūtasyopari nipatati badhnātyasaṃdeham // GRht_16.21 //
children.translated_text: Having sealed the crucible by the [proper] method, [and] smelted [it] in the furnace, the seed melted,

children.text: anyayantravidhānamāha mūṣe kārye // GRhtCM_16.19-21:1 //
children.translated_text: knowing [this], then inverting [it] — it binds the king of mercury. (GRht 16.23)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭe tadagrato vitastimātranapike vitastiparimāṇe napike yayoste
                            evaṃvidhe sudṛḍhe ubhe kārye ityabhiprāyaḥ // GRhtCM_16.19-21:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Sā' (that) and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.22-23:1)

children.text:
tayormadhye ekā mūṣā uttānā kāryā aparā nimneti bhāvaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_16.19-21:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, that one-span tube [serves as] the open crucible — set in at half a finger-breadth, having entered inside the crucible — face-down, mouth-downward — should be made. The tube of that open crucible — the channel — should be made according to the method, the tradition of the treatise and commentary, such that mercury is above and the seed below — this is the meaning. 'The crucible' and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.22-23:2)

children.text:
uttānā kiṃviśiṣṭā niśchidrā nirvraṇā chidramudritā chidraṃ mudritaṃ
                            yasyāṃ tanau mūṣāśarīre iti // GRhtCM_16.19-21:4 //

taccāha pūrvaṃ prathamaṃ sūtaṃ yantre pūrvokte sāraṇataipānvitaṃ dattvā
                            bhuvi nidhāpya tasyāṃ uktāyāṃ uttānāyāṃ mūṣāyāṃ bījaṃ mahābījaṃ
                            samāvṛtya dravīkṛtya dattvetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_16.19-21:5 //

tato+anantaraṃ bījaṃ svacchamamapaṃ dravarūpaṃ jñātvā chidrasaṃsthitaṃ
                            kuryāt chidrāntaḥ kṣipedityabhiprāyaḥ chidrāntaḥkṣepaṇāt bījaṃ
                            rasasyopari patati sati sūtaṃ asaṃdehaṃ yathā syāttathā badhnāti bīje
                            chidrāntaḥkṣepaṇānantaraṃ chidramacchidraṃ syādityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_16.19-21:6 //
sāraṇā (6)
sā ca prakāśamūṣā nyubjā kāryārdhāṅgulasaṃniviṣṭā /
nalikā kāryā vidhinā ūrdhve sūtastvadho bījam // GRht_16.22 //
mūṣāṃ nirudhya vidhinā dhmātā koṣṭhe drutaṃ bījam /
jñātvā parivartya tato nibadhnāti sūtarājaṃ ca // GRht_16.23 //
setyādi // GRhtCM_16.22-23:1 //

punaḥ sā vitastimātranapikā prakāśamūṣā ardhāṅgupasuniviṣṭā mūṣāntaḥ
                            praviṣṭā nyubjā adhomukhī kāryā tasyāḥ prakāśamūṣāyāḥ napikā praṇāpikā
                            vidhinā śāstravārtikasaṃpradāyena kāryā yathordhve sūto bhavedadho
                            bījamityarthaḥ mūṣām ityādi // GRhtCM_16.22-23:2 //

mūṣāṃ nirudhya randhraṃ dūrīkṛtya vidhinā koṣṭhe koṣṭhīyantre sā mūṣā
                            dhmātā kāryā drutaṃ dravarūpaṃ kṛtaṃ bījaṃ jñātvā parivartya ca mūṣāyāṃ
                            bījasya parivartanaṃ kṛtvā tato bījaṃ sūtarājaṃ badhnātīti //
                            GRhtCM_16.22-23:3 //
children.translated_text: Having sealed the crucible — closing the hole — by the [prescribed] method, that crucible should be blown in a furnace (<s>koṣṭhī</s>)-apparatus; having known the seed to have become liquid — in molten form — and having turned [it] in the crucible — having turned the seed over in the crucible — then the seed binds the king of mercury (<s>sūtarāja</s>). (GRhtCM 16.22-23:3)

children.text: sāraṇā:: with ḍamaruyantra
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>sāraṇā</s> (liquefaction): with the <s>ḍamaru</s>-apparatus

children.text: athavā ḍamarukayantre sāraṇavidhinā niyojitaḥ sūtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Or, mercury employed in the <s>ḍamaruka</s>-apparatus (<s>ḍamarukayantra</s>) by the liquefaction method —

children.text: sarati rasendro vidhinā jñātvā tatkarmakauśalyam // GRht_16.24 //
children.translated_text: the king of mercury flows by the [proper] method, having understood the skill of that operation. (GRht 16.24)

children.text: athānyadyantram āha athavetyādi // GRhtCM_16.24:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now he describes another apparatus, with 'or' and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.24:1)

children.text:
vidhinā sāraṇavidhānena ḍamarukayantre uktapakṣaṇapātanakaraṇocite yantre
                            sūto niyojitaḥ san sarati bījena mipati // GRhtCM_16.24:2 //
children.translated_text: By the method — the liquefaction procedure — mercury employed in the <s>ḍamaruka</s>-apparatus — an apparatus suited for the described extraction operation — flows, i.e., combines with the seed. (GRhtCM 16.24:2)

children.text: jāraṇā after sāraṇā => vedha potency
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>jāraṇā</s> (digestion) after <s>sāraṇā</s> (liquefaction) ⇒ <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) potency

children.text: tatsāritaṃ rasendraṃ grāsavidhānena jārayettadanu /
children.translated_text: That liquefied mercury (<s>rasendra</s>) should then be digested by the bolus method;

children.text: punarapi sāritasūto vidhyati koṭyaṃśataḥ śulbam // GRht_16.25 //
children.translated_text: furthermore, the liquefied mercury transmutes copper in the proportion of one <s>koṭi</s> (ten million). (GRht 16.25)

children.text:
kiṃ kṛtvā rasendro niyojitaḥ jñātvā tatkarmakauśapyaṃ
                            rasendrakarmaprāvīṇyaṃ jñātveti // GRhtCM_16.25:1 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? The mercury is employed having known the skill of that operation — the expertise in mercury-work — having known [it]. (GRhtCM 16.25:1)

children.text: sāraṇā:: with krāmaṇāvasā
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>sāraṇā</s>: with <s>krāmaṇa</s>-fat (<s>krāmaṇāvasā</s>)

children.text: krāmaṇavasādiyogādvidhinā sūtaḥ saratyeva /
children.translated_text: Through the application of <s>krāmaṇa</s>-fat and other [substances], mercury indeed flows by the [proper] method;

children.text: capalatvātilaghutvādbījaṃ yato+atha vipluṣaḥ kāryaḥ // GRht_16.26 //
children.translated_text: because of its fickleness and extreme lightness — since the seed [tends to scatter] — therefore droplets should be consolidated. (GRht 16.26)

children.text: pūrvoktaṃ dṛḍhīkartumāha krāmaṇetyādi // GRhtCM_16.26:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] To confirm what was previously stated, he says 'by <s>krāmaṇa</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.26:1)

children.text:
sūto vidhinoktavidhānena krāmaṇocitā yā vasā maṇḍūkādīnāṃ tā eva ādayo
                            yeṣāṃ teṣāṃ yogātsarati sāraṇā syāt punarbījayuto+api sūtaḥ
                            capapatvātipaghutvāt capapatvaṃ cañcapatvaṃ ca atipaghutvaṃ ca
                            tasmāddhetoḥ avippuṣaḥ sthiraḥ kāryaḥ // GRhtCM_16.26:2 //
children.translated_text: Mercury, by the prescribed method, through the application of <s>krāmaṇa</s>-suited fat — such as that of frogs and the like — these are the 'and others' — by their combination, flows — liquefaction occurs; furthermore, even mercury combined with seed, because of fickleness and extreme lightness — fickleness meaning instability, and extreme lightness — for that reason, should be made stable — not scattered into droplets. (GRhtCM 16.26:2)

children.text: sāraṇa, krāmaṇa:: with lead etc.
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>sāraṇa</s> (liquefaction), <s>krāmaṇa</s> (transmutation): with lead etc.

children.text: sarati sukhena ca sūto dahati mukhaṃ naiva hastapādādi /
children.translated_text: Mercury flows easily, and does not burn the mouth, hands, feet, or other [body parts];

children.text: kramati rasaḥ phaṇiyogānmākṣikayutahemagairikayā // GRht_16.27 //
children.translated_text: mercury transmutes through the application of lead (<s>phaṇi</s>), together with pyrite-combined gold and ochre (<s>gairikā</s>). (GRht 16.27)

children.text: pūrvoktaguṇānāha saratītyādi // GRhtCM_16.27:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the qualities mentioned before, with 'flows' and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.27:1)

children.text:
pūrvavidhānā sūtaḥ sarati sāritaḥ sūto mukhaṃ na dahati hastapādādi ca
                            aṅgavibhāgaṃ naiva dahati // GRhtCM_16.27:2 //
children.translated_text: Mercury prepared by the aforesaid method flows — liquefied mercury does not burn the mouth, and does not burn the hands, feet, or other limb-parts either. (GRhtCM 16.27:2)

children.text:
punaḥ phaṇiyogāt nāgasaṃyogataḥ mākṣikayutahemagairikayā saha
                            tāpyamipitasvarṇagairikayā sārdhaṃ krāmati // GRhtCM_16.27:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, through the application of lead (<s>phaṇi</s>/nāga), together with pyrite-combined gold-ochre — together with <s>tāpya</s>-mixed <s>svarṇagairikā</s> (gold-ochre) — it transmutes. (GRhtCM 16.27:3)

children.text: druti, sāraṇā
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>druti</s> (melting), <s>sāraṇā</s> (liquefaction)

children.text: mākṣīkasattvayogātphaṇiyogānnāgavad dravati śīghram /
children.translated_text: Through the combination of <s>mākṣika</s>-essence (pyrite-essence) and lead (<s>phaṇi</s>), [mercury] melts rapidly like lead;

children.text: dravati ca kanake sūtaḥ saṃsāryate vidhinā // GRht_16.28 //
children.translated_text: and mercury melts in gold, [and] is liquefied by the [proper] method. (GRht 16.28)

children.text: sukhena sāraṇavidhānamāha mākṣiketyādi // GRhtCM_16.28:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the easy liquefaction method, with '<s>mākṣika</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.28:1)

children.text:
kanakaṃ hema mākṣikasattvayogāt phaṇisaṃyogānnāgasaṃyogācca śīghraṃ
                            dravati kanake dravati sati vidhinā sāraṇataipādinā saṃsāryate sāraṇā
                            kriyata iti // GRhtCM_16.28:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kanaka</s> means gold; through the combination of <s>mākṣika</s>-essence and lead (<s>phaṇi</s>/nāga), it rapidly melts in gold; when melted, by the method of liquefaction-oil and the like, the liquefaction is performed. (GRhtCM 16.28:2)

children.text: mercury:: preparation for vedha
children.translated_text: [Section on] mercury: preparation for <s>vedha</s> (transmutation)

children.text: tasmād dravyavidhāyī sūto bījena sārito laghunā /
children.translated_text: Therefore mercury becomes an agent of transformation (<s>dravyavidhāyī</s>), when liquefied with a small seed;

children.text: samasāritaḥ subaddho mūṣāyāṃ syātsamāvartaḥ // GRht_16.29 //
children.translated_text: when equally liquefied and well-bound, it becomes a homogeneous melt (<s>samāvarta</s>) in the crucible. (GRht 16.29)

children.text: sāraṇayā pāradaguṇānāha tasmādityādi // GRhtCM_16.29:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the qualities of mercury [achieved] through liquefaction, with 'therefore' and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.29:1)

children.text:
tasmāddhetoḥ sūto dravyavidhāyī syāt iti śeṣaḥ dravyakartetyartha //
                            GRhtCM_16.29:2 //
children.translated_text: Therefore — for that reason — mercury becomes an agent of transformation — this is the completion; meaning: a maker of [new] substances. (GRhtCM 16.29:2)

children.text:
apaghunā bījena anappaparimāṇena mahābījena sāritaḥ san samasāritaḥ san
                            baddho bhavet ityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_16.29:3 //
children.translated_text: When liquefied with a small seed — with a great seed (<s>mahābīja</s>) of not-small measure — when equally liquefied, it would become bound — this must be supplied. (GRhtCM 16.29:3)

children.text:
mūṣāyāṃ samāvarto dravaṇaṃ syāt vahnidhamanāt iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_16.29:4
                            //
children.translated_text: In the crucible, <s>samāvarta</s> means melting — [this] would occur through bellows-blowing with fire, this is the completion. (GRhtCM 16.29:4)

children.text: (prati-, anu-)sāraṇā
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>pratisāraṇā</s> (counter-liquefaction) and <s>anusāraṇā</s> (follow-up liquefaction)

children.text: sāritavartitasūtaḥ samānabījena milati yaḥ sāryaḥ /
children.translated_text: Mercury that has been liquefied and rolled — that which combines with an equal seed is called <s>sārya</s> (to-be-liquefied);

children.text: dviguṇena pratisāryaḥ sa cānusāryaśca triguṇena // GRht_16.30 //
children.translated_text: that [which combines] with double [the seed] is <s>pratisārya</s> (counter-liquefied); and that with triple is <s>anusārya</s> (follow-up-liquefied). (GRht 16.30)

children.text: sāraṇakramamāha sarityādi // GRhtCM_16.30:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the sequence of liquefaction, with 'flows' and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.30:1)

children.text:
sāritavartitasūtaḥ sāritaścāsau vartitaś ceti vigrahaḥ // GRhtCM_16.30:2
                            //
children.translated_text: 'Liquefied-and-rolled mercury' — the resolution is: 'both liquefied and rolled.' (GRhtCM 16.30:2)

children.text:
yaḥ samānabījena tupyamahābījena mipati sa sāryaḥ yo dviguṇena mipati saḥ
                            pratisāryaḥ yaśca triguṇena so+anusārya iti sāraṇākramo darśitaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_16.30:3 //
children.translated_text: That which combines with an equal seed — the great seed in equal proportion — is <s>sārya</s>; that which combines with double is <s>pratisārya</s>; and that with triple is <s>anusārya</s> — thus the sequence of liquefaction is shown. (GRhtCM 16.30:3)

children.text: sāraṇa ~ vedha potency
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>sāraṇa</s> ~ <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) potency

children.text: śatavedhī sāryaḥ pratisāritaḥ syātsahasravedhī ca /
children.translated_text: The <s>sārya</s> (simply liquefied) transmutes a hundredfold; the <s>pratisārita</s> (counter-liquefied) becomes a thousandfold transmuter;

children.text: anusārito+ayutena ca vidhināpi balābalaṃ jñātvā // GRht_16.31 //
children.translated_text: the <s>anusārita</s> (follow-up-liquefied) [transmutes] ten-thousandfold — by the method, having known [the mercury's] strength and weakness. (GRht 16.31)

children.text: sāraṇakramasya guṇānāha śatetyādi // GRhtCM_16.31:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the virtues of the liquefaction sequence, with 'hundred' and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.31:1)

children.text:
yaḥ sāryaḥ samasāritaḥ sa śatavedhī syād ityabhiprāyaḥ // GRhtCM_16.31:2
                            //
children.translated_text: That which is <s>sārya</s> — equally liquefied — that would be a hundredfold transmuter, is the intended meaning. (GRhtCM 16.31:2)

children.text:
punaḥ pratisāritaḥ dviguṇabījena sārito yaḥ sūtaḥ sa sahasravedhī syāt //
                            GRhtCM_16.31:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>pratisārita</s> — mercury liquefied with double the seed — that would be a thousandfold transmuter. (GRhtCM 16.31:3)

children.text:
ca punaḥ anusāritaḥ triguṇabījena sāritaḥ sa ayutena ayutavedhī syāditi
                            vyaktiḥ // GRhtCM_16.31:4 //
children.translated_text: And furthermore, <s>anusārita</s> — liquefied with triple the seed — that would be a ten-thousandfold (<s>ayuta</s>) transmuter; this is the explanation. (GRhtCM 16.31:4)

children.text: vidhinā ityuktavidhānena // GRhtCM_16.31:5 //
children.translated_text: 'By the method' means by the stated procedure. (GRhtCM 16.31:5)

children.text:
bapābapaṃ jñātvā nyūnādhikyaṃ matvā vidhinā yukta iti śeṣaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_16.31:6 //
children.translated_text: 'Having known the strength and weakness' — having ascertained the greater and lesser [capacity], [applying it] properly by the method, is the completion. (GRhtCM 16.31:6)

children.text: anusāritena tu samaḥ svacchaḥ sūtaḥ sāritastadanu /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, pure mercury, liquefied with [a seed] equal to the <s>anusārita</s>, [and] then liquefied —

children.text: sa bhavati lakṣavedhī pratisāritaḥ prayutavedhī ca // GRht_16.32 //
children.translated_text: that becomes a hundred-thousandfold (<s>lakṣa</s>) transmuter; the <s>pratisārita</s> becomes a millionfold (<s>prayuta</s>) transmuter. (GRht 16.32)

children.text:
sāritapratisāritādanusāritasya viśeṣamāha anvityādi // GRhtCM_16.32:1
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the distinction of <s>anusārita</s> from <s>sārita</s> and <s>pratisārita</s>, with 'follow-up' and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.32:1)

Furthermore, 'pure' — mercury refined by the primary processes — if it is equal to <s>anusārita</s> — liquefied with a seed triple [in quantity], i.e., <s>anusārita</s> — if it were equal to that, then it would be a hundred-thousandfold transmuter. (GRhtCM 16.32:2)

children.text:
evaṃ pratisāritaḥ sūtaḥ samena sārito 'yutavedhī syāt // GRhtCM_16.32:3
                            //
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>pratisārita</s> mercury, when liquefied with an equal [seed], would be a ten-thousandfold transmuter. (GRhtCM 16.32:3)

children.text:
evaṃ svecchātisvacchavṛddhau vedhasyāpi vṛddhiḥ syāditi rahasyam //
                            GRhtCM_16.32:4 //
children.translated_text: Thus, with increasing purity and super-purity, there is also increase in transmutation-potency — this is the secret. (GRhtCM 16.32:4)

children.text: koṭiṃ vidhyati sūto+apyanusāritaḥ sarati bījena /
children.translated_text: Mercury that is further <s>anusārita</s> — flows with the seed;

children.text: pratisārito+anusārito daśakoṭiṃ vidhyate sūtaḥ // GRht_16.33 //
children.translated_text: [when] <s>pratisārita</s> and then <s>anusārita</s>, mercury transmutes ten million (<s>daśakoṭi</s>). (GRht 16.33)

children.text: tathottarasattvena guṇādhikyamāha koṭimityādi // GRhtCM_16.33:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the increased virtue through superior essence, with '<s>koṭi</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.33:1)

children.text:
sūte sarito bījena grāsanyāyaṃ vihāya samena bījenānusārito yaḥ sa
                            koṭisaṃkhyāṃ dhātūnāmiti śeṣaḥ sūto vidhyati // GRhtCM_16.33:2 //
children.translated_text: When mercury has been liquefied — setting aside the bolus-method — when <s>anusārita</s> with an equal seed, it transmutes a <s>koṭi</s>-number [of parts] — of metals, this is the completion. (GRhtCM 16.33:2)

children.text:
yathoktasārite sūte daśaguṇavṛddhiḥ sarvatraiveti veditavyam //
                            GRhtCM_16.33:3 //
children.translated_text: It should be understood that in mercury liquefied as described, there is always a tenfold increase throughout. (GRhtCM 16.33:3)

children.text: pratisāritastathābjaṃ tvanusāritaḥ kharvavedhī ca /
children.translated_text: The <s>pratisārita</s> likewise [transmutes] an <s>abja</s> (billion); and the <s>anusārita</s> becomes a <s>kharva</s>-fold (ten-billion) transmuter;

children.text: evaṃ sāraṇayogātkurute vedhaṃ yathepsitaṃ vidhinā // GRht_16.34 //
children.translated_text: thus, through the application of liquefaction, [mercury] effects transmutation as desired, by the [proper] method. (GRht 16.34)

children.text: viśeṣamāha pratītyādi // GRhtCM_16.34:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the distinction, with '<s>prati</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.34:1)

children.text:
pratisāritaḥ sūto dviguṇabījena vāraikena sārito rasaḥ abjasaṃkhyāṃ
                            vidhyati // GRhtCM_16.34:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Pratisārita</s> mercury — liquefied once with double the seed — transmutes an <s>abja</s>-number [of parts]. (GRhtCM 16.34:2)

children.text:
tu punar anusāritaḥ triguṇena bījena vāraikena sāritaḥ sūtaḥ kharvavedhī
                            syāt kharvasaṃkhyāke dravyasaṃbandhaṃ karotītyabhiprāyaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_16.34:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>anusārita</s> — liquefied once with triple the seed — mercury would be a <s>kharva</s>-fold transmuter; the meaning is that it makes contact with a <s>kharva</s>-numbered quantity of substance. (GRhtCM 16.34:3)

Thus, in the described manner, by the method — according to the tradition of those learned in the śāstra-commentaries — through the application of liquefaction, it effects transmutation as desired — as wished, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 16.34:4)

children.text: anusāritena sārito vidhyati śulbaṃ nikharvasaṃkhyākam /
children.translated_text: Liquefied with [a seed] equal to <s>anusārita</s>, [mercury] transmutes copper in the amount of a <s>nikharva</s> (hundred-billion);

children.text: pratisāritastu vidhyati padmaṃ svanusāritaḥ śaṅkham // GRht_16.35 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>pratisārita</s> transmutes a <s>padma</s> (trillion); and its <s>anusārita</s>, a <s>śaṅkha</s> (ten-trillion). (GRht 16.35)

children.text: punarviśeṣamāha anvityādi // GRhtCM_16.35:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states further distinctions, with 'follow-up' and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.35:1)

children.text:
anusāritena triguṇaprathamagrāsanyāyena bījena sāritaḥ sūto
                            nikharvasaṃkhyākaṃ śupbaṃ vidhyati tu punaḥ pratisāritaḥ
                            ṣaḍguṇaprathamagrāsanyāyena sāritaḥ sūtaḥ padmasaṃkhyākaṃ vidhyati //
                            GRhtCM_16.35:2 //
children.translated_text: Liquefied with <s>anusārita</s> — by the triple-first-bolus method with seed — mercury transmutes a <s>nikharva</s>-number [of parts] of copper; furthermore, <s>pratisārita</s> — liquefied by the six-fold-first-bolus method — mercury transmutes a <s>padma</s>-number. (GRhtCM 16.35:2)

children.text:
punar anusārito navaguṇagrāsanyāyena bījena sāritaḥ sūtaḥ śaṅkhasaṃkhyāṃ
                            vidhyatīti // GRhtCM_16.35:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>anusārita</s> — mercury liquefied by the nine-fold-bolus method with seed — transmutes a <s>śaṅkha</s>-number. (GRhtCM 16.35:3)

children.text: lead (?):: vedha (?)
children.translated_text: [Section on] lead (?): <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) (?)

children.text: vidhyed dviguṇaṃ dravyaṃ nāgaṃ dattvānuvāhayecchanakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: One should transmute double the quantity of substance; having added lead, one should gradually propel [it];

children.text: tāvadyāvatkanakaṃ divyaṃ pronmīlayetsakalam // GRht_16.36 //
children.translated_text: until all the gold is completely revealed as divine. (GRht 16.36)

children.text:
iti paramahaṃsaparivrājakācāryaśrīmadgovindabhagavatpādaviracite
                                rasahṛdayatantre sāraṇātmakaḥ ṣoḍaśo+avabodhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixteenth chapter, on the topic of <s>sāraṇā</s> (liquefaction), in the <s>Rasahṛdayatantra</s> composed by the revered <s>Govindabhagavatpāda</s>, the supreme ascetic and wandering teacher.

children.text: punarviśeṣamāha vidhyedityādi // GRhtCM_16.36:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states further distinctions, with 'should transmute' and so forth. (GRhtCM 16.36:1)

children.text:
kanakaṃ hema dattvā śanakair nīcais tāvadanuvāhayet yāvaddivyaṃ pravaraṃ
                            kanakaṃ bhavediti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_16.36:2 //
children.translated_text: Having added gold (<s>kanaka</s>/hema), one should gently — slowly — propel [it] until the gold becomes divine — excellent — this is the completion. (GRhtCM 16.36:2)

children.text:
punaryāvatsakapaṃ samastaṃ nāgaṃ pronmīpayenniḥśeṣaṃ kuryādityabhiprāyaḥ
                            // GRhtCM_16.36:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, until all the lead is completely made to vanish — is entirely removed — this is the intended meaning. (GRhtCM 16.36:3)

children.text:
punastatkanakaṃ dviguṇaṃ svato dravyaṃ vidhyet vā sūtakena sāritaṃ sat
                            dravyaṃ kanakaṃ śatasahasrādisaṃkhyāto dviguṇasaṃkhyākaṃ dravyaṃ
                            śupbādikaṃ vidhyed iti rahasyam // GRhtCM_16.36:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, that gold — double of itself in quantity of substance — should be transmuted; or, the substance — gold — [when] liquefied by mercury, [effects transmutation of] double the hundred-thousand and other numbers of copper and other substances — this is the secret. (GRhtCM 16.36:4)

children.text: iti kṛtasāraṇavidhirapi balavānapi sūtarāṭ kriyāyogāt /
children.translated_text: Thus, even though the king of mercury has had the liquefaction procedure performed and is powerful, due to the operation-connection,

children.text: saṃveṣṭya tiṣṭhati lohaṃ no viśati krāmaṇārahitaḥ // GRht_17.1 //
children.translated_text: [if it] wraps around the metal and does not enter — [it is because it is] devoid of <s>krāmaṇa</s> (transmutation-activation). (GRht 17.1)

children.text: susaṃskṛtā mukhāntaḥsthā viśadāśca hitārthakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Well-refined, situated within the mouth [of the metal], clear, and beneficial in purpose,

children.text: tathā parocitāḥ pūtā bhavantyamarajā giraḥ // GRhtCM_17.1:1 //
children.translated_text: likewise suitable for others, purified — such become the immortal-born words. (GRhtCM 17.1:1)

children.text: atha krāmaṇapraśaṃsām āha itītyādi // GRhtCM_17.1:2 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now he states the praise of <s>krāmaṇa</s>, with 'thus' and so forth. (GRhtCM 17.1:2)

children.text:
uktavidhānena kṛtaḥ sāraṇasya vidhir yasmin sūtarāje evaṃvidhiḥ sūtarāṭ
                            bapavān bhavediti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_17.1:3 //
children.translated_text: The king of mercury in whom the liquefaction procedure has been performed as described — such a mercury-king becomes powerful, is the completion. (GRhtCM 17.1:3)

children.text: kutaḥ kriyāyogāt kṛtyakaraṇāt // GRhtCM_17.1:4 //
children.translated_text: From what? From the operation-connection — from the performance of the work. (GRhtCM 17.1:4)

children.text:
yādṛk kṛtyaṃ kriyate tādṛk bapavān syād ityabhiprāyaḥ // GRhtCM_17.1:5
                            //
children.translated_text: Whatever work is performed — accordingly [the mercury] becomes powerful, is the intended meaning. (GRhtCM 17.1:5)

children.text:
evaṃvidho+api krāmaṇārahitaḥ krāmaṇavarjito pohaṃ na viśati
                            pohāntaḥpraveśaṃ na karoti tato hetor pohaṃ dhātuṃ saṃveṣṭya
                            pariveṣṭanaṃ kṛtvā tiṣṭhati bāhyarāgadāyī syāditi // GRhtCM_17.1:6
                            //
children.translated_text: Even such [mercury], devoid of <s>krāmaṇa</s> (permeation), lacking permeation, does not enter the metal — does not make entry into the interior of the metal; therefore, having enveloped the metal — having performed the wrapping — it remains [on the surface], becoming a giver of external color only. (GRhtCM 17.1:6)

children.text: annaṃ vā dravyaṃ vā yathānupānena dhātuṣu kramate /
children.translated_text: Just as food or a substance, with an <s>anupāna</s> (vehicle), permeates the bodily tissues (<s>dhātus</s>),

children.text: evaṃ krāmaṇayogādrasarājo viśati loheṣu // GRht_17.2 //
children.translated_text: so, by the conjunction of <s>krāmaṇa</s> (permeation), the king of mercury enters into metals. (GRht 17.2)

children.text: dehapohayoḥ sādṛśyamāha annamityādi // GRhtCM_17.2:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the analogy between the body and the metal, beginning with 'food' and so on. (GRhtCM 17.2:1)

children.text: yatheti sādṛśye // GRhtCM_17.2:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Just as' [is used] in the sense of analogy. (GRhtCM 17.2:2)

children.text:
annaṃ godhūmādikaṃ vā dravyaṃ auṣadhaṃ anupānena saha japādinā sārdhaṃ
                            dhātuṣu māṃsādiṣu saptasu kramate vyāpnoti tathā amunā
                            vakṣyamāṇavidhānena krāmaṇayogāt krāmaṇāya yogaḥ kunaṭīmākṣikaviṣādis
                            tataḥ sūtarājo poharūpyādiṣu viśati bāhyābhyantaraṃ vidhyatītyarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_17.2:3 //
children.translated_text: Food — wheat and the like — or a substance, i.e., a medicine, with an <s>anupāna</s> (vehicle) — together with water and such — permeates — pervades — the seven bodily tissues (<s>dhātus</s>) such as flesh and the like; similarly, by this procedure to be described, by the conjunction of <s>krāmaṇa</s> — the yoga for <s>krāmaṇa</s> (permeation), consisting of <s>kunaṭī</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, poison, and the like — the king of mercury enters into metals such as iron, silver, and the like — it pervades [them] both externally and internally; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 17.2:3)

children.text: krāmaṇayoga (1)
children.translated_text: <s>Krāmaṇa</s>-conjunction (1)

children.text: kāntaviṣarasakadaradai raktailendragopikādyaiśca /
children.translated_text: With lodestone (<s>kānta</s>), poison (<s>viṣa</s>), <s>rasaka</s> (calamine), cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), red oils, <s>indragopa</s> (cochineal insect), and the like —

children.text: krāmaṇametacchreṣṭhaṃ lepe kṣepe sadā yojyam // GRht_17.3 //
children.translated_text: this <s>krāmaṇa</s> (permeation) is the best; it should always be employed in coating (<s>lepa</s>) and projection (<s>kṣepa</s>). (GRht 17.3)

children.text: krāmaṇayoga (2)
children.translated_text: <s>Krāmaṇa</s>-conjunction (2)

children.text: kunaṭīmākṣikaviṣaṃ nararudhiraṃ vāyasasya viṣṭhā ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Kunaṭī</s> (a plant), <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), poison, human blood, crow's excrement,

children.text: mahiṣīṇāṃ karṇamalaṃ strīkṣīraṃ krāmaṇe balakṛt // GRht_17.4 //
children.translated_text: ear-wax of she-buffaloes, woman's milk — [these are] strength-givers in <s>krāmaṇa</s>. (GRht 17.4)

children.text: krāmaṇayoga (3)
children.translated_text: <s>Krāmaṇa</s>-conjunction (3)

children.text: ṭaṅkaṇakunaṭīrāmaṭhabhūmilatāsaṃyutaṃ mahārudhiram /
children.translated_text: Borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), <s>kunaṭī</s>, <s>rāmaṭha</s> (a plant), and <s>bhūmilatā</s> (a creeper), combined with great blood (<s>mahārudhira</s>) —

children.text: krāmaṇametatkathitaṃ lepe kṣepe sadā yojyam // GRht_17.5 //
children.translated_text: this <s>krāmaṇa</s> is declared; it should always be employed in coating and projection. (GRht 17.5)

children.text: krāmaṇayogamāha kāntaviṣetyādi // GRhtCM_17.3-5:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the <s>krāmaṇa</s>-conjunction, beginning with 'lodestone, poison' and so on. (GRhtCM 17.3–5:1)

children.text:
kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ viṣaṃ kandajaṃ viṣaṃ kandaviṣāṇi kāpakūṭādīni trayodaśa
                            daradaṃ hiṅgupaṃ taiḥ ca punaḥ raktataipendragopādyaiḥ rakto
                            raktakavargaḥ taipaṃ kaṅguṇyādeḥ indragopo jīvaviśeṣaḥ ityādyāḥ
                            krāmaṇocitās tacca // GRhtCM_17.3-5:2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Kānta</s>' is lodestone; '<s>viṣa</s>' means tuberous poisons — the thirteen tuberous poisons such as <s>kālakūṭa</s> and the like; '<s>darada</s>' is <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar); with these, and further with red oils, <s>indragopa</s>, and the like — the 'red' group being the [previously described] red class, the oils being [those] of <s>kaṅguṇī</s> and the like, <s>indragopa</s> being a specific insect — such and similar [substances] suitable for <s>krāmaṇa</s>; and that — (GRhtCM 17.3–5:2)

children.text:
etat śreṣṭhaṃ sarvottamaṃ krāmaṇaṃ anena sūtaḥ krāmati viśati poheṣviti
                            vyāptiḥ tatkrāmaṇaṃ kathitam // GRhtCM_17.3-5:3 //
children.translated_text: this is the best — the most excellent — <s>krāmaṇa</s>; by this, mercury permeates — enters — into metals; that is the pervasion. That <s>krāmaṇa</s> has been stated. (GRhtCM 17.3–5:3)

children.text: tappepe kṣepe ca yojyamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_17.3-5:4 //
children.translated_text: It should be employed in coating (<s>lepa</s>) and projection (<s>kṣepa</s>); that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 17.3–5:4)

children.text: krāmaṇayoga (4): für Gold-/Silberherstellung
children.translated_text: <s>Krāmaṇa</s>-conjunction (4): for gold and silver production

children.text: śilayā nihato nāgo vaṅgaṃ vā tālakena śuddhena /
children.translated_text: Lead (<s>nāga</s>) killed with realgar (<s>śilā</s>), or tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) [killed] with pure orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>) —

children.text: kramaśaḥ pīte śukle krāmaṇametatsamuddiṣṭam // GRht_17.6 //
children.translated_text: respectively in yellow [i.e., gold-making] and white [i.e., silver-making] [operations], this <s>krāmaṇa</s> is prescribed. (GRht 17.6)

children.text: anyaccāha śipayetyādi // GRhtCM_17.6:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another [method], beginning with 'realgar' and so on. (GRhtCM 17.6:1)

children.text:
nāgaḥ sīsakaḥ śipayā manohvayā nihato māritaḥ punaḥ vaṅgaṃ śuddhena
                            doṣavarjitena tāpena nihataṃ kramaśaḥ krameṇa pīte hemakarmaṇi śukpe
                            rūpyakarmaṇi etatkrāmaṇaṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ samyak prakāśitaṃ pītakarmaṇi
                            nāgaḥ śukpakarmaṇi vaṅgaṃ ca niyojitavyam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_17.6:2
                            //
children.translated_text: '<s>Nāga</s>' is lead; killed — destroyed — with realgar (<s>manohvā</s>); furthermore, tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) [killed] with pure — defect-free — orpiment (<s>tāla</s>); respectively — in order: in yellow [operations], i.e., gold-making, and in white [operations], i.e., silver-making, this <s>krāmaṇa</s> is prescribed — well-proclaimed. Lead should be employed in yellow [gold] operations, and tin in white [silver] operations; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 17.6:2)

children.text: krāmaṇa
children.translated_text: <s>Krāmaṇa</s> (permeation)

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ daradena hataṃ śulbaṃ vā tāpyamāritaṃ vidhinā /
children.translated_text: Steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) killed with cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), or copper (<s>śulba</s>), or pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>) killed by the [proper] method —

children.text: krāmaṇametatkathitaṃ kāntamukhaṃ mākṣikairvāpi // GRht_17.7 //
children.translated_text: this <s>krāmaṇa</s> is declared; with lodestone as the primary [agent], or with <s>mākṣika</s>-[essences]. (GRht 17.7)

children.text: anyaccāha tīkṣṇamityādi // GRhtCM_17.7:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another [method], beginning with 'steel' and so on. (GRhtCM 17.7:1)

children.text:
daradena hiṅgupena hataṃ māritaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ sāro vidhinā arivargavidhānena
                            tāpyena svarṇamākṣikena māritaṃ śupbaṃ tāmraṃ etadapi krāmaṇaṃ kathitaṃ
                            vā kāntamukhaṃ kāntaṃ pohajāti uktaṃ granthādau tat mukhaṃ pradhānaṃ
                            yasya tat mākṣikairvā māritaṃ niyojyaṃ iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_17.7:2 //
children.translated_text: Killed — destroyed — with cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>), steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), i.e., the essence [of iron]; by the [proper] method — by the enemy-group procedure — copper (<s>śulba</s>), i.e., copper (<s>tāmra</s>), killed with <s>tāpya</s> (gold-pyrite, <s>svarṇamākṣika</s>); this too is declared as <s>krāmaṇa</s>. Or, with lodestone as the primary [agent] — <s>kānta</s> is the iron-type stated at the beginning of the treatise, that being primary — or with <s>mākṣika</s>-[essences] killed; it should be employed; this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 17.7:2)

children.text: mākṣikasattvaṃ nāgaṃ vihāya na krāmaṇaṃ kimapyasti /
children.translated_text: Except for <s>mākṣika</s>-essence and lead (<s>nāga</s>), there is no <s>krāmaṇa</s> whatsoever;

children.text: dalasiddhe rasasiddhe vidhāvasau bhavati khalu saphalaḥ // GRht_17.8 //
children.translated_text: in the leaf-procedure and the mercury-procedure, this method becomes truly fruitful. (GRht 17.8)

children.text: viśeṣavidhānamāha mākṣikasattvam ityādi // GRhtCM_17.8:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the special procedure, beginning with '<s>mākṣika</s>-essence' and so on. (GRhtCM 17.8:1)

children.text:
mākṣikasattvaṃ tāpyasāraṃ nāgaḥ sīsakaḥ taṃ vihāya nānyatkimapyasti
                            krāmaṇaṃ na krāmaṇamiti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_17.8:2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Mākṣika</s>-essence' means pyrite-essence (<s>tāpyasāra</s>); '<s>nāga</s>' is lead — except for that, there is no other <s>krāmaṇa</s> whatsoever — it is not [true] <s>krāmaṇa</s>; that is the purport. (GRhtCM 17.8:2)

children.text: khapviti jijñāsāyām // GRhtCM_17.8:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Indeed' [is used] in the sense of inquiry. (GRhtCM 17.8:3)

children.text:
dapasiddhe vidhau saṃskāraiḥ pūrṇatāṃ nīte sati asau vidhiḥ saphapaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_17.8:4 //
children.translated_text: In the leaf-procedure, when [the process] has been brought to completion through the [various] preparatory operations, this method becomes fruitful. (GRhtCM 17.8:4)

children.text: vedhamahattva
children.translated_text: The greatness of transmutation (<s>vedha</s>)

children.text: anayā khalu sāraṇayā krāmaṇena ca viśati yojito vidhivat /
children.translated_text: By this very <s>sāraṇā</s> (extraction) and <s>krāmaṇa</s> (permeation), [mercury], when combined properly according to method,

children.text: asati vedhavidhau na rasaḥ svaguṇānprakāśayati // GRht_18.1 //
children.translated_text: enters; in the absence of the <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) procedure, mercury does not manifest its own qualities. (GRht 18.1)

children.text: vyavāyibheṣajopete dravye kṣipto rasaḥ khapu /
children.translated_text: When mercury, combined with <s>vyavāyin</s> (pervasive) medicinal [substances], is projected into a substance —

children.text: vedha ityucyate tajjñaiḥ sa ca naikavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: that is called <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) by the knowers; and it is declared to be of more than one kind.

children.text: iti paribhāṣā // GRhtCM_18.1:1 //
children.translated_text: Thus [is] the technical definition. (GRhtCM 18.1:1)

children.text: krāmaṇasaṃskārādhikāramāha anayetyādi // GRhtCM_18.1:2 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the topic of <s>krāmaṇa</s>-preparation, beginning with 'by this' and so on. (GRhtCM 18.1:2)

children.text:
anayā uktayā sāraṇayā saha krāmaṇasaṃskāre kṛte sati raso viśati krāmati
                            punarvedhavidhau kṛte sati rasaḥ svaguṇān prakāśayatīti veditavyam //
                            GRhtCM_18.1:3 //
children.translated_text: By this — by the stated — <s>sāraṇā</s> (extraction), together with the <s>krāmaṇa</s>-preparation having been performed, mercury enters — permeates; furthermore, when the <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) procedure is performed, mercury manifests its own qualities — this should be understood. (GRhtCM 18.1:3)

children.text: hemakṛṣṭi
children.translated_text: Gold-production (<s>hemakṛṣṭi</s>)

children.text: rasadaradatāpyagandhakamanaḥśilārājavarttakaṃ vimalam /
children.translated_text: Mercury (<s>rasa</s>), cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), pyrite (<s>tāpya</s>), sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>), and <s>rājavartaka</s> (lapis lazuli), [with] pure [silver-pyrite (<s>raupyamākṣika</s>)] —

children.text: puṭamṛtaśulbaṃ tāre nirvyūḍhaṃ hemakṛṣṭiriyam // GRht_18.2 //
children.translated_text: copper killed by fire-calcination (<s>puṭa</s>), [projected] into silver (<s>tāra</s>), thoroughly processed — this is gold-production (<s>hemakṛṣṭi</s>). (GRht 18.2)

children.text: vedhavidhānamāha rasetyādi // GRhtCM_18.2:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the transmutation procedure, beginning with 'mercury' and so on. (GRhtCM 18.2:1)

children.text:
rasaḥ sūtaḥ daradaṃ hiṅgupaṃ tāpyaṃ mākṣikaṃ gandhakaḥ pratītaḥ manaḥśipā
                            manohvā rājavarttakaṃ rājāvartaṃ vimapaṃ raupyamākṣikaṃ
                            ekavadbhāvadvandvaḥ // GRhtCM_18.2:2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Rasa</s>' is mercury; '<s>darada</s>' is cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>); '<s>tāpya</s>' is <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite); '<s>gandhaka</s>' is well-known; '<s>manaḥśilā</s>' is realgar (<s>manohvā</s>); '<s>rājavartaka</s>' is <s>rājāvarta</s> (lapis lazuli); '<s>vimala</s>' is silver-pyrite (<s>raupyamākṣika</s>) — [this is] a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative) compound treated as a unity. (GRhtCM 18.2:2)

children.text: puṭamṛtaśupbaṃ rasādīnāṃ puṭena mṛtamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.2:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Copper killed by fire-calcination' — killed by fire-cake of the [aforementioned] mercury and other [substances]; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 18.2:3)

children.text:
evaṃvidhaṃ śupbaṃ tāre nirvāhitaṃ iyaṃ hemakṛṣṭiḥ svarṇakaraṇamityarthaḥ
                            // GRhtCM_18.2:4 //
children.translated_text: Such copper, thoroughly processed in silver (<s>tāra</s>) — this is gold-production (<s>hemakṛṣṭi</s>), meaning the making of gold; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 18.2:4)

children.text: śatāṃśavidhi/-vedha (1)
children.translated_text: Hundredth-part method/transmutation (1)

children.text: aṣṭānavatirbhāgāstārastveko+api kanakabhāgaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: Ninety-eight parts of silver (<s>tāra</s>), one part of gold, and
