children.text: sūtasyaiko bhāgaḥ śatāṃśavidhireṣa vikhyātaḥ // GRht_18.3 //
children.translated_text: one part of mercury — this is the well-known hundredth-part method (<s>śatāṃśavidhi</s>). (GRht 18.3)

children.text: vedhavidhānamāha aṣṭānavatir ityādi // GRhtCM_18.3:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the transmutation procedure, beginning with 'ninety-eight' and so on. (GRhtCM 18.3:1)

children.text:
eṣa rasadaradetyādiśatāṃśavedhavidhiḥ kathaṃ atra śatāṃśe
                            aṣṭānavatirbhāgāstārasya rūpyasya punariha kanakabhāgaḥ syāt eka eveti
                            punaḥ sūtasya daradādimipitarasasyaiko bhāgaḥ ekāṃśaḥ iti sarve śatāṃśāḥ
                            śatāṃśena vedha iti // GRhtCM_18.3:2 //
children.translated_text: This hundredth-part transmutation method [described] in 'mercury, cinnabar' and so forth — how? Here, in the hundredth-part: ninety-eight parts of silver (<s>tāra</s>), i.e., of silver (<s>rūpya</s>); furthermore, one part of gold should be [added]; furthermore, one part of mercury — of mercury mixed with cinnabar and the like; thus all [total] one hundred parts; transmutation by one hundredth part. (GRhtCM 18.3:2)

children.text: śatāṃśavidhi (2)
children.translated_text: Hundredth-part method (2)

children.text: ekonapañcāśadbhāgāstārasyeha tathaiva śulvasya /
children.translated_text: Forty-nine parts of silver and likewise of copper,

children.text: kanakasyaiko bhāgo vedhaścaikena sūtasya // GRht_18.4 //
children.translated_text: one part of gold, and transmutation with one [part] of mercury. (GRht 18.4)

children.text: anyaccāha ekonapañcāśadityādi // GRhtCM_18.4:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another [method], beginning with 'forty-nine' and so on. (GRhtCM 18.4:1)

children.text:
ekonapañcāśadbhāgāḥ tārasya rūpyasya kāryāḥ tathaiva śupvasya tāmrasya
                            ekonapañcāśadbhāgāśca kāryāḥ punaḥ kanakasya hemnaśca eko bhāgaḥ kāryaḥ
                            sūtasya ca ekena bhāgena vedha iti eṣo+api śatāṃśavidhiḥ //
                            GRhtCM_18.4:2 //
children.translated_text: Forty-nine parts of silver (<s>tāra</s>), i.e., silver (<s>rūpya</s>), should be prepared; likewise of copper — forty-nine parts of copper (<s>tāmra</s>) should be prepared; furthermore, one part of gold should be prepared; and by one part of mercury, transmutation [occurs]; this too is the hundredth-part method. (GRhtCM 18.4:2)

children.text: Definition sahasravedhin und hṆher
children.translated_text: Definition of thousand-fold transmuter and higher

children.text: evaṃ sahasravedhī niyujyate koṭivedhī ca /
children.translated_text: Thus, a thousand-fold transmuter (<s>sahasravedhin</s>) is employed, and a <s>koṭi</s>-fold (ten-million-fold) transmuter as well;

children.text: jāraṇabījavaśena tu sūtasya balābalaṃ jñātvā // GRht_18.5 //
children.translated_text: according to the capacity of the <s>jāraṇa</s>-seed, knowing the strength and weakness of mercury. (GRht 18.5)

children.text: pūrvoktavidher viśeṣamāha evamityādi // GRhtCM_18.5:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the distinction from the previously stated method, beginning with 'thus' and so on. (GRhtCM 18.5:1)

children.text:
evaṃ śatāṃśavedhanyāyena daśavṛddhivibhāgena sahasravedhī syāt //
                            GRhtCM_18.5:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus, by the principle of hundredth-part transmutation, by the division of tenfold increase, one would become a thousand-fold transmuter. (GRhtCM 18.5:2)

children.text:
evaṃ ca jāraṇabījavaśena jāraṇāyāṃ yadbījaṃ kiyadguṇajāritamiti bhāvaḥ
                            tadvaśena koṭivedhī ca syāt // GRhtCM_18.5:3 //
children.translated_text: And thus, according to the capacity of the <s>jāraṇa</s>-seed — the seed in digestion, the purport being how many times it has been digested — according to that capacity, one would become a <s>koṭi</s>-fold transmuter as well. (GRhtCM 18.5:3)

children.text:
kiṃ kṛtvā tenaiva jāraṇabījavaśena yattasya bapābapaṃ nyūnādhikyaṃ tat
                            jñātvetyabhiprāyaḥ // GRhtCM_18.5:4 //
children.translated_text: Having done what? By that very capacity of the <s>jāraṇa</s>-seed, knowing its strength and weakness — its deficiency and excess — that is the purport. (GRhtCM 18.5:4)

children.text: kuntavedha
children.translated_text: Spear-transmutation (<s>kuntavedha</s>)

children.text: dattvādau prativāpaṃ lākṣāmatsyādipittabhāvanayā /
children.translated_text: Having first given a counter-sprinkling (<s>prativāpa</s>), with steeping in lac, fish-bile, and the like —

children.text: tāre vā śulbe vā tārāriṣṭe tathā kṛṣṭau // GRht_18.6 //
children.translated_text: in silver or in copper, or in silver-<s>ariṣṭa</s> (a preparation), and likewise in gold-production. (GRht 18.6)

children.text: viśeṣeṇa vedhavidhānamāha dattvetyādi // GRhtCM_18.6:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the transmutation procedure in particular, beginning with 'having given' and so on. (GRhtCM 18.6:1)

children.text:
ādau prathamaṃ pākṣāmatsyādipittabhāvanayā pākṣā pratītā matsyādipittāni
                            matsyamāhiṣamayūrājasūkarasaṃbhavāni pittāni teṣāṃ bhāvanayā kṛtvā
                            prativāpaṃ gapite nikṣepaṃ tattāre dattvā athavā śupbe prativāpaṃ kuryāt
                            athavā kṛṣṭau hemakaraṇe vāpaṃ dattvā niyuñjyāditi śeṣaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_18.6:2 //
children.translated_text: First — at the beginning — by steeping in lac and fish-bile and the like: lac is well-known; the biles of fish, buffalo, peacock, goat, and boar — bile originating from these; by steeping with these, having made a counter-sprinkling (<s>prativāpa</s>) — a projection — into the liquefied [metal], one should give that into silver, or one should make a counter-sprinkling into copper, or in gold-production give the sprinkling and employ it; this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 18.6:2)

children.text: tadanu krāmaṇamṛdite tatkalkenāpi piṇḍitarasena /
children.translated_text: Then, softened by <s>krāmaṇa</s> [agents], with mercury consolidated even with that [same] powder (<s>kalka</s>) —

children.text: atividrute ca tasmin vedho+asau kuntavedhena // GRht_18.7 //
children.translated_text: and in that [metal] when fully liquefied, the transmutation is by the spear-method (<s>kuntavedha</s>). (GRht 18.7)

children.text: viśeṣāccāha tadanvityādi // GRhtCM_18.7:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the particular [method], beginning with 'then' and so on. (GRhtCM 18.7:1)

children.text:
tadanu pākṣāmatsyādipittabhāvanāyā anantaraṃ tasmin pākṣādikapke
                            krāmaṇamṛdite kāntarasakadaradaraktataipendragopādyair mṛdite sati
                            punastatkapkena taccūrṇenāpi piṇḍitarasena vedhaḥ kartavya iti śeṣaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_18.7:2 //
children.translated_text: Then — after the lac-fish-bile steeping, subsequently — in that lac-powder (<s>kalka</s>), softened by <s>krāmaṇa</s> — softened with lodestone, <s>rasaka</s>, cinnabar, red oils, <s>indragopa</s>, and the like — then with that powder, with that very powder, mercury having been consolidated — transmutation should be performed; this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 18.7:2)

children.text:
kasmin tāre vā śupbe vā vidrute japarūpe kārya ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.7:3
                            //
children.translated_text: In what? In silver or in copper, when fully liquefied — in water-like form; it should be done; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 18.7:3)

children.text: krāmaṇa (?)
children.translated_text: <s>Krāmaṇa</s> (permeation)

children.text: tattailārdrapaṭena sthagayet palalena bhasmanā vāpi /
children.translated_text: One should cover that [substance] with an oil-moistened cloth, or with flesh, or with ash;

children.text: vidhivadvedhyaṃ dravyaṃ rasarājakrāmaṇārthaṃ hi // GRht_18.8 //
children.translated_text: [this is] the substance suitable for transmutation, for the purpose of making the king of mercury permeate. (GRht 18.8)

children.text: viśeṣamāha tadityādi // GRhtCM_18.8:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the particular [method], beginning with 'that' and so on. (GRhtCM 18.8:1)

children.text:
vedhyaṃ vedhocitaṃ dravyaṃ rasarājakrāmaṇārthaṃ yathā raso viśati
                            tadarthaṃ taṃ taipārdrapaṭena sāraṇataipārdravastreṇa sthagayet
                            ācchādayet vā papapena kenacinmāṃsena vā bhasmanā ācchādayedityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_18.8:2 //
children.translated_text: The substance suitable for transmutation — suitable for piercing — for the purpose of <s>krāmaṇa</s> of the king of mercury — so that mercury enters — should be covered with an oil-moistened cloth — with a cloth moistened with <s>sāraṇa</s>-oil — or covered with some flesh, or covered with ash; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 18.8:2)

children.text: iti sāritasya kathitaṃ rasasya vedhādi krāmaṇaṃ karma / GRht_18.9ab
children.translated_text: Thus, the <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) and other <s>krāmaṇa</s> (permeation) operations of extracted mercury have been stated. (GRht 18.9ab)

children.text: viśeṣamāha itītyādi // GRhtCM_18.9ab:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the particular [method], beginning with 'thus' and so on. (GRhtCM 18.9ab:1)

children.text:
sāritasya uktavidhānena sāraṇākṛtasya vedhādi krāmaṇaṃ karma
                                vedhavidhānoditakrāmaṇaṃ karma kathitam // GRhtCM_18.9ab:2 //
children.translated_text: Of extracted [mercury] — of mercury that has undergone extraction (<s>sāraṇā</s>) by the stated procedure — the <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) and <s>krāmaṇa</s> (permeation) operations stated in the transmutation-procedure have been declared. (GRhtCM 18.9ab:2)

children.text: lepavedha/pattrarañjana
children.translated_text: Coating-transmutation (<s>lepavedha</s>) / leaf-coloring (<s>pattrarañjana</s>)

children.text: pādādijīrṇabījo yujyate patralepena // GRht_18.9cd //
children.translated_text: [mercury] whose seed has been digested starting from one-quarter [upward] is suitable for leaf-coating (<s>patralepa</s>). (GRht 18.9cd)

children.text:
pādādijīrṇabījaḥ pādādinā pādārdhena samato nyūnena ca jīrṇaṃ bījaṃ
                            yasmin saḥ patrapepena yujyate ataḥ patrarañjanaṃ syādityabhiprāyaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_18.9cd:1 //
children.translated_text: 'Whose seed has been digested starting from one-quarter' — in which [mercury] the seed has been digested starting from one-quarter, one-eighth, equal, or less [quantities] — [such mercury] is suitable for leaf-coating; therefore, leaf-coloring would result — this is the intent. (GRhtCM 18.9cd:1)

children.text: pattrarañjana (2) durch lepa
children.translated_text: Leaf-coloring (2): through coating (<s>lepa</s>)

children.text: amlādyudvartitatārāriṣṭādipatram atiśuddham /
children.translated_text: A leaf of <s>tārāriṣṭa</s> (silver or gold), rubbed with acids and the like, thoroughly purified,

children.text: ālipya rasena tataḥ krāmaṇalipte puṭeṣu viśrāntam // GRht_18.10 //
children.translated_text: having coated with mercury, then [placed] in a sweeping-coated (<s>krāmaṇa-lipta</s>) [wrap], rested in fire-calcinations (<s>puṭas</s>). (GRht 18.10)

children.text:
atiśuddhaṃ nirmapaṃ ampādyudvartitaṃ tārāriṣṭaśabdātsitaṃ svarṇaṃ grāhyaṃ
                            tataḥ rasenāpipya tataḥ kramaṇāpipte krāmaṇapiṇḍena pepe kṛte sati
                            puṭeṣu utpapāgnau viśrāntaṃ sthāpitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_18.10:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Thoroughly purified' means spotless; 'rubbed with acids and the like' — by the word <s>tārāriṣṭa</s>, white [silver] or gold should be taken; then, having coated with mercury; then 'sweeping-coated' — coated with the sweeping-bolus (<s>krāmaṇa-piṇḍa</s>); when [so] coated, 'rested in fire-calcinations' — one should place [it] in <s>upalā</s>-fire (cow-dung-cake fire). (GRhtCM 18.10:1)

children.text: patrarañjanavidhir ayam // GRhtCM_18.10:2 //
children.translated_text: This is the procedure for leaf-coloring. (GRhtCM 18.10:2)

children.text: Weiterverarbeitung des pattras; varṇapuṭa
children.translated_text: Further processing of the leaf; color-calcination (<s>varṇapuṭa</s>)

children.text: ardhena miśrayitvā hemnā jyeṣṭhena taddalaṃ puṭitam /
children.translated_text: Having mixed that leaf with half [its weight of] the best gold, and calcined,

children.text: kṣitikhagapaṭuraktamṛdā varṇapuṭo+ayaṃ tato deyaḥ // GRht_18.11 //
children.translated_text: with earth-powder (<s>kṣiti</s>), <s>khaga</s> (yellow vitriol), salt (<s>paṭu</s>), and red earth (<s>raktamṛd</s>) — this color-calcination (<s>varṇapuṭa</s>) should then be given. (GRht 18.11)

children.text: atha svarṇavidhānamāha ardhenetyādi // GRhtCM_18.11:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now he states the gold procedure, with 'half' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.11:1)

children.text:
ardhena ardhavibhāgena rañjitadapādita iti jñeyam // GRhtCM_18.11:2
                            //
children.translated_text: 'With half' — with half the portion; the colored leaf is to be understood. (GRhtCM 18.11:2)

children.text:
jyeṣṭhena hemnā pravarakanakena taddapaṃ rañjitapatraṃ miśrayitvā puṭitaṃ
                            kuryāt yathā mipati // GRhtCM_18.11:3 //
children.translated_text: With the best gold — the finest gold — having mixed that leaf — the colored leaf — one should calcine it so that it merges. (GRhtCM 18.11:3)

children.text:
punaḥ kṣitikhagapaṭuraktamṛdā kṛtvā kṣitiḥ sphaṭikaḥ khagaḥ pītakāsīsaṃ
                            paṭu saindhavaṃ pavaṇaṃ raktamṛt gairikaṃ ekavadbhāvadvandvaḥ tena
                            kṣityādinopari piptaṃ dapaṃ prati ayaṃ puṭo deyaḥ vanopapair iti śeṣaḥ
                            // GRhtCM_18.11:4 //
children.translated_text: Again, with earth-powder (<s>kṣiti</s>), <s>khaga</s>, salt (<s>paṭu</s>), and red earth (<s>raktamṛd</s>), having prepared [a paste]: <s>kṣiti</s> is crystal (<s>sphaṭika</s>); <s>khaga</s> is yellow vitriol (<s>pītakāsīsa</s>); <s>paṭu</s> is rock-salt (<s>saindhava lavaṇa</s>); red earth is ochre (<s>gairika</s>) — a copulative compound treating them as one group — with this, beginning with <s>kṣiti</s>, smeared over the leaf above, this calcination should be given; 'with cow-dung cakes,' is the completion. (GRhtCM 18.11:4)

children.text: vedha:: white gold => red gold
children.translated_text: Transmutation (<s>vedha</s>): white gold to red gold

children.text: bhūpativartakacūrṇaṃ śirīṣapuṣparasabhāvitaṃ bahuśaḥ /
children.translated_text: The powder of <s>bhūpativartaka</s> (lapis lazuli, <s>rājāvarta</s>), steeped many times in <s>śirīṣa</s>-flower juice,

children.text: sadyaḥ karoti raktaṃ sitakanakam aśītibhāgena // GRht_18.12 //
children.translated_text: instantly makes white gold red, at one-eightieth part. (GRht 18.12)

children.text: varṇavidhānamāha bhūpatītyādi // GRhtCM_18.12:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the color procedure, with '<s>bhūpati</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.12:1)

children.text:
bhūpativartakacūrṇaṃ rājāvartarajaḥ bahuśo bahuvāraṃ
                            śirīṣapuṣparasabhāvitaṃ kuryāt ityadhyāhāryam // GRhtCM_18.12:2 //
children.translated_text: The powder of <s>bhūpativartaka</s> — the dust of <s>rājāvarta</s> (lapis lazuli) — should be steeped many times, i.e., many rounds, in <s>śirīṣa</s>-flower juice; this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 18.12:2)

children.text: bhāvitaṃ gharmapuṭitamiti vidhānavit iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_18.12:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Steeped' means sun-calcined (<s>gharmapuṭita</s>) — the one who knows the procedure [understands this]; this is the completion. (GRhtCM 18.12:3)

children.text: vedha:: silver => gold
children.translated_text: Transmutation (<s>vedha</s>): silver to gold

children.text: rasadaradavimalatāpyaṃ paṭuśilāmākṣīkanṛpāścaiva /
children.translated_text: Mercury (<s>rasa</s>), cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), <s>vimala</s> (copper-pyrite), <s>tāpya</s> (gold-pyrite), salt (<s>paṭu</s>), realgar (<s>śilā</s>), <s>mākṣīka</s> (pyrite), and <s>nṛpa</s> (lapis lazuli), and also

children.text:
pravālakaṃkuṣṭhaṭaṅkaṇagairikaprativāpitaṃ sitaṃ kanakam //
                                GRht_18.13 //
children.translated_text: coral (<s>pravāla</s>), <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> (a mineral), borax (<s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>), and ochre (<s>gairika</s>) — [silver] treated with these becomes gold. (GRht 18.13)

children.text: anyaccāha rasetyādi /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another [method], with '<s>rasa</s>' and so forth.

children.text:
rasaḥ sūtaḥ daradaṃ hiṅgupaḥ vimapaṃ tāpyabhedaḥ paṭu saiṃdhavaṃ śipā
                            manohvā mākṣikaṃ pratītaṃ vaṇigdravyaṃ nṛpo rājāvartaḥ pravāpaṃ vidrumaṃ
                            kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ viraṅgaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ gairikaṃ pratītaṃ etaiḥ
                            prativāpitaṃ sitadravyaṃ kanakaṃ bhavet ityadhyāhāryam // GRhtCM_18.13:1
                            //
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> is mercury (<s>sūta</s>); <s>darada</s> is cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>); <s>vimala</s> is a variety of <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite); <s>paṭu</s> is rock-salt (<s>saindhava</s>); <s>śilā</s> is realgar (<s>manohvā</s>); <s>mākṣika</s> is the well-known commercial substance; <s>nṛpa</s> is <s>rājāvarta</s> (lapis lazuli); <s>pravāla</s> is coral (<s>vidruma</s>); <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is <s>viraṅga</s> (a mineral); <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is borax (<s>saubhāgya</s>); <s>gairika</s> is well-known — [silver] treated with these [becomes] a white substance [that is then] gold; this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 18.13:1)

children.text: colouring of gold
children.translated_text: Coloring of gold

children.text: tāpībhavanṛpāvartabījapūrarasārditam /
children.translated_text: With <s>tāpībhava</s> (<s>mākṣika</s>-essence) and <s>nṛpāvarta</s> (<s>rājāvarta</s>, lapis lazuli), ground with citron (<s>bījapūra</s>) juice,

children.text: karoti puṭapākena hema sindūrasannibham // GRht_18.14 //
children.translated_text: [the mixture] makes gold resemble vermilion (<s>sindūra</s>) through fire-calcination (<s>puṭapāka</s>). (GRht 18.14)

children.text: anyaccāha tāpībhavetyādi // GRhtCM_18.14:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another [method], with '<s>tāpībhava</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.14:1)

children.text:
tāpībhavaṃ mākṣikasattvaṃ nṛpāvartaṃ rājāvartakaṃ etaddvayaṃ
                            bījapūrarasārditaṃ mātupuṅgarasamarditaṃ kuryāt etadubhayoryogāt kanakaṃ
                            puṭapākena vahnividhānena kanakaṃ pūrvoktaṃ yatkanakaṃ vā
                            hīnavarṇakanakaṃ sindūrasannibhaṃ karoti // GRhtCM_18.14:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Tāpībhava</s> is <s>mākṣika</s>-essence (pyrite-essence); <s>nṛpāvarta</s> is <s>rājāvartaka</s> (lapis lazuli) — these two, ground with citron (<s>bījapūra</s>, i.e., <s>mātuluṅga</s>) juice — should be prepared; through the combination of both, by fire-calcination (<s>puṭapāka</s>), meaning by the fire-procedure, the aforementioned gold, or any inferior-colored gold, is made vermilion-like (<s>sindūra-sannibha</s>). (GRhtCM 18.14:2)

children.text: sindūravannibhā yasyeti samāsaḥ // GRhtCM_18.14:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Whose luster is like vermilion' — this is the compound [analysis]. (GRhtCM 18.14:3)

children.text: silver:: improvement of colour
children.translated_text: Silver: improvement of color

children.text: vaṅgābhraṃ sitamākṣīkaṃ śailaṃ vā vāhayetsite /
children.translated_text: One should digest tin-mica (<s>vaṅgābhra</s>), white <s>mākṣīka</s> (pyrite), or mineral pitch (<s>śaila</s>) into silver;

children.text: tattāraṃ ca daśāṃśena tārotkarṣaṃ karoti hi // GRht_18.15 //
children.translated_text: that silver, at one-tenth [proportion], produces enhancement of silver (<s>tārotkarṣa</s>). (GRht 18.15)

children.text: atha tāravarṇavidhānamāha vaṅgetyādi // GRhtCM_18.15:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now he states the procedure for silver-color, with '<s>vaṅga</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.15:1)

children.text:
vaṅgābhramiti vaṅgaṃ trapu abhraṃ śvetābhraṃ punaḥ sitamākṣīkaṃ vimapaṃ
                            śaipaṃ śvetaśipājatu vā site tāre vāhayet // GRhtCM_18.15:2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Vaṅgābhra</s>' — <s>vaṅga</s> is tin; <s>abhra</s> is white mica; again, 'white <s>mākṣīka</s>' is <s>vimala</s> (copper-pyrite); '<s>śaila</s>' is white mineral pitch (<s>śilājatu</s>); into silver (<s>site tāre</s>), one should digest [these]. (GRhtCM 18.15:2)

children.text:
punardaśāṃśena etadauṣadhanicayaṃ tārato daśamavibhāgena kṛtvā hi
                            niścitaṃ tārotkarṣaṃ karoti hīnavarṇata uttamaṃ karotītyabhiprāyaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_18.15:3 //
children.translated_text: Again, at one-tenth — having made one-tenth the portion of silver from this collection of medicines — it certainly produces enhancement of silver — it makes [silver] of inferior color into excellent [silver]; this is the intent. (GRhtCM 18.15:3)

children.text: nirvāhaṇa of diff. substances => phys. results
children.translated_text: Digestion (<s>nirvāhaṇa</s>) of different substances: physical results

children.text: nāgaḥ karoti mṛdutāṃ nirvyūḍhastāṃ ca raktatāṃ ca raviḥ /
children.translated_text: Lead (<s>nāga</s>), when digested [into silver], produces softness; copper (<s>ravi</s>), [produces] both that and redness;

children.text: tāṃ pītatāṃ ca tīkṣṇaṃ kācastatkālikavināśaṃ ca // GRht_18.16 //
children.translated_text: iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), [produces] both that and yellowness; glass (<s>kāca</s>), [produces] that and also immediate destruction. (GRht 18.16)

children.text: tāre viśeṣamāha nāga ityādi // GRhtCM_18.16:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the specific [effects] on silver, with '<s>nāga</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.16:1)

children.text:
nāgaḥ sīsakas tāre nirvyūḍho mṛdutāṃ komapatvaṃ karoti // GRhtCM_18.16:2
                            //
children.translated_text: <s>Nāga</s> — lead (<s>sīsaka</s>) — when digested into silver, produces softness — tenderness. (GRhtCM 18.16:2)

children.text:
punaḥ ravistāmraṃ nirvyūḍhaṃ sat tāṃ mṛdutāṃ ca punaḥ raktatāṃ
                            pohitanibhāṃ karoti // GRhtCM_18.16:3 //
children.translated_text: Again, copper (<s>ravi</s>, i.e., <s>tāmra</s>), when digested, produces both that softness and also redness — a crimson appearance. (GRhtCM 18.16:3)

children.text:
ca punastīkṣṇaṃ tāranirvyūḍhaṃ tāṃ raktatāṃ pītatāṃ ca karoti //
                            GRhtCM_18.16:4 //
children.translated_text: And again, iron (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), when digested into silver, produces both that redness and also yellowness. (GRhtCM 18.16:4)

children.text:
punaḥ kācaḥ pratīto poke sa kāpikavināśaṃ karotīti tāre nirvyūḍha iti
                            saṃbandhaḥ // GRhtCM_18.16:5 //
children.translated_text: Again, glass (<s>kāca</s>) — the well-known [substance] — produces temporary destruction; the connection is 'when digested into silver.' (GRhtCM 18.16:5)

children.text: gold:: improvement
children.translated_text: Gold: improvement

children.text: kanakāruṇasamamākṣikakarañjatailāpluto dhmātaḥ /
children.translated_text: Gold, copper, [and] equal [portions of] <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), flooded with <s>karañja</s> (Pongamia) oil and smelted —

children.text: pāte pāte daśa daśa vindati yāvaddhi koṭimapi // GRht_18.17 //
children.translated_text: at each application, [it] multiplies ten-fold, up to even ten million. (GRht 18.17)

children.text: hemno viśeṣamāha kanakāruṇetyādi // GRhtCM_18.17:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the specific [treatment] for gold, with '<s>kanaka-aruṇa</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.17:1)

children.text:
kanakaṃ hema aruṇaṃ tāmraṃ samaṃ tupyabhāgaṃ mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ ayaṃ gaṇaḥ
                            karañjataipapputo dhmātaḥ kāryaḥ // GRhtCM_18.17:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kanaka</s> is gold (<s>hema</s>); <s>aruṇa</s> is copper (<s>tāmra</s>); 'equal' means in equal portions; <s>mākṣika</s> is <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite) — this group, flooded with <s>karañja</s> oil, should be smelted. (GRhtCM 18.17:2)

children.text:
punaḥ pāte pāte vāraṃvāraṃ nikṣepe sati daśa daśa guṇotkarṣaṃ vidanti
                            dhmāta ityadhyāhāraḥ // GRhtCM_18.17:3 //
children.translated_text: Again, at each application — at each successive addition — [it] attains a ten-fold enhancement; 'smelted' is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 18.17:3)

children.text: hi niścitam // GRhtCM_18.17:4 //
children.translated_text: 'Indeed' (<s>hi</s>) means certainly. (GRhtCM 18.17:4)

children.text: kiyatkāpaṃ yāvatkoṭisaṃkhyāṃ vindati // GRhtCM_18.17:5 //
children.translated_text: For how long? Until it attains the count of ten million (<s>koṭi</s>). (GRhtCM 18.17:5)

children.text: gold:: bīja for improvement of colour
children.translated_text: Gold: seed for color improvement

children.text: sa cāyamativilīnaḥ kaṃguṇītailasecito bahuśaḥ /
children.translated_text: And this very [preparation], when extremely dissolved, sprinkled many times with <s>kaṅguṇī</s> (Celastrus) oil,

children.text: mākṣīkaravinivāpaṃ vidhyati kanakaṃ śatāṃśena // GRht_18.18 //
children.translated_text: [used as] a <s>mākṣīka</s>-copper (<s>ravi</s>) addition, transmutes gold at one-hundredth part. (GRht 18.18)

children.text: viśeṣamāha sa ityādi // GRhtCM_18.18:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the specific [quality], with 'this' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.18:1)

children.text:
saḥ karañjataipapputo yogo bahuśo vāraṃvāraṃ kaṅguṇītaipena secito yathā
                            syāttathāyaṃ ati vipīnaḥ san mākṣikaravinivāpāṃ punaḥ kārya evaṃvidhaṃ
                            ca kanakaṃ śatāṃśena śatavibhāgena vidhyati sitakanakam iti //
                            GRhtCM_18.18:2 //
children.translated_text: That very preparation — the one flooded with <s>karañja</s> oil — sprinkled many times, i.e., repeatedly, with <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil so as to be [properly prepared]; this, being extremely dissolved, should be made with pyrite-copper (<s>mākṣika-ravi</s>) addition; again, [such a preparation] transmutes gold at one-hundredth part — at one-hundredth proportion; 'white gold' [is to be supplied]. (GRhtCM 18.18:2)

children.text: gold:: bīja for improvement (?)
children.translated_text: Gold: seed for improvement (?)

children.text: śulbahataṃ rasagandhāhatakhagapītaṃ daśāṃśena /
children.translated_text: Killed with copper (<s>śulba</s>), killed by mercury-sulphur (<s>rasagandha</s>), [combined with] yellow vitriol (<s>khagapīta</s>), at one-tenth part,

children.text: vidhyati kanakaṃ kurute tannirvyūḍhaṃ marditaṃ sudṛḍham // GRht_18.19 //
children.translated_text: it transmutes gold; one should grind that digested [mixture] very firmly. (GRht 18.19)

children.text: viśeṣamāha śupbetyādi // GRhtCM_18.19:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the specific [method], with '<s>śulba</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.19:1)

children.text:
śupbahataṃ śupbena saha hataṃ rasagandhaṃ sūtagandhaṃ tena āhataṃ
                            pañcatvam āpannaṃ yatkhagapītaṃ pītakāsīsaṃ etadauṣadhasamuccayaṃ
                            sudṛḍhaṃ yathā syāttathā marditaṃ kuryāt punastat nirvyūḍhaṃ daśāṃśena
                            vidhyati sitakanakaṃ kurute svarṇamiti viśeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_18.19:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Killed with copper' — killed together with copper (<s>śulba</s>); '<s>rasagandha</s>' — mercury and sulphur (<s>sūta-gandha</s>); killed by that — reduced to death (<s>pañcatva</s>); the '<s>khagapīta</s>' is yellow vitriol (<s>pītakāsīsa</s>) — this collection of medicines should be ground very firmly; again, that digested [mixture], at one-tenth part, transmutes white gold — makes it [into true] gold; this is the specific [method]. (GRhtCM 18.19:2)

children.text: vedha
children.translated_text: Transmutation (<s>vedha</s>)

children.text: rasakasamaṃ sudhmātaṃ kanakaṃ bhuktvā tato+arkacandralepena /
children.translated_text: Gold, well-smelted with equal [parts of] calamine (<s>rasaka</s>), having consumed, then with sun-moon coating (<s>arkacandra-lepa</s>) —

children.text: mākṣikasattvaṃ hemnā karoti jīrṇo rasaḥ śatāṃśena // GRht_18.20 //
children.translated_text: <s>mākṣika</s>-essence (pyrite-essence) with gold, [when] mercury has digested [it], transmutes at one-hundredth part. (GRht 18.20)

children.text: anyaccāha rasaketyādi // GRhtCM_18.20:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another [method], with '<s>rasaka</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.20:1)

children.text:
tato+anantaraṃ arkacandrapepena kanakaṃ rasakasamaṃ dhmātaṃ kuryāt
                            punaretadauṣadhaṃ bhuktvā kanakaṃ syāt punarmākṣikasattvaṃ hemnā saha
                            jīrṇaṃ rasaṃ śatāṃśena vidhyatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.20:2 //
children.translated_text: Thereafter, with sun-moon coating (<s>arkacandra-lepa</s>), gold should be smelted with equal [parts of] calamine; again, having consumed this medicine, [it] would become gold; again, <s>mākṣika</s>-essence (pyrite-essence) with gold — mercury digested [with these] — transmutes at one-hundredth part, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 18.20:2)

children.text: vedha; silver => gold
children.translated_text: Transmutation (<s>vedha</s>): silver to gold

children.text: aṣṭaguṇaṃ mṛtaśulbaṃ kaladhautena mūkamūṣayā liptam /
children.translated_text: Killed copper (<s>śulba</s>) at eight times [the weight], with silver (<s>kaladhautena</s>), sealed in a blind crucible (<s>mūkamūṣā</s>),

children.text: tatṣoḍaśāṃśajīrṇaṃ vidhyati tāraṃ śatārdhena // GRht_18.21 //
children.translated_text: that [mercury], having digested [it] at one-sixteenth part, transmutes silver at one-fiftieth. (GRht 18.21)

children.text: anyaccāha aṣṭaguṇetyādi // GRhtCM_18.21:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another [method], with 'eight times' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.21:1)

children.text:
aṣṭaguṇaṃ mṛtaśupbaṃ arivargeṇa saha hataṃ yat śupbaṃ tāmraṃ tataḥ
                            kapadhautena ṣoḍaśāṃśena jīrṇaṃ śatārdhena pañcāśadvibhāgena tāraṃ
                            vidhyati kanakaṃ karotītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.21:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Eight times killed copper' — copper (<s>tāmra</s>) killed together with the enemy-group (<s>arivarga</s>); then, 'with silver' (<s>kaladhautena</s>), digested at one-sixteenth, [it] transmutes silver at one-fiftieth — half a hundredth — making it gold, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 18.21:2)

children.text: vedha:: daśāṃśa~; silver => gold
children.translated_text: Transmutation (<s>vedha</s>): one-tenth proportion; silver to gold

children.text: āvṛtya kanakakariṇau śilayā prativāpitau tato bhuktvā /
children.translated_text: Having wrapped the gold-elephant [pair] (<s>kanaka-karin</s>), meaning gold and lead in equal parts, [and] treated with realgar (<s>śilā</s>), then having consumed,

children.text: dolāyantre gandhakajīrṇastāre daśāṃśavedhī syāt // GRht_18.22 //
children.translated_text: in a swing-apparatus (<s>dolāyantra</s>), [mercury] digested with sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>) would transmute silver at one-tenth [proportion]. (GRht 18.22)

children.text: anyaccāha āvṛtyetyādi // GRhtCM_18.22:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another [method], with 'having wrapped' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.22:1)

children.text:
kanakakariṇau samahemanāgau āvṛtya gāpayitvā śipayā manohvayā
                            prativāpitau tato+anantaraṃ dopāyantre kanakakariṇau bhuktvā
                            gandhakajīrṇo yo rasaḥ sa tāre daśāṃśavedhī syāt daśāṃśena
                            vidhyatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.22:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Gold-elephant [pair]' (<s>kanaka-karin</s>) — gold and lead (<s>nāga</s>) in equal parts — having wrapped, meaning having melted [them together]; treated with realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>); then, thereafter, in a swing-apparatus (<s>dolāyantra</s>), having consumed the gold-elephant [pair]; the mercury that has digested sulphur — that [mercury] would transmute silver at one-tenth — it transmutes at one-tenth proportion, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 18.22:2)

children.text: vedha:: śatāṃśa; bronze => gold
children.translated_text: Transmutation (<s>vedha</s>): one-hundredth; bronze to gold

children.text: ripunihatalohaṣaṭkaṃ jīrṇo dhānyasthitaścaturmāsam /
children.translated_text: [Mercury] having digested the six metals killed by the enemy-group (<s>ripu</s>), stored in grain for four months,

children.text: sahitaḥ purasurābhyāṃ vidhyati ghoṣaṃ śatāṃśena // GRht_18.23 //
children.translated_text: combined with guggulu resin (<s>pura</s>) and liquor (<s>surā</s>), transmutes bronze (<s>ghoṣa</s>) at one-hundredth [proportion]. (GRht 18.23)

children.text: anyaccāha ripunihatetyādi // GRhtCM_18.23:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another [method], with 'killed by the enemies' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.23:1)

children.text:
ripunihatapohaṣaṭkaṃ ripubhir arivargair nihataṃ māritaṃ yat pohaṣaṭkaṃ
                            svarṇatāratāmranāgavaṅgapohābhidhānaṃ tat caturmāsaṃ yathā syāttathā
                            dhānyasthito+annakoṣṭhīdhṛto raso jīrṇaḥ // GRhtCM_18.23:2 //
children.translated_text: 'The six metals killed by the enemies' — killed, meaning calcined, by the enemies, i.e., the enemy-group (<s>arivarga</s>); the six metals designated as gold, silver, copper, lead, tin, and iron — [mercury] having digested those, stored in grain — kept in a grain-bin — for four months. (GRhtCM 18.23:2)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭo dhānyasthitaḥ purasurābhyāṃ guggupumadirābhyāṃ sahito mipitaḥ
                            śatāṃśena ghoṣaṃ kāṃsyaṃ vidhyati kanakaṃ karotītyarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_18.23:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality [is the mercury] stored in grain? Combined, meaning mixed, with guggulu resin (<s>pura</s>, i.e., <s>guggulu</s>) and liquor (<s>surā</s>, i.e., <s>madirā</s>); [it] transmutes bronze (<s>ghoṣa</s>, i.e., <s>kāṃsya</s>) at one-hundredth — at one-hundredth proportion — it makes [it] gold, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 18.23:3)

children.text: vakṣye samprati samyagyad bījaṃ samarase jīrṇam /
children.translated_text: I shall now describe properly what seed, digested in equal [parts of] mercury,

children.text: piṣṭistambhādividhiṃ prakāśyamānaṃ budhāḥ śṛṇuta // GRht_18.24 //
children.translated_text: [produces] the procedures of pellet (<s>piṣṭī</s>), fixation (<s>stambha</s>), and so forth — O wise ones, listen to what is being revealed! (GRht 18.24)

children.text: viśeṣamāha vakṣya ityādi // GRhtCM_18.24:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the distinctive [procedure] with 'vakṣya' (I shall describe) and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.24:1)

children.text:
bho budhāḥ mayā prakāśyamānaṃ sat śṛṇuta sāvadhānā ityadhyāhāryam //
                            GRhtCM_18.24:2 //
children.translated_text: O wise ones! Listen attentively to what is being revealed by me — this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 18.24:2)

children.text:
tatkiṃ saṃprati yad bījaṃ samarase tupyasūte samyak jīrṇaṃ jāraṇamāpannaṃ
                            tadahaṃ govindanāmā vakṣye kathayāmi // GRhtCM_18.24:3 //
children.translated_text: What [will he say] now? That seed which is properly assimilated in mercury with equal gold — I, named <s>Govinda</s>, shall describe. (GRhtCM 18.24:3)

children.text:
punaḥ piṣṭistambhādividhiṃ piṣṭistambha ādir yasya vidhestaṃ vidhiṃ
                            pāṭakhoṭajapaukākhyaṃ ca vakṣye // GRhtCM_18.24:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the procedure of <s>piṣṭistambha</s> (pellet-fixation) and the like — the procedure whose beginning is <s>piṣṭistambha</s> — that procedure called <s>pāṭa</s> (split), <s>khoṭa</s> (ingot), and <s>jalaukā</s> (leech) — I shall describe. (GRhtCM 18.24:4)

children.text: vedha; ghoṣākṛṣṭa => gold
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Vedha</s> (transmutation); <s>ghoṣākṛṣṭa</s> (bell-metal-drawn) [copper] becomes gold

children.text: rājāvartakavimalapītābhragandhatāpyarasakaiśca /
children.translated_text: With <s>rājāvarta</s> (lapis lazuli), <s>vimala</s> (silver-pyrite), yellow mica, sulfur, <s>tāpya</s> (iron pyrite), and <s>rasaka</s> (calamine),

children.text: kāṃkṣīkāsīsaśilādaradaiśca samanvitaṃ nāgam // GRht_18.25 //
children.translated_text: and with <s>kāṅkṣī</s> (orpiment variety), <s>kāsīsa</s> (green vitriol), realgar (<s>śilā</s>), and cinnabar (<s>darada</s>) — lead combined [with these]. (GRht 18.25)

children.text: ahimārarasaiḥ puṭitaṃ māraya nāgaṃ nirutthakaṃ yāvat /
children.translated_text: Calcinated with oleander (<s>ahimāra</s>) juices, kill the lead until it no longer rises;

children.text:
tadanu ca tasya hi madhye śulbaṃ gandhaṃ ca lavaṇakaṃkuṣṭham //
                                GRht_18.26 //
children.translated_text: thereafter, in its midst [add] copper, sulfur, and salt and <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> (red arsenic). (GRht 18.26)

children.text: tatsarvaṃ śatavārān bhāvaya pakvārkapatrasalilaiśca /
children.translated_text: Treat all of that a hundred times with the juices of cooked <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) leaves;

children.text: ghoṣākṛṣṭe śulbe cūrṇaṃ nirvāhayecchataśaḥ // GRht_18.27 //
children.translated_text: on <s>ghoṣākṛṣṭa</s> (bell-metal-drawn) copper, discharge the powder hundreds of times. (GRht 18.27)

children.text: śulbena tena hi samaṃ rasakapītābhrasatvavimalaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: With that copper, in equal [parts]: <s>rasaka</s> (calamine), yellow-mica-essence, <s>vimala</s>,

children.text: gairikamākṣikasattvaṃ ṭaṅkaṇanāgaṃ ca tīkṣṇayutam // GRht_18.28 //
children.translated_text: ochre-pyrite-essence, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), lead, and combined with steel. (GRht 18.28)

children.text: etair dvandvaṃ kṛtvā mākṣikavāpena rañjayecchulvam /
children.translated_text: Having made a binary [fusion] with these, one should color the copper with <s>mākṣika</s>-deposition;

children.text: vārāṃśca viṃśatirapi galitaṃ secayettadanu // GRht_18.29 //
children.translated_text: and even twenty more times — when melted, one should sprinkle thereafter. (GRht 18.29)

children.text: nirguṇḍīkākamācīkanyārasamelanaṃ kṛtvā /
children.translated_text: Having made a combination of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (vitex), <s>kākamācī</s> (nightshade), and <s>kanyā</s> (aloe) juices,

children.text: vārān sapta ca vidhinā tadapi ca nirvāpayeddhemni // GRht_18.30 //
children.translated_text: seven times by the [proper] method — one should also quench that in gold. (GRht 18.30)

children.text: yāvaccaturviṃśatiguṇaṃ bījavaraṃ rañjayettacca /
children.translated_text: Until the excellent seed colors twenty-four-fold, and that

children.text: pakvaṃ mākṣikameva hi tena ca vidhinā tadapi caturviṃśatiguṇam // GRht_18.31 //
children.translated_text: [is] indeed cooked <s>mākṣika</s> itself; and by that method, that also [becomes] twenty-four-fold. (GRht 18.31)

children.text: tadbījaṃ laghumātraṃ rasarāje saṃskṛte pūrvam /
children.translated_text: That seed, in a small amount, in the king of mercury previously prepared,

children.text: mūṣāyāṃ khalu dattvā daśaguṇaṃ ca gandhakaṃ dāhyam // GRht_18.32 //
children.translated_text: having placed [it] in a crucible, one should burn tenfold sulfur. (GRht 18.32)

children.text: athavā vālukayantre sudṛḍhe caturdaśāṃgulamūṣāyām /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, in a firm sand-bath apparatus (<s>vālukayantra</s>), in a crucible of fourteen finger-breadths,

children.text: madhye sūtaṃ muktvā laghutarapuṭayogataḥ pihitā // GRht_18.33 //
children.translated_text: having placed the mercury in the middle, sealed with the lightest heat-treatment. (GRht 18.33)

children.text: tena samaṃ bījavare piṣṭiḥ pādāṃśataḥ kāryā /
children.translated_text: With that, in the excellent seed in equal [parts], a pellet should be made from a quarter-portion;

children.text: aṃgulinavaparimāṇe mūṣāmadhye ca piṣṭikāṃ dattvā // GRht_18.34 //
children.translated_text: and in a crucible of nine finger-breadths measure, having placed the pellet, (GRht 18.34)

children.text: nirguṇḍīkākamācīgojihvādugdhikāraktā /
children.translated_text: <s>Nirguṇḍī</s> (vitex), <s>kākamācī</s> (nightshade), <s>gojihvā</s> (oxtongue), <s>dugdhikā</s> (milkweed), <s>raktā</s> (red variety),

children.text: gṛhakanyāmadhusaindhavapiṇḍairapi samantataśchādyā // GRht_18.35 //
children.translated_text: <s>gṛhakanyā</s> (aloe), honey, and rock-salt pills — [the pellet] should be covered all around. (GRht 18.35)

children.text: tāvatkāryaḥ puṭayogo yāvad dṛḍhatāṃ samāyāti /
children.translated_text: Heat-treatment should be applied until [the pellet] attains firmness;

children.text: ṣaḍguṇagandhakatālakakāṃkṣīkāsīsalavaṇakṣāram // GRht_18.36 //
children.translated_text: sixfold sulfur, orpiment, <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s>, salt, and alkali, (GRht 18.36)

children.text: tāpyaṃ tatsarvasamaṃ deyaṃ bāhye tadauṣadhipiṇḍam /
children.translated_text: <s>tāpya</s> (iron pyrite) — all these in equal [amounts] should be given externally as a medicinal ball;

children.text: ṣaḍguṇaṣaḍguṇasahitaṃ piṣṭīṃ yantre'tha kacchape dattvā // GRht_18.37 //
children.translated_text: combined in sixfold upon sixfold [quantity], having placed the pellet in the tortoise-apparatus, (GRht 18.37)

children.text: svedyaṃ puṭayogena tu tridinaṃ ghaṭikātrayaṃ yāvat /
children.translated_text: it should be steamed by heat-treatment for three days, up to three <s>ghaṭikās</s> (72 minutes);

children.text: uddhṛtya tato yatnāt piṣṭvā sucūrṇitāṃ kṛtvā // GRht_18.38 //
children.translated_text: then extracting [it] carefully, having ground and well-pulverized [it], (GRht 18.38)

children.text: samabījena tu sāryo nāgaṃ triguṇaṃ tataḥ samuttārya /
children.translated_text: it should be streamed with equal seed; then having removed the threefold lead,

children.text: pratisāraṇā ca kāryā jāritasūtena bījayuktena // GRht_18.39 //
children.translated_text: counter-streaming should also be done with the assimilated mercury combined with seed. (GRht 18.39)

children.text: anusāraṇā ca paścāttriguṇaṃ bījaṃ bhavedyatra /
children.translated_text: Follow-up streaming [should be done] afterward, where the seed is threefold;

children.text: prāguktaṃ tasyopari mṛtanāgaṃ śataguṇaṃ vāhyam /
children.translated_text: upon that, as previously stated, calcined lead in hundredfold [quantity] should be discharged;

children.text: tena ca ghoṣākṛṣṭe śulbe vedho+atha saptaśataiḥ // GRht_18.40 //
children.translated_text: and with that, on <s>ghoṣākṛṣṭa</s> (bell-metal-drawn) copper, transmutation [occurs] at seven hundred[-fold]. (GRht 18.40)

children.text: atha nāgamāha rājāvartaketyādi // GRhtCM_18.25-40:1 //
children.translated_text: Now he describes the lead [procedure] with '<s>rājāvartaka</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.25-40:1)

children.text:
rājāvartakaṃ prasiddhaṃ vimapaṃ śvetamākṣikaṃ pītābhraṃ pītavarṇaṃ
                            yadabhraṃ gandho gandhakaḥ tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ rasakaṃ kharparikaṃ
                            etaiḥ punaretaiḥ kāṅkṣī kāhīti poke kāsīsaṃ pītakāsīsaṃ śipā manohvā
                            daradaṃ hiṅgupaṃ taiśca samanvitaṃ mipitaṃ nāgaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_18.25-40:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rājāvartaka</s> is well-known (lapis lazuli); <s>vimala</s> is silver-pyrite; yellow mica is mica of yellow color; <s>gandha</s> is sulfur; <s>tāpya</s> is gold-pyrite; <s>rasaka</s> is calamine — with these; furthermore with these: <s>kāṅkṣī</s> is called <s>kāhī</s> in the vernacular; <s>kāsīsa</s> is yellow vitriol; <s>śilā</s> is realgar; <s>darada</s> is cinnabar — with these combined, one should make the lead [preparation] — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 18.25-40:2)

children.text: taccāha ahītyādi // GRhtCM_18.25-40:3 //
children.translated_text: He states that with 'ahi' (serpent) and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.25-40:3)

children.text:
pūrvauṣadhasaṃyutaṃ nāgaṃ ahimārarasaiḥ karavīradrāvaiḥ puṭitaṃ kuryāt //
                            GRhtCM_18.25-40:4 //
children.translated_text: Lead combined with the aforementioned medicines should be calcinated — made into <s>puṭa</s> — with <s>ahimāra</s> (oleander, lit. 'snake-killer') juices, decoctions of oleander. (GRhtCM 18.25-40:4)

children.text:
nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ tāvanmāraya yāvannirutthakaṃ yathā punarutthitaṃ na syāt //
                            GRhtCM_18.25-40:5 //
children.translated_text: Kill the lead — the <s>sīsaka</s> (lead) — until it becomes <s>nirutthaka</s> — such that it does not rise again. (GRhtCM 18.25-40:5)

children.text:
tadanu tatpaścāt tasya nāgasya madhye śupbaṃ tāmraṃ gandhaṃ pratītaṃ
                            pavaṇaṃ saindhavaṃ kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ viraṅgaṃ etatsarvaṃ miśritaṃ kuryāt
                            ityadhyāhāryam // GRhtCM_18.25-40:6 //
children.translated_text: Thereafter, in the midst of that lead — copper, well-known sulfur, salt meaning rock salt, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> meaning <s>viraṅga</s> (red arsenic) — all this should be mixed — this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 18.25-40:6)

children.text: kṣepavedha
children.translated_text: [Section:] <s>Kṣepavedha</s> (transmutation by projection)

children.text: krāmaṇam etatprāgapi mākṣikadaradagandhakaśilābhiḥ /
children.translated_text: This <s>krāmaṇa</s> (progressive transmutation agent), as stated earlier too, with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), cinnabar, sulfur, and realgar;

children.text: rājāvartakavimalapravālakaṅkuṣṭhatutthaviṣaiḥ // GRht_18.41 //
children.translated_text: with <s>rājāvartaka</s> (lapis lazuli), <s>vimala</s> (silver-pyrite), coral, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> (red arsenic), <s>tuttha</s> (copper sulfate), and <s>viṣa</s> (poison); (GRht 18.41)

children.text: kāntagairikaṭaṃkaṇabhūmilatārudhiraśakragoparasaiḥ /
children.translated_text: with lodestone, ochre, borax, <s>bhūmilatā</s> (earth-creeper), blood, <s>indragopa</s> (cochineal insect), and mercury;

children.text: mahiṣīṇāṃ karṇamalair mṛtalohaṃ vāyasasya viṣṭhā ca // GRht_18.42 //
children.translated_text: with the ear-secretions of buffalo-cows, calcined iron, and the dung of crows; (GRht 18.42)

children.text: pārāvatasya viṣṭhā strīpayaḥ sarvam ekataḥ kṛtvā /
children.translated_text: the dung of pigeons, woman's milk — having combined all together,

children.text: krāmaṇakalkaṃ caitacchatavārān raktapītagaṇaiḥ // GRht_18.43 //
children.translated_text: this <s>krāmaṇa</s>-paste [should be treated] a hundred times with the red and yellow groups [of substances]; (GRht 18.43)

children.text: bhāvyaṃ kaṃguṇitaile krauñcīpittabhāvanāḥ sapta /
children.translated_text: it should be treated in <s>kaṅguṇī</s>-oil; seven treatments with <s>krauñcī</s> (crane-herb) bile;

children.text: kalkenānena pacet sāritapiṣṭiṃ ca haṇḍikāyāṃ hi // GRht_18.44 //
children.translated_text: with this paste, one should cook the streamed pellet in a pot. (GRht 18.44)

children.text: yāvadraktā bhavati hi gacchati nāgaṃ samuttārya /
children.translated_text: Until it becomes red and it goes [into] lead — having removed [the lead],

children.text: tāvatkṣepaṃ ca kṣipetsarvasminsāraṇādau ca // GRht_18.45 //
children.translated_text: one should then cast the projection in everything — in streaming and the rest. (GRht 18.45)

children.text: evaṃ hi koṭivedhī rasarājaḥ krāmito bhūtvā /
children.translated_text: Thus indeed the king of mercury, having been subjected to <s>krāmaṇa</s>, becomes a transmuter at the <s>koṭi</s>-level (ten-million-fold);

children.text: puṃstvāderucchrāyaprado bhūtvā bhogāndatte // GRht_18.46 //
children.translated_text: becoming a giver of enhancement in manhood and the rest, it bestows enjoyments. (GRht 18.46)

children.text: krāmaṇamāha krāmaṇam ityādi // GRhtCM_18.41-46:1 //
children.translated_text: He describes the <s>krāmaṇa</s> (progressive transmutation) with '<s>krāmaṇam</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.41-46:1)

children.text: prāgapīti pūrvādhyāye'pi proktaṃ iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_18.41-46:2 //
children.translated_text: 'As stated earlier' — as stated in the previous chapter also — this is the complement. (GRhtCM 18.41-46:2)

children.text:
punaretadvakṣyamāṇaṃ krāmaṇaguṇaṃ kuryād ityadhyāhāraḥ //
                            GRhtCM_18.41-46:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, one should make this forthcoming <s>krāmaṇa</s> quality — this is to be supplied. (GRhtCM 18.41-46:3)

children.text: sa kathaṃ tadāha mākṣiketyādi // GRhtCM_18.41-46:4 //
children.translated_text: How so? He states that with '<s>mākṣika</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.41-46:4)

children.text:
mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ daradaṃ hiṅgupaṃ gandhakaḥ pratītaḥ śipā manohvā tābhiḥ
                            // GRhtCM_18.41-46:5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> is iron pyrite; <s>darada</s> is cinnabar; <s>gandhaka</s> is well-known; <s>śilā</s> is realgar — with these. (GRhtCM 18.41-46:5)

children.text: punaḥ rājāvartaketyādi // GRhtCM_18.41-46:6 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, '<s>rājāvartaka</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.41-46:6)

children.text:
rājāvartakaṃ pājavarada iti bhāṣāyāṃ vimapaṃ sitamākṣikaṃ pravāpaṃ
                            vidrumaṃ kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ viraṅgaṃ tutthakaṃ śikhigrīvaṃ viṣaṃ
                            saktukādikandajaṃ etaiśca // GRhtCM_18.41-46:7 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rājāvartaka</s> — called <s>lājavarda</s> in the vernacular — <s>vimala</s> is silver-pyrite; <s>pravāla</s> is coral; <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is <s>viraṅga</s> (red arsenic); <s>tutthaka</s> is 'peacock-neck' (copper sulfate); <s>viṣa</s> is a tuberous poison from <s>saktuka</s> and the like — with these also. (GRhtCM 18.41-46:7)

children.text:
kāntetyādi kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ gairikaṃ pratītaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ
                            bhūmipatā bhūnāgaḥ rudhiraṃ śakragopaḥ raso viṣaṃ punaruktādviṣamatra
                            dviguṇaṃ taiḥ // GRhtCM_18.41-46:8 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Kānta</s>' and so forth — <s>kānta</s> is lodestone; <s>gairika</s> is well-known; <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgya</s> (borax); <s>bhūmilatā</s> is <s>bhūnāga</s> (earth-serpent herb); <s>rudhira</s> is blood; <s>śakragopa</s> is <s>indragopa</s> (cochineal insect); <s>rasa</s> is mercury — [since] '<s>viṣa</s>' is repeated, the poison here is double [in quantity] — with these. (GRhtCM 18.41-46:8)

children.text:
ca punar mahiṣīṇāṃ karṇamapair hayāripatnīnāṃ śravaṇayor mapāni taiḥ saha
                            mṛtapohaṃ mṛtaṃ ca tappohaṃ ceti vāyasasya kākasya viṣṭhā śakṛt //
                            GRhtCM_18.41-46:9 //
children.translated_text: And furthermore, with the ear-secretions of buffalo-cows — the secretions from the ears of she-buffaloes — with those; also calcined iron — calcined metal — and the dung of the crow — the feces of the <s>vāyasa</s> (crow). (GRhtCM 18.41-46:9)

children.text:
pārāvatasya viṣṭhā kapotaśakṛt strīpayo nārīkṣīraṃ etatsarvaṃ
                            mākṣikādistrīkṣīrāntam ekataḥ kṛtvā miśritaṃ vidhāya ca
                            punaretatkrāmaṇakapkaṃ raktapītagaṇaiḥ kiṃśukādiharidrādyaiḥ śatavārān
                            bhāvayedityāgāmiśpokasaṃbandhāt // GRhtCM_18.41-46:10 //
children.translated_text: The dung of pigeon — pigeon-feces; woman's milk — woman's breast-milk — all this from <s>mākṣika</s> up to woman's milk, having combined together — having mixed; and furthermore this <s>krāmaṇa</s>-paste, with the red and yellow groups — <s>kiṃśuka</s> and the like, turmeric and the like — should be treated a hundred times — from the connection with the forthcoming verse. (GRhtCM 18.41-46:10)

children.text: sāraṇakapkavidhānamāha bhāvyam ityādi // GRhtCM_18.41-46:11 //
children.translated_text: He describes the method of the streaming-paste with 'bhāvyam' (should be treated) and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.41-46:11)

children.text:
pūrvoktasāraṇakapkaṃ kaṅguṇītaipe jyotiṣmatīsnehe bhāvyaṃ tataḥ
                            krauñcīpittabhāvanāḥ sapta deyāḥ dātavyāḥ // GRhtCM_18.41-46:12 //
children.translated_text: The previously stated streaming-paste should be treated in <s>kaṅguṇī</s>-oil — in <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> (Celastrus) fat; then seven treatments with <s>krauñcī</s> (crane-herb) bile should be given. (GRhtCM 18.41-46:12)

children.text:
punaḥ sāritapiṣṭiṃ sāritā yā rasendrabījapiṣṭis tām anena kapkena
                            haṇḍikāyāṃ pacet vahninā pākaḥ kartavyaḥ // GRhtCM_18.41-46:13 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the streamed pellet — the pellet of mercury-king-and-seed that has been streamed — should be cooked in a pot with this paste — cooking with fire should be done. (GRhtCM 18.41-46:13)

children.text: sāraṇakapkapācanamāha yāvadityādi // GRhtCM_18.41-46:14 //
children.translated_text: He describes the cooking of the streaming-paste with 'yāvat' (until) and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.41-46:14)

children.text:
pūrvakapkasaṃyutāṃ piṣṭiṃ kiyatkāpaṃ pacet yāvadraktā bhavati nāgaṃ ca
                            gacchati nāganāśaḥ syāt nāge gacchati sati samuttārya
                            punastāvatsarvasminsāraṇādau ca kṣepakrameṇa kṣepaṃ kṣipet //
                            GRhtCM_18.41-46:15 //
children.translated_text: The pellet combined with the aforementioned paste — for how long should it be cooked? Until it becomes red and goes into lead — meaning the lead is destroyed. When the lead goes [away], having removed [it], then one should cast the projection by the projection method — in everything, in streaming and the rest. (GRhtCM 18.41-46:15)

children.text:
puṃstvādyān ākāśagamanaparyantān bhogān dadātītyabhiprāyaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_18.41-46:16 //
children.translated_text: It bestows enjoyments — from manhood up to sky-traversing — this is the intent. (GRhtCM 18.41-46:16)

children.text: silver => gold
children.translated_text: [Section:] Silver becomes gold

children.text: abhrakamākṣikakanakaṃ nāgayutaṃ militaṃ vidhinā /
children.translated_text: Mica, <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), gold, and lead combined, fused by the [proper] method,

children.text: sūte piṣṭiḥ kāryā divyauṣadhiyogataḥ puṭitā // GRht_18.47 //
children.translated_text: [united] with mercury — a pellet should be made, calcinated by divine herbs. (GRht 18.47)

children.text: ṣaḍguṇagandhakadāhaḥ śilayā nāgaṃ samuttārya /
children.translated_text: Sixfold-sulfur burning, with realgar; having removed the lead,

children.text: tāre hemākṛṣṭirmilitā syāt ṣoḍaśāṃśena // GRht_18.48 //
children.translated_text: in silver, gold-extraction occurs — [it] would be fused at one-sixteenth part. (GRht 18.48)

children.text: piṣṭividhyantaramāha abhrakam ityādi // GRhtCM_18.47-48:1 //
children.translated_text: He describes an alternative pellet method with 'abhraka' (mica) and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.47-48:1)

children.text:
abhrakaṃ pratītaṃ mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ kanakaṃ hema nāgayutaṃ nāgena sīsakena
                            yutaṃ sahitaṃ vidhinā kartavyopadeśena etatsarvaṃ sūte mipitaṃ sat
                            piṣṭiḥ kāryā divyauṣadhiyogataḥ puṭitā piṣṭiḥ kāryā iti //
                            GRhtCM_18.47-48:2 //
children.translated_text: Mica is well-known; <s>mākṣika</s> is iron pyrite; <s>kanaka</s> is gold; combined with lead (<s>nāga</s>) — combined with <s>sīsaka</s> (lead); by the [proper] method, the instructional procedure — all this, when fused with mercury, a pellet should be made, calcinated by the conjunction with divine herbs — a pellet should be made. (GRhtCM 18.47-48:2)

children.text: tāre hemākṛṣṭim āha ṣaḍityādi // GRhtCM_18.47-48:3 //
children.translated_text: He describes the gold-extraction in silver with 'ṣaṭ' (six) and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.47-48:3)

children.text:
pūrvoktāyāṃ piṣṭyāṃ ṣaḍguṇagandhakadāhaḥ kāryaḥ punaḥ ṣaḍguṇaśipayā kṛtvā
                            nāgaṃ samuttārya sīsakamapahāya sā niṣpannā piṣṭī ṣoḍaśāṃśena tāre rūpye
                            mipitā satī hemākṛṣṭiḥ syātkanakoddhāraṇaṃ bhavet tāmranāgādiṣu dhātuṣu
                            hema sthitameva tata ākṛṣṭiśabdo yuktaḥ // GRhtCM_18.47-48:4 //
children.translated_text: In the aforementioned pellet, sixfold-sulfur burning should be done; furthermore, having done [it] with sixfold realgar, having removed the lead — having eliminated the <s>sīsaka</s> — that accomplished pellet, at one-sixteenth part, when fused in silver, becomes gold-extraction — would produce gold-drawing. Gold remains present in metals such as copper, lead, and the like; therefore the word 'extraction' (<s>ākṛṣṭi</s>) is appropriate. (GRhtCM 18.47-48:4)

children.text: silver => gold
children.translated_text: [Section:] Silver becomes gold

children.text: mākṣikanihataṃ śulbaṃ śilayā nihataṃ ca nāgatulyāṃśam /
children.translated_text: Copper killed by <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), and [copper] killed by realgar, in portions equal to lead,

children.text: puṭitaṃ jambīrarasaiḥ saindhavasahitaṃ pacetsthālyām // GRht_18.49 //
children.translated_text: calcinated, with lemon juices combined with rock-salt — one should cook [it] in a pot. (GRht 18.49)

children.text: taccūrṇaṃ ghṛtamadhukaṭaṅkaṇasahitaṃ ca guptamūṣāyām /
children.translated_text: That powder, combined with ghee, honey, and borax, in a sealed crucible (<s>guptamūṣā</s>),

children.text: tāre triguṇaṃ vyūḍhaṃ hemākṛṣṭirbhaveddivyā // GRht_18.50 //
children.translated_text: fused threefold into silver — a divine gold-extraction results. (GRht 18.50)

children.text: nāgamāraṇavidhānamāha mākṣiketyādi // GRhtCM_18.49-50:1 //
children.translated_text: He describes the method of killing lead with '<s>mākṣika</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.49-50:1)

children.text:
mākṣikeṇa nihataṃ māritaṃ yat śupvaṃ śipayā manaḥśipayā nāgaṃ ca nihataṃ
                            māritaṃ ubhayaṃ tupyāṃśaṃ samabhāgaṃ kāryaṃ punar jambīrarasaiḥ
                            jambīradrāvaiḥ saindhavasahitam ubhayaṃ puṭitaṃ bhāvitaṃ satpacedvahninā
                            pakvaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_18.49-50:2 //
children.translated_text: That copper which is killed — calcined — by <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), and lead killed by realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>) — both should be made in equal portions to the lead; furthermore, with lemon juices — lemon decoctions — combined with rock-salt, both calcinated — treated — being such, one should cook — make cooked — with fire. (GRhtCM 18.49-50:2)

children.text: kva sthāpyāṃ mṛdbhājane ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.49-50:3 //
children.translated_text: Where should [it] be placed? In an earthen vessel, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 18.49–50:3)

children.text: copper + silver => gold
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Copper + silver → gold]

children.text: śulbaṃ balinā nihataṃ tīkṣṇaṃ daradena nihatasamabhāgam /
children.translated_text: Copper (<s>śulba</s>), killed with sulphur (<s>balin</s>); steel (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), killed with cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), in equal portions —

children.text: ekīkṛtvā puṭayetpacen mātārasenaiva // GRht_18.51 //
children.translated_text: having combined [these], one should calcine with fire-cakes and cook with woman's milk (<s>mātārasa</s>) alone. (GRht 18.51)

children.text: tāre vyūḍhaṃ triguṇaṃ mārjārākṣanibhaṃ bhavettacca /
children.translated_text: Processed in silver (<s>tāra</s>) in triple [quantity], it becomes like a cat's eye in appearance;

children.text: liptaṃ rasena puṭitaṃ hemārdhena mātrayā tulyam // GRht_18.52 //
children.translated_text: that, coated with mercury and calcined, becomes equal in measure to half-gold. (GRht 18.52)

children.text: nāge tāre hemākṛṣṭimāha śupvamityādi // GRhtCM_18.51-52:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the attraction of gold from lead and silver, with 'copper' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.51–52:1)

children.text:
bapinā gandhakena nihataṃ sat samabhāgaṃ tupyāṃśaṃ kuryāt iti śeṣaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_18.51-52:2 //
children.translated_text: Killed with sulphur (<s>balin</s>, i.e., <s>gandhaka</s>), being in equal portion — one should make it in mercury-portion, is the completion. (GRhtCM 18.51–52:2)

children.text:
ubhayamekīkṛtya saṃmiśrya mātārasenaiva nārīkṣīreṇa puṭayet paced iti
                            śpokārthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.51-52:3 //
children.translated_text: Having combined both — mixed together — with woman's milk (<s>mātārasa</s>, i.e., <s>nārīkṣīra</s>) alone, one should calcine with fire-cakes and cook — this is the meaning of the verse. (GRhtCM 18.51–52:3)

children.text: hemākṛṣṭervidhānamāha tāre ityādi // GRhtCM_18.51-52:4 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the procedure for gold-attraction, with 'in silver' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.51–52:4)

children.text:
pūrvoktaṃ cūrṇaṃ śupbajaṃ tīkṣṇajaṃ vā tāre triguṇaṃ vyūḍhaṃ vāhitaṃ sat
                            mārjārākṣasaṃnibha otunetrābhaṃ tāraṃ bhavet // GRhtCM_18.51-52:5 //
children.translated_text: The aforementioned powder — whether produced from copper or from steel — when processed in silver in triple [quantity], the silver becomes like a cat's eye (<s>mārjārākṣa</s>) — resembling a cat's eye in luster. (GRhtCM 18.51–52:5)

children.text:
hemārdhena mātrayā tārārdhabhāgena parimāṇena hemnā tupyam anyūnādhikaṃ
                            rasena payasā // GRhtCM_18.51-52:6 //
children.translated_text: With half-gold — in measure equal to half of the silver — with gold, equal in mercury-portion, neither less nor more; with mercury — with milk. (GRhtCM 18.51–52:6)

children.text: lead => gold
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Lead → gold]

children.text: liptaṃ tadanu puṭitaṃ nāgaṃ hi rasena pādayuktena /
children.translated_text: Coated; then, calcined — lead (<s>nāga</s>) indeed, with mercury combined with a quarter-portion,

children.text: kharparakasthaṃ kṛtvā kāryaṃ vidhinā dṛḍhaṃ tāpyam // GRht_18.53 //
children.translated_text: having placed in a calamine (<s>kharpara</s>) vessel, should be firmly heated (<s>tāpya</s>) by the [proper] method. (GRht 18.53)

children.text: nirguṇḍīrasabhāvitapuṭitaṃ śilayā vartitaṃ ślakṣṇam /
children.translated_text: Calcined after being soaked in <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex negundo) juice, rolled with realgar (<s>śilā</s>) until smooth,

children.text: tāvanmṛditapuṭitaṃ nirutthabhāvaṃ vrajedyāvat // GRht_18.54 //
children.translated_text: ground and calcined repeatedly until it reaches the state of non-rising (<s>niruttha</s>). (GRht 18.54)

children.text: tāre tannirvyūḍhaṃ yāvatpītaṃ bhavedruciram /
children.translated_text: That, processed in silver, until [the silver] becomes pleasingly yellow;

children.text: hemasamena ca militaṃ mātrātulyaṃ bhavetkanakam // GRht_18.55 //
children.translated_text: and when combined with gold in equal measure, it becomes gold. (GRht 18.55)

children.text: punarnāgavidhānamāha piptamityādi // GRhtCM_18.53-55:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another lead procedure, with 'coated' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.53–55:1)

children.text:
triguṇaṃ yathā syāt tathā pādayuktena rasena caturthāṃśasahitasūtena saha
                            nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ kharparakasthaṃ mṛdbhājanakhaṇḍasthitaṃ kṛtvā vidhinā
                            rasajñopadeśena dṛḍhaṃ tāpyaṃ vahniyutaṃ sat nihataṃ kuryāditi
                            vākyārthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.53-55:2 //
children.translated_text: So that it becomes triple — with mercury combined with a quarter-portion, meaning mercury with a fourth part added — lead (<s>nāga</s>, i.e., <s>sīsaka</s>), having been placed in a calamine vessel — placed in a fragment of an earthen vessel — by the method, meaning by the instruction of one who knows mercury, should be firmly heated (<s>tāpya</s>) — when combined with fire, it should be killed — this is the meaning of the sentence. (GRhtCM 18.53–55:2)

children.text: taccāha nirguṇḍītyādi // GRhtCM_18.53-55:3 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That he states, with '<s>nirguṇḍī</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.53–55:3)

children.text:
pakvaṃ nāgacūrṇaṃ śpakṣṇaṃ śreṣṭhavidhānaṃ yathā syāttathā śipayā
                            vartitaṃ san nirguṇḍīrasabhāvitapuṭitaṃ pūrṇaṃ bhāvitaṃ gharmapuṭitaṃ
                            paścātpuṭitaṃ vahnipuṭitaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_18.53-55:4 //
children.translated_text: The cooked lead-powder, smooth — of the finest preparation — rolled with realgar (<s>śilā</s>), soaked in <s>nirguṇḍī</s> juice and then calcined — fully processed, fire-calcined — and afterwards calcined again with fire-cakes. (GRhtCM 18.53–55:4)

children.text:
punaryāvannirutthabhāvaṃ aśīratvaṃ vrajet tāvanmṛditapuṭitaṃ
                            marditapācitaṃ kuryād ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.53-55:5 //
children.translated_text: Again, until it reaches the state of non-rising (<s>niruttha</s>) — the state of non-elevation — it should be ground and calcined — pounded and cooked, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 18.53–55:5)

children.text: taccāha tāre ityādi // GRhtCM_18.53-55:6 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That he states, with 'in silver' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.53–55:6)

children.text:
tannirutthanāgacūrṇaṃ yāvatpītaṃ pītavarṇaṃ tāraṃ bhavet tāvadvāraṃ
                            nirvyūḍhaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_18.53-55:7 //
children.translated_text: That non-rising lead powder, until the silver becomes yellow — yellow-colored — one should process it that many times. (GRhtCM 18.53–55:7)

children.text:
punarhemasamena kanakatupyāṃśena mātrātupyaṃ mipitaṃ sat ruciraṃ
                            manoramaṃ kanakaṃ sarvaṃ bhavedityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.53-55:8 //
children.translated_text: Again, with gold in equal [measure] — with gold in mercury-portion — equal in measure, when combined, it all becomes beautiful gold, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 18.53–55:8)

children.text: svarṇamākṣika => gold
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: <s>Svarṇamākṣika</s> (gold-pyrite) → gold]

children.text: tāpyaṃ cāṃgulisaṃjñaṃ cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tadantare dattvā /
children.translated_text: <s>Tāpya</s> (pyrite), known as 'finger' (<s>aṅguli</s>), having been powdered and placed inside [the crucible] —

children.text: śulbasya guptamūṣā kāryā puṭitāpyatha ca dhmātā // GRht_18.56 //
children.translated_text: a sealed crucible (<s>guptamūṣā</s>) of copper should be made, calcined, and then smelted. (GRht 18.56)

children.text: hemnā militaṃ vidhinā mātrātulyaṃ bhavatyeva /
children.translated_text: When combined with gold by the [proper] method, it becomes equal in measure.

children.text: tāpyavidhānamāha tāpyamityādi // GRhtCM_18.56:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the pyrite procedure, with '<s>tāpya</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.56:1)

children.text:
aṅgulisaṃjñaṃ tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tadantare taccūrṇam
                                antare madhye dattvā śulbasya tāmrasya guptamūṣā andhamūṣā kāryā
                                tatra nale ityabhiprāyaḥ // GRhtCM_18.56:2 //
children.translated_text: The pyrite known as 'finger' (<s>aṅgulisaṃjña</s>) — <s>svarṇamākṣika</s> (gold-pyrite) — having powdered it and placed inside — that powder in the middle — a sealed crucible (<s>guptamūṣā</s>, i.e., <s>andhamūṣā</s>) of copper should be made; therein, in the tube — this is the intent. (GRhtCM 18.56:2)

children.text: sā mūṣā puṭitā dhmātā kāryeti vidhānam uktam // GRhtCM_18.56:3 //
children.translated_text: That crucible, calcined and smelted, should be made — thus the procedure is stated. (GRhtCM 18.56:3)

children.text: taccāha hemnetyādi // GRhtCM_18.56:4 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That he states, with 'with gold' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.56:4)

children.text: pakvaṃ yanmākṣikacūrṇaṃ taddhemnā kṛtvā // GRhtCM_18.56:5 //
children.translated_text: The cooked pyrite-powder, having combined with gold — (GRhtCM 18.56:5)

children.text: gold:: rañjana (??)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Gold — coloring (<s>rañjana</s>) (?)]

children.text: pādādijīrṇasūte lihyāt patrāṇi hemakṛṣṭīnām // GRht_18.57 //
children.translated_text: In mercury in which a quarter and so forth have been digested, one should apply the leaves of gold-extracts. (GRht 18.57)

children.text: krāmaṇayogena tato vilipya vidhinā nidhāya tulyādhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having smeared with the <s>krāmaṇa</s> (creeping) formula, having placed [it] according to procedure, with an equal [portion] below,

children.text: paścāddhemnā sahitaṃ dhmātaṃ mūṣodare samāvartya // GRht_18.58 //
children.translated_text: afterwards, combined with gold, smelted inside the crucible, having turned [it]. (GRht 18.58)

children.text: yantraṃ haṇḍyāṃ pakvaṃ pañcamṛdāvāpya puṭapakvam /
children.translated_text: The apparatus [placed] in a pot, cooked; having applied the five clays (<s>pañcamṛd</s>), calcined with fire-cakes.

children.text:
pādādijīrṇasūte pādādinā pādārdhasamānadinā jīrṇo yo+asau sūtaḥ
                                tasmin hemakṛṣṭīnāṃ patrāṇi kaluṣakanakānāṃ patrāṇi lihyāt
                                krāmaṇayogena lepayedityāgāmiślokāt // GRhtCM_18.57-58:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In mercury in which a quarter and so forth have been digested — <s>pādādi</s> means beginning with a quarter, then half, then equal — that mercury in which [these portions] are digested; one should apply the leaves of gold-extracts — the leaves of impure gold — with the <s>krāmaṇa</s> formula, meaning smear [them] — as will be explained in the following verse. (GRhtCM 18.57–58:1)

children.text: taccāha krāmaṇetyādi // GRhtCM_18.57-58:2 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That he states, with '<s>krāmaṇa</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.57–58:2)

children.text:
tato rasalepānantaraṃ krāmaṇayogena kunaṭīmākṣikaviṣam ityādinoktena
                                vilipya tulyādhaḥ tulyaṃ yathā syāttathā adhobhāge nidhāya mūṣodare
                                dhmātaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_18.57-58:3 //
children.translated_text: Then — after the mercury-coating — having smeared with the <s>krāmaṇa</s> formula stated as '<s>kunaṭī</s>-pyrite-poison' and so forth, with an equal [portion] below — so that it is equal, placed on the lower side — one should smelt inside the crucible. (GRhtCM 18.57–58:3)

children.text:
punaḥ paścāddhemnā kanakena sahitaṃ āvartya dhmātaṃ kuryāt //
                                GRhtCM_18.57-58:4 //
children.translated_text: Again, afterwards, combined with gold — with <s>kanaka</s> — having turned, one should smelt. (GRhtCM 18.57–58:4)

children.text: gold:: production (?)
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Gold — production (?)]

children.text: vakṣyāmi cālepavidhiṃ kramati ca sūto yathā hi patreṣu /
children.translated_text: I shall describe the coating-method (<s>ālepavidhi</s>) — how mercury indeed creeps upon the leaves,

children.text: rañjati yena vidhinā samāsataḥ sūtarājastu // GRht_18.59 //
children.translated_text: and by what method the king of mercury colors — in brief. (GRht 18.59)

children.text: kṛtvālaktakavastraṃ liptamanusnehamupari cūrṇena /
children.translated_text: Having made a lac-dyed cloth, coated with unctuant (<s>sneha</s>) on top, with powder,

children.text: avacūrṇitaṃ tu kṛtvā gandhakaśilayā vidhānena // GRht_18.60 //
children.translated_text: having dusted it, with sulphur and realgar (<s>gandhakaśilā</s>), by the [proper] method. (GRht 18.60)

children.text: tadupari śṛtaṃ ca dattvā gandhakaśilācūrṇaṃ ca sūtavare /
children.translated_text: On top of that, having placed the cooked [substance], and sulphur-realgar powder on the best of mercuries,

children.text: paścādvartiḥ kāryā pātre dhṛtvāyase ca same // GRht_18.61 //
children.translated_text: afterwards, a wick should be made; having placed [it] on an even iron vessel. (GRht 18.61)

children.text: dīpaṃ pratibodhya tatastailaṃ dattvā tataḥ stokam /
children.translated_text: Having lit the lamp, then giving oil, then a little [at a time],

children.text: pākaṃ yāmasyārdhaṃ svāṅge śītaṃ tataḥ kāryam // GRht_18.62 //
children.translated_text: cooking for half a <s>yāma</s> (watch, ~3 hours); then it should be cooled naturally. (GRht 18.62)

children.text: gṛhṇīyādatha sūtakṛṣṭīṃ liptā tatastena /
children.translated_text: One should then collect the mercury-extract; coated with that,

children.text: krāmaṇayogairliptvā puṭitā sā hemni nirdhmātā // GRht_18.63 //
children.translated_text: smeared with <s>krāmaṇa</s> formulas, calcined — that is smelted upon gold. (GRht 18.63)

children.text: taccāha yantramityādi // GRhtCM_18.59-63:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That he states, with 'apparatus' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.59–63:1)

children.text:
vā yantraṃ pañcamṛdā vapmīkamṛt gairikaṃ khaṭikā saindhavaṃ iṣṭikā ceti
                            pañcamṛdaḥ tayā kṛtvā haṇḍyāṃ sthāpyāṃ pakvaṃ kāryam //
                            GRhtCM_18.59-63:2 //
children.translated_text: Or — the apparatus; the five clays (<s>pañcamṛd</s>) are: anthill-earth, ochre (<s>gairika</s>), chalk (<s>khaṭikā</s>), rock-salt (<s>saindhava</s>), and brick (<s>iṣṭikā</s>) — these are the five clays; having made [the apparatus] with these, one should place [it] in a pot and cook. (GRhtCM 18.59–63:2)

children.text: atha puṭapakvaṃ gajapuṭādinā pācyamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.59-63:3 //
children.translated_text: Now, calcined with fire-cakes — should be cooked with elephant-cake (<s>gajapuṭa</s>) and the like, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 18.59–63:3)

children.text:
pepanavidhiṃ vakṣyāmi yathā patreṣu pepaḥ kāryaḥ punar yathā patreṣu
                            kramati svaguṇān prakāśayati punaryena vidhinā rañjanaṃ rāgaṃ dadāti
                            samāsataḥ saṃkṣepataḥ vidhinā vidhānataḥ sūtarāja evaṃvidho bhavet
                            tamupāyaṃ vakṣyāmīti // GRhtCM_18.59-63:4 //
children.translated_text: I shall describe the coating method — how the coating should be done on the leaves; again, how [mercury] creeps on the leaves — manifests its qualities; again, by what method it gives coloring (<s>rañjana</s>) — color — in brief, concisely, by [proper] method, by procedure — the king of mercury would become thus; I shall describe that means. (GRhtCM 18.59–63:4)

children.text:
atha pepakrāmaṇaṃ rañjanavidhānamāha kṛtvāpaktakavastram ityādi //
                            GRhtCM_18.59-63:5 //
children.translated_text: Now he states the coating-creeping-coloring procedure, with 'having made a lac-dyed cloth' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.59–63:5)

children.text:
prathamaṃ āpaktakaṃ vastraṃ apaktena rañjitaṃ yadvastraṃ tad āpaktakaṃ
                            anu paścāt snehaṃ kaṅguṇyādīnāṃ taipaṃ piptaṃ kāryaṃ
                            tattaipapiptavastropari vakṣyamāṇauṣadhānāṃ cūrṇena avacūrṇanaṃ kuryāt
                            taipapiptavastraṃ gandhakaśipayā avacūrṇitaṃ kṛtvā tadupari dātavyaṃ
                            darśayati // GRhtCM_18.59-63:6 //
children.translated_text: First, a lac-dyed cloth — a cloth dyed with lac; after that, unctuant — oil of <s>kaṅguṇī</s> and the like — should be applied; on top of that oil-applied cloth, one should dust with the powder of the medicines to be described. The oil-applied cloth dusted with sulphur and realgar — having prepared [it], on top of that, what is to be given, he shows. (GRhtCM 18.59–63:6)

children.text:
punastadupari gandhakaśipācūrṇopari śṛtaṃ dattvā punargandhakaśipācūrṇaṃ
                            sūtavare sūtarājopari dattvā paścāttatkaraṇānantaraṃ vartiḥ kāryā sā
                            vartir āyase pohamaye same samabhūmau pātre dhṛtvā tatropari kāryā //
                            GRhtCM_18.59-63:7 //
children.translated_text: Again, on top of that — on top of the sulphur-realgar powder — having placed the cooked [substance]; again, having placed sulphur-realgar powder on the best of mercuries — on the king of mercury; afterwards — after that preparation — a wick should be made; that wick, having placed [it] on an even — level-surfaced — iron vessel, should be made on top of it. (GRhtCM 18.59–63:7)

children.text: vidhyantaraṃ darśayati dīpam ityādi // GRhtCM_18.59-63:8 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He shows an alternative method, with 'lamp' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.59–63:8)

children.text:
tato varteḥ pātropari karaṇānantaraṃ dīpaṃ pratibodhya prajvāpya tato
                            vāraṃvāraṃ stokamappaṃ taipaṃ dattvā yāvadyāmasya praharasya ardhaṃ
                            syāttāvatpākaṃ kuryāt iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_18.59-63:9 //
children.translated_text: Then — after the preparation of the wick on the vessel — having lit the lamp — having ignited [it] — then repeatedly, a little — a small [amount] of oil having been given — for as long as half a <s>yāma</s> (watch) — one should cook, is the completion. (GRhtCM 18.59–63:9)

children.text:
tato+anantaraṃ tatpatitaṃ taipaṃ svāṅgaśītaṃ kāryaṃ aṅge taipadravarūpe
                            śarīre yathāsvaṃ svayameva śītaṃ yathā syāttathā kāryam //
                            GRhtCM_18.59-63:10 //
children.translated_text: Then — afterwards — that fallen oil should be cooled naturally — in its own body, meaning in the oil-liquid form, it should be allowed to cool on its own — thus it should be done. (GRhtCM 18.59–63:10)

children.text: taccāha gṛhṇīyād ityādi // GRhtCM_18.59-63:11 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That he states, with 'one should collect' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.59–63:11)

children.text: atha śītakaraṇānantaram // GRhtCM_18.59-63:12 //
children.translated_text: Now, after the cooling — (GRhtCM 18.59–63:12)

children.text: sūtakṛṣṭīṃ ca gṛhṇīyāt karmavit iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_18.59-63:13 //
children.translated_text: one should collect the mercury-extract — one who knows the procedure, is the completion. (GRhtCM 18.59–63:13)

children.text:
tato+anantaraṃ sā sūtakṛṣṭī tena patreṇa piptā satī krāmaṇayogair piptvā
                            hemni suvarṇe nirdhmātā kāryeti // GRhtCM_18.59-63:14 //
children.translated_text: Then — that mercury-extract, coated with that leaf, smeared with <s>krāmaṇa</s> formulas, should be smelted upon gold — upon <s>suvarṇa</s> — thus it should be done. (GRhtCM 18.59–63:14)

children.text: gold:: production
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: Gold — production]

children.text: athavā daradaśilālair gandhakamākṣīkapakvamṛtanāgaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, with cinnabar (<s>darada</s>), realgar (<s>śilā</s>), and alum (<s>āla</s>); with sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>) and pyrite (<s>mākṣika</s>), cooked, with killed lead (<s>mṛtanāga</s>);

children.text: kaṃkuṣṭhapravālasahitaiḥ piṣṭaiśca kaṅguṇītaile // GRht_18.64 //
children.translated_text: accompanied by <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> (orchid) and coral (<s>pravāla</s>), ground in <s>kaṅguṇī</s> (Celastrus) oil. (GRht 18.64)

children.text: madhye sūto yukto mṛditaḥ khalve tathāyase vidhinā /
children.translated_text: Mercury, combined in the middle [of these], ground in an iron mortar, by the [proper] method;

children.text: saṃsvedya vaṃśanalikāṃ dolāyantreṇa sveditaṃ tridinam // GRht_18.65 //
children.translated_text: having heated [it] in a bamboo tube (<s>vaṃśanalikā</s>), steamed with a swing-apparatus (<s>dolāyantra</s>) for three days. (GRht 18.65)

children.text: etairliptvā kṛṣṇaiḥ patraṃ pūrvoktavidhānena /
children.translated_text: Having smeared [the leaves] with these black [substances], the leaf, according to the previously stated method;

children.text: nāgaṃ dattvā prakaṭaṃ stokaṃ stokaṃ krameṇaiva // GRht_18.66 //
children.translated_text: having given lead (<s>nāga</s>) openly, little by little, in sequence — (GRht 18.66)

children.text: bhavati hi kanakaṃ divyamakṣīṇaṃ devayogyaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: it becomes divine gold, imperishable, worthy of the gods;

children.text: evaṃ jāritasūte sakalāḥ khalu haṇḍikāḥ sarvāḥ // GRht_18.67 //
children.translated_text: thus, when mercury is [so] digested, all the pots (<s>haṇḍikā</s>) indeed [yield gold]. (GRht 18.67)

children.text: vidhyantaramāha athavetyādi // GRhtCM_18.64-67:1 //
