children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another method, with 'alternatively' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.64–67:1)

<s>Darada</s> is cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>); <s>śilā</s> is realgar (<s>manaḥśilā</s>); <s>āla</s> is orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>); with those — and sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), well-known; <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), which is cooked, meaning rendered into red lead (<s>sindūra</s>); and killed lead — with those. (GRhtCM 18.64–67:2)

children.text:
punaḥ kaṅkuṣṭhapravāpasahitaiḥ kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ viraṅgaṃ pravāpaṃ vidrumaṃ
                            tābhyāṃ sahitaiḥ // GRhtCM_18.64-67:3 //
children.translated_text: Again, accompanied by <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> and coral — <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is <s>viraṅga</s> (orchid resin); <s>pravāla</s> is coral (<s>vidruma</s>) — accompanied by these two. (GRhtCM 18.64–67:3)

children.text:
punaretaiḥ kaṅguṇītaipe jyotiṣmatītaipe piṣṭaiś cūrṇīkṛtaiḥ madhye sūto
                            yuktaḥ kārya ityagrimaśpokasaṃbandhāt // GRhtCM_18.64-67:4 //
children.translated_text: Again, with these, in <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil — <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> oil — ground into powder, mercury should be combined in the middle — this is the connection with the following verse. (GRhtCM 18.64–67:4)

children.text: taccāha madhye ityādi // GRhtCM_18.64-67:5 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That he states, with 'in the middle' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.64–67:5)

children.text:
pūrvoktairauṣadhaiḥ kṛtvā madhye auṣadhāntaḥ sūto yuktaḥ kāryaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_18.64-67:6 //
children.translated_text: Having prepared with the aforementioned drugs, the mercury should be placed within the drugs, in the middle. (GRhtCM 18.64-67:6)

children.text:
punarmardayitvā vaṃśanapikāṃ riktodarāṃ prati saṃvedya dinatrayaṃ
                            dopāyantreṇa sveditaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.64-67:7 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, having ground [it], one should convey [it] into an empty bamboo tube and steam it for three days by the <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing-steaming apparatus), is the meaning. (GRhtCM 18.64-67:7)

children.text: taccāha piptvetyādi // GRhtCM_18.64-67:8 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that, with 'having smeared' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.64-67:8)

children.text:
etāni sveditauṣadhāni saṃyuktāni taiḥ kṛṣṇaiḥ kṛṣṇapavaṇaiḥ
                            pūrvoktavidhānena sūtakṛṣṭīvidhānena patraṃ piptvā punaḥ prakaṭaṃ yathā
                            syāt tathā stokaṃ appamappaṃ krameṇa nāgaṃ dattvā kanakaṃ jāyate
                            ityagrimaśpokasaṃbandhaḥ // GRhtCM_18.64-67:9 //
children.translated_text: These steaming-drugs, combined with those black [salts] — black salts — by the previously described method of mercury-extraction (<s>sūtakṛṣṭi</s>), having smeared a foil, then, so that it becomes manifest, gradually — little by little — having added lead, gold is produced — from the connection with the following verse. (GRhtCM 18.64-67:9)

children.text:
evaṃ kṛte sati akṣīṇaṃ akṣayaṃ divyaṃ pravaraṃ devayogyaṃ devā
                            indrādayastadyogyaṃ kanakaṃ bhavati // GRhtCM_18.64-67:10 //
children.translated_text: When done thus, imperishable — undecaying — divine, excellent, fit for the gods — the gods being <s>Indra</s> and others — gold fit for them is produced. (GRhtCM 18.64-67:10)

children.text: yukto+ayamarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.64-67:11 //
children.translated_text: This meaning is appropriate. (GRhtCM 18.64-67:11)

children.text:
evaṃ jāritasūte jāritakarmakṛte rase khapu niścitaṃ sarvā haṇḍikāḥ sarve
                            dhātvādyāḥ sakapāḥ saprasavāḥ syurityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.64-67:12 //
children.translated_text: Thus, when mercury has been digested — when the digestion-operation has been performed on the mercury — certainly all the vessels (<s>haṇḍikā</s>) — all the metals and such — become complete, with full progeny, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 18.64-67:12)

children.text: relation between bīja and gold (?)
children.translated_text: [Section:] Relation between seed and gold (?)

children.text: nirbījaṃ samajīrṇe pādaikenaiva ṣoḍaśāṃśena /
children.translated_text: Seed-free — when equally digested, by one-quarter alone, by one-sixteenth;

children.text: ardhena pādayogaṃ pādenaikena tulyakanakaṃ ca // GRht_18.68 //
children.translated_text: by half, a quarter-conjunction; by one [whole part], equal gold. (GRht 18.68)

children.text: viśeṣamāha nirbījamityādi // GRhtCM_18.68:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the distinction, with 'seed-free' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.68:1)

children.text:
nirbījaṃ yathā syāttathā samajīrṇaṃ pādena turyāṃśena phapaṃ dadāti tathā
                            ardhena jīrṇena ṣoḍaśāṃśena phapaṃ dadāti ca punastadardhena jīrṇena
                            tatpādayogaṃ tatpādena ekena tatpādayogaṃ phapaṃ dadātīti sarvatra
                            vācyam // GRhtCM_18.68:2 //
children.translated_text: So that it be seed-free — when equally digested, by a quarter — a fourth part — it gives the result; likewise, when digested by half, by one-sixteenth it gives the result; and furthermore, when digested by half of that, by its quarter-conjunction — by one [part] of its quarter — it gives the result — this should be stated throughout. (GRhtCM 18.68:2)

children.text: tupyakanakaṃ ca jīrṇaṃ pūrṇaṃ phapaṃ dadātīti // GRhtCM_18.68:3 //
children.translated_text: And when digested as equal gold — fully digested — it gives the complete result. (GRhtCM 18.68:3)

children.text: tārākṛṣṭi
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>tārākṛṣṭi</s> (silver-extraction/transmutation)

children.text: tārākṛṣṭiṃ vakṣye mṛtavaṅgaṃ tālakena tulyāṃśam /
children.translated_text: I shall describe <s>tārākṛṣṭi</s> (silver-extraction): killed tin, in equal parts with orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>),

children.text: lambitamatha nirdhmātaṃ tāmraṃ tārachaviṃ vahati // GRht_18.69 //
children.translated_text: hung [in a crucible] and then blown — copper acquires the luster of silver. (GRht 18.69)

children.text:
hemākṛṣṭyanantaraṃ tārākṛṣṭiṃ vakṣye ahaṃ kaviḥ kathayāmi mṛtavaṅgaṃ
                            māritaṃ vaṅgaṃ tāpakena haritāpeneti // GRhtCM_18.69:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] After gold-extraction, 'I shall describe <s>tārākṛṣṭi</s>' — I, the author, state [the following]: killed tin — calcined tin — with orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>/haritāla). (GRhtCM 18.69:1)

children.text:
atha tāmraṃ tupyāṃśaṃ pambitaṃ vistīrṇaṃ yathā syāt tathā nirdhmātaṃ sat
                            tārachaviṃ vahati rūpyadyutiṃ prāpnotītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.69:2 //
children.translated_text: Then copper, in equal parts, having been spread out — made flat — when blown, acquires the luster of silver — attains the brilliance of silver, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 18.69:2)

children.text: paścānnāgaṃ deyaṃ prakāśamūṣāsu nirmalaṃ yāvat /
children.translated_text: Afterwards, lead should be added; in open crucibles, until [it becomes] pure;

children.text: tāvad dhmātaṃ vidhinā sunirmalaṃ nistaraṅgaṃ tu // GRht_18.70 //
children.translated_text: it should be blown by the [proper] method until it is very pure and wave-free. (GRht 18.70)

children.text: taccāha paścādityādi // GRhtCM_18.70:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that, with 'afterwards' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.70:1)

children.text:
paścādvaṅgatāmrayogānantaraṃ prakāśamūṣāsu yāvat nirmapaṃ mapavarjitaṃ
                            syāttāvannāgaṃ deyaṃ punaryāvannirmapam ujjvapaṃ nistaraṅgaṃ
                            nāgormivarjitaṃ syāt tāvadvidhinā dhmātaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_18.70:2 //
children.translated_text: Afterwards — after the tin-copper combination — in open crucibles, lead should be added until it becomes pure — free of impurity; furthermore, it should be blown by the [proper] method until it is pure, bright, and wave-free — devoid of lead-waves, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 18.70:2)
[Unclear passage]

children.text: tālaśilāsarjikābhiḥ saindhavalavaṇena nayanahitasahitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With orpiment, realgar, and <s>sarjikā</s> (soda), together with rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>) and eye-beneficial [substances] —

children.text: ekaikaṃ sahitaṃ vā vedhaṃ dattvā punaḥ śulbe // GRht_18.71 //
children.translated_text: each one separately or all combined — having given <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) again into copper — (GRht 18.71)

children.text: chagaṇaṃ māhiṣatakraṃ snuhīkṣīreṇa sarpiṣā kramaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Goat-dung, buffalo buttermilk, <s>snuhī</s> (Euphorbia) milk, and ghee, in succession;

children.text: saguḍadugdhamadhuvimiśraiḥ kramaśo vedhe niṣekaśca // GRht_18.72 //
children.translated_text: mixed with jaggery, milk, and honey — quenching in succession during <s>vedha</s> (transmutation). (GRht 18.72)

children.text: viśeṣamāha tāpetyādi // GRhtCM_18.71-72:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the distinction, with 'orpiment' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.71-72:1)

children.text:
tāpaṃ haritāpaṃ śipā manohvā sarjikā pratītā tābhiḥ saindhavaṃ ca tat
                            pavaṇaṃ ca tena nayanahitasahitaiḥ etaiḥ kṛtvā ekaikaṃ pṛthaktvena vā
                            sahitam ekatvena punaḥ śupve tāmre vedhaṃ pratidadhyāditi //
                            GRhtCM_18.71-72:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Tāla</s> means orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>); <s>śilā</s> is realgar (<s>manohvā</s>); <s>sarjikā</s> is well-known — with these, and <s>saindhava</s> — that salt — together with eye-beneficial [substances]; with these, [applied] each separately, or combined as one; furthermore, one should administer <s>vedha</s> (transmutation) into copper (<s>śulva</s>/tāmra). (GRhtCM 18.71-72:2)

children.text: tāravedhaniṣekānyāha chagaṇam ityādi // GRhtCM_18.71-72:3 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the quenching for silver-transmutation, with 'goat-dung' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.71-72:3)

children.text:
chagaṇaṃ vanotpannaṃ māhiṣaṃ takraṃ mahiṣyāḥ idaṃ māhiṣaṃ snuhikṣīreṇa
                            sehuṇḍadugdhena saha punaḥ sarpiṣā ghṛtena saha guḍadugdhamadhubhir
                            miśraiḥ mipitaṃ kṛtvā kramaśo vedhakarmaṇi niṣekaḥ kāryaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_18.71-72:4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Chagaṇa</s> means forest-produced [goat-dung]; <s>māhiṣa takra</s> means buffalo buttermilk — that of a she-buffalo, hence <s>māhiṣa</s>; with <s>snuhī</s>-milk — <s>sehuṇḍa</s> (Euphorbia) milk; furthermore, with ghee (<s>sarpiṣ</s>/ghṛta); mixed with jaggery, milk, and honey — having combined [them]; in the transmutation operation, quenching should be done in succession. (GRhtCM 18.71-72:4)

children.text: tārakṛṣṭī; copper => silver
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>tārākṛṣṭi</s>: copper → silver

children.text: kāñcī brāhmī kuṭilaṃ tālakaṃ samabhāgayojitaṃ dhmātam /
children.translated_text: <s>Kāñcī</s> (gold-pyrite), <s>brāhmī</s> (<s>somāhvā</s>), <s>kuṭila</s> (lead), and orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>), combined in equal parts, [when] blown —

children.text: śulbaṃ viddhamanena tu tārākṛṣṭirbhaveddivyā // GRht_18.73 //
children.translated_text: copper transmuted with this produces divine <s>tārākṛṣṭi</s> (silver). (GRht 18.73)

children.text: tārākṛṣṭimāha kāñcītyādi // GRhtCM_18.73:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the silver-extraction, with '<s>kāñcī</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.73:1)

children.text:
kāñcī svarṇamākṣikaṃ brāhmī somāhvā kuṭipaṃ sīsaṃ tāpakaṃ pratītaṃ
                            etatsamayojitaṃ samāṃśamepitaṃ sat dhmātaṃ kuryāt punaranena
                            kāñcyādigaṇena viddhaṃ śupbaṃ divyā manoramā tārākṛṣṭirbhavet //
                            GRhtCM_18.73:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kāñcī</s> is gold-pyrite (<s>svarṇamākṣika</s>); <s>brāhmī</s> is <s>somāhvā</s>; <s>kuṭila</s> is lead (<s>sīsa</s>); <s>tālaka</s> is well-known — these, combined in equal parts — mixed in equal measures — should be blown; furthermore, copper transmuted with this — the <s>kāñcī</s>-group — produces divine — beautiful — silver-extraction (<s>tārākṛṣṭi</s>). (GRhtCM 18.73:2)

children.text: silver:: optimization
children.translated_text: [Section on] silver: optimization

children.text: evaṃ tārākṛṣṭirliptvā viddhā rasena sāritena /
children.translated_text: Thus, [copper given] silver-extraction, smeared and transmuted with liquefied mercury —

children.text: tāraṃ karoti vimalaṃ lepaṃ vā pādajīrṇādi // GRht_18.74 //
children.translated_text: produces pure silver; or [with] a quarter-digestion-coating and so forth. (GRht 18.74)

children.text: iti miśrīkṛtaviddhaṃ kramitaṃ tvatha mātṛkātulyam /
children.translated_text: Thus, what is mixed and transmuted, when activated — becomes equal to the mother [metal];

children.text: tāradalaṃ bhavati chedanatāḍananikaṣaiśca nirdoṣam // GRht_18.75 //
children.translated_text: a silver-foil results, faultless under cutting, hammering, and touchstone [tests]. (GRht 18.75)

children.text: tārākṛṣṭimāha evamityādi // GRhtCM_18.74-75:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the silver-extraction, with 'thus' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.74-75:1)

children.text:
evaṃ uktavidhānena sāritena sāraṇākarmakṛtena piptvā viddhā satī
                            tārākṛṣṭirbhavet // GRhtCM_18.74-75:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus — by the stated method — having smeared and transmuted with liquefied — i.e., mercury that has undergone the liquefaction operation — silver-extraction results. (GRhtCM 18.74-75:2)

children.text:
punariyaṃ tārākṛṣṭiḥ tāraṃ vimapaṃ mapavarjitaṃ karoti vā pādajīrṇādi
                            pādena jīrṇaṃ yasmin ādiśabdād ardhasamagrahaṇaṃ kāryaṃ tat pepamiti //
                            GRhtCM_18.74-75:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, this silver-extraction produces pure silver — free of impurity; or by quarter-digestion and so forth — 'digested by a quarter' — from the word 'ādi,' half and full should also be understood — that [determines] the coating. (GRhtCM 18.74-75:3)

children.text: viśeṣamāha itītyādi // GRhtCM_18.74-75:4 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the distinction, with 'thus' and so forth. (GRhtCM 18.74-75:4)

children.text:
iti pūrvoktavidhānena miśrīkṛtaṃ mipitaṃ viddhaṃ kramitaṃ mātṛkātupyaṃ
                            samāṃśaṃ sat tāradapaṃ rūpyapatraṃ bhavati tadrūpyadapaṃ
                            chedanatāḍananikaṣaiḥ chedanaṃ khaṇḍanaṃ tāḍanaṃ ghanaghātaḥ nikaṣaṃ
                            śipopari parīkṣaṇaṃ tairiti tāpaiśca nirdoṣaṃ tadbhavati //
                            GRhtCM_18.74-75:5 //
children.translated_text: Thus — by the previously stated method — [that which is] mixed, i.e., combined, and transmuted, [when] activated — [becomes] equal to the mother [metal], i.e., in equal measure — a silver foil — a silver leaf — results. That silver foil [is tested] by cutting — severing, hammering — striking with a hammer, and touchstone — testing on a stone — by those tests it is faultless. (GRhtCM 18.74-75:5)

children.text: evaṃ vedhavidhānaṃ śāstravidhijñena karmakuśalena /
children.translated_text: Thus, the <s>vedha</s>-procedure (transmutation method) should be performed by one who knows the rules of the <s>śāstra</s>, who is skilled in operations,

children.text: jñātvā gurūpadeśaṃ kartavyaṃ karmanipuṇena // GRht_18.76 //
children.translated_text: having known the guru's instruction — [it should be done] by one proficient in the work. (GRht 18.76)

children.text:
evaṃ amunā prakāreṇa śāstravidhijñena śāstrasya vidhiṃ jānātīti saḥ tena
                            karmanipuṇena saṃskārapravīṇena kuśapena kartrā gurūpadeśaṃ
                            gururuktapakṣaṇo granthādau tasya upadeśaṃ jñātvā vedhavidhānaṃ
                            kartavyam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_18.76:1 //
children.translated_text: Thus — in this manner — by one who knows the rules of the <s>śāstra</s> — who knows the method of the <s>śāstra</s>, hence 'he'; by one proficient in the work — skilled in processes — as the doer; having known the guru's instruction — the guru described at the beginning of the text, his instruction — having understood [it], the transmutation procedure should be performed, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 18.76:1)

children.text: iti rasarājasya vidhau vedhavidhānaṃ prasaṃgataḥ proktam /
children.translated_text: Thus, in the procedure of the king of mercury (<s>rasarāja</s>), the transmutation procedure has been stated incidentally;

children.text: adhunā proktānapi vakṣyāmi rasāyane yogān // GRht_19.1 //
children.translated_text: now I shall also describe formulations for <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) that have been stated [by predecessors]. (GRht 19.1)

children.text: atha bhakṣaṇavidhānamāha itītyādi // GRhtCM_19.1:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now he states the method of internal consumption, with 'thus' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.1:1)

children.text:
rasarājasya vidhau rasendrakarmavidhāne vedhavidhānaṃ prasaṅgataḥ
                            prastāvataḥ proktaṃ na tu svaprajñāsamam // GRhtCM_19.1:2 //
children.translated_text: In the procedure of the king of mercury — in the operational method of <s>rasendra</s> — the transmutation procedure has been stated incidentally — by way of context, not as [derived from] one's own intelligence alone. (GRhtCM 19.1:2)

Now — [the formulations] that have been stated and also experienced — from the word 'api'; for <s>rasāyana</s> — for the method of destroying old age and disease — the formulations — assemblages of substances — I shall describe — I shall state, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.1:3)

children.text: kṣetrīkaraṇa (śarīraśodhana)
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s> (body-purification/field-preparation)

children.text: ādau prātaḥ prātaḥ saindhavayuktaṃ ghṛtaṃ pibettridinam /
children.translated_text: First, every morning, one should drink ghee mixed with rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>) for three days;

children.text: tadanu kvāthaṃ tridinaṃ yuñjīyāt ketakītanujam // GRht_19.2 //
children.translated_text: thereafter, one should take a decoction — of the offspring of <s>ketakī</s> (Pandanus) — for three days. (GRht 19.2)

children.text: vidhinā svedyo dehaḥ kartavyo vārtikendreṇa /
children.translated_text: The body should be steamed by the method, by the master of the tradition (<s>vārtikendra</s>);

children.text: kvathitaṃ kaṭurohiṇyāḥ saṃśodhanam anuprayuñjīta // GRht_19.3 //
children.translated_text: one should administer a decoction of <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s> (Picrorhiza) as purification. (GRht 19.3)

children.text: tadanu ca śuddhādūrdhvaṃ śleṣmānte recite sakalam /
children.translated_text: Then, after purification from above, when all phlegm has been expelled,

children.text: yāvakapathyaṃ tridinaṃ ghṛtasahitaṃ tatprayuñjīta // GRht_19.4 //
children.translated_text: one should take barley-gruel with <s>pathyā</s> (Terminalia chebula), mixed with ghee, for three days. (GRht 19.4)

children.text: kāyaśodhanamāha ādāvityādi // GRhtCM_19.2-4:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the body-purification, with 'first' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.2-4:1)

children.text:
prathamaṃ prātaḥ prātaḥ pratyūṣe tridinaṃ saindhavamipitaṃ ghṛtam ājyaṃ
                            pibet // GRhtCM_19.2-4:2 //
children.translated_text: First — every morning, at dawn — for three days, one should drink ghee (<s>ājya</s>) mixed with rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>). (GRhtCM 19.2-4:2)

children.text:
anyasaṃyogamāha tadanu ghṛtasaindhavānantaraṃ ketakītanujaṃ kvāthaṃ
                            ketakyāḥ tanuḥ śarīraṃ tasmājjātaṃ ketakīmūpasaṃbhavam ityarthaḥ
                            aṅge'pyanukte vihitaṃ tu mūpaṃ iti nyāyāt tridinaṃ prayuñjīyādityarthaḥ
                            // GRhtCM_19.2-4:3 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the [next] combination, with 'thereafter': after ghee and rock salt, the decoction of the offspring of <s>ketakī</s> — the body of <s>ketakī</s> being the plant, what is born from it — meaning derived from the root of <s>ketakī</s>, is the meaning; by the maxim 'when a part is not specified, the root is intended,' one should take [it] for three days, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.2-4:3)

children.text: vidhyantaram āha vidhinetyādi // GRhtCM_19.2-4:4 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states an alternative method, with 'by the method' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.2-4:4)

children.text:
tato vidhinā svedavidhānena dehaḥ śarīraṃ vārtikendreṇa
                            rasasaṃpradāyavidā svedyaḥ svinnaḥ kartavyaḥ // GRhtCM_19.2-4:5 //
children.translated_text: Then, by the method — by the steaming procedure — the body should be steamed — made to perspire — by the master of the tradition — one who knows the mercury-tradition (<s>rasasaṃpradāya</s>). (GRhtCM 19.2-4:5)

children.text:
anyatkiṃ kaṭurohiṇyāḥ tiktāyāḥ kvathitaṃ prasādhitaṃ samyak śuddhikaraṇaṃ
                            anuprayuñjīta svedānantaram ityabhiprāyaḥ // GRhtCM_19.2-4:6 //
children.translated_text: What else? The decoction — the prepared [extract] — of <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s> (the bitter one/<s>tiktā</s>) should be properly administered as purification — after the steaming, is the intended meaning. (GRhtCM 19.2-4:6)

children.text: vidhyantaramāha tad ityādi // GRhtCM_19.2-4:7 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states an alternative method, with 'thereafter' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.2-4:7)

children.text:
tadanu kaṭukarohiṇīsevanānantaraṃ śuddhād ūrdhvaṃ yathā syāt tathā
                            śpeṣmāntarecite sati yathā śpeṣmaṇo+antaḥ syāttathā recite sati
                            tridinaparimāṇaṃ yāvakapathyaṃ ghṛtasahitaṃ prayuñjīteti //
                            GRhtCM_19.2-4:8 //
children.translated_text: Thereafter — after taking <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s> — after purification from above, so that it be [complete]; when all phlegm has been expelled at its end — when phlegm has been fully discharged — for the duration of three days, one should take barley-gruel with <s>pathyā</s> (Terminalia chebula), mixed with ghee. (GRhtCM 19.2-4:8)

children.text: punarapi ca pānayogaṃ vakṣyāmi ca sakalabhuvanahitakṛtaye /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, I shall also describe a drinking formulation, for the benefit of all the worlds;

children.text: pītvā prathame yāme coṣṇodakasamamidaṃ cūrṇam // GRht_19.5 //
children.translated_text: having drunk [it] in the first watch [of the day], this powder [should be taken] with warm water. (GRht 19.5)

children.text: pathyāsaindhavadhātrīmaricavacāguḍaviḍaṅgarajanīnām /
children.translated_text: Of <s>pathyā</s> (Terminalia chebula), rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>), <s>dhātrī</s> (Emblica), pepper (<s>marica</s>), <s>vacā</s> (Acorus), jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>), <s>viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia), and <s>rajanī</s> (turmeric) —

children.text: śuṇṭhīpippalyor api cūrṇaṃ tridinaṃ prayuñjīta // GRht_19.6 //
children.translated_text: and also of <s>śuṇṭhī</s> (dry ginger) and <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper) — the powder should be taken for three days. (GRht 19.6)

children.text: amunā śuddhaśarīraḥ parihatasaṃsargadoṣabalī /
children.translated_text: By this [method], the body becomes purified, freed from the fault of [bad] associations, and strong;

children.text: pītvā payasā sahitaṃ yāvakamamunā bhavecchuddhaḥ // GRht_19.7 //
children.translated_text: having drunk barley-gruel with milk, by this [method] one becomes purified. (GRht 19.7)

children.text: vidhyantaramāha punarapītyādi // GRhtCM_19.5-7:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states an alternative method, with 'furthermore' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.5-7:1)

children.text:
punarapīti yāvakapathyayogānantaraṃ ca punaḥ pānayogaṃ vakṣyāmi kimarthaṃ
                            sakapabhuvanahitakṛtaye samastasaṃsārahitakaraṇāya idaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ
                            cūrṇaṃ pathyādyaṃ uṣṇodakasamaṃ taptajapena saha prathamayāme
                            prathamapraharāntaḥ pītvā śuddhaśarīro bhaved ityāgāmiśpokasaṃbandhāt //
                            GRhtCM_19.5-7:2 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, 'again' means after the barley-water and <s>pathyā</s> (Terminalia chebula) conjunction, he will describe the drinking-conjunction. For what purpose? For the welfare of all the worlds — for bringing benefit to the entire worldly existence. This powder to be described, consisting of <s>pathyā</s> and the like, equal to hot water — together with heated water — having drunk it in the first watch — within the first <s>prahara</s> (three-hour period) — one would become purified in body; from the connection with the following verse. (GRhtCM 19.5–7:2)

children.text: śodhanāya cūrṇamāha pathyetyādi // GRhtCM_19.5-7:3 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the powder for purification, beginning with '<s>pathyā</s>' and so on. (GRhtCM 19.5–7:3)

children.text:
pathyā harītakī saindhavaṃ pratītaṃ dhātrī āmapakaṃ marīcam ūṣaṇaṃ vacā
                            ugragandhā guḍaḥ pratītaḥ viḍaṅgaṃ kṛmighnaṃ rajanī haridrā
                            śuṇṭhīpippapyor apīti śuṇṭhī nāgaraṃ pippapī māgadhī āsāṃ auṣadhīnāṃ
                            cūrṇaṃ tridinaṃ prayuñjīta // GRhtCM_19.5-7:4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Pathyā</s> is <s>harītakī</s> (Terminalia chebula); <s>saindhava</s> (rock salt) is well-known; <s>dhātrī</s> is <s>āmalaka</s> (Indian gooseberry); <s>marīca</s> is black pepper (<s>ūṣaṇa</s>); <s>vacā</s> is <s>ugragandhā</s> (sweet flag); <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) is well-known; <s>viḍaṅga</s> is the worm-destroying [herb] (Embelia ribes); <s>rajanī</s> is turmeric (<s>haridrā</s>); '<s>śuṇṭhī</s> and <s>pippalī</s> also' — <s>śuṇṭhī</s> is dry ginger (<s>nāgara</s>), <s>pippalī</s> is long pepper (<s>māgadhī</s>) — the powder of these herbs should be employed for three days. (GRhtCM 19.5–7:4)

children.text: uṣṇajapasamamiti jñeyam // GRhtCM_19.5-7:5 //
children.translated_text: It should be known [to be taken] with hot water in equal [measure]. (GRhtCM 19.5–7:5)

children.text: amunetyādi /
children.translated_text: 'By this' and so on. (GRhtCM 19.5–7:6 intro)

children.text:
amunā vakṣyamāṇavirecanena yāvakādinā śuddhaśarīraḥ san
                            parihatasaṃsargadoṣabapī bhavati saṃsargeṇa ye doṣāḥ śarīrābhyantarāste
                            saṃsargadoṣāḥ te parihatā jitā yena saḥ parihatasaṃsargadoṣaḥ tena bapī
                            bapayuktaḥ doṣanivṛttau guṇapravṛttir ityavaśyam // GRhtCM_19.5-7:6
                            //
children.translated_text: By this purgative to be described — of the barley-water type and the like — one whose body is purified becomes one whose contact-born defects are overcome — the defects that exist within the body due to contact, these contact-born defects, being overcome — conquered — by that, he becomes strong (<s>balin</s>) — endowed with strength. When defects are removed, the arising of good qualities is inevitable. (GRhtCM 19.5–7:6)

children.text:
kiṃ kṛtvā parihatadoṣaḥ amunā payasā uṣṇodakena yāvakaṃ apaktaṃ pītvā
                            śuddho bhavedityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.5-7:7 //
children.translated_text: Having done what to overcome the defects? By this liquid — by hot water — having drunk barley-water (<s>yāvaka</s>), the uncooked [preparation], one becomes purified; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.5–7:7)

children.text: akṛtakṣetrīkaraṇe rasāyanaṃ yo naraḥ prayuñjīta /
children.translated_text: One who employs <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation therapy) without having first prepared the body (<s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s>) —

children.text: tasya krāmati na rasaḥ sa rasaḥ sarvāṅgadoṣakṛdbhavati // GRht_19.8 //
children.translated_text: in him, mercury does not permeate; that mercury becomes a cause of defects in all the limbs. (GRht 19.8)

children.text: saṃśodhanasyākaraṇe doṣamāha akṛtetyādi // GRhtCM_19.8:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the fault of not performing purification, beginning with 'not having prepared' and so on. (GRhtCM 19.8:1)

children.text:
yo naraḥ pumān akṛtakṣetrīkaraṇe dehe iti śeṣaḥ na kṛtaṃ akṛtaṃ
                            kṣetrīkaraṇaṃ yasmin tasminsati rasāyanaṃ jarāvyādhivināśanauṣadhaṃ
                            prayuñjīta tasya puṃso raso na krāmati svaguṇānna prakāśayati tarhi kiṃ
                            sarvāṅgadoṣakṛdbhavati bāhucaraṇādiṣu ṣaṭsvaṅgeṣu vikārakṛt syāt //
                            GRhtCM_19.8:2 //
children.translated_text: The person who, without body-preparation (<s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s>) — 'in the body' is to be supplied — [where] the preparation has not been done, employs <s>rasāyana</s> — medicine that destroys old age and disease — in him, mercury does not permeate — does not manifest its own qualities. What then? It becomes a cause of defects in all the limbs — it produces disorders in the six limbs such as arms, legs, and the like. (GRhtCM 19.8:2)

children.text: iti śuddho jātabalaḥ śālyodanayāvakākhyamudgarasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus purified, with strength arisen, [consuming] rice-gruel (<s>śālyodana</s>), barley-water (<s>yāvaka</s>), and <s>mudga</s> (mung bean) broth —

children.text: kṣetrīkṛtanijadehaḥ kurvīta rasāyanaṃ vidhivat // GRht_19.9 //
children.translated_text: one whose own body has been prepared (<s>kṣetrīkṛta</s>) should perform <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) according to the proper method. (GRht 19.9)

children.text: rasāyanādhikāratvam āha itītyādi // GRhtCM_19.9:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the eligibility for <s>rasāyana</s>, beginning with 'thus' and so on. (GRhtCM 19.9:1)

children.text:
pūrvoktavidhānena śuddhaḥ san yo jātabapo bhavati sa kṣetrīkṛtanijadehaḥ
                            akṣetraṃ kṣetraṃ kriyata iti kṣetrīkṛto nijadehaḥ śarīraṃ yena saḥ
                            matimān rasāyanaṃ vidhivatprakurvīta // GRhtCM_19.9:2 //
children.translated_text: One who, by the previously stated procedure, being purified and having attained strength, whose own body has been prepared — 'the unprepared is made prepared,' thus '<s>kṣetrīkṛta</s>' means one whose own body has been [so] prepared — such a wise one should properly perform <s>rasāyana</s>. (GRhtCM 19.9:2)

children.text:
kaiḥ jātabapaḥ śāpyodanaṃ ca yāvakākhyaṃ ca mudgāśca taiḥ //
                            GRhtCM_19.9:3 //
children.translated_text: Through what does strength arise? Through rice-gruel (<s>śālyodana</s>), barley-water (<s>yāvaka</s>), and mung beans (<s>mudga</s>). (GRhtCM 19.9:3)

children.text: suratarutailaghṛtamadhudhātrīrasapayāṃsi nirmathya /
children.translated_text: Oil of the celestial tree (<s>surataru</s>, i.e., deodar), ghee, honey, juice of <s>dhātrī</s> (āmalaka), and milk — having churned [these together],

children.text: pītvā viśuddhakoṣṭho bhavati pumānantaritaśuddhaḥ // GRht_19.10 //
children.translated_text: having drunk [them], a person becomes purified in the abdomen — purified internally. (GRht 19.10)

children.text: māsena kāntimedhe dvābhyāṃ praśamayati doṣanikaraṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Within a month, [he attains] beauty and intellect; within two [months], he pacifies the multitude of diseases;

children.text: māsatritayena punaḥ svādamaravapurmahātejāḥ // GRht_19.11 //
children.translated_text: within three months, again, [he attains] a body like that of the immortals (<s>amara</s>), resplendent with great luster. (GRht 19.11)

children.text: vidhyantaramāha suratarvityādi // GRhtCM_19.10-11:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another formulation, beginning with 'celestial tree' and so on. (GRhtCM 19.10–11:1)

children.text:
antaritaśuddhaḥ antaritaṃ śuddhaṃ yasya saḥ grahaṇīrogādivarjita
                            ityarthaḥ etāni auṣadhāni nirmathya pītvā viśuddhakoṣṭho bhavati
                            viśuddhaṃ mapavarjitaṃ koṣṭhaṃ udaraṃ kasyetyevaṃvidho bhavati //
                            GRhtCM_19.10-11:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Purified internally' — one whose internal [constitution] is purified — meaning free from ailments like <s>grahaṇī</s> (digestive disorders) and the like; having churned and drunk these medicines, he becomes purified in the abdomen — the abdomen, meaning the stomach, becomes purified — free from impurities; such he becomes. (GRhtCM 19.10–11:2)

children.text:
tāni kāni suratarutaipetyādīni suratarur devavṛkṣaḥ tattaipapeṣaṇaṃ
                            taipamityarthaḥ ghṛtaṃ ājyaṃ madhu kṣaudraṃ dhātrīrasaḥ āmapakīsapipaṃ
                            payo dugdhaṃ etāni sarvāṇi nirmathya ekīkṛtyetyarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_19.10-11:3 //
children.translated_text: What are those [medicines]? 'Oil of the celestial tree' and so on — <s>surataru</s> is the divine tree (deodar, <s>devavṛkṣa</s>); its oil — meaning that obtained by pressing; ghee (<s>ājya</s>); honey (<s>kṣaudra</s>); juice of <s>dhātrī</s> — the liquid of <s>āmalakī</s> (Indian gooseberry); milk (<s>payas</s>) — all these, having churned — having unified them; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.10–11:3)

children.text:
etadauṣadhabhakṣaṇaguṇaṃ māsakrameṇāha māsenetyādi // GRhtCM_19.10-11:4
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the benefits of consuming this medicine, month by month, beginning with 'within a month' and so on. (GRhtCM 19.10–11:4)

children.text:
asya auṣadhasya māsena māsapramāṇena bhakṣaṇāt kāntir bhavati medhā ceti
                            dvābhyāṃ dvimāsābhyāṃ doṣanikaraṃ gadasamudāyaṃ praśamayati śāntiṃ
                            nayati punarmāsatritayena trimāsapramāṇena svāt svasāmānyaśarīrāt
                            amaravapurdevaśarīro mahātejāḥ dīptimān syādityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_19.10-11:5 //
children.translated_text: By consuming this medicine for a month's duration, beauty (<s>kānti</s>) and intellect (<s>medhā</s>) arise; within two months — by two months' [consumption] — it pacifies the multitude of diseases — the collection of ailments — brings them to cessation; furthermore, within three months — by the measure of three months — [one attains a body] superior to one's ordinary body — a body like that of the gods, resplendent with great luster; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.10–11:5)

children.text: suradārutailamājyaṃ triphalārasasaṃyutaṃ ca samabhāgam /
children.translated_text: Deodar oil (<s>suradāru-taila</s>), ghee, combined with <s>triphalā</s>-juice, in equal parts —

children.text: pītaṃ tat saptāhānnayanavikāraṃ śamaṃ nayati // GRht_19.12 //
children.translated_text: when drunk, within a week, it brings eye-disorders to cessation. (GRht 19.12)

children.text: yogāntaramāha suradārvityādi // GRhtCM_19.12:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another formulation, beginning with 'deodar' and so on. (GRhtCM 19.12:1)

children.text:
suradārutaipaṃ devadārutaipaṃ ājyaṃ ghṛtaṃ triphapārasasaṃyutaṃ
                            triphapāyā rasena draveṇa saṃyutaṃ sahitaṃ ca punaḥ samabhāgaṃ tupyāṃśaṃ
                            tatpītaṃ sat saptāhāt saptadinapramāṇataḥ nayanavikāraṃ netrasaṃbhavaṃ
                            rogaṃ śamaṃ nayati śāntiṃ prāpayati // GRhtCM_19.12:2 //
children.translated_text: Deodar oil — the oil of deodar (<s>devadāru</s>); ghee; combined with <s>triphalā</s>-juice — combined with the liquid of <s>triphalā</s>; and furthermore in equal parts — in equal proportions; when drunk, within a week — within seven days — it brings eye-disorders — diseases born in the eyes — to cessation — to pacification. (GRhtCM 19.12:2)

children.text: suratarutailaṃ saghṛtaṃ pītvā śālyodanaṃ ca sakṣīram /
children.translated_text: Deodar oil (<s>surataru-taila</s>) together with ghee, having drunk [it], and rice-gruel (<s>śālyodana</s>) with milk —

children.text: jīrṇāhāre bhuktvā harati hi sakuṣṭhān pīnasādīṃśca // GRht_19.13 //
children.translated_text: eaten when the previous meal is digested, it indeed removes [diseases] including leprosy (<s>kuṣṭha</s>) and catarrh (<s>pīnasa</s>). (GRht 19.13)

children.text: yogāntaramāha suratarutaipam ityādi // GRhtCM_19.13:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another formulation, beginning with 'deodar oil' and so on. (GRhtCM 19.13:1)

children.text:
devadārutaipaṃ saghṛtaṃ sājyaṃ etadubhayaṃ pītvā sakṣīraṃ śāpyodanaṃ
                            bhuktvā ṣaṣṭikaudanam ityabhiprāyaḥ punarjīrṇāhāre pratidinaṃ
                            dināntavīradvaye veditavyam // GRhtCM_19.13:2 //
children.translated_text: Deodar oil together with ghee — with clarified butter — having drunk both of these; having eaten rice-gruel with milk — meaning <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> (sixty-day ripening) rice-gruel; furthermore, when the previous meal is digested — at the interval of two digestive periods each day; this should be understood. (GRhtCM 19.13:2)

children.text:
ca punaḥ sakuṣṭhān kuṣṭhaiḥ saha vartante evaṃvidhān pīnasādīn rogān
                            harati dūrīkaroti // GRhtCM_19.13:3 //
children.translated_text: And furthermore, [diseases] including leprosy — those accompanied by leprosy and similar [conditions] — [and] catarrh (<s>pīnasa</s>) and other diseases — it removes — eliminates. (GRhtCM 19.13:3)

children.text: ghṛtasahitaḥ pittakṛtāntailayukto vātasaṃbhavān rogān /
children.translated_text: Combined with ghee, it destroys <s>pitta</s>-born [diseases]; combined with oil, it [destroys] <s>vāta</s>-born diseases;

children.text: guḍasahito madhunā vā kaphajān hantyamaradārurasaḥ // GRht_19.14 //
children.translated_text: combined with jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>) or with honey, the deodar juice (<s>amaradāru-rasa</s>) destroys <s>kapha</s>-born [diseases]. (GRht 19.14)

children.text: yogāntaramāha ghṛtasahita ityādi // GRhtCM_19.14:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another formulation, beginning with 'combined with ghee' and so on. (GRhtCM 19.14:1)

children.text:
amaradāruraso devadārujapaṃ ghṛtasahitaṃ ājyamiśritaḥ pittakṛtān rogān
                            harati nāśayati // GRhtCM_19.14:2 //
children.translated_text: The deodar juice (<s>amaradāru-rasa</s>) — the liquid of <s>devadāru</s> — combined with ghee — mixed with clarified butter — destroys <s>pitta</s>-born diseases — eliminates them. (GRhtCM 19.14:2)

children.text:
punastaipayutastaipena miśrito devadārurasaḥ vātasaṃbhavān rogān hanti //
                            GRhtCM_19.14:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, combined with oil — mixed with oil — the deodar juice destroys <s>vāta</s>-born diseases. (GRhtCM 19.14:3)

children.text:
punarguḍasahitaḥ vā madhunā kṣaudreṇa sahito devadārurasaḥ vātasaṃbhavān
                            rogān hanti // GRhtCM_19.14:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, combined with jaggery, or combined with honey (<s>kṣaudra</s>), the deodar juice destroys <s>vāta</s>-born diseases. (GRhtCM 19.14:4)

children.text:
punar guḍasahitaḥ vā madhunā kṣaudreṇa sahito devadārurasaḥ kaphajān
                            rogān hantīti vākyārthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.14:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, combined with jaggery, or combined with honey (<s>kṣaudra</s>), the deodar juice destroys <s>kapha</s>-born diseases; this is the sentence-meaning. (GRhtCM 19.14:5)

children.text: varjitakāṃjikaśākaṃ payasā śālyodanaṃ ca yuñjīta /
children.translated_text: Avoiding sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>) and leafy vegetables (<s>śāka</s>), one should consume rice-gruel with milk;

children.text: dvicatuḥṣaṭpalamānaṃ mātrādhamamadhyamajyeṣṭhāḥ // GRht_19.15 //
children.translated_text: in measures of two, four, or six <s>palas</s> — [these being] the inferior, middling, and superior dosages. (GRht 19.15)

children.text: rasāyane bhojyābhojyamāha varjitetyādi // GRhtCM_19.15:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states what is to be eaten and avoided in <s>rasāyana</s>, beginning with 'avoiding' and so on. (GRhtCM 19.15:1)

'Avoiding sour gruel and vegetables' — [that in which] sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>, i.e., <s>sauvīra</s>) and vegetables (<s>śāka</s>) such as <s>vāstuka</s> (Chenopodium) and the like have been excluded — thus [constituted], one should eat rice-gruel with milk. (GRhtCM 19.15:2)

children.text: punaḥ śāpyodanaṃ kiyanmānaṃ dvicatuḥṣaṭpapamānam // GRhtCM_19.15:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, how much rice-gruel? In the measure of two, four, or six <s>palas</s>. (GRhtCM 19.15:3)

children.text:
atra mātrādhamamadhyamajyeṣṭhā dvicatuḥṣaṭpapapramāṇā
                            adhamamadhyamottamabapeṣu prayojyetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.15:4 //
children.translated_text: Here, the inferior, middling, and superior dosages are in the measures of two, four, and six <s>palas</s> [respectively] — they should be employed according to [the patient's] weak, moderate, or strong constitutions; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.15:4)

children.text: tadanu pātanaśuddhaṃ sūtakam āroṭam aśnīyāt /
children.translated_text: Thereafter, mercury (<s>sūtaka</s>) purified by distillation (<s>pātana</s>), in the <s>āroṭa</s> form, one should consume;

children.text: svedanamūrcchotthāpanapātanarodhāśca niyamaśca // GRht_19.16 //
children.translated_text: sweating (<s>svedana</s>), swooning (<s>mūrcchā</s>), reviving (<s>utthāpana</s>), distillation (<s>pātana</s>), and sealing (<s>rodha</s>) — and the observance (<s>niyama</s>) — (GRht 19.16)

children.text: abhrakasahitaḥ pātyo vidhinā yāvatsthiro bhavati /
children.translated_text: combined with mica (<s>abhraka</s>), it should be distilled by the [proper] method until it becomes stable;

children.text: athavā mākṣikasahitaḥ pātyaḥ sūto vidhānena // GRht_19.17 //
children.translated_text: or alternatively, combined with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), mercury should be distilled by the [proper] procedure. (GRht 19.17)

children.text: ityāroṭaḥ sūtaḥ kṣetrīkaraṇe niyujyate prathamam / GRht_19.18ab
children.translated_text: Thus, mercury in the <s>āroṭa</s> form is first employed in body-preparation (<s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s>). (GRht 19.18ab)

children.text: atha rasayogamāha tadityādi // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now he states the mercury-formulation, beginning with 'thereafter' and so on. (GRhtCM 19.16–18ab:1)

children.text:
tadanu pathyamātropayogānantaraṃ pātanaśuddhaṃ pātanena śuddhaṃ
                                sūtakaṃ āroṭam eva sāmānyam evāśnīyāt bhakṣayet //
                                GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:2 //
children.translated_text: Thereafter — after the employment of <s>pathyā</s> and other [herbs] in proper measure — mercury purified by distillation — purified through the distillation process — in the <s>āroṭa</s> form alone, the ordinary [form], one should consume — should ingest. (GRhtCM 19.16–18ab:2)

children.text:
ca punaḥ svedanamūrchotthāpanarodhāśca svedanaṃ ca mūrchā ca
                                utthāpanaṃ ca pātanāni ca nirodhaśceti dvandvaḥ ete yadyapi santi
                                niyamaśca yadyapyasti tathāpyāroṭaḥ pātanena syād ityarthaḥ //
                                GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:3 //
children.translated_text: And furthermore, sweating, swooning, reviving, distillation, and sealing — sweating and swooning and reviving and distillation and sealing — [this is] a copulative compound. Although these [processes] exist, and although the observance also exists, nevertheless the <s>āroṭa</s> would be [produced] by distillation [alone]; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.16–18ab:3)

children.text: prasaṅgataḥ pātanamāha abhraketyādi // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:4 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Incidentally, he states the distillation, beginning with 'mica' and so on. (GRhtCM 19.16–18ab:4)

children.text:
sūtaḥ abhrakasahitaḥ gaganamilitaḥ san pātyaḥ // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:5
                                //
children.translated_text: Mercury, combined with mica (<s>gagana</s>) — mixed with mica — should be distilled. (GRhtCM 19.16–18ab:5)

children.text: kena vidhānena ḍamarukayantrādinā // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:6 //
children.translated_text: By what method? By the <s>ḍamaruka</s>-apparatus (double-drum apparatus) and such. (GRhtCM 19.16–18ab:6)

children.text: punastāvadyāvatsthiro bhavati // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:7 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, [it should be distilled] until it becomes stable. (GRhtCM 19.16–18ab:7)

children.text:
athavā vidhyantare sūto mākṣikasahitaḥ pātyo vidhānena ayamapi
                                yāvatsthiro bhavati // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:8 //
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, in another method, mercury combined with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite) should be distilled by the [proper] procedure; this too, until it becomes stable. (GRhtCM 19.16–18ab:8)

children.text:
rasāyane sūtasya āroṭādividhānamāha itītyādi // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:9
                                //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the procedure of <s>āroṭa</s> and the like for mercury in <s>rasāyana</s>, beginning with 'thus' and so on. (GRhtCM 19.16–18ab:9)

children.text:
āroṭa iti pūrvoktena pātanakarmaṇā ūrdhvādhastiryagbhavena sādhita
                                āroṭaḥ saḥ prathamaṃ yathā syāttathā rasāyane jarāvyādhināśane
                                niyujyate iti // GRhtCM_19.16-18ab:10 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Āroṭa</s>' — [mercury] prepared by the previously described distillation process, [whether] upward, downward, or sideways — [this is the] <s>āroṭa</s>; that [mercury] should first be employed — in the manner [described] — in <s>rasāyana</s>, i.e., the destruction of old age and disease. (GRhtCM 19.16–18ab:10)

children.text:
athavā kalkayogena rasādisambhūtena raso bhasma kṛtvā //
                                GRhtCM_19.17:1 //
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, by the <s>kalka</s> (paste) conjunction — produced from mercury and the like — mercury should be made into ash (<s>bhasma</s>). (GRhtCM 19.17:1)

children.text: athavā bhasma ca kṛtvā baddho vā kalkayogena // GRht_19.18cd //
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, having made [mercury into] ash, or bound (<s>baddha</s>), by the <s>kalka</s> (paste) conjunction. (GRht 19.18cd)

children.text: mākṣikaśilājatulohacūrṇapathyākṣaviḍaṅgaghṛtamadhubhiḥ /
children.translated_text: with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), mineral pitch (<s>śilājatu</s>), iron powder (<s>lohacūrṇa</s>), <s>pathyā</s> (Terminalia chebula), <s>akṣa</s> (Terminalia bellirica), <s>viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia ribes), ghee, and honey —

children.text: saṃyuktaṃ rasamādau kṣetrīkaraṇāya yuñjīta // GRht_19.19 //
children.translated_text: combined [with these], mercury should first be employed for bodily preparation (<s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s>). (GRht 19.19)

children.text:
dvividhaṃ bhasma ūrdhvagaṃ tapabhasma ca varṇabhedena ṣaḍvidhaṃ śvetaṃ
                            bhasma pītaṃ bhasma haritaṃ bhasma raktaṃ bhasma kṛṣṇaṃ bhasma karburaṃ
                            bhasma iti ṣaḍvidhaṃ tatkṛtvā kṣetrīkaraṇe niyujyate prathamam //
                            GRhtCM_19.18cd-19:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The ash is of two kinds — upward-rising and downward-ash — and by color-distinction is six-fold: white ash, yellow ash, green ash, red ash, black ash, and variegated ash — thus six-fold. Having prepared that, it is first employed in bodily preparation (<s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s>). (GRhtCM 19.18cd–19:1)

children.text: rasayogamāha mākṣiketyādi // GRhtCM_19.18cd-19:2 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the mercury formulation, with '<s>mākṣika</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.18cd–19:2)

children.text:
mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ śipājatu prasiddhaṃ pohacūrṇaṃ māritamuṇḍasya rajaḥ
                            pathyā harītakī akṣo vibhītakaḥ viḍaṅgaṃ kṛmighnaṃ ghṛtam ājyaṃ madhu
                            kṣaudraṃ etaiḥ samprayuktaṃ rasaṃ kṣetrīkaraṇāya prayuñjīteti vākyārthaḥ
                            // GRhtCM_19.18cd-19:3 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> is <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite); <s>śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch) is well-known; <s>lohacūrṇa</s> is the powder of calcined <s>muṇḍa</s> (iron); <s>pathyā</s> is <s>harītakī</s> (Terminalia chebula); <s>akṣa</s> is <s>vibhītaka</s> (Terminalia bellirica); <s>viḍaṅga</s> is the worm-destroyer [herb] (Embelia ribes); <s>ghṛta</s> is clarified butter; <s>madhu</s> is honey — combined with these, mercury should be employed for bodily preparation (<s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s>); this is the sentence-meaning. (GRhtCM 19.18cd–19:3)

children.text: iti kalkīkṛtasūtaṃ ghanakāntamadhughṛtādisaṃyuktam /
children.translated_text: Thus, mercury made into a paste (<s>kalkīkṛta</s>), combined with dense [mica-essence] (<s>ghana</s>), lodestone (<s>kānta</s>), honey, ghee, and the like —

children.text: bhuktvāmaratāṃ gacchetkṣetrīkaraṇaṃ pradhānamidam // GRht_19.20 //
children.translated_text: having consumed [this], one attains immortality (<s>amaratā</s>); this bodily preparation (<s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s>) is primary. (GRht 19.20)

children.text:
ityuktavidhānena kapkīkṛtaṃ sūtaṃ bhuktvā amaratāṃ devatvaṃ gacchet //
                            GRhtCM_19.20:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] By the method just described, having consumed mercury made into a paste, one attains immortality — the state of the gods. (GRhtCM 19.20:1)

children.text:
iti kiṃ ghanakāntamadhughṛtādisaṃyuktaṃ ghano+abhrakaḥ kāntaṃ pohajāti
                            madhu kṣaudraṃ ghṛtam ājyaṃ ādiśabdāt sitā grāhyā etaiḥ saṃyuktaṃ sat
                            kapkīkṛtaṃ idaṃ ca pradhānaṃ kṣetrīkaraṇaṃ kṣetrī kriyate'neneti //
                            GRhtCM_19.20:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus, what? Combined with dense [mica-essence], lodestone, honey, ghee, and the like — <s>ghana</s> is mica (<s>abhraka</s>); <s>kānta</s> is a type of iron; <s>madhu</s> is honey; <s>ghṛta</s> is clarified butter; by the word 'and the like' (<s>ādi</s>), sugar should be taken; combined with these, made into a paste — and this is the primary bodily preparation — 'the body is prepared by this' [is the etymology]. (GRhtCM 19.20:2)

children.text: ityāroṭakriyā // GRhtCM_19.20:3 //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the <s>āroṭa</s> (body-preparation) procedure. (GRhtCM 19.20:3)

children.text: atha kṛṣṇaṃ vā pītaṃ vā saṃyojyaṃ ghanaṃ śikhiprabhaṃ bahuśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, black or yellow mica (<s>ghana</s>), with peacock-like luster, [processed] many times,

children.text: surabhīkṣīraniṣiktaṃ gatagiridoṣaṃ rasāyane yojyam // GRht_19.21 //
children.translated_text: sprinkled with cow's milk, freed from mineral defects (<s>giridoṣa</s>), should be employed in rejuvenation (<s>rasāyana</s>). (GRht 19.21)

children.text: atha patrābhrakriyā // GRhtCM_19.21:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now [begins] the leaf-mica (<s>patrābhra</s>) procedure. (GRhtCM 19.21:1)

children.text:
kṛṣṇaṃ śyāmavarṇaṃ ghanaṃ abhraṃ pītaṃ pītavarṇaṃ ghanaṃ vā bahuśo
                            naikavāraṃ śikhiprabhaṃ agniprabhaṃ sat surabhīkṣīraniṣiktaṃ secitaṃ
                            kāryaṃ punargatagiridoṣaṃ yathā syāttathā gatā girijā doṣā
                            mahīdharasaṃbhavā doṣā yasmāt tadevaṃ saṃśodhayitvā tat ghanaṃ rasāyane
                            jarāvyādhivināśakaraṇe yojyam // GRhtCM_19.21:2 //
children.translated_text: Black — dark-colored mica (<s>ghana</s>), or yellow — yellow-colored mica, [heated] many times, not just once, until it has peacock-like — fire-like — luster, [then] sprinkled with cow's milk — wetted, should be prepared; again, freed from mineral defects — made such that the defects born of the mountain (<s>giridoṣa</s>) have departed — having thus purified it, that mica should be employed in rejuvenation (<s>rasāyana</s>) — for the destruction of aging and disease. (GRhtCM 19.21:2)

children.text: niścandrikamapi śuddhaṃ viḍaṃgatriphalājyamadhusamāyuktam /
children.translated_text: Even without luster (<s>niścandrika</s>), [mica that is] pure, combined with <s>viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia), <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits), ghee, and honey,

children.text: pratidivasaṃ palamekaṃ bhuktvā kṣīrāśano vidhinā // GRht_19.22 //
children.translated_text: [if] one consumes one <s>pala</s> (measure) daily, subsisting on milk, according to the proper method — (GRht 19.22)

children.text: abhrakayogamāha niścandrikamityādi // GRhtCM_19.22:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the mica formulation, with 'without luster' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.22:1)

children.text:
ghanaṃ niścandrikamapi śuddhaṃ candrikārahitamapi nirdoṣaṃ
                            viḍaṅgatriphapājyamadhurasamāyuktaṃ
                            kṛmighnaharītakīvibhītakāmapakaghṛtakṣaudramipitaṃ pratidivasaṃ
                            pratidinaṃ ekapapapramāṇaṃ sarvaṃ bhuktvā vidhinā śuddhaśarīravidhānena
                            kṣīrāśano bhavet kṣīreṇa saha śāpyodanāśanaṃ samācaredityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_19.22:2 //
children.translated_text: Mica (<s>ghana</s>), even without luster (<s>niścandrika</s>) — even lacking shine — [if] pure, i.e., free from defects; combined with <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, ghee, and honey — mixed with Embelia (the worm-destroyer), <s>harītakī</s>, <s>vibhītaka</s>, <s>āmalaka</s> (Indian gooseberry), ghee, and honey; daily — every day — in the measure of one <s>pala</s>; having consumed all [of this], according to the proper method — with the regimen of a purified body — one should subsist on milk — one should eat rice-gruel with milk, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.22:2)

children.text: trikaṭukaviḍaṅgatriphalāmākṣikaśilājatuyutaṃ vyoma /
children.translated_text: Mica (<s>vyoma</s>), combined with the three pungents (<s>trikaṭuka</s>), <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), and mineral pitch (<s>śilājatu</s>),

children.text: kṣīraudanam aśnīyājjīvati jantuḥ śataṃ varṣam // GRht_19.23 //
children.translated_text: [if one] eats milk-rice, the creature lives a hundred years. (GRht 19.23)

children.text: taccāha trikaṭuketyādi // GRhtCM_19.23:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that, with 'three pungents' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.23:1)

children.text:
vyoma abhrakaṃ trikaṭukaviḍaṅgatriphapāmākṣikaśipājatuyutaṃ
                            pippapīmaricanāgaraharītakīvibhītakāmapakakṣaudraśipājatumipitaṃ aśnīyād
                            bhakṣayet // GRhtCM_19.23:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vyoma</s> is mica (<s>abhraka</s>); combined with the three pungents, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, and mineral pitch — mixed with long pepper (<s>pippalī</s>), black pepper (<s>marica</s>), dry ginger (<s>nāgara</s>), <s>harītakī</s>, <s>vibhītaka</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>, honey, and mineral pitch; one should eat — consume [it]. (GRhtCM 19.23:2)

children.text: punaḥ kṣīraudanaṃ pathyamaśnīyāt // GRhtCM_19.23:3 //
children.translated_text: Again, one should eat milk-rice as the [proper] diet. (GRhtCM 19.23:3)

children.text:
eva kṛte sati jantuḥ śataṃ jīvati jantujanyuśarīriṇaḥ ityamaraḥ //
                            GRhtCM_19.23:4 //
children.translated_text: When so done, the creature (<s>jantu</s>) lives a hundred [years]; <s>jantu</s>, <s>janyu</s>, and <s>śarīrin</s> [are synonyms for 'living being'] — thus [says] the <s>Amarakośa</s>. (GRhtCM 19.23:4)

children.text: iti patrābhrakaprakriyā // GRhtCM_19.23:5 //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the leaf-mica (<s>patrābhraka</s>) procedure. (GRhtCM 19.23:5)

children.text: ityevamādayo+anye kāñjikayuktāśca kīrtitā bahuśaḥ /
children.translated_text: These and other such [preparations], combined with sour gruel (<s>kāñjika</s>), have been praised many times —

children.text: patrābhrakaprayogā varjyā niryuktikāste hi // GRht_19.24 //
children.translated_text: [but] those leaf-mica preparations are to be rejected, for they are devoid of [proper] reasoning (<s>niryuktika</s>). (GRht 19.24)

children.text: abhrakasyottarottaraṃ darśayannāha itītyādi // GRhtCM_19.24:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Showing the progressive superiority of mica [preparations], he says 'these' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.24:1)

children.text:
ityevamādayaḥ iti pūrvoktā yogā ādayo yeṣāṃ te anye kāñjikayuktāśca
                            kāñjikenāranāpena yuktāḥ yogīkṛtāḥ granthāntare rasāvatārādau bahuśaḥ
                            kīrtitāḥ kathitāḥ te patrābhrakayogāḥ niryuktikāḥ niryukte bhavā
                            ikpratyayāntās te varjyāḥ sevane'yogyā ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.24:2
                            //
children.translated_text: 'These and so forth' — the formulations described above, 'and others combined with sour gruel' — prepared with sour rice-water (<s>kāñjika</s>, i.e., <s>aranāla</s>); [these have been] 'praised many times' — proclaimed in other treatises such as the <s>Rasāvatāra</s> and others; those leaf-mica preparations that are 'devoid of reasoning' — lacking proper justification — are to be rejected — unfit for use, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.24:2)

children.text: ye patrābhrakayogā rasāyanārthaṃ kīrtitā vidhinā /
children.translated_text: Those leaf-mica preparations that have been prescribed for rejuvenation (<s>rasāyana</s>) according to [proper] method,

children.text: ajñātadravyaguṇaistairupadiṣṭo jarāmṛtyuḥ // GRht_19.25 //
children.translated_text: by those who do not know the qualities of the substances — by them, aging and death have been prescribed. (GRht 19.25)

children.text:
avidhinā patrābhrakayogo vikārāyetyata āha ya ityādi // GRhtCM_19.25:1
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because leaf-mica preparation [used] improperly leads to harm, he says 'those' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.25:1)

children.text:
ye ajñātadravyaguṇaiḥ ajñātā dravyāṇāṃ abhrādināṃ guṇā yais tair
                            evaṃvidhaiḥ puṃbhiḥ vidhinā sāmānyavidhānena patrābhrakayogāḥ
                            rasāyanārthaṃ kīrtitās tair eva jarā mṛtyuśca upadiṣṭaḥ jarā pāpityaṃ
                            mṛtyur vyādhiḥ // GRhtCM_19.25:2 //
children.translated_text: By those — by persons of this kind — who do not know the qualities of substances — whose knowledge of the qualities of substances like mica and others is unknown; by them, leaf-mica preparations prescribed for rejuvenation according to the general method — by those very [persons], aging and death have been prescribed — aging means decrepitude; death means disease. (GRhtCM 19.25:2)

children.text: aprāptalokabhāvaṃ ghano+asya jaṭharāgnimupaśamaṃ nayati /
children.translated_text: Mica (<s>ghana</s>) that has not attained the [proper] worldly state drives the digestive fire (<s>jaṭharāgni</s>) to extinction;

children.text: agniṃ vināpi naśyati paribhūto vividharogagaṇaiḥ // GRht_19.26 //
children.translated_text: even without [the digestive] fire, [the person] perishes, overcome by hosts of various diseases. (GRht 19.26)

children.text:
jarāmṛtyorupadeśe hetumāha aprāptetyādi aprāptapokabhavaṃ yathā syāttathā
                            asya kartuḥ ghanaḥ // GRhtCM_19.26:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the reason for the prescription of aging and death, with 'not attained' and so forth — 'not having attained the worldly state' — mica (<s>ghana</s>) of such [improper quality], of the one who uses it — (GRhtCM 19.26:1)

children.text: jaṭharāgniṃ vināpi pumān naśyati nāśaṃ prāpnoti // GRhtCM_19.26:2 //
children.translated_text: [drives] the digestive fire to extinction; even without fire, the person perishes — reaches destruction. (GRhtCM 19.26:2)

children.text:
kiṃbhūtaḥ san vividharogagaṇaiḥ nānārogasamūhaiḥ paribhūto vijitaḥ san
                            iti vākyārthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.26:3 //
children.translated_text: In what condition? Being overcome — defeated — by hosts of various diseases — by multitudes of diverse illnesses; this is the sentence-meaning. (GRhtCM 19.26:3)

children.text:
kāṣṭhe sthitam api ghanapaṭapamadhye'pi abhre'bhrasattvaṃ sthitaṃ tadāha
                            abhrasatvaṃ ghanasāraṃ ghanapaṭape sthitamapi nijakāryaṃ svakīyakṛtyaṃ
                            tathā na kurute vahniragniḥ // GRhtCM_19.26:4 //
children.translated_text: Just as [fire] situated in wood — the mica-essence (<s>abhrasattva</s>) situated within the mica-leaf (<s>ghanapaṭala</s>) — he states: the mica-essence, the core of mica (<s>ghanasāra</s>), even though situated in the mica-leaf, does not perform its own function; fire [does not perform its function when in wood]. (GRhtCM 19.26:4)

children.text:
kāṣṭhe dāruṇi sthitaḥ san nijakāryaṃ na kurute tu punaḥ yathā ghṛtaṃ
                            payasi dugdhe sthitaṃ sat svīkāryaṃ na kurute cāgrahir iva dhanasthamiva
                            madhye sthitaṃ kāryaṃ kurute'tiniḥsṛtaṃ sat pṛthagbhūtaṃ sat nijakāryaṃ
                            kuruta iti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_19.26:5 //
children.translated_text: [Just as fire] situated in wood does not perform its own function, and [just as] ghee (<s>ghṛta</s>) situated in milk does not perform its own function, and like a captive (<s>āgrahi</s>) like one whose wealth is held [in custody] — [the essence] situated in the midst performs its function [only] when fully extracted, i.e., when separated; this is the purport. (GRhtCM 19.26:5)

children.text: abhra:: inedible
children.translated_text: Mica: inedible [forms]

children.text: abhrasya rasāyanināṃ bhakṣyamiha kīrtitaṃ paraṃ satvam /
children.translated_text: For those seeking rejuvenation (<s>rasāyanin</s>), the supreme edible [form] of mica proclaimed here is the essence (<s>sattva</s>);

children.text: trividhaṃ gaganamabhakṣyaṃ kācaḥ kiṭṭaṃ ca pattrarajaḥ // GRht_19.27 //
children.translated_text: mica is inedible in three [forms]: glass-like (<s>kāca</s>), slag (<s>kiṭṭa</s>), and leaf-powder (<s>pattrarajas</s>). (GRht 19.27)

children.text: bhakṣyābhakṣyam abhramāha abhrasyetyādi // GRhtCM_19.27:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the edible and inedible [forms] of mica, with 'of mica' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.27:1)

children.text:
abhrakasatvamiha kṣetrīkaraṇe rasāyanināṃ jarāvyādhivināśecchūnāṃ param
                            utkṛṣṭaṃ bhakṣyaṃ aśanayogyaṃ kīrtitam // GRhtCM_19.27:2 //
children.translated_text: The essence of mica (<s>abhrakasattva</s>), here in bodily preparation (<s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s>), for those seeking rejuvenation — for those desiring the destruction of aging and disease — is the supreme, i.e., the best, edible [form] — fit for consumption — so proclaimed. (GRhtCM 19.27:2)

children.text:
punastrividhaṃ triprakāraṃ gaganamabhraṃ abhakṣyaṃ abhojyam //
                            GRhtCM_19.27:3 //
children.translated_text: Again, mica in three forms — three varieties — is inedible — not to be consumed. (GRhtCM 19.27:3)

children.text:
kiṃ tat kācaḥ kācarūpaṃ kiṭṭaṃ maparūpaṃ pattrarajaḥ sāmānyābhracūrṇaṃ
                            ceti trividhamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.27:4 //
children.translated_text: What are they? <s>Kāca</s> — the glass-like form; <s>kiṭṭa</s> — the slag form; <s>pattrarajas</s> — ordinary mica powder — thus three-fold, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.27:4)

children.text: ādau ghanaloharajastriphalārasabhāvanaiś ca nirghṛṣṭam /
children.translated_text: First, mica-iron powder (<s>ghanalohrajas</s>), ground with <s>triphalā</s> (three-fruits) juice steepings,

children.text: kurvītāñjanasadṛśaṃ sthagitavastreṇa sūryakaraiḥ // GRht_19.28 //
children.translated_text: one should make [it] collyrium-like, covered with cloth, [dried] in sunlight. (GRht 19.28)

children.text: itthaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ kṛtvā vividhakāntalohacūrṇasamam /
children.translated_text: Having thus made [it] fine, [mixed] equally with powders of various [types of] lodestone (<s>kānta</s>) and iron (<s>loha</s>),

children.text: lohaghanaṃ ca tadevaṃ bhṛṅgeṇa ca sādhayed bahuśaḥ // GRht_19.29 //
children.translated_text: and mica-iron (<s>lohaghana</s>) likewise, one should process [it] many times with <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta alba). (GRht 19.29)

children.text: triphalāghṛtamadhumiśritam amṛtam idaṃ māsasthitaṃ dhānye /
children.translated_text: Mixed with <s>triphalā</s>, ghee, and honey — this immortal [preparation], stored in grain for a month,

children.text: śastrakaṭorikasampuṭamadhyagataṃ pūjitaṃ mantraiḥ // GRht_19.30 //
children.translated_text: placed inside a sealed pair of iron bowls, worshipped with <s>mantras</s>, (GRht 19.30)

children.text: māsena tu taduddhṛtya jñātvā balaṃ tatprayuñjīta /
children.translated_text: after a month, having extracted it, knowing its potency, one should employ it;

children.text: kāntaṃ vinātha gaganaṃ gaganaṃ vinā tathā ca kāntam // GRht_19.31 //
children.translated_text: [it may be used] with lodestone (<s>kānta</s>) without mica, or with mica (<s>gagana</s>) without lodestone. (GRht 19.31)

children.text: sthaulyaṃ paṭalaṃ kācaṃ timirārbudakarṇanādaśūlāni /
children.translated_text: Obesity, cataracts (<s>paṭala</s>), glass-eye (<s>kāca</s>), darkness-tumors (<s>timira-arbuda</s>), ear-ringing, headaches,

children.text: hantyarśāṃsi bhagandaramehaplīhādi pālityam // GRht_19.32 //
children.translated_text: it destroys hemorrhoids (<s>arśas</s>), fistula (<s>bhagandara</s>), urinary disorders (<s>meha</s>), splenic enlargement (<s>plīhā</s>), and graying of hair (<s>pālitya</s>). (GRht 19.32)

children.text: etatkurvanmatimān gorasamastupradhānam aśnīyāt /
children.translated_text: The wise person performing this should eat [a diet of] primarily cow's milk and buttermilk,

children.text: jāṅgalamudgājyapayaḥ śālyodanaṃ brahmacaryeṇa // GRht_19.33 //
children.translated_text: meat of [animals from] arid lands (<s>jāṅgala</s>), green gram (<s>mudga</s>), ghee, milk, and rice-gruel (<s>śālyodana</s>), observing celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>). (GRht 19.33)

children.text: adhunā ghanasattvapohasādhanam āha ādāvityādi // GRhtCM_19.28-33:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now he states the preparation of mica-essence with iron, with 'first' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.28–33:1)

children.text:
ādau prathamaṃ ghanapoharajaḥ ghanamabhrasatvaṃ poharajaḥ kāntacūrṇaṃ
                            triphapārasabhāvanaiḥ harītakīvibhītakāmapakadravapuṭanair nirghṛṣṭaṃ
                            sat añjanasadṛśaṃ sauvīrāñjanatupyaṃ kurvīta kaiḥ kṛtvā sūryakaraiḥ kena
                            sthagitavastreṇa ācchāditapaṭena vastreṇācchādya sūryakarasannidhau
                            dhāryamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.28-33:2 //
children.translated_text: First — initially — mica-iron powder: <s>ghana</s> is mica-essence (<s>abhrasattva</s>); iron powder (<s>loharajas</s>) is lodestone powder — [these,] ground with <s>triphalā</s>-juice steepings — with the juice-steeped [preparation] of <s>harītakī</s>, <s>vibhītaka</s>, and <s>āmalaka</s>; having ground, one should make [it] collyrium-like — resembling <s>sauvīra</s>-collyrium; with what? With sunlight; how? With cloth covering — having covered with cloth, it should be kept in the presence of sunlight, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.28–33:2)

children.text: itthamityādi // GRhtCM_19.28-33:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Thus' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.28–33:3)

children.text:
itthamamunā prakāreṇa śpakṣṇam añjanasannibhaṃ yathā syāt tathā
                            ghanasatvakāntaṃ kṛtvā punarpohaghanaṃ pohaṃ muṇḍādi ghanaṃ abhrasatvaṃ
                            etadubhayaṃ vividhakāntapohacūrṇasamaṃ vividhā nānājātayaḥ
                            ayaskāntabhedāḥ teṣāṃ cūrṇaṃ tatsamaṃ kṛtvā bhṛṅgeṇa ca
                            bahuśo+anekavāraṃ sādhayedbhāvayedityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.28-33:4 //
children.translated_text: Thus — in this manner — having made [it] fine — collyrium-like — the mica-essence-lodestone [mixture]; again, iron-mica (<s>lohaghana</s>) — iron meaning <s>muṇḍa</s> and the like, mica meaning mica-essence — these two, [mixed] equally with powder of various types of lodestone (<s>kānta</s>) — the various kinds being different varieties of magnetic stone — with their powder in equal measure; having prepared [this], one should process [it] with <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta alba) many times, i.e., many rounds — meaning one should steep [it], is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.28–33:4)

children.text: taccāha triphapetyādi // GRhtCM_19.28-33:5 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that, with '<s>triphalā</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.28–33:5)

children.text:
tadbhṛṅgarājena bahuśo bhāvitaṃ ghanasatvakāntaṃ idam amṛtaṃ sudhāsamaṃ
                            na mṛtamamṛtaṃ tat triphapāmadhughṛtamiśritaṃ
                            harītakīvibhītakāmapakaghṛtakṣaudramipitaṃ dhānye kasyacidannasyāntaḥ
                            māsasthitaṃ kuryāt māsaikaparimāṇaṃ tatra vidhātavyamiti vyaktiḥ //
                            GRhtCM_19.28-33:6 //
children.translated_text: That [preparation], treated many times with <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (Eclipta alba), the mica-essence-and-lodestone [compound] — this is <s>amṛta</s> (nectar), equal to divine nectar, not dead [but] immortal — that, mixed with <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits), honey, and ghee — mixed with <s>harītakī</s> (chebulic myrobalan), <s>vibhītaka</s> (beleric myrobalan), <s>āmalaka</s> (Indian gooseberry), ghee, and honey — should be placed inside grain, inside some [type of] food, for the duration of one month; it should be kept for one month's measure therein — this is the clarification. (GRhtCM 19.28-33:6)

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ mantraiśca sampūjitam // GRhtCM_19.28-33:7 //
children.translated_text: Of what specification? Also worshipped with mantras. (GRhtCM 19.28-33:7)

children.text: tathā mantrastu /
children.translated_text: The mantra is as follows:

children.text: mandāramāpākupitāpakāyai kapāpamāpāṅkitaśekharāya /
children.translated_text: To her who is angered by the <s>mandāra</s> (coral tree) garland, to him whose crest is marked by a skull,

children.text: divyāmbarāyai ca digambarāya namaḥ śivāyai ca namaḥ śivāya /
children.translated_text: to her who wears divine garments, to him who is sky-clad — homage to <s>Śivā</s>, and homage to <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: ityādibhiḥ // GRhtCM_19.28-33:8 //
children.translated_text: With these and similar [mantras]. (GRhtCM 19.28-33:8)

children.text: taccāha māsenetyādi // GRhtCM_19.28-33:9 //
children.translated_text: He states that with 'māsena' (in a month) and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.28-33:9)

children.text:
dhānyānmāsena māsaikaparimāṇenoddhṛtya bahirnītvā punarapi bapaṃ jñātvā
                            prayuñjīta bhoktre dadyāt atha viśeṣaṃ darśayati kāntaṃ vinā
                            abhrakasatvameva kṛtvā prayuñjīta ca punargaganaṃ vinā kāntaṃ kevapaṃ
                            pūrvavidhānena sādhayitvā prayuñjītetyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.28-33:10
                            //
children.translated_text: From the grain, after one month — after the duration of one month — having extracted [it], having taken [it] out, furthermore knowing the strength [appropriate to the patient], one should administer — should give to the consumer. Now he shows a distinction: without <s>kānta</s> (lodestone), making the mica-essence alone, one should administer; or furthermore, without mica (<s>gagana</s>), <s>kānta</s> alone, having prepared [it] by the previous procedure, one should administer — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.28-33:10)

children.text: phapamāha sthaupyam ityādi // GRhtCM_19.28-33:11 //
children.translated_text: He states the result with 'sthaulya' (obesity) and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.28-33:11)

children.text:
sthaupyamiti medorogaḥ paṭapakācatimirāṇi netrarogāḥ arbudaṃ
                            granthiviśeṣaḥ karṇanādaḥ pratītaḥ śūpamaṣṭavidhaṃ etāni hanti arśāṃsi
                            gudajāni bhagandaramehappīhādi bhagandaraḥ gudavraṇaṃ mehaḥ pramehaḥ
                            bījavikāraḥ ppīhā ppīharogaḥ ete rogā ādiryasya tat hanti pāpityaṃ jarāṃ
                            ca nāśayatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.28-33:12 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Sthaulya</s>' is obesity (<s>medoroga</s>); '<s>paṭalakā</s>' and cataracts (<s>timira</s>) are eye diseases; '<s>arbuda</s>' is a type of tumor; '<s>karṇanāda</s>' (ear-ringing) is well-known; '<s>śūla</s>' is of eight kinds — these it destroys; '<s>arśas</s>' (hemorrhoids) are those arising in the rectum; '<s>bhagandarameha</s>' — <s>bhagandara</s> is a rectal fistula; <s>meha</s> is <s>prameha</s> (urinary disease), a disorder of the seed; '<s>plīhā</s>' is splenic disease — these diseases are the 'ādi' (etc.) of which — that it destroys; and it destroys grey hair (<s>pālitya</s>) and old age (<s>jarā</s>) — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.28-33:12)

children.text: pathyam āha etadityādi // GRhtCM_19.28-33:13 //
children.translated_text: He describes the dietary regimen with 'etat' (this) and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.28-33:13)

children.text:
etanniṣpannauṣadhabhakṣaṇaṃ kurvan matimān puruṣaḥ gorasamastupradhānaṃ
                            goraso godugdhaṃ mastu dadhimastu evaṃpradhānamannamaśnīyāt bhuñjīta //
                            GRhtCM_19.28-33:14 //
children.translated_text: A wise man consuming this perfected medicinal preparation should eat food principally consisting of cow's products and buttermilk — cow's product is cow's milk; <s>mastu</s> is curd-buttermilk — food whose principal [ingredient] is such [should be eaten]. (GRhtCM 19.28-33:14)

children.text:
punarjāṅgapamudgājyapayo+aśnīyāt jāṅgapasyedaṃ jāṅgapaṃ
                            svappāmbuśākhīdeśaḥ jāṅgapaḥ mudgaḥ pratīto+annaviśeṣaḥ ājyaṃ ghṛtaṃ
                            payo dugdhaṃ vā sapipaṃ yanmudgājyapayaḥ taccāśnīyāt //
                            GRhtCM_19.28-33:15 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, one should eat <s>jāṅgala</s> [food], green gram, ghee, and milk — this is <s>jāṅgala</s> (arid region) [food]; the <s>jāṅgala</s> is a dry, sparsely-wooded region; green gram (<s>mudga</s>) is a well-known grain variety; ghee (<s>ājya</s>) is clarified butter; milk (<s>payas</s>) or [food] with fat — that which is green-gram-ghee-milk should be eaten. (GRhtCM 19.28-33:15)

children.text: ca punaḥ śāpyodanamaśnīyāt // GRhtCM_19.28-33:16 //
children.translated_text: And furthermore, one should eat rice and vegetables. (GRhtCM 19.28-33:16)

children.text: etatsarvaṃ brahmacaryeṇa kartavyamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.28-33:17 //
children.translated_text: All this should be done with <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.28-33:17)

children.text: iti satvābhrakriyā // GRhtCM_19.28-33:18 //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the mica-essence procedure (<s>sattvābhrakriyā</s>). (GRhtCM 19.28-33:18)

children.text: ghanasatvapādajīrṇaḥ kāntajīrṇo yattīkṣṇasamajīrṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Mercury in which mica-essence has been digested in a quarter-portion, and in which <s>kānta</s> (lodestone) has been digested, and in which an equal [portion of] steel has been digested —

children.text: kṣetrīkaraṇaḥ paramaḥ prayujyate'pi punarāroṭaḥ // GRht_19.34 //
children.translated_text: is supremely effective for <s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s> (preparation of the body); and the <s>āroṭa</s> (mercury pellet) is also employed. (GRht 19.34)

children.text: atha jīrṇarasasyādhikyaṃ darśayannāha ghanetyādi // GRhtCM_19.34:1 //
children.translated_text: Now, showing the superiority of digested mercury, he says 'ghana' (mica) and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.34:1)

children.text: ghanasatvaṃ pādapramāṇaṃ jīrṇaṃ yasmin saḥ // GRhtCM_19.34:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Mica-essence digested in a quarter-portion' — that in which mica-essence in a quarter-measure has been digested — such [mercury]. (GRhtCM 19.34:2)

children.text: kāntajīrṇa iti pādapramāṇakāntajīrṇa ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.34:3 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Kānta</s>-digested' means digested with a quarter-measure of <s>kānta</s> — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.34:3)

children.text: punastīkṣṇaṃ samaṃ jīrṇaṃ yasminnevaṃvidho rasaḥ // GRhtCM_19.34:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, steel in equal [portion] has been digested in which — such mercury. (GRhtCM 19.34:4)

children.text: kṣetrīkaraṇaṃ pradhānaṃ sarvatretyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣetrīkaraṇa</s> (body-preparation) is primary — in all [contexts] — this is the meaning.

children.text: baddho yaḥ khoṭatāṃ yāto dhmāto dhmātaḥ kṣayaṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: 'That which is bound, having attained the state of a <s>khoṭa</s> (ingot), when smelted, does not undergo loss —

children.text: khoṭo bandhaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ śīghraṃ sarvagadāpahaḥ /
children.translated_text: the <s>khoṭa</s>-binding should be known as that; it swiftly removes all diseases.'

children.text: iti granthāntare // GRhtCM_19.34:5 //
children.translated_text: Thus in another text. (GRhtCM 19.34:5)

children.text: ghanasatvakāntasūtaṃ mṛtahema śatāvarīrasopetam /
children.translated_text: Mica-essence, <s>kānta</s>, and mercury [combined with] calcined gold, endowed with <s>śatāvarī</s> (asparagus) juice,

children.text: ghṛtamadhulīḍhaṃ varṣānnihanti mṛtyuṃ jarāṃ caiva // GRht_19.35 //
children.translated_text: licked with ghee and honey — within a year, it destroys death and old age. (GRht 19.35)

children.text:
ghanasatvam abhrasāraḥ kāntaṃ cumbakotthaṃ sūto rasaḥ ekavadbhāvo
                            dvandvasamāsāt tathā mṛtaṃ hema pañcatvamāptaṃ kanakaṃ ca etaccatuṣkaṃ
                            śatāvarīrasopetaṃ śatamūpīdravabhāvitaṃ punarghṛtamadhupīḍhaṃ
                            ghṛtamadhubhyāṃ pīḍhaṃ āsvāditaṃ sat varṣādvarṣaparimāṇāt mṛtyuvyādhiṃ
                            jarāṃ ca hanti nāśayatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.35:1 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Ghanasattva</s>' is mica-extract; '<s>kānta</s>' is that produced from lodestone; '<s>sūta</s>' is mercury — these have single-entity nature from the <s>dvandva</s> compound; likewise '<s>mṛtahema</s>' is gold that has attained destruction (calcination) — this group of four, endowed with <s>śatāvarī</s> juice — treated with <s>śatamūlī</s> (asparagus) decoction; furthermore, licked with ghee and honey — tasted with ghee and honey; within a year — from the measure of one year — it destroys death-disease and old age — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.35:1)

children.text: eṣāmekaṃ yogaṃ kṣetrīkaraṇārthamāditaḥ kṛtvā /
children.translated_text: One of these formulas, having performed [it] from the beginning for <s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s> (body-preparation),

children.text: saṃvatsaramayanaṃ vā niḥśreyasasiddhaye yojyam // GRht_19.36 //
children.translated_text: for a year or half-year should be employed for the attainment of supreme liberation. (GRht 19.36)

children.text: viśeṣamāha eṣāmityādi // GRhtCM_19.36:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the distinction with 'eṣām' (of these) and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.36:1)

children.text:
eṣāṃ pūrvoktānāṃ yogānāṃ madhye ādita ārambhataḥ ekaṃ yogaṃ kṛtvā
                            niḥśreyaso mokṣaḥ tatsiddhaye niṣpattaye saṃvatsaraṃ varṣaparimāṇaṃ
                            ayanaṃ ṣaṇmāsaparyantaṃ yojyaṃ bhoktṛṣu iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_19.36:2
                            //
children.translated_text: From among these — the previously stated formulas — from the beginning, having made one formula, for the attainment — the accomplishment — of supreme liberation (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>, <s>mokṣa</s>), for a year — the measure of one year — or for an <s>ayana</s> (half-year), up to six months — it should be employed in patients — this is the complement. (GRhtCM 19.36:2)

children.text:
muktiḥ kaivapyanirvāṇaśreyoniḥśreyasāmṛtam ityamaraḥ // GRhtCM_19.36:3
                            //
children.translated_text: '<s>Mukti</s>, <s>kaivalya</s>, <s>nirvāṇa</s>, <s>śreyas</s>, <s>niḥśreyasa</s>, <s>amṛta</s>' — thus [says] the <s>Amarakośa</s>. (GRhtCM 19.36:3)

children.text: abhrakasasyakamākṣikarasakadaradavimalavajragirijatubhiḥ /
children.translated_text: With mica, <s>sasyaka</s> (vitriol), <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), <s>rasaka</s> (calamine), cinnabar, <s>vimala</s> (silver-pyrite), diamond, and bitumen;
