children.text: vaikrāntakāntatīkṣṇair hāṭakatārāratāmraiśca // GRht_19.37 //
children.translated_text: with <s>vaikrānta</s>, <s>kānta</s> (lodestone), steel; and with gold, silver, brass, and copper — (GRht 19.37)

children.text: saṃyuktairvyastairvā dvitricaturbhir yathālābham /
children.translated_text: combined together or separately, with two, three, or four [of these], as available;

children.text: jīrṇahato rasendro rasāyane śasyate sadbhiḥ // GRht_19.38 //
children.translated_text: the lord of mercury, killed with digested [substances], is praised by the wise for <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation). (GRht 19.38)

children.text: bahūnnirdiśan viśeṣamāha abhraketyādi // GRhtCM_19.37-38:1 //
children.translated_text: Indicating many [options], he states the distinction with 'abhraka' (mica) and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.37-38:1)

children.text:
abhrakaḥ prasiddhaḥ sasyakaś capapaḥ mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ rasakaṃ kharparaṃ
                            daradaṃ hiṅgupaṃ vimapaṃ sitamākṣikaṃ vajrakaṃ hīrakaṃ girijatu śipājatu
                            etaiḥ // GRhtCM_19.37-38:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Abhraka</s> (mica) is well-known; <s>sasyaka</s> is <s>capalā</s> (vitriol); <s>mākṣika</s> is iron pyrite; <s>rasaka</s> is calamine; <s>darada</s> is cinnabar; <s>vimala</s> is silver-pyrite; <s>vajraka</s> is diamond; <s>girijatu</s> is bitumen — with these. (GRhtCM 19.37-38:2)

children.text:
punar vaikrāntetyādi vaikrāntaṃ vajrabhūmijaṃ rajaḥ kāntaṃ pohajāti
                            tīkṣṇaṃ sāraḥ etaiśca // GRhtCM_19.37-38:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore '<s>vaikrānta</s>' and so forth — <s>vaikrānta</s> is diamond-earth dust; <s>kānta</s> is a type of metal (lodestone); <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is steel — with these also. (GRhtCM 19.37-38:3)

children.text:
hāṭakatārāratāmraiś ca hāṭakaṃ hema tāraṃ rūpyaṃ āraṃ rājarītiḥ tāmraṃ
                            śupbaṃ etaiśca etair uddiṣṭaiḥ abhrakāditāmrāntaiḥ samastair
                            ekatrīkṛtair vyastairvā pṛthakkṛtairvā yathāpābhaṃ pābhamanatikramya
                            bhavatīti yathāpābhaṃ dvitricaturbhirvā abhrādyairjīrṇahato rasendro
                            jīrṇābhrādīnāṃ hatiryasmin sa tathoktaḥ rasāyane jarāvyādhivināśane
                            rasaśāstramarmajñaiḥ śasyate abhrādayaḥ praśastā uktā ityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_19.37-38:4 //
children.translated_text: And with gold, silver, brass, and copper — <s>hāṭaka</s> is gold; <s>tāra</s> is silver; <s>āra</s> is <s>rājarīti</s> (brass); <s>tāmra</s> is copper. With these enumerated [substances], from mica to copper, combined — made into one — or separately — made individual — or as available — not exceeding what is obtainable; with two, three, or four of the mica and other [substances] — the lord of mercury in which the digested [substances] have been killed — so described — is praised for <s>rasāyana</s>, the destruction of old age and disease, by those who know the essence of the alchemical treatises — mica and the like are praised, recommended — this is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.37-38:4)

children.text: yugmam // GRhtCM_19.37-38:5 //
children.translated_text: [This is] a paired [verse]. (GRhtCM 19.37-38:5)

children.text: vajrādibhirhataḥ sūto hatasūtasamo+aparaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Mercury killed by diamond and the like; another [preparation] equal to killed mercury;

children.text: śṛṅkhapābaddhanāmā syāddehapohavidhāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: that called chain-bound (<s>śṛṅkhalābaddha</s>) — [it is] a bestower of body and metal [transmutation].'

children.text: asya prabhāvādvegena vyāptirbhavati niścitam /
children.translated_text: 'By its power, pervading occurs swiftly — certainly.'

children.text: iti granthāntare // GRhtCM_19.37-38:6 //
children.translated_text: Thus in another text. (GRhtCM 19.37-38:6)

children.text: viṣanāgavaṅgabaddho bhukto hi rasaḥ karoti kuṣṭhādīn /
children.translated_text: Mercury bound with poison, lead, and tin, when consumed, produces skin diseases (<s>kuṣṭha</s>) and the like;

children.text: uparasabaddhe tu rase sphuṭanti bhukte tathāṅgāni // GRht_19.39 //
children.translated_text: and when mercury bound with subsidiary minerals is consumed, the limbs burst. (GRht 19.39)

children.text: kutsitavidhānaṃ darśayannāha viṣetyādi // GRhtCM_19.39:1 //
children.translated_text: Showing the condemned procedure, he says 'viṣa' (poison) and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.39:1)

children.text:
viṣanāgavaṅgabaddho rasaḥ viṣaṃ saktukādikaṃ nāgaḥ sīsakaḥ vaṅgaṃ trapu
                            etairbaddho bandhanamāptaḥ sa bhuktaḥ san hi niścitaṃ kuṣṭhādīn
                            kuṣṭhajvarakṣayādīn // GRhtCM_19.39:2 //
children.translated_text: Mercury bound with poison, lead, and tin — <s>viṣa</s> is <s>saktuka</s> and the like; <s>nāga</s> is lead; <s>vaṅga</s> is tin — bound with these, having attained binding; that, when consumed, certainly produces <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease), fever, consumption, and the like. (GRhtCM 19.39:2)

children.text:
uparasabaddhe rase uparasair gandhādibhiḥ aṣṭabhiḥ baddho bandhanam
                            āpanno yo+asau rasaḥ tasmin bhukte sati bhokturaṅgāni hastapādādīni
                            sphuṭanti // GRhtCM_19.39:3 //
children.translated_text: When mercury bound with subsidiary minerals is consumed — mercury in which binding has been attained with the eight <s>uparasas</s> beginning with sulfur — when that is consumed, the limbs of the consumer — hands, feet, and the like — burst apart. (GRhtCM 19.39:3)

children.text: ghanasattvakāntakāñcībhāskaratīkṣṇaiś ca cīrṇajīrṇasya /
children.translated_text: Mercury in which mica-essence, <s>kānta</s>, gold (<s>kāñcī</s>), copper (<s>bhāskara</s>), and steel have been fed and digested —

children.text: sūtasya guñjāmātrā māṣakamekaṃ parā mātrā // GRht_19.40 //
children.translated_text: the dose of that mercury is one <s>guñjā</s> (unit); one <s>māṣaka</s> (bean-weight) is the maximum dose. (GRht 19.40)

children.text: śatavedhino dviguñjā tathā sahasraikavedhino guñjā /
children.translated_text: For hundredfold-transmuting [mercury], two <s>guñjās</s>; likewise for thousandfold-transmuting, one <s>guñjā</s>;

children.text: ardhā ca lakṣavedhinaḥ siddhārthaḥ koṭivedhinaḥ sūtāt // GRht_19.41 //
children.translated_text: half [a <s>guñjā</s>] for hundred-thousand-fold-transmuting; a mustard-seed [measure] from <s>koṭi</s>-transmuting (ten-million-fold) mercury. (GRht 19.41)

children.text: jīrṇarasasya mātrām āha ghanetyādi // GRhtCM_19.40-41:1 //
children.translated_text: He states the dose of digested mercury with 'ghana' (mica) and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.40-41:1)

children.text:
etaiścīrṇajīrṇaṃ pūrvaṃ cīrṇaṃ kavapitaṃ paścājjīrṇaṃ jāraṇam āpannaṃ
                            tasya sūtasya guñjā mātrā bhakṣaṇāya guñjā yathā /
children.translated_text: With these, [mercury that has been] fed and digested — first fed (<s>cīrṇa</s>, consumed), afterward digested (<s>jīrṇa</s>, assimilated) — of that mercury, the dose for consumption is one <s>guñjā</s>. A <s>guñjā</s> is as follows:

children.text: ṣaṭsarṣapair yavastveko guñjaikā tu yavaistribhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Six mustard seeds equal one barley; one <s>guñjā</s> equals three barleys.'
Thus. (GRhtCM 19.40-41:2)

children.text: parā anyā mātrā anyajīrṇasūtasya mātrā māṣamekaṃ māṣako yathā /
children.translated_text: The 'other' (<s>parā</s>) dose — the dose of differently-digested mercury — is one <s>māṣaka</s>. A <s>māṣaka</s> is as follows:

children.text: guñjābhirdaśabhiḥ prokto māṣako brahmaṇā purā /
children.translated_text: 'A <s>māṣaka</s> is declared by <s>Brahmā</s> of old to be ten <s>guñjās</s>.'
Thus. (GRhtCM 19.40-41:3)

children.text:
etaiḥ kaiḥ ghanasattvakāntakāñcībhāskaratīkṣṇaiḥ
                            abhrakasattvacumbakatāpyatāmrasārair iti // GRhtCM_19.40-41:4 //
children.translated_text: With these — which? With mica-essence, <s>kānta</s>, gold (<s>kāñcī</s>), copper (<s>bhāskara</s>), and steel — meaning with mica-extract, lodestone, pyrite, copper, and steel-essence. (GRhtCM 19.40-41:4)

children.text: atha vedhaviśeṣeṇa parimāṇamāha śatetyādi // GRhtCM_19.40-41:5 //
children.translated_text: Now he states the measure according to the type of transmutation with 'śata' (hundred) and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.40-41:5)

children.text:
śatavedhinaḥ sūtasya guñjāpramāṇā mātrā jñeyā tathā tena prakāreṇa
                            sahasraikavedhinaḥ sūtasyāpi guñjāmānameva pakṣavedhinaḥ sūtāt ardhā
                            raktikā punaḥ koṭivedhinaḥ sūtāt siddhārthaḥ sarṣapamānā //
                            GRhtCM_19.40-41:6 //
children.translated_text: The dose of hundredfold-transmuting mercury should be known as one <s>guñjā</s> in measure; likewise, the dose of thousandfold-transmuting mercury is also one <s>guñjā</s> in measure; for hundred-thousand-fold-transmuting mercury — half a <s>raktikā</s> (half-<s>guñjā</s>); furthermore, from <s>koṭi</s>-transmuting (ten-million-fold) mercury — a <s>siddhārtha</s> (mustard-seed) measure. (GRhtCM 19.40-41:6)

children.text:
śatāṃśena vedho vidyate yasmin sa śatavedhī tasya śatavedhinaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_19.40-41:7 //
children.translated_text: That which transmutes at one-hundredth [ratio] — that is a 'hundredfold-transmuter'; of that hundredfold-transmuter. (GRhtCM 19.40-41:7)

children.text: evaṃ sarvatra jñeyam // GRhtCM_19.40-41:8 //
children.translated_text: Thus it should be understood everywhere. (GRhtCM 19.40-41:8)

children.text: hemaniyojitasūtaṃ kāntamaṇiṃ vividhaguṭikāśca /
children.translated_text: Mercury conjoined with gold, a <s>kānta</s>-gem (lodestone amulet), and various pills —

children.text: japahomadevatārcananirataḥ pumāniti dhārayet // GRht_19.42 //
children.translated_text: a man devoted to <s>japa</s> (mantra-recitation), <s>homa</s> (fire-oblation), and worship of deities should wear [these]. (GRht 19.42)

children.text:
japaḥ aghorādijapaḥ homastaddaśāṃśena havanaṃ devatārcanaṃ devatānāṃ
                            gaṇeśaviṣṇuraviśivacaṇḍīnāṃ arcanaṃ eteṣu nirataḥ saktaḥ evaṃvidhiḥ
                            pumān // GRhtCM_19.42:1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Japa</s> is the recitation of <s>Aghora</s> and similar [mantras]; <s>homa</s> is fire-oblation [done] at one-tenth [of the japa count]; deity-worship is the worship of the deities — <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Ravi</s> (Sun), <s>Śiva</s>, and <s>Caṇḍī</s>; devoted to these — engaged [in these practices] — such a man. (GRhtCM 19.42:1)

children.text:
iti kiṃ hemaniyojitasūtaṃ dhārayet hemnā saha niyojito miśrito yaḥ sūtaḥ
                            taṃ kāntamaṇiḥ kāntaścāsau maṇiśca vā kāntamaṇiḥ kāntasaṃjñako maṇiḥ ca
                            punaḥ vividhaguṭikāḥ vividhāśca tā guṭikāśceti // GRhtCM_19.42:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus what [should he wear]? Mercury conjoined with gold — mercury which has been conjoined, mixed with gold — that; a <s>kānta</s>-gem — <s>kānta</s> which is also a <s>maṇi</s> (gem), or a gem designated as '<s>kānta</s>'; furthermore, various pills — various kinds, and they are pills. (GRhtCM 19.42:2)

children.text: śālestu piṣṭakodbhavabhojanam ājyaṃ ca mudgamāṃsarasaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Rice, food made from prepared [flour], ghee, and green-gram-meat-broths —

children.text: yavagodhūmānnāni ca gokṣīraṃ mastu ca viśeṣāt // GRht_19.43 //
children.translated_text: and foods of barley and wheat, and especially cow's milk and buttermilk (<s>mastu</s>). (GRht 19.43)

children.text: pāne jalamakṣāraṃ madhurāṇi yāni kāni śastāni /
children.translated_text: For drinking, non-alkaline water; whatever [foods are] sweet are recommended;

children.text: peyaṃ cāturjātakarpūrāmodamuditamukham // GRht_19.44 //
children.translated_text: the beverage should have a pleasant face (taste) perfumed with the four spices (<s>cāturjāta</s>) and camphor. (GRht 19.44)

children.text: atha pathyānāha śāperityādi // GRhtCM_19.43-44:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now he states the wholesome foods (<s>pathya</s>), with 'of rice' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.43–44:1)

children.text:
śāpeḥ ṣaṣṭikādeḥ piṣṭodbhavabhojanaṃ piṣṭakotpannaṃ ca tadbhojanaṃ ceti
                            // GRhtCM_19.43-44:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Of rice' (<s>śāli</s>) such as <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> and the like; 'food produced from flour' — food that is produced from flour, and that food. (GRhtCM 19.43–44:2)

children.text: ājyaṃ ghṛtam // GRhtCM_19.43-44:3 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ājya</s> means ghee (<s>ghṛta</s>). (GRhtCM 19.43–44:3)

With what? With green-gram (<s>mudga</s>) and meat-broths; <s>mudga</s> is well-known. Here, especially, meats should be eaten; and cow's milk should be consumed. Again, <s>mastu</s> — a cow's-milk product — should especially be eaten. (GRhtCM 19.43–44:4)

children.text:
pāne akṣāraṃ japaṃ miṣṭajapaṃ prayojyaṃ punaḥ yāni kāni miṣṭāni dravyāṇi
                            atrānuktatamāni praśastāni śreṣṭhāni punaḥ
                            caturjātakakarpūrāmodamuditamukhaṃ yathā syāt tathā dravyaṃ peyaṃ
                            pātavyaṃ caturjātakaṃ tvakpatraipānāgakesaraṃ karpūraṃ ghanasāraṃ eṣām
                            āmodena parimapena muditaṃ yanmukhaṃ vāsitamukham ityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_19.43-44:5 //
children.translated_text: For drinking, non-alkaline water — sweet water — should be used. Again, whatever sweet substances [there are], those unspecified here, are recommended — the best. Again, the beverage should be such that the mouth becomes delighted by the fragrance of the four spices (<s>cāturjāta</s>) and camphor. The four spices are: cinnamon bark (<s>tvak</s>), bay leaf (<s>patra</s>), cardamom (<s>elā</s>), and saffron (<s>nāgakesara</s>); camphor is <s>ghanasāra</s>; by their fragrance — their perfume — the mouth that is delighted, meaning scented-mouth, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.43–44:5)

children.text: yuvatyā jappanaṃ kāryaṃ yuvatyā cāṅgamardanam /
children.translated_text: Conversation with a young woman should be done; and by a young woman, body-massage [should be performed];

children.text: tasyāḥ sparśanamātreṇa dehe kramati sūtakaḥ /
children.translated_text: by the mere touch of her, mercury pervades the body —

children.text: iti viśeṣo granthāntarāt // GRhtCM_19.43-44:6 //
children.translated_text: thus is the special [instruction] from another treatise. (GRhtCM 19.43–44:6)

children.text: madyāranālapānaṃ tailaṃ dadhi vā rase neṣṭam /
children.translated_text: Drinking of liquor and sour gruel (<s>āranāla</s>), oil, or yogurt is undesirable during <s>rasa</s> [treatment];

children.text: kaṭutailenābhyaṅgaṃ vapuṣi na kuryādrasāyane matimān // GRht_19.45 //
children.translated_text: an intelligent person should not apply pungent oil (<s>kaṭutaila</s>) for body-massage during <s>rasāyana</s>. (GRht 19.45)

children.text: apathyānyāha madyetyādi // GRhtCM_19.45:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the unwholesome things (<s>apathya</s>), with 'liquor' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.45:1)

children.text:
madyāranāpetyādi madyaṃ surā āranāpaṃ kāñjikaṃ tayoḥ pānaṃ neṣṭaṃ na
                            praśastaṃ vā taipaṃ dadhi na neṣṭaṃ taipaṃ tipodbhavaṃ dadhi
                            dugdhavikāraḥ etayorapi pānaṃ na praśastaṃ kaṭutaipena sarṣapataipena
                            vapuṣi abhyaṅgaṃ mardanaṃ na kuryāt // GRhtCM_19.45:2 //
children.translated_text: 'Liquor and sour gruel' and so forth — liquor (<s>madya</s>) is <s>surā</s> (alcohol); sour gruel (<s>āranāla</s>) is <s>kāñjika</s> (fermented rice-water); drinking of these two is undesirable — not recommended; or oil — oil derived from sesame seeds; yogurt — a milk product; drinking of these two also is not recommended. With pungent oil — mustard oil — one should not perform body-massage — rubbing — on the body. (GRhtCM 19.45:2)

children.text: matimān rasāyane adhikaraṇe ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.45:3 //
children.translated_text: An intelligent person — [should observe this] in the context of <s>rasāyana</s>, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.45:3)

children.text: dagdham apakvam amadhuram uṣṇaṃ kṣīraṃ na naṣṭamāṃsaṃ tu /
children.translated_text: Burnt [food], uncooked, non-sweet, hot milk, nor spoiled meat;

children.text: paryuṣitaṃ phalamūlaṃ bhakṣyaṃ naivātra nirdiṣṭam // GRht_19.46 //
children.translated_text: stale fruits and roots — these are not prescribed as food here [in <s>rasāyana</s>]. (GRht 19.46)

children.text:
dagdhaṃ dravyaṃ rasāyane neṣṭaṃ apakvaṃ ca neṣṭaṃ amadhuraṃ
                            kaṭutiktakaṣāyāmpapavaṇaṃ ca neṣṭaṃ uṣṇaṃ vahnitaptamiti tu punaḥ
                            naṣṭamāṃsaṃ ninditamāṃsaṃ neṣṭaṃ punaḥ paryuṣitaṃ saṃdhānīkṛtaṃ
                            evaṃvidhaṃ phapamūpaṃ phapaṃ mūpaṃ ca atra rasāyane bhakṣyaṃ na
                            nirdiṣṭaṃ kathitaṃ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Burnt substances are undesirable in <s>rasāyana</s>; uncooked is also undesirable; non-sweet — that which is pungent, bitter, astringent, sour, or salty — is also undesirable; hot — heated by fire; again, spoiled meat — condemned meat — is undesirable. Again, stale — fermented — such fruits and roots — fruits and roots — are not prescribed as food, not spoken of, here in <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: kūṣmāṇḍaṃ karkaṭī caiva kapiṅgaṃ kāraveppakam /
children.translated_text: Pumpkin (<s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s>), cucumber (<s>karkaṭī</s>), sparrow (<s>kapiṅga</s>), <s>kāravelā</s> (bitter melon),

children.text: kusumbhikā ca karkoṭī kadapī kākamācikā /
children.translated_text: <s>kusumbhikā</s>, spiny gourd (<s>karkoṭī</s>), plantain (<s>kadalī</s>), black nightshade (<s>kākamācikā</s>) —

children.text: kakārāṣṭakametaddhi varjayedrasabhakṣakaḥ /
children.translated_text: this group of eight [foods] beginning with 'ka' should be avoided by one who consumes mercury.

children.text: iti granthāntare // GRhtCM_19.46:1 //
children.translated_text: Thus from another treatise. (GRhtCM 19.46:1)

children.text: atha laṅghanaṃ na kāryaṃ yāmādho bhojanaṃ naiva /
children.translated_text: Now, fasting (<s>laṅghana</s>) should not be done; nor should one eat before a <s>yāma</s> (watch) [has elapsed];

children.text: ityapanīya niṣiddhaṃ rasarāje dhīmatā kāryam // GRht_19.47 //
children.translated_text: thus, having removed what is forbidden, the intelligent person should attend to the king of <s>rasas</s>. (GRht 19.47)

children.text:
asmin rasāyane paṅghanaṃ na kāryaṃ punar yāmādhaḥ praharamadhye bhojanaṃ
                            na kāryam ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.47:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In this <s>rasāyana</s>, fasting should not be done; again, one should not eat within a <s>yāma</s> (watch) — within the middle of a <s>prahara</s> (three-hour period), is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.47:1)

children.text: varjitacintākopaḥ kuryācca sukhāmbunā snānam /
children.translated_text: Having abandoned worry and anger, one should bathe with pleasant water;

children.text: noccāṭayed grahajvararākṣasabhūtāni mātṛdevīṃśca // GRht_19.48 //
children.translated_text: one should not exorcise (<s>uccāṭayet</s>) planetary demons (<s>graha</s>), fever, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>bhūtas</s>, or the mother-goddesses (<s>mātṛdevī</s>). (GRht 19.48)

children.text: taccāha varjitetyādi // GRhtCM_19.48:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That he states, with 'having abandoned' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.48:1)
'Having abandoned worry and anger' — worry and anger, being of this nature, one in whom these are abandoned; being such, one should bathe with pleasant water — pleasantly warm water. (GRhtCM 19.48:2)

children.text:
graharākṣasabhūtāni noccāṭayet grahaṇādgrahāḥ piśācādayaḥ jvaro rogarājaḥ
                            rākṣasāḥ kravyādāḥ bhūtāni devayonayaḥ etāni noccāṭayet svasthānānna
                            cāpayet // GRhtCM_19.48:3 //
children.translated_text: Planetary spirits (<s>graha</s>), <s>rākṣasas</s>, and <s>bhūtas</s> — one should not exorcise [them]. <s>Grahas</s> — from seizing — are <s>piśācas</s> (goblins) and the like; fever is the king of diseases; <s>rākṣasas</s> are flesh-eaters; <s>bhūtas</s> are beings of divine origin; one should not exorcise these — should not drive them from their places. (GRhtCM 19.48:3)

children.text:
punarmātṛdevīṃśca mātaraḥ saptamātaraḥ devyo dakṣiṇyādayaḥ tā api
                            noccāṭayet // GRhtCM_19.48:4 //
children.translated_text: Again, the mother-goddesses (<s>mātṛdevī</s>) — the mothers are the seven mothers (<s>saptamātṛ</s>); the goddesses are <s>Dakṣiṇā</s> and the like; those too one should not exorcise. (GRhtCM 19.48:4)

children.text: parame brahmaṇi līnaḥ praśāntacittaḥ samatvamāpannaḥ /
children.translated_text: Absorbed in the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, with mind at peace, having attained equanimity,

children.text: āśvāsayan trivargaṃ vijitya rasānandaparitṛptaḥ // GRht_19.49 //
children.translated_text: reassuring the three aims (<s>trivarga</s>), having conquered [the senses], filled with the bliss of <s>rasa</s>. (GRht 19.49)

children.text: cintākopanirodhe hetum āha parame ityādi // GRhtCM_19.49:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the reason for restraining worry and anger, with 'supreme' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.49:1)

children.text:
rasāyanakartā parame brahmaṇi citsvarūpe pīnaḥ tanmayatāṃ prāpto bhavet
                            praśāntacittaśca viṣayebhyo nivṛttamanā bhavet samatvamāpannaḥ svasute
                            śatrau ca nirvairo yathā syāt tathā trivargaṃ dharmārthakāmarūpaṃ
                            vijitya rasānandaparitṛpto bhavet harṣaparipūrita ityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_19.49:2 //
children.translated_text: The practitioner of <s>rasāyana</s> should be absorbed in the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — in the nature of pure consciousness — having attained identity with it; with peaceful mind — with thoughts withdrawn from sense-objects; having attained equanimity — impartial toward one's own son and toward an enemy; having conquered the three aims (<s>trivarga</s>) — <s>dharma</s> (duty), <s>artha</s> (wealth), and <s>kāma</s> (desire) — filled with the bliss of <s>rasa</s> — filled with joy, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.49:2)

children.text: yastyaktvā śāstravidhiṃ pravartate svecchayā rase mūḍhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whoever, having abandoned the rules of the <s>śāstra</s>, proceeds by his own will, deluded, regarding mercury,

children.text: tasya viruddhācārād ajīrṇamutpadyate nitarām // GRht_19.50 //
children.translated_text: for him, from contrary conduct, indigestion (<s>ajīrṇa</s>) arises greatly. (GRht 19.50)

children.text: vidherniyatatvaṃ darśayannāha ya ityādi // GRhtCM_19.50:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Showing the strict necessity of the rules, he says, with 'whoever' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.50:1)

children.text:
yaḥ pumān śāstravidhiṃ tyaktvā svecchayā ucchṛṅkhapamanasā rase sūte
                            pravartate sa mūḍhaḥ jñānaśūnyaḥ tasya puṃsaḥ viruddhācārāt
                            nitarāmatiśayena ajīrṇam utpadyate tadrasājīrṇamiti // GRhtCM_19.50:2
                            //
children.translated_text: Whatever man, having abandoned the rules of the <s>śāstra</s>, by his own will — with an unrestrained mind — proceeds regarding mercury, that deluded one — devoid of knowledge — for that man, from contrary conduct, greatly — exceedingly — indigestion arises; that is <s>rasājīrṇa</s> (mercury-indigestion). (GRhtCM 19.50:2)

children.text: sambhavatīhājīrṇe nidrālasyaṃ jvarastamo dāhaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is possible that in indigestion [there arises]: excessive sleep, lethargy, fever, stupor (<s>tamas</s>), burning;

children.text: nābhitalaśūlamalpaṃ jaḍatāruciraṅgabhaṅgaśca // GRht_19.51 //
children.translated_text: slight pain in the lower abdomen (<s>nābhitala</s>), dullness, loss of appetite (<s>aruci</s>), and body-ache (<s>aṅgabhaṅga</s>). (GRht 19.51)

children.text: rasājīrṇapakṣaṇamāha sambhavatītyādi // GRhtCM_19.51:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the symptoms of <s>rasājīrṇa</s> (mercury-indigestion), with 'it is possible' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.51:1)

children.text:
iha rasāyane ajīrṇaṃ yadā sambhavati utpadyate tadā etāni pakṣaṇāni syuḥ
                            // GRhtCM_19.51:2 //
children.translated_text: In this <s>rasāyana</s>, when indigestion occurs — arises — then these symptoms would appear. (GRhtCM 19.51:2)

children.text:
nidrā atiśayena nidrā āpasyaṃ aṅgāṅgaśaithipyaṃ jvaraḥ prasiddhaḥ tamo
                            mūrchā dāha ūṣmā punarnābhitape bastau appamappaṃ śūpaṃ jaḍatāsyasya
                            aruciḥ nirabhipāpitā bhaṅgo+aṅgasya aṅgamardanaṃ bhokturetāni pakṣaṇāni
                            rasājīrṇe syur ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.51:3 //
children.translated_text: Sleep — excessive drowsiness; lethargy — looseness of all limbs; fever — well-known; stupor (<s>tamas</s>) — fainting; burning — heat. Again, slight pain in the lower abdomen (<s>nābhitala</s>) — in the bladder; dullness — of the mouth, meaning loss of taste; loss of appetite — lack of desire [for food]; body-ache — pounding of the body. For the eater [of mercury], these symptoms would occur in <s>rasājīrṇa</s>, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.51:3)

children.text: jñātvetyevam ajīrṇam asya pracchādanāya yogo+ayam /
children.translated_text: Having recognized such indigestion, this formula is for its concealment (remedy);

children.text: kāryo divasatritayaṃ saṃtyajya rasāyanaṃ sudhiyā // GRht_19.52 //
children.translated_text: the wise person should apply [it] for three days, having suspended the <s>rasāyana</s>. (GRht 19.52)

children.text: ajīrṇe'pyupāyamāha jñātvetyādi // GRhtCM_19.52:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the remedy even for indigestion, with 'having recognized' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.52:1)

children.text:
ityevam uktaprakāreṇa nidrādipakṣaṇenājīrṇaṃ jñātvā dhīmatā puṃsā
                            asyājīrṇasya pracchādanāya vināśāya rasāyanaṃ saṃtyajya divasatritayaṃ
                            yogaḥ kāryaḥ // GRhtCM_19.52:2 //
children.translated_text: Thus — in the aforesaid manner — having recognized the indigestion through symptoms such as excessive sleep and the like, the intelligent person, for the concealment — destruction — of this indigestion, having suspended the <s>rasāyana</s> for the duration of three days, should apply the formula. (GRhtCM 19.52:2)

children.text: karkoṭīmūlarasaṃ kaṣāyam atha sindhunā pibettridinam /
children.translated_text: One should drink <s>karkoṭī</s> (spiny gourd) root-juice, or a decoction, with rock salt (<s>sindhu</s>), for three days;

children.text: sauvarcalasahitaṃ vā gojalasahitaṃ rasājīrṇe // GRht_19.53 //
children.translated_text: or [drink it] with <s>sauvarcala</s> (black salt), or with cow's urine (<s>gojala</s>), in <s>rasājīrṇa</s> (mercury-indigestion). (GRht 19.53)

children.text: taccāha karkoṭītyādi // GRhtCM_19.53:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That he states, with '<s>karkoṭī</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.53:1)

children.text:
karkoṭīmūparasaṃ karkoṭī yā vappī tasyāḥ mūparasaṃ tridinaṃ pibet vātha
                            kaṣāyaṃ kathaṃ sindhunā saindhavena sahitaṃ pibet vā tatkvāthaṃ
                            gojapasahitaṃ gomūtramipitaṃ rasājīrṇe pibet sauvarcapasahitamiti
                            sauvarcapasya prativāpaṃ karkoṭīrase nikṣipya pibet tridinaṃ
                            sarvatretyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.53:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Karkoṭī</s> root-juice — <s>karkoṭī</s> is the plant <s>vallī</s> (creeper); its root-juice — one should drink for three days. Or the decoction; how? With rock salt (<s>sindhu</s>, i.e., <s>saindhava</s>), one should drink. Or that decoction, with cow's urine (<s>gojala</s>, i.e., <s>gomūtra</s>), combined — in <s>rasājīrṇa</s>, one should drink. With <s>sauvarcala</s> (black salt) — having added <s>sauvarcala</s> as a counter-additive into the <s>karkoṭī</s>-juice — one should drink for three days in all [cases], is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.53:2)

children.text: piṣṭvātha mātuluṅgīṃ pibati rasaṃ śuṇṭhisaindhavaṃ prātaḥ /
children.translated_text: Or, having ground <s>mātuluṅgī</s> (citron), one should drink the juice with dry ginger (<s>śuṇṭhī</s>) and rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>), in the morning;

children.text: kvathitaṃ gosalilena tu rakṣati samyak rasājīrṇam // GRht_19.54 //
children.translated_text: boiled with cow's urine (<s>gosalila</s>), it properly protects against <s>rasājīrṇa</s> (mercury-indigestion). (GRht 19.54)

children.text: anyaccāha piṣṭvetyādi // GRhtCM_19.54:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states another [remedy], with 'having ground' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.54:1)

children.text:
mātupuṅgasyeyaṃ jaṭā mātupuṅgī tāṃ piṣṭvā tasyā rasaṃ śuṇṭhī saindhavaṃ
                            ca yaḥ pumān prātaḥ pibati tu punaḥ kvathitaṃ tasyāḥ kaṣāyaṃ gosapipena
                            yaḥ pibati rasājīrṇe taṃ puruṣaṃ rakṣati na vināśayatītyarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_19.54:2 //
children.translated_text: The root (<s>jaṭā</s>) of <s>mātuluṅga</s> (citron) — that is <s>mātuluṅgī</s>; having ground it, one who drinks its juice with dry ginger (<s>śuṇṭhī</s>) and rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>) in the morning; again, whoever drinks the decoction — its extract — boiled with cow's urine (<s>gosalila</s>), in <s>rasājīrṇa</s> — it protects that person, meaning it does not destroy [him], is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.54:2)

children.text: kathamapi yaccājñānāt nāgādikalaṅkito raso bhuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: If somehow, through ignorance, mercury tainted with lead (<s>nāga</s>) and such is consumed,

children.text: tannodanāya ca pibet gojalakaṭukāravalliśiphāḥ // GRht_19.55 //
children.translated_text: for expelling that, one should drink cow's urine (<s>gojala</s>) with bitter <s>kāravallī</s> (Momordica charantia) roots. (GRht 19.55)

children.text: nāgādiyuktarasabhuktopāyam āha katham apītyādi // GRhtCM_19.55:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the remedy for one who has consumed mercury mixed with lead and the like, with 'somehow' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.55:1)

children.text:
ca punaḥ yat yasmāt nāgādikapaṅkito rasaḥ nāgavaṅgasahito
                            raso+ajñānātkathamapi bhuktaḥ tannodanāya tasya nāgavaṅgāṅkitarasasya
                            nodanāya gojapakaṭukāravappiśiphāḥ gojapaṃ gomūtraṃ kaṭutiktā
                            kāravappīśiphā kāravappīpatāyāḥ śiphā jaṭā etadauṣadhaṃ pibet tena
                            nāgavaṅgādidoṣo vinaśyati // GRhtCM_19.55:2 //
children.translated_text: Again, since mercury tainted with lead (<s>nāga</s>) and the like — combined with lead and tin — [was consumed] through ignorance, somehow; for expelling that — for the expulsion of that mercury tainted with lead and tin — [one should drink] cow's urine (<s>gojala</s>, i.e., <s>gomūtra</s>) with bitter <s>kāravallī</s> roots — the roots (<s>śiphā</s>, i.e., <s>jaṭā</s>) of the <s>kāravallī</s> creeper, which is bitter; this medicine one should drink — by that, the fault of lead and tin is destroyed. (GRhtCM 19.55:2)

children.text: śarapuṃkhāsuradālīpaṭolabimbīśca kākamācī ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Śarapuṅkhā</s> (Tephrosia), <s>suradālī</s> (Caesalpinia), <s>paṭola</s> (pointed gourd), <s>bimbī</s> (Coccinia), and <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade) —

children.text: ekatamā ceduditā śṛtāmajīrṇe hi seveta // GRht_19.56 //
children.translated_text: whichever one among these is prescribed, boiled, one should consume in indigestion. (GRht 19.56)

children.text: taccāha śarapuṅkhetyādi // GRhtCM_19.56:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That he states, with '<s>śarapuṅkhā</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.56:1)

Among these medicines, whichever one is prescribed — mentioned — boiled, meaning decocted — that one should certainly be consumed in indigestion; by that, indigestion is destroyed, is the purport. (GRhtCM 19.56:2)

What are those medicines? <s>Śarapuṅkhā</s> — well-known; <s>suradālī</s> — <s>devadālī</s>; <s>paṭola</s> — well-known by name; <s>bimbī</s> — <s>gopā</s> (Coccinia); <s>kākamācī</s> — well-known; these [are they], is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.56:3)

children.text: atyamlalavaṇakaṭukai rasasaṃsrāvo jaro bhavati /
children.translated_text: From excessively sour, salty, and pungent [foods], mercury-flux (<s>rasasaṃsrāva</s>) or aging (<s>jara</s>) occurs;

children.text: atimadhuraiśca vinaśyati jaṭharavahniḥ satatabhuktaiśca // GRht_19.57 //
children.translated_text: and from excessively sweet [foods] consumed constantly, the digestive fire (<s>jaṭharavahni</s>) is destroyed. (GRht 19.57)

children.text: taccāha atyampetyādi // GRhtCM_19.57:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That he states, with 'excessively sour' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.57:1)

'Exceedingly sour' — vinegar and the like; 'exceedingly salty' — alkalis and the like; 'exceedingly pungent' — neem, <s>kaṭukī</s> and the like — by these, the digestive fluid (<s>rasasaṃsrāva</s>) becomes <s>jara</s> — an agent of aging; 'that which ages' is <s>jara</s>. (GRhtCM 19.57:2)

children.text:
punarapi madhuraiḥ ikṣurasādibhiḥ satatabhuktaiḥ jaṭharavahniḥ koṣṭhāgniḥ
                            vinaśyati abhyāśrayo vinaśyatītyabhiprāyaḥ // GRhtCM_19.57:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, sweet [substances] — such as sugarcane juice and the like — when constantly consumed, the gastric fire (<s>jaṭharavahni</s>) — the digestive fire of the gut — is destroyed; the intended meaning is that the receptacle is destroyed. (GRhtCM 19.57:3)

children.text: yaḥ punarevaṃ satataṃ karoti mūḍhaḥ samāhāram /
children.translated_text: He who, being foolish, constantly makes such a diet,

children.text: tasya vinaśyatyagnirna khalu krāmati raso bhaved vyādhiḥ // GRht_19.58 //
children.translated_text: his [digestive] fire is destroyed; the mercury certainly does not transmute; and disease arises. (GRht 19.58)

children.text: tadviśeṣamāha ya ityādi // GRhtCM_19.58:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the distinction of that, with 'he who' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.58:1)

children.text:
yaḥ punar mūḍho mūrkho 'jīrṇānantaraṃ atyampapavaṇakaṭukāhāraṃ satataṃ
                            nirantaraṃ karoti tasyāgniḥ koṣṭhāgnir vinaśyati rasaśca na krāmati
                            svaguṇānna prakāśayati // GRhtCM_19.58:2 //
children.translated_text: He who — a fool, an ignorant person — after indigestion, constantly — without interruption — makes a diet of excessively sour, salty, and pungent [foods] — his [digestive] fire — the fire of the gut — is destroyed; and the mercury does not transmute — does not manifest its qualities. (GRhtCM 19.58:2)

children.text: tarhi kiṃ bhavedityāha vyādhirbhaved ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.58:3 //
children.translated_text: Then what would happen? He states: 'Disease would arise,' is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.58:3)

children.text: yastu mahāgnisahatvād rasācchatasahasralakṣavedhīśaḥ /
children.translated_text: But he who, due to the power of great [digestive] fire, from mercury becomes a hundred-thousand-<s>lakṣa</s>-fold transmuter —

children.text: anayā kriyayā sidhyati sa yatnādrasakriyāyogāt // GRht_19.59 //
children.translated_text: he is perfected by this procedure, through effort, by the application of mercury-operations. (GRht 19.59)

children.text:
rasācchatasahasrapakṣavedhī bhavet sa yatnāt anayā pūrvoktakriyayā
                            sidhyati // GRhtCM_19.59:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] From mercury, [one who] becomes a hundred-thousand-<s>lakṣa</s>-fold transmuter — he, through effort, is perfected by this previously stated procedure. (GRhtCM 19.59:1)

children.text: śatasahasralakṣavedhī koṭir athārbudanirbudaṃ vāpi /
children.translated_text: [Whether] a hundred-thousand-<s>lakṣa</s>-fold transmuter, or a <s>koṭi</s>-fold, or even an <s>arbuda</s>-<s>nirbuda</s>-fold —

children.text: piṣṭaṃ bhuñjīta rasaṃ balisahitaṃ siddhido bhavati // GRht_19.60 //
children.translated_text: one should consume the ground mercury, accompanied by sulphur (<s>bali</s>); it becomes a bestower of perfections. (GRht 19.60)

children.text: athottaravidhānena pakṣaṇamāha śatetyādi // GRhtCM_19.60:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the characteristics by the superior method, with 'hundred' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.60:1)

children.text: śatasahasrapakṣavedhī rasaḥ // GRhtCM_19.60:2 //
children.translated_text: Mercury [that is] a hundred-thousand-<s>lakṣa</s>-fold transmuter. (GRhtCM 19.60:2)

children.text:
bapisahitaṃ piṣṭaṃ rasaṃ bhuñjīta bapinā gandhakena sahitam śatādārabhya
                            sahasrapakṣakoṭyarbudānāṃ krameṇa daśaguṇottaraṃ saṃkhyā jñātavyā //
                            GRhtCM_19.60:3 //
children.translated_text: One should consume the ground mercury accompanied by sulphur (<s>balin</s>/gandhaka); the numerical sequence from hundred through thousand, <s>lakṣa</s>, <s>koṭi</s>, and <s>arbuda</s> should be understood as increasing tenfold in succession. (GRhtCM 19.60:3)

children.text:
evaṃ kṛtaḥ san rasaḥ siddhido yathoktaguṇakṛdbhavatītyarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_19.60:4 //
children.translated_text: Mercury prepared in this manner becomes a bestower of perfections — produces the stated qualities, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.60:4)

children.text: krāmati tato hi sūto janayati putrāṃśca devagarbhābhān /
children.translated_text: Then mercury transmutes, and [the practitioner] begets sons resembling divine offspring;

children.text: strīṣu ca niścalakāmo bhavati valīpalitanirmuktaḥ // GRht_19.61 //
children.translated_text: in women, his desire remains unwavering; he becomes freed from wrinkles and grey hair. (GRht 19.61)

children.text: buddhirbalaṃ prabhāvaḥ saha cāyuṣā vardhate rasāyaninaḥ /
children.translated_text: Intelligence, strength, and power increase along with lifespan for the practitioner of <s>rasāyana</s>;

children.text: prāptasya divyabuddhiṃ divyāśca guṇāḥ pravardhante // GRht_19.62 //
children.translated_text: for one who has attained divine intelligence, the divine qualities flourish. (GRht 19.62)

children.text: evaṃ rasasaṃsiddho duḥkhajarāmaraṇavarjito guṇavān /
children.translated_text: Thus, one perfected by mercury, freed from suffering, old age, and death, endowed with virtues,

children.text: khegamanena ca nityaṃ saṃcarate sakalabhuvaneṣu // GRht_19.63 //
children.translated_text: by means of sky-travel (<s>khecara</s>), always wanders through all the worlds. (GRht 19.63)

children.text: dātā bhuvanatritaye sraṣṭā so+apīha padmayoniriva /
children.translated_text: A giver in the three worlds, a creator here like <s>Padmayoni</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>),

children.text: bhartā viṣṇuriva syātsaṃhartā rudravadbhavati // GRht_19.64 //
children.translated_text: a sustainer like <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and becomes a destroyer like <s>Rudra</s>. (GRht 19.64)

children.text: pūrvavidhānaṃ praśaṃsayann āha krāmatītyādi // GRhtCM_19.61-64:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Praising the previously stated method, he says 'transmutes' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.61-64:1)

children.text:
tataḥ pūrvavidhānataḥ sūtaḥ krāmati svaguṇān prakāśayati sūte krāmati
                            sati devagarbhābhān putrān janayati devagarbhavat ābhā kāntir yeṣāṃ te
                            tān punaḥ strīṣu niścapaḥ sadāsthāyī kāmo ratyabhipāṣo vā madano yasya
                            sa tathoktaḥ punar vapīpapitanirmuktaḥ vapyaśca papitāni ca tair
                            nirmukto vivarjitaḥ vapiścarma jarākṛtaṃ ityamaraḥ papitaṃ keśaśvetatvaṃ
                            evaṃvidho bhavati pumān iti śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_19.61-64:2 //
children.translated_text: Then — from the previously stated method — mercury transmutes — manifests its qualities; when mercury transmutes, [the practitioner] begets sons resembling divine offspring — whose luster is like that of divine embryos; furthermore, in women, his desire — the ever-abiding passion for love, or <s>Madana</s> (the god of love) — [remains steady]; he of such description; furthermore, freed from wrinkles and grey hair — <s>vali</s> is skin-wrinkling caused by old age, as per <s>Amara[kośa]</s>; <s>palita</s> is whiteness of hair — freed from, i.e., devoid of, these; such becomes the man, is the completion. (GRhtCM 19.61-64:2)

children.text: punaḥ kiṃ syādityāha buddhirityādi // GRhtCM_19.61-64:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, what would happen? He states, with 'intelligence' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.61-64:3)

children.text:
rasāyaninaḥ rasāyanaṃ prāptasya hi puṃsaḥ buddhirvardhate bapaṃ ca
                            vardhate kena saha āyuṣā jīvitakāpena saha punar divyabuddhiṃ prāptasya
                            rasāyaninaḥ divyāḥ prakaraṇādguṇā medhādayaḥ pravardhante prakāśanta
                            ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.61-64:4 //
children.translated_text: For the practitioner of <s>rasāyana</s> — for the man who has attained <s>rasāyana</s> — intelligence increases, and strength increases; with what? Together with lifespan — with the duration of life; furthermore, for the practitioner of <s>rasāyana</s> who has attained divine intelligence, the divine qualities — from context, those such as memory and the like — flourish, i.e., become manifest, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.61-64:4)

children.text: taccāha evamityādi // GRhtCM_19.61-64:5 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states that, with 'thus' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.61-64:5)

children.text:
evamamunā prakāreṇa rasasaṃsiddhaḥ puruṣaḥ rasaḥ pāradaḥ saṃsiddhaḥ
                            samyak siddho yasya vā rasena saṃsiddhaḥ jarāmaraṇavarjito bhavati
                            vṛddhatvavyādhirahita ityarthaḥ guṇavāṃśca bhavati guṇā medhādayaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_19.61-64:6 //
children.translated_text: Thus — in this manner — a man perfected by mercury — either mercury (<s>pārada</s>) is perfectly accomplished, or he is accomplished by means of mercury — becomes freed from old age and death — devoid of aging and disease, is the meaning; and becomes endowed with virtues — the virtues being memory and the like. (GRhtCM 19.61-64:6)

children.text:
punaḥ khegamanena ākāśagamanena nityaṃ sakapabhuvaneṣu samastapokeṣu
                            saṃcarate ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.61-64:7 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, by sky-travel — by aerial movement — he always wanders through all worlds — all realms, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.61-64:7)

children.text:
dātā bhuvanatritaye svargamṛtyupātāpe bhavati sarvādhika ityabhiprāyaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_19.61-64:8 //
children.translated_text: [He becomes] a giver in the three worlds — the heavenly, earthly, and subterranean [realms] — surpassing all, is the intended meaning. (GRhtCM 19.61-64:8)

children.text:
so+api pumān iha bhuvanatritaye svargamṛtyupātāpe sraṣṭā sarjako bhavati
                            // GRhtCM_19.61-64:9 //
children.translated_text: That man, here in the three worlds — the heavenly, earthly, and subterranean — becomes a creator, a maker. (GRhtCM 19.61-64:9)

children.text: ka iva padmayoniriva brahmeva // GRhtCM_19.61-64:10 //
children.translated_text: Like whom? Like <s>Padmayoni</s> — like <s>Brahmā</s>. (GRhtCM 19.61-64:10)

children.text:
punaḥ bhartā pāpanārthaṃ trikasya viṣṇuriva ca bhavati //
                            GRhtCM_19.61-64:11 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, he becomes a sustainer — for the protection — of the triple [world], like <s>Viṣṇu</s>. (GRhtCM 19.61-64:11)

children.text:
punaḥ saṃhartā rudravat bhavati sṛṣṭisthitivināśeṣu brahmādīnāṃ trayīva
                            syādityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.61-64:12 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, he becomes a destroyer like <s>Rudra</s>; in creation, sustenance, and dissolution, he becomes like the triad of <s>Brahmā</s> and others, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.61-64:12)

children.text: amarasundarīguṭikā
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>Amarasundarī guṭikā</s> (the Immortal-Beauty pill)

children.text: kāntābhrasattvahematāraṃ cārkaḥ samāṃśataḥ saṃkhyā /
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s> (magnetite), <s>abhrasattva</s> (mica-essence), gold, silver, and copper — in equal proportions [by] count;

children.text: baddhaṃ sūtasamāṃśaṃ dhmātaṃ golaṃ kṛtaṃ khoṭam // GRht_19.65 //
children.translated_text: bound [mercury] in equal parts, blown — [forms] a globule, made into an ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>). (GRht 19.65)

children.text: bāhye rasena liptaṃ vadanagataṃ śastravārakaṃ rogān /
children.translated_text: On the outside, smeared with mercury, [when] placed in the mouth, it wards off weapons [and]

children.text: hanti hi śarīrasaṃsthān nāmnāmarasundarī guṭikā // GRht_19.66 //
children.translated_text: destroys diseases residing in the body — [this is] the pill named <s>Amarasundarī</s>. (GRht 19.66)

children.text:
amarasundarīguṭikāvidhānaṃ guṇāṃścāha kāntetyādi // GRhtCM_19.65-66:1
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the method and virtues of the <s>Amarasundarī guṭikā</s>, with '<s>kānta</s>' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.65-66:1)

children.text: kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ abhraṃ yugmam // GRhtCM_19.65-66:2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s> is loadstone; <s>abhra</s> is the pair [of substances]. (GRhtCM 19.65-66:2)

children.text:
abhrakasattvaṃ pratītaṃ hema kanakaṃ tāraṃ ca tat ekavadbhāvo dvandvatvāt
                            punararkaḥ tāmram eṣāṃ kāntādīnāṃ saṃkhyā gaṇanā samāṃśataḥ samabhāgato
                            jñeyā // GRhtCM_19.65-66:3 //
children.translated_text: <s>Abhrasattva</s> (mica-essence) is well-known; <s>hema</s> is gold; and <s>tāra</s> (silver) — these are treated as one [compound] being a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound); furthermore, <s>arka</s> is copper — of these, <s>kānta</s> and others, the count — the enumeration — should be known as being in equal proportions. (GRhtCM 19.65-66:3)

children.text:
punaḥ sūtasamāṃśaṃ pāradena tupyabhāgaṃ dhmātaṃ kuryāt andhamūṣāyāṃ iti
                            śeṣaḥ // GRhtCM_19.65-66:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, in equal parts with mercury — in equal proportion with <s>pārada</s> — one should blow [it] in a closed crucible (<s>andhamūṣā</s>), is the completion. (GRhtCM 19.65-66:4)

children.text:
kiṃkṛtaṃ sat bāhye baddhagopopari rasena māraṇāyām uktadraveṇa piptaṃ sat
                            dhmātaṃ kuryāt // GRhtCM_19.65-66:5 //
children.translated_text: What should be done? On the outside — on top of the bound globule — having smeared with mercury — with the liquid mentioned for calcination — one should blow [it]. (GRhtCM 19.65-66:5)

children.text:
itthaṃ kṛtaṃ khoṭaṃ piṣṭistambhaḥ gopākāraṃ bhavati // GRhtCM_19.65-66:6
                            //
children.translated_text: Made in this manner, the ingot (<s>khoṭa</s>) — [the <s>piṣṭi-stambha</s>] — becomes globule-shaped. (GRhtCM 19.65-66:6)

children.text:
tat vadanagataṃ mukhāntaḥsthitaṃ śastravārakaṃ syāt asmiṃśca vadanaṃ gate
                            sati śarīre khaḍgādīnāṃ prahāro na pagati // GRhtCM_19.65-66:7 //
children.translated_text: That, placed in the mouth — situated inside the mouth — would ward off weapons; and when this is placed in the mouth, the blow of swords and the like does not reach the body. (GRhtCM 19.65-66:7)

children.text:
guṭir iyaṃ nāmnā abhidhānena amarasundarīguṭikā jñeyā //
                            GRhtCM_19.65-66:8 //
children.translated_text: This pill should be known by the name <s>Amarasundarī guṭikā</s>. (GRhtCM 19.65-66:8)

children.text:
iyaṃ śarīrasthā mukhe anyasthape vā sthitā satī śarīrasthān rogān hanti
                            vināśayati // GRhtCM_19.65-66:9 //
children.translated_text: This [pill], residing in the body — situated in the mouth, or placed elsewhere [on the body] — destroys — eliminates — diseases residing in the body. (GRhtCM 19.65-66:9)

children.text:
anuktamapi mānaṃ pañcaniṣkapramāṇaṃ jñeyamityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.65-66:10
                            //
children.translated_text: The measure, though unstated, should be understood as five <s>niṣkas</s> in weight, is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.65-66:10)

children.text: ityamarasundarī guṭikā // GRhtCM_19.65-66:11 //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends the description of] the <s>Amarasundarī guṭikā</s>. (GRhtCM 19.65-66:11)

children.text:
hemnā vā rajatena vāpi sahito dhmāto vrajatyekatāmakṣīṇo niviḍo guḍaśca
                            guṭikāḥ karoti dīrghojjvapāḥ // GRhtCM_19.65-66:12 //
children.translated_text: Combined with gold or with silver, when blown it attains unity — imperishable, dense, and compact — it makes pills, long and bright. (GRhtCM 19.65-66:12)

children.text:
cūrṇaṃ tatpaṭuvatprayāti vihitaghṛṣṭo na muñcenmapaṃ nirgandho dravati
                            kṣaṇātsa hi mato baddhābhidhāno rasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Its powder flows like salt; when properly rubbed, it does not release impurity; odorless, it melts in an instant — such is considered mercury called 'bound.'

children.text: iti granthāntare // GRhtCM_19.65-66:13 //
children.translated_text: Thus in another text. (GRhtCM 19.65-66:13)

children.text: mṛtasaṃjīvanīguṭikā
children.translated_text: [Section on] <s>Mṛtasaṃjīvanī guṭikā</s> (the Reviver-of-the-Dead pill)

children.text: yaḥ pūrvoktaḥ sūto lakṣādūrdhvaṃ ca vedhate lohān /
children.translated_text: The mercury described before, [which] transmutes metals beyond a <s>lakṣa</s>-fold —

children.text: baddhe sāraṇayogair mukhāsthe ca jārayedratnam // GRht_19.67 //
children.translated_text: when bound by liquefaction methods, and placed in the mouth, one should digest a gem [into it]. (GRht 19.67)

children.text: yuktaḥ samāṃśanāgaiḥ suralohāyaskāntatāpyasattvaiśca /
children.translated_text: Combined with equal parts of lead, divine-metal (gold), magnetite, and pyrite-essence —

children.text: abhrakasattvasametā guṭikā mṛtasaṃjīvanī nāma // GRht_19.68 //
children.translated_text: together with mica-essence — [this] pill is named <s>Mṛtasaṃjīvanī</s> (Reviver-of-the-Dead). (GRht 19.68)

children.text: hemayutā gulucchake mukuṭe vā kaṇṭhasūtrakarṇe vā /
children.translated_text: Combined with gold, [placed] in a topknot or in a crown, or on a neck-cord or ear —

children.text: mṛtyubhayaśokarogaviṣaśastrajarāsatataduḥkhasaṅghātam // GRht_19.69 //
children.translated_text: [it destroys] the aggregate of death, fear, grief, disease, poison, weapons, old age, and constant suffering. (GRht 19.69)

children.text: yasyāṅge nihiteyaṃ guṭikā mṛtasaṃjīvanī nāma /
children.translated_text: On whose body this pill named <s>Mṛtasaṃjīvanī</s> is placed —

children.text: so+asurayakṣakinnarapūjyatamaḥ siddhayogīndraiḥ // GRht_19.70 //
children.translated_text: he becomes most worshipped by <s>asuras</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, perfected ones, and lords of <s>yogins</s>. (GRht 19.70)

children.text: prakṣālya toyamadhye guṭikā ghaṭikādvayaṃ tataḥ kṣiptvā /
children.translated_text: Having washed [it], [if] the pill is cast into water for two <s>ghaṭikās</s> (48 minutes), then —

children.text: tacceyaṃ vadanagatā mṛtakasyotthāpanaṃ kurute // GRht_19.71 //
children.translated_text: that [water], [or] this [pill] placed in the mouth, effects the raising of a dead person. (GRht 19.71)

children.text: toyaṃ tadeva pibati svasthaṃ pathyānvitastataḥ puruṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: A healthy man, following the proper diet, drinks that very water; thereafter

children.text: labhate divyaṃ sa vapurmṛtyujarāvarjitaḥ sudṛḍham // GRht_19.72 //
children.translated_text: he obtains a divine body, freed from death and old age, very firm. (GRht 19.72)

children.text:
mṛtasaṃjīvanīguṭikāvidhānaṃ guṇāṃścāha ya ityādi // GRhtCM_19.67-72:1
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the method and virtues of the <s>Mṛtasaṃjīvanī guṭikā</s>, with 'he who' and so forth. (GRhtCM 19.67-72:1)

children.text:
yaḥ pūrvoktaḥ sūto pakṣādūrdhvaṃ koṭyarbudādi pohān rūpyādīn vedhate
                            tasminbaddhe sūte mukhasthe prakāśamukhayantre sthāpite sāraṇayogaiḥ
                            sāraṇataipādibhiḥ ratnaṃ vajrādikaṃ jārayet // GRhtCM_19.67-72:2 //
children.translated_text: The mercury described before — [that which transmutes] beyond a <s>lakṣa</s>-fold — <s>koṭi</s>, <s>arbuda</s>, etc. — metals such as silver and the like — it transmutes; when that mercury is bound, and placed in the mouth — set in an open-mouth apparatus — it should digest a gem — diamond and the like — by means of liquefaction methods — liquefaction-oil and the like. (GRhtCM 19.67-72:2)

children.text:
punaḥ samāṃśanāgais tupyāṃśasīsakaiḥ sūto yuktaḥ kāryaḥ
                            surapohāyaskāntatāpyasattvaiśca yuktaḥ kāryaḥ surapohaṃ kanakaṃ
                            ayaskāntaḥ kāntapohaṃ tāpyasattvaṃ mākṣikasāraṃ etaiḥ
                            abhrakasattvasametā satī mṛtasaṃjīvanī nāma guṭikā bhavati punastatra
                            mūṣāyāmiyaṃ hemayutā kāryā // GRhtCM_19.67-72:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, mercury should be combined with equal parts of lead — in equal proportion with lead; and combined with divine-metal (gold), magnetite-iron (<s>kānta</s>), and pyrite-essence — divine-metal is gold; <s>ayaskānta</s> is the magnetite-metal; <s>tāpyasattva</s> is pyrite-essence — with these; together with mica-essence — the pill named <s>Mṛtasaṃjīvanī</s> comes into being; furthermore, in a crucible, this should be made combined with gold. (GRhtCM 19.67-72:3)

children.text:
punar iyaṃ guṭikā nityaṃ yasya gupucchake nihitā bhavati vā mukuṭe kirīṭe
                            vā kaṇṭhasūtrakarṇe kaṇṭhasūtraṃ ca karṇaśca kaṇṭhasūtrakarṇaṃ tasmin vā
                            aṅge hastapādādau tasya
                            mṛtyubhayaśokarogaśastrajarāsatataduḥkhasaṃghātaṃ naśyati ityadhyāhāraḥ
                            // GRhtCM_19.67-72:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, this pill — [when] always placed in one's topknot, or in a crown — a diadem — or on a neck-cord and ear — 'neck-cord and ear' being a compound, meaning on that [place]; or on any limb such as hand, foot, etc. — [for that person,] the aggregate of death, fear, grief, disease, weapons, old age, and constant suffering is destroyed — this must be supplied. (GRhtCM 19.67-72:4)

children.text:
eteṣu sthāneṣu yasyeyaṃ nihitā sthāpitā bhavati sa
                            asurayakṣakinnarapūjyatamaḥ asurā daityāḥ yakṣā devayonayaḥ kinnarāḥ
                            turaṅgavaktrāḥ teṣāṃ pūjyatamo bhavati atiśayena pūjyaḥ pūjyatamaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_19.67-72:5 //
children.translated_text: In those places, he in whom this [pill] is deposited — placed — becomes most revered by <s>Asuras</s> (demons), <s>Yakṣas</s> (nature spirits), and <s>Kinnaras</s> (celestial musicians) — <s>Asuras</s> are <s>Daityas</s>; <s>Yakṣas</s> are a class of divine beings; <s>Kinnaras</s> are horse-faced [celestials] — he becomes most revered by them — revered with supreme distinction. (GRhtCM 19.67–72:5)

children.text:
siddhayogīndraiḥ pūjyatamaḥ siddhā devaviśeṣāḥ yogīndrā nāgārjunādayaḥ
                            tato+anantaraṃ mṛtajīvanī japamadhye kṣiptvā prakṣāpya ghaṭikādvayaṃ
                            vadanagatā satī mṛtakasya puruṣasyotthāpanaṃ prabodhanaṃ kurute yaḥ
                            pumān puruṣaḥ tadeva toyaṃ guṭikākṣāpanaṃ svacchaṃ nirmapaṃ pibati
                            kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ pathyānvito hitāvahadravyabhakṣaṇayuktaḥ sa puruṣo divyaṃ
                            vapuḥ devaśarīraṃ pabhate kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ divyaṃ punaḥ mṛtyujarāvarjitaṃ
                            vyādhipāpityarahitaṃ punaḥ sudṛḍhaṃ vajravad guṭikāparimāṇaṃ
                            pākavidhānaṃ ca pūrvavad ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.67-72:6 //
children.translated_text: Most revered by <s>Siddhas</s> and lords of <s>Yogīs</s> — <s>Siddhas</s> are a special class of divine beings; lords of <s>Yogīs</s> are <s>Nāgārjuna</s> and the like. Then immediately, the death-reviving [pill] (<s>mṛtajīvanī</s>), having been cast — immersed — into water for two <s>ghaṭikās</s> (48 minutes), being placed in the mouth, effects the revival — the awakening — of a dead person. The man who drinks that very water — clear and pure — in which the pill was immersed, being accompanied by a wholesome diet — consuming beneficial substances — that person obtains a divine body — a body like that of the gods. Of what quality is that divine body? Free from death and old age, devoid of disease and calamity, and furthermore, exceedingly firm — like a diamond. The measure of the pill and the preparation-procedure are as previously described; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.67–72:6)

children.text: iti mṛtajīvanīguṭikā // GRhtCM_19.67-72:7 //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the death-reviving pill (<s>mṛtajīvanī guṭikā</s>). (GRhtCM 19.67–72:7)

children.text: vajriṇīguṭikā
children.translated_text: <s>Vajriṇī</s> (diamond) pill

children.text: kāntaghanasattvakamalaṃ hema ca tāraṃ yathā kṛtadvandvam /
children.translated_text: Lodestone (<s>kānta</s>) and mica (<s>ghana</s>) essences, copper (<s>kamala</s>), gold (<s>hema</s>), and silver (<s>tāra</s>), paired as appropriate,

children.text: samajīrṇaṃ bījavaraṃ vajrayutaṃ vajriṇī guṭikā // GRht_19.73 //
children.translated_text: equally digested, the best seed (<s>bījavara</s>), combined with diamond (<s>vajra</s>) — [this is] the <s>vajriṇī</s> pill. (GRht 19.73)

children.text: eṣā mukhakuharagatā kurute navanāgatulyabalam /
children.translated_text: This [pill], placed in the cavity of the mouth, confers strength equal to nine elephants (<s>navanāga</s>);

children.text: tadvapurapi durbhedyaṃ mṛtyujarāroganirmuktam // GRht_19.74 //
children.translated_text: that body also [becomes] impenetrable, freed from death, old age, and disease. (GRht 19.74)

children.text: vajriṇīguṭikāvidhānaṃ guṇāṃścāha kāntetyādi // GRhtCM_19.73-74:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the procedure and qualities of the <s>vajriṇī</s> pill, beginning with 'lodestone' and so on. (GRhtCM 19.73–74:1)

children.text:
kāntaṃ ca ghanaṃ ca anayoḥ sattvaṃ kāntaghanasattvaṃ kāntasattvaṃ
                            cumbakasattvaṃ ghanasattvaṃ abhrakasāraṃ kamapaṃ ceti kamapaṃ tāmraṃ ca
                            punarhema svarṇaṃ tāraṃ ca rūpyaṃ pūrvavat yathā yena vidhānena
                            kṛtadvandvaṃ kṛtaṃ ca tat dvandvaṃ ceti bījavaraṃ samajīrṇaṃ kāryaṃ
                            kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ bījavaraṃ vajrayutaṃ hīrakayutam iyaṃ guṭikā nāmato vajriṇī
                            punareṣā vajriṇīguṭikā mukhakuharagatā satī mukhāntaḥprāptā satī
                            navanāgatupyabapaṃ navasaṃkhyākā nāgāḥ hastinastaistupyaṃ tatsamaṃ
                            yadbapaṃ tatkurute tadvapustasya mukhe guṭikādhāriṇo vapuḥ śarīraṃ
                            durbhedyaṃ duḥkhena bhettuṃ śakyaṃ punarmṛtyujarāvyādhibhir nirmuktam
                            ityarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.73-74:2 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Kānta</s>' and '<s>ghana</s>' — the essence of these two: <s>kānta-sattva</s> is lodestone-essence; <s>ghana-sattva</s> is mica-essence; and '<s>kamala</s>' is copper; and furthermore '<s>hema</s>' is gold; '<s>tāra</s>' is silver; as before, by whatever procedure they are paired — 'the pairing has been made' [this is] the compound — [they should be] equally digested with the best seed (<s>bījavara</s>). Of what quality? The best seed combined with diamond (<s>hīraka</s>). This pill is called <s>vajriṇī</s> by name. Furthermore, this <s>vajriṇī</s> pill, being placed in the cavity of the mouth — having entered inside the mouth — confers strength equal to nine elephants — '<s>navanāga</s>' means nine elephants in number; the strength that is equal to theirs, that [this pill] confers. That body — of the person holding the pill in his mouth — [becomes] impenetrable — difficult to pierce. Furthermore, freed from death, old age, and disease; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.73–74:2)

children.text: iti vajriṇī guṭikā // GRhtCM_19.73-74:3 //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the <s>vajriṇī</s> pill. (GRhtCM 19.73–74:3)

children.text: khecarīguṭikā
children.translated_text: <s>Khecarī</s> (sky-moving) pill

children.text: dhūmāvalokitarase pañcamahāratnajārite sārite /
children.translated_text: In mercury that has been smoke-transmuted (<s>dhūmāvalokita</s>), digested with the five great gems, and extracted (<s>sārita</s>),

children.text: bījena gaganasattve mākṣikakāntaprayuktena // GRht_19.75 //
children.translated_text: with a seed [composed] of mica-essence, <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite), and lodestone (<s>kānta</s>) — (GRht 19.75)

children.text: khecarasaṃjñā guṭikā patati mukhe kṣiptamātreṇa /
children.translated_text: the pill called <s>khecarī</s> (sky-mover), merely by being placed in the mouth, falls [i.e., manifests its power];

children.text: devāsurasiddhagaṇaiḥ pūjyatamo bhavati cendrādyaiḥ // GRht_19.76 //
children.translated_text: by the hosts of gods (<s>devas</s>), demons (<s>asuras</s>), and <s>siddhas</s>, he becomes most revered — [even] by <s>Indra</s> and the rest. (GRht 19.76)

children.text: khecarīguṭikāvidhānaṃ guṇāṃścāha dhūmetyādi // GRhtCM_19.75-76:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He states the procedure and qualities of the <s>khecarī</s> pill, beginning with 'smoke' and so on. (GRhtCM 19.75–76:1)

children.text:
dhūmāvapokite dhūmavedhini rase sūte pañcamahāratnajārite
                            pañcasaṃkhyākair mahāratnair vajrādibhiḥ tathā ca /
children.translated_text: 'Smoke-transmuted' means smoke-pierced mercury (<s>dhūmavedhin</s>); 'digested with the five great gems' — with the five great gems such as diamond and the like; and thus:

children.text: vajraṃ ca mauktikaṃ caiva māṇikyaṃ nīpameva ca /
children.translated_text: Diamond, pearl, ruby, sapphire,

children.text: marakataṃ ca vijñeyaṃ mahāratnāni pañcadhā /
children.translated_text: and emerald — these should be known as the five great gems.
Thus. (GRhtCM 19.75–76:2)

children.text:
punar mākṣikakāntaprayuktena tāpyacumbakamipitena bījena rase
                            gaganasattve sārite sati khecarasaṃjñā guṭikā bhavati //
                            GRhtCM_19.75-76:3 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, with a seed composed of <s>mākṣika</s> and lodestone — combined with pyrite and lodestone — in [such] mercury, with mica-essence having been extracted, the pill called <s>khecarī</s> comes into being. (GRhtCM 19.75–76:3)

children.text:
tasmin guṭikārūpe rase kṣiptamātreṇa mukhe patati sati indrādyaiḥ
                            devāsurasiddhagaṇaiśca pūjyatamo bhavati indro maghavā ādyo yeṣāṃ te
                            taiḥ // GRhtCM_19.75-76:4 //
children.translated_text: In that mercury in pill form, merely by being placed — dropped — into the mouth, being present [therein], by <s>Indra</s> and the rest — by the hosts of gods, demons, and <s>siddhas</s> — he becomes most revered. <s>Indra</s> is <s>Maghavan</s>; 'those of whom he is foremost' — by them. (GRhtCM 19.75–76:4)

children.text:
devā amarāḥ asurāḥ daityāḥ siddhā devaviśeṣāḥ teṣāṃ ye gaṇāḥ samūhāḥ taiḥ
                            kṛtvā atiśayena pūjyo bhavatītyarthaḥ // GRhtCM_19.75-76:5 //
children.translated_text: 'Gods' are immortals; 'demons' are <s>Daityas</s>; '<s>Siddhas</s>' are a special class of divine beings; their hosts — assemblages — by them, he becomes revered with supreme distinction; that is the meaning. (GRhtCM 19.75–76:5)

children.text: iti khecarasaṃjñāguṭikā // GRhtCM_19.75-76:6 //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the pill called <s>khecarī</s>. (GRhtCM 19.75–76:6)

children.text: rasavādo+anantaguṇo dravagolakakalkabhedena /
children.translated_text: The science of mercury-alchemy (<s>rasavāda</s>) is of infinite qualities, [varying] by the distinctions of liquid (<s>drava</s>), pellet (<s>golaka</s>), and paste (<s>kalka</s>);

children.text: kalitaḥ pradhānasiddhairyair dṛṣṭaste jayanti narāḥ // GRht_19.77 //
children.translated_text: those men who have mastered [it], envisioned by the foremost <s>Siddhas</s>, are triumphant. (GRht 19.77)

children.text: rasavādasyānantatvaṃ sūcayannāha rasetyādi // GRhtCM_19.77:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Indicating the infinitude of <s>rasavāda</s>, he says 'mercury' and so on. (GRhtCM 19.77:1)

children.text:
rasavādo 'nantaguṇaḥ anantā guṇā yasya sa tathoktaḥ // GRhtCM_19.77:2
                            //
children.translated_text: <s>Rasavāda</s> (mercury-alchemy) is 'of infinite qualities' — that whose qualities are infinite is so described. (GRhtCM 19.77:2)

children.text: anantā aparimitāḥ // GRhtCM_19.77:3 //
children.translated_text: 'Infinite' means unlimited. (GRhtCM 19.77:3)

children.text:
kena kṛtvā rasavādo+anantaḥ dravagopakakapkānāṃ pratyekamanantatvāt
                            rasavādo+apyanantaḥ // GRhtCM_19.77:4 //
children.translated_text: Why is <s>rasavāda</s> infinite? Because each of the [forms] — liquid, pellet, and paste — is individually infinite, <s>rasavāda</s> too is infinite. (GRhtCM 19.77:4)

children.text:
kiṃbhūtaḥ pradhānasiddhaiḥ nityanāthādibhiḥ kapitaḥ racitaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_19.77:5 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality? Composed — created — by the foremost <s>Siddhas</s> such as <s>Nityanātha</s> and others. (GRhtCM 19.77:5)

children.text:
yairmahadbhiḥ siddhaiḥ rasavādo dṛṣṭaste narā jayanti sarvotkarṣeṇa
                            vartante // GRhtCM_19.77:6 //
children.translated_text: Those great <s>Siddhas</s> by whom <s>rasavāda</s> was envisioned — those men are triumphant — they exist in supreme excellence. (GRhtCM 19.77:6)

children.text: śītāṃśuvaṃśasambhavahaihayakulajanmajanitaguṇamahimā /
children.translated_text: Born in the Lunar Dynasty (<s>Śītāṃśu-vaṃśa</s>), of the <s>Haihaya</s> clan, whose glory of qualities was produced by [his noble] birth —

children.text: sa jayati śrīmadanaśca kirātanātho rasācāryaḥ // GRht_19.78 //
children.translated_text: he, the illustrious <s>Madana</s>, lord of the <s>Kirātas</s>, master of mercury-science (<s>rasācārya</s>), is triumphant. (GRht 19.78)

children.text: yasya svayamavatīrṇā rasavidyā sakalamaṅgalādhārā /
children.translated_text: He to whom mercury-science (<s>rasavidyā</s>), the foundation of all auspiciousness, descended of its own accord —

children.text: paramaśreyasahetuḥ śreyaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ pūrvam // GRht_19.79 //
children.translated_text: [this science,] the supreme cause of the highest good, [was] first the good [attained by] <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>). (GRht 19.79)

children.text:
atha granthakārayitur vaṃśavarṇanam āha śītāṃśuvaṃśetyādi //
                            GRhtCM_19.78-79:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now he states the lineage-description of the one who caused the treatise to be composed, beginning with 'Lunar Dynasty' and so on. (GRhtCM 19.78–79:1)

children.text:
śrīmadano madanābhidho rājā jayati sarvotkarṣeṇa vartate //
                            GRhtCM_19.78-79:2 //
children.translated_text: The illustrious <s>Madana</s> — the king named <s>Madana</s> — is triumphant — exists in supreme excellence. (GRhtCM 19.78–79:2)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ kirātanāthaḥ kirātāḥ bhippāsteṣāṃ svāmī // GRhtCM_19.78-79:3
                            //
children.translated_text: Of what quality? Lord of the <s>Kirātas</s> — '<s>Kirātas</s>' are tribal people (<s>Bhillas</s>); he is their lord. (GRhtCM 19.78–79:3)

children.text:
punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ śītāṃśuvaṃśasaṃbhavahaihayakupajanmajanitaguṇamahimā
                            śītāṃśuvaṃśe candravaṃśe saṃbhava utpattiryasya tat evaṃvidhaṃ yat
                            haihayakupaṃ tatra kupe janmanā udbhavena janito guṇānāṃ mahimā yena sa
                            tathoktaḥ // GRhtCM_19.78-79:4 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, of what quality? 'Born in the Lunar Dynasty, of the <s>Haihaya</s> clan, whose glory of qualities was produced by [his noble] birth' — born in the Lunar Dynasty (<s>Candra-vaṃśa</s>), of such a nature that the <s>Haihaya</s> clan — by birth in that clan — his glory of qualities was produced; he is so described. (GRhtCM 19.78–79:4)

children.text:
punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭo madanaḥ rasācāryaḥ rasavidyājanaka ityarthaḥ //
                            GRhtCM_19.78-79:5 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, of what quality is <s>Madana</s>? A master of mercury-science (<s>rasācārya</s>) — meaning the originator of mercury-science. (GRhtCM 19.78–79:5)

children.text:
atha cāsya kārayitur guṇavarṇanamāha yasyetyādi // GRhtCM_19.78-79:6
                            //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now he states the praise of the qualities of the patron, beginning with 'to whom' and so on. (GRhtCM 19.78–79:6)

children.text:
yasya kārayituḥ śrīmadanasaṃjñasya rasavidyā svayaṃ svarūpatvenāvatīrṇā
                            prādurbhūtā // GRhtCM_19.78-79:7 //
children.translated_text: To this patron named <s>Madana</s>, mercury-science descended of its own accord — manifested spontaneously. (GRhtCM 19.78–79:7)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭā rasavidyā sakapamaṅgapādhārā sakapāni ca tāni maṅgapāni
                            uttamarūpāṇi teṣāmādhāraḥ āśrayo yasyāṃ sā // GRhtCM_19.78-79:8 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality is the mercury-science? 'The foundation of all auspiciousness' — all things that are auspicious — of excellent form — [this science] is their foundation — the abode in which [they reside]. (GRhtCM 19.78–79:8)

children.text:
eṣā rasavidyā śarīraṃ ajarāmaraṇaṃ ajarāmaraṃ kurute śarīraṃ ca
                            dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ mūpaṃ ataḥ sakapamaṅgapādhāreti yuktam //
                            GRhtCM_19.78-79:9 //
children.translated_text: This mercury-science makes the body free from aging and death — ageless and immortal; and the body is the root of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>artha</s> (wealth), <s>kāma</s> (desire), and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation); therefore, it is fitting [to call it] 'the foundation of all auspiciousness.' (GRhtCM 19.78–79:9)

children.text:
punaḥ rasavidyā śreyase muktau parama utkṛṣṭo hetuḥ kāraṇam //
                            GRhtCM_19.78-79:10 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, mercury-science is the supreme — the most excellent — cause of the highest good, i.e., liberation (<s>mukti</s>). (GRhtCM 19.78–79:10)

children.text:
anayaiva rasavidyayā parameṣṭhino brahmaṇaḥ pūrvaṃ prathamaṃ śreyo
                            'jarāmaraṇarūpaṃ saṃjātam // GRhtCM_19.78-79:11 //
children.translated_text: By this very mercury-science, the highest good — in the form of agelessness and deathlessness — first arose for <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>). (GRhtCM 19.78–79:11)

children.text: tasmāt kirātanṛpater bahumānam avāpya rasakarmanirataḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, having obtained the great esteem of the <s>Kirāta</s> king, devoted to the work of mercury —

children.text: rasahṛdayākhyaṃ tantraṃ viracitavān bhikṣugovindaḥ // GRht_19.80 //
children.translated_text: the mendicant <s>Govinda</s> (<s>Bhikṣu Govinda</s>) composed this treatise called <s>Rasahṛdaya</s>. (GRht 19.80)

children.text: kartā svanāmamahattvaṃ sūcayannāha tasmādityādi // GRhtCM_19.80:1 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The author, indicating his own name and greatness, says 'therefore' and so on. (GRhtCM 19.80:1)

children.text:
idaṃ rasatantraṃ śāstraṃ viracitavān kṛtavāniti bhāvaḥ // GRhtCM_19.80:2
                            //
children.translated_text: This mercury-treatise (<s>rasatantra</s>), this scientific work, was composed — created; that is the purport. (GRhtCM 19.80:2)

children.text:
kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ idaṃ tantraṃ rasahṛdayākhyaṃ kiṃ kṛtvā tasmādityādi //
                            GRhtCM_19.80:3 //
children.translated_text: Of what quality is this treatise? Called <s>Rasahṛdaya</s> (Heart of Mercury). Having done what? 'Therefore' and so on. (GRhtCM 19.80:3)
